name: Reduced Emissions from Avoided Deforestation in the Multiple Use Zone of the Maya Biosphere Reserve in Guatemala (GuateCarbon)
project_type: Agriculture Forestry and Other Land Use
description: The Guatecarbon REDD+ project is a voluntary forest carbon project that is jointly managed by the local community forestry association of the Petén (ACOFOP) and the national council for protected areas of Guatemala (CONAP) The project activities take place within the Multiple-use Zone (MUZ), 797,868ha or 38%, of the total Maya Biosphere Reserve (MBR), which encompasses 2,080,298 ha. The project seeks to produce a net reduction in greenhouse house gas emissions from deforestation (RED) of approximately 41,579,156 tCO2e by strengthening and improving the existing model of co-management arrangements in the MUZ between local residents and the national government, and by improving zoning, land use planning and enforcement.
abuse_descr: Despite the efforts in capacity building, the project participants have not received payments for carbon credits to date (10 April 2025)
abuseuno_id: From promises to practice: Persistent challenges in safeguarding local rights in forest carbon market initiatives

name: Programa Jurisdicional de REDD+ do Tocantins
developer: Secretary of Environment and Water Resources (SEMARH), state of Tocantins
project_type: Agriculture Forestry and Other Land Use
description: The Tocantins Jurisdictional REDD+ Programme is a REDD+ initiative using the market approach at sub-national level in Brazil, which aims to value the state's efforts to reduce greenhouse gas (GHG) emissions from deforestation and forest degradation, as well as forest conservation activities throughout the state. The programme was structured on the basis of two legal frameworks: the State Policy for Environmental Conservation and Sustainable Development (PEMC) and the State Policy for Payment for Environmental Services (PEPSA).
abuse_descr: The Tocantins Articulation of Agroecology (ATA) has reported several irregularities concerning the Tocantins Jurisdictional REDD+ Programme to the Federal Public Prosecutor's Office (MPF) and the National REDD+ Safeguards Committee (CONAREDD+), including the violation of the right to Free, Prior and Informed Consultation (FPIC) of the state's traditional communities, quilombolas and babassu coconut breakers. According to the document, the REDD+ programme promoted by the state government has failed to comply with Convention 169 of the International Labour Organisation (ILO), by not guaranteeing a transparent process of access to information and consultation with the peoples and communities involved. According to the complaint, the state has only held consultations on the benefit-sharing sub-programmes - aimed at Indigenous Peoples, Traditional Peoples and Communities and Family Farmers (PIPCTAF) - within the scope of the Climate Fund, and not on the programme as a whole.
abuseuno_id: Movimentos sociais denunciam irregularidades no Programa de REDD+ Jurisdicional do Tocantins ao MPF e CONAREDD+

name: Kajiado Rangelands Carbon Project
developer: Soils for the Future Africa Ltd
project_type: Agriculture Forestry and Other Land Use
description: This project features implementation of rapid rotational grazing practices by dense aggregations of livestock to restore perennial grasses on degraded rangelands across 1.5 million hectares in southern Kenya. These new grazing practices are additional because they differ from the seasonal shifts in grazing activity from wet to dry season ranges and would not be possible without carbon revenues to support governance and monitoring of grazing activities. Rapid rotational grazing will enhance adaptation to climate change by improving soil water holding capacity, increasing surface water availability and providing grass banks as a hedge against drought. Habitat improvement from new grazing practices will restore wildlife corridors between iconic High Conservation Areas such as Serengeti, Kilimanjaro, Nairobi, and Tsavo National Parks and their associated ecosystems and enhance diversity of endemic taxa of plants, birds and insects. Finally, the project will provide direct benefits to 17 or more pastoralist communities in form of funds for bursaries to support women and the poorest community members as well as to construct water capture structures and infrastructure for delivering livestock to market. The project is expected to remove more than 63 million tons CO2e over the project lifetime of 40 years, or nearly 1.6 million tons CO2e a year on average.
abuse_descr: The Oldonyonyokie Community Group Ranch in Kajiado County in Kenya, in a bold act of resistance, has pushed back against the wave of land acquisition by organizations in the name climate action. In the latest turn of events (May 2025), the community turned against carbon offset projects which they believe threaten to displace indigenous people and undermine centuries-old land rights. The group was promised to earn Sh1,165 (nine dollars) per acre upon selling of the carbon credits. They were not told how much the company will be selling them for. 'We are still learning about that…..ni ngumu kuelewa hiyo ( it is hard to understand that).' The agreement states that they will earn Sh360 (two dollars). 'Even the dead have been counted among those who gave consent. How can we trust this?'
abuseuno_id: No carbon credits!: Chaos erupts over 40-year land deal in Kajiado
abusedue_id: Kajiado community fights back against carbon offset land grabs

name: Sofala Community Carbon Project (formerly the N'hambita Community Carbon Project)
project_type: Agriculture Forestry and Other Land Use
description: The project has implemented agroforestry activities as well as interventions that have resulted in avoided deforestation. The project enabled individuals and companies to effectively invest in new forests and agroforestry. By becoming trained crop farmers, local people contributed significantly to their own environments whilst securing regular income and stable, sustainable food supplies. The revival of agroforestry among impoverished communities generated crops that enriched rather than exhausted their fragile forest soils. The project seeked to link the establishment and protection of carbon stocks to sustainable development by using carbon revenues to kickstart small commercial enterprises. Moreover, the project offered protection to African wildlife. The Sofala project also has extended farming and capacity-building to project participants, and had a strong focus on diversifying farmers’ income streams. The project trained smallholders in the sustainable farming of important cash crops, which most farmers then incorporated into their plantings. This not only contributed to improving food security for themselves, but also enabled them to access additional income streams.
abuse_descr: The UK company Envirotrade began a REDD+ project in 2003 that involved communities in the buffer zone of the Gorongosa National Park in nothern Mozambique. The project sold carbon credits on the voluntary market. Envirotrade recruited hundreds of villagers to plant trees. Families that received payments during only seven years, were obliged to take care of the trees for many more years. In 2018, the company abandoned the region, leaving behind unfulfilled obligations, debts to villagers and hundreds of perplexed families.
abuseuno_id: The Legacy of the Community Carbon Project in Nhambita, Mozambique: Nostalgia, Disillusionment and Indignation
abusedue_id: Bank of evidence on false climate solutions

name: SIVIRÚ-USARAGÁ-PIZARRO-PILIZÁ (SUPP) REDD+ Project
project_type: Agriculture Forestry and Other Land Use
description: REDD+ Project to mitigate climate change, protect rich biodiversity, and generate sources of income for poor communities, through forest governance, capacity building, and productive activities that will prevent selective logging of native forests, avoiding degradation and deforestation. Located in the South of Choco, Pacific coast of Colombia. Developed by BIOREDD+/USAID

project_type: Agriculture Forestry and Other Land Use
description: Proyecto REDD+ para mitigar el cambio climático, proteger la rica biodiversidad y generar fuentes de ingresos para las comunidades pobres, a través de la gobernanza forestal, el desarrollo de capacidades y las actividades productivas que evitarán la tala selectiva de bosques nativos, evitando la degradación y la deforestación. name: UPPER TANA NAIROBI WATER FUND
project_type: Agriculture Forestry and Other Land Use
description: The Upper Tana-Nairobi Water Fund, a charitable trust in Kenya, operates in the Tana watershed. The project engages local communities in conservation, particularly through the promotion of agroforestry and tree growing for carbon sequestration. This generates carbon credits validated and managed under the Plan Vivo Standard. The water fund is working with tens of thousands of farmers across four counties - Laikipia, Nyeri, Murang’a, and Nyandarua, conserving over 330,000 hectares of land and sequestering millions of tonnes of carbon (removal). The trees planted are designed to provide long-term cover, reduce soil erosion, and provide livelihood benefits to communities. This complements the Trust’s biodiversity conservation work.

name: Drawa Rainforest Carbon Project
developer: Drawa Block Forest Communities Cooperative Ltd
project_type: Agriculture Forestry and Other Land Use
description: The project, as part of the Nakau Programme and owned by indigenous land owners, protects over 4,000 ha of tropical rainforest in Vanua Levu, Fiji. It helps the Fijian clans to protect their rainforests, therefore providing greater resilience against climate change, and also form community businesses including honey enterprises.

name: Luangwa Community Forests Project
project_type: Agriculture Forestry and Other Land Use
description: The Luangwa Community Forests Project is a large-scale REDD+ project implemented in Eastern and Lusaka Province, Zambia with an initial and second project activity instance of 943,646 ha and 92,990 ha respectively. A third project activity instance was added in 2022, comprising 199,622 ha, bringing the total project area to 1,236,258 ha. It is being implemented on communal land in 17 chiefdoms falling within Game Management Areas (GMA) and four private ranches. Implementation is in partnership with the traditional authorities and the government of the Republic of Zambia. The project will generate emissions reductions through avoided deforestation, using the following mitigation activities: a combination of direct conservation support (forest monitoring and encroachment prevention) engagement and capacity building with key Government and community stakeholders, and conservation incentives for the area protected: including performance-based payments delivered to empowered community stakeholders, through local institutions, and support to deforestation mitigation activities, including sustainable, improved livelihoods activities.
abuse_descr: Greenpeace Italy’s report points out that the statutory instrument, determined in collaboration between the government and BCP, gives the communities living in the project area full rights to the forest while excluding neighboring communities that would normally benefit from the forest’s resources, creating a type of fortress conservation. Despite this, safari companies organize trips for (normally white) paying customers within fenced territories where animals are hunted for sport. In contrast, community members living in the project area are also not allowed to use the forests except for certain non-timber resources.
abuseuno_id: Global Atlas of Environmental Justice. Luangwa Community Forests REDD+ Project (LCFP), Zambia

name: Guajira I Wind Farm
description: The Project consists of a Greenfield wind power plant with a rated capacity of 20 MW and a net annual energy production of 106,288 MWh per year, which will lead to an annual GHG emission reduction estimated by 50,699 tCO2 per year. The Project will be connected to the National Interconnected Grid through the transmission line owned by CARBONES DEL CERREJÓN LIMITED.
abuse_descr: The Colectivo Geografia Critica del Ecuador, via the ‘Map of False Solutions’ platform, identifies the following impacts for the project: Loss or alteration of land use rights (water, ecosystems, roads, seeds, etc.); Loss of habitats, biodiversity or agro-diversity; Extinction of species; Deepening of previous inequalities (racial, gender, class, etc.); Increased dependence on external inputs; Loss of local practices and knowledge; Loss of territorial autonomy.
abuseuno_id: Mapeo falsas soluciones al cambio climático

name: Reforestation of Degraded Lands in Sierra Leone
project_type: Agriculture Forestry and Other Land Use
description: Miro Forestry has over 10,000 hectares of standing plantations, expanding this plantation area at a rate of 3,000 hectares per year and producing sustainable timber products including plywood, rotary veneer, poles, sawn timber, and wood biomass. The plantations are Forest Stewardship Council™ (FSC™) certified meaning the voluntary compliance with the international gold standard of responsible forest management. The Yoni Plantation is around 8.5° north of the equator and has a tropical climate with average monthly temperatures ranging between 26°C and 36°C and annual rainfall in excess of 2,000mm. The dry season typically spans between December and March having less than 100mm of rainfall. The land on which the Company is establishing plantation forests was once forested with primary forest, however, the land now consists of secondary growth including grasses, low level bush and palms. The land is being leased under longterm agreements with landowners ratified by the chief’s and government as legal custodians. The land area has limited subsistence farming going on which is primarily centered around the low lying swampy areas for rice cultivation unsuitable for forestry. The Company works in ongoing consultation with local farmers and aims to bring additional benefit to such farmers through opening up swampy areas for rice cultivation and enabling controlled agroforestry thus providing clear land for subsistence farming, mutual crop protection and keeping the land free of nutrient sapping undergrowth. Miro Forestry aims to conform to high environmental, ethical, financial and social standards, and achieve international forestry certification on all plantations. It aims to be the preferred partner for local communities, the national government, and international development and finance.
abuse_descr: The developer Miro leases land from communities for a rental fee (reportedly only $2 ha/yr) and its promised social projects have not materialised. The communities say the company's plantations block their access to critical transport routes and water sources.
abuseuno_id: Friends of the Earth comments letter to the U.S. International Development Finance Corporation

name: AFFORESTATION OF DEGRADED GRASSLANDS IN VICHADA, COLOMBIA
project_type: Agriculture Forestry and Other Land Use
description: The grouped project aim is to recover degraded grasslands in Vichada, Colombia, through the establishment of timber plantations. The first instance consists of the afforestation of 30,605 ha of low-fertility grasslands that have been degraded by livestock in the municipalities of Puerto Carreño and La Primavera, it includes the planting of Eucalyptus (Eucalyptus pellita) and Acacia (Acacia mangium) as timber species. Through afforestation activities to recover degraded lands, the project aims to promote connectivity between ecosystems. In addition, this project is expected to provide more than 200 full-time employment opportunities (with equal access to women and men) in a zone historically affected by poverty. Furthermore, the increase in the forest cover and sequestration of carbon in living biomass will contribute to the reduction of GHG emissions by acting as sink that sequesters an average of 139,489 tCO2e per year.
abuse_descr: 'There are severe tensions over land in Vichada, which is home to numerous Indigenous communities and peasant families displaced from other parts of the country, and large agribusiness corporations, like Cargill, that have recently started moving into the area and grabbing lands' (grain.org, 2024). It is expected that landgrabbing, even for carbon offsetting projects, will increase the ongoing land conflict.
abuseuno_id: Vichada: tierra de hombres para hombres sin tierra

name: Proyecto de compensación de emisiones Conservación del bosque Galilea-Amé
developer: Fundación Fundame.Col, Ecocarbono SAS ZOMAC Universidad del Tolima
project_type: Agriculture Forestry and Other Land Use
description: The Galilea Forest Conservation REDD+ Project Amé, has the main objective to preserve the region's native forests by reducing Greenhouse Gas (GHG) emissions caused by deforestation and degradation, also preserving and protecting local biodiversity through inter-institutional programs and initiatives, the development of activities that promote CO2 emissions reduction, execution of social strategies with the purpose of maintaining these forests in a state of conservation. From a biophysical perspective, the region where the project is located (Department of Tolima) characterizes itself by having a high diversity of fauna and flora distributed in different types of ecosystems, as well as a large supply of water resources. In addition these forests are part of the priority areas for conservation in the Andean and Amazonian region, since they are located in the biological corridor that connects the Andean and High Andean forests with the Sumapaz Paramo, National Natural Park and the Galilea Forest Regional Natural Park. It is the last relict of primary forest in eastern Tolima which contains the river Río Negro, main source of the Hidro Prado dam that generates and supplies clean energy to most of the local communities.
abuse_descr: Leaders, settlers and peasants in the region claim to have been excluded from the project. Approximately 87% of the area included in the compensation programme is part of a regional park, which is managed and protected by the Colombian state through the departmental environmental authority (Cortolima), while the project proponents claim it is a private reserve.
abuseuno_id: En un proyecto de bonos de carbono en bosques andinos colombianos todo parece estar bajo la niebla

name: Batéké Carbon Sink (BaCaSi)
project_type: Agriculture Forestry and Other Land Use
description: Batéké Carbon Sink (BaCaSi) is an integrated landscape management project taking place in the Plateaux Province of the Republic of Congo, close to the city of Ngo, including planting and Assisted Natural Regeneration (ANR) activities. The Project proposes solutions to the local problem of ecosystem degradation by meeting the needs of local populations. The establishment of agroforestry plantation and plantation for timber purpose will (i) improve livelihoods of local populations in the long term, (ii) decrease pressure on ecosystems, and (iii) permanently increase the amount of carbon stored in the area.
abuse_descr: Indigenous peoples, banned from accessing the forest from late 2021 to early 2023, has directly threatened their harvesting activities, thereby jeopardising their livelihoods and income. The tree planting site affects four indigenous communities located near Ngo: the Olly community (408 residents), Indion community (253 residents), Socofran community (207 residents), and Ngo 2 community (142 residents).
abuseuno_id: CARBON OFFSETTING AT THE COST OF HUMAN RIGHTS? The case of TotalEnergies’ BaCaSi project in Congo
abusedue_id: Republic of Congo: expansion of tree plantations linked to the carbon market - the underside of an opaque business and greenwashing

name: Proyecto Ambiental de Protección Pachamama Cumbal
developer: Global Consulting and Assessment Services S.A. de C.V., SPV Business S.A.S
project_type: Agriculture Forestry and Other Land Use
description: The Pachamama Cumbal Environmental REDD+ Protection Project is an initiative of the Pasto indigenous people of the Cumbal, Mayasquer, Panam and Chiles 'resguardos', represented by their own governance organisation. The project aims to protect and conserve ecosystems dominated by high and sub-Andean forests, as well as a large paramo region in the southern Colombian Andes, over a 100-year loan period, by implementing additional activities designed primarily to mitigate and adapt the region to the adverse effects of climate change. In addition to climate and ecosystem benefits, the project will provide employment opportunities and direct and indirect benefits for 37,033 inhabitants of 38 villages. The project covers about 103,154 ha, of which 42,413 ha correspond to the project implementation area and 60,770 ha to the leakage area. The Pachamama Cumbal Environmental REDD+ Protection Project is located in southern Colombia, at the southern end of the Western Cordillera in the department of Nariño within the boundaries of the municipalities of Cumbal and Ricaurte. It is located in the Chiles and Cumbal paramo complex. It is bordered to the north by the municipality of Ricaurte (Nariño), to the south by the border with Ecuador, to the east by the municipality of Causpud (Nariño) and to the west by the municipality of Ricaurte.
abuse_descr: A carbon project began selling credits from the indigenous reservation of Cumbal, in the paramos of southern Colombia, despite the fact that most of its inhabitants were not even aware of its existence. At the forefront of the initiative, which has caused tension in the community and whose documents are not public, is a Mexican company and its Colombian subsidiary, whose manager was a founder and shareholder of the company that audited its own project.
abuseuno_id: Un resguardo vendía bonos de carbono y los indígenas no lo sabían
abusedue_id: El proyecto de carbono suspendido que sigue transando bonos e incumple fallo judicial

name: DEIYIABENA REDD+ NÜKAK BAKA
project_type: Agriculture Forestry and Other Land Use
description: The DEIYIABENA REDD+ NÜKAK project is being developed in a territorial extension of 824,842 hectares of project area and 275,337 hectares of 'cinturón de fugas', without overlapping with National Natural Parks, in the jurisdiction of the Nükak Makú Indigenous Resguardo. These hectares correspond to tropical forest of the Colombian Amazon biome in the department of Guaviare under the jurisdiction of the Corporación para el Desarrollo Sostenible del Norte y el Oriente Amazónico (Corporation for the Sustainable Development of the Northern and Eastern Amazon). The purpose of the project is the mitigation of the emissions of Carbon Dioxide CO2, Greenhouse Gases (GHG), through the promotion of Nature Based Solutions by the local communities. The communities are made up of 14 semi-nomadic indigenous clans that are constituted in the Mauro Munu assembly that still survive from the Nükak ethnic group. The objective of this project is to generate an integrated sustainable management of the forest that generates social, environmental and economic co-benefits for the Nükak community and other stakeholders in the mitigation of emissions from deforestation and forest degradation.
abuse_descr: According to Akubadaura, an NGO that offers legal support to indigenous communities in Colombia, the contract signed in 2021 between the project developer Waldrettung and the Nukak indigenous leadership, containing a 100-year exclusivity and irrevocability clause in favour of the developer for the development of projects to sell carbon credits, takes advantage of the situation of lack of knowledge about carbon credits mechanism, the context of hunger and extermination in which the Nukak are forced, demonstrating a condition of inequality and disproportionality between the company and the indigenous authority that signs.
abuseuno_id: Indígenas negocian bonos de carbono en desventaja y sin respaldo estatal
abusedue_id: REDD+ projects in the Colombian Amazon: Social challenges and lack of transparency

name: BAKA ROKARIRE ~IA TIR+~DITO
project_type: Agriculture Forestry and Other Land Use
description: The Baka Rokarire ~Ia Tir+~dito project is a project focused on mitigating greenhouse gas emissions through comprehensive forest management in the Colombian Amazon region, seeking to reduce greenhouse gas emissions resulting from the deforestation and degradation of natural forests found in the project area, and removal of greenhouse gases due to the implementation of actions that promote forest restoration.
abuse_descr: On 28 April 2023, the Colombian Constitutional Court ruled on a lawsuit filed by the indigenous authorities of the Pirá Paraná against a carbon credit project in their territory. The claimants argue that the person who signed the legal document on behalf of the indigenous people with Masbosques (the project developer) in March 2021 was the previous legal representative of the Association of Indigenous Traditional Authorities of the Pirá Paraná River (Acaipi), who had been removed from office two weeks before the signing. They also claim that Masbosques negotiated individually with several leaders of the territory, in addition to the one who was no longer the legal representative of Acaipi. However, the claimants argue, Masbosques never sought out the Indigenous Council, which has been the highest authority in Pirá Paraná since May 2019. For the current authorities, the way Masbosques promoted the project - in their words ‘through documentary artifices and fraudulent manoeuvres’ - violated their fundamental rights.
abuseuno_id: Primer fallo de la Corte sobre bonos de carbono acerca a indígenas y empresarios
abusedue_id: The grey carbon tangle in Pirá Paraná

name: Mitigation of GHG: Rubber based agro-forestry system for sustainable development and poverty reduction in Pakkading, Bolikhamsay Province, Lao PDR
developer: Lao Thai Hua Rubber Co. Ltd
project_type: Agriculture Forestry and Other Land Use
description: The project aims at developing a forestry project in Lao PDR by establishing 969.20 hectares of rubber plantations according to a pioneering social and economic formula that provides sustainable change to poor rural communities without adverse impact on land ownership issues. The proposed project will sequestrate approximately 1,107,495 tCO2-e during its 30 year project period. Annual average GHG removals are estimated to be approximately 36,916 tCO2-e. The project will provide over and above the carbon sequestration: 1. Poverty alleviation and wealth creation in rural areas, 2. Communities empowerment through active participation in all stages of the project, and 3. Improvement of basic infrastructure for rural communities.
abuse_descr: The lack of adequate consultation fuels conflicts over allocation of plots and price setting. Only a tiny minority of people had ever heard of the concept of carbon sequestration, and those that had rarely understood the concept, which is often translated and referred to by locals as ‘selling oxygen’. While carbon sequestration can arguably be a complex concept to explain, it is nevertheless every company’s duty to make an effort to do so, particularly to the affected populations. As enshrined in Free, Prior, and Informed Consent (FPIC). Even so, the difficulties in understanding carbon trading are not only due to language and cultural barriers; it is often incomprehensible to farmers why large investors should suddenly receive money for activities that they themselves have been carrying out for centuries, such as planting trees or cultivating rubber.
abuseuno_id: WHO BENEFITS FROM TREE-PLANTING IN THE GLOBAL SOUTH? The case of two carbon offset projects in Laos
abusedue_id: Land tenure lesson from Laos for forest carbon projects

name: Afforestation in Eucalyptus and Acacia plantations for Burapha Agroforestry Co., Ltd.
project_type: Agriculture Forestry and Other Land Use
description: The proposed VCS grouped project “Afforestation in Eucalyptus and Acacia plantations for Burapha Agroforestry Co., Ltd.”, represents one of the first major afforestation projects of the private sector in Lao PDR. It promotes and implements afforestation of Eucalyptus and Acacia agroforestry plantations on degraded areas. These areas are either privately owned, village owned or part of governmental “Production Forest Areas”, which entirely are degraded by swidden agriculture for rice cropping by local communities. The plantations are established in the Prefecture of Vientiane and the Provinces of Vientiane, Xayabouly, and Saysomboun in Lao PDR. Local villagers are allowed to use the plantations for intercropping or grazing, which is part of the agroforestry approach of the project. The project generates GHG removals through tree and soil carbon sequestration. These credits are generated using the CDM methodology AR-ACM0003: “Afforestation and reforestation of lands except wetlands” (version 2). Burapha is also FSC certified and managed to plant successfully about 3,500 ha by 2020, contracted from 28 villages and plans to scale up its plantations to 15,000 ha by 2025. 20% of the total area which are set aside for conservation management. The main tree species of the project are the exotic species of Eucalyptus cumadulensis (98%) and acacia auriculiformis (2%). The rotation period is 7 years and during the first years the local farmers can do intercropping. Between years 3 to 7 cattle grazing is allowed on the plantation areas and in the years 3 and 4 the plantations get thinned out. After the first rotation the Eucalypts get coppiced and replanted after each second rotation. The project will generate average removals of 205 t CO2/ha. Over a crediting period of 20 years the project will generate 604,015 tCO2e and 30,201 tCO2/yr.

Only a tiny minority of people had ever heard of the concept of carbon sequestration, and those that had rarely understood the concept, which is often translated and referred to by locals as ‘selling oxygen’. While carbon sequestration can arguably be a complex concept to explain, it is nevertheless every company’s duty to make an effort to do so, particularly to the affected populations. As enshrined in Free, Prior, and Informed Consent (FPIC). Even so, the difficulties in understanding carbon trading are not only due to language and cultural barriers; it is often incomprehensible to farmers why large investors should suddenly receive money for activities that they themselves have been carrying out for centuries, such as planting trees or cultivating rubber.

name: Ipixuna REDD+ Project
developer: Associacao do Povo Parintintin da Terra Indigena I (02367282293), Organization do Povo Indigena Parintintim do Amazonas – OPIPAM (01444198000165)
project_type: Agriculture Forestry and Other Land Use
description: The Project is located in western region of the state of Mato Grosso along the border with Rondônia comprising of the municipalities of Humaita, Amazonas. The project has a total of 212 720.64 hectares where 196 025.30 are cover by forest land. After an analysis of agents and causes of deforestation, a leakage belt of a buffer project area of 2 km was defined. This leakage area includes 43 461.62 ha of forest area. The Project is structured as a 30-year REDD project starting officially on July 1, 2017 ending on June 30, 2047, that has the total participation of all the community. The project foresees the reduction of emissions of 15 483 577 tCO2e during the 30 years of its useful life, that is, an average 516 119 tCO2e per year. For this purpose, the implementation of a REDD+ project (Reduction of Emissions due to Deforestation and Forest Degradation), which includes the conservation of carbon reserves, sustainable management of forests and improvement of forest reserves, is proposed. This will allow providing payments for emission reductions, considered an ecosystem service of the forests that the communities preserve through the care of the forests.
abuse_descr: The National Foundation for Indigenous Peoples (FUNAI) has asked federal authorities to consider opening an investigation and cancelling all contracts for the commercialisation of carbon credits with indigenous communities in the Amazon that involve companies owned or run by US businessman Michael Greene. A report published at the end of June by SUMAÚMA revealed questions raised by indigenous people and the Federal Public Prosecutor's Office about carbon projects drawn up by companies linked to Greene with Brazilian indigenous associations. FUNAI is also asking the authorities to evaluate measures to ban the American and his employees from entering Indigenous Lands 'for any and all purposes'. In the documents, the government agency in charge of defending the interests of indigenous peoples in Brazil assessed that there is 'strong evidence of violations of indigenous rights' in contracts negotiated between Agfor Empreendimentos, a company in which Greene is a partner, and representatives of the Parintintin indigenous peoples of the Ipixuna and Nove de Janeiro territories in Amazonas. According to FUNAI, the contracts are 'excessively disadvantageous' for the indigenous people and have enough problems to 'question the conduct and good faith' of the company.
abuseuno_id: Funai recomenda anulação de contratos de Michael Greene com indígenas

name: GKF AGROFORESTRY PROJECT IN TELANGANA
project_type: Agriculture Forestry and Other Land Use
description:
This is an agroforestry project on minor agriculture crop land and barren land aims to promote sustainable agroforestry practices across Telangana state of India. By planting diverse range of trees the project seeks to empower smallholders and tribal communities, increase tree cover, enhance income, conserve biodiversity, improve soil health, and generate emission reductions. The targeted farmers are small landholders and the land earmarked for plantation activities is privately owned.

Encompassing a total planttion of 6,000,000 trees in 10,000 ha of land, the farmers have undertaken tree plantations, primarily featuring Mangifera indica (mango), Santalum album (sandalwood), Psidium guajava (guava), Tectona grandis (teak), Azadirachta indica (neem), Swietenia macrophylla (mahogany), Casuarina equisetifolia (horsetail she-oak), Dalbergia sissoo (Indian rosewood), Aquilaria malaccensis (agarwood), Phyllanthus emblica (amla), Punica granatum (pomegranate), and Manilkara zapota (sapota) during the years 2021, 2022, and 2023. The districts included in the project area are :  Vikarabad, Ranga Reddy, Mahabub Nager, Narayanapeta, Sanga Reddy, Jogulambha Gadwal, Wanaparthy and Medchiel.

name: Global Safe Drinking Water for Schools in Cambodia
developer: Sustainability Investment Promotion and Development Joint Stock Company
description:
The proposed grouped projects aim at improving the quality of drinking water through dissemination of zero greenhouse gas emitting water purification systems to provide safe drinking water for schools and institutions throughout Cambodia that previously do not have access to public distribution network supply safe drinking water. In this grouped projects, schools include Kindergartens, nurseries, primary schools, secondary schools, high schools. Institutions would cover pagodas, community home, home for disabled, orphanage, nursing home, mental home. For this reason, this proposed project activity will avoid the use of thermal energy and/or low energy and associated emissions.
The grouped project activity will minimize the use of fossil fuels and non-renewable biomass utilized for boiling water as a means purification to achieve safe drinking water quality in the absence of this project activity. This directly leads to reduced greenhouse gas emissions. Furthermore, it can be helpful to user’s health.

name: Global Safe Drinking Water for Schools in Lao
developer: Sustainability Investment Promotion and Development Joint Stock Company
description:
The purpose of the group project activity is to provide safe drinking water to schools/institutions in rural communities of Laos. The proposed project activity aims to reduce the use and demand of wood fuel and fossil fuel that would have been used to boil the water to purify water in the absence of the proposed project activity by installation of safe drinking water treatment stations and distribution of safe drinking water purifier.
The project activity targets schools/institutions with no previous safe drinking water access. The geographical boundary is in Laos. In this grouped projects, schools include Kindergartens, nurseries, primary schools, secondary schools, high schools. Institutions would cover community home, home for disabled, orphanage, nursing home, mental home, pagodas… The stations and water purifiers are distributed free of cost to schools/institutions. Sustainability Investment Promotion and Development Joint Stock Company (SIPCO) shall finance the implementation of the project in full.

name: Global Safe Drinking Water for Schools in Viet Nam
developer: Sustainability Investment Promotion and Development Joint Stock Company
description:
The proposed group projects aim to improve the quality of drinking water by promoting water filtration systems that do not emit greenhouse gases (GHG). The projects will provide safe drinking water by water purifiers and stations to schools and institutions throughout Viet Nam. In this grouped project, schools include Kindergartens, nurseries, primary schools, secondary schools, high schools. Institutions include community home, home for disabled, orphanage, nursing home, mental home. Sustainability Investment Promotion and Development Joint Stock Company (SIPCO) shall finance the implementation of the project in full.
The project group includes two main technologies: ceramic water purifier and the safe drinking water treatment station. Both technologies offer odor removal and 99.999% sterilization efficiency, significantly reducing the accumulation and growth of harmful bacteria. The distribution of purifiers and stations will be tailored to the number of users at each school or institution. The use of these purifiers and stations also minimizes the need for wood fuel and fossil fuel for boiling water, thereby reducing greenhouse gas emissions.
The grouped project activity will minimize the use of non-renewable biomass and fossil fuel utilized for boiling water as a means purification to achieve safe drinking water quality in the absence of this project activity. This directly leads to reduced greenhouse gas emissions. Furthermore, it can be helpful to user’s health.

name: Agroforestry Corridors for Multi Cropping Systems in Brazil
project_type: Agriculture Forestry and Other Land Use
description:
The project aims to rehabilitate the local forest ecosystem and introduce agroforestry methods to communities within watersheds and along riverbanks across a 1.7 million hectare expanse spanning São Paulo, Rio de Janeiro, and Maranhão. It plans to rejuvenate over 6,000 hectares through reforestation and will incorporate agroforestry near local farms, targeting pasturelands, deteriorated areas, and mono-crop fields. The project's core goal is to restore deforested and degraded lands, enhancing farmers' ability to sustainably produce food and generate income. 

Through agroforestry, the project offers alternative livelihoods, encouraging farmers to shift from traditional to sustainable land management practices. Agroforestry systems of coffee and cocoa will be implemented in partnership with local farmers in pastureland, degraded land, and monocultures, with capacity-building initiatives and training programs planned as part of the project.

name: Farm Resilience and Regeneration in France
project_type: Agriculture Forestry and Other Land Use
description:
The grouped project “Farm Resilience and Regeneration in France” is developed by ReGeneration S.a.s. and aims to empower and derisk farmers in their transition to regenerative agriculture, enabled by individualized regenerative agronomic support and financial support.
The geographic zone is mainland France except for mountainous areas. The project accompanies farm types of arable farming, livestock farming, as well as mixed crop-livestock farming.
The project follows the VM0042 v2.0 Methodology for improved Agriculture and Land Management (ALM), and applies Approach 1: Measure and Model.
This project aims to create resilient farms by regenerating and reviving the ecosystem and the soil.
The resulting adoption of regenerative practices will generate climate benefits by sequestering carbon into the soil. It is conservatively anticipated that this would equate to annual emission removals (ERs) averaging 476,000 tCO2e/year. The project aims to accompany 6,000 farms in total over 20 years, putting 600,000 ha on a regenerative transition.
The program’s successful implementation is expected to bring about outcomes contributing to a whole set of SDGs, tracked by pre-defined indicators. Program participation improves access to knowledge and opportunities for small-scale and family farmers, implementation of resilient agricultural practices, and improved seed diversity (SDG 2), it enhances gender inclusion (SDG 5), increases water-use efficiency, and reduces water pollution from agricultural inputs (SDG 6), improves resource efficiency (SDG 8), reduces the release of chemicals to water, air, and soil (SDG 12), contributes to GHG emission reductions and fosters climate resilience and adaptive capacity (SDG 13), restores degraded land and soil and improves farm biodiversity (SDG 15), and fosters communication and partnerships between the industry, the population and the often isolated and misunderstood farming population (SDG 17).

name: Bamboo King Vina Biochar Project
developer: Bamboo King Vina Joint Stock Company
description:
The Bamboo King Vina Biochar Project aims to address the substantial waste generated from bamboo and wood processing at the Bamboo King Vina (BKV) factory in Lang Chanh district, Thanh Hoa province, Vietnam. The factory, with a daily processing capacity of 1,500 tons, generates approximately 800-900 tons of waste per day. To mitigate this environmental impact, the project will install and operate six biochar production facilities using pyrolysis technology. This process converts bamboo and wood waste into biochar, a carbon-rich material.
The produced biochar will be applied directly to soil or used indirectly in agricultural land through animal feed, livestock bedding, sludge management, composting, or anaerobic digestion. The project's objectives include reducing bamboo waste sent to landfills or left to decay, which contributes to greenhouse gas emissions. Utilizing biochar in soil management aims to enhance agricultural land, promote carbon-rich ecosystems, improve crop yields, and boost food security. Additionally, it seeks to foster healthier communities and economic prosperity for local at-risk populations.

name: OYU - Powering Kenyan SMEs with Clean Energy
description: The grouped project activity comprises solar power plants on both rooftops and ground-mounted systems, empowering small and medium enterprises across Kenya to generate clean energy for captive use. This will significantly reduce reliance on Kenyan national grid and contribute to reduction of greenhouse gas emissions. The project activity provides clean electricity through solar power plants displacing consumption of electricity that would have been supplied by National grid of Kenya in the absence of the project activity.

name: Grouped Projects for Safe Water Program in Uganda
description: The intention of the grouped project involves the installation of low greenhouse gas emitting water purification systems i.e., chlorine dispensers, to provide clean drinking water to low income households/communities in Uganda. For this reason, this proposed grouped project aims at reducing the non-renewable woody biomass consumption from traditional stove users by installing chlorine dispensers at communal water points.

name: Grouped Projects for Safe Water Program in Malawi
description: The intention of the grouped project involves the installation of low greenhouse gas emitting water purification systems i.e., chlorine dispensers, to provide clean drinking water to low income households/communities in Malawi. For this reason, this proposed grouped project aims at reducing the non-renewable woody biomass consumption from traditional stove users by installing chlorine dispensers at communal water points.

name: TERAKA MADAGASCAR: SMALLHOLDER TREE PLANTING PROGRAM
project_type: Agriculture Forestry and Other Land Use
description:
The TERAKA program is a comprehensive reforestation and sustainable development initiative in Madagascar, led by subsistence farmers. Inspired by the successful TIST model in East Africa, farmers plant and own trees on their land, receiving training from TERAKA and 70% of carbon benefits. Small Groups of farmers are empowered to combat deforestation, poverty, and drought. By integrating sustainable practices with carbon sequestration, the program supports farmers in reforestation and biodiversity preservation, creating a 'virtual' cash crop from carbon credits. 
Operating in central and eastern Madagascar, TERAKA aims to plant trees across 6,000 hectares within the initial eight years. This initial phase is expected to remove approximately 1,971,413 tonnes of greenhouse gases over 40 years, while restoring degraded land, improving the livelihoods and well-being of local communities, fostering sustainable employment, and promoting biodiversity.

name: FX Group Biomass to Energy Project
description: The proposed project activity concerns a greenfield biomass to energy power plant at the FX Group Lothair facility, which is situated in the Mpumalanga province of South Africa. The Project will source biomass from local sawmills and biomass wastes for the generation of electricity in a power-only plant. The woody biomass will be fed into a biomass boiler to create super-heated high-pressure steam. The steam is used to spin a 4.5MW power output steam turbine and electrical generator. The renewable energy produced by the plant will displace the grid electricity, which would have been used to power the industrial facility in the absence of the biomass power plant. Electricity on the South African National grid is largely generated by the state-owned entity Eskom and is highly carbon-intensive due to the reliance on fossil-fuels such as coal and diesel.

name: Yunnan Zhenxiong Zhujiawan CMM Power Generation Project
developer: Zhenxiong Yonder New Energy Development Co., Ltd
description:
The project is located in Banqiao Village, Chishuiyuan Town, Zhenxiong County, Shaotong City, Yunnan Province, P.R.China. The project owner is Zhenxiong Yonder New Energy Development Co., Ltd.
The purpose of the Project is to utilize the extracted CMM with low concentration methane concentration to produce electricity. No coal bed methane (CBM) or ventilation air methane (VAM) utilization is involved. It is expected that 13.0392 million Nm3 of methane annually will be destroyed to generate electricity. According to Feasibility Study Report (FSR) of the project, 14 sets of CMM power generators will be installed with a total installed capacity of 9.8 MW (14*700 kW).
After the full operation of the project, the expected annual exported electricity is 49,476 MWh, which is supplied to the coal mine through the electricity distribution network in Zhujiawan coal mine and to China Southern Power Grid (CSPG) if there is any electricity surplus, thus displace equivalent amount of electricity that would be supplied by CSPG dominated by fossil fuel-fired power plants. 
 It is estimated that in the 10 years crediting period of the project (from 13-May-2023 to 12-May-2033), the expected average annual GHG emission reduction will be 243,241 tCO2e, with the total emission reduction of 2,432,410 tCO2e.

name: Livelihood improvement by Shashwat agroforestry plantation through carbon Finance in Maharashtra
project_type: Agriculture Forestry and Other Land Use
description: Agroforestry can help in conservation and rehabilitation of the ecosystem along with providing better livelihood opportunities to the rural community. The proposed VCS agroforestry project, titled Livelihood improvement by Shashwat agroforestry plantation through carbon Finance in Maharashtra (also referred to as Palghar Agroforestry project) operates in Palghar district, situated in the western line of Maharashtra, India. Currently, the project spans eight blocks of Palghar District namely Dahanu, Jawahar, Mokhada, Palghar, Talasari, Vasai, Vikramgad and Wada, and have potential to expand in other districts of Maharashtra

name: Zhiduo Sustainable Grassland Management Project
developer: Hangzhou Chaoteng Energy Technology Co., Ltd
project_type: Agriculture Forestry and Other Land Use
description: Zhiduo Grassland Sustainable Management Project  is located in Zhiduo County, Yushu Tibetan Autonomous Prefecture, Qinghai Province, China, The project’s aim is to restore the local degraded grassland by adopting a variety of measures including grass planting, fertilization, fence installation, and etc., and protect the grassland ecosystem from further degradation by sustainable grazing management. Finally the project will increase carbon sequestration by reversing grassland degradation, and will also contribute to local development ,preserve cultural traditions, and increase ecosystem biodiversity.

name: Pingnan MSW Incineration and Power Generation
developer: BEWG Environmental Protection Guangxi Pingnan Co., Ltd.
project_type: Energy industries (renewable/non-renewable sources); Waste handling and disposal
description:
Pingnan municipal solid waste (hereafter referred to as “MSW”) incineration and power generation project (hereafter referred to as “the project”) is located in Shangdu Town, Pingnan County, Guangxi Zhuang Autonomous Region, China, with geographic location of 110.356977°E and 23.483333°N. The Project is invested, constructed and operated by BEWG Environmental Protection Guangxi Pingnan Co., Ltd.
The combustion system is composed of one 600t/d mechanical grate incinerator, matched with one set of 12MW steam turbine generator. The project will treat 219,000 tons of MSW every year. The MSW combustion line will work over 8,000 hours every year. The project is expected to generate 88,010 MWh electricity, of which 74,810 MWh will be exported to the China Southern Power Grid (hereinafter referred to as CSPG). When turbine generator is repaired, it may involve in purchased electricity from CSPG. The implementation of the project meets the requirement of local MSW harmless treatment, and significantly improve local environment. Also, the project could reduce GHG emission that would occur in baseline scenarios such as power generating by fossil fuel fired plants and MSW treatment.
Before the implementation of the project, the local MSW was usually disposed of at nearby landfill, where no landfill gas capturing system erected and the landfill gases are released to atmosphere directly. In the meanwhile, by utilizing the waste heat from the combustion of MSW, the boilers can transfer steam to generate electricity power to replace the electricity that would be generated by fossil- fuel fired power plants. 
The total GHG emission reduction is expected to be 780,570 tCO2e and the average annual emission reduction is   111,570 tCO2e in a period of 7 years (from 7/7/2022 to 6/7/2029 both included).

name: Therm- Reducing Food Loss and Waste
description: The project seeks to reduce greenhouse gas emissions by keeping food in the human food chain. This is a group project that spans over locations in AL, FL, GA, NC, SC, TN, and VA. This project utilizes food donation programs to achieve emission reductions from diverting food from a food loss and waste (FLW) destination in conformance to the VM0046 Methodology for Reducing Food Loss and Waste, v1.0.

name: KA'A PYAHU
project_type: Agriculture Forestry and Other Land Use
description:
The KA’A PYAHU Project is located in Maranhão, Brazil, within the Indigenous Territory of the Guajajara ethnicity, one of the country's most populous. It aims to benefit approximately 13,000 indigenous individuals. Named after the Tupi-Guarani words meaning 'New Forest,' the Ka’a Pyahu project represents 'a new care for nature' for the community. The project area is managed by local communities in the territories of Cana Brava, Rodeador, Lagoa Comprida, and Urucu Juruá, organized around the CONSELHO SUPREMO association since 2019.

Through the establishment of the association and organizational efforts, the community has achieved significant milestones in protecting their territories. Legal actions against damages caused by projects from companies have resulted in decisions favoring the community, leading to reduced deforestation and compensation for previous degradation.

The community's history of organization and strengthened internal governance has empowered them to safeguard the forests in their territories. Additionally, they have gained familiarity with the REDD+ initiative and the carbon market through this process.
The KA’A PYAHU PROJECT aims to ensure better conditions for environmental conservation and sustainable use of forests, ultimately enhancing the quality of life for local communities, particularly in terms of clean water, sanitation, and education.

name: Tond Tenga
project_type: Agriculture Forestry and Other Land Use
description:
Tree Aid (TA) is an international development non-governmental organisation (INGO) that focuses on working with people in the Sahel region of Africa to tackle poverty and the effects of climate change by growing trees, improving people's incomes, and restoring and protecting land. It is a registered charity in the UK. TA is partnering with Earthshot Labs PBC (Earthshot) and Capricorn Investment Group LLC (Capricorn) to restore degraded landscapes in Burkina Faso through enrichment planting and agroforestry activities.
TA has partnered with local communities to identify 37 sites of degraded woodland and shrublands located in 18 communes and 4 regions with the potential to become new forest sites through enrichment planting. These sites have been affected by deforestation and decades of unsustainable agricultural activity, leading to soil degradation that has prevented further agricultural activity. This has resulted in desertification and the loss of access to culturally relevant non-timber forest products (NTFPs) that are extremely significant in socio-economic terms. Thus, the project identified activities in enrichment planting and agroforestry to restore native forests and increase access to NFTPs. 
Through enrichment planting, the project will restore native tree species with high importance to the biodiversity of the area, high restoration potential and some NTFP uses. In total 12,000 ha will be targeted across these 37 forest sites. In total just over 142,500 trees will be targeted on farmland in and around the 37 forest sites.
The project is estimated to remove 3.7 million tCO2e during the project lifetime, with estimated annual GHG emission removals of 92,576.9 tCO2e.

name: Safe Water Supply in Zambia
description: The project tackles the critical water crisis by strategically deploying deep-well drilling to tap into natural underground aquifers. This ensures a long-term, sustainable solution for clean water access. Our robust disinfection and distribution system guarantees safe drinking water at the tap. The benefits extend further: eliminating the need to use non-renewable biomass (or fossil fuels) for boiling water fosters environmental sustainability by curbing deforestation and greenhouse gas emissions. Additionally, the project aims to contribute to the Sustainable Development Goals (SDGs) by fostering well-being, increasing local employment, promoting gender equality, reducing water collection time, and increasing opportunities for education, income generation, and healthier lifestyles.

name: CTR Metropolitana Landfill Gas
description:
The proposed project activity has the objective to capture, flare and generate electricity through the use of landfill gas (LFG)  produced in anaerobic conditions into the landfill called “CTR Metropolitana Landfill” (hereinafter referred to as “CTR Metropolitana Landfill”) located in the city of Pilar in the state of Alagoas, Brazil. The landfill started the operation on May 2015, receiving solid waste (type Class II-A Inert and Class II-B Non-inert) .
The project activity results in greenhouse gas (GHG) emission reduction from the CTR Metropolitana landfill through two ways:

i.	Burning CH4 in flares and/or group generators;
ii.     The amount of electricity generated in the project activity is dispatched to the Brazilian Interconnected Electrical System (SIN), avoiding the dispatch of an equal amount of energy produced by fossil-fuelled thermal plants to that grid. The initiative avoids CO2 emissions and contributes to the regional and national sustainable development.

The project activity aims to capture and to flare the LFG and to generate electricity through the implementation of a power generation plant using LFG. The generation installed capacity during the first crediting period will be equal to 3.71 MW.

The project constructed an efficient capture, collection and flaring system to burn CH4 (a greenhouse gas), and this reduced odours and adverse environmental impacts. Moreover, it installs generators that combusts the LFG to produce electricity, using part of the electricity for self-consumption and the other part is exported to the grid. The flares are kept in operation due to LFG excess, periods when electricity is not be produced or other operational considerations. The LFG power plant has 3.71 MW installed capacity.

name: Liza Protect Forest
project_type: Agriculture Forestry and Other Land Use

name: ARR REWILDING HUB IN GRAN CHACO ARGENTINA
project_type: Agriculture Forestry and Other Land Use
description:
The ARR Rewilding Hub spearheaded and fully owned by Forest Defense AG in northeastern Las Lajitas, Salta Province, Argentina, is set to transform 18,450 hectares into a vibrant conservation area. Using the latest methodology VM0047, this initiative is the largest and most comprehensive ecological restoration project in the region. Previously utilized for agriculture and livestock, the land will be reforested with native species to reestablish typical native forest ecosystems of the semi-arid Chaco region. This project is dedicated to long-term conservation, with plans to maintain its sanctuary status beyond the initial 40-year accreditation period.

This pioneering effort is uniquely positioned at the agricultural and cattle production frontier, set to be a game changer for the region. It promises significant ecological balance and serves as a sustainable model for similar transitions towards environmentally friendly practices across the region. The strategic location enables a substantial multiplier effect, inspiring broader shifts towards sustainability and biodiversity preservation.

Collaborations with The Nature Conservancy (TNC), the National Institute of Agricultural Technology (INTA), and universities ensure a multi-faceted approach, combining traditional practices with scientific research. As a quality-driven project, it aims to create a sustainable ecosystem that supports biodiversity and local communities, setting a new standard for conservation efforts in Argentina.

As the most extensive and quality-driven project in the region, the ARR Rewilding Hub sets a new standard for ecological restoration in Argentina, aiming to create a sustainable and resilient ecosystem that supports both biodiversity and the local community.

name: Water Purification System for Safe Drinking Water  (SDW) in Cambodia
description: The ‘Water Purification System for Safe Drinking Water (SDW) in Cambodia’ (hereinafter referred to as ‘the Project’) aims to expand pipelines connected to low greenhouse gas (GHG) emitting water treatment facilities. The goal is to provide clean drinking water to communities that previously lacked access to a public distribution network for SDW within the host country, the Kingdom of Cambodia. This is achieved through a network of high-density polyethylene (HDPE) pipelines that connect to water purification facilities equipped with coagulant chemicals, sand filters, disinfectant chemicals, and other substances. The Project serves as an open platform for various water treatment technologies, which are eligible under the methodology AMS-III.AV (Version 08.0).

name: Aeco Peatland Restoration Latvia #1
project_type: Agriculture Forestry and Other Land Use
description: The project restores a 438 hectares drained grassland fen peatland in Eastern Latvia.

name: Xinghua Improved Agriculture Land Management Project
project_type: Agriculture Forestry and Other Land Use
description:
Xinghua City Improved Agriculture Land Management Project is developed by Meicun  Atmosphere Environmental Technology (Chongqing) Co, Ltd. It aims to- raise farmers' awareness of the benefits of sustainable agriculture and how to change agricultural practices to help in climate change mitigation and adaptation. The project will assist farmers to overcome barriers that prevent the adoption of improved agricultural land management practices and provide technical assistance where needed. The objectives of the project are to reduce emissions from agricultural practices and increase soil carbon storage. In order to achieve these objectives, a package of practices including improved residue management that change the pre-existing agricultural management activities will be carried-out.

The project activity is located in Xinghua City, which is a county-level city under the administration of Taizhou City in Jiangsu Province, China. The area of the project activity is 26673 ha, including farmland spreading over 17 towns. Prior to the start of the implementation of the project, there was no similar activities of carbon sequestration, GHG removals or net reduction. The baseline scenario is the continuation of pre-project agricultural land management practices including conventional tillage and straw not returned to fields, which are common agricultural practices in the project area. Over the 20 years of the first crediting period, the project will generate an estimated annual average removal and reduction of 96,236 tCO2e. and 1,924,720 tCO2e in total 20 years.

Besides climate change mitigation, the project will also result in a lot of benefits in various social and environmental aspects, such as Enhance soil quality, Reduce pollution and protect the local ecological environment, Develop sustainable local agriculture, Provide training and on-site demonstration activities on convention tillage.

name: Sakahk Papakititamo (Forest Breathes)
project_type: Agriculture Forestry and Other Land Use
description:
Project Sakahk Papakititamo (Forest Breathes) is an Indigenous-owned forest carbon project that creates net climate benefits through improved forest management of lands located in northeastern Saskatchewan, Canada. Project Sakahk Papakititamo (Forest Breathes) is a grouped project which will be comprised of individual project instances brought forward by Peter Ballantyne Cree Nation (PBCN) communities. The collection of PBCN project instances will make up the grouped project as a whole. This project uses the Verified Carbon Standard (VCS) VM0034 Canadian Forest Carbon Offset Methodology, V 2.0 and will apply the Climate, Community & Biodiversity (CCB) Standard. 

Under CCB this project will also emphasize the biodiversity and the community benefits of protecting native forests. This project will support and strengthen traditional, cultural, and heritage values for the PBCN members within and external to the project area. This project ensures that future generations will thrive thanks to the sustainable practices, and that Indigenous ways of knowing are being understood and valued. As a whole, this project strives to advance Reconciliation.

Under Improved Forest Management (IFM) – Logged to Protected Forest (LtPF), projects utilize practices that reduce net greenhouse gas (GHG) emissions by permanently converting logged forests to protected forests. It includes forest health monitoring, and low levels of timber harvest may be required for forest health maintenance or improved forest productivity. This project’s activity will switch from a baseline of commercial clearcut harvesting to protected forest, with permissible harvesting of trees to advance conservation purposes (e.g., the removal of diseased trees) and improve forest growth and stocking density to accelerate the sequestration of additional carbon over time. As such, the PBCN project will result in significant GHG emission reductions and additional carbon sequestration.

name: ARC Restaura Azuero
project_type: Agriculture Forestry and Other Land Use
description: Azuero Reforestación Colectiva (ARC) is implementing a grouped restoration project in the Azuero Peninsula of Panama. Together with cattle ranchers and the local communities, the project is expected to plant native and native-adapted species on approximately 10,000 hectares that will contribute to the removal of greenhouse gasses (GHG) while restoring the land, enhancing the well-being of local communities, fostering sustainable job prospects, and promoting biodiversity.

name: EASY BREATHE INDIA SMART COOKSTOVE PROGRAM
description:
Household air pollution is a global crisis and India is not unaffected by the problem. There is significant dependence on 3-stone stoves (Chullah) or traditional pot support for cooking in rural households in the country. Household pollution can cause diseases and women are particularly affected due to their direct exposure to cooking fires and involvement in daily cooking. Combustion of the non-renewable fuels and release of greenhouse gas emissions in the environment adds to global warming problem. 

The proposed project will be addressing this problem by providing access to Improved Cooking Solutions (ICS) in the form of energy efficient cookstoves. This is a voluntary initiative by EVI Green Markets Pte. Ltd. (Project Proponent or PP). PP will be collaborating with local implementation partners to provide ICS for marginalized households living in rural areas of the host country.

name: ETHIOPIA AGROFORESTRY PROJECT ON SMALL-SCALE COFFEE PARCELS
project_type: Agriculture Forestry and Other Land Use
description:
At present, this project is located within the area served by the Sidama Coffee Farmers’ Cooperative Union (SCFCU) in the Sidama region of Ethiopia and was started with the Bokasso Cooperative. Since then, the project area has expanded to include 11 different cooperatives as of February 2024. The project may continue to expand to other similar coffee-growing regions of Ethiopia as it grows. The project objectives include:

•	Implementing Afforestation, Reforestation, and Revegetation (ARR) interventions, including reforestation of degraded land and agroforestry on smallholder producer coffee farms to mitigate the impacts of climate change and develop new, diverse income streams for producers; and
•	Improving yield and quality of coffee, stabilizing the productivity on enrolled farms and ensuring high taste and aroma quality.

This project will implement reforestation interventions on degraded land and agroforestry interventions on the coffee plantations of smallholder producers to generate climate, nature, and socioeconomic benefits. The majority of the greenhouse gas benefits associated with the project will come from the carbon dioxide removed by the trees planted and by the carbon sequestered within the soil as a result of improved agricultural practices by coffee farmers.

name: Açaí REDD+ Project
project_type: Agriculture Forestry and Other Land Use
description:
The Açaí REDD+ project aims to promote forest conservation and reduce potential greenhouse gas (GHG) emissions from unplanned deforestation and forest degradation.The property where the project is located covers a continuous area of 16,229.09 ha of Amazon Forest, of which 15,715.82 ha are destined for Avoiding Unplanned Deforestation (AUD).
The Açaí REDD+ project is located in the municipality of Envira, in the state of Amazonas (39,90% of the project area), and in the municipality of Feijó, in the state of Acre (60,10% of the project area). 
The project will conserves 15,715.82 hectares of Amazon rainforest and its biodiversity through the surveillance of the project area by land and river performed by outsourced people and companies, monitoring of forest fires, annual monitoring of forest cover through forest inventories and satellite images, and periodic monitoring of endangered species.

name: Tech-Bank Swine Manure Composting Project in Jiangsu Province
project_type: Livestock, enteric fermentation, and manure management; Waste handling and disposal
description: Tech-Bank Swine Manure Composting Project in Jiangsu Province (hereafter referred to as the project) introduces 2 sets of aerobic composting systems to treat the swine manure from Huai’an Huanghuatang swine farm and Yangzhou Huangcheng swine farm in Jiangsu Province, China, which are owned by Tech-Bank Food Co., Ltd. Each subsidiary swine farm will install one aerobic composting system, and the manure is treated on site. The purpose of the project activity is to avoid methane emissions through controlled aerobic treatment by composting of swine manure.

name: Yangquan Guzhuang 8MW CMM Power Generation Project
project_type: Energy industries (renewable/non-renewable sources); Fugitive emissions from fuels (solid, oil and gas); Mining/mineral production
description:
Yangquan Guzhuang 8MW CMM Power Generation Project is located at the former site of Guzhuang Coal Mine Cement Plant in Yangquan, Shanxi Province. The Project utilizes coal mine methane (CMM) with a methane concentration of 16% to generate electricity, and the electricity generated is fed into the North China Power Grid for the self-consumption of the Guzhuang Coal Mine, while the heat output is recovered by a waste heat hot water boiler, replacing the original coal-fired boiler for heating in the mine area. The Project Owner is Yangquan Zhonglian Energy Technology Co.
The purpose of this project is to reduce greenhouse gas emissions through the combustion of methane in the coal mine gas during the power generation process. No coal bed methane (CBM) or ventilation air methane (VAM) utilization is involved. The total installed capacity of the project is designed as 8MW, with eight 1000kW gas-fired internal combustion generator sets, which utilize coal mine gas with a concentration of less than 30% to generate electricity, and utilize the waste heat hot water boiler to recover the flue gas waste heat at the tail end of the units. After running at full load, the project can consume 1,262.88*104Nm3 of pure gas per year, with an estimated annual power generation of 4800*104kWh, which will be used for the mine's self consumption through integration into the North China Power Grid, and 5.184*104GJ of residual heat per year, which will be supplied to the outside world for the heating of the buildings on the site. However, to be conservative, emission reductions will not be claimed for waste heat recovery.
During the renewable 7-year crediting period(28-Oct-2022 to 27-Oct-2029, both days included), the total GHG emission reduction of the project can reach 1,748,817 tCO2e, with an average annual emission reduction of 249,831tCO2e.

name: EARTH MAA LLC- BAMBOO, CASHEWNUT AND MANGO PLANTATIONS FOR FARMERS ECONOMIC UPGRADE
project_type: Agriculture Forestry and Other Land Use
description:
The Afforestation, Reforestation, and Revegetation (ARR) project is an ambitious initiative aimed at combating climate change, restoring biodiversity, and supporting sustainable development through largescale tree planting and ecosystem restoration efforts. The aim of the project is to address global climate change through promoting native forestry trees, specifically, bamboo, cashew nut and mango plantations in the project area. Bamboo, Cashew nut and Mango have a natural capacity to absorb CO2. The Bamboo has growth from 1.0 to1.2 meters per day and gain mature status within 2.5 to 3 years. All three plants; i.e. Bamboo, Cashew nut and Mango help in preventing soil erosion and restoring degraded areas caused by deforestation or natural disasters which serve various environmental benefits and have the potential impact to the fight against climate change.

The project activity has the following objectives: 

1. The activity encourages plantation of bamboo, cashew nut and mango trees as all these three contribute to carbon sequestration by absorbing carbon dioxide (CO2) from the atmosphere
during the process of photosynthesis. This not only helps mitigate the effects of climate change but also improves air quality. Mature Bamboo, Mango and Cashew trees are particularly effective
in this regard, storing significant amounts of carbon in their biomass over their lifespan, which can extend up to 50 years or more.

2. By engaging local communities, such as landowners and their families especially tribal women in plantation, this project not only helps reduce greenhouse gas emissions but also provides a
sustainable source of income and livelihood for farmer communities. 

3. The project provides a sustainable source of timber through bamboo, cashew nut and mango. Bamboo a type of grass has the special ability to keep absorbing carbon even after selective
harvesting. This=means that carbon sequestration continues, making it an effective and long lasting solution.

name: Heilongjiang Zhaoyuan Improved Agricultural Land Management Project
developer: Zhaoyuan Qingyuan Agricultural Development Group Co., Ltd.
project_type: Agriculture Forestry and Other Land Use
description:
Heilongjiang Zhaoyuan Improved Agricultural Land Management Project (hereinafter referred to as “the project”) is located in Zhaoyuan County, Daqing City, Heilongjiang Province, China. The purpose of the project is to adopt improved agricultural land management practices to prevent the severe soil degradation caused by pre-existing conventional tillage in local crop land.
The improved agricultural land management practices of the project focus on no-tillage on fields evenly mulched with crushed straw for two or three years, followed by plowing or subsoiling once and continued no-tillage for another two or three years. No-tillage can effectively reduce the loosening of the surface soil layer and soil disturbance, reduce the loss of water and nutrients in the soil, ensure the retention of organic matter in the soil, reduce the degree of compaction of the tillage equipment on the tillage soil layer, and preserve appropriate space for the growth of crops, which is convenient for ventilation and keeps the soil with good water storage capacity. The application of no-tillage sowing has solved the problem of sand blowing in bare farmland to a certain extent and played a role in windbreak and sand fixation. No-tillage can maximize the protective effect of straw mulching on soil.  
The project plans to implement improved agricultural land management practices in 87,479 ha corn field in the first crediting period to increase soil organic carbon (SOC). The project proponent not only introduced more efficient and appropriate tillage method with Zhaoyuan Agriculture and Rural Affairs Bureau (ZARAB) to the farmers, but also provide technical training and support to the farmers.

name: East Africa Soil and Biodiversity improvement project
project_type: Agriculture Forestry and Other Land Use
description:
East Africa Soil and Biodiversity improvement project in Eastern Africa is a voluntary carbon project that implements Agricultural Land Management (ALM) practices developed and owned by eAgronom. This initiative is currently underway in Rwanda, Kenya, and Tanzania, with the potential for further expansion into neighbouring countries. It follows Verra's VM0042 methodology for Improved Agricultural Land Management, version 2.0, referred to as VM0042, the project is dedicated to enhancing soil organic carbon levels within annual cropping systems.
The project aims to spread adoption of regenerative agricultural practices, ultimately leading to increased carbon sequestration. By doing so, it seeks to improve soil health and deliver significant benefits to farmers. Simultaneously, the project is driven to sequester greenhouse gas (GHG) emissions.
The Regenerative Agriculture Project in Eastern Africa focuses on elevating soil health, benefiting farmers, and mitigating greenhouse gas emissions and build agricultural resilience. By initiating positive changes in East Africa and contemplating expansion, the project holds the potential to become a catalyst for transformative practices in the broader region.

name: ARAGUAIA REDD+ BOCALON PROJECT
developer: Nova-Agri Infra-Estrutura De Armazenagem E Escoamento Agricola S.A.A.
project_type: Agriculture Forestry and Other Land Use
description:
NOVAAGRI, the proponent and developer of the present project, is a company founded in 2008 as a visionary and innovative player in the Agribusiness sector. We drive a strict control under the process of farmers' prospection and selection, adopting internal criteria for analysis and approval of the growing/production areas, such as compliance with the national forestry legislation and other socio-environmental regulations related to combating deforestation, work conditions and conservation of sensitive areas and indigenous lands. This control is carried out through geo-monitoring systems, by using satellite images, applied to 100% of the commercial contracts carried out at NovaAgri.

Although the development of Carbon Credits projects is not a main service of NovaAgri’s portfolio, neither intend to make it a core source of revenue to the company, these projects are totally strategic and aligned to the Group´s beliefs and philosophy, which counts on challenging targets of carbon reduction for the medium and long term – the carbon credit projects are vital to orientate the company into the carbon neutrality path, encouraging good actions among its value chain players.

The ARAGUAIA REDD+ BOCALON PROJECT is taken in Santa Terezinha, a municipality from the Mato Grosso State in Brazil. The property’s is composed by an area of 24,100 hectares in total, and its project area composes an area of 13,926 hectares of native forest. The project expects to avoid net emissions of 1,683,481.14 tCO2e, which means an average of 28,058 tCO2e per year and 10,012 hectares preserved during a horizon of 60 years, by using high level technology of satellites and geomonitoring system.  Regarding social responsability, every carbon project developed and managed by NovaAgri intends to ensure a share of the project’s financial returns to implement social actions within the local communities located in the surroundings of the project area.
