abusedue_id: Marudi Indigenous communities oppose Samling’s carbon project in Sarawak, Malaysia

name: URSTAMM GROUPED PROJECT IFM SWITZERLAND & PILOT PROJECT KELLERAMT
project_type: Agriculture Forestry and Other Land Use
description:
The Urstamm project is an Improved Forest Management (IFM) project in Switzerland. It is a grouped project. The scope of the project is set to be the entire Swiss forest territory since landowners from the whole country are invited to join the project. The registration period for landowners is organized in cohorts. The pilot project “Kelleramt” is based in the Central Plateau, or “Mittelland” of Switzerland near Zurich.

The project will apply selective logging to the parcels in accordance with the methodology VM0012 Improved Forest Management in temperate and boreal forests. The project will increase the carbon inventory by selective logging. The effectiveness and importance of this method has been confirmed by latest research and it will enable to build a climate anti-fragile or at least resilient forest population that becomes a carbon sink rather than a source.

The management plan is in accordance with the forest goals of the Swiss Confederation in terms of climate change mitigation and increased resilience of the forest to climate change. Indeed, it advises the forest managers to (i) increase biodiversity, (ii) increase structural diversity, (iii) increase genetic diversity, (iv) increase individual tree resistance to stress and (v) decrease the target Diameter at Breast Height (DBH). Selective logging allows the forest manager to actively control the development of the forest and therefore hinder the effect of climate change of the forest carbon sink. For example, this method allows the forest manager to increase light availability on the floor and promote light demanding and climate change resilient species. Also, the project is looking to increase the frequency of logging activities on each parcel in accordance with point (v) of the Swiss government and its forest strategy. 

To monitor the implementation of the sustainable forest management and provide precise information monitoring through remote sensing will be carried out (dMRV).

name: Project Terre Boost: Biochar for a Better Tomorrow
description:
India's agricultural sector faces pressing environmental challenges, notably due to conventional waste disposal methods such as open field burning and unmanaged biomass decay. These practices contribute significantly to greenhouse gas emissions and broader environmental degradation. Addressing this, Together for Restoration (a program by SRCNatura Sure Pvt. Ltd.) introduces Project Terre Boost, an initiative aimed at transforming agricultural residues into biochar for soil enhancement across seven Indian states—Assam, Nagaland, Rajasthan, Maharashtra, Madhya Pradesh, Chhattisgarh, and Jharkhand. 
 
Project Terre Boost employs flame curtain pyrolysis technology in steel-shielded soil pits to convert agricultural waste into biochar. This biochar, mixed with manure and applied deep into the soil, promises a sustainable solution to waste management in agriculture. The project includes an initial cohort of 5,000 farmers (biochar producers). Environmental impacts of Project Terre Boost are substantial, with an estimated annual removal of 116,961 tons of CO2 equivalent (tCO2e), totalling 818,727 tCO2e over a seven-year crediting period. Moreover, the advantages of Project Terre Boost transcend environmental considerations, creating a dual advantage by significantly elevating the welfare of marginalised local farming communities.

name: Energy Efficiency Measures Across Commercial Buildings in India by SJPL 001
description: The Project Proponent, Smart Joules Private Limited, identified various energy saving opportunities and provided EPC services to achieve energy savings across identified Facilities of Apollo Hospitals in India. The Energy Savings are achieved through a combination of various measures including System Design Optimization, Installation of Energy Efficient Equipment and Operational Optimization.

name: BURKINA FASO AGRICULTURAL CARBON PROJECT (BUFACAP)
project_type: Agriculture Forestry and Other Land Use
description:
BUFACAP is a national program that contributes to climate mitigation and adaptation efforts set out in the country’s Nationally Determined Contribution (NDC) in the Agriculture, Forestry and Other Land Use (AFOLU) sector. It promotes sustainable agricultural land management on smallholder landholdings and is implemented across all administrative regions in the country, which fall within the Sudanian and Sudano-Sahelian Agro-Ecological Zones (AEZs). The main objectives are to sustainably increase smallholders’ agricultural productivity, food security, income, and welfare, build resilience /adaptation of the agrarian landscapes to climate change, reduce land degradation, and enhance tree/forest cover in line both the National Strategy for Soil Restoration, Conservation and Reclamation in Burkina Faso (SNRCRS) 2020-2024 and the National REDD+ agenda. The improved agricultural land management (IALM) practices promoted include compost/manure application, residue management (mulching), a menu of agroforestry, natural regeneration of trees, a menu of soil and water conservation practices, e.g., erosion control structures, a menu of integrated livestock management, e.g., forage crops, livestock housing, biogas digesters, etc., and a menu of agronomic practices, e.g., mixed cropping, intercropping, crop rotation, etc.  
The BUFACAP is a grouped project as defined in the VCS Standard version 4.5, i.e., “projects structured to allow the expansion of a project activity subsequent to project validation”.  
The project is using a partnership approach with the technical lead being the REDD+ Permanent Secretariat. The activities are expected to result in increased and sustainable agricultural production, tree/forest conservation and land restoration. GHG emission reductions will be generated through increased carbon storage in tree biomass and in soils within the agricultural landscapes. VM0042 will be used to account, monitor, and quantify the project’s GHG emission reductions.

name: Rio Muru REDD+ Project
project_type: Agriculture Forestry and Other Land Use
description: The Rio Muru REDD+ Project is a partnership between WayCarbon Soluções Ambientais e Projetos de Carbono S.A and Angelim Participações S.A, which belongs to the Perfin Group. Its main objective is to promote forest conservation and mitigate climate change by reducing greenhouse gases from deforestation and forest degradation. The project operates in two other spheres, in addition to the climate sphere: social and biodiversity. In this way, the Rio Muru REDD+ Project aims to promote socio-economic and environmental benefits, promoting activities that boost sustainable economic development and improve the community's well-being. The total project area is around 30,319 hectares and is located in the Amazon biome, in the municipality of Feijó, Acre. The predominant vegetation in the area is Lowland Open Ombrophilous Forest and there are at least six mammal species listed on the IUCN Red List, highlighting the need for forest conservation. In the area surrounding the project, communities have been identified that use the area directly or indirectly for subsistence activities.

name: Agroforestry Initiative through carbon finance to strengthen rural livelihoods and ecosystems in India
project_type: Agriculture Forestry and Other Land Use
description: The project activity, an agroforestry project, aims to regenerate low-quality agricultural lands and generate livelihood opportunities within the geographical boundary of India through the plantation of trees of native species. The project promotes carbon sequestration, reduces pressure on natural forests, and benefits nearby communities. The project activity intends to increase the tree outside forest (TOF) areas which will help in carbon sequestration by trees and thereby mitigating climate change. The project will engage local communities, including small farmers, self-help groups (SHGs) and farmer produce organizations (FPOs) in the plantation efforts to not only reduce greenhouse gas emissions but also provide a sustainable source of income and livelihood for these marginalized sections.

name: National Shale Oil Low-Carbon Intelligent Demonstration Base Carbon Sink Afforestation Project
developer: PetroChina Company Limited Changqing Oilfield Shale Oil Development Branch
project_type: Agriculture Forestry and Other Land Use
description:
National Shale Oil Low-Carbon Intelligent Demonstration Base Carbon Sink Afforestation Project (hereafter referred to as “the Proposed Project”) is located in Xinbao Village, Yule Town, Huachi County, Qingyang City, Gansu Province, People’s Republic of China.
In the absence of the Proposed Project, the sites of the project are all low-nutrient, low-supply land, and the terrain is steep, with few herbaceous plants growing. Without its implementation, all the sites will keep the same circumstances with no natural renewal and reforestation within the project area. Through the implementation of the proposed project, it enhances ecosystem services through carbon storage, and soil and water conservation. It has a significant potential to mitigate the effects of climate change effects through microclimate moderation and natural resources conservation in the short run and through carbon sequestration in the long run. It also provides employment to rural population, and promote the sustainable development of local economy and society.
The project estimates the GHG removals occurring from afforestation activities in accordance with the methodology AR-AMS0007: “Afforestation and reforestation project activities implemented on lands other than wetlands”, Version 03.1 developed under Clean Development Mechanism (CDM) for small-scale plantations. The project intends to generate carbon credits for the voluntary market under the VCS standard. The total GHG emission reduction quantified under the project for crediting period of 20 years is 13,184 tCO2e with average CO2 removal of 659.20tCO2e per year.

name: BAULU PROJECT, DEMOCRATIC REPUBLIC OF CONGO
location: Congo, The Democratic Republic of The
project_type: Agriculture Forestry and Other Land Use
description:
Located in the center of the Democratic Republic of Congo, in the “Cuvette Centrale”, the Baulu Project is designed to protect 277,131 ha of native Congolese forests legally designated for selective logging. The Project is situated within Forest Concession 009/11 – Baulu, hereinafter referred to as the Baulu Concession. Since January 2018, this concession has been managed by the company Industrie Forestière du Congo (IFCO), which harvests volumes of commercial timber from it, following the terms of the Management Plan that was drawn up at the start of management. In 2023, as part of this project, IFCO has transferred the Baulu Concession to KNCC, with the objective of converting the logging concession into a protected forest.
The main activity of the Baulu Project is to set-aside areas of Logged-to-Protected Forests (LtPF), in the timber production series of 116,181 ha, to maintain and protect ecosystem services in forest production areas legally designated for selective logging. From the cessation of timber harvesting activities, which are present in the baseline scenario, the project aims to avoid emissions generated by logging, transport, processing of raw material as well as collateral damage to vegetation caused by the fall of cut trees on surrounding plants, decomposition of material left in the forest, construction of forest tracks for transport to the storage point and other infrastructure. A further advantage that the project will bring to the area is due to the cessation of the disturbance caused by logging activities to the fauna present in this area, which is very rich and varied, thanks also to the proximity of the Lomako-Yokokala Wildlife Reserve, which includes, among other species, bonobo, forest elephant, or Bongo antelope. Community activities will also be developed in the rural development area, such as awareness raising on illegal logging and poaching activities, awareness raising and training on sustainable agricultural practices, etc.

name: Carbon Disclosure SA Solar PV Grouped Project 1
description: This Carbon Disclosure SA Solar PV Grouped Project 1 consists of commissioning new, small-scale solar photovoltaic (PV) installations and/or obtaining the rights to pursue carbon reduction from installations in the Republic of South Africa. The PV installations provide a clean, renewable source of electricity. In addition, the PV facilities increase the security of electricity supplies in South Africa. This is primarily because the national utility, Eskom, cannot provide consistent electricity supplies due to aged and failing infrastructure. The quantity and duration of power cuts in 2022 were expected to be the highest since load shedding was initiated in 2007. The Grouped Project is managed by Carbon Disclosure SA (Pty) Ltd. Carbon Disclosure SA outsources the commissioning of the PV facilities to third parties. The grouped project will comprise various project activity instances. Each project activity instance will comprise one or more solar PV facilities, where the total maximum installed capacity of the facilities is below 15 MW, per project activity instance.

name: Evander Solar Solutions PV Grouped Project
description:
This is a grouped project for the installation and operation of solar photovoltaic (PV) facilities in South Africa. The purpose of the group project is to generate renewable electricity which will be distributed into the South African grid. The project activities will lead to a reduction of greenhouse gas emissions due to the displacement of carbon-intensive coal-based electricity by zero-emission PV based electricity.
The first project activity under the grouped project entails the implementation of the 10 MW Evander Solar Solutions (Pty) Ltd Solar PV facility, located in close proximity to the Evander mine’s processing facility in the Mpumalanga Province, South Africa. Evander Solar Solutions is the owner of the PV plant. The PV plant is located in an area that has previously been disturbed within the mining right area.

name: CACHOEIRA PORTEIRA CONSERVATION PROJECT
project_type: Agriculture Forestry and Other Land Use
description: The Cachoeira Porteira Conservation Project is located within the Brazilian Amazon, specifically in Oriximiná municipality in the Pará State, Brazil. The project zone, Cachoeira Porteira territory, has 225,289.53 hectares while the project area encompasses 178,450.77 hectares. Cachoeira Porteira, a remnant quilombo community, is represented by AMOCREQ-CPT, one of the project proponents. Systemica Inteligência em Sustentabilidade S.A is the other project proponent. The Cachoeira Porteira Conservation Project falls under the category of Improved Forest Management. The project activity is Logged to Protected Forest (LtPF), and it utilizes the VM0010 v.1.3 methodology. Therefore, the project shall reduce emissions and combat decreased carbon stocks by conserving the area that would be subject to planned timber harvest in the baseline scenario. The project´s crediting period is 30 years, commencing on November 7th, 2022, and it is expected to be concluded on November 6th, 2052. The estimated average net GHG emission reductions is 567,544.43 tCO2e per year, totaling 17,026,332.88 tCO2e, over the crediting period. It is noteworthy that the Cachoeira Porteira Conservation Project meets the gold level criteria for, climate, community, and biodiversity. In a comprehensive approach, seven activities have been meticulously planned, which are synergistic with the Sustainable Development Goals, including Zero Hunger, Good Health and Well-being, Quality Education, Clean Water and Sanitation, Affordable and Clean Energy, Decent Work and Economic Growth, Industry, Innovation, and Infrastructure, Reduced Inequalities, and Life on Land.

name: Wuzhong Composting Project
project_type: Livestock, enteric fermentation, and manure management; Waste handling and disposal
description:
Wuzhong Composting Project (hereafter referred to as the project) includes two plants, one is Xinwo plant (hereafter referred to as the Plant A) owned by Xinwo Biotechnology Co., Ltd. and the other is Ruiweier plant (hereafter referred to as the Plant B) owned by Ningxia Ruiweier Energy Environment Engineering Co., Ltd.. Both plants, located in Wuzhong City, Ningxia Hui Autonomous Region, People’s Republic of China, have installed two sets of organic fertilizer production lines to treat the cattle manure.  The purpose of the project activity is to avoid methane emissions from uncovered anaerobic lagoons through composting techniques.

In absence of the project, all manure waste produced was left to decay in uncovered anaerobic lagoons, which is the most economic, viable and reasonable for livestock farm owners. 

The project was designed to treat the manure to produce organic fertilizer. The project comprises fermentation system and fertilizer production system. It uses aerobic composting and fermentation technology to treat manure. It is estimated that approximately 210,000 tons of manure can be composted aerobically annually for the project. The final compost product obtained has been sold to local businesses and farmers. 

The project activity reduces GHG in the atmosphere through avoiding methane emissions from uncovered anaerobic lagoons. The project is expected to achieve an annual emission reduction of 46,602 tCO2e and a total emission reduction of 326,214 tCO2e during the first crediting period.

name: Leiyang Hexi Animal Manure Composting Project
developer: Leiyang Cailun Contemporary Agricultural Science and Technology Park Development Co., Ltd.
description:
Leiyang Hexi Animal Manure Composting Project (hereafter referred to as “the Project”) is a centralized manure treatment plant established in Group 1, Wufeng Village, Xiaoshui Town Leiyang City, Hengyang City, Hunan Province, People's Republic of China. The project recycles animal manure from local swine farms in Leiyang City and removes solids through a solid liquid separation system. 
Prior to the implementation of the project, manure from swine barns was left to decay in uncovered lagoons for uncontrolled anaerobic decay and was used seasonally for irrigation. The lagoons were barely fully drained and cleaned , and the methane produced was not recovered and was emitted directly to the atmosphere.The project activity, which introduces an animal manure composting system associated with solid separation techniques, avoids methane emissions through the separation of manure solids that are prevented from entering uncovered anaerobic lagoons, and further eliminates any potentials for methane emissions from the manure solids, as well as lowers the risk of exceeding nutrient application limits in the irrigation lands.

name: RECOVERY AND AVOIDANCE OF METHANE FROM INDUSTRIAL WASTEWATER TREATMENT PROJECT AT TSE GROUP, INDONESIA
developer: KNOWLEDGE INTEGRATION SERVICES SINGAPORE PTE. LTD.
project_type: Energy industries (renewable/non-renewable sources); Waste handling and disposal
description:
The proposed small-scale project is methane recovery measures to be implemented in wastewater treatment facility at palm oil mill of PT. Berkat Cipta Abadi Mill, a member of Tunas Sawa Erma Group (TSE Group). The palm oil mill is already in operation and has series of open anaerobic lagoons for palm oil mill effluent (POME) treatment system.
The palm oil mill processes fresh fruit bunch (FFB) with a capacity of 100 tonnes FFB/hour to produce palm oil. During this process, wastewater effluent (around 1000 m3/day) is generated which contains high content of organic compound (around 66,900 mg COD/l). In the absence of the project activity, the POME is treated in open anaerobic lagoons. Decomposition of the organic compound in the POME produces biogas (i.e. methane gas) which under the baseline scenario (i.e. open anaerobic lagoons) is emitted to the atmosphere.
The purpose of proposed project is extraction and capture of methane enriched bio-gas generated from treatment of waste water (POME) and to utilize it for generation of steam/power required for the operating process and any excess methane gas will be flared in controlled manner in an Open flare. This reduces methane emissions a potential greenhouse gas (GHG) into the atmosphere that would have otherwise been emitted from the treatment of wastewater in anaerobic open lagoons without methane recovery. The CME will not account emission reduction from the end use of captured Biogas Plant.

name: Regenerative Agriculture and Forestry Technologies (RAFT) 1
developer: C-Quest Capital SG Africa Holdings Private Limited
project_type: Agriculture Forestry and Other Land Use
description: C-Quest Capital’s Regenerative Agriculture and Forestry Technologies project aims to reverse the trends of soil and land degradation by promoting project activities that sequester carbon in agricultural soils and biomass; reduce dependency on nitrogen fertilizers; increase soil organic matter, moisture retention and health; reduce erosion; and diversify crop production and agricultural income streams. Specifically, this project will support conservation agriculture (CA), intercropping of leguminous shrubs, alley cropping, and farmer managed natural regeneration (FMNR) of trees on farmland across Malawi. CA includes adopting minimum or no-till practices, retaining crop residues, and rotating or intercropping multiple crops. Intercropping practices will focus mainly on Tephrosia vogelii, an indigenous fast growing, deep rooted leguminous shrub that can be used as green manure and produces abundant firewood. For alley cropping, multi-use trees or shrubs are planted in rows between crop strips to promote soil fertility and stability as well as diversify farm products. Lastly, FMNR practices vary widely according to the preferences of individual farmers but in general involve the selective protection of trees regenerating naturally from existing rootstock or stumps on croplands. Together, these practices transfer carbon from the atmosphere to above and belowground biomass through photosynthesis, a portion of which is further transferred to the SOC pool through biomass residues and root exudates. Reduced soil disturbance from no-till further protects SOC stocks, increased soil fertility reduces fertilizer use and its associated emissions, and crop residue retention avoids emissions from biomass burning.

name: SUSTAINABLE PERENNIAL ORCHARDS IN ISRAEL (SPOI)
project_type: Agriculture Forestry and Other Land Use
description:
Climate change mitigation in the agricultural sector falls into three approaches. First, by reducing the current carbon emissions, via a better management of the carbon fluxes. Secondly, by avoiding potential emissions (e.g., by reusing the crop residues). Lastly, by enhancing the removals of carbon from the atmosphere (Smith et al., 2008). Regenerative agriculture (RA) is a farming approach which includes several practices (e.g., use of cover crops, reduced tillage) aiming at sequestrating soil carbon and contributing to those three approaches. RA also aims at implementing practices increasing biodiversity (e.g., crop diversity), improving the water cycle (e.g., use of drip irrigation) and increasing resilience to climate change. 
In the present project, the three mentioned approaches are applied in the framework of the Sustainable perennial orchards in Israel (SPOI). The goal of this initiative is to reduce the carbon emissions currently emitted and to raise the carbon stored in the soil and in the biomass. In addition, the selected measures will contribute to improving crop yields and soil health. With perennials, year-round carbon removals will increase; the land will be irrigated with more precision which will increase the micro-organism activity. The leaves and the other biomass residue will remain on the ground from pruning, increasing the organic matter in the project areas. Orchards require less monitoring by tractors, thus reducing the demand of energy and the amount of fuel required, this reduces CO2 emissions in the project area, compared with the baseline scenario. Also, intercrops will be sown to increase the soil organic content. This is a grouped project, located in Israel. The main environmental and sustainable development objectives pursued by the grouped project are: a) reduce carbon emissions from less intensive agricultural practices, b) promote regeneration of soil and the increase of soil organic carbon (SOC), c) increase carbon sequestration.

name: Guangxi Guigang Food Waste Recycling Project
developer: Guangxi Guigang Beikong Environmental technology Co., Ltd
project_type: Energy industries (renewable/non-renewable sources); Waste handling and disposal
description: Guangxi Guigang Food Waste Recycling Project (hereinafter referred to as the project) is located at Northwest of Guigang City's Circular Economy and Environmental Protection Industry Demonstration Base, Guigang City, Guangxi Zhuang Autonomous Region, P.R China. The project is owned and implemented by Guangxi Guigang Beikong Environmental technology Co., Ltd. The purpose of the project is to treat MSW with anaerobic digesters and utilize recovered biogas for electricity generation. The project activity includes MSW collection, MSW pre-treatment system, anaerobic digester, biogas purification, biogas utilization system and emergency flaring system. The project is to utilize the biogas produced by anaerobic digestion for power generation. The electricity generated by the project is first used for the project and the surplus will be supplied to China South Power Grid (CSPG) which is dominated by coal-fired power stations.

name: South Barito Kapuas Project
project_type: Agriculture Forestry and Other Land Use
description:
The South Barito Kapuas Project (the Project) seeks to preserve and restore an estimated 39,853 ha of dryland and peatland ecosystem. 

The Project will :
•	Avoid  28,363 ha of forest clearing and conversion to an industrial forestry plantation. 
•	Avoid 8,824 ha of peatland degradation through the conservation of these wetlands and avoidance of conversion to an industrial forestry plantation. 
•	Reforestation of 195 ha of non-forest areas back into natural forest.

The Project is in the Province of Central Kalimantan. Specifically, it is in the Barito Selatan and Kapuas Regencies, in a tropical forest landscape comprising of a mixture of dryland and peatland forest made up of approximately an unallocated license area of 39,853 ha of unallocated lands assigned for conversion to plantation forest concession to PT Nusantara Solusi Raya (NRS).

name: Wuhan Jiangxia Changshankou LFG Power Project Phase I
developer: Wuhan Huantou Environmental Technology Co., Ltd.
project_type: Energy industries (renewable/non-renewable sources); Waste handling and disposal
description:
Wuhan Jiangxia Changshankou LFG Power Project Phase I (hereafter referred to as the Project ””) is a landfill gas (LFG) recovery and utilization project d is located at
Changshankou Landfill Jinkou Street Jiangxia District, Wuhan City, Hubei province, People’s Republic of China.
Prior to the implementation of the project activity, the LFG generated from Changshankou Landfill was totally released into the atmosphere; the equivalent amount of electricity supplied by the project activity was supplied by the fossil-fuel-dominated Central China Power Grid (CCPG). The baseline scenario is the same as the conditions existing prior to the implementation of the project activity.
The Project achieves emission reductions in two aspects: 1) it avoids methane emissions by capturing and destroying LFG which would have been directly vented into the atmosphere in the baseline scenario; 2) it reduces CO2 emissions by displacing part of the electricity that would otherwise have been supplied by CCPG.

name: Floating Solar Power Project by AMP Energy In Madhya Pradesh
developer: Amp Energy Markets India Private Limited
description: AMP Energy Green Seven Private Limited, a wholly owned subsidiary of M/s AMP Solar India Private Limited (the Promoter) is a special purpose vehicle incorporated by AMP Energy Green Private Limited to develop a 140 MWp (100 MWAC) floating solar PV plant (the Project) at Omkareshwar water reservoir located near Punasa Tehsil, Khandwa District, Madhya Pradesh State, INDIA. The purpose of this Project is to utilize the area of the reservoir to generate clean energy & supply the same to M.P. Power Management Company Limited (MPPMCL). A long term PPA (Power Purchase Agreement) had been executed between MPPMCL (Procurer) & AMP (Developer).

name: Sichuan Ganluo IFM (conversion of logged to protected forest) Project
project_type: Agriculture Forestry and Other Land Use
description:
The Sichuan Ganluo IFM (conversion of logged to protected forest) Project (hereafter “the project activity”) is implemented in the Liangshan Yi Autonomous Prefecture and the Ganzi Tibetan Autonomous Prefecture, Sichuan Province of China by Chengdu Haisha Technology Co.,Ltd.. The project is located in two autonomous prefectures. The geographic coordinate  is 102°27′~103°32′ E and 28°28′~29°18′ N and 101°07′~102°16′ E and 28°09′~29°20′ N respectively. The total area is 894,128 ha, which includes the Improved Forest Management (IFM) of the forests in the conversion of logged to protected forest.
The area of the project activity is 4321.92 ha, including 450 subcompartments. The ownership and the right to use the forest land belongs to Ganluo County Xincai Forestry Plantation Co. and Jiulong County Jutiantai Forestry Development Co.. They signed Project Development Cooperation Agreement with Chengdu Haisha Technology Co.,Ltd. (hereafter referred as the project proponent). It authorized the project proponent to use the land for the forest management. The species involved in the project are Liquidambar formosana Hance, Masson Pine, soft broadleaved species, Taxodiaceae, hard broadleaved species and PopulusL. These are common local tree species.
Prior to the implementation of the project activity, the trees are logged annually according to a valid and verifiable government-approved timber management plan for harvesting the project area. The implementation of the project activity converses the trees to protected forest to reduce the GHG emissions for about 1,377,720 tCO2e in 30 years, the average annual emission reduction is 45,924 tCO2e and Verified Carbon Units with buffer deduction is about 1,074,617 tCO2e in 30 years, the average annual VCUs with buffer deduction is 35,821 tCO2e.

name: Vencedor Guajoya REDD+
project_type: Agriculture Forestry and Other Land Use
description:
The Vencedor Guajoya REDD+ project is aimed at reducing and preventing GHG emissions from deforestation activities in the forests present in the territory of the Native Community located in the basin and right bank of the Napo River, through the development and implementation of a REDD+ strategy built in a collective and participatory manner with community members and that is also aligned with the objectives of the life plan, which is conceived as a community planning instrument that contains the worldview, history and future vision of community. Likewise, the territorial planning and environmental protection instruments of the region are taken into account.
Within the framework of the development and implementation of the project, the intervention strategy consists of the execution of actions framed in four main components: i) strengthening governance; ii) development of sustainable productive activities compatible with the conservation of biodiversity; iii) increase in social investment; iv) monitoring. This is how the REDD+ project strategy also seeks to integrate different interventions in the territory, by offering economic resources that can potentiate processes in progress or to be implemented and that in turn allows attracting greater investment to the territory for the benefit of the communities.

name: Grouped Solar Power Project by Indospace Development Management Pvt. Ltd.
description:
The project involves installation of Solar Photovoltaic Panels on rooftops/ground mounted in various states of India. The sole purpose of the project activity is “Production of electricity using renewable energy technologies (Solar PV Technology in this project activity) that supply electricity to user(s). 
All the rooftop solar panel units involved in this project are owned by the building owners as mentioned in the table below (as investor name) & the purpose of electricity generated also mentioned in the table. name: NATURAL SILVOPASTORAL SYSTEMS IN THE COLOMBIAN ORINOQUIA REGION
project_type: Agriculture Forestry and Other Land Use
description:
The project “Natural silvopastoral systems in the Colombian Orinoquia Region” is a grouped project comprising a set of activities to improve grassland management. The project primary objective is to achieve a reduction in overall emissions by focusing on carbon sequestration. This will be accomplished by enhancing livestock practices through the following project activities:

- Implementation of adaptive multi-paddock grazing with improved deep-rooted grass cultivars, specifically Urochloa humidicola,
- Human-assisted regeneration of arbustive chaparros (Curatella americana) on paddocks to harness the potential of existing natural processes of seed dispersal and resources to restore woody vegetation,
- Cease grassland burns, and 
- Natural regeneration of tropical, highland savannah vegetation in buffer zones around riparian forests, and environmental.

The project activities will take place in approximately 150,000 ha of Vichada and Meta, two of the four departments of the Orinoquia region in Colombia, referred to here as “Colombian Orinoquia”. The crediting period is 2020 to 2040 applying the VCS Methodology for Improved Agricultural Land Management VM0042 Version 2.0. An estimate of the annual average and total GHG emission reductions and removals are approximately 270,000 t CO2eq per year and 5,400,000 t CO2eq, respectively.

With its implementation, project instances will see an increase in livestock production, alongside overall emissions reduction driven by soil carbon sequestration. Prior to the implementation of the project, livestock practices in the regions are characterized by annual burning of savannas and low-quality animal feed. It is also expected substantial contribution to the sustainable development goals (SDGs) 2 Zero hunger, 8 Decent work and economic growth, 9 Industry, innovation and infrastructure, 12 Responsible consumption and production, 13 Climate action, 15 Life on land, and 17 Partnerships for the goals.

name: Electric Forklifts and Trucks Nigeria
description:
The Project operates battery electric forklifts, material handling equipment and trucks for commercial operations and management of goods in Nigeria. Electric Vehicles (EVs) are charged from electricity provided by the grid. EVs are deployed on a national level within the entire country. Vehicles are owned and/or operated by Bisedge Ltd.. The Project activity adds on vehicles over the project operations but the project owner and operating system is always the same. Please note, there are multiple locations/project activity instances so the geodetic points provided in the next section are for one site only. 

The Project reduces Greenhouse Gas (GHG) emissions by using electricity for propulsion instead of the commonly used fossil fuels (gasoline, diesel). Electric engines are far more energy efficient than internal combustion engines. Even including upstream emissions for electricity generation based on the Nigerian grid factor, EVs reduce considerably GHG emissions compared to fossil units. The situation prior to implementation of the Project is the use of fossil vehicles.  

Average annual GHG emission reductions under this Project are estimated at  29,389 tCO2 or a total of 293,996 tCO2 over the crediting period. The amount of emission reductions is directly correlated to the number of EVs which can be included by the Project. The Project is established for a 10-year crediting period.

name: HORTICULTURE PLANTATION IN CENTRAL INDIA
project_type: Agriculture Forestry and Other Land Use
description:
Project Summary

The project activity “Horticulture Plantation in Central India” is being proposed under Verra VCS Program for generation of carbon credits. It is proposed by AadharStambh Consultancy Services Private Limited, who is the Project Proponent of the project activity. It involves the planting, nurturing, and management of horticultural fruit bearing species including guava, orange, lemon, etc. The lands on which horticulture plantation is being done are owned by small-scale farmers who have voluntarily enrolled into the project activity. The project is located Mandsaur, Dhar districts of Madhya Pradesh. The project started from 2021 onwards and estimated to generate 1,15,000 tCO2e of average annual carbon emission reductions. Since then, the Project Proponent has multiple farmers for carbon credit project under Verra VCS Program. The project has applied AR-ACM0003: Afforestation and reforestation of lands except wetlands --- Version 2.0. In addition to carbon credit generation, the project also provides multiple sustainable development benefits as well (UN Sustainable Development Goals) – such as, SDG 5-Gender Equality; SDG 13-Climate Action and SDG 15 – Life on Land.

name: Xinjiang Fuyun Improved Grassland Management Project
developer: Xinjiang Fuyun County State-owned Assets Investment Management Co., Ltd.

The project will increase carbon sequestration, reverse grassland degradation, contribute to local development and preserve cultural traditions. The implementation of the project will significantly improve the local climate benefits, community benefits, and biodiversity benefits.

name: Xinjiang Kalamaili Improved Grassland Management Project

The project will increase carbon sequestration, reverse grassland degradation, contribute to local development and preserve cultural traditions.The implementation of the project will significantly improve the local climate benefits, community benefits, and biodiversity benefits.

name: PROMOTING REGENERATIVE AGRICULTURE AND GROWTH THROUGH INCOME GENERATION
project_type: Agriculture Forestry and Other Land Use
description: Grow Indigo is implementing a regenerative agriculture-based carbon project in the extensive rice cultivation states of Andhra Pradesh, Chhattisgarh, Karnataka, Odisha, and Telangana in India. The project area is characterized by traditional and intensive cultivation practices within diverse ecological systems, which emit significant amounts of greenhouse gas (GHG) emissions. The southern region, encompassing Andhra Pradesh, Telangana, and Karnataka, excels in irrigated rice farming and cultivation in deltaic and non-deltaic regions. At the same time, Chhattisgarh and Odisha specialize in rainfed upland and lowland rice cultivation. Intensive agriculture practices in the project area have threatened food security and contributed to increased GHG emissions. The Grow Indigo project aims to incentivise farmers for adopting regenerative agriculture practices, thereby achieving the mitigation of greenhouse gas (GHG) emissions and fostering positive environmental and economic outcomes. Regenerative agriculture is a holistic farming system that focuses on improving soil health, biodiversity, and water quality. It can help to reduce GHG emissions by sequestering carbon in the soil. These practices include improved fertilizer management, cover cropping, crop rotation, reduced tillage, improved water management, crop residue management, agroforestry, etc. The project will also help to build the capacity of farmers to adopt regenerative agriculture practices through training and technical support. The project aims to scale up to 4 million hectares within the project area over a 5-year period. During the 20-year crediting period, it is estimated that there will be an average annual reduction and removal of 5,326,066 tCO2e. This innovative project has the potential to make a significant contribution to sustainable agriculture and climate change mitigation in India.

name: REGENERATIVE AGRICULTURE IN THE GANGA-BASIN FOR FARMER INCOME AND CLIMATE IMPACT
project_type: Agriculture Forestry and Other Land Use
description: Grow Indigo is implementing a regenerative agriculture-based carbon project that spans across Bihar, Madhya Pradesh, Rajasthan, and Uttar Pradesh. This project is taking a bold step towards environmental sustainability in the Ganga basin region of India. Common agricultural practice in these areas includes conventional methods such as heavy use of synthetic fertilizers, intensive tillage, crop residue burning, and excessive water consumption for irrigation. These practices have led to soil depletion and accelerated greenhouse gas (GHG) emissions, threatening the ecosystem of the Ganga basin. The transition to regenerative agriculture is vital to counteract soil degradation, fertility loss, water pollution, and natural resource depletion. This shift is crucial to maintain the ecosystem services of the Ganga basin. The potential impact of the VCS carbon project is immense. It promises to significantly reduce GHG emissions, improve soil health, and enhance biodiversity. Beyond environmental benefits, the project aims to uplift the livelihoods of smallholder farmers and enhance the resilience of the Ganga basin ecosystem in the face of climate change. Over a five-year period, the project aims to scale up to cover 4 million hectares within the Ganga basin region of the project area. The 20-year crediting period is expected to yield an average annual emission reduction and removal of 5,048,425 tCO2e. Grow Indigo's efforts in this project exemplify a proactive and holistic approach to tackle environmental challenges, offering a ray of hope for the Ganga basin and its residents.

name: Tamusu Improved Grassland Management Project
developer: Inner Mongolia Chengyao Grassland, Forestry and Animal Husbandry Ecological Technology Co., Ltd.
project_type: Agriculture Forestry and Other Land Use
description: Yabu Ala Improved Grassland Management Project (hereinafter referred to as “the project”) is located in Alashan Right Banner, Inner Mongolia Autonomous Region of China. The project is aimed to improve the rotation of grazing animals, limit the timing and number of grazing animals on degraded pastures, and restore degraded land by replanting with grasses and ensuring appropriate management over the long-term. The project proponent is Inner Mongolia Chengyao Grassland, Forestry and Animal Husbandry Ecological Technology Co., Ltd (hereinafter referred to as the Project Proponent or PP). According to the baseline survey, before the implementation of the project, the grassland in the region has experienced serious degradation and even desertification due to the impact of climate change and human activities. Totally, 354,435.75 ha of degraded grassland has been managed properly and there are three main restoration measures namely rest grazing and rotational grazing implemented in moderate degraded area and the categorization is in line with Parameters for Degradation, Sandification and Salification of rangelands (GB19377-2003).

name: HEBEI WEI COUNTY IMPROVED AGRICULTURAL LAND MANAGEMENT PROJECT
project_type: Agriculture Forestry and Other Land Use
description:
Hebei Wei County Improved Agricultural Land Management Project  is located in Wei County, Handan City, Hebei Province of China. The goal of this initiative is to reduce the carbon emissions currently emitted by the farms taking part to the project and raise the carbon storage in the soil. In addition, the selected measures will contribute to improving crop yields and soil health. The project was implemented by the Weixian Capital Investment and Operation Co., Ltd and Hainan icarbon Ecological Development Co.,Ltd.
The project is located in Wei County. The project area is 46,666.7 ha. The crop rotation system in this project is winter wheat-summer corn.The proposed project is aimed to prevent the soil degradation through adoption of the improved crop land management practices (collectively referred to conservational tillage) to replace the conventional cultivation mode.

name: Mixed afforestation with native and non-native species in Argentina-I
project_type: Agriculture Forestry and Other Land Use
description:
This Mixed afforestation with native and non-native species in Argentina-I project consists of the afforestation of 1,006.98 hectares with different types of pine and eucalyptus species and a 3% of the area with a mix of native species. No harvesting activity will be done, to maximize the CO2 sequestration from the atmosphere. 
The project activity will be carried out in two locations owned by Garruchos S.A and managed by Cambium. Puerto Valle Ranch and Garruchos Ranch, located in the province of Corrientes, Argentina. The area has a suboptimal quality and degraded soil due to the historical unmanaged cattle raising. 
This afforestation project will be carried out considering the existing local guidelines of Good Forest Practices and it will have the FCS certificate, which ensures that the design, planting and maintenance of the forest are carried out through a sustainable forest management program avoiding negative impacts on biodiversity, local communities, and water bodies.
The project activity converts a degraded area, where extensive livestock activity was historically carried out, into an afforestation project activity with no harvest. As the goal is carbon capture, pruning activities are also not anticipated. In addition, the afforestation will contribute to minimizing soil erosion, protecting, and restoring areas degraded by extensive cattle raising. Moreover, a native species domestication program will be implemented together with Misiones National University, aiming to further study native species´ growth demands and conditions.
The absorption of GHGs will occur through the carbon reservoirs that will be generated through afforestation, with a start date of September 1st 2022. These include aboveground biomass, belowground biomass, and soil organic carbon. The project is estimated to remove a total amount of 993,822 tCO2 over a 40-year period, which works out at an average reduction of 24,845 tCO2 per year.

name: JIANGSU SUQIAN AWMS Biogas Recovery and Utilization Project
project_type: Livestock, enteric fermentation, and manure management; Waste handling and disposal
description: Jiangsu Suqian AWMS Biogas Recovery and Utilization Project (hereinafter referred to as the grouped project) is a grouped project which installs 4 new animal waste management systems (AWMSs) to treat the manure for 4 newly built swine farms in Suqian, Jiangsu Province. The grouped project is a greenfield project, it is owned and implemented by Muyuan Foods Co., Ltd. (hereinafter referred to as the project proponent). Each swine farm installs one set of AWMS to treat the manure on site. The purpose of the project activity is to treat the manure and wastewater to avoid methane emissions generated in the baseline uncovered anaerobic lagoons.

name: Fangcheng Improved Cropland Management Project
project_type: Agriculture Forestry and Other Land Use
description:
The project is in Fangcheng County, Nanyang City, Henan province, China. It changes the previous traditional agricultural management practices to multiple Improved agricultural land management practices. 54,901 ha cropland with corn and wheat rotated is involved in the project.
The intensity of tillage in the project scenario is decreased by reducing the frequency of tillage. The tillage is conducted every three years instead of each year. Organic fertilizer is used to replace part of the inorganic fertilizers. Moreover, the crop straw in the project area is returned to the field. These IALM practices can improve soil health and the SOC content will also be increased. Besides, N2O emissions are avoided due to reduced application of nitrogen fertilizer.

name: Puning MSW Incineration and Power Generation
developer: Puning Guangye Yueneng Environmental Protection Energy Co., Ltd.
project_type: Energy industries (renewable/non-renewable sources); Waste handling and disposal
description:
Puning MSW incineration and power generation project (hereafter referred to as the project) is located in Yunluo Town, Puning City, Guangdong province, China. The Project is invested, constructed and operated by Puning Guangye Yueneng Environmental Protection Energy Co., Ltd.. (hereafter referred to as the project owner).
With two 600t/d MSW combustion production lines, the project will treat 1,200 tons of MSW per day. The combustion system is composed of two 600t/d mechanical grate incinerators, matched with one set of 25MW steam turbine generator. The project will process 438,000 tons of MSW every year, and consume 90 tons of 0# light diesel as auxiliary fuel. The MSW combustion line will work over 8,000 hours every year, generating 153,300 MWh electricity, of which 122,640 MWh will be exported to the China Southern Power Grid (hereinafter referred to as CSPG). The remaining electricity will be used by the project itself and there will be no purchased electricity. 
By combusting MSW that would otherwise be disposed of at landfill, the proposed project activity avoids the emission of methane that would be generated under landfill condition. In the meanwhile, by utilizing the waste heat from the combustion of MSW, the boilers can produce steam to generate power to replace the electricity that would otherwise be generated by fossil- fuel fired power plants which are connected to the CSPG.The baseline scenario of this project is the same as the scenario prior to the implementation of the project, namely the landfill gas is vented directly and the equivalent power is supplied by the CSPG.
The project is expected to provide electricity of 122640 MWh annually into CSPG. The total emission reduction is expected to be 940030 tons of CO2 and the average annual 
emission reduction is 134290 tons of CO2 in a period of 7 years (from 25 April 2022 to 25 April 2029).

name: Core Carbon Electric Vehicles Project
description:
This project activities involves introduction and operation of new electric and/or hybrid vehicles that displace the use of fossil fuel vehicles in passenger and freight transportation. The vehicles include two-wheelers, electric four wheelers, electric three wheelers, electric light trucks, heavy trucks, haulage trucks, pick-up trucks, tractors, tippers and electric buses in transportation, last-mile logistics and delivery, this will replace the use of fossil fuel-based vehicles. The project vehicles use electric batteries, which displaces the GHG emissions produced by traditional internal combustion engines. As a result, the project results in lower GHG emissions, reduces the cost per delivery, and contribute to a cleaner environment. 
The project activity will be grouped project activity which will include new instances of vehicles in every verification cycle, each vehicle will consider as individual instances and follow the applicability criteria of instances given below. Based on emission reduction calculation of applicable CDM methodology AMS-III.C. “Emission reductions by electric and hybrid vehicles” version 16, overall emission reduction of project activity will not increase from 60,000 tCO2e/year for each instance. In 10 years, crediting period project will generate approx. 69,664 tCO2e and annual average emission reduction will 6,966 tCO2e.

name: BULGARIAN SUSTAINABLE FARMING CARBON PROJECT
project_type: Agriculture Forestry and Other Land Use
description:
The “Bulgarian Sustainable Farming Carbon Project” aims to raise farmers' awareness on the benefits of regenerative agriculture and how changes in agricultural practices can help in climate change mitigation and adaptation. 
Regenerative agriculture land management practices refer to farming and grazing practices that aim to reverse climate change by rebuilding soil organic matter, sequestering carbon, improving degraded soil biodiversity, improving water cycle, and restoring soil fertility. Regenerative agriculture does not imply only one practice, instead, it is generally a combination of techniques.
To achieve this objectives, different regenerative agricultural practices will be implemented. These will include, among others: 
-	Promoting no tillage or minimal tillage: this practice aims to avoid soils tillage which is one of the main causes of soil losses/erosion. This practice helps not only to conserve the soil structure but also to improve it and improve the soil organic carbon levels.
-	Introducing cover crops: this practice aims to avoid having soils without vegetation cover by introducing alternative crops in-between the main productive ones. This promotes soils conservation by avoiding erosion.  For this activity, Agrovar counts with a personalized information platform that processes the soils data which comes from laboratories and satellite information and as a result provides very specialized mixes of cover crops suggested for each land area according to every specific situation.
-	Information system for optimizing farming activities.
The project is developed as a grouped project within the boundaries of Bulgaria. The project activity intends to add more instances over the upcoming years. The project implementation will result in an increase of carbon stocks and a reduction of GHG emissions.

name: Panambi REDD+ Project: Forest Conservation in the Paraguayan Chaco
project_type: Agriculture Forestry and Other Land Use
description:
Paraguay, renowned for its abundant fauna and vegetation, has emerged as an area of concern regarding deforestation in Latin America. Both legal and illegal practices are slowly depleting these natural resources. Beyond their role as host of a vast biodiversity, the forests are also a crucial carbon sink.
The conversion of forests into cattle ranching, agriculture and timber production is one of the main drivers of legal deforestation in the country. Despite the Oriental Region of Paraguay has a zero-deforestation policy, the Occident, known as the Chaco Region, lost around 4.37 million hectares of forest between 2005 and 2020 to these practices (INFONA, 2022).
Under these circumstances, this project has been designed to preserve the Paraguayan Chaco forests by grouping landowners that have plans and permits to clear land but are willing to reduce this planned deforestation. Our goals include raising awareness about conservation and its positive effects, controlling logging practices and monitoring environmental and social indicators.
According to VCS Standard 4.5, eligible REDD activities are those that reduce net GHG emissions by reducing deforestation and/or forest degradation and, since the land is legally authorized to be converted to a non-forest area, project activities fall under the Avoiding Planned Deforestation category.
In the long term, specific actions related to biodiversity and community will be defined to be developed within the project framework.
Under the selected methodology, the carbon project is expected to generate a total of 45 million tCO2e in emission reductions over the course of a 30-year period. In other words, a yearly emission reduction equivalent to 1,5 million tCO2e.

name: Henan CP Group Swine Farm Biogas Recovery and Utilization Project
project_type: Livestock, enteric fermentation, and manure management; Waste handling and disposal
description:
Henan CP Group Swine Farm Biogas Recovery and Utilization Project (hereinafter referred to as the project) installs animal waste management systems (AWMSs) to treat the manure from 5 swine farms in Henan Province, China. Each swine farm is to build anaerobic animal manure treatment systems to treat manure waste of Breeding Swine Farms separately in Luoyang, Shangqiu, and Pingdingshan owned and implemented by subsidiaries of Charoen Pokphand Group (CP Group). The purpose of the project activity is to treat the manure and wastewater on site to avoid methane emissions generated in the baseline uncovered anaerobic lagoons.
All the manure and wastewater are collected and is flushed and pumped to the aerobic treatment system (HDPE Membrane Enclosed Anaerobic Digester). The biogas generated during the treatment process will be captured for heat generation and food processing facility for self-use. An emergency flare is installed in each project activity instance to ensure that biogas would be destroyed when exigencies happened. After anaerobic digestion, the digestate is sent out and used for agriculture fertilization aerobically in the nearby farmlands for free. The effluent will be used for agricultural irrigation. 
The project is expected to avoid GHG emission of methane through recovery and destruction of biogas. It is estimated that 22,432tCO2e emission reductions will be generated annually and total emission reductions are 224,320tCO2e in the 10 years’ fixing crediting period.

name: Carbono Rural Paraguayan Chaco
project_type: Agriculture Forestry and Other Land Use
description:
The Carbono Rural Paraguayan Chaco project aims to promote sustainable grazing practices in degraded pastures in Western Paraguay, targeting farmers practicing continuous or unsustainable grazing. The project aims to enhance grazing system productivity, soil carbon sequestration, and reduce GHG emissions. Paraguayan Chaco's primary economic activity is livestock farming, with farms ranging from 1,000 ha to 60,000 ha. Traditional management includes extensive pastures, resulting in degradation due to mismanagement, pests, weed proliferation, and overgrazing, mainly due to a lack of technical advice and high costs for sustainable practices. The project leverages carbon market incentives to promote sustainable farming.

Current practices lead to severe pasture and soil degradation, reducing land productivity and carbon retention capacity. The project seeks to restore soil properties, prevent degradation, and increase livestock productivity through controlled grazing, pest and water management, and producer capacity building. Desde el Suelo, an agronomic extensionist team, will implement and monitor project activities.

Increased grassland productivity is expected to sequester carbon, improve livestock production, and bring community and biodiversity benefits: i) enhance livestock production efficiency and stability, ii) improve soil quality, iii) raise livestock farming incomes, iv) enhance soil and grassland biodiversity, v) reduce pollution, vi) strengthen community resilience, vii) boost rural employment and skills in grazing management, viii) improve rural worker well-being, and ix) enhance animal welfare. The project aligns with UN Sustainable Development Goals:

SDG Goal 2: Zero Hunger
SDG Goal 8: Decent work and economic growth
SDG Goal 13: Climate Action
SDG Goal 15: Life on Land
The project is a grouped initiative in Paraguayan Chaco, aiming to generate 445,697 tCO2e/year reductions and removals using Methodology VM0042 v2.0.

name: Pantanal REDD+ Program
project_type: Agriculture Forestry and Other Land Use
description:
The Pantanal biome is located in the center-west of Brazil, covering portions of the states of Mato Grosso and Mato Grosso do Sul. Considered the largest continuous freshwater wetland on the planet, this biome oscillates between terrestrial and aquatic phases, forming a mosaic of landscapes that provide great biodiversity of flora and fauna. Analyzing the historical context of the region where the Pantanal is located, there has been a considerable expansion of agricultural activities (the main local economic activity, mainly focused on the breeding of Pantanal cattle) and this factor, together with the high rates of forest fires in this area, results in a scenario of unsustainable exploitation of the natural resources of this biome.
Considering all the applicable legal requirements, landowners who have a surplus of native vegetation on their property and choose to preserve it, would fulfill the first requirement for obtaining economic incentives from the voluntary carbon market, through Reducing Emissions from Deforestation and Forest Degradation (REDD) through Avoided Planned Deforestation (APD). Given all this context, the implementation of the REDD+ Carbon Program on a scale for the Pantanal biome is possible, providing a model of sustainable economic development that can help to redress the balance, reconciling the conservation of environmental services with traditional economic activities. Biofílica Ambipar, in partnership with rural landowners in the Pantanal of Mato Grosso do Sul who are committed to promoting dialogue that benefits both the environment and sustainable economic development, aims to develop economic activities linked to the conservation of environmental services and all their ecological functions through the implementation of the Pantanal REDD+ Program.

name: RESTORED PRODUCTIVE LANDSCAPES IN THE MAGDALENA RIVER MIDDLE BASIN IN COLOMBIA
project_type: Agriculture Forestry and Other Land Use
description:
The main objectives of this project are: First, to recover lands degraded by land uses related to deforestation, such as cattle ranching; through ecological restoration, agroforestry systems and assisted natural regeneration, to ensure the recovery of forests inhabited by many species of flora and fauna, including endangered species such as the brown spider monkey, the blue-billed curassow, capuchin monkey, the white-faced curassow, and the night monkey. Second, by implementing restoration corridors to reconnect wild populations within a grassland matrix to increase the flow of individuals, and therefore the genetic flow, of these populations and thus increase their resilience and probability of survival in the medium and long term. And third, to recover strategic areas that are degraded, such as the banks of rivers and other bodies of water or areas where grassland productivity is low. 
FPP Colombia (project proponent) is a non-profit organization promoting biodiversity research and conservation focusing on endangered primate species. FPP initiated one of Colombia's first studies and conservation programs for the brown spider monkey. FPP operates one of the longest-running research projects in Latin America, focusing on the brown spider monkey, one of the world's most endangered primates. FPP's activities have been concentrated in the Middle Magdalena River Valley, an area relatively little studied affected by human activity and part of a global biodiversity hotspot (Tumbes-Chocó-Magdalena).
The Proyecto de Vida Silvestre, an initiative of Ecopetrol SA, Fondo Acción and WCS, seeks to conserve biodiversity in 3 regions of Colombia of biological and cultural importance, but which face increasing pressures that threaten natural resources. Through the articulation of these conservation initiatives, sustainability is sought through the development of a grouped carbon project which will generate income from carbon credits to achieve the objectives of ecosystem recovery

name: TAJIMAT PUJUT - El buen vivir - Restauración y conservación de los bosques Awajún del Alto Mayo
project_type: Agriculture Forestry and Other Land Use
description:
The “Tajimat Pujut, Restoration and Conservation of the Alto Mayo Awajun Forests” is a grouped project jointly developed by the Federacion Regional Indigena Awajun del Alto Mayo (Regional Awajun Indigenous Federation of Alto Mayo - FERIAAM) and Conservation International Foundation (CI). FERIAAM is an indigenous territorial organization that groups and represents 16 indigenous Awajun communities (13 in the department of San Martin, and 3 in the department of Loreto). FERIAAM is the lead project proponent and CI is the co-proponent. The project is located in the provinces of Moyobamba, Rioja and Datem del Marañon, and covers an area of 235,455ha.
The main goal of the “Tajimat Pujut” project is to achieve the restoration and conservation of Awajun forests. In recent decades, deforestation within the Awajun communities has accelerated, with greater impact since 1990 after the opening of the Fernando Belaunde Terry highway. The increase in deforestation is mainly due to a heavy migration of people from the Andes and coastal region of Peru to the Amazon, causing a significant change in forest cover due to the expansion of the agricultural frontier and the illegal logging of high-value timber species. The forests of native communities have been replaced by commercial crops, mainly by farmers (tenants), invaders and illegal loggers. 
The project will focus on implementing strategies and activities to achieve better management of the Awajun territory, strengthen its governance and indigenous identity, restore degraded areas, and diversify sources of income and sustainable productive activities that secure wellbeing for the Awajun people. Tajimat Pujut expects to generate 8,788,206 tCO2eq over the 30 year project lifetime, with an average of 292,940 tCO2eq per year.

name: WANAMEI (Árbol de vida) Conservando los bosques de Amarakaeri
project_type: Agriculture Forestry and Other Land Use
description:
The “WANAMEI” Project is located in Peru, within the province of Manu (department of Madre de Dios), and the province of Paucartambo (department of Cusco). The Executor of the Administration Contract of the Amarakaeri Communal Reserve (ECA – Amarakaeri) is the lead project proponent and will work with Conservational International Foundation (CI) and the National Association of Administration Contract Executors of Communal Reserves from Peru (ANECAP) as co-proponents. The Project area includes the Amarakaeri Communal Reserve, its 10 associated indigenous communities and the Quero Haramba conservation concession, covering nearly 599,286 ha  

The Amarakaeri landscape is under high risk of deforestation as a result of the expansion of illegal gold mining into Madre de Dios. The main agents of deforestation are migrants, who come from neighboring regions in Peru due to the profitability of the mining activity. In addition, increasing migration to the region is driving an increase in deforestation through the conversion of forests to agriculture and cattle pastures.
The Project will reduce GHG emissions by implementing participatory conservation strategies with the indigenous communities’ partners of the ECA, and will be developed based on the RIA (Amazon Indigenous REDD+) guidelines established by indigenous national organizations as safeguards for carbon projects within their territories. These strategies include the strengthening of capacities for landscape monitoring and surveillance, developing sustainable economic activities, strengthening the organizations that lead the indigenous communities and ensuring financial sustainability of the initiative. The project expects to reduce 8.2 million tCO2 over the 30 year project lifetime with an average of 276,419tCO2 per year.

name: CHENGZI RECYCLED AL PROJECT A
description:
Chengzi Recycled Al Project A aims to produce recycled aluminium from aluminium waste products (e.g., window frames, aluminium cans, etc.) sourced from the MSW and to replace primary aluminium produced from raw materials. The Project located in Group 6, Lotus Village, Chengguan Town, Fang County, Shiyan City, Hubei Province, China and is developed and operated by Hubei Chengzi Aluminum Industry Co., Ltd. and Zhonghe Carbon Sink Science and Technology Research (Wuhan) Co., Ltd..
Prior to the project, pure aluminium was extracted from the aluminium ore obtained from the mining of aluminium mines by means of an electrolytic cell, which was the basic scheme of the project. Therefore, the GHG emission reduction will be generated through the implementation of the project by avoiding the consumption of the equivalent raw materials and reducing related energy consumption as well. The project has started constructed since May 2021, and the date of production line putting into operation is March 2022.
The project activity will reduce GHG in the atmosphere through an avoiding extraction of raw materials and production of virgin materials. It is estimated that the project will result a total of 410,305 tCO2e emission reductions in the first crediting period of 7 years and with annual average of 58,615 tCO2e emission reduction in the 1st crediting period.

name: Land Life Reforestation and Restoration of Degraded Land in Spain - B
project_type: Agriculture Forestry and Other Land Use
description:
The proposed ARR-VCS project is a large-scale grouped project that aims for the long-term restoration of Spain’s forests, achieved through native mixed-species reforestation that reverses the impact of land degradation and the loss of flora and fauna. Land regeneration and biodiversity rejuvenation are central objectives of this reforestation project, which employs the latest technologies and planting techniques. Project activities are implemented by Land Life, a Dutch technology-driven reforestation company that grows forests by planting trees at scale. Land Life uses innovative technology for the planting of native tree species by optimizing tree selection, survival, and resilience. Science-driven nature restoration activities ensure the highest tree survival rate and support the permanent establishment of native forests that complement rural communities.

Project activities are implemented and monitored according to the VCS-approved project methodology AR-ACM0003, with the expectation that additional project instances are to be added over the coming years. The first group of instances of the project covers 285.56 of degraded land in Spain, located at two planting sites: Vega de Doña Olimpa, (116.21 ha), located in the province of Palencia, and Ariza (169.35 ha), located in Zaragoza province. While each project instance is expected to sequester carbon across the entire 100-year crediting period, the ex-ante estimate focuses on the initial 40 years for practical reasons to determine the annual average profile. These project instances (implemented across 2020 and 2021) are expected to sequester approximately 79,613 tCO2e over the initial 42 years of the 100-year crediting period. The estimated annual average of GHG emission removals is 1,990 tCO2e. A total of 245,927 native trees are expected to become established in the project areas described in this PD.

name: Land Life Reforestation and Restoration of Degraded Land in Spain - A
project_type: Agriculture Forestry and Other Land Use
description:
The proposed ARR-VCS project is a large-scale grouped project that aims for the long-term restoration of Spain’s forests, achieved through native mixed-species reforestation that reverses the impact of land degradation and the loss of flora and fauna. Land regeneration and biodiversity rejuvenation are central objectives of this reforestation project, which employs the latest technologies and planting techniques that ensure the highest tree survival rate and support the permanent establishment of native forests that complement rural communities. The project proponent is Defined B.V., a private limited liability company based in the Netherlands. Defined B.V. is an investment vehicle that holds various climate impact investments all dedicated to reducing worldwide CO2 emissions. Project activities are implemented by Land Life, a Dutch technology-driven reforestation company that grows forests by planting trees at scale.

Project activities are implemented and monitored according to the VCS-approved project methodology AR-ACM0003, with the expectation that additional project instances are to be added over the coming years. The first group of instances of the project covers 186.3 ha of degraded land in Spain, at two planting sites: Pison (52.69 ha), located in the province of Palencia, and Mata de Hoz (69.22 ha), located in Cantabria, and Agallas, in Salamanca (64.39 ha). While each project instance is expected to sequester carbon across the entire 100-year crediting period, the ex-ante estimate focuses on the initial 40 years for practical reasons to determine the annual average profile. These project instances, implemented between 2020 and 2022, are expected to sequester approximately 55,4120 tCO2e over the initial 43 years of the 100-year crediting period. The estimated annual average of GHG emission removals is 1,385 tCO2e. A total of 144,561 native trees are expected to become established in the project areas.

name: The Resilient Tarangire Ecosystem Project
project_type: Agriculture Forestry and Other Land Use
description:
The Resilient Tarangire Ecosystem Project (RTEP) builds upon the prior work of Northern Tanzania Rangelands Initiative (NTRI). NTRI is a collaborative effort between The Nature Conservancy (TNC) and several local partner organizations (Ujamaa Community Resource Team and Tanzania People and Wildlife) to work with pastoralist communities to conserve rangelands and improve rangeland management in the Tarangire ecosystem of Northern Tanzania. Increasing population has led to increased pressure on rangeland resources, resulting in an overall decline in rangeland health and loss of carbon stocks over the past several decades. Simultaneously, this increased pressure on rangeland resources has exacerbated human-wildlife conflict and conflict among communities.
The project will focus on increasing soil carbon stocks through improved rangeland management in participating communities. Through RTEP, communities establish seasonal grazing areas to ensure efficient use of forage in the wet and dry seasons. These areas are then subdivided into smaller grazing blocks in which high-intensity, short-duration grazing can be implemented, leading to an increase in soil organic carbon stocks by increasing annual net primary productivity and allowing for recovery of forage species that typically decline under continuous grazing. The project will also help train and support community grazing coordinators who are responsible for overseeing implementation of these grazing plans. The expected long-term average annual emissions removals on a per area basis 0.73 t CO2-eq ha-1. The expected project size is about 830,000 ha, meaning the expected average annual emissions removal for the entire project area is 607,360 t CO2-eq resulting in a total of 12,147,200 t CO2-eq over the project’s lifetime.
abuse_descr: The FPIC process is deeply flawed, with limited community participation, exclusion of women and youth, and non-transparent agreements. Community members often lack basic knowledge of carbon markets, contract terms, and their implications. Carbon projects introduce rotational grazing practices that will restrict traditional Maasai grazing patterns, undermining pastoral mobility — a cornerstone of Maasai culture and rangeland sustainability. These changes risk compromising food security and adaptive strategies against climate change. Maasai communities are under strong pressure to enter into deals, because the two competing carbon project proponents are racing to submit their respective projects to validation by international standards. For this, they must sign with a minimum number villages, complete their project document and show evidence of consent. Communities fear long-term land use restrictions, loss of communal grazing areas, intra- and inter-community conflicts, and cultural erosion. The prospect of 40-year carbon contracts has raised alarms about locking future generations into potentially harmful agreements.
