name: Yvoty REDD+ Project: Forest Conservation in Eastern Paraguay
project_type: Agriculture Forestry and Other Land Use
description: The Yvoty REDD project is an initiative aimed at addressing unplanned deforestation in eastern Paraguay, with its initial focus on the Mbaracayú Reserve. This reserve, spanning 64,400 hectares, houses significant biodiversity and was established in 1992 through an international treaty. However, since 2007, it has faced illegal deforestation due to cannabis cultivation, leading to increased fire incidents. The project, led by the Fundación Moises Bertoni (FMB), aims to reduce these threats by implementing management plans that enhance security, monitoring, environmental education, and community outreach. The project will be funded through carbon certification, specifically the Verified Carbon Standard (VCS) and methodology VM0007, with an expected reduction of 19,466,334 tCO2e in emissions over 30 years, equivalent to 645,100 tCO2e per year.

name: Switching from Internal Combustion Engine Vehicles to Electric Vehicles of RÊVER Automotive’s Customers, Thailand
description:
RÊVER Automotive Co., Ltd (RÊVER or PP) is persuading users in Thailand to switch their fossil fuel-based vehicles with traditional internal combustion engines emitting pollutions and greenhouse gases (GHG) to battery electric vehicles (BEVs) for passenger transportation. BEVs are run by electric motors powered by electricity stored in batteries, instead of an Internal Combustion Engine (ICE), that do not emit GHGs per distance driven. 
This project is a grouped project, which allows to include multiple project activity instances throughout the crediting period and intends to generate Verified Carbon Units (VCUs) through the switching of user in Thailand who directly buy the BEVs from RÊVER. All carbon credits issued are owned and managed by RÊVER upon the mutual consent with users. The VCUs will be the promoting factor in term of environment and sustainability awareness rising that persuade users to the switching.
This grouped project applies the CDM methodology AMS-III.C. ver. 16.0, which describes the requirements for displacing the use of fossil fuel vehicles in passenger and freight transportation with new electric and/or hybrid vehicles to issue carbon credits across a range of their applicable vehicles. Based on emission reduction (ER) calculation, estimated ER from this grouped project activity must less than or equal to 60,000 tCO2 equivalent annually.
Before the implementation of this grouped project, the typical mode of transport within the boundary of Thailand is petrol combustion vehicles, with the market penetration of BEVs is lower than 2.5% (0.7% over the last 3 years, 2020-2022). To elaborate, ICE vehicles dominate with approximately 620,961 of its population compared to 9,584 of total BEVs in 2022.
The first and later project activity instance is set to be developed within the boundary of Thailand only. The first instance is the ER from the estimated RÊVER’s BEVs sale value in Thailand during 1 November 2022 to 31 December 2023.

name: Tang River Improved Cropland Management Project
project_type: Agriculture Forestry and Other Land Use
description:
The project changes the previous traditional agricultural management practices to multiple Improved agricultural land management practices. The project is in Tanghe County, Nanyang City, Henan province, China. It involves 94,614 ha cropland where corn and wheat are rotated.
Before implementation of the project, long-term and high-intensity deep tillage were conducted every year in the project area and no organic fertilizer was used. Additionally, no crop straw was returned to the field. The soil structure was damaged by these traditional ALM practices, which causes the loss of organic carbon in the soil, and leads to soil degradation. The project activity is expected to improve soil SOC and soil health through multiple ways of IALM practices. The intensity of tillage in the project scenario is decreased by reducing the frequency of tillage. The tillage is conducted every three years instead of each year. Organic fertilizer is used to replace part of the inorganic fertilizers. Moreover, the crop straw in the project area is returned to the field. These IALM practices can improve soil health and the SOC content will also be increased. Besides, N2O emissions are avoided due to reduced application of nitrogen fertilizer.

name: Biogas based Poultry Waste Management Project at Siddipet District, Telangana State, India
project_type: Energy industries (renewable/non-renewable sources); Waste handling and disposal
description:
The project activity is a biogas-based electricity generation project. The project involves methane recovery through controlled anaerobic digestion of poultry waste and utilization of recovered biogas to produce electricity. The project involves installation of two centralized anaerobic bio-digesters having capacities of 1500m3/day each, at the existing two poultry firms of the project owner with a total capacity of 3000 m3/day and utilization of one number of 100 KVA and one number of 250 kVA capacity biogas based electrical engines for each biogas unit.   On an average each poultry farm produces about 18 MT of poultry manure per day with total of 36 MT from two poultry firms. The electricity generated from the project is utilized for the captive use in the poultry farms.  The project activity is being implemented in phased manner where the first 1500m3 biogas unit is installed in phase I and second 1500 m3 biogas unit is installed in phase II. The project is owned and operated by Sunmax Hatcheries Private Limited company. The project is located in DasarlaPalli Village in Siddipet district of Telangana State, India.

Prior to the implementation of the project activity, the poultry manure waste utilized by the project activity is left to decay in open pits, tanks or anaerobic lagoons at the poultry farms, where the manure undergoes fermentation and release methane, that is emitted to the atmosphere directly without any methane recovery and destruction facility. 
For electricity component, prior to the implementation of the project activity, the electricity supply for the poultry farm was generated mainly from grid connected power plants.

name: NatureRe assisted natural regeneration project in degraded lands in Antioquia, Colombia
project_type: Agriculture Forestry and Other Land Use
description: The NatureRe project is a grouped project that seeks to sustainably manage 4,500 ha, within which it is estimated there is potential to restore approximately 2,925 ha. This area corresponds to livestock-degraded lands in the Antioquia Department (Colombia), in three subregions: Magdalena Medio, Bajo Cauca, and Nordeste. The project aims to restore native forest species by applying different ANR models.

name: Reforestation activities in Brazil for carbon removals from the atmosphere
project_type: Agriculture Forestry and Other Land Use
description: The grouped project proposed by SADA Participações Ltda (hereinafter SADA), “Reforestation activities in Brazil for carbon removals from the atmosphere”, consists of the implementation of new plantations of African mahogany (e.g. Khaya grandifoliola and Khaya senegalensis) and Australian cedar (e.g.  Toona ciliata) in the state of Goiás (GO), in the Midwest region of Brazil. This region is notably marked by the historical tradition in livestock activities and, more recently, by the implementation of agricultural activities.

name: Xinjiang Habahe Improved Grassland Management Project
developer: Habahe Xinghua Agricultural Investment Development Co., Ltd.
project_type: Agriculture Forestry and Other Land Use
description:
Xinjiang Habahe Improved Grassland Management Project is located in Habahe County, Altay Region, Xinjiang Uygur Autonomous Region, China. The Project aims to reduce the duration and amount of grazing on degraded grasslands by planting pasture grasses and improving grazing practices, in order to restore local degraded grassland systems and ensure grassland sustainability.
The project implemented sustainable grassland management on 91,976.85 hectares of degraded grassland through three measures: artificial grass planting, fencing and grazing ban, and rotational grazing. The implementation of the management measures can effectively increase the carbon stock and reduce non-CO2 greenhouse gas emissions, and ultimately achieve the purpose of greenhouse gas emission reduction. 
The project is expected to generate GHG emission removals of 6,283,832 tCO2e in 40 years, with an average annual GHG emission removals of 157,096 tCO2e.

name: Rabo Carbon Bank Trees for Farmers (TFF) Brazil ARR Grouped Project
project_type: Agriculture Forestry and Other Land Use
description:
This is an afforestation, reforestation and revegetation (ARR) Grouped Project aiming at establishing, restoring and/or increasing vegetative cover through planting and assisted natural regeneration in degraded forestlands, bare soils, degraded or low productivity pasture/agricultural lands and areas undergoing regeneration, located in the Amazon, Cerrado and Atlantic Forest Biomes. The project uses a mix of native species to create biodiverse forests and woodlands, and in the future potentially complemented with a share of non-native tree plantings if it is proven to be beneficial to the ecosystem and local communities. 
The project is proposed by the Trees for Farmers initiative of the Rabobank Carbon Bank, which leads and facilitates Brazilian farmers to establish, restore and/or increase vegetative cover with financing, project management as well as technical and logistical knowledge on implementation and maintenance of reforestation activities.
The first instance will be implemented in a 68.06ha area inside Fazenda Santa Paulina which in turn has 1,962 ha in the municipality of Gaúcha do Norte, State of Mato Grosso, Brazil. Since 2018, the project area has had no agropastoral activity and gave way to an area with very little and/or slow growing patchy vegetation and bare soils.
These bare areas are being replanted by the project with a mix of native species while keeping the existing patches of woody vegetation in place. This project will utilize a (Plan Vivo approved) method with remote sensing technology, called Acorn, to monitor the biomass increments and carbon sequestration.
The TFF Brazil Project foresees a gradual expansion of planted areas throughout three Brazilian biomes between 2022 and 2062. It is expected that a total of 20.000 ha (to be expanded in the final version) planted during the project lifetime.

name: CTR IPATINGA LANDFILL GAS PROJECT
description:
The proposed VCS project activity has the objective to avoid emission of Greenhouse Gases (GHG) through collection, flaring/combustion and energy use of the LFG. The proposed VCS project activity will also assist Brazil to meet its demand for energy due to the economic growing scenario, improving energy supply and contributing, at the same time, to the environmental, social and economic sustainability through climate change global mitigation and local air pollution. This initiative aims to increase renewable energy participation in relation to the total Brazilian energy consumption.
Prior to the implementation of the project activity the landfill gas is being released to atmosphere and the electricity was generated by other sources in the Brazilian national electricity grid.
Located in the southeast region of Brasil, state of Minas Gerais, city of Santana do Paraíso, the proposed VCS project activity encompasses a voluntary initiative to encourage clean technology investments in the country.
As per its design configuration, combustion of collected LFG occurs in the following methane destruction device(s): 
-	1 high temperature open flare;
-	2 engine-generator sets  of an electricity generation infrastructure (in which collected LFG will be utilized as gaseous fuel for electricity generation).
-	Possibility of future increase of the number of engine-generator sets, maintaining a total combined nameplate capacity up to 10 MW.

name: Xinjiang Altay Improved Grassland Management Project
developer: Xinjiang Altay City Zhujin Investment Co., Ltd.
project_type: Agriculture Forestry and Other Land Use
description:
Xinjiang Altay Improved Grassland Management Project (hereafter as ‘the project’) is located in Altay City, Altay Prefecture, Xinjiang Uygur Autonomous Region, China. The project aims to restore the local degraded grassland ecosystem by Improved sustainable grassland management measures, such as rotating grazing and grazing prohibition in the project area by building fences, and improving the degraded grassland ecosystem by reseeding high-quality local grass seeds. After the implementation of the project, the grassland will be scientifically and rationally utilized according to the health status of the local grassland ecosystem. Achieve long-term sustainable management of degraded local grasslands. The implementation of the project has significantly improved the local climate benefits, community benefits and biodiversity benefits. The project sponsor is Xinjiang Altay City Zhujin Investment Co., LTD..
The project is estimated to generate GHG emission removals of 18,687,019 tCO2-e in 40 years, with an average annual GHG emission removal of 467,175.475 tCO2-e.

name: Livestock 2040/ Uruguay
project_type: Agriculture Forestry and Other Land Use
description: The Livestock 2040/Uruguay project is driven and conceived by the consulting firm Profesionales SRL.It involves the participation of farmers in Uruguay who practice rotational grazing and have implemented good management practices on their property. Project is a grouped project.Rotational grazing is the primary activity of the project, which brings benefits to the ecosystem: it prevents and reduces soil erosion, improves the nutrient cycle, increases soil organic carbon (SOC) levels, and boosts pasture production. Participants also implement good practices in grass-fed livestock management with the goal of enhancing the ecosystem's well-being through the management of the plant-soil-animal relationship. Grazing management that enables higher quantity and quality of pasture to support high stocking rates while respecting animal welfare is a key component. Activities that increase biodiversity, such as the inclusion of native species and hunting prohibition, are considered relevant.Additionally, actions are proposed to reduce the use of external inputs, such as fertilizers or livestock feed, which contributes to decreasing greenhouse gas emissions. The result of these practices is an increase in organic matter in the soil, i.e., higher SOC content. Furthermore, the process of grassland degradation is reversed.The baseline consists of soils that were previously used for agriculture or extensive livestock farming. These soils have lost productive plant species, with areas of bare soil, compaction, low fertility, and a high risk of erosion.The project scenario consists of structured soils with a good amount of organic matter, high fertility levels, and enhanced plant growth. Compaction, erosion risk, and the amount of bare soil decrease.Estimations of emission reductions and absorption were made for the first project activity instant located in Sierra de las Animas, Maldonado, Uruguay. Greenhouse gas removals for this phase totaled 12,007 tCO2 over the 20 years.

name: Hainan Baisha Improved Forest Management Project
developer: Fujian Jinsen Carbon Sink Technology Co. Ltd.
project_type: Agriculture Forestry and Other Land Use
description: Hainan Baisha Improved Forest Management (conversion of logged to protected forest) Project (hereafter “the project”) is located in Baisha County, Hainan Province, China. It is implemented by the representative Project Proponent Baisha Li Autonomous County Rural Revitalization and Development Co., Ltd (hereafter “Project Proponent”). The project has about 2,336.5 ha commercial forest, which is nearly mature or mature. Before the implementation of the project, the forest in the project area shall be planted according to the design of commercial forest, and logged annually according to the timber logging and managing plan issued by the local forest authority. The main object of the project is to improve the forest coverage rate, protect local ecological environment, reduce carbon emissions and carbon sequestration by enhance the management level and converse logged to protected forest in the project area. The implementation of the project will result in significant carbon sequestration and improve the sustainable development of ecological system.

name: Bundled Captive Solar Power Project by Dalmia Cement
description:
The project involves installation of Solar Photovoltaic (SPV) Panels on ground mounted and
floating base solar power plant in various states of India. The sole purpose of project activity is
to install solar power plant for captive purpose and surplus generated electricity can be supplied
to grid and further equivalent energy will be consumed from grid through net metering
arrangement with state electricity board.

name: Reforestation of Lands for Multiple Purposes as a Sustainable Development Driver
project_type: Agriculture Forestry and Other Land Use
description:
The grouped project “Reforestation of lands for multiple purposes as a sustainable development driver” has as its stated goal the promotion of sustainable reforestation in Southern Brazil, specifically in the states of Paraná and Santa Catarina, aiming to achieve net removals of greenhouse gases from the atmosphere. 
The land use that has historically predominated in these states is non-forested lands, such as agriculture and cattle raising. The project proposes a change in the traditional land use of this region, promoting reforestation practices as a sustainable alternative, either to produce wood for multiple purposes based on rapid-growth species (for example, Pinus.spp or Eucalyptus.spp), and/or to restore areas based on native species of the local phytophysiognomy. The overall purpose of this initiative is to develop economically profitable reforestation system, integrating reforestation activities for the purposes of production and restoration of conservation areas, which simultaneously provides environmental and social benefits to the region. This grouped project also contemplates the possibility of silvopastoral systems implementation, nonetheless, emission removals will only be claimed for the reforestation activities.

name: Bundled Solar Power Project by AMP Energy - 02
description: The project involves installation of bundled Solar Photovoltaic (SPV) power plant with a cumulative capacity of 12.37 MW primarily to meet the captive demand of the premises owners and the rooftop, ground mounted and carport solar units are connected to the national grid through net metering mechanism. The premises owners are the customers of the power generated from the solar panels who purchase the power under long term power purchase agreements signed for 25 years. Before installation of the solar units, the Shrinath Rotopack premises and VW2 premises owners used to meet the electricity demand from the national grid of the India. The project thus replaces fossil fuel dominated grid electricity thereby reducing the equivalent amount of GHG emission. The project company for Shrinath Rotopack is AMPSolar Power Generation Private Limited and for VW2, it is AMP Energy Distributed Generation One Pvt. Ltd.

name: Jinghai Leachate Anaerobic Biogas Utilization Project
project_type: Energy industries (renewable/non-renewable sources); Waste handling and disposal
description:
Jinghai Leachate Anaerobic Biogas Utilization Project (hereafter referred to as the project) is located at Jinghai New Energy Environmental Protection Power Generation Project, in Chenguantun Town, Jinghai District, Tianjin City, P.R. China. The project is constructed and operated by Tianjin BCCY New Energy Co., Ltd.
Before the implementation of this project, Jinghai New Energy Environmental Protection Power Generation Project invested by Tianjin Gaoneng Environmental Protection Energy Co., Ltd. incinerates domestic waste with a daily treatment capacity of 1,000t /d. Leachate will be produced during the storage and fermentation process in the garbage bin. The supporting treatment system of the factory is Anaerobic (UASB) + membrane bioreactor (MBR) + nanofiltration system (NF)+reverse osmosis system (RO) treatment process. A large amount of biogas is produced in the anaerobic treatment section of UASB. Because it was difficult to collect and treat biogas, the biogas generated by the UASB was emitted to the atmosphere directly without any recovery and utilization. The biogas was being vented to the atmosphere in 28/12/2020 when the Jinghai New Energy Environmental Protection Power Generation Project started operation.
This project collects the biogas generated by the anaerobic treatment section of leachate to generate electricity and connect to the grid, which can effectively utilize biogas resources.
The project started to construct on 13/12/2021 and started operation on 12/07/2022. The project has a total designed capacity 1MW (2*500KW) and combusts the leachate biogas, which contains nearly 65% of methane, to generate electricity and export it to the North China Power Grid (NCPG). Total electricity supplied to the grid in the crediting period will be 6,630MWh. VCUs will be claimed from the methane destroyed and the grid.

name: Permaculture initiative through community participation
location: Congo, The Democratic Republic of The
project_type: Agriculture Forestry and Other Land Use
description:
This project aims to implement permaculture activities through community participation in 9,400 ha in the region of Moba, Democratic Republic of Congo. The specific objectives of the grouped project are:
1.	Setting up large-scale tree planting projects on 9,400 ha based on the “direct seeding” technique.
2.	Implement solutions for soil fertility, water conservation, climate change mitigation, and animal habitat.
3.	To raise awareness of climate change and adaptation strategies.
4.	Creation of permaculture schools’ farms through the implementation of a community program that fosters the training of the community on permaculture practices with native species with the aim of creating a community using self-sustaining systems.
The project contributes to the mitigation of greenhouse gases through a combination of sustainable land management practices and principles that promote carbon sequestration and reduced greenhouse gas emissions.

name: Enhancing rural livelihoods of farmers through carbon finance
project_type: Agriculture Forestry and Other Land Use
description:
Agroforestry can help in the conservation and rehabilitation of ecosystems and provide better livelihood opportunities for rural communities. The proposed Verified Carbon Standard (VCS) GKF agroforestry project, titled 'Enhancing Rural Livelihoods of Small and Marginalised Farmers through Carbon Finance,’ operates in several districts across Telangana and Andhra Pradesh, situated in the southeastern region of India. The project spans five districts in Telangana, namely Bhadradri Kothagudem, Khammam, Suryapet, Karimnagar, and Mancherial, as well as six districts in Andhra Pradesh, namely West Godavari, East Godavari, Eluru, Kakinada, Konaseema, and Alluri Seetharama Raju.
The agroforestry project seeks to foster sustainable agroforestry practices among small-scale farmers in Telangana and Andhra Pradesh, India. The primary objectives are to enable farmers to attain financial benefits while also ensuring greenhouse gas (GHG) mitigation within the region.

name: Tasar Forest Carbon Project
project_type: Agriculture Forestry and Other Land Use
description:
This Tasar Forest Carbon Project will promote tree-based wild silk production outside traditional forests by utilizing privately owned barren / fallow uplands of tribal farmers. The project will undertake wild silk (locally called Tasar) tree planting and promote sericulture-based livelihoods. Sericulture is a traditional livelihood, however lack of availability of host trees in natural forests constrains its expansion. Traditionally, the tribal communities in the targeted areas depend majorly on forests for their livelihoods and have a long history of wild silk production from natural forests – wild silk is second to agriculture as a source of livelihoods. However, production from the forests declined due to government regulation of forest access rights. Yet there are large areas in these regions that are severely degraded, fallow, etc. that would benefit from restoring their productive capacity and biodiversity through profitable tree planting investments. 
The project is implemented by Cognisphere Solutions Ltd. (CSL) with investment from Climate Partner Impact GmbH starting in 2022. The project will afforest 2,000 hectares of privately-owned wastelands with Tasar silk-host trees in the adjoining states of Jharkhand and West Bengal in India. The project implementation started from May 2022 and plantations were initiated in the season Jun to Oct 2022.
It will involve the participation of ~3,000 households in 125 villages, grouped into two clusters broadly in Jharkhand, and West Bengal. People in the project areas are majorly tribals with limited options to escape poverty and deprivation. Tasar host trees such as Terminalia arjuna and T. tomentosa will form the core species, accompanied with a diversity of other indigenous tree species. The planted trees will be managed as long-term agroforestry systems –integrating crop production (intercropping), Tasar silk production and associated value chain development.

name: Strengthening rural livelihood through carbon finance: Agroforestry practices in Gorakhpur Forest Circle of Uttar Pradesh
developer: Department of Environment, Forest and Climate Change, Government of Uttar Pradesh
project_type: Agriculture Forestry and Other Land Use
description: The proposed ARR VCS project plans to promote sustainable agroforestry for farmers to provide financial benefits and ensure GHG mitigation in Uttar Pradesh, India.  Agroforestry in Uttar Pradesh is a dynamic, ecologically based natural resource management system through which the integration of trees/woody perennials in farms and rangelands diversifies, and sustains production for increased social, economic, and environmental benefits.The project shall enhance farmer communities’ income, biodiversity conservation, and soil health improvement.

name: Energy Drive Energy Efficiency Grouped Project
description: The Energy Drive Energy Efficiency Grouped Project (the Project) is a grouped project applying Variable Speed Drive (VSD) technology to achieve electrical energy efficiency improvements in industrial facilities within the Republic of South Africa. The Project Proponent offers energy efficiency solutions for medium and low voltage motor systems. The motor system is retrofitted with a VSD and data collection system which is capable of actively optimising the way power is delivered to the motor system and thus reducing electricity consumption. Energy Drive actively maintains the VSD system and analyses significant amounts of data about the VSD system, motor system and other facility parameters.

name: Brightly - Reducing Food Loss and Waste
description: Food rescue organizations play a pivotal role in our society, and represent an unexpected yet critical force to mitigate the speed of climate change. This project aims to measure avoided food loss and waste, and in particular, the avoidance of toxic methane gas and other greenhouse gasses into the atmosphere. This occurs as a result of the diversion of edible food from a landfill to feed those experiencing food insecurity, thereby keeping food within the human supply chain in accordance with Verra Methodology VM 00046 v.1.

name: KIS BIOFUELS- UKINDO PROJECT
developer: KNOWLEDGE INTEGRATION SERVICES SINGAPORE PTE. LTD.
project_type: Energy industries (renewable/non-renewable sources); Waste handling and disposal
description:
This project description (PD) contains information about the KIS BIOFUELS- UKINDO Methane Avoidance from Industrial Wastewater in Indonesia.
The proposed project will implement biogas recovery, flaring and/or utilization systems for industrial wastewater treatment in Indonesia. The project involves installation of ZPHB® biogas tank & lagoon system plant for the treatment of wastewater from PT. UKINDO mill along with capturing the methane emissions from the plant and thereby reducing greenhouse gases (GHG) emissions into environment.
The project is located PT United Kingdom Indonesia Plantations (PT. UKINDO), a member of Anglo Eastern Plantations (AEP) Group, Blankahan POM, Desa Blankahan, Kec. Kuala, Kab. Langkat, Sumatera Utara Province, Indonesia.

name: NATURE PANELS, GABON
description:
The proposed project activity will utilize the wood waste as feed stock for production of particle board. The project activity is first of its kind in host country to use a wood waste as a resource for industrial production of particle board, which will replace wood log-based plywood produced from virgin wood sourced from forest.
The project activity has installed 350 m3/day particle board production capacity, which requires around 550 Tonnes of dry wood waste per day. The manufacturing of particle board involves use adhesive and paraffin wax.
Prior to project activity, majority of wood waste is generally managed as a waste product. In the Nkok SEZ region, most of the wood waste are deposited in landfills. A small percentage of the wood waste is used for energy generation for captive usage.
The project activity will reduce greenhouse gas emissions by reducing methane emissions from biomass waste that is otherwise left to decay in a dedicated landfill in the area.

name: Chahar Right Rear Banner Improved Grassland Management Project
developer: Hangzhou Chaoteng Energy Technology Co., Ltd
project_type: Agriculture Forestry and Other Land Use
description: The Chahar Right Rear Banner Improved Grassland Management Project aims to restore degraded grassland ecosystems through grazing management in the project zone. By introducing sustainable grazing practices such as grazing prohibition and grassland-livestock balance, manual restoration measures such as fence building, rodent control, and other sustainable grassland management measures, this project is expected to enhance local carbon sequestration and contribute to the development of local ecosystems. The existing degradation and salinization area accounts for 99.67% of the local grassland. To combat and reverse this degradation, the project proposes to implement improved grassland management across 225,382.93 ha of degraded grassland.

name: Xingning Tokzin PET Recycling Project
developer: Xingning Tokzin Yinghui Resources Co., Ltd.
description: The Project activity, under the premise of ensuring the quality of the product, will recycle andprocess the waste plastic PET instead of using the raw material (crude oil and natural gas) to produce the PET flakes. Therefore, the GHG emission reductions will be generated through the implementation of the project by avoiding the consumption of the equivalent raw materials andreducing related energy consumption as well. The project is owned by Xingning Tokzin Yinghui Resources Co., Ltd. Its annual productivity is55,000 tons PET flakes, and the Project will recycle 65,000 tons waste plastic PET. The estimated annual emission reductions are 59,201 tons CO2e.

name: Xinxiang Yanmai Biogas Utilization Project
project_type: Energy industries (renewable/non-renewable sources); Waste handling and disposal
description:
Xinxiang Yanmai Biogas Utilization Project (hereinafter referred to as the project) is located at Yanjin County Industrial Agglomeration Zone, Yanjin County, Xinxiang City, Henan Province, P.R. China. The project is owned and implemented by Xinxiang Yanmai Food Co., Ltd

The project will introduce new anaerobic waste water treatment system (Two anaerobic
Digesters with effective volume of 8000m3 and 5000m3 separately) to treat waste water from starch production of Xinxiang Yanmai Food Co., Ltd.. The project uses digesters to treat waste water, collect and utilized the generated biogas to avoid methane emissions. The generated biogas will be captured and used for heat generation which will be used for starch production
with 8t/h biogas boiler within the project site. The residual waste from the digester will be used for soil application. Wastewater from the waste water treatment system will be discharged to Yanjin Municipal Sewage Treatment Plant for advanced treatment. 

Prior to the implementation of the project, the waste water was treated in open anaerobic lagoon at the project site and generated methane was emitted to the atmosphere directly without any methane recovery and destruction facility. The project is expected to avoid GHG emissions of methane through recovery and destruction of biogas.

name: Biaofa Juancheng Animal Manure Management Project
project_type: Energy industries (renewable/non-renewable sources); Livestock, enteric fermentation, and manure management; Waste handling and disposal
description:
Biaofa Juancheng Animal Manure Management Project (hereafter referred to as the project) is located at Wanhua Industrial Zone, Hongchuan Town, Juancheng County, Heze City, Shandong Province, P.R.China. The project is invested, constructed and operated by Biaofa Ecological (Juancheng) Co., Ltd. 

The purpose of the project is to treat the manure to avoid methane emissions generated in the baseline uncovered anaerobic lagoons. The project will introduce a new waste management system (enclosed anaerobic digesters) to treat animal manure from 19 livestock farms in Juancheng County to replace the existing open anaerobic lagoons at the livestock farms. The treated manure is collected by tank trucks from the livestock farms to the project site and the collected manure is subsequently treated at
project site. 

By treating the manure with enclosed anaerobic digester with total effective volume of 75.360 cubic meters. The project will avoid the emissions of methane that would be generated from animal manure treatment in the existing open anaerobic lagoons at the 19 livestock farms. The biogas generated during the treatment process will be partly used for electricity generation used for operation of the project, partly used for heat generation used within the project and the rest will be supplied to users nearby for heat generation (the generated GHG emission reductions from electricity generation and heat utilization will not be claimed for conservativeness). The fermented sludge from the enclosed anaerobic digesters will be treated aerobically and used in nearby farmland as organic fertilizer. Wastewater from the treatment system will be used for agriculture irrigation.

name: Hive Ecosystems project
project_type: Agriculture Forestry and Other Land Use
description: The Hive Ecosystems Project is a revegetation and restoration project aimed at addressing the impact of long-term degradation caused through unsustainable livestock production over the past century within the Albany Thicket Biome of South Africa.The initial project instances are located on a 7,300 hectare private landholding. The project aims to rehabilitate degraded farmlands through extensive planting and management of P. afra. Active restoration has been shown to successfully rehabilitate the vegetation type and lead to gradually recovery of carbon stocks that were released following early degradation.  The outcomes of the project extend far beyond the sequestration of carbon. A primary outcome is the rehabilitation of an indigenous, diverse vegetation type that in a functional state, provides resilient ecosystem services to both local residents and downstream urban hubs. In an area that is predicted to become warmer and drier over time and has recently experienced a protracted drought (Mahlalela et al. 2020), the climate change adaptation benefit of raising livestock and securing water in a resilient manner is perhaps of greater importance than the climate change mitigation outcome of the initiative.

name: Baviaanskloof Carbon Project
project_type: Agriculture Forestry and Other Land Use
description: The Baviaanskloof Carbon Project will seek to sequestrate carbon through rehabilitation and restoration of the subtropical Albany Thicket biome The project includes a broad set of additional activities, including initial land rehabilitation (e.g., erosion control measures), the establishment of nurseries and replanting of specific indigenous species, as well as the long-term management of grazing pressure at a level that allows thicket recovery. This process leads to an increase in both biomass- and soil organic- carbon stocks, thereby gradually sequestering atmospheric carbon over time.

name: COMPOSTING OF ORGANIC WASTE PROJECT IN HUBEI PROVINCE
project_type: Energy industries (renewable/non-renewable sources); Waste handling and disposal
description:
The composting of organic waste project in Hubei province(hereafter referred to as the project) is located in Hubei province, China. The project is invested and owned by Hubei Jiubao Ecological
agriculture Co.,Ltd. The proposed project is a new building composting plant which designed to treat organic wastes to produce organic fertilizer. The proposed project comprises of fermentation system and organic fertilizer production system, etc. The purpose of the project activity is to avoid methane emissions through controlled aerobic treatment by composting of manure and biomass residue.. The project is
designed to treat 280,000 tonnes wet organic waste per year and produce 100,000 tonnes organic fertilizer per year.
In absence of the project, the organic wastes would have been dumped in the landfill sites. This new project will avoid CH4 emissions from the disposal of the waste in a landfill site in absence of the
Project. The proposed project is estimated to deliver totally 3,110,009 tCO2e emission reduction during the 10 years’ crediting period, at an average amount of 311,000 tCO2e per year. This project started operation on 05/05/2021. 
The contributions of the proposed project to local, host country and global environment and economy sustainable developments are shown as follows:
- The proposed project will avoid GHG emissions by treatment organic waste that would have been dumped in landfill site. Thus will effectively improve the living circumstances for local people.
- This project will also improve soil condition by providing organic fertilizer for local people, boosting farm crop production and promote the incomes of local farmers.
- This project could provide job opportunities for local people, which is beneficial for local livelihood.

name: GUANGZHOU EASTERN SOLID RESOURCE RECYCLING CENTER FOOD WASTE TREATMENT PHASE II PROJECT
developer: Grandtop  Fushan  Environmental  Protection  Energy  Co., Ltd.
description: The purpose of this project is to utilize anaerobic digesters to treat the city's food waste and utilize the recovered biogas for external power generation. The project activities include waste collection, waste pretreatment system, biodiesel production system, anaerobic digesters, and biogas purification. The project utilizes anaerobic digestion tanks to process urban catering food waste and collects and destroys/utilizes the biogas generated by the anaerobic system, thereby preventing the methane emissions produced during the anaerobic fermentation of fresh waste in local landfills from being released into the atmosphere.

name: Ningxia Pengyang 2021-2023 Afforestation Project
developer: Bureau of Natural Resources in Pengyang
project_type: Agriculture Forestry and Other Land Use
description:
The Ningxia 2021-2023 Pengyang Afforestation Project, Ningxia Hui Autonomous Region (hereafter as ‘the project’) is located in Pengyang County, Guyuan City, Ningxia Hui Autonomous Region of China. The aim of the project is to increase carbon sequestration and to contribute to the local sustainable development by planting the trees and shrubs on the barren mountains and barren land. The project was implemented by Bureau of Natural Resources in Pengyang, who is the proponent of this project (hereafter ‘the project proponent’). The forest is to be established in the project in 10,150 hectares by direct planting various tree and shrub species on barren hills in the selected states. These tree species include Robinia pseudoacacia, Populus hopeiensis, Pinus tabuliformis, Picea, Pinus sylvestris, Red Armeniaca sibirica, Dahurian larch, Salix matsudacernegundo, Acer truncatum, Platycladus orientalis, Pinus bungeana Zucc, Salix matsudana, Chinese Robinia, Robinia, Acer negundoaurea, Ulmus pumila, Armeniaca sibirica, Prunus davidiana, and shrub species involves Shinyleaf Yellowhorn, Hippophae Fructus, Korshinsk Peashrub, Cerasus humilis, Rosa xanthina Lindl and Clove. 
The project is located in the Pengyang County, which covers 12 towns and 3 tree farms, Baiyang Town, Caomiao Town, Chengyang Town, Fengzhuang Town, Gucheng Town, Honghe Town, Jiaocha Town, Luowa Town, Mengyuan Town, Wangwa Town, Xiaocha Town, Xinji Town, Caiyang Town, and Ruhe Tree farm, Caomiao Tree farm, Xiaoyuanzi Tree farm.
The land in the project area was barren mountains and barren land, according to the baseline survey, before the implementation of the project, there was no natural or secondary forest in the project area. The implementation of the afforestation project will generate GHG emission removals and mitigate climate change improve soil and water conservation and forest cover; enhance local biodiversity by increasing the connectivity of forest.
The implementation of the project activity converses the trees to protected forest to reduce the GHG emissions for about 3,197,649 tCO2e in 60 years, the average annual emission reduction is 53,294 tCO2e.

name: Selabam Hydropower Extension Project
description: The project is installation of 8 MW hydro project in Lao PDR. The project is being developed by EDL-Generation Public Company in Champasak province of Lao PDR.  The primary purpose of the project is to generate electricity to the Lao Power Grid. Total installed capacity of the project is 8MW, provided by two (2) Kaplan turbine and the unit capacity is 4MW. Project is commissioned on 14/12/2022 with an expected average annual electricity output of 22,640 MWh. The baseline scenario of the project is continuation of the present situation, i.e., electricity supplied from the power grid. By displacing part of the power generated by thermal power plants, the project is therefore expected to reduce equivalent CO2 emissions from grid-connected power plants.

name: Tueré REDD+ Project
project_type: Agriculture Forestry and Other Land Use
description:
The Tueré REDD+ Project is a partnership between Biofílica Ambipar Environment and Brascomp  Compensados do Brasil S.A. and aims to promote forest conservation, maintain carbon stocks and mitigate climate change by reducing Greenhouse Gas (GHG) emissions from land use changes. In addition to  climate benefits, the Project also aims to generate social benefits based on sustainable economic development practices and improving the well-being of surrounding communities, in addition to environmental benefits through actions aimed at the conservation of local fauna and flora.
The Project Area has 135,342 ha of Amazon forest, located in the mesoregion of Marajó, in the municipality of Portel, state of Pará, and is located on the banks of the Anapu and Tueré Rivers. Communities have been identified that are directly or indirectly influenced by the Project, and that are geographically close to the Project Area and depend on its ecosystem services.

name: Ateles REDD+
project_type: Agriculture Forestry and Other Land Use
description: The Ateles REDD+ Project is a partnership between Biofílica Ambipar Environment and AgroSB Agropecuária and aims to promote forest conservation and mitigate climate change by reducing Greenhouse Gas (GHG) emissions from changes in land use. It is made up of a significant part of the Amazon rainforest, located in the municipality of São Félix do Xingú, in the southeast of the state of Pará. The entire project is part of the APA Triunfo do Xingu, a conservation unit with the greatest pressure from deforestation in Brazil, which over the last few decades has suffered major threats to the maintenance of its forest remnants due to large-scale illegal deforestation. Furthermore, the region is of great importance in terms of its biodiversity, as it is located in the Tapajós Endemism Center, a place with a high concentration of rare and endemic species. In addition to climate benefits, the project aims to ensure the conservation and protection of biodiversity and natural resources through mitigating and preventative measures such as strengthening asset surveillance, social inclusion and regional socio-economic development through alternative practices to deforestation and the development and strengthening of value chains, the establishment of a biodiversity conservation program, promoting in situ monitoring of fauna and flora in the Project Area, the development of strategies that seek to bring land security and territorial belonging, as well as the strengthening of local governance, stimulated mainly by the engagement and involvement of stakeholders.

name: Wardwizard EV Project In India
description: The purpose of this project activity is the introduction and distribution of electric two-wheelers and three-wheelers which will displace the use of fossil fuel-based mainly motor gasoline-fueled vehicles in the transportation sector. The project is owned and implemented by Wardwizard Innovations & Mobility Limited. In the absence of the proposed project activity, the beneficiaries/users would have been used the motor gasoline-powered vehicles for the transportation purpose which will lead to greenhouse emissions into the atmosphere

name: YBYRÁ REDD+ Project
project_type: Agriculture Forestry and Other Land Use
description:
The YBYRÁ REDD+ Project is a unique REDD+ Project, composed by 74 rural private properties with a project area of 76,481.34 hectare of Amazon rainforest. The project is located in four municipalities: Paragominas, Ipixuna do Pará, Tomé-Açu and Ulianópolis, in the state of Pará, Brazil. The main goals are forest conservation and reduction of GHG emissions of 12,065,803.14 tCO2 in 30 years by avoiding deforestation of 38,317.74 ha in the Project area. 
Pará explores unsustainably the Amazon Forest since its historical occupation. In 2021, almost 25% deforested areas in Brazil were in Pará.  The document known as “Deforestation Arc” presented a list with 52 cities considered priority for prevention, monitoring, and control actions against deforestation  in the Amazonian region (decree nº 6.321/2007 and Ordinance n° 428 (2018) by the Ministry of Environment). The list includes Paragominas and Ulianópolis. 
The deforestation of the amazon forest in the region of the project is due to anthropic activities: timber exploration, pasture for cattle raising and agriculture. The pressure on turning forest into non-forested areas is consequence of the expansion of these economic activities, leading to invasions of private properties. For the project region, the main land use activity is the implementation of pasture for cattle raising. In relation to the social aspects, most of the communities are formed by rural farmers with social vulnerabilities, with presence of food insecurity, low income and lack of job opportunity.
Considering the aspects presented, the Project’s main goals, through conservation of forest areas and combating deforestation of the Amazon Forest, are: 1) To promote adaptations to climate change in the region; 2) To improve the quality of life of the population that lives close to the forest and 3) To conserve biodiversity and ecosystem services, through environmental education actions and foment initiatives to connect forest fragments of the PA.

name: Project Reignite: Turning Farm Waste to Climate Action
description: The agricultural sector in India faces challenges due to traditional waste disposal methods of open field burning and decay of biomass, leading to greenhouse gas emissions and environmental degradation. Together for Restoration presents Project Reignite, aimed at transforming agricultural waste into biochar for soil enrichment in India, with an initial cohort of 5,000 farmers in the state of Odisha. The project employs flame curtain pyrolysis in steel-shield soil pits, producing biochar that is mixed with manure and applied to soil. Estimated to remove 110,760 tCO2e annually and 775,320 tCO2e over a seven-year crediting period, the project offers a triple win: removing carbon, enhancing soil fertility, and uplifting marginalised local communities.

name: Jinshan Songlin Market Swine Manure Utilization Project
developer: Shanghai Songlin Industrial & Trade Co., Ltd.
description:
Jinshan Songlin Market Swine Manure Utilization Project (hereinafter referred to as the project) locates in Wanchun Village, Langxia Town, Jinshan District, Shanghai, P.R China. The project builds an anaerobic animal manure treatment system for the treatment of swine manure in Jinshan Modern Agricultural Park Songlin Market  Swine Farm. The project uses animal manure waste as ferment material to produce biogas in the Completely Stirred Tank Reactor (CSTR) type anaerobic digesters. At this stage, part of the recovered biogas will be used to generate electricity at the biogas power plant for the daily use of the swine farm. According to the feasibility study report, the designed installed capacity of the biogas power plant is 0.52MW. Waste heat recovery boiler will also be installed at the biogas power plant to recover and supply waste heat to the auxiliary equipment of the project. The residual waste from the CSTR digesters will be used as organic fertilizer directly on agricultural land in the project vicinity.
Prior to the implementation of the project, the animal manure waste was left to decay in anaerobic manure management system (lagoon) and methane is emitted to the atmosphere directly without any methane recovery and destruction facility.
The project is expected to avoid GHG emission of methane through recovery and destruction of biogas.

name: Knollwood Improved Forest Management Project
project_type: Agriculture Forestry and Other Land Use
description: This IFM project is roughly 3,800 acres and is projected to generate 152,000 credits by extending the rotation age of a mixed hardwood stratum and a planted pine stratum.

name: HUOSHENGYUAN COMPOSTING PROJECT IN MIANYANG CITY
project_type: Livestock, enteric fermentation, and manure management; Waste handling and disposal
description: Huoshengyuan Composting Project in Mianyang City (hereafter referred to as the project) installs a set of organic fertilizer production lines with an annual capacity of 50,000 tons to treat manure (cow and swine manure) from livestock farms and biomass waste residue, i.e.straw, in Santai County, Mianyang City, Sichuan Province, China. The project is invested and owned by Sichuan Huoshengyuan Biotechnology Co., Ltd. The purpose of the project activity is to avoid methane emissions through controlled aerobic treatment by composting of manure and biomass waste residue straw. This project was designed to treat the cow, swine manure and biomass waste residue (straw) to produce organic fertilizer. This project comprises of fermentation system and fertilizer production system. It is estimated that approximately 117,000 tonnes of manure and 32,000 tonnes of biomass waste residue can be treated annually, therefore total 149,000 tonnes of waste can be composted aerobically for this project. A portion of the organic fertilizer obtained is sold to the local government for improving the quality of local high-standard farmland, and another portion is sold to local farmers, farmer cooperatives and businesses. The construction start date of the project is 6 August 2019 and was put into operation on 1 January 2022. The project activity will reduce of GHG in the atmosphere through avoiding methane emissions from controlled aerobic treatment by composting of manure and biomass residue. It is estimated that 58,686 tCO2e emission reductions will be generated annually and total emission reductions are 586,856 tCO2e in the 10 years’ fixing crediting period.

name: Jiangxi Jinwang Waste Aluminum Recycling Project
developer: Jiangxi Jinwang Aluminum Development Co., Ltd
description:
Jiangxi Jinwang Waste Aluminum Recycling Project(hereafter referred to as the project) aims to produce the aluminum product by reprocessing the waste aluminum products (like disassemble aluminum from scrap cars, scrap the motorcycle disassembles the aluminum, scrap aluminum wire and cable, used cans etc.) and to replace the same aluminum product produced from the raw materials. The total production capacity is about 180,000 tons of aluminum product per year, Among them, 15,500 tons of waste cans are used every year. The Project located in  Yujiang County, Jiangxi Province, China and is developed and operated by Jiangxi Jinwang Aluminum Co., Ltd. (hereinafter called the Project Owner).
Prior to the project implementation, the same amount of aluminum alloy was produced from raw materials (crude oil and natural gas); the baseline scenario is the same as the condition prior to project initiation. The Project achieves GHG emission reductions by avoiding the consumption of the equivalent raw materials and by reducing related energy consumption as well.
The first crediting period of the project is from 28-March-2022 to 27-March-2029. The estimated annual average GHG emission reductions are 58,871 tCO2e and the total estimated GHG emission reductions over the first crediting period are 412,097 tCO2e

name: Selva Norte Conservation Project (CSN+)
project_type: Agriculture Forestry and Other Land Use
description:
The Selva Norte Conservation project (CSN+) is a grouped REDD+ initiative developed by Projet Café Selva Norte Eleva Finca Inc and ECOTIERRA, supported by Café Selva Norte SAC, and financed by URAPI Sustainable Land Use Fund. CSN REDD+ is pioneering and unique in its kind, working with farmer communities, local governments, conservation organizations and private forest owners to enable them to access climate finance tools and consolidate their conservation efforts.

The project aims to reduce GHG emissions related to deforestation, over 200 000 ha in the department of Amazonas, Cajamarca and San Martin, in the north of Peru. The project will also contribute to consolidate an important conservation corridor and protect key ecosystems in the region.

Over the life of the project, we aim to diversify the income of more than 20 local organizations or communities. Currently, small and medium-scale conservation areas have little investment capacity and low or no income, a situation that can influence deforestation and forest degradation, thus generating loss or reduction of carbon stocks. CSN+ will make use of technical and financial tools available for conservation to generate greater benefits and create a diversified portfolio of activities, with the objective of creating a sustainable model for conservation.

CSN+ will enable the creation of a strong partnership between the communities, URAPI  and ECOTIERRA with the objective of reducing forest degradation and deforestation processes, introducing high productivity agricultural systems, ensuring the sustainable development of value chains; empowering producers, cooperatives, associations and the community in general; creating mechanisms for enforce conservation; and increase environmental awareness of the communities.

name: TTCA ORGANIC COMPOSTING PROJECT IN ATTAPEU
developer: TTC Attapeu Sugar Cane Sole Co.,Ltd
project_type: Livestock, enteric fermentation, and manure management; Waste handling and disposal
description:
TTCA Organic Composting Project in Attapeu province, Laos was constructed to produce organic fertilizer with an annual output of 34,000 tons from the treatment of cattle manure from livestock farmers in Attapeu province and from biodegradable waste residue such as Crotalaria spp. (a nitrogen fixation belonged to legume family which is used for rotation in sugarcane plantation), bagasse, mud and ash from a sugarcane processing factory in the site. The project is invested in and owned by TTC Attapeu Sugar Cane Sole Co., Ltd. The project aim is to avoid methane emissions through controlled aerobic decomposition in a windrow composting process of cattle manure, Crotalaria spp. waste and sugarcane processing waste (mud, ash, bagasse) in a landfill site.
The aerated composting process will avoid methane emissions and will also result in compost as a product that can be utilized as organic fertilizer for agricultural purposes. With financial support from the carbon credit, this project will demonstrate that the carbon credit finance mechanism can catalyze environmentally sustainable and financially viable waste management practices.
Its operation will be made sustainable by covering the installation and operation cost through sale of compost and revenue from CDM. The CDM benefits would act as a means of subsidizing the cost of compost production to ensure the project’s financial sustainability. 
The final compost obtained will be sold to organic sugarcane plantations in the province which lateral supply sugarcane to processing factory. The construction start date of the project was 28/01/2021 and was put into operation on the 16/11/2021. 
It is estimated that an average of 10,823 tCO2e emission reductions will be generated annually and total emission reductions are 108,230 tCO2e in the 10 years’ fixed crediting period.

name: 100 MW Solar PV project by ERBL, Bangladesh
description: Energon Renewables (BD) Limited (ERBL) is a special purpose vehicle (SPV) formed by Orion Group is implementing a 100MW solar PV plant near Moidhara village of Bagerhat district in the Khulna division of Bangladesh. The proposed project is a greenfield project activity. The project will achieve the greenhouse gas (GHG) emission reductions through the displacement of grid electricity which is mainly fossil-fuel dominated, by electricity generated through solar power which is a renewable source. In absence of this project activity equivalent amount of electricity would have been delivered to the grid by existing fossil fuel-based power plants or by addition of more fossil fuel based power plants. The baseline scenario of the proposed project is the same as the scenario prior to the start of the implementation of the project activity.

project_type: Agriculture Forestry and Other Land Use
description: The TAUARI REDD+ PROJECT aims to protect 21 016. 3 8 hectare s of Amazon rainforest located in Aripuanã and Juína m u nicipalities Mato Grosso State, Brazil The project promotes forest conservation and estimates to reduce 1,908,218 tCO 2 e (average of 63 ,607 tCO 2 e/year) in 30 years by A voiding U nplanned D eforestation ( in four farms which are Continental, União, Recanto do Sinuelo and Cachoeir inha.

name: One Mara Carbon Project
project_type: Agriculture Forestry and Other Land Use
description: The One Mara Carbon Project (OMCP) is an ecosystem-level conservation initiative that aims to protect ecological resources and provide economic and social co-benefits for communities by incentivizing conservancy formation and grassland restoration in the Maasai Mara landscape in Kenya. The goal of OMCP is to restore the degraded rangelands through improved grazing management and prevent further loss of grasslands by providing alternative livelihoods for communities, build resilient conservancies, ensure biodiversity conservation, and enhance tourism. This region is world-renown for the expansive rangelands where agropastoralists and wildlife co-exist. However, historical land sub-division into small, fenced land parcels and long term extensive grazing by livestock has led to land degradation, including the gradual loss in soil organic carbon (SOC). Communities living within the ecosystem depend on the condition of the grasslands to provide livelihoods that will meet their socio-economic needs. Implementing climate change mitigation measures and halting land degradation are vital to ensuring the longevity of this world-famous conservation area.

name: Guangdong Foshan Improved Forest Management Project
developer: Foshan Gaoming District Forestry Research Institute
project_type: Agriculture Forestry and Other Land Use
description: The Guangdong Foshan Improved Forest Management Project is implemented in Gaoming District, Foshan City, Guangdong Province of China by Foshan Gaoming District Forestry Research Institute. The total area is 1760.4ha, which includes the Improved Forest Management (IFM) in the conversion from logged to protected forest.

name: Energy Efficient Stoves Program (EESP) - CER Conversion
description: This small scale PoA involves the distribution of energy efficient cooking stoves to households in The Federal Democratic Republic of Ethiopia. The majority of households in rural areas of The Federal Democratic Republic of Ethiopia cook over open fires1, and this leads to a very significant consumption of wood, as well as a major health risk. To combat this problem, this PoA will distribute low cost, high efficiency stove designs that use considerably less wood than conventional open fires. Users are households who previously used inefficient, traditional open fireplaces. Deforestation and degradation have become a major concern in rural areas of Africa, as wood demand for household energy largely exceeds the available renewable woody biomass. By reducing the fuel wood consumption, the project activity hence reduces greenhouse gas emissions stemming from the use of non-renewable biomass. More information on the project can be found at CDM Project ID 9769: https://cdm.unfccc.int/ProgrammeOfActivities/poa_db/5TE6HLP1Z4KOABSDI873YQCFGXW2RM/view?cp=1
status: Units Transferred from Approved GHG Program

name: Lavardin Improved Forest Management through the Extension of Rotation Age
project_type: Agriculture Forestry and Other Land Use
description: The Lavardin IFM (Improved Forest Management) project aims to sequester carbon through improvements in the management of commercial Eucalyptus plantations in the southeastern and central-eastern region of Uruguay. The project will implement changes in the current plantation management regime, which includes two scenarios (A and B). Scenario A involves a current management of Eucalyptus globulus plantations with a 10-year harvest cycle for pulp production, covering a total planted area of 9,436 hectares. Scenario B covers a total planted area of 5,543 hectares and involves the current management of E. globulus and E. maidenii plantations with a commercial thinning at 10 years and a final harvest for high-quality wood at 20 years. The Lavardin IFM project will be implemented following the Verra Standards and is designed to have the same environmental and social impacts as all the carbon projects presented in the VCS, which sequester carbon through commercial plantations in Uruguay. Through a substantial capital investment, Lavardin will implement a unique management regime for the region (regime C) to sequester more atmospheric carbon dioxide. This new regime involves changing the species planted, selecting new ones which will increase productivity, and adjusting the rotation ages to maximize carbon sequestration and manage forests sustainably

name: Hengyang Peike Animal Manure Composting Project
developer: Hengyang Peike Ecological Technology Co., Ltd.
description:
Hengyang Peike Animal Manure Composting Project (hereafter referred to as the project) is a centralized manure treatment plant established in Hengyang County using aerobic composting system. The project collects and composts swine, chicken, and duck manure produced by livestock farms in Hengyang County to produce organic fertilizer.
The project introduces the aerobic composting system that is designed to treat swine, chicken, and duck manure from livestock farms in Hengyang County to produce organic fertilizer. The project comprises of pretreatment system, composting system, and fertilizer packaging system. It is estimated that approximately 50,000 tonnes of manure can be treated annually, and the annual organic fertilizer production is 30,000 tonnes. Part of the organic fertilizer will be sold to nearby farmers and most of it will be sold to local businesses.

name: Improved Grazing Management in Mosaic Forest - Grasslands Landscapes in the Centre-North of Argentina.
project_type: Agriculture Forestry and Other Land Use
description:
The Improved Grazing management in Mosaic Forest-Grasslands Landscapes in the centre-north of Argentina aims to remove greenhouse gases from the atmosphere by implementing regenerative grazing practices across different properties of the northern-central region of Argentina. The fundamental axis of this approach is the division of large pastures into smaller paddocks, implementing rotational grazing, which allows periods of rest and recovery for the land.
The grouped project area covers 1,212,583 km2 in the north-center of Argentina. The region is dominated by grasslands with varying degrees of tree or shrub cover, ranging from savanna ecosystems characterized by sparse tree density to mosaic landscapes of grasslands and patches of native forests. These types of ecosystems, which integrate trees, forages, and livestock, can create significant synergies that improve soil health, while sequestering significant amounts of carbon from the atmosphere.

Developing these regenerative grazing activities in areas with remnants of native trees or forests also plays and important role in the conservation of natural habitats. These productive systems mitigate climate change without the need for a change in land use, thereby safeguarding habitats that support a rich diversity of native flora and fauna. On this basis, the Project will in the future develop plans for biodiversity conservation and integration of the communities involved in each socio-ecosystem. In this way, conservation will be integrated into productive systems, encouraging landowners to change their paradigms about non-productive areas of ranches.

The first Project Activity Instance is being carried out in the “La Alicia” property, located in the province of Santa Fe. The values obtained for this PAI determined that the project activities can result in a net GHG emissions reduction and removals of ~ 231,829 tCO2e in the SOC pool, with an annual average of 11,590 tCO2e in 20 years of the project.

name: The New Zealand Transitional Afforestation Project
project_type: Agriculture Forestry and Other Land Use
description:
The New Zealand Transitional Afforestation Project is a grouped ARR; afforestation project located in New Zealand developed using the Methodology for Afforestation, Reforestation and Revegetation Projects. The grouped project area encompasses both the North and South Islands of New Zealand, with project instances geographically dispersed throughout. Project instances are predominantly properties of degraded, unproductive or erosion prone farmland or abandoned gorse land. The project will plant exotic species as a nursing crop to eventually transition into a permanent native forest. New Zealand Forestry Removals Limited (an entity within New Zealand Carbon Farming Group) either owns or has a legal right to control such properties in order to convert the plantations into protected forests, with the long-term goal of transitioning them to permanent native forest. 

As indigenous forest species in New Zealand are notoriously slow growing, difficult, and expensive to establish on bare land, an exotic nurse crop of Pinus radiata is planted for both initial rapid sequestration and to provide cover to enhance the regeneration of indigenous undergrowth. Over time the indigenous forest species are managed to succeed the exotic species through the creation of light wells, pest and predator eradication, seed island planting and gradual selective thinning of exotics. This process made possible through the financing of VCU sales.

Under the baseline scenario, business as usual management practices are assumed with the typical regional practices of extensive livestock grazing, and in some cases abandonment of degraded scrubland of invasive species which is reflective of broader land management practices in New Zealand, without carbon financing. The project scenario is conservation management activities, wherein an exotic nurse crop is established initially to provide ecosystem protection and indigenous species enhancement activities.

name: CBG GENERATION FROM MSW
developer: Indo Enviro Integrated Solutions Private Limited
project_type: Energy industries (renewable/non-renewable sources); Waste handling and disposal
description:
The project activity aims to improve municipal solid waste (MSW) management through the
installation of an anaerobic digestion system to generate Compressed Biogas (CBG) in the city
of Indore, Madhya Pradesh in India. The installed capacity of the project is to treat 500TPD of
segregated MSW to generate approx. 42,500 N-m3/day of CBG. CBG generated is purified and
processed for various thermal applications such as use in vehicles use for transportation or
bottled for use in Industrial energy applications. Technical details of the equipment installed
in the project are provided in section 1.11 of this PD.
The project is implemented by Indo Enviro Integrated Solutions Private Limited (IEISL). The
project is commissioned on 22-May-2022 and is in operation since.
In the absence of the project activity, MSW would be left to decay in the landfill site without
any controlled treatment and such decay would lead to methane emission, a greenhouse gas,
into the atmosphere. CBG generated in the project is a direct replacement of fossil fuels (e.g.
CNG) used in the baseline. CNG combustion in the baseline would have resulted into CO2
emissions.

name: The New Zealand Indigenous Forest Regeneration Project
project_type: Agriculture Forestry and Other Land Use
description: The New Zealand Indigenous Forest Regeneration Project is an Improved Forest Management, Logged to Protected Forest (LtPF) project located in New Zealand that was developed using the VM0012 methodology. The project is a grouped project, with the project area encompassing both the North and South Islands of New Zealand, with project instances geographically dispersed throughout. Project instances predominantly include properties of Pinus radiata plantations that were established with the objective of harvesting the timber for commercial purposes. New Zealand Forestry Removals Limited (an entity within the New Zealand Carbon Farming Group) will either own or have a legal right to control, such properties in order to convert the plantations into protected forests, with the long-term goal of transitioning them to permanent native forest.

name: CBG Plant at Sainsons
description: The purpose of project activity is extraction and capture of methane enriched bio-gas generated from treatment of waste water. The captured biogas is treated further to remove impurities and bottled as compressed biogas to supply to oil company for replacing fossil origin natural gas used in vehicles for transportation. In case any shutdown of CBG plant excess methane gas will be flared in controlled manner in an open flare.

name: Muyuan Bengbu AWMS GHG Mitigation Project in Anhui Province
project_type: Energy industries (renewable/non-renewable sources); Livestock, enteric fermentation, and manure management; Waste handling and disposal
description:
Muyuan Bengbu AWMS GHG Mitigation Project in Anhui Province (hereafter referred to as the project) installs new animal waste management systems (AWMSs) to treat the manure from swine farms in Bengbu City, Anhui Province, China, which are owned by Muyuan Foods Co.,Ltd. Each subsidiary swine farm shall install one AWMS, and the manure is treated on site. The purpose of the project activity is to treat the manure and wastewater to avoid methane emissions generated in the baseline uncovered anaerobic lagoons.
All the manure and wastewater are collected and then be separated first. The solid will be treated in aerobic composting system and the organic fertilizers will be produced, the fertilizer produced in this process will be distributed to local farmers for free and the surplus will be sold in domestic market. The liquid will be treated through anaerobic digestion and the biogas released during the anaerobic digestion will be partly used as fuel for the canteens of swine farms, partly for the biogas boiler for the feedlot, and the remaining biogas will be flared. The sludge produced from anaerobic digestion will be treated through aerobic composting together with the solid, the effluent will be supplied to the farmers living around free for agriculture irrigation.
It is estimated that approximately 266.590 tons of animal manure will be handled daily by the AWMSs. The biogas released during the anaerobic digestion will be partly used as fuel for the canteens of swine farms, partly for the biogas boiler for the feedlot, and the remaining biogas will be flared. For conservativeness, baseline emissions from heat generation are neglected.
The project activity will reduce GHG in the atmosphere through avoiding methane emissions from anaerobic treatment of swine manure and wastewater. It is estimated that 240,368 tCO2e emission reductions will be attained annually.

The liquid will be treated through anaerobic digestion and the biogas released during the anaerobic digestion will be partly used as fuel for the canteens of swine farms, partly for the biogas boiler for the feedlot, and the remaining biogas will be flared. The sludge produced from anaerobic digestion will be treated through aerobic composting together with the solid, the effluent will be supplied to the farmers living around free for agriculture irrigation.
It is estimated that approximately 582.0532 tons of animal manure will be handled daily by the AWMSs. The biogas released during the anaerobic digestion will be partly used as fuel for the canteens of swine farms, partly for the biogas boiler for the feedlot, and the remaining biogas will be flared. For conservativeness, baseline emissions from heat generation are neglected.
The project activity will reduce GHG in the atmosphere through avoiding methane emissions from anaerobic treatment of swine manure and wastewater. It is estimated that 528,261 tCO2e emission reductions will be attained annually.
