name: Wudi Lvhe Composting project
developer: Wudi County Lvhe Organic Fertilizer Co., Ltd.
project_type: Livestock, enteric fermentation, and manure management; Waste handling and disposal
description:
Wudi Lvhe Composting project (hereinafter as “the project”) installs a set of organic fertilizersproduction lines with an annual output of 50,000 tones to treat the manure from the cattle 
farms in Wudi Country, Binzhou city, Shandong Province, China. The project is owned by WudiCounty Lvhe Organic Fertilizer Co., LTD. The purpose of the project activity is to avoid methane
emissions through controlled aerobic treatment by composting of manure and microbial strains.In absence of the project, all manure waste produced was left to decay in uncovered anaerobic 
lagoons, which is the most economic, viable and reasonable for livestock farm owners.In this project, the collected cattle manure will be utilized through a fermentation composting 
process. After the fermentation, both solids and wastewater are then treated by a fertilizer production system, of which can produce organic fertilizers used for application to lands. Without 
this project, the farms in project areas remain conditions of uncovered anaerobic lagoons that may bring a larger amount of GHG emissions sent to the atmosphere.
During the implementation of the project, it is estimated that about 165,000 tons of cattle manure would be treated and composted, with 50,000 tons of organic fertilizer generated per 
year. Besides, the GHG emissions is expected to reduce 57,116 t CO2e per year and 571,160 tCO2e in a 10-year crediting period.

name: TIST Program in Kenya, VCS-011
project_type: Agriculture Forestry and Other Land Use
description: Since its inception in 1999, over 170,000 participants organized into over 26,000 TIST Small Groups have planted over 25 million trees in Tanzania, India, Kenya, and Uganda - accomplishing GhG sequestration through tree planting, creating a potential long-term income stream, and developing sustainable environments and livelihoods. Kenya 011 is a subset of the TIST project in Kenya and applies to 12,892 Small Groups, 79,089 Participants, 53,357 active Project Areas, and 23,747 hectares.  TIST farmers use a mosaic restoration approach, planting on thousands of individual farms spread across the landscape. The individual farms are found throughout Kenya and concentrated around Mt Kenya.

name: Fortaleza Ituxi II REDD+
project_type: Agriculture Forestry and Other Land Use
description: The Fortaleza Ituxi II REDD+ Project aims at protecting private forests located in one of the regions having the highest deforestation rate in the Amazon Biome: the municipality of Lábrea. The south region of the municipality of Lábrea has already been reached by the “Arc of Deforestation”: for the last 10 years, Lábrea has been one of the most deforested municipalities in the Amazon Biome. Besides the damage caused to natural ecosystems, the land-use changes have provoked severe social conflicts through processes of land-grabbing and installation of agriculture and cattle ranching activities, contributing to the expulsion of family-scale forest extractives from that region. The primary objective of the Fortaleza Ituxi II REDD+ Project is to avoid planned (APD) and unplanned (AUD) deforestation in an area of 69,185.87 ha of Amazonian forest. The APD REDD project area is expected to avoid a predicted 5,153.00 ha of legal deforestation, equating to 1,721,301 tCO2e in emissions reductions over the 30-year project lifetime, an annual average of 57,376 tCO2e. The AUD REDD project area is expected to avoid a predicted 64,023.44 ha of illegal deforestation, equating to 16,066,567 tCO2e in emissions reductions over the 30-year project lifetime, with an annual average of 535,552 tCO2e.

name: Lishu Blackland Conservation Project in Jilin Province
developer: Jilin Kangfu Environmental Energy Co., Ltd.
project_type: Agriculture Forestry and Other Land Use
description:
Heilongjiang Lishu Improved Agricultural Land Management Project (hereafter referred to as “the project”) is located in Lishu County, Jilin Province, China. The purpose of the project is to adopt improved agricultural land management practices including no tillage/reduced tillage，returning straw in fields and applying organic fertilizer, and to prevent the severe soil degradation caused by pre-existing conventional tillage in local crop land.
Since straw contains a large amount of organic matter and trace elements such as nitrogen, phosphorus, and potassium, returning straw to the field can effectively use organic fertilizer resources and increase soil organic matter (SOM). Straw returning to the field also can improve soil physical and chemical properties, enhance soil aggregate structure, and increase soil permeability. Applying organic fertilizer can reduce nitrous oxide emission compared to synthetic fertilizer.
The project plans to implement no tillage/reduced tillage practice, straw returning and organic fertilizer application in 15,385 ha of agricultural land in the first crediting period to increase soil organic carbon (SOC) and reduce nitrous oxide emission. The project proponent not only introduced more efficient and appropriate tillage method with Lishu County Agriculture and Rural Affairs Bureau to the farmers, but also provide technical training and support to the farmers.
The scenario existing prior to the project’s implementation is primarily conventional tillage without straw returning, which cause greater soil disturbance and increase the loss of SOM.
During the first crediting period from 20-Nov-2022 to 19-Nov-2042, the project is expected to generate GHG emission removals of 1,110,180 tCO2e, with an average annual GHG emission removal of 55,509 tCO2e.

name: AGROFORESTRY PLANTATIONS TO ENHANCE THE LIVELIHOOD OF RURAL COMMUNITIES IN INDIA
project_type: Agriculture Forestry and Other Land Use
description: The project is an initiative of various NGOS for the plantation activities. IICare Foundation is the aggregator and would act as the project proponent. The plantation activities are based in India. Project aims to plant 1 million trees which will contribute in carbon sequestration and promote the message of ‘green living’ among local community. The project plans the introduction of trees to farms and other landscapes for multiple productive purposes which could play a key role in climate change mitigation and adaptation and help increase tree cover at the selected sites. The project started in August 2020. The project encompasses scattered parcels of land measuring about 800 hectares distributed in 14 Indian states namely Uttarakhand, West Bengal, Odisha, Tamil Nadu, Maharashtra, Gujarat, Telangana, Uttar Pradesh, Madhya Pradesh, Assam, Rajasthan and Haryana with over 60% on aggregate basis in just two western states of Maharashtra and Gujarat.

name: Regeneration Meghalaya
project_type: Agriculture Forestry and Other Land Use
description: The Regeneration Meghalaya Project is a grouped project under ARR (Afforestation, Reforestation, and Revegetation) category that aims to increase tree cover through planting a majority of indigenous trees that are suited to local conditions of the bioregion. The project is located in the Khasi, Ri Bhoi Jaintia and Garo Hills regions, in the Northeastern state of Meghalaya, India. Regeneration Meghalaya will plant trees across up to 30,000 ha of wasteland. The project aims to plant up to 40 - 64 million trees sequestering up to 23 Million tonnes of CO2e in Meghalaya. In addition, the project aims to reach a significant number of beneficiaries over a period of 35 years. The GHG (greenhouse gas) removals in the project would be created by improving the land though planting new trees and plants in the eligible project areas. The project’s broader aims are to restore ecological integrity, reduce soil erosion, improve ecological functions, increase biodiversity and improve livelihoods. In this regard, the project will monitor and report on the co-benefits for climate adaptation, biodiversity and people through the climate, community and biodiversity standard (CCB). The project taps into and is led by indigenous knowledge custodians to accelerate landscape restoration and sustainably develop both tree-based and non-tree based products to create value chains and grow sustainable livelihoods. The project goals are aligned to the local needs and existing land use systems, farmer-led species selection that prioritise indigenous and naturalised species, and customised solutions to challenges identified by local stakeholders. The project area is home to the Khasi, Jaintia and Garo tribes, and the majority of the land is held under private / clan ownership, with some community control and management.

name: Trees for Livelihood in Madhya Pradesh, India
developer: Value Network Ventures Advisory Services PTE. LTD
project_type: Agriculture Forestry and Other Land Use
description: The objective of the project is to increase the tree cover outside forest (ToF) areas through ARR activities on privately owned lands of farmers who belong to the local communities. Some plantation is also undertaken on common lands under the village or Gram Panchayat if the GP wishes to include the same. Apart from ARR activities, the project also works closely with the communities to address livelihoods. The project aims to secure the financial security of the local farming and other communities through planting of farmer friendly trees to support traditional crop-based agriculture systems and through support through supplementary community-based interventions. The PP implements the project through service providers, who work closely with farmers to assess willingness to participate in the project, engage them in project activities and undertake project activities with high levels of participation from the local communities. The project team on the ground are employed from the local community, and care is taken to ensure participation of women and other marginalized members of the community.

name: PROJECT FOR VERMICOMPOSTING OF LIVESTOCK MANURE IN CHHATTISGARH, INDIA
project_type: Livestock, enteric fermentation, and manure management; Waste handling and disposal
description:
Gauthans are village-based cow-dung processing premises that have emerged as multi-activity centres supporting vermicomposting production and livelihood-based activities for Self-help groups in the Chhattisgarh state of India. The avoidance of methane emissions is achieved with treatments of aerobic composting with the help of Worms, which replaces the baseline scenario where the manure would undergo anaerobic decomposition conditions. 

In this project, the collected cattle manure is utilised through a composting process with the help of Worms. Worms convert the cattle manure aerobically into vermicompost used for application to lands.  Without this project, the farms in project areas remain conditions of uncovered anaerobic lagoons that may bring a larger amount of GHG emissions sent to the atmosphere.

Utilising cattle manure for vermicompost preparation has the primary benefit of reduced methane emission along with secondary benefit of replacing fertilisers in farm inputs which contribute for emission reduction. During the implementation of the project, it is estimated that about 117,000 tons of dairy manure would be treated and composted, with 30,000tons of organic fertiliser generated per year. Besides, the GHG emissions are expected to reduce 59918 tCO2e per year and 419424 tCO2e in a 7-year crediting period.

name: Shandong Ju County ALM Project
project_type: Agriculture Forestry and Other Land Use
description:
Shandong Ju County ALM Project (hereafter as “the project”) is located in Ju County, Rizhao City, Shandong Province of China. The goal of this initiative is to reduce the carbon emissions currently emitted by the farms taking part to the project and raise the carbon storage in the soil. In addition, the selected measures will contribute to improving crop yields and soil health. The project was implemented by the Ju County Urban Construction Investment Group Co.,Ltd. and Hainan icarbon Ecological Development Co.,Ltd. (hereafter “the project proponent”).
The proposed project is aimed to prevent the soil degradation through adoption of the improved crop land management practices (collectively referred to conservational tillage) to replace the conventional cultivation mode.
Main activities about conservational tillage adopted in the project include： 
Organic fertilizer application (reduce inorganic fertilizer application): 53,422 ha of cropland has reduced the use of chemical fertilizer.
Straw incorporation (Improve crop residue management): straw in 53,422 ha of cropland has been buried and returned, with the depth of 30 cm.
A total of 53,422 ha of farmland has been managed under conservation tillage, The project is estimated to generate GHG emission removals of 2,684,200 tCO2e from 01-Jan-2021 to 31-Dec- 2040, with an average annual GHG emission removal of 134,210 tCO2e.
For the project the validation date and the specific date of the first monitoring period of this project has not been determined, and will be supplemented in the latest PD.

name: ESTIMATION OF THE GHG EMISSIONS OF THE GRUPO TRANSPORTES MONTERREY S.A.P.I. DE C.V. VEHICLE FLEET
description:
Grupo Transportes Monterrey S.A.P.I. de C.V (GTM) is a company in the road freight transportation sector in Mexico, where the baseline scenario is the situation where, in the absence of project activity, the fleet used for freight transportation in the different routes does not change in technology or type of fuel. Throughout the project, cargo is transported using less GHG-intensive modes of transport.
The baseline considers a fleet growth of 12.5%. The existing fleet has 94% Diesel vehicles and 6% compressed natural gas (CNG), which is maintained throughout the period. According to the methodology, the average tons transported annually, and the total distance traveled are considered.
The project includes re-newing vehicles from the existing fleet, with vehicles with better technology in both fuel efficiency and emission control, maintaining the CNG-Diesel vehicle composition and the annual growth of the baseline.
According to the methodology, the project boundary includes the following: Fleet to which low-emission vehicles are introduced:
a)	The geographical area in which these vehicles operate.
b)	Auxiliary facilities such as fueling stations, workshops, and service stations that are used by vehicles.
The conditions which govern the operation of the fleet (e.g., tariffs, regulations) should be homogeneous within the project boundary. The origin and end points of the routes carried out, where complete coverage is observed in Mexico, reaching the 32 states.
Baseline emissions are calculated as per the consolidated Methodology AMS III.S version 04.0.
The annual estimated emission reductions are 67,775 tCO2/yr. The total emission reductions for the period of 10 years of crediting years are 677,553 tCO2.

name: 14 MW Waste-to-Energy Project by Antony Lara Renewable Energy Pvt. Ltd
developer: Antony Lara Renewable Energy Pvt. Ltd
project_type: Energy industries (renewable/non-renewable sources); Waste handling and disposal
description:
The project activity is 14MW Waste to Energy Power Plant located at Moshi Kachara Depot, Pimpri, Pune, India. The plant utilizes Refuse-Derived Fuel (“RDF”) as feedstock derived from the separation and sorting of Municipal Solid Waste (“MSW”) excluding the recyclable or potentially hazardous materials from the waste stream. The MSW will be sourced from the Pimpri Chinchwad Municipality area as per the concession agreement with Pimpri Chinchwad Municipal Corporation.
The main purpose of this project activity is to generate clean form of electricity through waste to energy-based power generation. The project will treat about 700 ton of RDF per day and generate electricity with the installed capacity of 14 MW. The project activity helps to avoid methane emissions from open dump site iand generate renewable electricity, which displaced part of the electricity otherwise supplied by grid connected power plants. The expected average emission reduction from the project is 65,318 tCO2e annually.

name: Shunfeng Erhai Composting project in Yousuo
developer: Dali Erhai Biological Fertilizer Co., Ltd.
project_type: Livestock, enteric fermentation, and manure management; Waste handling and disposal
description:
Shunfeng Erhai Composting project in Yousuo (hereinafter as “the project”) designed to construct an organic fertilizer factory in Songqu Village, Yousuo Town, Eryuan County, Dali Bai Autonomous Prefecture, Yunnan Province, China. The project is owned by Dali Erhai Biological Fertilizer Co., Ltd. The purpose of the project activity is to avoid methane emissions through controlled aerobic treatment by composting of manure.
In absence of the project, all manure waste produced was left to decay in uncovered anaerobic lagoons, which is the most economic, viable and reasonable for livestock farm owners, and methane would emit to the atmosphere.
The project is designed to treat livestock manure collected from Niujie Town, Sanyin Town, Zhibi Lake Town, Fengyu Town, Yousuo Town and Dengchuan Town to produce organic fertilizer in Songqu Village. The proposed comprises of composting system and fertilizer packaging system. It is estimated that about 168,088 tons of cattle manure, 127,688 tons of swine manure, 8,842 tons of chicken manure and 66,960 tons of straw will be treated to produce 200,000 tons of organic fertilizer annually. The organic fertilizer produced will be sold to local government, farmers and businesses. Without this project, the manure produced in these farms in project areas remain conditions of uncovered anaerobic lagoons that may bring a larger amount of GHG emissions sent to the atmosphere.
The project activity will reduce GHG in the atmosphere by avoiding methane emissions through controlled aerobic treatment of organic waste. During the implementation of the project, it is estimated that about 57,435 tCO2e emission reductions will be generated annually, and total 574,350 tCO2e in a 10-year crediting period.

name: Kwango River Project, Democratic Republic of Congo
location: Congo, The Democratic Republic of The
project_type: Agriculture Forestry and Other Land Use
description:
This afforestation project, set up in anthropogenic savannahs on the Batéké Plateau east of Kinshasa, aims to develop carbon sink plantations, i.e. plantations where wood is little or no harvested, in order to maximize greenhouse gas sequestration in the long term. The majority of the project's area will therefore be dedicated to forest plantations with this main objective. Another objective of these forest plantations will be the timber production: some trees will be cut down very selectively in order to maintain the constant volume of the forest stand over time, while sustainably a local timber sector, replacing informal logging of natural forests. We also know that another effective tool to combat deforestation is an alternative and renewable source of charcoal for urban use and agricultural products, based on the establishment of agroforestry plantations (trees rows will be intercropped with lines of food crops).
As a result, the Project will have several social and environmental benefits such as (1) CO2 sequestration on land that is currently non-forested and unused, (2) Less pressure on the surrounding natural forests, thanks to the production of charcoal and timber from sustainably managed plantations, and the sensitization of local populations to agroforestry, that is more sustainable and productive than slash-and-burn agriculture or (3) Job creation, increased incomes and local development in a territory heavily affected by unemployment.
In this project, we account for the removals of GHG that occurred through the creation of the plantations: we use the UNFCCC AR-ACM0003 CDM methodology and the VCS Guidance AFOLU Guidance: Example for Calculating the Long-Term Average Carbon Stock for ARR Projects with Harvesting (Version of the 8 March 2011). The project plans to generate carbon credits for the voluntary market under the VCS standard. The first accreditation period is 30 years. The sequestration of GHG is estimated at 5,000,075 tCO2-e.

name: GER Recycled PP Project
description:
GER Recycled PP Project (hereinafter called “the Project”) aims to recycled PP plastic particles by using waste PP products (like packaging bags, sheeting, pipes, household daily necessities etc.) and to replace the same PP produced from the raw materials. The Project located at Fengcheng Circular Economy Park, Yichun District, Fengcheng City, Jiangxi Province, China and is developed and operated by Jiangxi Green Recycling Co.,Ltd. (hereinafter called “The Project Proponent”).
Prior to the project implementation, the same amount of PP particles would be produced from raw materials (crude oil and natural gas) which is also the baseline scenario of the project. Therefore, the GHG emission reduction will be generated through the implementation of the project by avoiding the consumption of the equivalent raw materials and reducing related energy consumption as well. The project has started constructed since 03/2021, and the date of production line putting into operation is 31/12/2021.
The project activity will reduce GHG in the atmosphere through an avoiding extraction of raw materials and production of virgin materials. It is estimated that the project will result a total of 137,200 tCO2e emission reductions in the first crediting period of 7 years and with annual average of 19,600 tCO2e emission reduction in the 1st crediting period.

name: PANÃMA REDD+ PROJECT
project_type: Agriculture Forestry and Other Land Use
description: The Panãma REDD+ Project is a partnership between Biofílica Investimentos Ambientais S.A.  Fundação Jari and Jari Celulose, with the purpose of promoting forest conservation and reducing potential greenhouse gas emissions (GHG) based on a model of local economic development that values the “standing forest” through the integration of Sustainable Forest Management activities and the commercialization of environmental services. The Project is located in three municipalities: Almeirim, in the State of Pará, and Laranjal do Jari/Vitória do Jarí, in the State of Amapá. There is a very important role in this region as it serves as a home for many rural families and as an ecological corridor, with several Conservation Units (CUs) in its vicinity. It has a very rich biodiversity, its vegetation includes ten forest and non-forest formations and species of extreme ecological and social importance.

name: Hainan Jinhua IFM(Coversion of logged to protected forest)  Project
project_type: Agriculture Forestry and Other Land Use
description:
The Hainan Jinhua IFM (conversion of logged to protected forest) Project is implemented in Hainan Province of China by Hainan Jinhua Forestry Co., Ltd. 
In recent years, Hainan has been promoting the construction of tropical rainforest national parks and increasing the ecological restoration of tropical rainforests. In order to support Hainan's tropical rainforest protection and biodiversity conservation, since 01-Sep-2020, Hainan Jinhua Forestry Co., Ltd has taken the initiative to incorporate part of the company's forest land into the Hainan Tropical Rainforest National Park. Since the launch of Hainan Tropical Rainforest National Park, logging has been stopped in the protected area to achieve forest protection. The area of forest land allocated to Hainan Jinhua Forestry Co., Ltd is about 14,600 ha, including two tree species,  eucalyptus and Acacia mangium. Of these, the Acacia mangium forest land is involved in the the Improved Forest Management (IFM) project of the forests in the conversion of logged to protected forest.
The area of the project activity is 4863 ha, including 126 subcompartments spreading over Baisha, Baoting, Changjiang, Ledong, Lingshui, Qiongzhong, WuzhiMountain. All these departments are 100% owned by Hainan Jinhua Forestry Co., Ltd and have the legal right to forest ownership. The specie involved in the project is Acacia mangium. This is common local tree species.
Prior to the implementation of the project activity, Hainan Jinhua Forestry Co., Ltd harvested trees in the project area in accordance with a valid timber management plan approved by the government.
The implementation of the project activity converses the trees to protected forest to reduce the GHG emissions for about 3,187,713 tCO2e in 30 years, the average annual emission reduction is 106,257 tCO2e and Verified Carbon Units with buffer deduction is about 2,486,416 tCO2e in 30 years, the average annual VCUs with buffer deduction is 82,881 tCO2e.

name: Halmahera Zero-Waste Renewable Energy and Biochar Project
project_type: Energy industries (renewable/non-renewable sources); Waste handling and disposal
description:
The project activity is a combination of several waste management activities with purpose to valorize the coconut husks waste. The coconut husks waste biomass is fed into a gasification system to produce electricity and biochar. While the electricity is supplied to the coconut factory at the same location, the biochar is sold as soil enhancer for the surrounded coconut plantations. Through these activities, the project will avoid emitting CH4 to the atmosphere, producing renewable energy, and remove carbon through application of biochar as soil enhancer.

The new biomass gasification plant project will generate 1 MWe for its coconut processing plant in West Halmahera, North Maluku. The proposed project involves installing a gasifier unit and two internal combustion engines with a 1.0 MW installed capacity. Considering 24 hours of operation per day and 350 days of operation per year, the expected annual power generation is 8.400 MWh of electricity which will be absorbed by the coconut processing plant. The gasification process will produce biochar as the by-product, distributed as soil enricher for the farmers.

The Project Proponent plans to upgrade the coconut plant capacity to 200.000 coconuts per day after four years of stable production with increasing product demand. Following the plant capacity increase, biomass gasification would be upgraded to 2 MWe.

name: WEIYUAN COMPOSTING PROJECT
project_type: Livestock, enteric fermentation, and manure management; Waste handling and disposal
description: Weiyuan Composting Project (hereafter referred to as the project) installs a set of organic fertilizer production lines with an annual capacity of 50,000 tons to treat swine manure from swine farms and biomass waste residue (straw) in Weiyuan County, Neijiang City, Sichuan Province, China. The project is invested and owned by Sichuan Zhengwei Industry Co., Ltd. The purpose of the project activity is to avoid methane emissions through controlled aerobic treatment by composting of manure and biomass waste residue. This project comprises of fermentation system and fertilizer production system. It is estimated that approximately 102,000 tonnes of manure and 35,000 tonnes of biomass waste residue can be treated annually, therefore total 137,000 tonnes of waste can be composted aerobically for this project. A portion of the organic fertilizer obtained is sold to the local government for improving the quality of local high-standard farmland, and another portion is sold to local farmers, farmer cooperatives and businesses. The construction start date of the project is 21 July 2020 and was put into operation on 1 January 2022. The project activity will reduce of GHG in the atmosphere through avoiding methane emissions from controlled aerobic treatment by composting of manure and biomass residue. It is estimated that 59,518 tCO2e emission reductions will be generated annually and total emission reductions are 595,175 tCO2e in the 10 years’ fixing crediting period.

name: One Earth Fund BEC Compost Project 2022
description: One Earth Fund BEC-2022 will reduce emissions and reduce landfill inputs through composting residential and commercial food waste.
methodology: Climate Action Reserve Landfill Project Protocol

name: Hubei Longshen Composting Project
project_type: Livestock, enteric fermentation, and manure management; Waste handling and disposal
description:
Hubei Longshen Composting project (hereinafter as “the project”) employs aerobic composting
systems on organic fertilizer factory in Jianli City, Jingzhou City, Hubei Province, China. The
project is owned by Hubei Longshen fertilizer Co., Ltd. The avoidance of methane emissions
could be achieved with treatments of aerobic composting, which replaces the baseline scenario
where the swine manure and chicken manure would undergo an anaerobic decomposition
condition.
In absence of the project, all manure waste produced was left to decay in uncovered anaerobic
lagoons, which is the most economic, viable and reasonable for livestock farm owners, and
methane would emit to the atmosphere. The project introduces the aerobic composting system to treat livestock manure produced
around Jianli City, the project was designed to produce 14,000 tons of organic fertilizer by
treating 140,000 tons of livestock manure and 10,000 tons of straw. The organic fertilizer
produced will be sold to local farmers and businesses. Without this project, the farms in project
areas remain conditions of uncovered anaerobic lagoons that may bring a larger amount of
GHG emissions sent to the atmosphere. The project activity will reduce GHG in the atmosphere by avoiding methane emissions through
controlled aerobic treatment of organic waste. During the implementation of the project, it is
estimated that about 59,514 tCO2e emission reductions will be generated annually, and total
595,140 tCO2e in a 10-year crediting period.

name: Qinghai Gangcha Improved Grassland Management Project
developer: Gangcha County Urban and Rural Investment Development Co., Ltd
project_type: Agriculture Forestry and Other Land Use
description: Qinghai Gangcha Improved Grassland Management Project (hereafter referred to as “the project”) is located in Haibei Mongol and Tibetan Autonomous Prefecture, Qinghai Province, China. The project aims to restore 64,200 hectares (or 963,000 Mu) degraded grasslands in Gangcha by adopting a variety of measures including grass seeding, rotational grazing and rest grazing. The project will increase carbon sequestration, reverse grassland degradation, contribute to local development and preserve cultural traditions.

name: KOSHER BLUE CARBON -1
project_type: Agriculture Forestry and Other Land Use
description:
The proposed Project activity intends to restore degraded mangrove habitats in the Indian Sundarbans region.  The project activity plans to restore up to 3,000 hectares of degraded mangrove ecosystems in phased manner through the plantation of diverse native mangrove tree species. The project activity is being implemented in the Indian part of Sundarbans delta situated in the West Bengal state of India. The project is implemented by the proponent in collaboration with the project implementing partner organization, site specific ground partners, and the local communities. The project activity will ensure the active participation of women in various stages of project implementation and post implementation management of the project interventions

By restoring the degraded mangrove land with the native tree species, the project activity will remove atmospheric carbon dioxide through biological carbon sequestration in the tree biomass and in the soil there by avoiding the equivalent amount of GHG emissions which would have not been occurred in the pre-project scenario as the land remains degraded land with no carbon sequestration.

name: FST SMALL-SCALE SOLAR POWER PLANT IN KAMPHAENG PHET, THAILAND
description:
The FST solar project consists of the installation of solar photovoltaic power plants with a capacity of 9.98 MWp, located in Kamphaeng Phet Province, Thailand. 

Petroleum exploration and production required significant amounts of electricity use, baseline technology to produce electricity generate large amount of greenhouse gas (GHGs) emissions such as fossil-fuel power plant which use natural gas, diesel, and other fossil fuels used to generate electricity. The displacement of fossil fuel with solar power generation will generate GHGs emission reductions by replacing fossil fuels with renewable energy sources such as solar power. The project involves the installation of solar photovoltaic (PV) panels, which generate clean electricity without emitting GHGs emissions. In contrast, the use of fossil fuels for power generation produces significant GHGs emissions that contribute to climate change.  

Moreover, the excess solar energy generated will be stored in batteries, reducing the reliance on fossil fuel-based power generation. This will further reduce GHGs emissions associated with power generation. 

Overall, the replacement of fossil fuels with solar power generation projects will generate significant GHGs emissions reductions, contributing to fight against climate change. 

The annual emissions reduction is 13,061.87 tCO2e/annum.

name: An Qiu Biogas Utilization Project
project_type: Energy industries (renewable/non-renewable sources); Waste handling and disposal
description: The project recovers biogas from the wastewater generated in citric acid, corn flour, and protein production process and use the biogas to generate electricity and heat for TTCA Co. The project site includes two connected areas. The east area includes two generators, and the west area includes four generators.

name: REDD Carbon and Biodiversity Project, Greater El Rey Area, Jujuy, Argentina
project_type: Agriculture Forestry and Other Land Use
description:
Tropical rain forests with their rich fauna and flora are threatened worldwide from deforestation and forest degradation. In Argentina, deforestation rates are particularly high, caused mainly by conversion of forests to expand soy and beef production. Wintershall Dea AG, VisionNetZero GmbH and Banco de Bosques have joined forces to develop REDD+ carbon projects to conserve large forest patches with a high biodiversity in the Northwestern region of Argentina. 
The project intends to protect and conserve 24,154 hectares that are part of the Yungas forests in northwest Argentina. The main project activity is taking the property off the market to prevent agricultural development and conserve its high carbon values, rich biodiversity, and critical ecosystem functionality by avoiding planned deforestation and forest degradation. Therefore, the project intends a joint certification with CCB Standard.
The project will deliver significant carbon as well as non-carbon benefits by conserving the natural forest ecosystems of the Yungas, one of the most biodiverse natural systems in Argentina and home to nearly 50% of the country's biodiversity. Through the income of carbon revenues, forest areas with high conservation value can be purchased and conserved by donating and integrating them into national or provincial protection systems.
The development of REDD+ carbon projects contribute to climate change mitigation by reducing greenhouse gas emissions (GHG) from forest loss and forest degradation. The number of generated credits is estimated based on the comparison of the projected baseline and the effectiveness of the project activities targeting the drivers of deforestation and degradation. In the project area that would be protected, the weighted average of tons of carbon dioxide per hectare (tCO2/ha) is 884 tCO2/ha. On that basis, up to 1.8 Mio. VCUs can be expected within the duration of the project (30 years).

name: BATIKIPAS BIOGAS PLANT
developer: Batıkipaş Kağıt San. Ve Tic. A.Ş.
project_type: Energy industries (renewable/non-renewable sources); Waste handling and disposal
description: BATIKIPAS BIOGAS PLANT is located in Söke district of Aydın, Türkiye. The proposed project activity includes installation of anaerobic wastewater treatment plant to  generate biogas from wastewater of the paper mill. Installed capacity of project is planned to be 6.168 MWm.

name: Enhancing Livelihoods of Farmers in Gujarat through Agroforestry Plantations by SHBVM
project_type: Agriculture Forestry and Other Land Use
description:
The projected ARR VCS initiative aims to help farmers in Gujarat, India, by providing them with additional income via the sale of carbon credits created by agroforestry tree crops on their land.
Shri Hari Bhujal Vikash Mandal (SHBVM), the project's co-proponent, has supported farmers in providing quality planting material for agroforestry species. They also provide on-site help to farmers who have registered with them for plantation maintenance. The project is being implemented in six Gujarat districts: Chhota Udepur, Mahisagar, Vadodara, Bharuch, Aravalli, and Panchmahal. Roughly 15 million seedlings will be planted on an area of around 4,000 hectares.

name: Carbon Emission Reduction Project through Improved Water Management in Bio-farming
project_type: Agriculture Forestry and Other Land Use
description:
According to information from the Ministry of the Environment of Japan, total GHG emissions from the agricultural sector in Japan in 2018 were about 32.3 million t-CO2eq. Of these, emissions from rice cultivation were the largest, at approximately 12 million t-CO2eq. , accounting for 38.2% of total emissions. The implementation of this project will reduce emissions by tCO2eq. per year and contribute to the reduction of GHG emissions from these agricultural activities.
At this project, we use VM0042 to reduce CH4 by using no pesticides, no fertilizers, and by drying the soil in the middle of the year. As for environmental impact, the absence of chemical fertilizers reduces most of the nitrous oxide generated from the soil and the carbon dioxide produced during the production and transportation of fertilizers, and the absence of animal-based fertilizers eliminates concerns about methane emissions from the fertilizer production process.

name: Varanasi Harit Koyla Pariyojna
project_type: Energy industries (renewable/non-renewable sources); Waste handling and disposal
description: The project activity involves setting up and operation of a Municipal Solid Waste (MSW) to Torrefied Charcoal Pellets manufacturing facility by NTPC Vidyut Vyapar Nigam Ltd (NVVN) in Varanasi, Uttar Pradesh State, India. MSW collected from local Varanasi Municipal Corporation will be used to manufacture the Torrefied Charcoal Pellets; which shall then be supplied via Onward sale agreement to nearby operating coal fired power plant as replacement substitution for coal. The project will dispose of 600 TPD Fresh MSW to convert to 400TPD of Torrefied Charcoal for further use as fuel in power plant.

name: Nam Houng - 1 Hydro Power Project
developer: Nam Houng - 1 Hydro Power Co., Ltd
description:
Nam Houng - 1 Hydro Power Project is developed by Simoung Group Co., Ltd in Xayabouly province, Lao PDR. The primary purpose of the project is to generate electricity to the Lao Power Grid. The project activity is a run-off river hydro power project with a total installed capacity of 15 MW. The project is promoted by Simoung Group Co., Ltd. Project is expected to commission on 01/10/2023 with a expected net annual generation of 87,280 MWh.
The baseline scenario of the project is continuation of the present situation, i.e electricity supplied from the power grid. By displacing part of the power generated by thermal power plants, the project is therefore expected to reduce equivalant CO2 emissions from he grid connected power plants.

name: Biogas-based Manure Management Program
project_type: Energy industries (renewable/non-renewable sources); Waste handling and disposal
description: The proposed project activity involves methane recovery through controlled anaerobic digestion of animal waste (cow dung) and utilization of recovered methane (biogas) for thermal energy and electricity generation in the dairy plant. The project plans to install two centralized anaerobic bio-digesters having capacities of 2000m3/day each, a total of 4000 m3/day and two number of 125KVA capacity biogas-based electrical engine.  The proposed plant will treat about 100 MT/day of animal manure per day sourced from nearby farmers or aggregators. The project is being built, and is owned and operated by Dudh Utpadak Sahakari Sangh Limited (DUSSL). Project activity is located at Chandauli district of Uttar Pradesh state in India.

name: PIEMONTE BAMBOO
project_type: Agriculture Forestry and Other Land Use
description: Piantagione di rimboschimento con messa a dimora di piante bambù gigante nella regione Piemonte.

name: Symbiosis Continuous Cover Forest Project
project_type: Agriculture Forestry and Other Land Use
description:
The Symbiosis Continuous Cover Forest Project is a reforestation project, proposed by Symbiosis Investimentos e Participações S.A., a company focused on the restoration of degraded land through the sustainable commercial reforestation of the Atlantic Rainforest native species.
The Atlantic Forest Biome (Mata Atlântica) is the most degraded in Brazil, with less than 12.4% left of its original area and very fragmented. The degradation started in the 16th century in the State of Bahia. Today, the same pattern of destruction is seen in the Amazon Biome, which started in the 70’s after the Atlantic Rainforest resources were depleted. In addition, plant breeding with the Atlantic Forest native species has not been implemented before.
The project is designed as a grouped project, with an initial instance at “Fazenda Novo Horizonte”, in Trancoso District of Porto Seguro municipality, Bahia State. It is situated in close proximity to Symbiosis headquarters, where seedlings are produced and where research and development activities take place. Novo Horizonte has a total area of 669.28 ha, from which 236.50 consist of the initial project area. Symbiosis expansion plans for the grouped project are focused on the South of Bahia, with projected 50,000 hectares of mixed species reforestation, in addition to 15,000 hectares of ecological restoration and 5,000 hectares of agroforestry with cocoa (also a relevant product of the region).
The land use in the region is predominantly focused on pasture, which is also the prior condition of all of the regions where the grouped project is intended to occur.
The project is designed for a 40-year crediting period, in which 27,499,184 tCO2e will be reduced/removed

name: Cycling the Change
description: The main objective of the project Cycling the Change Latin America is to promote the sustainable mobility at the cities  covered by the grouped project through the implementation of new bicycle sharing programs with sharing stations. Beyond that the program aims at the expansion of the existing parking areas, expansion of existing bikes and introduction of e-bikes.

name: Myanmar Kyeeonkyeewa Solar Power Plant Project
description:
The Myanmar Kyeeonkyeewa Solar Power Plant Project is the construction of a new solar photovoltaic power plant project located 54km northeast from the capital city of Magway Division, Myanmar. 
The main purpose of the project is to generate power from clean renewable solar power and supply electricity to the Myanmar Power Grid while contributing to the sustainability of power generation of the Myanmar Power Grid.
The project scenario consists of the installation of 74,592 pieces of 540Wp polycrystalline silicon PV module, providing a total capacity of 40.28MWp. The expected net annual power supply to the grid is 64,641.35MWh. The expected full load operating hours are 1,604 h annually, and the plant load factor is 18.32%. The power generated by the project will be routed via an on-site step-up station to 132 kV and then connected to the Myanmar Power Grid.
By displacing fossil fuel fired power generation within the Grid by clean renewable energy, the project leads to the reduction of CO2 emissions into the atmosphere. Total annual Green House Gases emissions reduction is estimated to be of 23,339 tCO2e annually. The total emission reductions during the renewable 7-year crediting period will be 163,373 tCO2e.

name: Myanmar Satoketayar Solar Power Plant Project
developer: Timing Carbon Asset Management Co., Ltd.
description:

name: A-Thermal General & Hazardous Waste Treatment Plant
description:
A-Thermal has a pyrolysis process plant for the destruction of hazardous and general wastes in South Africa. The plant has a lower CO2e footprint than other current waste disposal methods that are both legal and lower cost  i.e., landfill. Further, the process captures and fixes carbon from the waste feed in the carbonized residue by-product.
The project meets the methodology requirements for avoidance of methane production from the waste going to landfills.
The plant has been in operation since 2009 and is fully permitted.

name: Better cooking for a better health In Rusizi district - Rwanda
description:
The project aims to distribute 100 000 fixed improved cookstoves to all eligible households in the district of Rusizi in Western Rwanda over the next 4 years. 
Those single-pot cookstoves will be built in-situ into domestic kitchens. Kiasi Energies will disseminate fixed Improved Cookstove Solutions (ICS) in Rwanda that will drastically increase community access to clean cooking solutions by providing, installing, and maintaining energy efficient and smoke reducing cookstoves. Those improved cookstoves will be distributed for free and the materials (bricks, clay, ...) needed for installation will be collected by the households themselves. 

The aim of the project is to reduce the emissions of greenhouse gases incurred by high wood consuming cooking practices. Indeed, in the district of Rusizi, a large part of the population is still cooking with a three-stone fire. The distribution of these stoves directly improves energy access and reduces wood fuel consumption, thus slowing down deforestation. It is expected to prevent the emission of 150kt of CO2eq per year, on average. It also benefits the local population with several other socio-economic matters addressed by the Sustainable Development Goals of the United Nations, such as improved health for the households, gender equality, reduced poverty, and others.

name: Myanmar Kindar Solar Power Plant Project

name: REGENERATIVE AGRICULTURE AND CARBON PROJECT IN SPAIN
project_type: Agriculture Forestry and Other Land Use
description:
The project basically consists of the application of regenerative agriculture techniques and strategies on different farms in Spain, to promote a more sustainable agronomic management, and as a result increasing the amounts of atmospheric carbon fixed in the soil.
Regenerative agriculture promotes practices such as the reduction or absence of tilling the soil, the presence of plant covers, the non-use of synthetic chemical products, organic fertilization, the optimization of water use, the improvement of by-products or waste management, and crop rotation, among others.
The project is national scope and will be carried out on all those farms within the boundaries of the Spanish State that adopt the commitment to improve their agronomic management and that meet the established requirements.
Regenerative agricultural management is focused on improving the soil’s properties and promoting conservation practices. The implementation of these measures will help to improve the health and fertility of agricultural soils which translates into an increase in the amount of organic matter (OM) in those soils. Carbon is one of the main components of OM, so increasing its percentage in soils is equivalent to increasing the amount of Soil Organic Carbon (SOC).
Each of the regenerative strategies proposed in the project has a direct or indirect effect on the reduction of Green-house Gases (GHG), either by reducing emissions or by increasing its fixation in the soil.
Although it is gaining ground in recent years, regenerative agriculture is not a common practice in the Spanish territory. Most farms are managed according to the principles of conventional agriculture, in which the soil is considered a mere support which generally has very little organic life and therefore, the amounts of OM and C are well below the levels that they could potentially contain.
The Sustainable Farming Carbon Project in Spain will be developed as a grouped project.

name: Biochar Project-1 by WeAct
description:
This project activity is a voluntary initiative by WeAct Pty Ltd in the Sangareddy district, in the state of Telangana in India. WeAct is a carbon asset management and carbon financing entity from Australia who deals in such GHG projects globally to address the concerns of climate change and ensures long term sustainability. The project activity uses Low technology production facilities to produce Biochar from biomass wastes in the project region. The project includes mainly soil-pit methods and box-kiln method which are two common low-tech approaches that can serve as a starting point for small-scale production, experimentation, and community-level initiatives. Under the facilities, the biomass undergoes pyrolysis process. The project activity mainly targets to include “Cotton Stalk” as a single type of waste biomass used as feedstock to produce biochar and the resulting biochar to be utilized for soil application. In the absence of the project activity, the cotton wastes would have been mainly combusted without any utilization for purposes and not utilized for producing biochar for either soil or non-soil application. 

The project activity is expected to generate an annual average of 22,376 tCO2e emission reductions which is estimated based on a projected generation of biochar from cotton stalks as feedstock during each harvesting season in each year. The project contributes to sustainable development by promoting various aspects including (but not limited to) environmental conservation, resource efficiency, rural development, climate change mitigation, and the transition towards a circular economy. It aligns agricultural practices with the principles of sustainable development, fostering a more resilient and equitable agricultural sector.

name: Muyuan Huainan AWMS GHG Mitigation Project in Anhui Province
project_type: Energy industries (renewable/non-renewable sources); Livestock, enteric fermentation, and manure management; Waste handling and disposal
description:
Muyuan Huainan AWMS GHG Mitigation Project in Anhui Province (hereafter referred to as the project) installs new animal waste management systems (AWMSs) to treat the manure from swine farms in Huainan City, Anhui Province, China, which are owned by Muyuan Foods Co.,Ltd. Each subsidiary swine farm shall install one AWMS, and the manure is treated on site. The purpose of the project activity is to treat the manure and wastewater to avoid methane emissions generated in the baseline uncovered anaerobic lagoons.
All the manure and wastewater are collected and then be separated first. The solid will be treated in aerobic composting system and the organic fertilizers will be produced, the fertilizer produced in this process will be distributed to local farmers for free and the surplus will be sold in domestic market. The liquid will be treated through anaerobic digestion and the biogas released during the anaerobic digestion will be partly used as fuel for the canteens of swine farms, partly for the biogas boiler for the feedlot, and the remaining biogas will be flared. The sludge produced from anaerobic digestion will be treated through aerobic composting together with the solid, the effluent will be supplied to the farmers living around free for agriculture irrigation.
It is estimated that approximately 359.022 tons of animal manure will be handled daily by the AWMSs. The biogas released during the anaerobic digestion will be partly used as fuel for the canteens of swine farms, partly for the biogas boiler for the feedlot, and the remaining biogas will be flared. For conservativeness, baseline emissions from heat generation are neglected.
The project activity will reduce GHG in the atmosphere through avoiding methane emissions from anaerobic treatment of swine manure and wastewater. It is estimated that 336,687 tCO2e emission reductions will be attained annually.

project_type: Energy industries (renewable/non-renewable sources); Livestock, enteric fermentation, and manure management; Waste handling and disposal
description:
Muyuan Urad AWMS GHG Mitigation Project in Inner Mongolia (hereafter referred to as the project) installs new animal waste management systems (AWMS) to treat the manure from swine farm in Urad City, Inner Mongolia, China, which are owned by Muyuan Foods Co.,Ltd. Each subsidiary swine farm shall install one AWMS, and the manure is treated on site. The purpose of the project activity is to treat the manure and wastewater to avoid methane emissions generated in the baseline uncovered anaerobic lagoon.
All the manure and wastewater are collected and then be separated first. The solid will be treated in aerobic composting system and the organic fertilizers will be produced, the fertilizer produced in this process will be distributed to local farmers for free and the surplus will be sold in domestic market. The liquid will be treated through anaerobic digestion and the biogas released during the anaerobic digestion will be flared. The sludge produced from anaerobic digestion will be treated through aerobic composting together with the solid, the effluent will be supplied to the farmers living around free for agriculture irrigation.
It is estimated that approximately 14 tons of animal manure will be handled daily by the AWMS. The biogas released during the anaerobic digestion will be flared. For conservativeness, baseline emissions from heat generation are neglected.
The project activity will reduce GHG in the atmosphere through avoiding methane emissions from anaerobic treatment of swine manure and wastewater. It is estimated that 120,250 tCO2e emission reductions will be attained annually.

name: MAHARASHTRA AND GUJARAT INITIATIVE FOR REGENERATIVE AGRICULTURE AND INCOME CREATION
project_type: Agriculture Forestry and Other Land Use
description:
Grow Indigo is implementing a project in Maharashtra and Gujarat to boost smallholder farmers' income through the adoption of regenerative agriculture, resulting in reduced greenhouse gas (GHG) emissions and positive environmental and economic outcomes.
The proposed project in Maharashtra and Gujarat addresses the GHG emissions caused by traditional agricultural practices in crops such as cotton, sugarcane, rice, wheat, maize, or soybean, without excluding other crops. Intensive agriculture practices in the project area have posed threats to land sustainability and contributed to increased GHG emissions.
The project aims to promote regenerative agricultural practices, such as optimized fertilizer management, cover cropping, zero- or reduced-tillage, improved water management/ irrigation, crop rotation, and agroforestry, to restore soil health, enhance biodiversity, and improve productivity.
The project takes an integrated and science-backed approach, including agricultural extension, outreach, agronomic support, digital data collection, and biogeochemical modeling.
The project will initially target 40,000 hectares in the project area and cover diverse cropping systems with regenerative agricultural practices that are known to reduce GHG emissions (N2O, CO2e, and SOC) and thus generate carbon credits.
The project also aims to link smallholder farmers to voluntary carbon markets, providing them with additional income opportunities and incentivizing the adoption of regenerative agriculture. With a cash incentive, smallholder farmers in the project boundary will adopt these practices more readily and contribute to sustainability and reduce GHG emissions.
Through these efforts, the project seeks to contribute to sustainability, reduce greenhouse gas emissions, and improve the overall livelihoods of smallholder farmers in the project area.

name: GROUPED ARR PROJECT IN TELANGANA
project_type: Agriculture Forestry and Other Land Use
description:
Grouped ARR Project in Telangana is an Agroforestry, Afforestation, Reforestation and Revegetation project being jointly developed by Tapovanam Organic Farming Systems (hereinafter referred as Tapovanam) and ClimeTrek Limited (hereinafter referred as ClimeTrek) in fallow agricultural, and wastelands owned by individual farmers and communities with low plant cover (hereinafter referred as project activity). The entire project lies within the geographical boundaries of Telangana state in India. In the first instance, the project activity is limited to the district of Nalgonda. Being a grouped project, more farmers and communities belonging to other districts of Telangana will be added as ‘future project instances. The project activity involves planting oil palm trees along with some cash crops like turmeric and groundnuts. In the first project instance, around 1,100 Ha will be covered in Nalgonda district in three years.  Future instances will cover 15 other districts of the state of Telangana. All project instances within this grouped project activity will consist of afforestation, reforestation and revegetation (ARR) primarily involving oil palm plantations with intercropping of turmeric and groundnuts. Based on ex-ante estimates the project will sequester around 1,073,817.9 tCO2e over 30-years (tree/ shrub biomass carbon and soil carbon) and an annual emissions reduction of 35,793.9 tCO2e.
Tapovanam is the coordinator for all the participating farmers and provides training to the farmers regarding the technologies/measures involved in the project activity. Tapovanam will have the right to carbon credits without any violation of farmers rights. The revenue after expenses from sale of carbon credits will be shared with the participating farmers. Clime Trek is the Carbon Project Developer. As per the agreement between Tapovanam and Clime Trek, the rights to carbon credits from the project will be transferred to ClimeTrek.Tapovanam and ClimeTrek are project pp.

name: AS KOC POLATLI BIOGAS POWER PLANT
description:
AS KOC POLATLI BIOGAS POWER PLANT (hereafter referred to as the Project) is a greenfield biogas-to-energy project that aims to captures biogas from animal manure, dairy cattle and other cattle manure in particular, -via anaerobic digestion- and utilizes it to generate electricity through cogeneration units. The animal manure is collected from the neighboring animal farms with special trucks and transferred to the biogas plant. Continuously stirred tank reactor (CSTR) type anaerobic digesters are used to capture methane-rich biogas.  Waste heat from two gas engines is utilized mainly for heating anaerobic fermenters. The electricity generated by the installed two biogas engines with the capacity of 1.501 MWe each and a total capacity of 3.120 MWe is not only supplied to the national grid, but also used as auxiliary/internal consumption required for the plant to function. Solid and liquid fermented products, by-products of biogas generation processes, are distributed to neighboring agricultural farms as fertilizer free of charge.

Prior to the project activity, livestock farms supplying animal manure to the project were, in the baseline scenario, storing the animal manure generated at their farms in uncovered anaerobic lagoons as Animal Waste Management System (AWMS) in a retention period of 2-3 months and then, generally applying to land, as fertilizer, directly without any proper treatment. In addition, untreated animal manure is an important source of methane which is one of the most potent GHGs. 
The project activity avoids methane emission through the above-mentioned capture and utilization processes.

name: ALLCOT BLUE CARBON MANGROVE PROJECT IN SENEGAL (ABC  Mangrove Senegal)
project_type: Agriculture Forestry and Other Land Use
description:
Allcot Blue Carbon Mangrove Restoration project in Senegal (ABC Mangrove Senegal) is a grouped project for the reforestation and conservation of mangrove ecosystems in Senegal. Through the restoration of at least 7,000 ha of mangroves, the project aims to:
o Strengthen the vegetation cover in the mangrove ecosystems.
o Improve the production and income of vulnerable groups.
o Strengthen the capacity of vulnerable groups to use land resources sustainably.
Involving the local communities since the beginning is one of the most important steps in the project. This includes providing information on all project activities and teaching basic concepts on climate change, and 
carbon sequestration projects. The project promotes a functioning family model where both women and 
men can equally participate in the project. People will show alternative livelihood opportunities that allow them to acquire and grow high-value crops, beekeeping, or ecotourism among other potential possibilities, 
which also reduces pressure on mangrove forests. An improvement of the basic infrastructure for rural communities is targeted as well.
The Project location is the Saloum Delta and the Casamance estuary respectively located in two regions (Fatick and Casamance) and 5 departments (Fatick, Foundiougne, Ziguinchor, Bignona, Oussouye), implemented in bare land, and at the end of the crediting period, the net emissions reductions are 2,241,960 tCO2 e.

name: 7.5 MW Waste-to-Energy Power Plant by Goodwatts WTE Jamnagar Private Limited in Gujarat, India
project_type: Energy industries (renewable/non-renewable sources); Waste handling and disposal
description: The main purpose of this project activity is to generate clean form of electricity through waste to energy-based power generation. The plant utilizes the Refuse-Derived Fuel (“RDF”) as feedstock derived from the separation and sorting of Municipal Solid Waste (“MSW”) excluding the recyclable or potentially hazardous materials from the waste stream. The MSW is sourced from the Jamnagar City and the project will utilise about 311 ton of RDF per day and generate electricity with the installed capacity of 7.5 MW. The project avoids CH4 emission from avoidance of waste going to landfills and also avoids CO2 emission by replacing grid electricity.

name: Anhui Zhujixi CMM Utilization Project
developer: Huainan Huamei Pushi New Energy Technology Co., Ltd
description:
Anhui Zhujixi CMM Utilization Project (hereinafter referred to as the Project) utilizes the low concentration coal mine methane (CMM) from Zhujixi coal mine to generate hot air to dry coal slime provided by Zhujixi coal mine. The Project is located in Hetuan Town, Panji District, Huainan City, Anhui Province, China.
The purpose of the Project is to utilize the extracted CMM with low concentration methane concentration to generate hot air to dry the coal slime. The project applies flameless oxidation process. Four sets of regenerative thermal oxidizers (RTOs), each with a treatment capacity of around 30,000 Nm3/h  are installed, able to destroy 10.368 million Nm3 of methane annually and dry 400,000 tonnes of wet coal slime ideally.

name: AJINOMOTO GROUPED PROJECT:  REDUCTION OF METHANE EMISSIONS IN  THE DAIRY SECTOR
project_type: Livestock, enteric fermentation, and manure management
description:
The Ajinomoto Co., Inc. grouped project aims to introduce feed additives to dairy farms in United States, Japan, EU, Australia, New Zealand, Chile, Costa Rica, and South Korea to reduce greenhouse gas (GHG) emissions from the livestock sector. Methane is a by-product of the enteric fermentation process in cattle and is mainly expelled by the animal through belching. The Agolin® Ruminant feed additive used in this project reduces methane (CH4) emissions from enteric fermentation by changing the microbial population in the rumen; it also increases milk production efficiency.

A VCS-grouped project combines multiple project activity instances into a single, combined project which adds new instances (farms) over time. The project instances of this grouped project are located in United States, Japan, EU, Australia, New Zealand, Chile, Costa Rica, and South Korea and will implement the Agolin® Ruminant in the cattle’s diet, starting from September 01, 2023.

The dairy farms included in the grouped project have not previously engaged in enteric methane reduction activities similar to those in the proposed grouped project activity and have otherwise been releasing CH4 into the atmosphere (“the business as usual” scenario). 

In the seven years of the first crediting period, when the project activities will be implemented, the project will organize the addition of a natural feed blend to the dairy cattle feed and to subsequent feeding to generate estimated emission reductions of 0.45 metric tons of carbon dioxide equivalent (tCO2e) per cattle per year, with an estimated total reduction of 231,518 tCO2e in the first crediting period, depending on the continuing success of enrolling more farms. The Project is quantified and will be monitored according to the VCS methodology “VM0041 Methodology for the Reduction of Enteric Methane Emission from Ruminants through the Use of Feed Ingredients”. It falls under VCS Sectoral Scope 15, livestock and manure management.

name: Shandong Zhucheng ALM Project
project_type: Agriculture Forestry and Other Land Use
description:
Shandong Zhucheng ALM Project (hereafter as “the project”) is located in Zhucheng City, Weifang City, Shandong Province of China. The goal of this initiative is to reduce the carbon emissions currently emitted by the farms taking part to the project and raise the carbon storage in the soil. In addition, the selected measures will contribute to improving crop yields and soil health. The project was implemented by the Shandong Herong Agricultural Technology Group Co., Ltd. and Hainan icarbon Ecological Development Co.,Ltd. (hereafter “the project proponent”).
The project is located in the Zhucheng City, which covers 3 Streets and 10 towns. Zhucheng City is located in the southeast of Shandong Peninsula, at the junction of Taiyi Mountain Range and Jiaowei Plain. The total area of Zhucheng City is 2182.7 square kilometres, with the geographic coordinates between 35°42′23′′ and 36°21′05′′ north latitude and 119°0′19′′ and 119°43′56′′ east longitude.
The proposed project is aimed to prevent the soil degradation through adoption of the improved crop land management practices (collectively referred to conservational tillage) to replace the conventional cultivation mode.
Main activities about conservational tillage adopted in the project include： 
Organic fertilizer application (reduce inorganic fertilizer application): 54,398.5 ha of cropland have reduced the use of chemical fertilizer.
Straw incorporation (Improve crop residue management): straw in 54,398.5 ha of cropland have been buried and returned, with the depth of 30 cm.
A total of 54,398.5 ha of farmland has been managed under conservation tillage, The project is estimated to generate GHG emission removals of 3,471,463 tCO2e from 01-Jan-2021 to 31-Dec- 2040, with an average annual GHG emission removal of 173,573 tCO2e.

name: IÇARA LANDFILL GAS PROJECT
project_type: Energy industries (renewable/non-renewable sources); Waste handling and disposal
description: The proposed VCS project activity titled “Içara Landfill Gas Project” encompasses the promotion of collection and destruction/utilization of landfill gas (LFG) (rich in methane) through collection LFG and its destruction in high temperature open flare(s) and utilization as gaseous fuel in engine-generator sets of an electricity generation infrastructure, and a LFG upgrading plant that produces biomethane for thermal use.

name: Xinhangdao AWMS GHG Mitigation Project In Shangqiu City
project_type: Livestock, enteric fermentation, and manure management; Waste handling and disposal
description: The project activity uses scraper system to collect the manure automatically. All the manure and wastewater are collected and then be separated first. The separated solid will be treated in aerobic composting system to produce fertilizer The separation liquid is treated by anaerobic digestion, and the biogas generated in the anaerobic digestion process is collected and utilized. Biogas is used as fuel for producing hot water and cooking for pig farms, which eliminated most of methane production and realized methane reduction. and the residual biogas will be flared by internal combustion emergency flare (closed flare) if there is any surplus biogas. The sludge produced by digestion is treated with aerobic composting together with solids, and the effluent is used as liquid organic fertilizer for agricultural irrigation.

name: Hunan Fufeng Composting Project
project_type: Livestock, enteric fermentation, and manure management; Waste handling and disposal
description:
Hunan Fufeng Composting project (hereinafter as “the project”) employs aerobic composting systems on organic fertilizer factory in Miluo City, Yueyang City, Hunan Province, China. The project is owned by Hunan Fufeng fertilizer Co., Ltd. The avoidance of methane emissions could be achieved with treatments of aerobic composting, which replaces the baseline scenario where the swine manure would undergo an anaerobic decomposition condition.
In absence of the project, all manure waste produced was left to decay in uncovered anaerobic lagoons, which is the most economic, viable and reasonable for livestock farm owners, and methane would emit to the atmosphere.
The project introduces the aerobic composting system to treat livestock manure produced around Miluo City, the project was designed to produce 42,000 tons of organic fertilizer by treating 14,000 tons of livestock manure and 50,000 tons of straw. The organic fertilizer produced will be sold to local farmers and businesses. Without this project, the farms in project
areas remain conditions of uncovered anaerobic lagoons that may bring a larger amount of GHG emissions sent to the atmosphere. 
The project activity will reduce GHG in the atmosphere by avoiding methane emissions through controlled aerobic treatment of organic waste. During the implementation of the project, it is estimated that about 41,213 tCO2e emission reductions will be generated annually, and total 412,130 tCO2e in a 10-year crediting period.

name: Huaian Tech-Bank Animal Waste Management Systems (AWMS) GHG Mitigation Project
project_type: Livestock, enteric fermentation, and manure management; Waste handling and disposal
description:
Huaian Tech-Bank Animal Waste Management Systems (AWMS) GHG Mitigation Project in Jiangsu Province (hereafter referred to as “the project”) installs new animal waste management systems (AWMS) to treat the manure from 3 existing swine farms at Huaian  County, Jiangsu Province, which are owned by Tech-Bank Food Co., Ltd. Each subsidiary swine farm installs one AWMS, and the manure is treated on-site. The purpose of the project activity is to treat the manure and wastewater to avoid methane emissions generated in the baseline uncovered anaerobic lagoons.
All manure and wastewater will be collected and then the next step will be solid-liquid separation. The solid manure will be processed in an aerobic composting system and organic fertilizer will be produced. The liquid will be treated by anaerobic digestion and biogas produced during this treatment process will be captured and sent to an on-site torch and destroyed. The biogas residue produced after fermentation is applied as fertilizer to nearby fields, and the wastewater from the anaerobic digester is used for agricultural irrigation. For conservativeness, baseline emissions from heat generation are neglected.
The project activity will reduce G HG emissions in the atmosphere by avoiding methane emissions from the anaerobic treatment of swine manure and wastewater. The annual emission reduction is estimated as 83,245tCO2e, and the total emission reductions are estimated as582,715tCO2e throughout the crediting period.

name: Strengthening rural livelihood through carbon finance: Agroforestry practices in Bareilly Forest Circle of Uttar Pradesh
project_type: Agriculture Forestry and Other Land Use
description: The proposed ARR VCS project plans to promote sustainable agroforestry for small-scale farmers to provide them with financial benefits and ensure GHG mitigation in the state of Uttar Pradesh, India. The project is being conducted in five divisions of Bareilly Forest Circle of Uttar Pradesh, namely Bareilly Social Forestry Division. The main agroforestry tree species planted by farmers for the year are Eucalyptus, Poplar, Teak, Guava and Mango. These species have higher productivity that leads to sequestration of carbon dioxide at faster pace and ultimately reduces GHG emissions.This project will also help in increasing tree outside forest (TOF) that will add in mitigating climate change. The project shall also enhance the income of farmer communities along with biodiversity conservation and improvement of soil health.
