project_type: Agriculture Forestry and Other Land Use
description:
Tianzhu Improved Grassland Management Project (hereafter as “the project”) is located in Tianzhu County, Gansu Province of China. Tianzhu County is located in the northwest of Gansu Province and in the middle of Hexi corridor where the Qinghai Tibet Plateau and  Mongolia Plateau meet. The project’s aim is to restore the local degraded grassland ecosystem by seeding grass and building fence on the degraded grassland, increase carbon  sequestration and contribute to local development by introducing sustainable grazing and management of grassland. The project proponent is Zhejiang Zhongzheng Forestry Development Co., Ltd.
According to the baseline survey, before the implementation of the project, the grassland in the region has been facing serious degradation and even desertification due to the impact of climate change and human activities. According to the National standard documents of the people's Republic of China and Project Design Report, moderately  degraded areas refer to the total grass yield decreased by 21%-50%compared with that before degradation and the total grass yield decreased by 50% compared with that before degradation is regarded as seriously degraded grasslands.

name: Shaanxi Zheng Neng AWMS GHG Mitigation Project
developer: Shaanxi Zhengneng Agriculture and Animal Husbandry Technology Co., Ltd.
project_type: Livestock, enteric fermentation, and manure management; Waste handling and disposal
description:
Shaanxi Zhengneng AWMS GHG Mitigation Project in Shaanxi Province (hereafter referred to as the project) installs new animal waste management systems (AWMSs) to treat the manure from 6 
existing swine farms in Shaanxi Province, which are owned by Shaanxi Zhengneng Agriculture and Animal Husbandry Technology Co., Ltd. Each subsidiary swine farm installs one AWMS, and the 
manure is treated on site. The purpose of the project activity is to treat the manure and wastewater to avoid methane emissions generated in the baseline uncovered anaerobic lagoons.All manure and wastewater will be collected and then solids and liquids will be separated. The solid manure will be processed in an aerobic composting system and organic fertilizer will be produced. 
The liquids will be treated by anaerobic digestion and the biogas produced during the treatment process will be captured and sent to a boiler to generate heat, with the excess gas being destroyed 
through a combustion system (if available). The sludge produced after fermentation is applied as fertilizer to nearby fields, and the wastewater from the anaerobic digester is used for agricultural 
irrigation. For conservativeness, baseline emissions from heat generation are neglected.The project activity will reduce of GHG in the atmosphere through avoiding methane emissions from anaerobic treatment of swine manure and wastewater. It is estimated that 442,037 tonnes of carbon dioxide equivalent emission reductions will be generated annually, and total emission reductions are 3,207,995 tonnes of carbon dioxide equivalent in the crediting period.

name: Waste to Energy Project in Chennai, Tamil Nadu
developer: Srinivas Waste Management Services Private Limited
project_type: Energy industries (renewable/non-renewable sources); Waste handling and disposal
description: The proposed project activity is an organic waste processing plant located at Plot No. A-2, S in Block No.0029, Survey No.465/4, 20, 30, Spur Tank Road, Egmore Taluk, Chennai, Tamil Nadu by Srinivas Waste Management Services Private Limited. The project activity involves anaerobic decomposition of degradable food and other organic waste and generate bioCNG and manure. This project is greenfield project activity with an installed capacity of 100 TPD. Required segregated food and other organic wastes would be sourced from bulk waste generators (BWG) like hotels, industries, fish/ vegetable markets, community hall, hospital Canteens and segregated waste from Apartments.

name: Zhenyuan Swine Farm AWMS GHG Mitigation Project
project_type: Livestock, enteric fermentation, and manure management; Waste handling and disposal
description:
Zhenyuan Swine Farm AWMS GHG Mitigation Project (hereinafter referred to as the Project) introduces 1 new animal waste management system (AWMS) to treat the manure from the existing swine farm in Zhenyuan County, Guizhou Province, which are owned by ZHENYUAN XINMU Agricultural Development Co., Ltd (hereinafter called the project owner). Each subsidiary swine farm will install one AWMS. The purpose of the project activity is to treat the manure and wastewater to avoid methane emissions generated in the baseline uncovered anaerobic lagoons.
The common practice for local swine farm owners to manage the manure is to have uncovered anaerobic lagoons/ponds at their farms in the region. As per “technical specification for sanitation treatment of livestock and poultry manure ”, in China, the uncovered anaerobic lagoons are a manure treatment method recognized by the state. In addition, since there is no legal regulation to mandate the livestock farm owners to implement anaerobic digestion, aerobic or other biological treatment techniques and to capture and/or utilize methane generated at their lagoons, therefore the continue of this common practice to treatment the manure i.e., uncovered anaerobic lagoons is the most economic, viable and reasonable for livestock farm owners.
It is estimated that approximately 388.64*104 m3 of biogas will be produced annually. The biogas will be captured and utilized for heat generation, the heat will be only used for the daily operation of the AWMS and the swine farm and will not be produced to other users. For conservativeness, baseline emissions from heat generation are neglected.
The project activity will reduce of GHG in the atmosphere through avoiding methane emissions from anaerobic treatment of swine manure and wastewater. It is estimated that 32,028 tCO2e emission reductions will be produced annually.

name: Puyang Swine Farm AWMS Project in Henan
project_type: Livestock, enteric fermentation, and manure management; Waste handling and disposal
description:
Puyang Swine Farm AWMS Project in Henan (hereinafter referred to as the grouped project) is a grouped project which installs eight new animal waste management systems (AWMSs) to treat the manure from eight existing swine farms in Puyang, Henan Province. The project is owned and implemented by the subsidiaries of Muyuan Foods Co., Ltd. (hereinafter referred to as the project proponent). Each swine farm installs one set of AWMS to treat the manure on site. The purpose of the project activity is to treat the manure and wastewater to avoid methane emissions generated in the baseline uncovered anaerobic lagoons.
The grouped project is to install AWMS for each subsidiary swine farm and treat the manure generated on site. Each project activity instance under the grouped project will involve the collection and utilization of the biogas generated from AWMS for energy generation, the part of biogas that cannot be utilized will be destructed by flaring.

name: Henan Shangqiu Animal Waste Management Systems Project
project_type: Energy industries (renewable/non-renewable sources); Livestock, enteric fermentation, and manure management; Waste handling and disposal
description:
Henan Shangqiu Animal Waste Management Systems project (hereafter referred to as the project) installs total 24 sets of new animal waste management systems (AWMSs) to treat the manure on site for 24 existing swine farms owned by ten subsidiaries of Muyuan Foods Co., Ltd. in Shangqiu city in Henan Province, i.e. one set for each swine farm. The purpose of the project is to treat the waste produced in swine farms by adopting AWMSs to avoid GHG emissions generated in the baseline uncovered anaerobic lagoons.
The treatment process employed by the newly built AWMSs consist of 3 steps: solid-liquid separation, anaerobic digestion, and aerobic composting. All manure and urine collected from swine farms are separated first. Solid components separated are then treated in aerobic composting system to produce organic fertilizer. And the liquids flow into anaerobic digestion process to generate biogas for utilization for energy. Surplus biogas if any is destroyed through the flaring system. The sludge produced from anaerobic digestion process are treated through aerobic composting together with the solid, the effluent is supplied to the farmers living around for free for agriculture irrigation.

name: Henan Xinyang Grouped AWMS Biogas Recovery Project
project_type: Livestock, enteric fermentation, and manure management; Waste handling and disposal

name: Jingmen AWMS GHG Mitigation Project in Hubei Province
project_type: Energy industries (renewable/non-renewable sources); Livestock, enteric fermentation, and manure management; Waste handling and disposal
description:
Jingmen AWMS GHG Mitigation Project (hereafter referred to as the project) installs total 3 sets of new animal waste management systems (AWMSs) to treat the manure on site for 3 existing swine farms owned by the subsidiary of Muyuan Foods Co., Ltd. in Jingmen city in Hubei Province, i.e. one set for each swine farm. name: Hunan Anfu PP Recycling Project
developer: Hunan Anfu Environmental Protection Technology Co.,Ltd
description: “Hunan Anfu PP Recycling Project” (hereafter referred to as “the project”) aims to produce PP flakes by recycling and processing post-consumer PP daily necessities (such as tubs, buckets, woven bags,etc.) to replace the same amount of PP products produced from raw materials. It is planned that 90,000 tons of post-consumer PP daily necessities per year will be recycled into 65,000 tons of PP flakes at maximum production capacity. The project located in Linli County, Changde City, Hunan Province, China and is developed and operated by Hunan Anfu Environmental Protection Technology Co., Ltd.(hereafter referred to as “the project proponent”). Prior to the project implementation, the same amount of PP flakes was produced from raw materials (crude oil and natural gas); the baseline scenario is the same as the condition prior to project initiation. The Project achieves GHG emission reductions by avoiding the consumption of the equivalent raw materials and by reducing related energy consumption as well. The first crediting period of the project is from 10-November-2021 to 09-November-2028. The estimated annual average GHG emission reductions are 42,918 tCO2e and the total estimated GHG emission reductions over the first crediting period are 300,427 tCO2e.

name: Yueyang LFG Power Generation Project
developer: Yueyang Weiteng New Energy Co., Ltd.
project_type: Energy industries (renewable/non-renewable sources); Waste handling and disposal
description:
Yueyang LFG Power Generation Project (hereafter referred to as “the Project”) is a landfill gas (LFG) recovery and utilization project developed by Yueyang Weiteng New Energy Co., Ltd. (hereinafter referred to as “the project proponent”). The Project is located at the west of Yueyang County MSW Landfill, Weixing Village, Xinkai Town, Yueyang County, Yueyang City, Hunan province, People’s Republic of China. 
The purpose of the Project is to collect LFG from Yueyang County MSW Landfill and utilize it for power generation. It includes LFG collection system, LFG pre-treatment system, flaring and electricity generation system. LFG collected will be used for electricity generation with internal combustion generators.
The Project achieves emission reductions in two aspects: 1) it avoids methane emissions by capturing and destroying LFG which would have been directly vented into the atmosphere in the baseline scenario; 2) it reduces CO2 emissions by displacing part of the electricity that would otherwise have been supplied by CCPG.

name: Chongqing Kaizhou Afforestation Project
developer: National Forestry and Grassland Administration Northwest Investigation and Planning Institute
project_type: Agriculture Forestry and Other Land Use
description:

name: Biogas Project in Cuddalore, India
description: The proposed project involves establishment of organic waste biorefinery. The project activity produces Bio-CNG and Bio Manure using biodegradable wastes. The purpose of the project activity is to recover and treat various types of organic wastes. The technology used is anaerobic decomposition in a continuous stirred tank reactor. The wastes to be considered under the project activity would have been otherwise openly decayed, leading to a significant quantity of methane emissions in the absence of the project activity. The total capacity of the plant is 90 tons of waste per day. Due to the inherent nature of the project activity the proposed project also contributes to various SDGs.

name: Grouped Commercial Electric Vehicles Project of Intelligent Link
developer: Zhejiang Green Intelligent Link Co., Ltd.
description:
The grouped project activity is carried out by Zhejiang Green Intelligent Link (hereafter Green Intelligent Link or Intelligent Link), which is a platform supplying environmental transport capacity and smart vehicle networking, to provide rental services of electric delivery vehicles in China.
In China, commercial vehicles sold out 3 million in 2022, including 2.893 million trucks. Most commercial vehicles burn fossil fuels. As one kind of commercials vehicles, the sales of pickup trucks were 519,000. By fuel, the sales of gasoline pickup trucks and diesel ones were 120,000 and 397,000 respectively. The new energy vehicles used for distribution in urban accounted for 8% of all new energy vehicles till 2020. 168,000 new energy vehicles were sold in 2021, with a penetration rate of 3.5%. Due to problem like lack of supporting infrastructure, and high price of power batteries, the fuel vehicles were commonly used in commercial transportation services.
In this project, project vehicles of the proponent, Intelligent Link, are divided into 2 categories, truck and van. They are all electric vehicles (hereafter EVs). EVs are driven by pure electric provided by energy stored in batteries. The project scenario is EVs instead of fuel-driven vehicles delivering goods in urban area of China. As an EV runs on electricity instead of fossil fuel (diesel and gasoline), the vehicle emits no exhaust from a tailpipe, which leads to lower GHG emissions per distance driven.
The project contributes in a significant manner to sustainable development, which are below: 
•	Project activity is generating employment for local drivers;
•	Project reduces the per capita negative environmental impact of cities within project area, especially the air quality improvement due to reduced vehicle exhaust emission;
•	Project reduces GHG emission reduction due to implementation of EVs and reducing fossil fuel-based vehicles.

name: LANDFILL GAS (LFG) CAPTURE AND COMBUSTION PROJECT OF AYDIN PROVINCE
description:
Landfill Gas (LFG) Capture and Combustion Project of Aydin Province is being developed by Eko En Enerji Elektrik Imalat Sanayi ve Ticaret Anonim Sirketi (Inc.) within the boundaries of Aydın province in Turkey. The project is being carried out simultaneously on 3 different landfill sites located in 3 districts belonging to the province of Aydın. 
The proposed project activity has a total installed capacity of 8.848 MWe, comprising of 1.204 MWe for the Didim landfill site, 5.026 MWe for the Efeler landfill site, and 2.618 MWe for the Kusadasi landfill site. 
The project activity is the capture and combustion of landfill gas via combustion engines. The generated electricity is sold to the national grid. 
Project has begun to capture the LFG and started to generate electricity by combusting on Jun 30th, 2021, which is regarded as the project start date.
This project adopts a first crediting period of 7 years. The expected average annual emission reductions are 215,153 tCO2e/yr. Accordingly, the project is expected to generate 1,506,069 tCO2e emissions reduction throughout the first crediting period.

The project is being carried out simultaneously on 3 different landfill sites located in 3 districts belonging to the province of Mersin. 
The proposed project activity has a total installed capacity of 12.040 MWe, comprising of 3.612 MWe for the Silifke landfill site, 7.224 MWe for the Akdeniz landfill site, and 1.204 MWe for the Tarsus landfill site. Project’s licensed capacity is total of 20.214 MWe .
The project activity is the capture and combustion of landfill gas via combustion engines. The generated electricity is sold to the national grid. 
Project has begun to capture the LFG and started to generate electricity by combusting on Jun 28th, 2021, which is regarded as the project start date.
This project adopts a first crediting period of 7 years. The expected average annual emission reductions are 445,743 tCO2e/yr. Accordingly, the project is expected to generate 3,120,198 tCO2e emissions reduction throughout the first crediting period.

name: ARJUNA Project
project_type: Agriculture Forestry and Other Land Use
description:
This project will promote tree-based wild silk production (sericulture) outside traditional forests by utilizing privately owned degraded lands that smallholder farmers currently do not significantly utilize for productive purposes. It will undertake host tree planting for the Tasar silkworm and silkworm rearing value chain development in two states in India: Jharkhand and West Bengal. Traditionally, the tribal communities in these areas depend significantly on forests for their livelihoods and have a long history of silk production from natural forests –silk is second to agriculture as a source of income/livelihoods. However, production from the forests have become uncertain due to government regulation of forest access rights and instability in the silk market. Yet there are large areas in these regions that are severely degraded, fallow, etc. that would benefit from restoring their productive capacity and biodiversity through profitable tree planting investments. Therefore, this project will undertake tree planting for Tasar production on an estimated 3,000 ha of such lands. 
The project is implemented by the Non-Governmental Organization (NGO): PRADAN - Professional Assistance for Development Action – which has a long-standing experience (50 years) in the area. It will involve the participation of ~4,000 households in 117 villages, grouped into two clusters. The project has a crediting period of 20-years renewable, and will employ the new VERRA ARR Methodology ”Methodology for Afforestation, Reforestation, and Revegetation Projects”. Its estimated annual average and total GHG emission removals are 89,847 and 1,796,931 t CO2e respectively.

name: Makueni Agroforestry Carbon Project
project_type: Agriculture Forestry and Other Land Use
description:
The Makueni Agroforestry Carbon Project (hereafter, “MACP”) is a carbon project in Kenya being developed together by Eni S.p.A. and Eni Kenya b.v. 
MACP will promote the establishment of Sustainable Agricultural Land Management (SALM) practices that will generate high-quality carbon credits, through carbon sequestration. MACP will implement a package of SALM practices, by working with a range of participants to implement these sustainable methods across landscapes in Makueni County, Kenya, particularly focusing on smallholder farms. Project activities will contribute to climate change mitigation, adaptation, and food security. The project has been designed as a grouped project and is targeting to be initially implemented in about 40,000 ha across the County of Makueni, with possibility of expansion into other Counties, since this is a grouped project.
The project has a 20-year crediting period and applies the VCS approved Methodology VM0017 Adoption of Sustainable Agricultural Land Management, Version 1.0. The project’s estimated annual average and total net GHG emission reductions/removals are 155,383 and 3,107,663 tCO2e, respectively.

name: CSA Carbon
project_type: Agriculture Forestry and Other Land Use
description: The C-SA Carbon Project focusses on this opportunity to restore subtropical thicket, sequester carbon and to deliver a broader range of social and ecological outcomes. The C-SA property includes a primary conservation area (in which the Kwandwe eco-tourism operation is located) as well as several severely degraded properties that have been acquired over time. The additional areas of at least 4,000 hectares were previously goat and ostrich farms and have been left in a degraded state, largely clear of vegetation and especially Portulacaria afra. The intention is to implement a landscape-scale rehabilitation project that includes the propagation and planting of Portulacaria afra as well as other species, combined with the long-term management of planted propagules and herbivory pressure. Such planting and management has led to the successful restoration of carbon stocks elsewhere in the biome. The outcome will extend beyond carbon sequestration to the delivery of further ecosystem services and a source of employment and income for local residents (in a region where such opportunities are rare). In an area that is predicted to become significantly warmer and drier over time, enhancing the resilient provision of water services to downstream communities and economies is of significant importance. Through direct restoration of over 4,000 hectares, the project is expected to sequester at least 1,078,000 tCO2e over a 40-year period or an average 26,950 tCO2e per year.

The current geographic area is composed of 11 private forest parcels located in the counties of, Buzău, Dâmbovița, with future instances to be located in Arges, Prahova, and Teleorman. The PAI areas are non-contiguous area. All properties were managed for timber harvest prior to the implementation of the carbon crediting project and forest operations occurred under existing forest management plans.

name: Transformational Regenerative Integrated Biodiverse Agriculture for Livelihoods (TRIBAL)
project_type: Agriculture Forestry and Other Land Use
description:
The Transformational Regenerative Integrated Biodiverse Agriculture for Livelihoods (TRIBAL) Project is a landscape approach that aims to make it viable for small and marginal farmers to live off their land in a sustainable and profitable manner. 
The project will promote agroforestry and sustainable farming practices across within the Araku Valley in Vishakhapatnam District, Andhra Pradesh, India. Planned agroforestry and sustainable farming practices that will be promoted by the project include agroforestry utilizing both fruit and multi-purpose tree species, shade coffee systems, intercropping of pulses and millets, green manuring, mulching and organic composting. These activities will improve the livelihoods and well-being of the tribal landowners by achieving multiple objectives such as improved soil fertility, increased revenue generation, food security, reduced drudgery for women and increased biodiversity. Through this positive impact on climate, communities, and biodiversity the TRIBAL project aims to achieve both VCS and CCB Gold certification. 
This grouped project is being initiated in Paderu and Pedabayalu Mandals of Paderu Division in Vishakhapatnam District, with the intention of expanding to up to 11 Mandals within the Araku Valley landscape in future. The tribal people of this region were traditionally hunters and gatherers, relying on the forest for sustenance. The practice of shifting cultivation came in at the turn of the century. As the- forest began to get depleted, the tribal communities gradually become engaged in agriculture. Now, subsistence agriculture is the primary livelihood for nearly 99% of the tribes within the project region, with over 80% of the landholdings being less than one hectare in size.

name: Regenerative Agriculture with small holder farming communities of Bangladesh
project_type: Agriculture Forestry and Other Land Use
description: The SALM project in Bangladesh aims to address the negative impacts of conventional farming practices on the environment, particularly greenhouse gas emissions. The project includes a range of measures and technologies designed to reduce emissions by promoting regenerative and sustainable farming practices.The activities include efficient use of irrigation water, mulching, reduction of chemical fertilizer and pesticide use through the use of organic amendments, applying green manure, and alternative pest control methods, avoidance of crop residue burning, and minimum tillage.

name: Carbon Group Program for sustainable low carbon crop and grassland management in Argentina II
project_type: Agriculture Forestry and Other Land Use
description:
The project intends to include producers dedicated to extensive agriculture (corn, soybeans, wheat, sunflower, cotton, and other crops), and extensive cattle ranching, mostly cattle and grazing grasslands, pastures, agropastoral, and silvo-pastoral. Given the characteristics of the country, farm and ranch  production dates from no more than 200 years ago.
During most of the 20th century, the farms were managed in a rather extensive manner and with aggressive tillage systems, which caused widespread declines in the organic matter content of the soils. This lasted until the end of that century, when for different reasons the producers adopted zero tillage systems, which are what predominate today (more than 90%).
The projects to be implemented are expected to mitigate climate change both by reducing greenhouse gas (GHG) emissions and by capturing atmospheric carbon dioxide (CO2) and storing it as stable carbon in the soil, which must be recarbonized. The greatest efforts to reduce GHG emissions will be due to the adoption of better nitrogen fertilization technologies, which include alternative sources of nitrogen and variable rate fertilization that reduce nitrous oxide (N2) emissions from fertilized soils, the intensification of agricultural rotations with greater incorporation of winter crops, nitrogen fixing species and cover crops, and improved grazing management in livestock, which increase carbon stocks and with improvements in digestibility that reduce methane (CH4) emissions due to enteric fermentation. 
It is estimated that with these improvements, which are not currently widespread even among producers, it will be possible to reduce between 0.5 and 3 tons of CO2e/ha/year. Obviously, the total amount will depend on the area committed by the producers. This area is expected to reach more than 160 thousand hectares. If this is so, it is expected to mitigate almost 2 million tons CO2e at the end of this project.

name: Household Energy Efficiency Programme in East India
developer: C-Quest Capital SG India Holdings Private Limited
description:
The purpose of this grouped project activity is to reduce       greenhouse gas emissions in the rural/semi urban households in India, by introducing energy efficient cookstoves, which will lead to a decrease in the use of non-renewable biomass (e.g., firewood). The ICS disseminated through this project will replace the baseline cookstoves. 

The first instance under this grouped project, will be implemented within the state boundary of the eastern states of India i.e., West Bengal, Bihar, Odisha, Jharkhand etc. It is envisaged that a combination of improved cook stoves (ICS) shall be provided to end user communities to completely replace baseline stoves. The ICS are designed to operate at higher efficiencies than the baseline stoves and result in reduced wood consumption as compared to baseline scenario. The overall effect is reduced emission of carbon dioxide and smoke, improving air quality within the household as well as the quality of life of women folk. At present the total stove distribution under this project activity is set at 3,500,000 out of which 3,000,000 will be Baldwin stoves and 500,000 Dinabandhu stoves for end user households. Each home will receive either a single Dinabandhu Cookstove or two Baldwin Cookstoves as part of the distribution of the stoves. However, the number of stoves that will be given to end user will depend on various factors such as household size, it’s cooking requirement etc. and the project proponent and/or the implementing partner shall have the discretion to decide on the combination as well as number of stoves each beneficiary household will receive. This is to ensure that the end user is not forced to go back to using baseline stoves on account of one project stove not being able to cater to complete requirements of the household.

developer: C-Quest Capital SGT Asia Stoves Private Limited
description:
The project aims to reduce greenhouse gas emissions from cookstoves using wood fuel derived from non-renewable sources in household. The project to achieve its goal by making efficient improved cooking stoves (ICS) using renewable biomass, affordable and available to household users. The strategy will be to supply ICS for domestic cooking in urban and rural areas.

ICS will be distributed to urban and rural households where it will be used for daily cooking in replacement of traditional wood stoves. Households may receive more than one ICS, depending on their size and cooking habits. 

Carbon finance will be used to facilitate the purchase, distribution and marketing of stoves and renewable fuels, so making these products more affordable to users; without carbon finance, these activities would not take place. The end user will be informed that carbon finance is being generated using the ICS and renewable fuels, and this finance is in turn used to lower the sales price of the ICS.  
The household may receive an ICS to enable a switch to energy efficiency measure, Introduction of high efficiency biomass fired improved cook stoves to replace existing devices and reduce the use of non-renewable biomass for combustion (Sectoral Scope 03). The ICS are provided to the end-user at no cost to them.

Through this project, the distribution and installation of approximately 2,50,000 SSM S-32-X and 2,50,000 locally produced “Naga Cookstove” will be undertaken for households in Cambodia. Each household will receive up to 2 ICS per household. Other ICS models may be added based on the requirement of end users. name: Yongji MSW Incineration Project
developer: Yongji Huaxinda Clean Energy Co., Ltd
project_type: Energy industries (renewable/non-renewable sources); Waste handling and disposal
description:
Yongji MSW Incineration Project is located between the Xiachao Village of the Chengbei Street and the Gucheng Village of the Kaizhang town, Yongji City, Shanxi Province, P.R. China. The Project is invested, constructed and operated by Yongji Huaxinda Cleaning Energy Co., Ltd.. 
With two 300t/d MSW combustion production lines, the project will treat 600 tons of MSW per day. The combustion system is composed of two 300t/d mechanical grate incinerators, matched with one set of 12MW steam turbine generator. The project will process 250,000 tons of MSW every year, and consume 130.3 tons of 0# light diesel as auxiliary fuel. The MSW combustion line will work 8,000 hours every year, generating 72,748 MWh electricity, of which 59,972 MWh will be exported to the North China Power Grid (NCPG). The implementation of the project will meet the requirement of local MSW harmless treatment, and significantly improve local environment. Also helps reduce GHG emission that would occur in baseline scenarios such as power generating by fossil-fuel fired plants and MSW treatment at landfill.
By combusting MSW that would otherwise be disposed of at landfill, the project avoids the emissions of methane that would be generated under landfill condition. In the meanwhile, the proposed project can produce steam to generate power to replace the electricity that would otherwise be generated by fossil- fuel fired power plants which are connected to the NCPG. The baseline scenario of this project is the same as the scenario prior to the implementation of the project, namely the landfill gas is vented directly and the equivalent power is supplied by the NCPG.
It is estimated that during the 10-year fixed crediting period of the project (from 30 June 2021 to 29 June 2031), the average annual GHG emission reductions will be 63,176 tCO2e.

name: COMACO Landscape Management Project-South
project_type: Agriculture Forestry and Other Land Use
description:
This project description document covers COMACO operations in part of the Central province (Mumbwa and Shibuyunji districts) and part of Southern province (Itezhi-Tezhi district) of Zambia. The COMACO Landscape Management Project – South (CLMP-South) promotes sustainable agriculture and forest management. The key objectives of the project are to increase smallholder farmer agricultural productivity, provide alternative livelihoods and reduce uncontrolled forest loss and degradation. Hence, the project comprises two components:
1. Sustainable Agricultural Land Management (SALM) component – which aims to promote widespread adoption of agricultural practices including conservation agriculture and agroforest that increases the food production per unit area and farmers’ income. The project promotes the adoption by farmers of legume-based alley cropping, residues management (e.g. mulching; cessation of residue burning), use of organic fertilizers such as composite and animal manure, and reduced tillage among other SALM practices and the intercropping of Gliricidia Sepium as part of Agroforestry to restore soil quality and sequestrate carbon.
2. REDD+ (Avoided Unplanned Deforestation) component – which aims to reduce forest loss, and protect and expand areas under natural forest, and conserve biodiversity. This is achieved primarily through land use planning and creation of Community Conservation Areas (CCAs) for protection of natural forest, coupled with sustainable non-extractive forest use, e.g. honey and mushrooms. The creation of CCAs and the enforcement of by-laws to protect them promotes the protection of ecosystems and biodiversity within and around the CCAs.

name: PROJECT TOURBA - ADOPTION OF IMPROVED AGRICULTURAL PRACTICES TOWARDS CARBON FARMING IN MOROCCO
project_type: Agriculture Forestry and Other Land Use
description:
The Carbon Credit project in Morocco initiated by Innovx proposes regenerative agricultural practices, focusing on conservation agriculture and crop nutrient stewardship. It aims to enhance agricultural soil health in six regions: Rabat-Salé-Kenitra, Beni Mellal-Khenifra, Marrakech-Safi, Tangier-Tetouan-Al Hoceima, Fes-Meknes (including the provinces of Fes, Meknes, Taounate, El Hajeb, Moulay Yacoub, Sefrou), and Casablanca-Settat (including the provinces of Casablanca, Settat, Berrechid, Benslimane, El Jaddida). The initiative covers 750,000 hectares, starting with 50,000 hectares in the first year and expanding annually.
The project targets application of regenerative agriculture at scale with the help of Employing Sustainable Agricultural Land Management (SALM) technology including conservation agriculture and reduced application of nitrogen, that results in increased crop yields, food security, diversified farmer income, and climate change mitigation through elevated soil carbon and plant biomass.
The Project is aligned with the Moroccan Ministry's goal to transition one million hectares to Zero-tillage by 2030, the project operates with a 10-year crediting period under the VCS-approved Methodology VM0017. Estimated annual average Emission Reductions (ER) reach 1402165, totalling 14021652 over the project duration. This initiative integrates environmental conservation, socio-economic development, and sustainable agriculture in Morocco's specified regions.

name: KSM Forest Carbon Project.
