name: Brascarbon Methane Recovery Project BCA-BRA-18
developer: Brascarbon Consultoria Projetos e Representacao S/A
description:
The purpose of BRASCARBON Methane Recovery Project BCA-BRA-18 project is to utilize the effluent produced on a total of 7 pig farms in the state of Mato Grosso do Sul, cities of Jarei and Gloria de Dourados, Brazil, to capture methane and generate biogas. The projects have the potential to generate energy from waste using the biogas produced and captured. Regardless this potential, energy will not be a part of this project activity.
Before the project activity, local farmers considered waste as an externality in the pig production process. As such, minimal finance was allocated to this issue and wastewater was often treated in open water lagoons – frequently with profound environmental impacts. The projects demonstrate how the construction of a set of new, covered, in-ground anaerobic digesters can utilize the organic material from the animal operations to produce biogas and fertilizer, whilst reducing greenhouse gas emissions.
The   basis   of   the   projects   is   the   anaerobic   digestion, whereby microorganisms break down biodegradable material in the absence of oxygen. As part of an integrated waste management system, anaerobic digestion reduces the emission of greenhouse gases into the atmosphere and produces a rich biogas, suitable for energy production, which can be used to replace fossil fuels. The nutrient-rich solids left after digestion are used as fertilizer and the better wastewater management allows more water for irrigation.

name: Brascarbon Methane Recovery Project BCA-BRA-19
developer: Brascarbon Consultoria Projetos e Representacao S/A
description:
The purpose of BRASCARBON Methane Recovery Project BCA-BRA-19 project is to utilize the effluent produced on a total of 10 pig farms in the state of Mato Grosso do Sul, in Brazil, to capture methane and generate biogas. The projects have the potential to generate energy from waste using the biogas produced and captured. Regardless this potential, energy will not be a part of this project activity.
Before the project activity, local farmers considered waste as an externality in the pig production process. As such, minimal finance was allocated to this issue and wastewater was often treated in open water lagoons – frequently with profound environmental impacts. The projects demonstrate how the construction of a set of new, covered, in-ground anaerobic digesters can utilize the organic material from the animal operations to produce biogas and fertilizer, whilst reducing greenhouse gas emissions.
The   basis   of   the   projects   is   the   anaerobic   digestion, whereby microorganisms break down biodegradable material in the absence of oxygen. As part of an integrated waste management system, anaerobic digestion reduces the emission of greenhouse gases into the atmosphere and produces a rich biogas, suitable for energy production, which can be used to replace fossil fuels. The nutrient-rich solids left after digestion are used as fertilizer and the better wastewater management allows more water for irrigation.

name: Aksai Sustainable Grassland Management Project
developer: Beijing Qianyuhui Environmental Technology Co., Ltd.
project_type: Agriculture Forestry and Other Land Use
description: The objective of the project is to restore the degraded grassland ecosystem through the sustainable grassland management practices, such as increasing the rotation of grazing between summer and winter pastures, limiting the grazing days on degraded pastures, and replanting with perennial grasses and ensuring appropriate management over the long-term, thereby increasing carbon sequestration, and promoting local development. The project is located in Aksai Kazakh Autonomous County, Jiuquan City, Gansu Province of China.

name: Leveraging carbon finance for smallholder farmers in India
developer: Value Network Ventures Advisory Services PTE. LTD
project_type: Agriculture Forestry and Other Land Use
description: The sustainable farming project aims to implement various technologies and measures to reduce greenhouse gas (GHG) emissions and enhance carbon sequestration. The project seeks to promote sustainable agricultural practices, including the adoption of conservation agriculture, agroforestry, and efficient use of water and energy.

name: Motor Verde+Floresta Forestry Carbon Project. Portugal Central Region I
project_type: Agriculture Forestry and Other Land Use
description:
Refloresta Portugal, Forestry Carbon Project (Central Region I) consists of the implementation of reforestation projects located in burned areas in Portugal. This project is part of Motor Verde, an offsetting initiative promoted by Fundación Repsol, based on Mediterranean forest reforestation and regeneration aiming for a triple goal social, environmental and economic. 
The project proponents of this single project are Grupo Sylvestris and Fundación Repsol. Sylvestris is a forestry consultancy located in Madrid, Spain, specialised in forestry restoration, rural development and environmental consulting, Spain; and Fundación Repsol is the fund responsible for Repsol’s social responsibility vocation. Both entities are connected by the fund's shareholding in Sylvestris. The project counts on Metsä, the project implementing partner, a local forestry consultancy located in Abrantes, Portugal, close to the affected areas to be restored.
The project intends to establish approximately 56,51 ha of Mediterranean forest. Plantations are being established in private-owned land located in the mid-centre of Portugal. These lands have been burned by 2017 and 2019 fires, where natural regeneration is inexistent. 
The project will generate GHG removals by the plantation growing, using native species such as Quercus suber and Pinus pinaster, among others. A total amount of 16,566 tonnes of CO2e are expected to be generated by the implementation of the project, equivalent to an average of 414 tonnes of CO2 per year, taking into account that this amount varies annually depending on the corresponding compensation.
Economic, environmental and social benefits are expected: 
-	recovering burned ecosystems with native species
-	creating jobs in the implementation areas,
-	contributing to minimise the risk of depopulation,
-	investing in natural resources, that allows a sustainable business development,
-	promoting the innovation and research for new technologies application in forestry

name: Sichuan Yuexi IFM Project
developer: Lingguan State-Owned Forest Protection Bureau of Yuexi County
project_type: Agriculture Forestry and Other Land Use
description:
Sichuan Yuexi IFM Project (herein after referred as “The project”) is located in Yuexi County, Sichuan
Province, China. The geographical coordinates of the project area are 102.389°-102.891°E, 28.332°-
28.857°N. This project improves GHG emissions reductions from forest management practices by
increasing on-land carbon stocks by extending the rotation period of a forest or a small area of forest
before harvesting. By extending the age at which trees are felled, projects increase the average
carbon stock on the land and remove more emissions from the atmosphere.
The total area of the project is 18,959.15 ha in Yuexi County. All the trees are native species,
including Pinus armandi, Alder and Pinus yunnanensis.
The project aims to mitigate the effects of climate change by increasing the average carbon stock on the
land and removing more emissions from the atmosphere by extending the age at which trees are felled,
thereby promoting sustainable forest management, productive activities and improving community
welfare. The project also seeks to protect biodiversity and high conservation values, enhance ecological
connectivity, and protect the natural habitats of vulnerable species, both those under some kind of threat
and those of ecological interest.
Moreover, expected GHG reductions corresponds to an annual average of 239,399 tCO2, so for the
lifetime of 60 years it could demonstrate reductions up to 14,363,970 tCO2.

name: Incentivizing Sustainable Maize Farming through Carbon Finance
project_type: Agriculture Forestry and Other Land Use
description: The project aims to promote sustainable agriculture practices among maize farmers and mitigate greenhouse gas emissions through the use of carbon finance mechanisms. The project will work with maize farmers in Belagavi to adopt sustainable farming practices, including the reduction of fertilizers and pesticides, crop mixing, and improving soil health. These practices will help reduce greenhouse gas emissions and improve the quality of soil, leading to increased crop yields and enhanced livelihoods for farmers.

name: Monsoon Methane Avoidance from Industrial Wastewater in Malaysia Grouped Project
description:
The Grouped Project will implement biogas recovery, flaring and/or utilization systems for industrial wastewater treatment in Malaysia. The Grouped Project will reduce greenhouse gas (GHG) emissions from industrial facilities by capturing biogas generated in open wastewater treatment systems instead of allowing biogas to escape to the atmosphere.

The first Project Activity Instance (PAI1) is the Langkap Biogas Plant, implemented at Langkap, in the State of Perak, Malaysia, about 80km south from the city of Perak and 150km north of Kuala Lumpur. PAI1 will treat wastewater from a palm oil mill, by installing a biogas digester system within the existing wastewater treatment system at the mill. It will also treat the biogas and use it to generate electricity for supply to the national electricity grid.

name: Heilongjiang Meilisi Improved Agricultural Land Management Project
developer: Heilongjiang Tanlv Ecological Resources Development Co., Ltd.
project_type: Agriculture Forestry and Other Land Use
description:
Heilongjiang Meilisi Improved Agricultural Land Management Project (hereinafter referred to as “the project”) is a project that change the pre-existing agricultural manag Heilongjiang Meilisi Improved Agricultural Land Management Project ement activities (conventional tillage) to the conservation agriculture management in fields located in Meilisi Daur district, Qiqihar city, Heilongjiang province, China. 
The project is expected to reduce GHG emissions by applying the conservation agriculture management. The conservation agriculture refers to a sustainable agricultural technology that can reduce farmland soil erosion, protect farmland ecological environment and achieve coordinated development of ecological benefits, economic benefits and social benefits through comprehensive supporting measures such as less tillage, no tillage, irrigation water management, residue management, surface covering and rational planting. Since the conservation agriculture can reduce soil disturbance and reduce the loss of soil organic carbon (SOC). Moreover, the project is expected to increase SOC by straw returning, since straw contains a large amount of organic matter and trace elements such as nitrogen, phosphorus, and potassium, returning straw to the field can effectively use organic fertilizer resources and increase soil organic matter (SOM).

name: OKINAWA EV PROJECT IN INDIA
description: The purpose of this project activity is the introduction and distribution of electric two-wheelers which will displace the use of fossil fuel-based mainly motor gasoline-fueled vehicles in the transportation sector. The project is owned and implemented by Okinawa Autotech Internationall Private Limited. In the absence of the proposed project activity, the beneficiaries/users would have been used the motor gasoline-powered two-wheelers for the transportation purpose which will lead to greenhouse emissions into the atmosphere

name: Sichuan Cangxi Improved Agricultural Land Management Project
developer: Sichuan Cangxi Urban Investment Carbon Sink Technology Co., Ltd.
project_type: Agriculture Forestry and Other Land Use
description:
Sichuan Cangxi Improved Agricultural Land Management Project (hereinafter referred to as “the project”) is located in Cangxi County in Sichuan Province, China. The purpose of the project is to adopt improved agricultural land management practices including returning straw in fields and applying organic fertilizer, and to prevent the severe soil degradation caused by pre-existing conventional tillage in local crop land.
The project implemented straw returning and organic fertilizer in 38,381 ha field to increase soil organic carbon (SOC) and reduce nitrous oxide emission, and the crops involved in the project are the wheat, corn and soybean. The project proponent not only introduced more efficient and appropriate tillage method to the farmers, but also provide technical training and support to the farmers.

name: BAMBOO MONTEMILONE
project_type: Agriculture Forestry and Other Land Use
description: Reforestation project with the use of bamboo plants on 35 hectares in the municipality of montemilone region of basilicata country italy10

name: Incentivising regenerative cotton farming through carbon finance
project_type: Agriculture Forestry and Other Land Use
description: The AFOLU Carbon project focuses on reducing greenhouse gas (GHG) emissions from cotton cultivation through a variety of measures and technologies The project will engage with medium, small and marginal farmers and promote managing the use of synthetic fertilizers, reduce the use of fossil fuels in cotton cultivation by promoting more efficient ways for irrigation and encourage the implementation of agroforestry practices.

name: Family Forest Carbon Project
project_type: Agriculture Forestry and Other Land Use
description: Family forests make up over one-third of America’s 765 million acres of forestland, according to a 2021 Congressional report. This fact puts management decisions providing clean water, recreation, and other valuable resources in the hands of everyday American families. The importance of American forests to the global ecosystem and climate is central to the work of Forest Carbon Works, PBC, a US based company that seeks to conserve and restore family-owned tracts of forestland throughout the United States. Forest Carbon Works is acutely aware of vulnerabilities particular to family forest owners. Without an alternative form of income, families face pressures to liquidate their timber to cover unforeseen expenses. By the year 2030, Forest Carbon Works anticipates protecting 500,000 acres of land owned by many individuals with durable agreements of permanent carbon storage. The project longevity shall be at minimum 60 years with possible extension to 100. Extending rotation ages on these at-risk forests increases carbon storage relative to the baseline case, as well as increases biodiversity and diversity in forest structure. Estimated average GHG emission reductions from the project are 845,991 tons CO2 equivalent per year, with total reductions over the first 25-year project crediting period of 21,149,786 tCO2e.  This is a grouped project. The geographic area of the entire project shall encompass is the contiguous United States and southern Alaska. To ensure sustainability in management, Forest Carbon Works requires enrolled forestland to be certified by the Forest Stewardship Council ® (FSC®) under the group certificate SCS-FM/COC-009247 prior to the commencement of any harvesting activities.

name: Hainan Grassland Sustainable Management Project
project_type: Agriculture Forestry and Other Land Use
description: The Hainan Grassland Sustainable Management Project is located in Hainan Tibetan Autonomous Prefecture, Qinghai Province, China, with a total area of 184,352.04 hectares. The local grassland environment had already been deteriorating because of overgrazing and climate change before the project was put into action. By reseeding grass and using sustainable grassland management techniques including rest grazing, rotational grazing, hazardous plant control, and insect control, the project aims to restore the local damaged grassland ecosystem. The project enhances the grassland covering, boosts carbon sequestration, and contributes to local development. With an average yearly GHG emission removal of 534,995 tCO2e, the project is expected to produce GHG emission removals of 21,399,792 tCO2e in 40 years.

name: REDD+ Café Apuí Agroflorestal
developer: Amazonia Agroflorestal Comercializacao de Produtos Agroflorestais Ltda
project_type: Agriculture Forestry and Other Land Use
description:
The REDD+ Café Apuí Agroforestry (CAA) project aims to expand the production chain of agroforestry coffee in southeastern Amazonas and avoid deforestation of native forests on rural properties in the municipalities of Apuí, Manicoré and Novo Aripuanã, in the state of Amazonas, Brazil. In the absence of the project, forests on the participating properties would be cleared for agricultural activities, especially pastures, for income generation.

REDD+ CAA is a 30-year grouped project that will have periodic membership of new participants over the first ten years. The initial project's participants are 42 family farmers (Project Activity Instances – PAI) that totalize a PA of 3.696 hectares around the town of Apuí (50km) in Amazonas State/Brazil. The project has a defined geographical area within which instances of project activities are located, totalling 19,874 km2. This area is composed of native forests and agricultural areas, mainly planted pastures, in addition to some enclaves of non-forest pioneer formations.

The project is based on long-term (30-yr) agreements with landowners to avoid deforestation in their areas in exchange for performance-based payment for avoided deforestation. In addition to monitoring, reporting, verification, and leakage mitigation activities, VCU revenues will be invested in agroforestry implementation, technical assistance, organic certification processes, administration, and marketing of coffee and other agroforestry products. The project aims to expand agroforestry coffee production using agroecological techniques and trained personnel in organic production promoted since 2012 in the region.

The project intends to generate climate, community and biodiversity benefits under CCB standard. The payment for avoided deforestation, investment in the agroforestry coffee chain, and support for the structuring of new agroforestry product chains offer an alternative sustainable income to producers while maintaining conserved forests.

name: Kalahari Grasslands Project
project_type: Agriculture Forestry and Other Land Use
description: Cattle ranching is one of the main pillars of Botswana’s largely agrarian society: livestock is the primary source of subsistence and income for two-thirds of rural households.  Furthermore, Botswana’s urban population is rapidly growing, increasing demand for food, land and fuel. This growth has taken place in tandem with threats to natural resources in the form of  rangeland degradation, loss of grazing habitat, and the over-exploitation of wildlife. The KALAHARI GRASSLANDS PROJECT (KGP) is a grouped project located in the heart of Botswana’s Kalahari, a semi-arid grassland and shrubland ecosystems. Since 2016, Botswana has lost over 800,000+ hectares of Wildlife Management Areas (GH10, GH11, SO2, and KW6) partly due to the ongoing cycle of land degradation and encroachment into nearby areas. The central piece of legislation regulating designated land use on protected wildlife areas is the Wildlife Conservation and National Parks Act of 1992, § 3(15)(2) and enables the President to rezone and/or modify WMAs. Currently, most ranchers across Botswana operate an average ranch of 5 hectares with a few head of cattle and lack an understanding of carrying capacity resulting in overgrazing. The lack of enforcement mechanisms to prevent encroachment past communal grazing lands into WMAs coupled with Big-Agriculture interests converting rangeland into commercial cattle operations has resulted in the degradation of over 91,000 km² or 15.5% of Botswana. The KGP program was launched to provide an alternative to land conversion for landowners and game ranchers located in high-risk areas adjacent to WMAs and other wildlife corridors. By leveraging the voluntary carbon market the KGP protects both the biodiversity and sequestration potential of these critical areas. The main agents of conversion, private landowners, forego their legal right to convert native grasslands, and in doing so avoid GHG emissions totaling over 2.23M mt/CO2e over 10 years.

name: Strengthening capacity through regenerative solutions for native sugarcane farmers in Maharashtra, India
project_type: Agriculture Forestry and Other Land Use
description: The objective of the proposed VCS Sustainable Agricultural Land Management (SALM) project activity aims to transition the farmers into practicing more sustainable cultivation practices in sugarcane production. The SALM project is expected to reduce greenhouse gas (GHG) emissions or increase sequestration of carbon in soil and biomass.These sustainable practices will improve the soils of the farmers and enhance their resilience to climate change

name: Guizhou Zhongzhichang CMM Power Generation Project
developer: Guizhou Yuezhong Comprehensive Energy Co., Ltd.
description:
Guizhou Zhongzhichang CMM Power Generation Project (hereinafter referred to as the Project) will utilize the low concentration coal mine methane (CMM) from Zhongzhichang coal mine for power generation to supply electricity to the coal mine where the Project is located and to China Southern Power Grid (CSPG) if there is any electricity surplus. The Project is located in Hongguo Town, Panzhou City, Liupanshui City, Guizhou Province, China.
The purpose of the Project is to utilize the extracted CMM with low concentration methane concentration to produce electricity. No coal bed methane (CBM) or ventilation air methane (VAM) utilization is involved. Seven sets of CMM power generators will be installed with a total installed capacity of 6.4MW (2*0.7MW+5*1MW), destroying 12.1 million m3 of methane annually. At the first operation year, it is expected the installed capacity will be 3.4MW (2*0.7MW+2*1MW). After the full operation of the Project after the second operation year, the expected annual exported electricity will be 32,998 MWh, which will be supplied to the coal mine first through the electricity distribution network in Zhongzhichang coal mine area, and then to China Southern Power Grid (CSPG) if there is any electricity surplus, replacing the electricity that would otherwise have been purchased from the CSPG and displace part of the electricity generated by CSPG dominated by fossil fuel-fired power plants.

name: Aksaray Landfill Gas Power Plant Project
project_type: Energy industries (renewable/non-renewable sources); Waste handling and disposal
description:
The Aksaray Solid Waste Management System and Electricity Generation Facility (hereafter named as “ the Aksaray LFG”) (1.414 MWe) is situated in the province of Aksaray, in the Merkez District, and is owned and operated by Biotrend. The facility is designed to process municipal waste from Aksaray province, classified as type-2 sanitary landfill, and serves a total of 8 districts. The facility consists of four key areas: a sanitary landfill, a mechanical separation facility, a compost facility, and an electricity generation facility. 
The Aksaray LFG plant has obtained a generation license from EMRA, with an expected annual generation of 42 420 .00 0 kWh/year. The project's first crediting period is set at 7 years, with expected average annual emission reductions of 29,019.74. Through this project, waste is stabilized, waste storage is minimized, electricity is produced, and negative environmental impacts are eliminated.

name: Sharjah Waste to Energy Plant project
project_type: Energy industries (renewable/non-renewable sources); Waste handling and disposal
description: Solid Waste to Energy Production Facility Sharjah UAE project (hereinafter referred as “the Project”) is invested and operated by SHARJAH ENVIRONMENT COMPANY LLC 1st Floor Lagoon Tower, Corniche Road, Sharjah UAE P.O. Box 20248 Sharjah. The purpose of the project is to dispose the municipal solid waste through incineration, and simultaneously utilizing the residual heat for power generation.

name: Sepoti REDD Project
project_type: Agriculture Forestry and Other Land Use
description:
The primary objective of the Sepoti REDD Project is to avoid unplanned deforestation (AUD) of a region within the municipalities of Novo Aripuanã and Borba. The first Project activity instance has 26,062 ha project area, which is within one private properties in Novo Aripuanã, consisting of 100% Amazon rainforest.

It is expected that, with the carbon project, it will be possible to expand the monitoring of the area, hiring new professionals to work on the farms. In addition to the project’s ecological and carbon benefits, a proportion of the carbon credits generated will be dedicated to improving the social and environmental conditions in the project region, specifically contributing to improving deforestation control, aiming at the propagation of environmental awareness, generation of alternative sources of income and environmental education actions.

The present REDD project is expected to avoid predicted 1,888 ha of deforestation, equating to 782,072 tCO2e in emissions reductions over the 30-year project lifetime, with an annual average of 26,069 tCO2e.

name: Linzhang Biogas Recovery and Utilization Project
developer: Zhonghuan Xinwei Green Technology (Lin Zhang) Co., Ltd.
project_type: Energy industries (renewable/non-renewable sources); Livestock, enteric fermentation, and manure management; Transport
description:
This project is a step towards supporting disposal and comprehensive utilization of animal waste in Hebei Province, one of the agriculture production bases in North China. This project has installed an environmentally friendly manure treatment solution: a system to produce bio-natural gas through plug-in dry fermentation treatment of manure collected from local livestock farms. Solid bio-organic fertilizer and liquid fertilizer are the by-products. The bio-natural gas is to be used in the transportation sector to displace traditional fossil CNG. 
Prior to the implementation of the project, manure is stored at individual livestock farms in uncovered anaerobic lagoons over a retention period of a couple of months before they were used for agriculture application as fertilizer, directly without any treatment. Significant amount of Greenhouse Gases (GHG), such as methane could be emitted directly into the atmosphere. 
From the perspective of bio-CNG produced by this project, without the project the fossil origin CNG would be continuously used by the transportation applications. 
The successful implementation of the project prevents GHG emissions, methane in particular, as well as generate a clean renewable energy that displaces fossil fuel CNG.

name: Distribution of fuel efficient improved cookstoves in Kenya and Uganda
description: The proposed group project aims to reduce greenhouse gas emissions by distributing fuel efficient improved cookstoves (ICS) to households in Kenya and Uganda. The goal of the project is to replace traditional cookstoves with the ICS, which are designed to burn wood more efficiently and save fuel by distributing approximately 200,000 ICS to households. The improved cook stoves will replace 3-stone fire, which is the predominant stove in the project area. By using the ICS, fuel consumption will be reduced, thereby reducing the time required for wood collection or reducing costs for firewood for households purchasing wood. The improved efficiency of the stove will also lead to reduced indoor air pollution, thereby improving the health situation especially of women and children.

name: Tianjun Grassland Sustainable Management Project
project_type: Agriculture Forestry and Other Land Use
description: Tianjun County Sustainable Grassland Management Project is located in Haixi Mongol and Tibetan Autonomous Prefecture, Qinghai Province, China. The project aims to restore degraded grasslands in Tianjun County, through degraded grassland improvement (including grass reseeding, fertilization, fence construction), sandy grassland management, rest grazing, rotational grazing and harmful weed control. As a result, 89,123 hectares degraded grassland has been managed sustainably.

name: Rewilding Maforki
project_type: Agriculture Forestry and Other Land Use
description: The Rewilding Maforki grouped project aims to recover low intensity and unproductive grasslands in Port Loko District, in the Northwest Province of Sierra Leone. Strategic activities to restore and conserve the areas will include tree nursery, tree planting , care and management of the tree plantation, prevention of pest and illegal activities within the project areas. The project will generate GHG removals by the plantation of indigenous species.
abuse_descr: People in affected communities in Port Loko allege that they did not consent in the required form to the planting of trees. Many of them neither know what carbon credits are, nor that their land will be forest-locked for decades. Moreover, little do they know how much money the companies will be making with their land. Sierra Leone’s Customary Land Rights Act states that at least 60% of the adult members of land-owning families must give their consent before any land transaction. Women enjoy the same rights to land as men under the Customary Land Rights Act. The consent must be informed, in writing, witnessed by the Paramount Chiefs, and registered with the authorities. Land surveying, clearing activities, and tree planting in Port Loko have started before any documents were signed, in breach of the Customary Land Rights Act.
abuseuno_id: Carbon done wrong. Controversial carbon credit project in Sierra Leone threatens people’s land rights
abusedue_id: ‘Saviour of carbon markets’ faces questions over African land rights

name: Subei Sustainable Grassland Management Project
developer: Beijing Qianyuhui Environmental Technology Co., Ltd.
project_type: Agriculture Forestry and Other Land Use
description: The objective of the project is to restore the degraded grassland ecosystem through the sustainable grassland management practices, such as increasing the rotation of grazing between summer and winter pastures, limiting the grazing days on degraded pastures, and replanting with perennial grasses and ensuring appropriate management over the long-term, thereby increasing carbon sequestration, and promoting local development. Totally, 326,819.9 ha of degraded grassland will be restore in Subei Mongilia Autonomous County, Jiuquan City, Gansu Province, China.

name: HISAR BIOGAS POWER PLANT
description:
HISAR BIOGAS POWER PLANT is a greenfield biogas-to-energy project that captures biogas from animal manure, cattle and chicken manure in particular, -via anaerobic digestion- and utilizes it to generate thermal and electric energy through cogeneration units. The animal manure as the main feedstock is collected from the neighboring animal farms with special trucks and transferred to the plant. Continuously Stirred Tank Reactor (CSTR) type anaerobic digesters are used to capture methane-rich biogas. Captured biogas is then utilized in cogeneration units. Waste heat from gas engines is utilized mainly for heating anaerobic fermenters. The generated electricity is not only supplied to the national grid but is also used as auxiliary/internal consumption required for the plant to function. Solid and liquid fermented products as by-products of biogas generation processes taken place at the project site are distributed to neighbouring agricultural farms as fertilizer.
The project is being implemented by HİSAR BİOGAZ TARIM VE HAYVANCILIK A.Ş., the Project Owner, Eskişehir province, in Turkey. The project began to collect animal waste from
neighbouring animal farms and generate electricity on July 06, 2021. Thus, the start date of the project and the crediting period is determined as July 06, 2021.
The project activity avoids methane emission through the above-mentioned capture and utilization processes. Furthermore, the project reduces CO2 emissions from fossil-fuel-based electricity generation by supplying biogas-based electricity to the national grid. 
This project adopts the renewable crediting period of 7 years, twice renewable for a total of 21 years. The estimated average net annual emission reductions are 210,728 tCO2eq/y. Accordingly, the project is expected to generate 1,475,096 tCO2eq/y emissions reduction during the first crediting period.

name: Haishang Shaoyang Composting Project
developer: Shaoyang County Haishang Ecological Agriculture Technology Co., Ltd.
project_type: Livestock, enteric fermentation, and manure management; Waste handling and disposal
description: Haishang Shaoyang Composting Project (hereinafter referred to as the project) locates in Sanxing Village, Jinchengshi Town, Shaoyang County, Shaoyang City, Hunan Province, P.R China. The project is owned and implemented by Shaoyang County Haishang Ecological Agriculture Technology Co., Ltd. (hereinafter referred to as the project owner).

name: Ordu Landfill Gas to Electricity Project
developer: Ordu Yenilenebilir Enerji Elektrik Üretim Sanayi ve Ticaret Anonim Şirketi
project_type: Energy industries (renewable/non-renewable sources); Waste handling and disposal
description:
In order to provide an environmentally friendly and sustainable municipal solid waste management system, Ordu Landfill Gas to Electricity Project is being implemented by Ordu
Yenilenebilir Enerji Elektrik Üretim Sanayi ve Ticaret Anonim Şirketi The project is built within the premises of the Ordu Landfill Facility in the Çaybaşı district of Ordu province . The Solid Waste Landfill Site is located on a total area of 132,84 37 m 2 1 The project start date is 24 June 2021 , and w ithin the crediting period between 24 June 2021 and 23 June 202 8 landfill gas is extracted, and electrical energy is obtained. The project activity includes capturing and utilizing landfill gas (landfill gas contains approximately 50 % methane and is a potent greenhouse gas) for power generation, which would have been vented to the atmosphere in the pre project/business as usual scenario. It has been determined that an average of 300 350 tonnes/day of waste will be stored in the landfill . The waste composition that the project receives has 7 8.4 2 organic materials.

name: CLEAN COOKSTOVE FOR GARO COMMUNITIES
description:
The proposed project aims at reducing the fuel wood consumption in traditional cook stoves by disseminating improved cook stoves (ICS) at a highly reduced cost of 200 INR. The transition from traditional to improved cookstoves will help in achieving significant firewood consumption that will enable climate change mitigation in a sustainable manner. Overall objective of the project is to improve the lives of the rural women by providing them with efficient cooking technology. This project will not only empower women, but also decrease fuelwood consumption at household level which will enable reduction of carbon emissions at a global scale. The project will ensure that just sources of renewable biomass are used that are in line with the requirements according to Glossary of CDM terms v 11.0.
The existing scenario prior to the implementation of the project activity involves the usage of traditional mud cookstoves with poor ventilation, causing excessive indoor air pollution (IAP) and has been a serious health risk for women and children who spend several hours in the kitchen. The State of Meghalaya has an abundance of forest reserves and the ethnic communities rely on firewood for cooking. The state has three hill regions of the united Khasi and Jaintia Hills and Garo Hills. Garo Hills comprises of five district and the communities rely on traditional cooking practices and sources firewood from nearby forests. Penetration of modern cooking mediums like LPG gas, electric induction etc. have remained out of bound for most households in the region. The project activity is aimed to implement 20,000 cookstoves in the Meghalaya state of India. The Project activity had started distribution of Improved Cookstoves from 19th October 2022. The estimated annual emission reductions for this crediting period are 8,05,612 tCO2e and 1,15,087 tCO2e/year.

name: Vega Diyarbakir Waste to Energy Project
project_type: Energy industries (renewable/non-renewable sources); Waste handling and disposal
description:
In order to develop a municipal solid waste management system that will be environmentally friendly and sustainable, Vega Diyarbakir Waste to Energy Project is being implemented by Vega Diyarbakır Atık Yönetim ve Enerji Üretim Sanayi Ticaret ve Anonim Şirketi. The project activity is a methane gas power generating plant with a licensed capacity of 14.509 MWe. The project was commissioned with the generation of electricity from June 11th, 2021, which is regarded as the project start date. The project's lifetime is 15 years, according to the EMRA Generation License.  
For sustainable waste management where municipal waste is utilized, the rehabilitation of the Diyarbakır Solid Waste Disposal Site, which receives approximately 1,500 tons of municipal waste from different districts of Diyarbakir province on a daily basis, and the generation of renewable electricity from landfill gas was planned and the rehabilitation project was approved by the Ministry of Environment and Urbanization in Turkey.
The main goal and objective of the project in the near future is the rehabilitation of the Diyarbakir Solid Waste Disposal Site and the generation of renewable electricity from landfill gas, as well as the introduction of the organic fraction separated by the planned separation unit and digester units into the controlled anaerobic digestion process and methane recovery from organic waste. Methane recovered from the digestion and landfill site is combusted through gas engines and the resulting electricity is supplied to the grid. The project is located in Yukarıakdibek, Baglar district city of Diyarbakir, in Turkey.
The expected average annual emission reductions are 182,826 tCO2eq/y. Accordingly, the project is expected to generate 1,279,780  tCO2eq emissions reduction throughout its first crediting period.

name: Biogas to electricity generation group project in India
project_type: Energy industries (renewable/non-renewable sources); Waste handling and disposal
description:
EKI Energy Services Ltd. is in the process of implementing grouped project based on biogas from cattle manure at different locations across various States and Union Territories in
India. The primary objective of the project is to effectively demonstrate the use of anaerobic biogas digesters to generate biogas based renewable energy connected with off grid. Thus, project will achieve an environment friendly way of managing wastes and renewable power generation by utilizing the wastes

name: HEFEI BIOGAS RECOVERY AND UTILIZATION PROJECT
project_type: Energy industries (renewable/non-renewable sources); Livestock, enteric fermentation, and manure management; Waste handling and disposal
description: Hefei Biogas Recovery and Utilization Project (hereinafter referred to as the project) locates in Feidong County, Hefei City, Anhui Province, P.R China. The project is owned and implemented by Hefei Modern Energy Co., Ltd. (hereinafter referred to as the project owner). The project is to collect methane from manure treatment at Modern Farming Feidong Farm in Feidong County, Hefei City, Anhui Province. The project treats the raw manure from 18,000 dairy cows annually by anaerobic digester, and uses the biogas generated during the treatment process for power generation. The electricity generated by the project will be transmitted to East China Power Grid (ECPG). The project is expected to produce 42,400 m3 biogas per day. All the manure is collected and transferred to the anaerobic digester. After anaerobic digestion, the digestate is sent out and used for agriculture fertilization aerobically in the nearby farmlands.

name: WUHE BIOGAS RECOVERY AND UTILIZATION PROJECT
project_type: Energy industries (renewable/non-renewable sources); Livestock, enteric fermentation, and manure management
description: Wuhe Biogas Recovery and Utilization Project (hereinafter referred to as the project) locates in Wuhe County, Bengbu City, Anhui Province, P.R China. The project is owned and implemented by Modern Energy Wuhe Co., Ltd. (hereinafter referred to as the project owner). The project is to collect methane from manure treatment at Modern Farming Wuhe Farm in Wuhe County, Bengbu City, Anhui Province. The project treats the raw manure from 18,000 dairy cows annually by anaerobic digester, and uses the biogas generated during the treatment process for power generation. The electricity generated by the project will be transmitted to East China Power Grid (ECPG). The project is expected to produce 80,500 m3 biogas per day. All the manure is collected and transferred to the anaerobic digester. After anaerobic digestion, the digestate is sent out and used for agriculture fertilization aerobically in the nearby farmlands.

name: Guinan Grassland Sustainable Management Project
project_type: Agriculture Forestry and Other Land Use
description:
Guinan Grassland Sustainable Management Project (hereafter“the project” ) is located in Hainan Tibetan Autonomous Prefecture, Qinghai Province, China. The project aims to restore the local degraded grassland ecosystem through fence construction, degraded grassland improvement and pest control on the degraded grassland to increase carbon sink capacity, and contribute to local development by the adoption of rational grazing and sustainable management of grassland over a long time.
Totally,107,326.16 ha of degraded grassland has been managed sustainably by seeding grass, pest control and fence construction. The project implements fence construction mainly containing rotational grazing and rest grazing in the degraded grassland to achieve sustainable grassland management. Degraded grassland improvement  has been managed sustainably by the implementation of seeding, reseeding, applying fertilizer and Black soil beach management. And,the project also implemented pest control to restore degraded grassland and improve soil carbon storage.

name: GAZIANTEP BIOGAS POWER PLANT
description:
GAZIANTEP BIOGAS POWER PLANT is a greenfield biogas-to-energy project that captures biogas from animal manure, cattle and chicken manure in particular, -via anaerobic digestion- and utilizes it to generate thermal and electric energy through cogeneration units. The animal manure as the main feedstock is collected from the neighboring animal farms with special trucks and transferred to the plant. Continuously Stirred Tank Reactor (CSTR) type anaerobic digesters are used to capture methane-rich biogas. Captured biogas is then utilized in cogeneration units. Waste heat from gas engines is utilized mainly for heating anaerobic fermenters. The generated electricity is not only supplied to the national grid but is also used as auxiliary/internal consumption required for the plant to function. Solid and liquid fermented products as by-products of biogas generation processes taking place at the project site are distributed to neighboring agricultural farms as fertilizer.
The project is being implemented by GAZİ BİYOGAZ ÜRETİMİ A.Ş., the Project Owner, Gaziantep province, in Turkey. The commissioning date of the project is June 30, 2021. However, there are some technical problems with digesters and there is neither electricity generation nor methane capture until April 22, 2022. The project's start date and the first crediting period are thus defined as April 22, 2022, the date on which the technical problems were resolved, and as a result, the project started capturing methane and began generating GHG emission reductions with electricity generated from animal manure. 
This project adopts the renewable crediting period of 7 years, twice renewable for a total of 21 years. The estimated average net annual emission reductions are 185,910 tCO2eq/y. Accordingly, the project is expected to generate 1,301,372 tCO2eq/y emissions reduction during the first crediting period.

name: ACCELERATING THE ADOPTION AND USE OF ELECTRIC VEHICLES
description: Under this project activity, BTR will work with EV OEMs to help accelerate the adoption and optimal use and charging of EVs and, through the collection of accurate and precise data, measure the GHG impact of those EVs’ charging relative to an assumed baseline of comparable-model ICE vehicles. Using an existing proprietary technology platform (the BTR Bridge platform), BTR will aggregate EV telematics data from participating EV OEMs to measure miles driven and kilowatt-hours charged and thus GHGs reduced. BTR’s technology enables the precise and accurate measurement of the GHG impact because the EV’s telematics systems collect data on the location, time, and amount of charging, which BTR then uses to determine the carbon intensity of the relevant grid during each charging event compared to the baseline of a comparable-model ICE vehicle. BTR intends to relay this information back to the EV OEMs and the EVs and thereby inform drivers about the GHG intensity of their charging and encourage them to optimize charging by shifting it to times when the grid is cleanest. BTR will act as the project proponent for this grouped project and undertake all of the monitoring and data collection required under VM0038. The carbon offsets representing the emissions reductions are generated by the charging data collected by the EV OEMs from the EVs, and ownership of the offsets has been contractually transferred from the EV OEMs to the project proponent. During the course of the crediting period, BTR estimates that 2,508,916 tons of CO2 will be reduced or an annual average of 250,892 tCO2. In the absence of this project, fewer EVs would displace the sale and use of ICE vehicles, fewer EV drivers would be informed about the GHG intensity of their charging and, therefore, fewer EV drivers would optimize their charging for GHG reductions.

name: Afforestation project with native and exotic species on degraded grasslands in Northeast, Argentina.
project_type: Agriculture Forestry and Other Land Use
description: The project activity is an afforestation project on multiple farms of extensive grazing lands. The overreaching goal is to promote innovative afforestation management activities on degraded lands. By combining native and exotic species to produce high-quality wood and other non-woody products and, in the long term, to generate new patches of managed native species forests. The grouped Project is located in Corrientes Province, in the Northeast region of Argentina (host country) and could include areas in the contiguous south of Misiones Province.  In this region, grazing and agriculture lands have different levels of degradation due to a long history of use without sustainable management. The activities proposed in the Project could stop the degradation processes and enhance the regional environmental conditions. For the design of the plantations, specific local conditions are considered to determine where species will be planted to promote facilitation strategies between them. Exotic species have favorable competition conditions over native ones (e.g., in standing flooded areas), but in return, they help native species with their development, protecting them from frosts, wind, and high radiation. Through forest plantation of native and exotic species, the Project sequesters CO2 by generating net anthropogenic removals by sinks that can be measured, monitored, and verified with known tools and approaches, contributing to the country's sustainable development.The initial activity instance comprises 2,331 hectares of degraded grassland generating an estimated average (long-term average) of ≈775.509 tCO2e net GHG emissions reductions and removals, implying a total GHG benefit for the environment of approximately ≈19.387. tCO2e per year for the length of the project (40 years).

name: RIDI Grouped Hydro Solar Power Project in Nepal
description: The main purpose of this Grouped project activity is to generate clean form of electricity through renewable Solar energy and Hydro energy sources. The project activity involves installation of combined capacity of 25.4 MW Solar power projects and Hydro Power projects in Nepal. The proposed grouped project activity supports development of renewable energy generation plants based on Solar PV technology in Nepal and delivering electricity to the NEA grid. Each instance of project activity under this grouped project consists of one or more renewable power generation plant using solar PV technology. The proposed grouped project is a voluntary action being undertaken by NEA .

name: Improved cropland management project in Anyang
project_type: Agriculture Forestry and Other Land Use
description:
The “Improved cropland management project in Anyang” is aimed to raise farmer's awareness on the benefits of sustainable agriculture and how to change the agricultural practices to help in climate change mitigation and adaptation. The project will assist farmers to overcome barriers that prevent adoption of improved agricultural land management practices and provide technical assistance where needed. The objectives of the project is to reduce emissions from agricultural practices and increase soil carbon storage, in order to achieve these, a package of practices that change the pre-existing agricultural management activities will be carried out, the specific activities are the following:
A. Reduce fertilizer (organic or inorganic) application;
B. Reduce tillage/improve residue management; and
C. Improve crop planting and harvesting.

name: Anew Agri-carbon Aggregation 1
project_type: Agriculture Forestry and Other Land Use
description:
The Anew Agri-Carbon Project Aggregation 1 enables the adoption of regenerative
agricultural practices on continental United States row crop land through financial incentives and
technical support. Participants in the Project are individual farmers and field managers who have
implemented one or more practice changes on their farm that will increase the deposition of soil
organic carbon, reduce nitrogen fertilizer losses in the form of N 2 O, or reduce on farm energy
consumption.

name: Public Lighting in Brazil Grouped Project
description:
The project involves demand side energy efficiency measures in public lighting infrastructure through the replacement of existing luminaires with more efficient technology, including “Light Emitting Diodes” (hereinafter referred to as “LEDs”) lightings in urban area of the municipality of Feira de Santana, state of Bahia (Instance 1) and Aracaju, state of Sergipe (Instance 2) in Brazil.
The project covers activities such as installation, maintenance, expansion, replenishment, operation and management of all the public lighting infrastructure in the municipality of Feira de Santana and Aracaju (Brazil).
This grouped project (Instances 1 and 2) will install 118,636 luminaires The public lighting infrastructure based on inefficient sodium mercury luminaires was the scenario prior to the implementation of the project.

name: Shanxi Changzhi Sanyuan CMM Power Generation Project
developer: Changzhi Suburb Baoneng New Energy Development Co., Ltd
description:
Shanxi Changzhi Sanyuan CMM Power Generation Project (hereinafter referred to as the Project) will utilize the low concentration coal mine methane (CMM) from Sanyuan coal mine for power generation to supply electricity to North China Power Grid (NCPG). The Project is located in the coal mine area of Shanxi Sanyuan Coal Industry Co., Ltd. in the south of Houxizhuang Village, Houbeizhuang Town, the suburb of Changzhi City, Shanxi Province, China.
The purpose of the Project is to utilize the extracted CMM with low concentration methane to generate electricity. No coal bed methane (CBM) or ventilation air methane (VAM) utilization is involved. The designed capacity is 7.6MW. Ten sets of CMM power generators will be installed with a total installed capacity of 7.6MW (6*0.6MW & 4*1MW), destroying 14.5659 million m3 of methane annually. With the full capacity operation of the Project, the expected annually exported electricity will be 40,641 MWh, which will be supplied to NCPG, displacing part of the electricity generated by NCPG which is dominated by fossil fuel-fired power plants.

name: SMG - Bamboo Plantations for a better tomorrow
project_type: Agriculture Forestry and Other Land Use
description: The afforestation project is a vital initiative that combats climate change by promoting the plantation of bamboo with landowners and communities. By absorbing carbon at an exceptional rate and preventing soil erosion, bamboo provides a sustainable and long-term solution for mitigating the effects of climate change. The project not only helps to create a healthier environment but also provides a valuable source of income for local communities, making it a truly impactful initiative. Furthermore, bamboo's versatility as a food source for wildlife, a sustainable material for construction and furniture, and a potential source of traditional medicine, makes it an invaluable resource for communities in tropical regions.

name: D.Light's Improved Cooking Project In Kenya
description: The “D. LIGHT’S IMPROVED COOKING PROJECT IN KENYA” is a large-scale project that aims dissemination of energy-efficient improved cookstoves (ICS) to replace existing traditional Cookstoves in domestic households and communities in Kenya. Traditional cooking methods prevalent across host country, contribute to greenhouse gas (GHG) emissions due to inefficient combustion of unsustainably sourced, non-renewable biomass (NRB) fuel. Furthermore, the use of solid biomass fuels (e.g., wood) in inefficient traditional stoves and/or open fires releases large amounts of particulate matter (PM), creating hazardous levels of indoor air pollution (IAP). The ICSs disseminated under the project are designed to improve fuel combustion and heat transfer. The ICS results in the reduction of fuel consumption and improvement in levels of Indoor air pollution for project users (reducing smoke, black soot, and particulate matter (PM) emissions). The reduction in consumption of cooking fuel also reduces equivalent greenhouse gas (GHG) emissions attributed to the use of non-renewable biomass. In the absence of this project, the project activity beneficiaries would cook primarily using traditional inefficient stoves for meeting their thermal energy needs, perpetuating environmental and health degradation. The project activity intends to access carbon finance to mitigate one of the main barriers (price) for end users towards adopting clean cookstoves.

name: Malatya 2 Landfill Gas Power Plant Project
project_type: Energy industries (renewable/non-renewable sources); Waste handling and disposal
description:
The Malatya Solid Waste Management System and Electricity Generation Facility (4.242 MWe) is situated in the province of Malatya, in the Merkez District, Kapıkaya neighborhood, and is owned and operated by Biotrend. The facility is designed to process municipal waste from Kapikaya province, classified as type-2 sanitary landfill, and serves a total of 8 districts. The facility consists of four key areas: a sanitary landfill, a mechanical separation facility, a compost facility, and an electricity generation facility.

The Malatya LFG plant has obtained a generation license from EMRA, with an expected annual generation of 31.815.000 kWh/year. The project's initial unit was commissioned on 27.06.2021, with an installed capacity of 1.412 MWe, marking the project's activity start date. The project's renewal crediting period is set at 7 years, with expected average annual emission reductions of 68.115,23 (tCO2e). Through this project, waste is stabilized, waste storage is minimized, electricity is produced, and negative environmental impacts are eliminated.

name: Seringueira II REDD+ Project
project_type: Agriculture Forestry and Other Land Use
description: The Seringueira II project will be developed in the municipality of Ipixuna, Amazonas State, Brazil. It falls under the Agriculture, Forestry and Other Land Uses (AFOLU) sector within the Reducing Emissions from Deforestation and Forest Degradation (REDD+) category. The project will conserve 23,851.88 hectares of native Amazon rainforests in a region where deforestation pressure is mainly due to land use conversion activities from forests to pastures aimed at raising livestock. The project area (16,483.02 ha) will be allocated to Avoided Unplanned Deforestation (AUD), and it is estimated that at the end of the project the emission of 591,917.73 tons of Greenhouse Gases will have been avoided. The project will be developed considering the CCB Standard. As benefits to the communities, the project will implement systems of underground water collection, installation of solar panels for electricity generation, provision of satellite internet service, construction of toilets with septic tanks, training of women in entrepreneurship, provision of assistance in the formation of community associations, and construction of a school. These measures will enable water security and access to information to minimize the impacts caused by climate change in traditional, low-income extractive communities. As benefits to the climate, the maintenance of forest cover results in exceptional benefits for adapting to the impacts caused by climate change as the area presents a dense hydrographic network that contributes to the provision and quality of water in the Amazon river basin. The maintenance of forest cover also ensures the conservation of biodiversity, the maintenance of ecosystem functioning and of ecosystem services provisioning performed by living organisms. It is noteworthy that the project includes a high priority area for biodiversity conservation with species classified in the categories Endangered (EN) and Critically Endangered (CR) according to the IUCN red list.

name: Distribution of Improved Cook Stoves in Sub-Saharan Africa–Zambia-CPA-005
developer: C-Quest Capital Malaysia Global Stoves Limited
description:
The project involves distribution of 60,000 domestic fuel-efficient improved cookstoves (ICS) in Zambia. The ICS distributed through this project will replace the prevailing inefficient three-stone fires, or traditional pot supports . The ICS combusts wood more efficiently and improves thermal transfer to pots, hence saving fuel and lowering greenhouse gas emissions.

This is the fifth CPA implemented under the CDM Programme of Activities (PoA) titled “Distribution of Improved Cook Stoves in Sub-Saharan Africa”. C-Quest Capital Malaysia Global Stoves Limited (CQC) is the Coordinating / Managing Entity (CME) for the PoA in which this CPA is to be included. Ecoeye Co., Ltd. (henceforth referred as Ecoeye) provide all implementation cost for all ICS under this CPA, so that affordable clean technology can be made available to the participating households. Ecoeye will also make available all operation and maintenance costs along with ICS production and distribution cost. Total LandCare (TLC) Zambia will implement this project, manage and coordinate activities of local partners, the promotion and installation of the ICS and also provide all necessary marketing and promotion assistance to partners. TLC is also responsible for monitoring activities of this project.

It is intended that under this project single pot, TLC-CQC Rocket Stove will be distributed. In this grouped project, each ICS constitutes a single project activity instance which is in line with its definition stated in VCS Program Definitions version 4.2

The end user will be informed that carbon finance is being generated by the use of the ICS, and this finance is in turn used to facilitate the access to ICS (eg. subsidize the price of the ICS) and helps to cover project implementation costs.

name: Wen County BCCY New Energy Co., Ltd Landfill Gas Direct Combustion Utilization Heating Project
project_type: Energy industries (renewable/non-renewable sources); Waste handling and disposal
description:
Wen County BCCY New Energy Co., Ltd landfill gas direct combustion utilization heating project (hereafter referred to as the project) is located at Wen County MSW landfill site, Baofeng Village North, Zhaobao Town, Wen County, Jiaozuo City, Henan Province, P.R. China. The project is invested, constructed, and operated by Wen County BCCY New Energy CO., Ltd. (hereafter referred to as the project owner). The objective is to collect the landfill gas (LFG) from Wen County MSW landfill site and utilize it to generate hot steam for the nearby factories.
Wen County MSW landfill site started collecting and handling waste in 2008 with a total design effective capacity of 590,000 m3 and a calculated operational lifespan of 25 years. The project has a total designed capacity 3.5t/h (1*3.5t/h) gas type boiler that combusts the LFG that contains nearly 50% of methane, to generate hot steam and export it to the nearby food industries. The project started to construct on 20/11/2020 and started to operate on 01/09/2021. The operation period of the project will end on 31/08/2031.
The LFG from Wen County MSW landfill site is greenhouse gas. In the absence of the project activity, the LFG would have released to the atmosphere, hence contribute to the global warming. Furthermore, the biogas utilized in the boiler replaces the fossil fuel that utilized in the food industries’ boilers. The gas boiler uses LFG will generate heat which will replace the Fuel-Gas type boiler and the biogas type boiler in the food industries. Therefore, the project activity significantly contributes to the reduction of GHG emission. 
Total heat supplied to the food industries by using the LFG in the crediting period will be 396,767t. VCUs will be claimed from the methane destroyed and the diesel oil displaced. The estimated average GHG emission reductions of the project are 39,676tCO2e and the total GHG emission reductions and the removals are 39,676tCO2e during the fixed 10 years crediting period.

name: Oeste de Caucaia Landfill Project Activity
developer: GNR FORTALEZA VALORIZACAO DE BIOGAS LTDA
description:
The primary objective of the Oeste de Caucaia Landfill Project Activity is to avoid greenhouse gases emission by the Oeste de Caucaia Landfill through landfill gas capture, purification and injection in a distribution grid, while contributing to the environmental, social and economic sustainability by minimizing global climate changes and local air pollution.
The proposed Project Activity consists of capturing the landfill gas (LFG) generated by the landfill using an active LFG capture system and injecting it into a natural gas distribution network (after a purification process), displacing the use of natural gas. Any LFG excess will be flared.
Applying the state-of-the-art on LFG capture technology, a collecting system is installed to avoid the free emission of methane to the atmosphere. The LFG captured is sent to the upgrading facility before being injected to the natural gas distribution grid.
This type of project, i.e., upgrading of landfill gas to natural gas and injection into a natural gas distribution grid is not usual in Brazil.The Oeste de Caucaia Landfill Project Activity has a substantial positive impact in terms of sustainable development as it is one of the first projects that purify the LFG and injects it to a network distribution grid being developed in Brazil that, as consequence, directly displaces natural gas.
An environmental benefit with the implementation of the Oeste de Caucaia Landfill Project is the destruction of methane that otherwise would be emitted to the atmosphere, increasing the impact on global warming.
The project invests on training engineers and operators to the qualification level required by these new activities. Oeste de Caucaia makes use of the experience of its own shareholders as well as its international consultants to train and qualify the human resources necessary for the implementation and operation of the magnitude of the Oeste de Caucaia Landfill Project.
