name: Feicheng Composting Project
developer: Taian Jinliyuan Fertilizer Technology Co., Ltd.
project_type: Livestock, enteric fermentation, and manure management; Waste handling and disposal
description:
Feicheng Composting Project (hereafter referred to as the project) installs a set of organic fertilizers production lines with an annual output of 50,000 tones to treat the manure from the dairy cow farms and biomass waste residue i.e., straw in Zhangling Village, Feicheng City, Shandong Province, China. The project is invested and owned by Taian Jinliyuan Fertilizer Technology Co., Ltd. The purpose of the project activity is to avoid methane emissions through controlled aerobic treatment by composting of manure and biomass waste residue.
In absence of the project, all manure waste produced was left to decay in uncovered anaerobic lagoons, which is the most economic, viable, and reasonable option for livestock farm owners, and the biomass waste residue was left to decay anaerobically in a solid waste disposal site (SWDS).
This project was designed to treat the dairy cow manure and biomass waste residue (straw) to produce organic fertilizer. This project comprises a fermentation system and a fertilizer production system. An estimated 130,000 tons of manure and 5,000 tons of biomass waste residue can be treated annually, so a total of 135,000 tons of waste can be aerobically composted for this project. The final compost product obtained are sold to local businesses and farmers. The construction start date of the project is 01-June-2020 and was put into operation on 01-January-2022.
The project activity will reduce the amount of GHG in the atmosphere by avoiding methane emissions from controlled aerobic treatment by composting manure and biomass residue. It is estimated that 59,122 tCO2e emission reductions will be generated annually, with a total of 591,217 tCO2e over the 10-year crediting period.

name: Combating climate change with sustainable agriculture and land use management project by Indian Farmers
project_type: Agriculture Forestry and Other Land Use
description:
The proposed VCS Agricultural Land Management project activity aims to implement organic farming to reduce the greenhouse gases emission of Carbon dioxide, Methane, and Nitrous oxide through enhancing soil carbon pool, reducing use of chemical fertilizer, making compost out of biomass residue, and fuel saving through lesser consumption of agricultural machineries.  Along with the reduction of greenhouse gases, the project also aims to increase the capacity of soil to sequester carbon and enhance nutrients by mulching through organic material, and assimilation of compost and vermicomposting manure. Prior to the project implementation –The farmers in the proposed project were managing their farmlands and agriculture using conventional farming which was causing high GHG emission. 
The project started on 17 June 2020 in the Maharashtra and Madhya Pradesh state of India.
The project is estimated to reduce emission by 57127 tCO2/annum and total 5,71,272 tCO2 throughout its crediting period of 10 years

name: The Carbon Farming Program of Lithuania
project_type: Agriculture Forestry and Other Land Use
description: The Carbon Farming Program of Lithuania is a joint initiative between UAB Heavy Finance (HF) and farmers within the Lithuanian Republic borders. The program utilizes private capital to implement and adopt improved agricultural land management long-term, thus changing the mindset and establishing climate change mitigation and biodiversity-friendly practices. The Program aims to reward farmers for the positive results of fostering improved agricultural land management practices by sharing the revenue obtained from the sale of VCUs generated through the verified greenhouse gas emissions reductions and removals projects. Project activities are helping farmers to reach the balance in the triple bottom line - economic, environmental, and social. Improved agriculture land management refers to the techniques that focus on soil health and fertility by storing and increasing organic carbon, reducing anthropogenic gasses from excessive use of chemical fertilizers in the context of the offered program, accelerating changes to pre-existing agricultural management practices, and adopting regenerative methods.

name: SANLI BIOGAS POWER PLANT
description:
Sanli Biogas Power Plant is a greenfield biogas-to-energy project that captures biogas from animal manure, cattle and chicken manure in particular, -via anaerobic digestion- and utilizes it to generate thermal and electric energy through cogeneration units. The animal manure as the main feedstock is collected from the neighboring animal farms with special trucks and transferred to the plant. Continuously Stirred Tank Reactor (CSTR) type anaerobic digesters are used to capture methane-rich biogas. Captured biogas is then utilized in cogeneration units. Waste heat from gas engine is utilized mainly for heating anaerobic fermenters. The generated electricity is not only supplied to the national grid but is also used as auxiliary/internal consumption required for the plant to function. Solid and liquid fermented products as by-products of biogas generation processes taken place at the project site are distributed to neighbouring agricultural farms as fertilizer.
The project is being implemented by ŞANLI BİYOGAZ ENERJİ VE SANAYİ ANONİM ŞİRKETİ, the Project Owner, Şanlıurfa province, in Turkey. The start date of the project and the first crediting period is determined as June 30, 2021. 
The project activity avoids methane emission through the above-mentioned capture and utilization processes. Furthermore, the project reduces CO2 emissions from fossil-fuel-based electricity generation by supplying biogas-based electricity to the national grid. 
This project adopts the renewable crediting period of 7 years, twice renewable for a total of 21 years. The estimated average net annual emission reductions are 311,544 tCO2eq/y. Accordingly, the project is expected to generate 2,180,808 tCO2eq/y emissions reduction during the first crediting period.

name: Yongtai Danyun Duck Farm Manure Composting Project
developer: Yongtai Golden Egg Development Co., Ltd
project_type: Livestock, enteric fermentation, and manure management; Waste handling and disposal
description:
Yongtai Danyun Duck Farm Manure Composting Project (hereafter referred to as the project) introduces the aerobic composting system to treat the duck manure from Yongtai Danyun Duck Farm of Yongtai Golden Egg Project in Danyun Village, Yongtai County, Fuzhou City, Fujian Province, China. The purpose of the project activity is to avoid methane emissions through controlled aerobic treatment by composting duck manure.
The project comprises of solid-liquid separation system, composting system, and fertilizer packaging system. It is estimated that approximately 47,413.5 tonnes of duck manure can be treated annually, and the annual organic fertilizer production is 15,000 tonnes. Part of the organic fertilizer will be distributed to nearby farmers for free and most of it will be sold to local businesses. The project activity will reduce GHG in the atmosphere by avoiding methane emissions from controlled aerobic treatment by composting duck manure.

name: Anlu Aonong Swine Farm Manure Management System GHG Mitigation Project
developer: Hubei Aonong Animal Husbandry Development Co., Ltd
project_type: Energy industries (renewable/non-renewable sources); Livestock, enteric fermentation, and manure management; Waste handling and disposal
description:
Anlu Aonong Swine Farm Manure Management System GHG Mitigation Project (hereinafter referred to as the Project) introduce animal waste management system (AWMS) to the two swine farms in Xundian Town, Anlu City, Hubei Province, China, which are owned by Hubei Aonong Animal Husbandry Development Co., Ltd. The project activity aims to treat the manure and wastewater from the 2 swine farms to avoid methane emissions generated in the baseline uncovered anaerobic lagoons.
The project activity will reduce of GHG in the atmosphere through avoiding methane emissions from anaerobic treatment of swine manure and wastewater.

name: MicroEnergy Credits - Microfinance for Efficient Lighting Product Lines - India
description: MicroEnergy Credits - Microfinance for Efficient Lighting Product Lines - India is aimed at reducing fossil-fuel based electricity consumption by distributing Light Emitting Diode (LED Inverter Bulbs) to local communities in India. This project will be developed under the VERRA which will ensure that enhanced local socio-economic benefits, as well as verifiable emission reductions, are achieved. The purpose of this grouped project is to reduce fossil fuel based electricity consumption in the Rural households of India by introducing more energy efficient LED lamps to replace incandescent light bulbs (“ICLs”), This would result in reduction in greenhouse gas emissions.

name: MANGROVE REFORESTATION IN DANZHOU, HAINAN PROVINCE
project_type: Agriculture Forestry and Other Land Use
description:
The project “Mangrove Reforestation in Danzhou, Hainan Province” (hereafter the project) is located at Danzhou Bay and Xinying Mangrove National Wetland Park, Danzhou, Hainan of China. The project is a mangroves reforetation project under the Reforestation, Reforestation, and Revegetation (ARR) category of the Verified Carbon Standard (VCS) contributing to carbon sequestration, biodiversity conservation, climate adaptation, and sustainable livelihood. The proponent of the project is Hainan University.
The project is located at Danzhou Bay and Xinying Mangrove National Wetland Park, a hotspot of mangrove biodiversity and conservation in China. After years of protection and management, Danzhou Bay and Xinying Mangrove National Wetland Park has retained the largest area of continuous mangrove forest in western Hainan, and, through many years of popularization of science, the local people's awareness of mangrove wetland protection has increased significantly, creating a good foundation for the project to be implemented. 
The objective of this project is to reconstruct the mangrove ecosystem from previously abandoned aquaculture ponds, enhance biodiversity, increase carbon sequestration of mangroves, and mitigate risks of marine disasters to the coastal communities. The restoration of the pond to its original state will expand the area of mangroves and the mangrove forest belt in Danzhou Bay, creating a complete mangrove shelterbelt. This will also establish a complete vegetation sequence along the coastline, including sea surface, tidal flat, mangrove, semi-mangrove, and terrestrial plants, thereby enhancing the structure and function of the mangrove ecosystem. This will improve the habitat of birds and marine organisms. The mangroves will play a crucial role in maintaining the coastal ecological function and biodiversity, as well as protecting the lives and property of the villagers residing around the bay.

name: Northeast Jiangsu Improved Cropland Management Project
project_type: Agriculture Forestry and Other Land Use
description:
The project activity is in Lianyungang City, Suqian City, Yancheng City and Huaian City within the
boundary of Northeast Jiangsu, eastern province in China. The climate type of Northeast
Jiangsu is typical temperate monsoon climate. Northeast Jiangsu is located in the border area
of Jiangsu and Shandong. The project involves 336,014 hectares of wheat field, 20,062hectares of corn field and 36,894 hectares wheat and corn rotation field. The scenario existingprior to the project’s implementation is primarily conventional tillage with synthetic fertilizer and without straw returning, which cause greater soil disturbance, increase the loss of SOC and nitrous oxide emission. Conventional practices require a significant amount of chemical and energy input and are also more likely to weaken the ecology of a landscape compared to the improved ALM practices advocated by this project. The estimated annual average GHG emission reductions and removals through the implementation of SALM activities in the agricultural land is 716,201 tCO2e year. Over the 20 years of the first crediting period, the project will generate an estimated removal and reduction of 14,324,026 tCO2e

name: COD BIOGAS ENERGY MANURE TREATMENT PLANT
description:
COD Biogas Energy Manure Treatment Plant is a greenfield biogas-to-energy project that that captures biogas from animal manure, cattle and chicken manure in particular, via anaerobic digestion and utilizes it to generate thermal and electric energy through cogeneration unit. The animal manure as the main feedstock is collected from the neighbouring animal farms with special trucks and transferred to the biogas plant. Continuously Stirred Tank Reactor (CSTR) type anaerobic digesters are used to capture methane rich biogas. Waste heat from gas engines is utilized for heating anaerobic fermenters. The electricity generated by the two installed biogas engines with the capacity of 1,501 KWe each is not only supplied to the national grid, but also used as auxiliary/internal consumption required for the plant to function. Solid and liquid fermented products as by-products of biogas generation processes taken place at the project site are distributed to neighbouring agricultural farms as fertilizer.
The project is being implemented by COD ENERJİ ÜRETİM SANAYİ TİCARET ANONİM ŞİRKETİ, as the Project Owner, in Pınarbaşı district, Kayseri province, in Turkey. The start date of the project and of the first crediting period is determined as June 28, 2021. 
The project activity avoids methane emission through the above-mentioned capture and utilization processes. Furthermore, the project also reduces CO2 emission from fossil-fuel based electricity generation by supplying biogas-based electricity to the national grid. 
The project adopts the renewable crediting period of 7 years, twice renewable for a total of 21 years. The estimated average net annual emission reductions are 189,969 tCO2eq/y. Accordingly, the project is expected to generate 1,329,783 tCO2eq/y emissions reduction during the first crediting period.

name: Yushu Improved Cropland Management Project
developer: Yushu Rongxing City Development Co., Ltd
project_type: Agriculture Forestry and Other Land Use
description: The project activity is located in Yushu City within the boundary of central and northern Jilin, northeast province in China. The climate type is mesotympana continental monsoon climate. The project involves 339,175 hectares of corn field. The scenario existing prior to the project’s implementation is primarily conventional tillage with synthetic fertilizer and without straw returning, which cause greater soil disturbance, increase the loss of SOC and nitrous oxide emission. Conventional practices require a significant amount of chemical and energy input and are also more likely to weaken the ecology of a landscape compared to the improved ALM practices advocated by this project. The estimated annual average GHG emission reductions and removals through the implementation of SALM activities in the agricultural land is 482,152 t CO2e year. Over the 20 years of the first crediting period, the project will generate an estimated removal and reduction of 9,643,034 tCO2e.

name: REDUCING EMISSIONS FROM DEFORESTATION DUE TO SLASH-AND-BURN CORN BY INTRODUCING CACAO FARMING IN GORONTALO PROVINCE, INDONESIA
project_type: Agriculture Forestry and Other Land Use
description:
This REDD+ project, titled “Reducing Emissions from Deforestation Due to Slash-and-Burn Corn by Introducing Cacao Farming in Gorontalo Province, Indonesia” is located in Gorontalo Province on northern Sulawesi Island in Indonesia. The Project Area is 43,014 ha of forest area in Gorontalo Province, consisting of dry land primary forest and dry land secondary forest. The area of the Reference Region for Deforestation is 185,403 ha in Gorontalo Province, consisting of primary dry land forest, and secondary dry land forest. In Gorontalo Province on Sulawesi Island, food for life and sources of income are dependent on corn crops, coconut palm, cacao, and forest timber and non-timber product extraction. Commercial opportunities for local communities are limited by the unsuitable low purchase
prices practiced by corn intermediates. In the last two decades, deforestation in Gorontalo Province has been observed at a rate of 0.65% per year. The “slash-and-burn” farming of corn is known to be the main factor contributing to deforestation in Gorontalo Province. In short, the main driver of deforestation is the socio-economic condition in this area. Decreasing deforestation will be achieved through a series of activities that are designed to improve the livelihoods of local people. The principal project activity is introducing improved cacao production as an alternative source of income to the slash-and-burn farming of corn. The Project is community-based and consists of the implementation of activities in conjunction with local people. The implementation of the management structure and activities addressing deforestation drivers began on, as well partially after, 2020, together with associated investments. These investments are related to field work, capacities and other related work provided by the project proponent, as well as management work and conservation work such as capacity building, reporting and control activities.

name: Floating Solar project of Greenam Energy
description: Greenam Energy Private Limited (GEPL/ the Developer) is a special purpose vehicle formed by AMIH (AM International Holdings) to develop a 24.7MWp (22 MWac) floating solar PV plant (the Project) on the surface of two water reservoirs located near Muthiahpuram village, Thoothukudi district in the Indian state of Tamil Nadu. The purpose of this Project is to utilize the area of the reservoir to generate clean energy for captive use by the AMIH Group c ompanies Southern Petrochemical Industries Corporation Limited (SPIC) and Greenstar fertilizers (GFL). A common power purchase agreement (PPA) had been executed between GEPL and the off takers, namely SPIC and GFL.

name: Grouped Captive Solar Power Project in Bangladesh
description: The proposed grouped project activity is a step towards supporting the implementation and installation of solar rooftop and ground mounted projects in the Various State of Bangladesh. The main goal of project activity is to implement renewable energy projects in the country and the significant importance of revenues from sale of Verified Carbon Units (VCUs) to achieve this goal forms the basis of the implementation of this project activity. The project activity is a voluntary action and each SPV will be the Project Proponent for their project activity.

name: Guantao Qingfeng Biological Manure Management Greenhouse Gas Emission Reduction Project
project_type: Livestock, enteric fermentation, and manure management; Waste handling and disposal
description:
The Guantao Qingfeng Biological Manure Management Greenhouse Gas Emission Reduction Project (hereafter referred to as the project) is located in Guantao County, Handan City, Hebei Province of China, and is used to treat biomass waste such as swine, cattle, chicken and sheep manure from seven local farms and straw from process of local agricultural production generated. Project is owned by Guantao County Qingfeng Biotechnology Co. The purpose of this project activity is to avoid and reduce methane emissions to the atmosphere through aerobic composting of manure and biomass residue. 
Livestock and poultry manure is an important source of greenhouse gas emissions. In absence of the project to deal with manure, in order to consider the economy and convenience of the previous breeding enterprises in surrounding villages and towns, all the generated manure will rot in the uncovered anaerobic lagoon, and methane will be directly discharged into the atmosphere, without any methane recovery and destruction facilities. The biomass waste residue is left in the solid waste treatment plant (SWDS) for decay.
The project uses livestock and poultry excrement resources generated by local farming as raw materials, and uses biomass residues, straw and other wastes generated in local agricultural activities as auxiliary materials for aerobic composting treatment. 
The annual feces treatment capacity is 80000 tons of swine manure, 18000 tons of cattle manure, 55000 tons of chicken manure, 12000 tons of sheep manure, 36000 tons of biomass waste residue, and produce approximately55000 tons of organic fertilizer every year. In the final production of organic fertilizer, some organic fertilizer will be distributed to nearby farmers for free, and some will be sold to local enterprises.
The project is estimated that average of 42175 t CO2e will be generated annually during the first 7-year accounting period. The total emission reduction is 295226 tCO2e.

name: Hunan Shimen IFM (conversion of logged to protected forest) Project
developer: Shimen County Economic Construction Investment Development Co., Ltd
project_type: Agriculture Forestry and Other Land Use
description:
The Hunan Shimen IFM (conversion of logged to protected forest) Project (hereafter “the project activity”) is implemented in Shimen County, Changde City, Hunan Province of China by Shimen County Economic Construction Investment Development Co., Ltd, the geo-coordinate of the project proponent is 110°29'E—111°33'E and 29°16'N-30°08'N, the total area is 39,7000 ha, which includes the Improved Forest Management (IFM) of the forests in the conversion of logged to protected forest.
The area of the project activity is 6475.51 ha, including 2220 subcompartments. All these forests are state-owned forests or privately-owned forests or collective-owned forests, and have the legal right to forest ownership. The species involved in the project are Broadleaf mix and Pinus massoniana.
Before the implementation of the project activity, the trees are logged based on a valid and verifiable government-approved timber management plan for harvesting the project area. The implementation of the project activity converses the trees to protected forest to reduce the GHG emissions for about 623,058 tCO2e in 20 years, the average annual emission reduction is 31,152 tCO2e and Verified Carbon Units with buffer deduction is about 479,747 tCO2e in 20 years, and average annual VCUs with buffer deduction is 23,987 tCO2e.
The project activity will contribute to the environment (biodiversity conservation, rocky desertification prevention and soil erosion control), thus contribute to sustainable development.

name: Talihya Nord I Hydro power rural electrification
location: Congo, The Democratic Republic of The
description:
The region of Butembo and Beni has one of the lowest rates of electricity access (around 3%) in the country and doesn’t have neither an electricity network nor the national electricity company services. The project is providing electricity for the first time to the population of the cities of Butembo and Beni and will be a major step for local SMEs as well. 30,000 households will use this green electricity, replacing diesel generators avai¬lable in limited numbers. Energie du Nord-Kivu SARL (ENK) is using a prepayment sys¬tem allowing the users to follow in real time their energy consumption and better manage their budget (no credit or debt collection). Within households, women are the most positively impacted by the arrival of electricity. In¬deed, they no longer have to fetch tens of kilos of char¬coal several times a week and transport them over many kilometers. They also benefit from a huge time saving when preparing meals and cooking. In addition, thanks to electricity, they can store food in fridges or freezers
The purpose of the project activity is to install and operate a run-of–river, greenfield 9.86 MW hydroelectric plant at Taliyah Nord I and electrify neighbouring communities through an isolated mini-grid, representing the consumption of up to 30,000 households and several small & medium enterprises. At least 75% of the clients in these communities will be households.
The project developer and operator of Talihya Nord Small Hydro Power Plant (SHPP) is ENK.

name: KARAMANLI BIOGAS ENERGY POWER PLANT
project_type: Energy industries (renewable/non-renewable sources); Livestock, enteric fermentation, and manure management; Waste handling and disposal
description:
Karamanlı Biogas Power Plant, built and operated in Burdur Province, Karamanlı District, Karamanlı Village has an installed capacity of 9.360 MWe/ 9.636 MWm. as per the generation licence, numbered EÜ/10831-1/05139. The purpose of the project activity is to produce electricity from poultry and cattle manure with biomethanization process which will also result in fermented products that could be utilized as fertilizers by local farmers. Karamanlı Biogas Power plant has been granted the generation license from EMRA on 10/03/2022. As per the generation license, the annual expected generation is 70,200 MWh/year.
The facility is expected to generate 70,200 MWh/year when operational capacity is 9.36 MWe. It is estimated that the project will help reduce carbon emissions by 243,845 tons annually. The total emission reduction for the whole crediting period is calculated as 2,194,606 tCO2e.

name: Myanmar Bago 2,450 acres afforestation project
project_type: Agriculture Forestry and Other Land Use
description:
Myanmar Bago 2,450 acres afforestation project of Color Park International Inc. (hereafter “the project) located in Oktwin Township, Taungoo District, Bago Region, Myanmar.
The project’s aim is to increase below benefits by planting Paulownia tomentosa:
- Providing and increasing employment opportunities
- Promoting employment opportunities for female employees
- Legal frameworks in company policy promote, enforce, and monitor any form of discrimination (e.g., discrimination based on gender, race, religion, sexual orientation or other habits) or sexual harassment with respect to the project.
- Substantially increase the number of youth and adults who have relevant skills, including technical and vocational skills
- Substantially increase water-use efficiency across all sectors and ensure sustainable withdrawals and supply of freshwater to address water scarcity and substantially reduce the number of people suffering from water scarcity
- Creating and developing new wooden buildings, reduce cement buildings, and enhance the meaning of sustainable coexistence between humans and nature
- Increase carbon sequestration and contribute to local sustainable development by planting Paulownia tomentosa
The location of the project.
The project area is located in Oktwin Township, Taungoo District, Bago Region, Myanmar. The plan for total area is 991.7 ha (2,450.6 Acre), cropland is 971.2 ha, (2,400 Acre) and 2.06% Set Aside Conservation area and staff quarters: 20.5 ha (50.6 Arce).
Using the high carbon adsorption properties of Paulownia tomentosa for large-scale planting of Paulownia tomentosa as a way to remove GHG emission.
The state of this afforestation is 10-year-old wasteland with grasses and shrubs not taller than 2.5 meters.
Annual average removals: 105,828.8 tCO2e, Total removals: 5,291,439.8 tCO2e

name: BAMBOO PLANTATION BASED GROUPED PROJECT IN INDIA
project_type: Agriculture Forestry and Other Land Use
description:
The purpose of the grouped project is to contribute to the removal and reduction of greenhouse gases (GHG) emission from the atmosphere by plantation of native bamboo species, which may or may not be harvested. Such bamboo plantations shall primarily take place on fallow and/or degraded lands, but also include, in specific cases, use of agricultural land owned by farmers/communities. 
Geographical boundary of the overall grouped project is India. The overall grouped project activity will cover a total land area of 500,000 hectares. The first project instance comprises of the plantations in Madhya Pradesh, the central part of India. The project shall also enhance income of the farmers/ communities.

name: Vemo Conduce - Mexico City
description:
Project activity is carried out in Mexico City, operating under a Ride Hailing platform. Electric vehicle recharge is carried out in six charging HUBs located in “Lomas Verdes”, “Aleph”, “Miyana”, “Artz”, “Puerta Polanco” & “Monumento a la Madre”, exclusively for VEMO’s fleet vehicles, where charging infrastructure is located. Each operational shift is 9.5 hours long, and each vehicle is meant to cover two shifts each day. Therefore, the vehicles are also charged twice a day. In these chargers, is where emission reductions are effectively carried out, given that electricity is energizing the vehicles, rather than conventional petrol fuels, which are less efficient and produce more emissions per kilometer traveled.

Fleet operation is monitored in real time through telemetry devices installed in each vehicle, being capable of monitoring key operation parameters such as depth of discharge (DoD), state of charge (SoC), battery temperature, mean speed, odometer, charging power, etc. Information is available in a vehicle database that can be accessed from different devices to carry out data analysis on electric vehicle operation, allowing VEMO to use real time information to carry out electric vehicles emissions tracking. Also, the operational information of the vehicles is used to calculate the emissions a conventional vehicle would have produced, had it been used to carry out the operation (baseline emissions).

The advantage of this system lies in information liability, being generated automatically as vehicles operate. If the vehicles do not operate, emission reductions are not carried out and thus, no carbon credit can be emitted. Vehicle and energy accounting become more liable because the information is gotten directly from operation and no estimations are done regarding travelled distance.

Emission reductions are a result of the difference generated between real electric vehicles emissions, & the emissions that would have occurred if the vehicles were ICEVs.

name: Greenzone Reforestation Project
project_type: Agriculture Forestry and Other Land Use
description:
Greenzone Reforestation Project is a reforestation and afforestation initiative designed, funded, and implemented by DGB Group. The project will increase tree cover in Cameroon by planting agroforestry crop trees on communal lands where smallholders wish to benefit from the income that perennial nuts and fruits, as well as indigenous trees can provide. This reforestation and afforestation will contribute to regional wildlife habitat or corridors, improve water infiltration, control erosion, and sequester carbon, among other ecosystem services.

Prior to project implementation, thousands of hectares of customary chiefdom land have been degraded to shrubby grasslands surrounding remnant islands of forest.  Individual farmers currently do not have the resources to invest in trees that they are interested in, and their farms lack canopy cover or any sort of perennial cash crops.The project activity will take place across Cameroon, starting in various sub-divisions of Mbam-et-Kim Department, and will involve communities who have access and permission to use customary chiefdom lands. At the individual farm level, the Project solicits a farmer’s needs and ascertains what crop trees are desired, and in what quantity. Contractual agreements are put in place to ensure the survival of these trees for at least forty years, and these varied agroforestry trees—such avocado, citrus, and macadamia—will provide income diversification for the farmers over time, while increasing vegetative cover on agricultural land.

name: HESHAN AWMS GHG Mitigation Project in GUANGDONG Province
developer: Heshan Lvhu (Green Lake) bioenergy CO., Ltd Company
project_type: Energy industries (renewable/non-renewable sources); Livestock, enteric fermentation, and manure management; Waste handling and disposal
description: Heshan animal waste management system GHG Mitigation Project in Heshan, a county-level city administered by Jiangmen City, Guangdong Province  (hereafter referred to as the Project) introduces new animal waste management systems to treat the manure from a market swine farm and a breeding swine farm in Heshan, Jiangmen City, Guangdong Province, which are owned by Heshan Lvhu （Green Lake） bioenergy CO., Ltd Company. The company and this AWMS are located in Zhaiwu Town, Heshan City. Since the company establishment, it has been committed to the development and investment of green energy, paying special attention to the investment and operation of biogas power generation projects with animal waste and agricultural and forestry wastes. Through the continuous in-depth research and development of biogas power generation projects, it has gradually expanded to the resource utilization of large-scale animal waste treatment and efficient biogas production.

name: XINJIANG YINING SUSTAINABLE GRASSLAND MANAGEMENT PROJECT
developer: Fujian Jinsen Carbon Sink Technology Co. Ltd.
project_type: Agriculture Forestry and Other Land Use
description: Xinjiang Yining County Sustainable Grassland Management Project (hereinafter referred to as “the Project“) is located in Yining County, Yili Autonomous Prefecture, Xinjiang Uygur Autonomous Region, China. The project aims to restore locally degraded grassland ecosystems by adopting sustainable grassland management practices, such as improving rotational grazing and limiting grazing amounts, and ensuring proper management in the long term. The project supporter is Yining County State-owned Investment Capital Management limited liability Company.

name: Distribution of Improved Cook Stoves in Sub-Saharan Africa-Malawi-CPA-004
developer: C-Quest Capital Malaysia Global Stoves Limited
description:
The project involves distribution of 30,000 domestic fuel-efficient improved cookstoves (ICS) in Malawi. The ICS distributed through this project will replace the prevailing inefficient three-stone fires, or traditional pot supports. The ICS combusts wood more efficiently and improves thermal transfer to pots, hence saving fuel and lowering greenhouse gas emissions.

This is the fourth CPA implemented under the CDM Programme of Activities (PoA) titled “Distribution of Improved Cook Stoves in Sub-Saharan Africa”. C-Quest Capital Malaysia Global Stoves Limited (CQC) is the Coordinating / Managing Entity (CME) for the PoA in which this CPA is to be included. Ecoeye Co., Ltd. (henceforth referred as Ecoeye) provide all implementation cost for all ICS under this CPA, so that affordable clean technology can be made available to the participating households. Ecoeye will also make available all operation and maintenance costs along with ICS production and distribution cost. Total LandCare (TLC) Malawi will implement this project, manage and coordinate activities of local partners, the promotion and installation of the ICS and also provide all necessary marketing and promotion assistance to partners. TLC is also responsible for monitoring activities of this project.

It is intended that under this project single pot, TLC-CQC Rocket Stove will be distributed. In this grouped project, each ICS constitutes a single project activity instance which is in line with its definition stated in VCS Program Definitions version 4.2

The end user will be informed that carbon finance is being generated by the use of the ICS, and this finance is in turn used to facilitate the access to ICS (eg. subsidize the price of the ICS) and helps to cover project implementation costs.

name: Huangping Aonong Swine Farm Composting Project
developer: Guizhou Aonong Qihuan Animal Husbandry Co., Ltd
project_type: Livestock, enteric fermentation, and manure management; Waste handling and disposal
description:
Huangping Aonong Swine Farm Composting Project (hereinafter referred to as the Project) is located at Shanping Village, Gulong Town, Huangping County, Qiandongnan Miao and Dong Autonomous Prefecture, Guizhou Province, P.R. China. The project is owned and implemented by Guizhou Aonong Qihuan Animal Husbandry Co., Ltd.
The project will introduce new anaerobic animal manure management system (Anaerobic Digester) to treat manure of from Huangping Gulong Swine Breeding Farm. The project uses digester to treat animal manure, collect the generated biogas to avoid methane emissions. The generated biogas will be captured and flared within the project site. The residual waste from the digester will be used for agriculture fertilization aerobically in the nearby farmland. Wastewater from the animal manure treatment system will be used for irrigation and no wastewater will be discharged to the environment. The project started operation on 01-Sep-2021.
Prior to the implementation of the project, the manure was left to decay in open anaerobic lagoon at the project site and generated methane is emitted to the atmosphere directly without any methane recovery and destruction facility.
The project is expected to avoid GHG emission of methane from the uncovered open lagoon. The project is expected to achieve annual GHG emissions reduction of 51,020 tCO2e and a total emission reduction of 510,200 tCO2e during the 10-year crediting period.

name: BAITANG AONONG SWINE FARM COMPOSTING PROJECT
developer: Guizhou Aonong Qihuan Animal Husbandry Co., Ltd
project_type: Livestock, enteric fermentation, and manure management; Waste handling and disposal
description:
Baitang Aonong Swine Farm Composting Project (hereinafter referred to as the Project) is located at Baitang Village, Xinzhou Town, Huangping County, Qiandongnan Miao and Dong Autonomous Prefecture, Guizhou Province, P.R. China. The project is owned and implemented by Guizhou Aonong Qihuan Animal Husbandry Co., Ltd.
The project will introduce new anaerobic animal manure management system (Anaerobic Digester) to treat manure of from Baitang Aonong Swine Breeding Farm. The project uses digester to treat animal manure, collect the generated biogas to avoid methane emissions. The generated biogas will be captured and flared within the project site. The residual waste from the digester will be used for agriculture fertilization aerobically in the nearby farmland. Wastewater from the animal manure treatment system will be used for irrigation and no wastewater will be discharged to the environment. Construction of the project started on 20-Feb-2020 and the project is started operation on 01-Aug-2021.
Prior to the implementation of the project, the manure was left to decay in open anaerobic lagoon at the project site and generated methane is emitted to the atmosphere directly without any methane recovery and destruction facility.
The project is expected to avoid GHG emission of methane from the uncovered open lagoon. The project is expected to achieve annual GHG emissions reduction of 28,075 tCO2e and a total emission reduction of 280,750 tCO2e during the 10-year crediting period.

name: Wuwei Liangzhou Municipal Solid Waste Incineration Power Generation Project
developer: Wuwei everbright Environmental Energy Co., Ltd.
project_type: Energy industries (renewable/non-renewable sources); Waste handling and disposal
description: Wuwei Liangzhou Municipal Solid Waste Incineration Power Generation Project is located 2km east of Shazigou Village, Fafang Township, 11 km northeast of Liangzhou District, Wuwei City, Gansu Province, China. The project is invested and operated by Wuwei Everbright Environmental Energy Co., Ltd.. The project includes two incinerators with a daily capacity of 400 tonnes of waste respectively, an 18 MW steam turbine generator set, and related auxiliary facilities. The annual processing capacity is about 292,000 tons. Based on the annual operation of 8000 h, the annual average power generation of the steam turbine generator set under rated conditions is about 1.23×108kWh, and the annual average on-grid power is about 1.03×108kWh.

name: Northeast Anhui Improved Cropland Management Project
developer: Anhui Enyang Ecological Agriculture Technology Co., Ltd
project_type: Agriculture Forestry and Other Land Use
description:
The project activity is in Suzhou City, Bengbu City and Huaibei City within the boundary ofNortheast Anhui, eastern province in China. The climate type of Northeast Anhui is seasonal
temperate semi-humid monsoon climate. The project involves 160,120 hectares of wheat field, 31,734 hectares of corn field and 181,110 hectares wheat and corn rotation field. The scenario existing prior to the project’s implementation is primarily conventional tillage with synthetic fertilizer and without straw returning, which cause greater soil disturbance, increase the loss of SOC and nitrous oxide emission. Conventional practices require a significant amount of chemical and energy input and are also more likely to weaken the ecology of a landscape
compared to the improved ALM practices advocated by this project. The estimated annual average GHG emission reductions and removals through the implementation of SALM activities in the agricultural land is 764,964 t CO2e year. Over the 20 years of the first crediting period, the project will generate an estimated removal and reduction of 15,299,274 tCO2e

name: Akalan Biogas Energy Power Plant
project_type: Energy industries (renewable/non-renewable sources); Livestock, enteric fermentation, and manure management; Waste handling and disposal
description:
Akalan Biogas Power Plant, built and operated in Denizli Province, Acıpayam Distrcit, Akalan Village has an installed capacity of 3.12 MWe/ 3.150 MWm. as per the generation licence, numbered EÜ/10274-1/04999. The purpose of the project activity is to produce electricity from poultry and cattle manure with biomethanization process which will also result in fermented products that could be utilized as fertilizers by local farmers. Akalan Biogas Power plant has been granted the generation license from EMRA on 24/06/2021. As per the generation license, the annual expected generation is 23,400 MWh/year.

The facility is planned to consist of 2 co-generation units. The first unit was commissioned on 30/06/2021, each with an installed capacity of 1.560 MWe. Accordingly, project activity start date is 30/06/2021. The remaining unit with an installed capacity of 1.560 MWe was commissioned on 09/09/2022.The facility is expected to generate 23,400 MWh/year when operational capacity is 3.12 MWe. It is estimated that the project will help reduce carbon emissions by 118,249 tons annually. The total emission reduction for the whole crediting period is calculated as 1.182.494 tCO2e.

name: Installation of high efficiency wood burning cookstoves in Côte d'Ivoire
developer: C-Quest Capital CR Stoves Pte. Ltd.
description:
The project is under development. The project involves distribution of fuel-efficient improved cookstoves (ICS) in Côte d’Ivoire. The ICS disseminated through this project will replace the baseline cookstoves. 

Through this project, the distribution and installation of approximately 500,000 ICS will be undertaken for households in Côte d’Ivoire. It is intended that under this project single pot, Total Land Care Rocket Stoves will be distributed, henceforth referred as TLC-CQC Rocket Stoves. Each household will receive up to 2 ICS per household. The ICS will burn wood more efficiently thereby improving thermal transfer to pots, hence saving fuel. Not only will this halt the rapidly progressing deforestation in Côte d’Ivoire but will also reduce health hazards from indoor smoke pollution and women and children will have to spend less time collecting firewood.

The project will take place in Côte d’Ivoire. The details of the project location are provided in Section 1.12. 

The ICS will substitute the currently common cooking on open fire. The ICS burns wood more efficiently thereby improving thermal transfer to pots, hence saving fuel and lowering greenhouse gas emissions.

The baseline scenario is the continued use of non-renewable wood fuel by the target population to meet similar thermal energy needs as provided by project cookstoves in absence of project activity.

The average annual GHG emission reduction from the project is expected to be 1,545,621 t CO2e and total 15,456,217 tCO2e over the entire crediting period of 10 years.

name: Otog Front Banner sustainable grassland management project
developer: Otog Front Banner Cultural Tourism Group Ltd.
project_type: Agriculture Forestry and Other Land Use
description: Otog Front Banner Sustainable Grassland Management Project is located in Otog Front Banner, Ordos City, Inner Mongolia Autonomous Region of China. The project is aimed to restore the local degraded grassland ecosystem from adoption of sustainable grassland management practices, such as improving the rotation of grazing animals between summer and winter pastures, limiting the timing and number of grazing animals on degraded pastures, and restoration of severely degraded land by replanting with perennial grasses and ensuring appropriate management over the long-term. Totally, 100,297.9 ha of degraded grassland has been managed scientifically by including by fence building and reseeding of native grass species.

name: Grouped Captive Solar Power Project by Kohinoor Maple Leaf Group
description: The proposed grouped project activity is a step towards supporting the implementation and installation of solar rooftop and ground mounted projects in the premises of Lahore, Pakistan. The main goal of project activity is to implement renewable energy projects in the country and the significant importance of revenues from sale of Verified Carbon Units (VCUs) to achieve this goal forms the basis of the implementation of this project activity. The project activity is a voluntary action and each SPV will be the Project Proponent for their project activity.

name: Seringueira REDD+ Project
project_type: Agriculture Forestry and Other Land Use
description: The Seringueira Project is implemented in the municipality of Ipixuna, Amazonas State, Brazil. It falls under the Agriculture, Forestry and Other Land Uses (AFOLU) sector within the Reducing Emissions from Deforestation and Forest Degradation (REDD+) category The project will conserve 2,773.79 hectares of native Amazon rainforests in a region where deforestation pressure is mainly due to pasture activities, designated to Planned Avoided Deforestation (APD). For the total area and by the end of the project, it is estimated a total avoided emissions of 1,100,000.00 tons of Greenhouse Gases (tCO2e). The project will be developed considering the CCB Standard, with benefits for Climate, Community and Biodiversity. As benefits to the climate, the maintenance of forest cover results in exceptional benefits for adapting to the impacts caused by climate change, such as changes in the rainfall regime, as the area presents a dense hydrographic network that contributes to the provision and quality of water in the Amazon River basin. As benefits to the communities, the project will implement systems of underground water collection, installation of solar panels for electricity generation, provision of satellite internet service, construction of toilets with septic tanks, training of fire brigades, training of women in entrepreneurship, provision of assistance in the formation of community associations, and construction of a school. These measures will enable water security and access to information to minimize the impacts caused by climate change in traditional, low-income extractive communities.The maintenance of forest cover ensures the conservation of biodiversity, the maintenance of ecosystem functioning (e.g., nutrient cycling) and of ecosystem services provisioning (e.g., carbon sequestration) performed by living organisms. It is noteworthy that the project includes a high priority area for biodiversity conservation, according to the CCB Gold Level vulnerability criteria.

name: Sustainable coffee landscapes in indigenous rural communities of Oaxaca, Mexico
project_type: Agriculture Forestry and Other Land Use
description:
This project is designed to support the livelihoods of at least 3,250 smallholder coffee producers from which at least 1,000 are women, in the State of Oaxaca, Mexico , by increasing the resilience of their coffee production systems after the impact caused by coffee rust. These producers are affi liated to the 45 cooperatives of CEPCO, The project will help CEPCO pursue and accelerate its efforts to restore coffee landscapes by focusing in areas with best potential for high adoption and technical success, around 4 main planting systems: New shade grown coffee systems set up on good potential plots (2,062 ha). Increased shade in existing coffee plots (3,300 ha). Productive forest set up (timber) in degraded land (1,031 ha). Diversification pilots on cocoa and maize/fruit trees intercropping (100 ha)
The 45 cooperatives members of CEPCO represent a total of 142 communities organized in 6 clusters: Cañada, Costa, Istmo. Mixteca, Papaloapam, Sierra Norte, Sierra Sur distributed in
several landscapes in Oaxaca state. Project beneficiaries will be farmers members of CEPCO and their families, who will join on a voluntary basis. It will consider a gender approach in which specific needs for women and youth will be identified and incorporated as much as possible in the activities and project tools. Plots will be selected in degraded and open lands, for new plantations of shaded coffee and timber plots. 3,300 hectares will be areas with already established in coffee plantations with some shade w h ere 50 trees per ha will be added to enrich the tree cover.
The Project activities are carried out according to the approved project methodology AR ACM0003 for the crediting period of 20 years. The project aims to remove ACM0003 for the crediting period of 20 years. The project aims to remove an estimated 54.675,24 tCO2e annually and 1,093.504,78 tCO2e during the crediting period.

name: Bamboo Afforestation in Malawi
developer: C-Quest Capital SG Africa Holdings Private Limited
project_type: Agriculture Forestry and Other Land Use
description:
The Malawi Bamboo Afforestation Project will distribute seedlings of giant bamboo, Dendrocalamus asper, to individual agricultural homesteads in rural Malawi. The project will also provide educational support and outreach for the long-term care of bamboo clumps. 

The project is located within the political boundary of the Republic of Malawi.

The project will generate GHG emission reductions by sequestering carbon in live above- and belowground biomass. When individual bamboo clumps reach the end of their lifespan, they will be replaced by a new clump, ensuring carbon remains sequestered over the project lifetime.

Smallholder agricultural homesteads are widespread across Malawi. A variety of trees are grown on farms, in gardens, and around homesteads to serve as fuel, timber, and other uses. However, fast-growing giant bamboo is not grown in Malawi at a large scale. 

Estimated annual average GHG emissions reductions: 174,301 tCO2e
Total GHG emission reductions: 5,054,739 tCO2e

name: Installation of high efficiency wood burning cookstoves in Tanzania - Project 3
developer: C-Quest Capital CR Stoves Pte. Ltd.
description:
The project activity includes the distribution of fuel-efficient improved cookstoves (ICS) in Tanzania. The ICS distributed through this project will replace the baseline cookstoves i.e., three-stone fire or conventional open fire.

An approximately 100,000 ICS through this project will be distributed and installed in the households of Tanzania. It is intended that under this project activity single or double pot TLC-CQC Rocket Stove will be distributed. The ICS burns wood more efficiently due to its higher thermal efficiency, hence saving fuel. As a result, deforestation will be slowed in Tanzania and will also reduce health hazards from indoor smoke pollution and women and children will spend less time gathering firewood.

The end user will be informed in advance that the use of ICS generates carbon finance to the project proponent which in turn is used for recovering the price of ICS and project implementation costs.

Each ICS is the project activity instance that will substitute the current practice of using the three stone fire or a conventional device with no improved combustion air supply or flue gas ventilation, that is without a grate or a chimney. Fuelwood is burnt more efficiently with the ICS because its thermal efficiency is higher, resulting in a reduction in fuel consumption and greenhouse gas emissions.

The baseline scenario is the continued use of three stone fired or a conventional cook stove without a grate or a chimney by the target population burning non-renewable wood fuel to meet similar thermal energy needs in the absence of project activity.

The average annual GHG emission reduction from the project is expected to be 285,339 t CO2e. Total GHG emission reduction from the project is expected to be 2,853,391 tCO2e over the entire crediting period of 10 years.
