name: The High Impact Soil Carbon Program of Lithuania
project_type: Agriculture Forestry and Other Land Use
description:
The High Impact Soil Carbon Program of Lithuania is a joint initiative between UAB Heavy Finance (HF) farmers within the Lithuanian Republic borders. The program utilizes private capital to implement, and adopt improved agricultural land management for a long-term period, thus changing the mindset and establishing climate change mitigation and biodiversity-friendly practices.  						
It is a first-of-its-kind program in Lithuania and the Baltics. It aims to assist farmers in overcoming barriers that prevent adopting sustainable land management practices by providing scientific knowledge, training, and technical and financial support to adopt mitigating climate activities successfully. The program is designed to expand over time and cover a range of conservational farming practices in Lithuania to help drive the change from the current conventional agriculture toward resilient and sustainable agrifood systems.

name: BioLite Africa Improved Stove Program
description: The goal of the proposed project is to distribute improved cookstoves (“ICS”) in the households/small and medium sized enterprises (SMEs) in Sub Saharan Africa, with the initial host countries being Rwanda, Malawi, Nigeria, Mali, Madagascar, Senegal, Côte d’Ivoire, Democratic Republic of the Congo, Zambia and Uganda (with a possibility of expansion to other countries e.g., Mozambique, Cameroon, Somalia/Somaliland, Tanzania, Ethiopia, Kenya, Sierra Leone, Liberia, Togo, Burundi, Ghana, Benin, Burkina, Guinea, Guinea Bissau, Zimbabwe and Namibia in Sub Saharan Africa in future).

name: Strengthening rural livelihood through carbon finance: Agroforestry practices in Lucknow Forest Circle of Uttar Pradesh
developer: Department of Environment, Forest and Climate Change, Government of Uttar Pradesh
project_type: Agriculture Forestry and Other Land Use
description: Agroforestry practices as an alternate to fulfil the rising demand for timber and other non-timber forest produce is promising in long term as it provides both wood and food. Agroforestry can help to conserve and rehabilitate the ecosystem along with providing better livelihood opportunities to the rural community. The proposed ARR VCS project plans to promote sustainable agroforestry for small-scale farmers to provide them with financial benefits and ensure GHG mitigation in the state of Uttar Pradesh, India.

name: CHITETEZO MBAULA PROJECT – MALAWI
description: The present project promotes the distribution and utilization of locally made Chitetezo Mbaula (CM) stoves in Malawi. The CM stove is significantly more efficient than the traditional three stone open fire and therefore contributes to reducing wood consumption, preserving local forests and reducing greenhouse gas (GHG) emissions resulting from unsustainably sourced wood. The CM stove also has further health and social benefits such as reduction of smoke produced during cooking or reduction of time required to collect wood.

name: BLACK SOLDIER FLY COMMERCIAL FARMING PROJECT
description:
Chanzi are a protein rich, animal feed producing company, located in Tanzania, and with expansions in place for Kenya as well. Their high protein animal feed is produced through the farming of Black Soldier Flies, and the use of their larvae either in whole form, or dried crushed form. 

The Black Solider Fly (BSF) is a particular species of fly that is commercially farmed around the world, for its ability to be converted into an insect-based animal feed. Its name comes from the color of the adult flies, which are black with metallic reflections. The commercialization of farming BSF’s came from the large demand for animal feed around the world and the concerns that fish meal and/soy-based meal (animal feed) would in the long term not be a sustainable solution.

The larvae are fed organic food waste, which come from a variety of sources, i.e. pre-consumer and post-consumer at industrial and household levels. This organic waste would have otherwise been sent to landfill, thus ensuring recovery for beneficiation of this waste. This diverting of organic waste from a landfill leads to the avoidance of carbon emissions and can therefore potentially be registered as a process which generates carbon credits.

name: Wetlands Along the Yangtze River and Dongting Lake Restoration Project in Junshan
project_type: Agriculture Forestry and Other Land Use
description:
Wetlands along the Yangtze River and Dongting Lake Restoration Project in Junshan (hereafter as “this project”) is an initiative to promote climate change mitigation and adaptation, maintain biodiversity, and create improved livelihoods, well-being, and employment for wetland-dependent communities in the Project Zone. The Project Zone is an area of 13093.19 ha located in the northeast of Junshan District, Yueyang City, Hunan Province, China. By sowing grass, cutting down invasive poplars, planting native vegetation, and digging ditches, this project is expected to increase local carbon sequestration and contribute to the development of the local wetland ecosystem.
This project anticipates mitigating or reversing the degraded wetlands and rewetting the drained wetlands in the 1,297.76 ha of wetlands in the project area. The invasive species Populus Canadensis, which may damage the wetlands, is also expected to be eliminated during the project’s lifetime.
This project anticipates the sequestration of an estimated 498,492tCO2e over its lifetime of 50 years at an estimated average of 9,774tCO2e annually.
The objectives of this project include bringing benefits to three main aspects including climate, community, and biodiversity. It will meet the Gold Level criteria for both climate change adaptation and biodiversity as demonstrated in the PD Report.

name: Productive Second Floor with Macaúba
project_type: Agriculture Forestry and Other Land Use
description:
The “Productive Second Floor with Macaúba” is a VCS AFOLU (Agriculture, Forestry and Other Land Use) grouped project, Scope 14, and, specifically, it falls under the ARR (Afforestation, Reforestation and Revegetation) category. 
The project works with local farmers to implement integrated systems in previously degraded pastures and/or croplands. The main project activity consists of the planting of Macaúba trees. This will be done considering two possible arrangements: (i) Macaúba intercropped with pasture (silvipastoral) or (ii) macuaba intercropped with agriculture (agrisilvicultural).
Through the planting of Macaúba trees the project will contribute to an increase in carbon stocks and associated GHG removals. The project activity will also improve the livelihood of local farmers and provide other ecosystem services, such as: maintaining the local microclimate, preventing erosion, conserving soil and moisture.

name: BRUSQUE LANDFILL GAS PROJECT
project_type: Energy industries (renewable/non-renewable sources); Waste handling and disposal
description:
The Brusque landfill is a well-managed landfill site located in the municipality of Brusque in Santa Catarina State (Southeastern region of Brazil). The landfill started its operations in year 2009. This landfill site was designed and has been operated by the host-country project proponent and project owner and project proponent Recicle Catarinense de Resíduos LTDA.
The proposed VCS project activity titled “Brusque Landfill Gas Project” encompasses the promotion of collection and destruction/utilization of landfill gas (LFG) (rich in methane) through collection LFG and its destruction in high temperature enclosed flare and utilization as gaseous fuel in a set of engine-generator sets of an electricity generation infrastructure (with final total combined nameplate installed capacity of 4.56 MW).  
As per its design configuration, combustion of collected LFG occurs in the following methane destruction device(s): 
-	1 high temperature enclosed flare;
-	3 engine-generator sets  of an electricity generation infrastructure (in which collected LFG will be utilized as gaseous fuel for electricity generation), that will be installed in 2024.
-	Possibility of future increase of the number of engine-generator sets, maintaining a total combined nameplate capacity up to 10 MW.

name: Grouped Hydro Power Project by EKI Energy Services Limited
description: The project serves the purpose of producing clean electrical energy in a sustainable manner. The project activity involves implementation of 2 turbines of 9.51 MW Mai Beni Hydropower Project (MBHP) and 6.2 MW Lower Jogmai Khola Hydropower Project (LJKHP) which utilize potential energy available for power generation. Therefore, no fossil fuels are involved for power generation in the project activity. The proposed project activity will also reduce the anthropogenic emissions of greenhouse gases into the atmosphere by avoiding business as usual operation of existing fossil fuels-based power plants to produce equivalent amount of electricity

name: Itamarati Grouped REDD Project
project_type: Agriculture Forestry and Other Land Use
description:
The Itamarati Grouped REDD Project is initially formed by 4 properties  located in the municipalities of Nova Olímpia, Denise, Barra dos Bugres, Salto do Céu and Reserva do Cabaçal in the State of Mato Grosso, Brazil. Instance 1 is located in the Amazon and Cerrado biomes. The total area of the properties is 69,207.15 ha. The project aims to avoid the unplanned deforestation (AUD) within the 22,753.36 ha project area, consisting of 64% Amazon rainforest and 36% Cerrado. The present REDD project is expected to avoid predicted 4,861 ha of deforestation, equating to 1,264,521 tCO2e in emissions reductions over the 30-year project lifetime, with an annual average of 42,151 tCO2e.

In addition to the project’s ecological and carbon benefits, a proportion of the carbon credits generated will be dedicated to improving the social and environmental conditions in the project region, specifically contributing to improving deforestation control, aiming at the propagation of environmental awareness, generation of alternative sources of income and environmental education actions.

name: Serenity Valley REDD Project
project_type: Agriculture Forestry and Other Land Use
description:
The Serenity Valley REDD Project is located in three different municipalities in a private propert in the State of Pará, Brazil: Cumuaru do Norte, Santana do Araguaia and Santa Maria das Barreiras consisting of 100% Amazon rainforest. The project aims to avoid the unplanned deforestation(AUD) within the 52,644.73 ha project area. The present REDD project is expected to avoid a predicted 19,220 ha of deforestation, equating to 6,251,508 tCO2e in emissions reductions over the 30-year project lifetime, with an annual average of 208,384 tCO2e.

In addition to the project’s ecological and carbon benefits, a proportion of the carbon credits generated will be dedicated to improving the social and environmental conditions in the project region, specifically contributing to improving deforestation control, aiming at the propagation of environmental awareness, generation of alternative sources of income and environmental education actions.

name: Urupianga Grouped REDD Project
project_type: Agriculture Forestry and Other Land Use
description:
The project area is located within 6 private properties, located in the municipality of Vila Rica, inthe State of Mato Grosso, Brazil , inserted in an area of transition from Cerrado to Amazon biome. The project aims to avoid unplanned deforestation (AUD) in a project area of 13,351 ha. The AUD REDD project is expected to avoid predicted deforestation of 6,214.13 ha of deforestation, equating to 2,309,793 tCO2e in emissions reductions over the 30-year project lifetime (01-February-2021 to 31-January-2051), with an annual average of 76,993 tCO2e.

Beyond the project’s ecological and carbon benefits, a proportion of the carbon credits generated will be dedicated to improving the social and environmental conditions in the project region, specifically contributing to improving deforestation control, and developing environmental education and other social activities.

name: Project Sathya Improved Cookstoves and Livelihood
description:
PROJECT SATHYA is an Improved Cookstoves and Livelihood project (hereafter referred to as “the Project” or “Project Sathya”) that aims for the sustainable development of the poor and marginalised communities residing in the core, buffer and fringe areas of the Sathyamangalam Tiger Reserve, a protected area in Erode District, Tamil Nadu State, India (hereinafter referred to as “STR”).  Key activities of Project Sathya include:
1)	Installation and maintenance of 7500 Sarala brand improved cookstoves (“ICS”), which are fuel-efficient in-situ cookstoves with a chimney, that are constructed inside homes. This reduces fuelwood usage, air pollution, deforestation, human-animal conflict, health risks, poverty, and gender inequality.  
2)	Creating awareness about the advantages of clean cooking practices and ongoing maintenance of devices to ensure continued health and economic benefits.
3)	Training of people from the community, primarily women, as cookstove makers to provide skilling, additional livelihood, supports higher adoption of devices and improves ongoing maintenance and usage.
4)	Training of community members in digital literacy, surveys, monitoring, project management, collaboration, and related skills to improve livelihood opportunities and reduce inequalities.
5)	Opening of bank accounts for members in the community to support financial inclusion and increase financial independence for women.
6)	Sourcing raw materials for cookstove making and installation from local micro, small and medium-sized enterprises to support economic development and employment opportunities in the region.
7)	Upgrading school infrastructure by supplying water filters, utensils, etc to support continued education and better health.
8)	Solar lighting in the villages to improve safety, reduce human-animal conflict and improve access to clean lighting.
This Project supports SDGs 1, 3, 4, 5, 6, 7, 8, 10, 13, 15, and 17.

name: GIRESUN LANDFILL GAS (LFG) PROJECT
project_type: Energy industries (renewable/non-renewable sources); Waste handling and disposal
description:
The project, Giresun Solid Waste Management Facility and Electricity Generation Facility (4.353 MWm / 4.242 MWe) is in Giresun Province, Görele District, Çavuşlu neighbourhood, and owned and operated by Biotrend.
Giresun LFG plant has been granted the generation license from EMRA on 24/12/2020. As per the generation license, the annual expected generation is 31,815,000 kWh/year. The first unit was commissioned on 02/04/2021. Accordingly, project activity start date is 02/04/2021.
This project adopts the renewal crediting period of 7 years. The expected average annual emission reductions are 52,207 (tCO2e).

name: Future Carbon Methane Capture Grouped Project
project_type: Energy industries (renewable/non-renewable sources); Waste handling and disposal
description:
Future Carbon Methane Capture Grouped Project is a grouped project. A centralized manure management plant operated by the International Center for Renewable Energy – CIBIOGAS serves as the first project instance. Such plant was designed to generate renewable electricity from the captured biogas and avoid environmental impacts due to inadequate treatment of swine manure. The plant is located in the municipality of Toledo, State of Paraná, in the South Region of Brazil and will replace animal waste management systems (anaerobic lagoons) from fourteen swine confinement farms located in the same city.

The project was developed to reduce methane emissions and adequately treat the waste produced by small and medium-sized swine and cattle farms in feedlots. The project activity involved the installation of a centralized waste treatment plant (Biodigesters or bioenergy plants), with the capture of biogas that will be used to generate energy in biogas generator systems. This will replace anaerobic lagoons, which are considered the baseline scenario for livestock farms.

Based on its first instance, this project is expected to reduce 93,085 tCO2e for its first crediting period, ranging from 01-March-2023 to 28-February-2030. Incremental emission reductions might be achieved with the inclusion of new project instances.

name: Household Appliance Distribution in Lao PDR-CPA-003
description:
The project activity involves distribution of improved cook stoves (ICS) to households in Lao People’s Democratic Republic (Lao PDR) by C Quest Capital Stoves Asia Limited (CQC). 

The distribution of improved cook stoves would displace the use of non-renewable biomass to meet similar thermal energy needs for cooking in households. Presently, the households use traditional cookstoves with very low efficiency, which leads to consumption of copious amount of firewood for preparing meals. 

The project activity was pursued as a component of the PoA “Household energy appliance programme” (ref. 10030) under CPA title “10030 P1 0003 CP1 Household Appliance Distribution in Lao PDR CPA003” 1 with Differ Cookstoves AS as the CME and is now being transitioned to VCS. First stove under this project activity was installed on 11 January 2018, and the project has accrued issuances under CDM until 31 December 2020.

Ecoeye Co., Ltd. (Ecoeye) will be responsible for financing the cost of production, distribution and maintenance of the stoves distributed under this project.

The project will facilitate the adoption of energy efficient ICS. This, in turn, will curb deforestation and forest degradation in Lao PDR by encouraging people to use energy efficient stoves and improve the quality of life of communities in Lao PDR by reducing drudgery, time and money spent in fuel wood collection and purchase, while also decreasing indoor air pollution. Worldwide, the effort will also lead to the reduction in GHG emissions into the atmosphere.

name: ECOPARQUE MACEIÓ LANDFILL GAS PROJECT
project_type: Energy industries (renewable/non-renewable sources); Waste handling and disposal
description: The proposed VCS project activity titled “EcoParque Maceió landfill gas project” encompasses the promotion at the Ecoparque Maceió landfill site of destruction and/or utilization and/or supply to consumer(s) of landfill gas (LFG) (rich in methane) through collection LFG and its destruction in high temperature enclosed flare(s), utilization as gaseous fuel in set of engine-generator sets of an electricity generation infrastructure (with final total combined nameplate installed capacity of 7.13 MW) and supply of upgraded  LFG to consumer(s) with a LFG processing and supply infrastructure of combined installed capacity of 2,500 Nm³/h.

name: Ground-Truth Australian Orchards
project_type: Agriculture Forestry and Other Land Use
description:
Regenerative farming practices have been proposed as a means to reduce the climate impact and carbon footprint of agriculture by, inter alia, enhancing the ability of agricultural soils to store carbon, buffering food production systems from environmental changes, improving water and nutrient use efficiency, and removing CO2 from the atmosphere. 
For this project, which encompasses regenarative orchards in Australia, GHG reductions and removals will be achieved by the implementation of a combination of the following practice changes: 
•	Reduce the intensity of agricultural practices, specifically reducing the use of synthetic fertilisers by incorporating organic amendments, and reducing the use of chemical pesticides via improved integrated pest management 
•	Cover cropping, including promoting inter-row biomass generation and the establishment of multi-species cover crops
•	Establishment of new permanent tree crops and associated canopy growth
•	Promote specific regeneration of soil and the increase of soil organic carbon (SOC)
•	Reduce water consumption and energy use through improved irrigation management 
•	Promote carbon sequestration in the above ground biomass
•	Improved crop residue management by re-incorporating prunings and crop waste into the soil
The undertaking of this project will support a number of United Nations Sustainable Development Goals in the project area, local communities, surrounding environments, and in the supply chain. The project will contribute towards SDG 2: Zero Hunger, SDG 3: Good Health and Wellbeing, SDG 6: Clean Water and Sanitation, SDG 12: Responsible Consumption and Production, SDG 13: Climate Action, SDG 14: Life Below Water, and SDG 15: Life on Land.

name: Qinghai Haixi Ulan Afforestation Project
developer: National Forestry and Grassland Administration Northwest Investigation and Planning Institute
project_type: Agriculture Forestry and Other Land Use
description:
Qinghai Haixi Ulan Afforestation Project (hereafter as “the project”) is located in Ulan County, Haixi Mongolian and Tibetan Autonomous Prefecture, Qinghai Province of China. The aim of the project is to increase carbon sequestration and to contribute to the local sustainable development by planting the trees and shrubs on the degraded mountains and degraded land.
7,045.27 ha of forest is about to be planted by direct planting on the degraded mountain and degraded land in Ulan County, and the planted species are all native species including Tamarix chinensis (Chinese tamarisk), Populus (aspen), Caragana korshinskii and Artemisia desertorum. The implementation of the afforestation project will generate GHG emission removals and mitigate climate change, improve soil and water conservation and forest cover; enhance local biodiversity by increasing the connectivity of forest, and bring income and job opportunities for local communities and residents.

name: Qinghai Ulan and Delingha Improved Grassland Management Project
developer: National Forestry and Grassland Administration Northwest Investigation and Planning Institute
project_type: Agriculture Forestry and Other Land Use
description:
Qinghai Ulan and Delingha Improved Grassland Management Project (hereafter referred to as “the project”) is located in Haixi Mongol and Tibetan Autonomous Prefecture , Qinghai Province, China. The project aims to restore 70,860 hectares (or 1,062,900 Mu ) degraded grasslands in Ulan and Delingha by adopting a variety of measures including grass planting, fence installation and sustainable grazing management. The project will increase carbon sequestration, reverse grassland degradation, contribute to local development and preserve cultural traditions.
The project focuses on 70,860 hectares of moderately or severely degraded grasslands in Ulan and Delingha and adopts a combination of the following measures:  
· Grass planting: native grass species Elymus nutans, Festuca sinensis, Poa crymophila are directly planted on severely degraded grassland.
· Fence installation: fences are installed to separate the project area from the rest of the land.
· Sustainable grazing management: depending on the grassland conditions and the timeline, different grazing approaches will be adopted: grazing will be prohibited for two years after the completion of grass planting and fence installation on severely degraded grassland; rotational grazing or rest periods of grazing will be introduced on moderately degraded grassland.

name: Siziwang Banner Improved Grassland Management Project
project_type: Agriculture Forestry and Other Land Use
description:
Siziwang Banner Improved Grassland Management Project aims to restore the degraded grassland ecosystem through grass-planting and grazing management in the project zone. This project locates in Siziwang Banner , Inner Mongolia Autonomous Region of China. It covers the entire grassland area of Siziwang Banner, including 13 minor administrative districts under the jurisdiction of the banner. By introducing sustainable grazing measures and managing the plants properly, this project is expected to increase local carbon sequestration and contribute to the development of the local ecosystem. 
Specifically, this project anticipates scientific management of 1966396.34 ha of degraded grassland in total to mitigate and reverse the degradation. Three main restoration measures are adopted, including rotational grazing, rest grazing and grassland reseeding.
This project is estimated to generate GHG emission removals of 54,091,628tCO2e in 40 years, with an average annual GHG emission removal of 1,352,291 tCO2e.
The objectives of this project include bringing benefits to three main aspects, climate, community, and biodiversity.

name: 1MTN Uganda Bamboo Planting Project
project_type: Agriculture Forestry and Other Land Use
description: The 1MT Nation Uganda Bamboo Planting project -the Project is an AFOLU project, located in Uganda. The project is located on depredated land - grassland, not used for many decades and/or land that has been heavily farmed for many decades, following the clearing of the native ecosystem many decades ago. An afforestation project has been designed to plant and maintain selected species of giant clumping bamboo. The Project is a grouped project, located in Uganda. Using native bamboo species, the Project aims to restore 10,000 hectares of degraded lands that were cleared of their native ecosystem more than 10 years ago.

name: BUYUKSISMANLAR BIOGAS ENERGY PLANT
project_type: Energy industries (renewable/non-renewable sources); Waste handling and disposal
description:
BUYUKSISMANLAR BIOGAS ENERGY PLANT is a biogas-to- energy project that involves methane capture through anaerobic digestion and utilization of methane for thermal energy and electricity generation via cogeneration units. The chicken manure as the main feedstock is collected from the neighbouring chicken farm with special trucks and transferred to the plant. Continuously Stirred Tank Reactor (CSTR) type anaerobic digesters are used to capture methane-rich biogas. Captured biogas is then utilized in cogeneration units. The thermal energy is used mainly for heating anaerobic fermenters. The generated electricity is not only supplied to the national grid but also used for auxiliary/internal consumption required for the plant to function.

The project is being implemented by BÜYÜK ŞİŞMANLAR YUMURTA VE GIDA MADDELERİ TİCARET LİMİTED ŞİRKETİ, the Project Owner, in Kalecik district, Ankara province, in Turkey.

The project adopts the renewable crediting period of 7 years, twice renewable for a total of 21 years. The estimated average net annual emission reductions are 42,289 tCO2eq/y. Accordingly, the project is expected to generate 296,026 tCO2eq emissions reduction during the first crediting period.

name: AS KOC KIRSEHIR BIOGAS POWER PLANT
description:
As Koç Kırşehir Biogas Power Plant is a biogas-to-energy project that captures biogas from animal manure, cattle and chicken in particular, -via anaerobic digestion- and utilizes it to generate thermal and electric energy through cogeneration units. The animal manure as the main feedstock is collected from the neighboring animal farms with special trucks and transferred to the plant. Continuously Stirred Tank Reactor (CSTR) type anaerobic digesters are used to capture methane-rich biogas. Captured biogas is then utilized in cogeneration units. Thermal energy is used mainly for heating anaerobic fermenters. The generated electricity is not only supplied to the national grid but also used for auxiliary/internal consumption required for the plant to function.

The project is being implemented by AKYURT ELEKTRİK SANAYİ VE TİCARET ANONİM ŞİRKETİ, the Project Owner, Kırşehir province, in Turkey.

The project activity avoids methane emission through the above-mentioned capture and utilization processes. Furthermore, the project reduces CO2 emissions from fossil-fuel-based electricity generation by supplying biogas-based electricity to the national grid.

This project adopts the renewable crediting period of 7 years, twice renewable for a total of 21 years. The estimated average net annual emission reductions are 256,351 tCO2eq/y. Accordingly, the project is expected to generate 1,794,457 tCO2eq/y emissions reduction during the first crediting period.

name: Community Restoration of Native Ecosystems in Ghana
project_type: Agriculture Forestry and Other Land Use
description: Community Restoration of Native Ecosystems in Ghana is a landscape-scale reforestation project designed by Three Trees and Climate Investment Partners that aims to increase tree cover in various regions of rural Ghana by planting native species on degraded communal lands or forest reserves. This reforestation will contribute to wildlife habitat or corridors, improve water infiltration, control erosion, and sequester carbon, among other ecosystem services. This grouped project is targeting a scale of up to 50,000 hectares.

name: Henan Luoning IFM (conversion of logged to protected forest) Project
project_type: Agriculture Forestry and Other Land Use
description:
Henan Luoning IFM (conversion of logged to protected forest) Project (hereafter referred as “the
project”) is located in Luoning County, Luoyang City, Henan Province, China. The project is to
protect forest from logging to generate GHG emission reductions and contribute to local
sustainable development. Before the implementation of the project activity, the trees are logged
based on a government-approved timber management plan for harvesting the project area. The
implementation of the project activity converses the trees to protected forest to reduce the GHG
emissions.
The project type is “Improved Forest Management: Logged to Protected Forest (LtPF)”. The
project start date is 01/04/2020, and the project area is 9,451.55 ha. The species of this project
are Robinia, Chinese pine, Hard Broad and Cypress.
With the implementation of the project activity, total GHG emission reductions or removals are
about 4,118,556 tCO2e in 30 years the average annual emission reduction is 137,285 tCO2e and
total GHG emission reductions or removals with buffer deduction is about 3,212,467 tCO2e in 30
years, the average annual GHG emission reductions or removals with buffer deduction is 107,082
tCO2e.

name: Core Carbon Sustainable Rice Productions 03
project_type: Agriculture Forestry and Other Land Use
description:
Paddy fields are the most dominant anthropogenic sources of methane in the atmosphere (5-20% of the total emission from all anthropogenic sources ). Anaerobic decomposition of organic material in flooded rice fields produces methane, which escapes to the atmosphere primarily by transport through the rice plants. The annual amount of CH4 emitted from a given area of rice is a function of the number and duration of crops grown, water regimes before and during the cultivation period, and organic and inorganic soil amendments. Soil type, temperature, and rice cultivar also affect CH4 emissions. This CH4 emission-intensive cultivation method will be targeted by the proposed programme, which will involve the implementation of the technology/measures that result in reduced anaerobic decomposition of organic matter in rice cropping soils and, thus, reduced generation of methane.
The project activity comprises grouped projects of rice fields implementing the following methods:
 (a) Rice farms that change the water regime during the cultivation period from continuously to intermittent flooded conditions and/or a shortened period of flooded conditions;
(b) Alternate wetting and drying method (AWD)
(c) Rice farms that change their rice cultivation practice from transplanted to direct-seeded rice (DSR).
Thus, the measure will consist of AWD and/or DSR in combination with an adjusted water management system in rice cultivation.
The Project Activity Instances will be implemented in Karimnagar and Jagtial districts in the state of Telangana.  Each instance of 5000 Hectares will be implemented in Karimnagar and Jagtial districts, Telangana State.

name: Heilongjiang Hulin Improved Agricultural Land Management Project
developer: Heilongjiang Tanlv Ecological Resources Development Co., Ltd.
project_type: Agriculture Forestry and Other Land Use
description:
Heilongjiang Hulin Improved Agricultural Land Management Project (hereafter as “the project”) is located in Hulin City, Jixi City, Heilongjiang Province of China. The goal of this initiative is to reduce the carbon emissions currently emitted by the farms taking part to the project and raise the carbon stored in the soil. In addition, the selected measures will contribute to improving crop yields and soil health.
The project is aimed to prevent the soil degradation through adoption of the improved crop land management practices (collectively referred to conservational tillage) to replace the conventional cultivation mode.

name: REDD Carbonflor
project_type: Agriculture Forestry and Other Land Use
description: The REDD Carbonflor is a multi-activity grouped project, located in Brazil, in the Amazon and Cerrado biomes. The project is classified in scope 14 - AFOLU (Agriculture, Forestry and Other Land Uses) and falls into the category Reducing Emissions from Deforestation and Degradation (REDD) in the scopes of planned (APD) and unplanned (AUDD) deforestation. The REDD Carbonflor´s main goal is to reduce global greenhouse gas emissions (GHG) through the conservation of native vegetation in the Amazon and Cerrado biomes. The project is based on the conservation of the remaining forest cover of properties under pressure from deforestation and degradation.

name: Electrical Hydrant Dispensers at İstanbul Airport
description:
The project activity (from now on referred to as ‘Project’) uses Electrical Hydrant Dispensers (from now on referred to as “EHDs”) in vehicle fleets located in İstanbul Airport to carry the aviation fuel for planes. The project consists of entirely new EHDs, which project proponent acquires instead of buying new diesel vehicles. Only EHDs are included where the project proponent has signed a contractual arrangement with the supplier of the vehicles that grants all reductions to Turkish Fuel Services (project proponent), thus having proof of title and avoiding double-counting issues. Only EHDs are included which continue to operate.
The primary purpose of this project is to use electric vehicles instead of fossil fuel-powered trucks at İstanbul Airport in Turkey to carry the aviation fuel. Using electric-powered vehicles instead of fossil fuel-powered ones leads to lower GHG emissions per distance driven.
The EHDs project involves 60 electric cars. Electric vehicles are run by electric motors powered by energy stored in batteries. Electric vehicles have an electric motor instead of an Internal Combustion Engine (ICE). As an electric vehicle runs on electricity, the vehicle emits no exhaust from a tailpipe, i.e., it has zero tailpipe emission and does not contain components, such as a fuel pump, fuel line, or fuel tank.

name: Water Purification System for Safe Drinking Water (SDW) in Indonesia
description:
The lack of a safe drinking water supply is one of the primary issues in Indonesia. The size of the population paired with an increase in clean water demand poses an enormous challenge to water provision. The poor quality of the existing water sources leaves the citizen with no choice but to rely on alternatives such as bottled and boiled water. The high reliance on non-renewable biomass and fossil fuels for typical household water boiling could contribute air pollution, deforestation, increase public health risks, and many more.

The grouped project will install low greenhouse gas (GHG) emitting water treatment facilities to provide clean drinking water to communities that previously had no access to a public distribution network supplying safe drinking water (SDW) within the host country, the Republic of Indonesia. The Project serves as an open platform for various water treatment technologies, which are eligible under the methodology AMS-III.AV (Version 08.0). 

Through the installation of water treatment facilities, the project reduces the use and demand for fossil fuels and non-renewable biomass that would have been used to boil water to purify water in the absence of the grouped project. Primarily, the operation of a water treatment facility reduces greenhouse gas emissions of around 21,475 t/CO2et per year along with various other environmental, social, and economic benefits. This project is thus designed for the long-term improvement of the living conditions of people in the Republic of Indonesia.

name: Bekmezci Biogas Energy Power Plant
project_type: Energy industries (renewable/non-renewable sources); Waste handling and disposal
description:
Bekmezci Biogas Power Plant, built and operated in Çankırı Province, Şabanözü District, Gürpınar Village has an installed capacity of 4.68 MWe/ 4.818 MWm as per the generation license. The purpose of the project activity is to produce electricity from laying chicken and cattle manure with biomethanization process. The biogas that will be released during the biodegradation of organic wastes is used for electricity, hot water and heat production in the cogeneration unit. The total power of the cogeneration system to be established will be designed to be 4,818 MWm – 4,680 MWe. Bekmezci Biogas Power plant has been granted the generation license from EMRA on 10/06/2021. As per the generation license, the annual expected generation is 35,100,000 kWh/year.

It is estimated that the project help reduce the carbon emissions average by 88,251 tons annually. The total emission reduction for the whole crediting period is calculated as 882,506 tons of CO2.

12,805.82 ha (192,087.26 Mu ) of forest is to be planted by direct planting native species and the species cultivated on local ecosystem for over 30 years  on degraded lands in Longnan City, and the planted species trees includes Platycladus orientalis (Cypress), Larix gmelinii (Pinaster), Robinia pseudoacacia (Robinia), Ulmus pumila (Elm), Picea asperata (Spruce). 
The implementation of the project would generate GHG emission removals and mitigate climate change; improve soil and water conservation and forest cover; enhance local biodiversity by increasing the connectivity of forests; bring job opportunities and increase income for local communities and residents by providing their relevant technical skills and training.

The aim of the project is to increase carbon sequestration and contribute to local sustainable development by planting trees on the barren mountains. developer: Guangdong Xinsheng Environmental Protection Technology Co., Ltd.
description:
Guangdong Xinsheng E-waste recovery and recycling project (hereafter referred to as the project) was expanded to match the larger lead recycling capacity to handle the increasing number of renewed and phased-out waste lead-containing waste and copper-containing waste from automobiles, electric bicycles, electric motorcycles, etc. in Guangdong East and Chaozhou City, Guangdong Province. The project is invested and owned by Guangdong Xinsheng Environmental Protection Technology Co., Ltd. The purpose of the project activity is to recycling instead of producing materials from virgin inputs reduces overall energy consumption, avoids direct GHG emissions, and reduces the environmental impact of natural resources extraction.
Given the current status of e-waste recycling in China, it can be assumed that in the absence of the project activity the e-waste would be either not recycled or, at best, certain fractions of it would be processed by informal recovery activities.
The proposed project was designed to reduce the Greenhouse Gas emissions by recovering metals and materials through Electronic Waste collection and recycling process performed at Guangdong Xinsheng Environmental Protection Technology Co., Ltd. located in Rao Ping County, Chaozhou City, China. It is planned that 200,000 tons of E-waste per year will be recycled into 40,815 tons of lead and 4822.5 tons of copper at maximum production capacity. The final product obtained will be sold to local businesses. The construction start date of the project is 01/08/2020 and was put into operation on 01/09/2021.
The project activity will reduce GHG in the atmosphere through a avoiding extraction of raw materials and production of virgin materials.  It is estimated that the project will result a total of 416,185 tCO2e emission reductions in the first crediting period of 7 years and with annual average of 59,455 tCO2e emission reduction in the 1st crediting period.

description:

The project involves 60,360 ha corn field and 82,341 ha soybean field.
The project is expected to reduce GHG emissions by no tillage and applying organic fertilizer, since no-tillage can reduce soil disturbance and reduce the loss of soil organic carbon (SOC) compared to conventional tillage. And applying organic fertilizer can reduce nitrous oxide emission compared to synthetic fertilizer. Moreover, the project is expected to increase SOC by straw returning, since straw contains a large amount of organic matter and trace elements such as nitrogen, phosphorus, and potassium, returning straw to the field can effectively increase soil organic matter (SOM). Straw returning to the field also can improve soil physical and chemical properties, enhance soil aggregate structure, and increase soil permeability.

name: VCS PROJECT FOR FARMERS ADOPTING ALTERNATE WETTING AND DRYING (AWD) METHOD FOR RICE CULTIVATION IN MADHYA  PRADESH
project_type: Agriculture Forestry and Other Land Use
description:
Rice is the country's most significant agricultural product; it is grown on 43.86 million hectares in India and contributes to more than 20% of world rice output (158.2 Tg in 2013).
Rice is farmed in practically every state in India, and its production is directly related to the country's food security. Additionally, it is a significant source of income and employment. Rice production, on the other hand, is a substantial source of critical and long-lasting GHGs such as CH 4 and N 2 O, posing a huge threat to sustainable agriculture. Rice fields provide approximately 30% and 11% of total agricultural CH 4 and N 2 O emissions, respectively. According to early US-EPA study, paddy in India produced around 37.8 Tg CH 4 per year. GHG emissions from rice fields may be minimized by changing irrigation patterns, managing organic additions, and utilizing the appropriate rate and amount of nitrogen fertilizer. Irrigation practices such as alternate wetting and drying (AWD) have been shown to lower GHG emissions when compared to typical flooding methods. The time intervals between dry and wet circumstances aid in the shift from aerobic to anaerobic soil conditions,
resulting in a considerable reduction in methane output. As a result, the project adopts the AWD approach to minimize CH 4 emissions. This will also result in a reduction in water use, lowering the farmer's input costs. Prior to the execution of the project activity, the farmers used the traditional flooding approach, which resulted in methane emissions into the atmosphere. The project proponent along with local implementation partner held training sessions and meetings with farmers to educate them on the benefits of using AWD, which was followed by the distribution and installation of AWD pipe in the fields of registered farmers. Location: The first instance of the project is located in Madhya Pradesh (Hoshangabad, Raisen, Sehore and Bhopal districts). The annual average emissions is 53,369 tCO 2 eq.

description:

The project is implemented by Guangzhou Huantou Environment Service Co.,Ltd (hereafter referred to as the project owner).
The purpose of the project is to utilize landfill gas (LFG), which consists mainly of methane, for LNG production for sale and electricity generation for self use. It includes LFG collection system, LFG pre-treatment system, and, liquefaction, by-product recovery, storing, loading, electricity generation, flare system, etc. LFG collected will be used for LNG production for sale and electricity generation with internal combustion generators for self use. The project started to construct on21/Feb/2020 and operated on 04/Aug/2021.The landfill gas treatment capacity of the project is 300,000 m3 per day(200,000 m3for LNG production and 100,000 m3for electricity generation). Greenhouse gas (GHG) emissions will be reduced by avoiding GHG emissions from releasing LFG into atmosphere at the landfill site. Meanwhile supplying liquefied LFG to consumers using trucks reduce GHG emissions from the use of natural gas. The expected average annual emission reductions are 392,583 tCO2e during the fixed 10 years crediting period.

name: D.Light's Improved Cooking Project In Africa
description: The “D.LIGHT’S IMPROVED COOKING PROJECT IN AFRICA” is a Grouped project that aims dissemination of energy-efficient improved cookstoves (ICS) to replace existing traditional Cookstoves in domestic households and communities throughout Kenya, Nigeria, Tanzania, and Uganda. The ICS results in the reduction of fuel consumption and improvement in levels of Indoor air pollution for project users (reducing smoke, black soot, and particulate matter (PM) emissions). name: La Yesca Landfill Gas Project
project_type: Energy industries (renewable/non-renewable sources); Waste handling and disposal
description:
The proposed project activity has the objective to capture and to flare/combustion the landfill gas produced in the landfill called, “RELLENO SANITARIO COLIHUES LA YESCA” located in the Rancagua Municipality, Chile. 
The project activity will result in greenhouse gas (GHG) emission reduction from the RSSP through: 1-Burning CH4 in flares and/or group generators; and 2- generating electricity that will be part used for self-consumption at the landfill facilities and the surplus part will be exported to the Chilean national grid, avoiding the dispatch of an equal amount of energy produced by fossil-fuelled thermal plants to that grid. The initiative avoids CO2 emissions and contributes to the regional and national sustainable development.

The project was the refurbishment to an efficient capture, collection and flaring system to burn CH4 (a greenhouse gas). These actions will reduce odors and adverse environmental impacts.
Also, the project will install group-generators that will combust the LFG to produce electricity, using part for self-consumption and the surplus part will be exported to the grid. The flares will be kept in operation due to LFG excess or other operational considerations. The LFG power plant will be expected to install up to 4.5 MW upon project completion. However, the final equipment that will be chosen (as well as the final installed capacity) may vary depending on the availability of the generator equipment in the market at the time of actual implementation of the second phase.

The landfill began its operation on July 1997, receiving of household waste. The landfill area is 21.79 hectares.
For this crediting period, estimates of GHG emission reductions are:

•	Annual average GHG emission reduction: 166,554 tCO2e
•	Total estimated GHG emission reductions: 1,165,880 tCO2e

name: MITIGATING CLIMATE CHANGE AND ENHANCING RURAL LIVELIHOODS THROUGH PLANTATIONS RAISED TO PROVIDE RAW MATERIAL TO THE PAPER INDUSTRY
project_type: Agriculture Forestry and Other Land Use
description:
The proposed project activity under VCS will mobilize resource-poor farmers to raise tree plantations on vacant farmlands. It proposes to link resource poor farmers and end users of wood products in order to optimize the land use and to facilitate the co-ordination of wood producers, agronomists, industry, social enterprises and non-governmental organizations to improve the livelihood opportunities of rural households. The project activity is implemented on the degraded farmlands or lands used for rainfed subsistence agriculture. 
Various environment friendly technology-based agroforestry practices and Natural Climate Solutions (NCS) will be adopted to help climate change adaptation and mitigation as part of sustainable land management.

This project will optimise the land use and generate Emission Reductions (ERs). The amount of carbon sequestered through the project activity will be measured and  quantified with reference to a baseline to determine the Emission Reductions (ERs) generated. The ERs will be calculated through quantifying  Above Ground Biomass, Below Ground Biomass and Soil Organic Carbon. In the absence of the project, the lands would have remained degraded and the resource poor farmers would have continued to practice subsistence agriculture. 

The participation of small and marginal farmers as part of the VCS project makes this initiative unique in contributing to their land use choice, improvement of livelihood opportunities and in promoting their capacity to organize and implement climate change mitigation initiatives.

The project implements reforestation on 13,500 ha of degraded private lands in the states of Andhra Pradesh, Telangana and Orissa. The reforestation activities under the project were initiated after 1 April 2020. 

The project is estimated to generate 94,200 credits / year on average over a period of 20 years.

name: Shangqiu Weijie Agricultural Development Co., Ltd Manure Management System GHG Mitigation Project
developer: Sino-Carbon Carbon Sink Science and Technology Development(Shangqiu) Co., LTD
project_type: Livestock, enteric fermentation, and manure management
description:
Shangqiu Weijie Agricultural Development Co., Ltd Animal Manure Management System GHG Mitigation Project (hereinafter referred to as the Project) introduce animal waste management system (AWMS) to swine farms in Hanying Village, Hedi Township, Sui County, Shangqiu city, Henan Province, China, which are owned by Shangqiu Weijie Agricultural Development Co., Ltd (hereinafter called” Weijie”). The purpose of the project activity is to treat the manure and wastewater from the swine farm to avoid methane emissions generated in the baseline uncovered anaerobic lagoons. In this project, a closed anaerobic lagoon was constructed to replace the traditional open anaerobic lagoon, for this project, animal waste management system (AWMS) refers to this closed anaerobic lagoon. The manure and waste will be collected in the anaerobic lagoons and the biogas produced during the anaerobic treatment will be collected, which is expected to produce 435 *10^4 m^3 of biogas per year. The biogas will then be used in the pig farm's electricity and heat generation system, and the electricity and heat generated will be used in the daily production and staff life of the pig farm. All the electricity and heat generated a reused by the pig farm, while the rest (if any) will be burned. The sludge produced after fermentation is applied to the corn fields as fertilizer, while the wastewater from the anaerobic
digester is used for agricultural irrigation.
Benefited from the “waste biogas fertilizer” pattern, harmlessness and ecological utilization of the swine manure can be realized. All the heat generated by the project will be used by the AWMSs and the swine farm. The heat generated will not be connected to other users or the regional heating supply system, and the baseline emissions associated with heat generation will not be claimed.

name: Jiangxi Zhenghe Livestock Manure Treatment Project
developer: Jiangxi Zhenghe Ecological Agriculture Co., Ltd.
project_type: Energy industries (renewable/non-renewable sources); Waste handling and disposal
description:
Jiangxi Zhenghe Livestock Manure Treatment Project (hereafter referred to as the project) is located in Jiangxi, China, which is operated by Jiangxi Zhenghe Ecological Agriculture Co., Ltd. The proposed project is an animal manure management system, which utilize livestock wastes from nearby farms, to produce biogas and organic fertilizer through an anaerobic digestion process. 
The raw material (i.e. livestock waste) from neighboring farms was collected and transported to each biogas plant by the principle of proximity. Continuously stirred tank reactor (CSTR) type anaerobic digesters are used to capture methane-rich biogas. Biogas is then utilized in cogeneration units for heat and electricity generation. The thermal energy is utilized only for heating anaerobic fermenters. The generated electricity is both used for internal electricity requirements and supplied to the Central China Power Grid (CCPG). The slurry produced by anaerobic fermentation is transported through pipe networks and utilized in nearby farmland to create an ecological recycling industry. The residue waste is used to produce solid organic fertilizer.
Before the implementation of the project, manure from livestock farms was treated by uncovered anaerobic lagoons without biogas recovery, and CCPG provided the same amount of electricity. This is also the baseline scenario for the project. The successful implementation of the project not only reduces greenhouse gas (GHG) emissions but also develops clean biomass energy. The project utilizes waste resources and achieves sustainable development of the agriculture industry.
The project activity will reduce GHG in the atmosphere through avoiding methane emissions from anaerobic treatment of manure. It is estimated to deliver totally   640,129  tCO2e emission reduction during the 7 years’ crediting period, at an average amount of  4,480,903  tCO2e per year.

name: CLIMATE SUSTAINABILITY THROUGH HORTICULTURE PROJECT IN INDIA
project_type: Agriculture Forestry and Other Land Use
description:
This is an Afforestation/Reforestation Project on degraded and fallow land and lies within the boundaries of India. The purpose of this grouped project is to promote the restoration of degraded and fallow land and improve the living conditions of farmers by planting horticulture and commercial species (indigenous species preferred). This is a grouped project.

The first project activity instance under the program is located in the state of Maharashtra, district Nandurbar in India. TATA Communications Limited (TCL) has implemented the VPA01 from 01-April-2022 with the coordination of implementing entity Collectives for Integrated Livelihood Initiatives (CINI). The area covered in this VPA is up to 303 hectare with an average land holding of approximately 0.40 hectare or one acre per farmer.
The villages under the project area predominantly have an agrarian economy. The conditions of lands covered under the project are either barren & fallow land with seasonal crops grown. The plantation under the project activity will lead to the sequestration of CO2 at a faster pace. 

The technology used for the tree plantation is simple as it just involves procurement of saplings from designated nurseries and planting various empty and barren locations of the districts. The first VPA is estimated to sequester average 5,645 tCO2e annually over 20 years.

name: Smart Cookstove Program by Tata Communications
description:
Household air pollution is a global crisis and India is not unaffected by the problem. There is significant dependence on polluting traditional chullahs (fuelwood stoves) for cooking in rural and semi-urban households in the country. Household pollution can cause diseases and women are particularly affected due to their direct exposure to cooking fires and involvement in daily cooking. Combustion of the non-renewable fuels and release of greenhouse gas emissions in the environment adds to global warming problem. 
The proposed project will be addressing this problem by providing access to improved cooking solutions (ICS) in the form of energy efficient cookstoves. This is a voluntary initiative by Tata Communications Limited (Project Proponent). PP will be collaborating with local implementation partners to provide improved cooking solutions for marginalized households living in rural and semi-urban areas in India. 

The baseline scenario is the continued use of non-renewable fuelwood by the target population in absence of project activity. 

Under the grouped project, three project activity instances are being implemented in the states of Meghalaya, Odisha and Jharkhand. Over a period a total of 20,000 ICS shall be deployed.

name: ENHANCING LIVELIHOOD OF TRIBAL COMMUNITIES THROUGH AGROFORESTRY IN SOUTH INDIA
project_type: Agriculture Forestry and Other Land Use
description:
Adoption of agroforestry approach is a viable alternative solution for the local communities in India to increase the fertility of their land and create livelihood opportunities to overcome extreme poverty. It is a system that can provide both food and income sources while preserving and rehabilitating the ecosystem. The proposed ARR VCS project aims to support tribal communities of ASR district in Andhra Pradesh, India. For the first project instance, approximately 12,500 hectares of area under agroforestry has been considered. The different species included in the proposed ARR project activity includes mango, silver oak, teak, jackfruit, cashew, and several other local tree species. The project area is located in 22 Mandals of ASR district in Andhra Pradesh state. The project aims to improve the livelihood of small and marginalized tribal communities in the  Alluri Sitarama Raju (ASR) district in the state of Andhra Pradesh by generating additional income via carbon credits. The project plans to generate carbon credits for the voluntary market under the VCS standard. 
The project is expected to sequester 140,864 tCO2 annually. The Project Proponent along with the implementation partner organized workshops in the forest  dwelling community areas and advised the community members to grow native trees with commercial importance in a sustainable manner to earn carbon revenue.

name: IMPROVED COOKSTOVES DISTRIBUTION IN MOZAMBIQUE – SOFALA AND MANICA PROVINCES
description:
The project activity involves the distribution of improved cookstoves (ICSs) among local communities based in some areas of Mozambique (Country), where currently several households still rely on inefficient and pollutant traditional cooking techniques.
The project aims to replace the traditional cooking mechanisms used by local people (three-stone fire or rudimental stoves) with ICSs that require less fuel and decrease the biomass combustion’s emissions, with a consequent reduction of health hazard coming from the indoor smoke pollution. The introduction of more efficient stoves will help to limit the demand for woody biomass, reducing the unsustainable use of forests and halting deforestation that is progressing rapidly in the Country. The improved cookstoves’ deployment will also have a positive impact on women’ life, reducing the time they spend for collecting woody biomass and cooking the meals, giving them the possibility to invest their time in a more effective way.
Through the implementation of engagement and training processes dedicated to the local communities involved in the project, all the households receiving the ICS will be aware of the environmental improvements and the carbon finance benefit generated by their effective use of the stove.
This project will be developed in the Republic of Mozambique. The areas of implementation will be the Central portion of the Country, considering in particular the provinces of Sofala and Manica.
The average annual GHG emission reduction expected with the implementation of the improved cookstove distribution project in the Country is around 120,000 tCO2e per year.

name: IMPROVING LIVELIHOOD OF FARMERS  VIA CARBON FINANCE PROJECT IN  NEPAL
project_type: Agriculture Forestry and Other Land Use
description:
The project area is in Nepal which is a home to a plethora of flora and fauna which spread across Terai to the middle to mountain of the country. Around 5962.03 (000 ha) of land was under forest cover in 2020. Forest Act 1993 recognizes two essential kinds (national and private) and five auxiliary kinds of forest beneath national forest (Government Managed, Community Managed, Protected Forests, Leasehold Forest, Religious Forest, and Private Forest). Deforestation, degradation and fragmentation of natural habitat of wildlife are a serious threat to forests of the country which alarm the need for protection of biodiversity. Adopting agroforestry practices is the best possible solution as this system can avail basic needs of an individual and rehabilitate the lost ecosystem. The primary objectives of agroforestry are to produce food, fodder, fuel-wood, and/or timber. There can also be co-benefits such as carbon sequestration, water quality enhancement, soil protection, and biodiversity conservation. 
Agroforestry system in Nepal is a traditional and ancient practice. Farmers in the hills have expanded the number of agroforestry trees on their farmland in response to forest degradation and deforestation, to meet their immediate demand for fodder, fuelwood, and small-sized timber products. The agroforestry systems deliver several forest products, agriculture products and ecosystem services which may enhance social well-being of the local farmers, national and global community. The small and marginal farmers are almost unaware of the scientific importance (economic and environmental aspects) of agroforestry, short- and long-term benefits, and technical requirements. There awareness efforts to educate farmers on the benefits of agroforestry practice in their farmlands.

name: Cauaxi REDD+ Grouped Project
project_type: Agriculture Forestry and Other Land Use
description:
The Cauaxi REDD+ Grouped Project (hereafter called GPD) aims to conserve forests in several private properties located in northeast portion of Pará, close to the border with Maranhão. The Cauaxi River, which gives the project its name, is one of the tributaries of the Capim River, located in the central portion of the project's reference region, at Paragominas municipality.
The GPD aims to create positive economic incentives for landowners to conserve rainforests in private areas that are vulnerable to degradation and deforestation, while contributing to net positive climate impacts as well as benefit to traditional communities and conserve biodiversity. By joining BRcarbon (hereafter known as BRC), forest owners can access funds from the carbon voluntary market to develop conservation and monitoring efforts in their forests. A partnership between BRC and landowners will result in the legal protection of forests, forest monitoring using satellite images, biodiversity inventory (including fauna e flora species), and forest biomass inventory in a broad scale, using 
a upscaling approach based on field collection, drone-borne and satellite sensors such as LiDAR (light detection and ranging). In addition, we will involve surveillance of property, wildfire monitoring, fire prevention and fighting, threatened species protection and social activities with traditional communities. 
As a result, BRC expects to enhance the climate impact of carbon projects, helping communities and biodiversity. The Cauaxi REDD+ Grouped Project is part of the company's initiative to promote forest conservation using the financial flows of the carbon market. This project is related to climate-positive impacts caused by the reduction of emissions 
caused by deforestation and avoided degradation (REDD+).

name: EVI BAMBOO AFFORESTATION PROJECT IN INDIA
project_type: Agriculture Forestry and Other Land Use
description:
The project activity focuses on the development of Bamboo as a key resource for catalyzing an inclusive green economy. In this project, different types of bamboo species will be planted to restore degraded lands. It will help the local communities and farmers generate income by involving them in different livelihood activities like making of bamboo handicraft and furniture. In addition, it will help to sequesters atmospheric carbon dioxide, which aids in climate change mitigation, as well as improving soil in the project area through conservation practices. 

The project activity will be implemented across states of India. This is a grouped project.

First project activity instance:
The Konkan Bamboo & Cane Development Centre (KONBAC) is a not-for-profit company, facilitated by the International Network for Bamboo and Rattan (INBAR) through the Centre for Indian Bamboo Resource and Technology (CIBART). 

The KONBAC organization planted bamboo species with the collaboration of local farmers in 24 districts (Ahmednagar, Akola, Amravati, Aurangabad, Beed, Bhandara, Buldhana, Chandrapur, Dhule, Jalna, Kolhapur,	Latur, Nagpur, Nanded, Nandurbar, Nashik, Palghar, Parbhani, Pune, Sangli, Satara, Solapur, Thane & Wardha) of Maharashtra, India. The area covered in the project is about 595.5 hectare.

The techniques used for the plantation are vegetative propagation, rhizome & the seedlings. This seedling are sourced from the various designated nurseries and planting from various empty and barren locations in the project.  KONBAC provides hands-on training to farmers in the scientific processes of propagation, cultivation and harvesting.

The first VPA is estimated to sequester average 26,292 tCO2e annually.

name: Agropalma REDD+ Project
project_type: Agriculture Forestry and Other Land Use
description: The Agropalma REDD+ Project is a partnership between Biofílica Ambipar Environment and Agropalma Group and its purpose is to promote forest conservation, maintenance of carbon stocks and mitigation of climate change through the reduction of Greenhouse Gas (GHG) emissions from land use change. In addition to the climate benefits, the Project also intends to generate social benefits based on sustainable economic development practices and improved well-being of the surrounding communities, as well as environmental benefits through actions aimed at the conservation of local flora and fauna. The Project area covers 50,519 hectares of Amazon forest and is located almost entirely in the northeastern mesoregion of Pará State, including the municipalities of Tailândia, Moju, Tomé Açu and Acará. The region has great relevance in relation to its biodiversity, since it is located in the Belém Center of Endemism (CEB), a place with a large concentration of rare and endemic species. The predominant vegetation is Dense Ombrophylous Forest with a high density of medium and large trees, besides woody lianas and epiphytes.

name: Agroforestry Plantation of ITC Limited In Selected Regions of North India
project_type: Agriculture Forestry and Other Land Use
description: The proposed ARR VCS project intends to promote sustainable agroforestry for small-scale traditional farmers to provide them with financial benefits and ensure GHG mitigation in the states of Punjab, Uttar Pradesh, Haryana and Uttarakhand, India. This project will help in increasing tree outside forest (TOF) that will add in mitigating climate change. The project shall also enhance the income of farmer communities along with biodiversity conservation and improvement of soil health.

name: Improved Agricultural Practices for Rice Cultivation in India
project_type: Agriculture Forestry and Other Land Use
description: This project aims to reduce the CH4 emissions through improved water management practices involving alternate wetting and drying (AWD) of the paddy lands instead of the traditional continuous flooding method. Along with reduced water usage by implementing AWD, the project also aims to improve soil health without any yield penalty.

name: 220MWDC MINBU SOLAR POWER  PLANT PROJECT
description:
220MWDC Minbu Solar Power Plant (hereafter simplified as “the project”) is a newly built grid-connected photovoltaic power plant with an installed capacity of 220MWp, which is located in Minbu
District, Magway Region, Myanmar. The project is divided into 4 phases with a capacity of 50WMp
for phases 1-3 and 70MWp for phase 4. Currently, phase 1 has been operated since 27 September
2019 while phase 2 is under construction with an expected COD in 2024. Phase 3 and
4 are expected to complete 1 and 2 years respectively from phase 2 COD’s date (2025-2026).
The project is ultimately owned by Green Earth Power (Thailand) Co. Ltd which the company hires
GEP (Myanmar) Co. Ltd (its subsidiary)The project is to develop and operate. by Green Earth
Power (Myanmar) Co. Ltd (it's subsidiary).
The existing scenario prior to the implementation of the project is the electricity being generated
by the Ministry of Electricity and Energy, Electric Power Generation Enterprise (EPGE), and the
baseline scenario of the project is the same as the existing scenario
The purpose of the project is to generate electricity by using renewable solar energy, and the
electricity generated by the project will be delivered to EPGE for 30 years period ending on 26
February 2049 to replace equivalent electricity generated by fossil fuel-fired power plants
connected to the EPGE.

name: GUAMÁ LANDFILL GAS PROJECT
project_type: Energy industries (renewable/non-renewable sources); Waste handling and disposal
description: The proposed VCS project activity titled “Guamá landfill Gas Project” encompasses the promotion of collection and destruction/utilization of landfill gas (LFG) (rich in methane) at the CPTR Guamá landfill through collection LFG and its destruction in high temperature enclosed flare and utilization as gaseous fuel in set of engine-generator sets of an electricity generation infrastructure (with final total combined nameplate installed capacity of about 2 MW).

name: CSG EV Charger Premier Aggregation
description: The Electric Vehicle Charger Premier Aggregation Project (Project) project is proposed for registration under the Verra Verified Carbon Standard (VCS) VCS Standard, Version 4.2, 20 January 2022 (Standard) and associated Program Guide, Version 4.1, 20 January 2022 (Guide). The Project is an Aggregate Project, consisting of multiple Project Activity Instances (Instances), and is proposed to be submitted following VCS Methodology VM0038, Methodology for Electric Vehicle Charging Systems, Version 1.0, 18 September 2018 (Methodology). The Project will generate GHG emission reductions through the displacement of fossil fuel powered vehicles across the included fleet categories as detailed below) with grid-connected electricity. The existing scenario prior to Project implementation (Baseline Scenario) is the operation of comparable fleets (as defined in the Methodology) that would have been used to provide the same transportation service in the absence of the project. Namely, the comparable fleets in the baseline comprise fossil fuel driven vehicles. As such, the energy generated by direct combustion of fossil fuels and release of emissions at the tailpipe of vehicles in the Baseline Scenario is equivalently displaced by less fossil-fuel intensive grid-connected electricity in the Project Scenario.

name: Strengthening rural livelihoods of smallholder farmers in tribal districts of Odisha,India
project_type: Agriculture Forestry and Other Land Use
description: The fragile ecosystem of the upland tribal regions in Keojhar and Mayurbhanj districts of Odisha have been affected by deforestation and rampant shifting cultivation practices causing extensive soil erosion, reducing the capacity of land to rejuvenate and affecting natural vegetation and water resources.In order to address some of the issues of the communities it becomes pertinent to adopt interventions based on improved land use planning, soil-moisture conservation measures and improved farming based agroforestry practices. This will not only strengthen the agrarian livelihoods of the tribal households, but also increase their food and nutritional security.The proposed project in the two districts of Keonjhar and Mayurbhanj is aimed at improving the livelihoods of the tribal communities by restoring 4000 hectares of barren uplands through plantation of forest and fruit tree species mostly in private lands. Additional components include land development, soil-moisture conservation, crop diversification and intercropping and promoting organic farm and pest management practices. The project will be implemented in 4000 hectares covering 3 blocks of Keonjhar district (Harichandanpur, Jhumpura and Champua) and 2 blocks of Mayurbhanj district (Udala and Khunta). The project aims for economic upliftment of the small holder famers through improved land use planning, increase in production and productivity, social empowerment of women along with enhancement of the carbon sequestration potential through such interventions.

name: Angola Caraculo PV Plant
description:
The proposed project activity aims to generate renewable electricity through a 25MWp photovoltaic power plant located in Caraculo, Nambibe province, in Angola Southern Region, which currently relies mainly on diesel thermal plants for electricity production. The project is implemented by Solenova, a company jointly owned by Sonangol and Eni Angola.
This project activity represents the first phase of a larger photovoltaic project having a total capacity of up to 50 MWp. The overall project is implemented in following phases as requested by the Rede Nacional de Transporte (“RNT”) as the sole offtaker, taking into consideration the current load and the need to ensure the full dispatchability of the energy produced.
The area identified for the project is located 2 km west from Caraculo village (Namibe Province), adjacent to the EN 280 road and the South Transmission Grid. The area covers about 165 ha and was proposed for this initiative by the Province Authorities.
The scope of Caraculo project is to ensure a reliable production of electrical renewable power to be dispatched into the Southern Transmission Grid of the Country, which currently relies mainly
on diesel thermal plants for its supply. The expected annual average energy production over the 24 years project technical lif etime is up to 59 GWh/year. The scope of works also includes the construction of a MV/HV substation inside the project area.
The project first phase implementation (25 MWp) will permit a diesel consumption reduction of about 18.000 m3/year. The average annual GHG emission reduction expected with the implementation
of the project activity is around 50,000 tCO2e per year.

name: Sustainable Agriculture Project by Arvind in India
project_type: Agriculture Forestry and Other Land Use
description: The project activity promotes sustainable agriculture practices among cotton farmers in order to reduce the usage of synthetic fertilizer and biomass burning. The project activity aims to reduce greenhouse gas (GHG) emissions from the agricultural fields which mainly source from the stubble burning, excess use of fertilizer and as a result excess water requirement for irrigation etc

name: AgreenaCarbon Project
project_type: Agriculture Forestry and Other Land Use
description: The AgreenaCarbon Project aims to reduce agricultural GHG emissions through the implementation of activities that are central principles of regenerative agriculture. The Project intends to help farmers transition to regenerative agriculture by applying sustainable agricultural land management practices (ALM) in order to maintain yields while ensuring long-term viability of their farms and land. Regenerative agriculture describes holistic farming practices that improve the soil fertility and enhance the storage of soil organic carbon (SOC) and ‘focuses on the regeneration of living soil, improved micro hydrology, and conserving biodiversity at all levels while enhancing inputs use-efficiency and ecosystem system services.’  The AgreenaCarbon Project assists farmers in the transition from conventional, intensive farming practices to ones that avoid soil disturbances and increase the amount of organic soil amendments all while reducing the use of synthetic fertilisers. The focal point of these practices is reducing tillage to reduce soil disturbance with the addition of the other activities as a combined suite of activities that contribute to soil fertility. The Project facilitates the transition through a carbon payment programme which provides economic incentives to change existing agricultural practices, described as project activities. The programme is located across Europe and is based in temperate climates.

name: CO2 UTILIZATION IN CONCRETE - Removals & Reductions - CarbonCure - U.S & Canada. Project #1
description: This project activity will capture waste CO2 which would have otherwise been emitted into the atmosphere, or atmospheric CO2 which would otherwise be in the atmosphere, and utilize that gas as a feedstock in the production of concrete. These project activities reduce greenhouse gas (GHG) emissions by sequestering CO2 via the production of concrete. This manufacturing process has the additional benefit of requiring less Portland cement, which further reduces emissions, because the cement production process is highly energy and carbon intensive. The project activity will take place at the location where the concrete is first manufactured (mixed with cement, water, aggregates, etc.). At its peak, this project activity will result in approximately 542,500 metric tons of CO2 reduced over the crediting period, the average annual emission reductions being 67,813 tCO2eq.

name: CO2 UTILIZATION IN CONCRETE - REMOVALS & REDUCTIONS – CarbonCure – Asia #1
description: This project activity will capture waste CO2 which would have otherwise been emitted into the atmosphere, or atmospheric CO2 which would otherwise be in the atmosphere, and utilize that gas as a feedstock in the production of concrete. These project activities reduce greenhouse gas (GHG) emissions by sequestering CO2 via the production of concrete. This manufacturing process has the additional benefit of requiring less Portland cement, which further reduces emissions, because the cement production process is highly energy and carbon intensive. The project activity will take place at the location where the concrete is first manufactured (mixed with cement, water, aggregates, etc.). At its peak, this project activity will result in approximately 249,200 metric tons of CO2 reduced over the crediting period, the average annual emission reductions being 31,150 tCO2eq.

name: CO2 Utilization in Concrete – Removals & Reductions – CarbonCure – U.S & Canada Project #1
description: This project activity will capture waste CO2 which would have otherwise been emitted into the atmosphere, or atmospheric CO2 which would otherwise be in the atmosphere, and utilize that gas as a feedstock in the production of concrete. These project activities reduce greenhouse gas (GHG) emissions by sequestering CO2 via the production of concrete. This manufacturing process has the additional benefit of requiring less Portland cement, which further reduces emissions, because the cement production process is highly energy and carbon intensive. The project activity will take place at the location where the concrete is first manufactured (mixed with cement, water, aggregates, etc.). At its peak, this project activity will result in approximately 300,500 metric tons of CO2 reduced over the crediting period, the average annual emission reductions being 37,563 tCO2eq.

name: Amazon Biome Conservancy Grouped REDD+ Project
