project_type: Agriculture Forestry and Other Land Use
description: The Amazon Biome Conservancy Grouped REDD+ Project (hereinafter also referred to as “ABC”) has as its main objective to contribute to the preservation with the biggest tropical forest of the world in the Brazilian territory, while providing significant improvements in the social interface. The project for this validation process has only one project activity instance located in the Itacoatiara municipality, state of Amazonas near its capital of Manaus. According to the geo-referencing data, the total area of the project is established at 5,140 ha, which is composed of native Amazon Rainforest vegetation, without the existence of secondary vegetation since the land has not been cleared of native ecosystems within the last 10 years before the project start date. The project area consist of the ABC project is equivalent to the 20% of the landowner property area that he could legally suppress, according to the Brazilian forest code (Law 12.651, 2012). This project will be eligible under the Reducing Emissions from Deforestation and Forest Degradation (REDD) category, using the VM0007 methodology for Avoiding Planned Deforestation (APDD). The crediting period of the project is 30 years. The start date is on 19/11/2022 and the crediting period is expected to end on 18/11/2052. To execute the installation of this project and to achieve its objectives the VCU generation is very important. A reduction of 2,605,773.23 t CO2-e of GHG is expected over the next ten years for the first baseline developed and presented in this Project Description - PD (average of 260,577.32 t CO2-e per year).

name: Sinop Landfill Gas to Electricity Project
developer: Biokütle Enerji Elektrik Üretim Anonim Şirketi
project_type: Energy industries (renewable/non-renewable sources); Waste handling and disposal
description: Sinop Landfill Gas to Electricity Project is located at Sinop Landfill Site in Hacioglu Neighborhood, Central District, Sinop Province Turkey. The project is owned by Biokütle Enerji Elektrik Üretim A.Ş. The facility started operation on 29/06/2021 and the feed-in electricity is estimated to be 21,210 MWh / year  at full capacity during the 7-year crediting period. The project is expected to reduce 30,789 tCO2e/y annually in the first 7-year crediting period between commission date of 29/06/2022 and ending date of 28/06/2028.

name: Sanergy Composting Group Project
description:
The Sanergy Composting Group Project is located in Kenya and produces compost and compressed fuel briquettes from various organic and biomass waste sources. These waste sources include food waste, wood dust, sugarcane bagasse, slaughterhouse waste and human sanitation waste. The processes also entail a pre-treatment step with the use of black soldier fly (BSF) insect larvae, which valorize some of the organics in an aerobic process and leave behind a residue which is called frass. The frass is then mixed with other types of organic waste aerobically composted into organic fertilizer for local farmers. Furthermore, the frass can be mixed and compressed into biomass briquettes which are in part used on site, and the residual briquettes are sold to local industry as a renewable fuel for industrial boilers generating heat and steam. 

The first project activity instance is located in Nairobi, Kenya. Sanergy Limited is the owner of the facility located in Nairobi and is the Project Developer for the Sanergy Composting Group Project. Circular Impact is the project proponent.

name: Installation of Solar Water Pump
description:
Agriculture is the mainstay of rural economy in the Indian state of Chhattisgarh and is the single largest employment generator. Of the total population of 25.5 million, 70% of the population is engaged in Agriculture of which 80% belonging to small & marginal category (around 3.746 million farm families) 1 with limited investment capacity. Poor irrigation
coverage, inability of the small farm holders to opt for irrigation has in turn forced small and margi nal farm holders towards subsistence and monocropping practice thereby narrowing farm sector income, declining interest in farming and farm investment, and triggering concerns over food security.

name: Qinghai Taiheyuan Swine Farm Manure Management System GHG Mitigation Project
developer: Qinghai Taiheyuan Agriculture Technology Co., Ltd
project_type: Livestock, enteric fermentation, and manure management; Waste handling and disposal
description:
Qinghai Taiheyuan Swine Farm Manure Management System GHG Mitigation Project introduce animal waste management system (AWMS) to the two swine farms in Huzhu County, Haidong City, Qinghai Province, China, which are owned by Qinghai Taiheyuan Agriculture Technology Co., Ltd. The project activity aims to treat the manure and wastewater from the 2 swine farms to avoid methane emissions generated in the baseline uncovered anaerobic lagoons.
 All the manure and wastewater are collected and then be separated first. The solid will be treated in aerobic composting system and the organic fertilizers will be produced, part of the fertilizer produced in this process will be distributed to local farmers for free and the others will be sold in domestic market. The liquid will be treated through anaerobic digestion and the biogas generated during the treatment process will be captured and sent to boilers for heat generation and Surplus biogas will be destroyed through the flaring system (if any). The sludge produced from anaerobic digestion will be treated through aerobic composting together with the solid, the effluent will be supplied to the farmers living around free for agriculture irrigation.
Benefiting from the “waste-biogas-fertilizer” pattern, harmlessness and ecological utilization of the swine manure can be realized. All the heat generated by the project will be used by the AWMS and the swine farm. The heat generated will not be connected to other users or the regional heating supply system and the baseline emissions associated with heat generation will not be claimed.
The project activity will reduce of GHG in the atmosphere through avoiding methane emissions from anaerobic treatment of swine manure and wastewater. It is estimated that
93,501 tCO2e emission reductions will be generated annually and total emissionreductions are 654,507 tCO2e in the first crediting period.

name: 8 MW NongKhai Waste to Energy Project in Thailand
description: The project activity involves installation of a 8 MW installed capacity of WTE power project in Phon Sawang Sub-District, Mueang Nong Khai District, Nong Khai province, Thailand. The electricity generated from the projects supplied to grid and thereby avoids CO2 emission associated with grid-based electricity generation.  The project also avoids methane emissions from waste management as the project avoids the organic waste going to landfill which would result in methane emission in the baseline senario.

name: Macaúba as a Productive Second Floor
project_type: Agriculture Forestry and Other Land Use
description:
The “Macaúba as a Productive Second Floor” is a VCS AFOLU (Agriculture, Forestry and Other Land Use) grouped project, Scope 14, and, specifically, it falls under the ARR (Afforestation, Reforestation and Revegetation) category. 
The project works with local farmers to implement integrated systems in previously degraded pastures and/or croplands. The main project activity consists of the planting of Macaúba trees. This will be done considering two possible arrangements: (i) Macaúba intercropped with pasture (silvipastoral) or (ii) macuaba intercropped with agriculture (agrisilvicultural).
Through the planting of Macaúba trees the project will contribute to an increase in carbon stocks and associated GHG removals. The project activity will also improve the livelihood of local farmers and provide other ecosystem services, such as: maintaining the local microclimate, preventing erosion, conserving soil and moisture.

name: Terraligna Afforestation Over Degraded Grasslands
project_type: Agriculture Forestry and Other Land Use
description: The project activity “Terraligna Afforestation over degraded grasslands” is an afforestation project over extensive cattle grazing pastures areas using exotic species (mostly Eucalyptus dunnii) aiming to produce biomass for energy and/or pulp. The Terraligna project eligible for the VCS standard is circumscribed to 4,282 ha effectively planted after the trust fund operation starting date, carried out in 8 properties (7 entire plots and 90% of the effectively planted area of the 8th). The area corresponding to the other 19 of the trust fund properties (5,896 ha) will not be presented as part of the project as it does not meet the requirements of the VCS Standard boundaries. The project activity is carried out on degraded land as a consequence of many decades of intensive cattle grazing. This degradation is expected to continue in the absence of the project. The project utilizes 2 species: mostly Eucalyptus dunnii and Eucalyptus smithii in a lesser extent, 95.9% and 4.1% of the planted area, respectively. The project sequesters CO2 through forest plantation in grassland areas, generating net anthropogenic removals by sinks. The long-term average GHG benefit (LTA) is determined by averaging the expected total GHG benefit for the length of the project (100 years: from 21/12/2019 – until 21/12/2119). The total GHG benefit for the length of the project is 1,112,972 tCO2e, when divided by 100 years results in 11,130 tCO2e.

name: The Native Ecosystem Restoration in Nicaragua Project
project_type: Agriculture Forestry and Other Land Use
description: The objective of the Native Ecosystem Restoration in Nicaragua Project is to reforest an area of around 20,000 hectares, starting with the acquisition of 6,000 hectares of unused or under-used, degraded land in Nicaragua currently managed as abandoned or cattle pasture grazed at very low densities, and restore this ecosystem with native trees in order to sequester carbon dioxide. The degraded land will thus be rehabilitated with native tree cover, and over time biodiversity and local hydrology will be restored. The grouped Project will control erosion, regenerate soil health, and increase water infiltration, consequently improving ground water levels in the area, as well as provide local employment opportunities. Most land being considered is in the Central and Pacific regions of Nicaragua, but all regions of the country with degraded cattle pasture are eligible.

name: Bundled Solar Power Project by AMP Energy - 01
description: The project involves the installation of bundled Solar Photovoltaic (SPV) power plant with a cumulative capacity of 9.51 MW primarily to meet the captive demand of the premises owners and export of surplus power to the grid through the mechanism of net metering. All the solar panel units involved in the project are implemented under the DBFOT model, i.e., Design, Build, Finance, Operate, and Transfer. The premises owners are the customers of the power generated from the solar panels which purchase the power under long-term power purchase agreements signed for 25 years. Before installation of the rooftop solar units, the Kochi Metro premises, Subros Ltd., SECI rooftop premises owners used to meet the electricity demand from the national grid of India. The project thus replaces fossil fuel-dominated grid electricity thereby reducing the equivalent amount of GHG emission.

name: Avcıkoru Landfill Gas to Electricity Project
developer: KORFEZ ENERJI SAN. VE TIC. A.S.
project_type: Energy industries (renewable/non-renewable sources); Waste handling and disposal
description: The project activity is a Landfill Gas Power Generating Plant. Electricity production will be done by burning the landfill gas. Landfill gas will be burned in gas engines and electrical energy will be obtained from the ends of the generator coupled to gas engines. Electrical energy to be taken from the ends of the generator will be increased to medium voltage level in transformers and given to the interconnected system. Whilst providing sustainable development benefits to the host communities and the host country, the project activity reduces greenhouse gas (GHG) emissions mainly by preventing GHG emissions, methane in particular, from being emitted directly to the atmosphere from waste at the solid waste disposal site that would be otherwise left to be decomposed; and by replacing the electricity that would have otherwise been generated by the national grid which is primarily dependent on fossil-fuel-based resources.

name: Agroforestry For Livelihoods Project
project_type: Agriculture Forestry and Other Land Use
description: The project aims to address widespread land and agro-ecosystem degradation and climate-change related hazards across the landscapes of Rulindo and Bugesera districts in northern and eastern provinces of Rwanda respectively. The project will undertake a number of activities including: 1) planting of around four million functional tree species on both smallholders’ farm plots and public suitable lands to restore degraded ecosystems, protect watersheds, sequester carbon, conserve biodiversity, and provide farmers with a diversified income streams, e.g., from fruits and timber; 2) establishing seedling nurseries to provide quality materials for tree planting 3) provide trainings to enhance knowledge to a wide range of key stakeholders, including farmer groups, the youth, community advisors, Community Extension Officers, nursery managers, project’s staff, etc. 4) promoting specific livelihoods activities, e.g., horticulture package, livestock husbandry, Village-based Savings & Loan Associations (VSLA), local investments, etc.; 5) facilitating market access for farmers products/produce by encouraging farmers to organize into cooperatives/ other community structures, and when possible, entering into supply agreements with off-takers; 6) engaging farmers in sustainability agreements - committing them to sustain the implementation of the project activities for the long-term, beyond the project’s crediting period (≥20 years). The project activities aim to address this land and agro-ecosystem degradation and directly contribute to climate mitigation through increased carbon storage in tree biomass and in soils within the agricultural landscapes. The new VERRA’s Verified Carbon Standard carbon methodology called Methodology for Afforestation, Reforestation, and Revegetation Projects will be used. The ex-ante annual average GHG emission reductions of the project are estimated at 70,470 tCO2e, and total GHG emission reductions over 20 years are estimated at 1,414,808 tCO2e.

name: Zambia Agroforestry Grouped Project
project_type: Agriculture Forestry and Other Land Use
description:
The project “Zambia Agroforestry Grouped Project” is comprised of the cashew plantation execution started as of January 2020 to 2021 for 5.5million of cashew nuts seedlings in the total of 72,000 hectares in ten districts (Mongu, Limulunga, Lukuku, Metete, Kalabo, Sikongo, Nalolo, Senanga, Sioma and Shangombo) in Western Province in Zambia. The project at the beginning initiated under the contract with CIDP in Western Province, in partnership with the Empowering Farmers Foundation, it is our intention to develop our project areas into a voluntary carbon project through the GHG emissions removals by such planting activities, which should in turn allow to perform regular gap filling, continue the plantations, thereby expanding the planted areas significantly.
We intend to perform a comprehensive environmental study, covering the feasibility of expanding the cashew plantations beyond the current project areas potentially to Eastern Province, in collaboration with ETG group companies and partners.
In the Eastern Province in Zambia, EFF had also executed 1 million (1.043.425) of cashew seedlings plantation in six districts namely: Nyimba, Petauke, Sinda, Chadiza, Mambwe, Lundazi.

name: DelAgua Clean Cooking Grouped Project in The Gambia
description: The Grouped Project activity “DelAgua Clean Cooking Grouped Project in The Gambia” aims at distribution of Improved Cooking Stoves (ICS) in the Least Developed Country The Gambia. The program is reducing the usage of firewood as fuel used for cooking at household level, thereby reducing the GHG emissions arising out of the burning of fossil fuels. This reduction in the firewood usage at the household level will be achieved by the usage of project ICS for cooking, as it has a higher thermal efficiency, therefore, consuming lesser amount of fuel and time in cooking a specific amount of meal.

name: Hubei Jinnonggu AWMS GHG Mitigation Project
developer: Hubei Jinnonggu Agriculture and Animal Husbandry Technology Co., Ltd
project_type: Energy industries (renewable/non-renewable sources); Livestock, enteric fermentation, and manure management; Waste handling and disposal
description:
Hubei Jinnonggu AWMS GHG Mitigation Project (hereinafter referred to as the Project) introduce animal waste management system (AWMS) to the two swine farms in Shilong Town, Jingshan City, Hubei Province, China, which are owned by Hubei Jinnonggu Agriculture and Animal Husbandry Technology Co., Ltd. The project activity aims to treat the manure and wastewater from the 2 swine farms to avoid methane emissions generated in the baseline uncovered anaerobic lagoons.
All the manure and wastewater are collected and then be separated first. The solid will be treated in aerobic composting system and the organic fertilizers will be produced, part of the fertilizer produced in this process will be distributed to local farmers for free and the others will be sold in domestic market. The liquid will be treated through anaerobic digestion and the biogas generated during the treatment process will be captured and sent to boilers for heat generation and Surplus biogas will be destroyed through the flaring system (if any). The sludge produced from anaerobic digestion will be treated through aerobic composting together with the solid, the effluent will be supplied to the farmers living around free for agriculture irrigation.
The common practice for the swine farm owners to manage the manure is to have uncovered anaerobic lagoons/ponds at their farms in the region. As per “technical specification for sanitation treatment of livestock and poultry manure[ https://oss.baigongbao.com/2020/12/14/MRyhTKQcWC.pdf]”, In China, the uncovered anaerobic lagoons are a manure treatment method recognized by the state. In addition, since there is no legal regulation to mandate the livestock farm owners to implement anaerobic digestion, aerobic or other biological treatment techniques and to capture and/or utilize methane generated at these lagoons, therefore the continue of this common practice to treatment the manure i.e., uncovered anaerobic lagoons is the most economic, viable and reasonable for livestock farm owners.
Benefiting from the “waste-biogas-fertilizer” pattern, harmlessness and ecological utilization of the swine manure can be realized. All the heat generated by the project will be used by the AWMS and the swine farm. The heat generated will not be connected to other users or the regional heating supply system and the baseline emissions associated with heat generation will not be claimed. 
The project activity will reduce of GHG in the atmosphere through avoiding methane emissions from anaerobic treatment of swine manure and wastewater. It is estimated that 65,470 tCO2e emission reductions will be generated annually and total emission reductions are 458,290 tCO2e in the first crediting period.

name: Family Forest Carbon Program - Central Appalachia
project_type: Agriculture Forestry and Other Land Use
description:
The Family Forest Carbon Program (FFCP), administered by the Family Forest Impact Foundation (FFIF), is an innovative, incentive-based program engaging private family and other non-industrial private forest landowners throughout the United States in improved forest management practices, promoting forest health, carbon sequestration and storage, and other environmental conservation and protection practices. 

Through its grouped project design, the FFCP is able to engage and achieve economies of scale with smaller non-industrial forestland owners, reaching ownerships that have been largely unrepresented in voluntary carbon markets. The FFCP solves challenges to small forest holdings participation in carbon projects, by reducing cost and complexity of participation. 

FFCP provides incentive payments to forest landowners to implement climate-smart practices that increase sequestration and storage of carbon. The FFCP further connects enrolled landowners with technical assistance from local consulting foresters, helping family landowners transition to long-term, sustainable forest management. 

The first project activities implemented in the FFCP program (directed towards the U.S. Central Appalachia region) include: Growing Mature Forests (GMF) –20-year, renewable agreement to limit timber harvest (with imposition of minimum residual basal area and riparian buffers and prohibition on high-grading/diameter limit cuts), thereby increasing net growth. The GMF practice, compared to common practice high-grading in the region, is expected to generate net emission reductions of ~1.6 t CO2e/acre/year. total GHG emission reductions and removals.

name: Inner Mongolia Yitulihe-Genhe Afforestation Project
developer: INNER MONGOLIA DAXING’ANLING CARBON SINK TECHNOLOGY CO.LTD
project_type: Agriculture Forestry and Other Land Use
description:
The Inner Mongolia Yitulihe-Genhe Afforestation Project (hereafter “the project”) is located in northern part of the western side of Greater Khingan Mountains, Hulun Buir City, Inner Mongolia Autonomous Region, P.R.C. The project is jointly implemented byInner Mongolia Yitulihe Forestry Co. LTD and Genhe Forest Industry Co. LTD, both of which belong to the China Inner Mongolia Forest Industry Group. The project is designed to establish forests on degraded lands previously deforested and/or converted (croplands or settlements).
Most of the lands to be planted were deforested since 1950s. Significant deforested lands were converted to croplands and settlements to support livelihood for increased residents. Other land remained as barren lands and have never been reforested since then. Due to human disturbance, desertification and sandification as well as soil erosion, the barren lands are degraded and degrading which would continue under the without project scenario.
2,059.4 ha of forest is to be established by direct planting on degraded lands in 12 forestry farm of Yitulihe Forestry Bureau and 12 forestry farms of Genhe Forestry Bureau. 66.3%% of reforestation activities are carried out in a mixture of different tree species for a purpose of enhancing resilience.
Major species and Afforestation models include 480.64 ha of Spruce (Picea meyeri Rehd.et Wils), 214.6 ha of Mongolian Scotch pine (Pinus sylvestris var. mongolica Litv.), 546.0 ha of mixture of spruce and larch (Larix gmelinii (Rupr.) Kuzen), 43.8 ha of mixture of spruce, Scotch pine and elm (Ulmus macrocarpa Hance), 187.2 ha of spruce and elm, 459.9 ha of mixture of spruce and Scotch pine, and 127.3 ha of mixture of Mongolian Scotch pine and elm. It is expected that the project would produce 800,326 tCO2e of GHG removals in 60 years, with an average annual GHG removals of 13,339 tCO2e, starting in 2020. All species are native. No invasive alien species or genetically modified organisms are involved. All lan

name: Sichuan Huashun PET Recycling Project
developer: Sichuan Huashun Haitian Chemical Fiber Co., Ltd.
description:
Sichuan Huashun PET Recycling Project (hereafter referred to as “the Project”) aims to produce PET fibers and PET particles by recycling and processing post-consumer PET bottles, to replace the same amount of PET products produced from raw materials. The total production capacity is about 60,000 tons of recycled polyester (PET) products per year. The project is located in Pengxi Country, Suining City, Sichuan, China and is developed and operated by Zhejiang Zhongwei Carbon Energy Technology Co., Ltd. (hereafter referred to as “the project proponent”).
Before the project implementation, the same amount of PET product was produced from raw materials (crude oil and natural gas); the baseline scenario is the same as the condition prior to project initiation. The Project achieves GHG emission reductions by avoiding the consumption of the equivalent raw materials and by reducing related energy consumption as well.
It is estimated that the Project will achieve annual GHG emission reductions of 59506 tCO2e and total emission reductions of 416,542 tCO2e over the first crediting period.

name: MEM OSB-1 SOLAR POWER PROJECT
developer: MEM TEKSTIL SANAYI VE TICARET ANONIM SIRKETI
description: MEM OSB-1 SOLAR POWER PROJECT includes installation of rooftop solar photovoltaic systems with the objective of generating clean energy (electricity) for the purpose of inhouse/captive consumption in the commercial facilities of the project owners. Consumption of clean electricity generated in the project activity by harnessing renewable energy (solar) resources has resulted in avoidance of grid power that was used by the project facility/project owner in the pre-project scenario. The project activity has therefore resulted in curbing emission of greenhouse gas, which would have been emitted from generation of equivalent amount of electricity in the grid tied power plant, that has been avoided due to the project activity. The project activity encompasses a rooftop solar power project with the capacity of 10.3 MWe. The proposed project activity deployed in Turkey by MEM Tekstil Sanayi ve Ticaret Anonim Şirketi. The project is expected to result in an average annual supply of 8,974 MWh/year. The average annual emission reduction from the project is estimated to be around 5,822 tCO2e/annum and a cumulative emission reduction of 40,753 tCO2e for the entire crediting period of 7 years.

name: CARBON GROUP PROGRAM FOR SUSTAINABLE LOW CARBON CROP AND GRASSLAND MANAGEMENT IN ARGENTINA
project_type: Agriculture Forestry and Other Land Use
description:
The project intends to include producers dedicated to extensive agriculture (corn, soybeans, wheat, sunflower, cotton, and other crops), and extensive cattle ranching, mostly cattle and grazing grasslands, pastures, agropastoral, and silvo-pastoral. Given the characteristics of the country, farm and ranch  production dates from no more than 200 years ago.
During most of the 20th century, the farms were managed in a rather extensive manner and with aggressive tillage systems, which caused widespread declines in the organic matter content of the soils. This lasted until the end of that century, when for different reasons the producers adopted zero tillage systems, which are what predominate today (more than 90%).
The projects to be implemented are expected to mitigate climate change both by reducing greenhouse gas (GHG) emissions and by capturing atmospheric carbon dioxide (CO2) and storing it as stable carbon in the soil, which must be recarbonized. The greatest efforts to reduce GHG emissions will be due to the adoption of better nitrogen fertilization technologies, which include alternative sources of nitrogen and variable rate fertilization that reduce nitrous oxide (N2) emissions from fertilized soils, the intensification of agricultural rotations with greater incorporation of winter crops, nitrogen fixing species and cover crops, and improved grazing management in livestock, which increase carbon stocks and with improvements in digestibility that reduce methane (CH4) emissions due to enteric fermentation. 
It is estimated that with these improvements, which are not currently widespread even among producers, it will be possible to reduce between 0.5 and 3 tons of CO2e/ha/year. Obviously, the total amount will depend on the area committed by the producers. This area is expected to reach more than 160 thousand hectares. If this is so, it is expected to mitigate almost 2 million tons CO2e at the end of this project.

name: MILOPRI PROJECT - PRECISION MANAGEMENT SYSTEMS FOR SUSTAINABLE ORCHARDS
project_type: Agriculture Forestry and Other Land Use
description:
The VCS Milopri project - Precision Management Systems for Sustainable Avocado Orchards, is the flagship project of We-Agri’s Regenerative Carbon Credit Network (RCCN) initiative - an intelligent platform designed to provide a holistic solution to endorse commercial fruit orchards and vineyards around the world. 

Fruit trees have great structural characteristics (e.g., long-life cycle; permanent organs such as the trunk, branches, and roots; minimum soil tillage; high quality and yield) which allow them to accumulate a significant amount of carbon (Sharma et al. 2021). Hence, the motivation to establish a sustainable agricultural system in orchards and vineyards that can further minimize emissions and is capable of efficiently sequestering carbon within the atmosphere.

This is a pioneering project that follows the SCOVY (i.e., Sustainable Carbon Orchards and Vineyards) methodology, which is currently being developed by We-Agri. This methodology will be the object of future works that will encompass different fruit crops. The main goal is to shift commercial fruit orchards into sustainable agricultural systems endorsed for the issuance of high-quality carbon credits by implementing smart-climate agricultural practices.

The Milopri grouped project is situated within the western Galilee region in the northern part of Israel. The project location has an overall area of circa 3,000 hectares which are owned by 25 different Israeli agricultural cooperative villages. These farms are consolidated into one Centralized packhouse & logistic center - Milopri Agricultural Cooperative. 

The project activities aim at increasing the capacity of soil to sequester carbon and reducing nitrogenous fertilizer-related greenhouse gas emissions. The project also holistically aims at achieving sustainable management practices which not only improve soil health and productivity but can also achieve socio-economic development in the project area.

name: Xinjiang Muge Swine Farm Manure Management System GHG Mitigation Project
developer: Aksu Xingjiang Muge FOOD Co., Ltd.
project_type: Energy industries (renewable/non-renewable sources); Livestock, enteric fermentation, and manure management; Waste handling and disposal
description:
Xinjiang Muge Swine Farm Manure Management System GHG Mitigation Project (hereafter referred to as the project) introduces new animal waste management systems (AWMSs) to treat the manure from 3 existing swine farms in  Xinjiang Province, which are owned by AKSU Xingjiang MUGE food Co., Ltd. The purpose of the project activity is to treat the manure and wastewater to avoid methane emissions generated in the baseline uncovered anaerobic lagoons. 
In this project, AWMS is built to replace the traditional open anaerobic lagoons, and each subsidiary swine farm installed one AWMS. The manure and waster will be collected into the anaerobic digesters and then biogas generated during the anaerobic treatment process will be captured and total of 3.7 million m3 biogas is expected to be generated annually. Biogas is then sent into biogas boilers for heat production. Every biogas boiler has been installed in each swine farm. All of the heat generated is used by AWMSs and the swine farms, while the rest (if any) will be burned. The sludge produced after fermentation is applied to cornfields as fertilizer, and the wastewater produced by anaerobic biogas digesters is used for agricultural irrigation.
Benefiting from the “waste-biogas-fertilizer” pattern, harmlessness and ecological utilization of the swine manure can be realized. All the heat generated by the project will be used by the AWMSs and 3 swine farms. The heat generated will not be connected to other users or the regional heating supply system and the baseline emissions associated with heat generation will not be claimed. The project activity will reduce GHG in the atmosphere by avoiding methane emissions from anaerobic treatment of swine manure and wastewater. The project is expected to achieve an annual emission reduction of 415,544 tCO2e and a total emission reduction of 2,908,811 tCO2e in the first crediting period.

name: Qinghai Muge Swine Farm Manure Management System GHG Mitigation Project
developer: Golmud Xingjiang MUGE FOOD Co., Ltd
project_type: Livestock, enteric fermentation, and manure management; Waste handling and disposal
description:
It is estimated that the total manure treatment capacity of the project is 6,000 m3 for the 4 digesters. The biogas produced by the swine farms using the digesters can be used for heating, for supplying organic fertilizer processing production, etc. It will not be provided to other users. Baseline emissions from heat generation have been ignored for the sake of prudence.
The project activity will reduce greenhouse gases in the atmosphere by avoiding methane emissions from the anaerobic treatment of pig manure and wastewater. It is estimated that  156,672 tCO2e of emission reductions will be generated annually, for a total of  1,096,702 tCO2e over the crediting period.

name: Improved Cookstove Distribution in Ghana by EKI Phase-II
description: The main purpose of project is distribution of fuel-efficient improved cook stoves (ICS) in Republic of Ghana (Ghana). The ICS disseminated through this project will replace the low efficient baseline cook stoves. Through this project, the distribution and installation of high thermal efficient improved cook stoves (ICS) will be undertaken for households and communities/non-household. The ICS will burn charcoal more efficiently thereby improving thermal energy transfer to pots, hence saving charcoal and greenhouse gases. Not only will this halt the rapidly progressing deforestation but will also reduce health hazards from indoor air (smoke) pollution and time & money of the participating household will be saved in the procurement of charcoal.

name: Leyuan ANIMAL Husbandry Weixian Co., Ltd. NO. 4 Pasture Wastes Recycling Project
developer: Hebei Zhonghai Huaneng Energy Co., Ltd
project_type: Energy industries (renewable/non-renewable sources); Waste handling and disposal
description:
Leyuan ANIMAL Husbandry Weixian Co., Ltd. NO. 4 Pasture Wastes Recycling Project (hereinafter referred to as the Project) locates in Xiwang Village, Houguan Town, Weixian District, Xingtai City, Hebei Province, P.R China. The project is to build a centralized anaerobic animal manure treatment system which collects manure waste (dairy cow) from Leyuan ANIMAL Husbandry Weixian Co., Ltd. NO. 4 Pasture in Weixian district. The project uses animal manure waste as ferment material to produce biogas in the Completely Stirred Tank Reactor (CSTR) type anaerobic digesters. The recovered biogas will be used for electricity generation at the project site. The electricity generated by the project will be delivered to North China Power Grid (NCPG). The residual waste from the CSTR digesters will be used to produce organic fertilizer at the project site.
The project is expected to avoid GHG emission of methane through recovery and destruction of biogas. In addition, the electricity generated from the biogas will be delivered to NCPG to replace equivalent electricity generated by the fossil fuel fired power plants connected to the grid.

name: Grouped Electric bikes project in Africa
description:
This group project activity (GPA) intends to replace motorcycle with internal combustion engines (ICE) which use petrol fuel sources, by electric motorcycles. Therefore, the GPA will replace fossil fuel powered motorcycles by electric motorcycles, thus leading to emissions reduction
In sub-Saharan Africa, the transport sector account for 14.5% of total energy combustion  representing 69 millions metrics tons of oils equivalent. This consumption is expected to grow to 10.1 quadrillon BTU by 2040 with an increase of 3.1%  per year. 
The transport sector is also the second largest source of emissions in Africa, accounting for 28% (348 Mt CO2)   of the total emissions of the continent.
The sector is also one of the main causes of urban pollution. It is estimated that 90% of urban air pollution is attributable to vehicles emissions, and according to the World Health Organisation, 176,000 deaths per year in Africa are due to outdoor air pollution .
The purpose of this grouped project (the project) is to tackle these issues by the dissemination of 753,300 of electric motorcycles 2 wheelers in different countries across Africa by 2026.
The first instance of the grouped project is the distribution of 67,746 e-motorcycles in Togo by 2026. The second instance is the distribution of 111,554 e-motorcycles in Benin by 2026.
The global CO2 emissions of Togo was 2,6 GtCO2 in 2018, with transport representing more than 77% of the total emissions .
This first instance in Togo may lead to emissions reductions of 460,644 tCO2e over the first crediting period, or on average 65,806 tCO2e/year.
The second instance in Benin may lead to emissions reduction of 754,247 tCO2e over the first crediting period, and 107,750 tCO2e/year on average.

name: Adjusted Water Management in Rice Cultivation in West of Fuling District in Chongqing City
project_type: Agriculture Forestry and Other Land Use
description:
Adjusted Water Management in Rice Cultivation in West of Fuling District in Chongqing City (hereinafter referred to as “the project”) is a project that changes the water regime during the rice cultivation period from continuously flooded to intermittently flooded on rice paddy fields located in the West of Fuling District in Chongqing City, China. The project involves 16,472.7 hectares of single cropping rice within the project boundary.
The project is expected to reduce GHG emissions by reducing the flooding time during the rice cultivation period. Since soil organic matters emits a large amount of methane (CH4) under flooded conditions because of anaerobic decomposition, when the flooded time of rice fields in the whole growth cycle is reduce, CH4 emissions are hence reduced; in addition, it provides other benefits such as creation of job opportunities, water saving, and yield increase compared to the traditional continuously flooded cultivation.

name: Adjusted Water Management in Rice Cultivation in East of Fuling District in Chongqing City
project_type: Agriculture Forestry and Other Land Use
description:
Adjusted Water Management in Rice Cultivation in East of Fuling District in Chongqing City (hereinafter referred to as “the project”) is a project that changes the water regime during the rice cultivation period from continuously flooded to intermittently flooded on rice paddy fields located in the south of Fuling District in Chongqing City, China. The project involves 16,504.35 hectares of single cropping rice within the project boundary.
The project is expected to reduce GHG emissions by reducing the flooding time during the rice cultivation period. Since soil organic matters emits a large amount of methane (CH4) under flooded conditions because of anaerobic decomposition, when the flooded time of rice fields in the whole growth cycle is reduced, CH4 emissions are hence reduced; in addition, it provides other benefits such as creation of job opportunities, water saving, and yield increase compared to the traditional continuously flooded cultivation.

name: Adjusted Water Management in Rice Cultivation in North Anyi
developer: Jiangxi Green Energy Agricultural Development Co., Ltd
project_type: Agriculture Forestry and Other Land Use
description:
The project changing from continuously flooded to intermittent flooded conditions during rice cultivation is conducted in Nanchang City， Jiangxi Province of China. Anyi County is located in the west part of Nanchang, with a total acreage of 6949.6 ha for double-cropping rice. Without implementing this project, which provides ditches to conduct the intermittently flooded method, the backward continuously flooded method would be continued, so the scenario that rice was cultivated by the continuously flooded method is the baseline scenario. Since the organic matter in rice soil under flooded conditions can emit a large amount of methane (CH4) because of anaerobic decomposition, the intermittently flooded method is more beneficial to water conservation, production increase and methane emission removal than the continuously flooded. 

This project solved the problems of excessive water used during rice cultivation which results in not only a large amount of methane (CH4) emissions but also low rice productivity by replacing the continuously flooded method with the intermittently flooded method, which shortens the period of anaerobic decomposition of soil organic matter. In this case, the CH4 emission can be declined by an average of 48% . 

The implementation of the project is expected to reduce the GHG emissions amounting to 1,603,490 tCO2e in 21 years, with an average annual GHG emission removal of 76,356.6 tCO2e.

name: Adjusted Water Management in Rice Cultivation in South Anyi
developer: Jiangxi Green Energy Agricultural Development Co., Ltd
project_type: Agriculture Forestry and Other Land Use
description:
The project changing from continuously flooded to intermittent flooded conditions during rice cultivation is conducted in south of Anyi County，Nanchang City, Jiangxi Province of China. Anyi County is located in the west part of Nanchang, with a total acreage of 6693.4 ha for double-cropping rice. Without implementing this project, which provides ditches to conduct the intermittently flooded method, the backward continuously flooded method would be continued, so the scenario that rice was cultivated by the continuously flooded method is the baseline scenario. Since the organic matter in rice soil under flooded conditions can emit a large amount of methane (CH4) because of anaerobic decomposition, the intermittently flooded method is more beneficial to water conservation, production increase and methane emission removal than the continuously flooded. 
This project solved the problems of excessive water used during rice cultivation which results in not only a large amount of methane (CH4) emissions but also low rice productivity by replacing the continuously flooded method with the intermittently flooded method, which shortens the period of anaerobic decomposition of soil organic matter. In this case, the CH4 emission can be declined by an average of 48% . 
The implementation of the project is expected to reduce the GHG emissions amounting to 1,544,376 tCO2e in 21 years, with an average annual GHG emission removal of 73,541.7 tCO2e.

name: involtor Future Agriculture, East-Europe
project_type: Agriculture Forestry and Other Land Use
description: The Involtor Future Agriculture East-Europe is a grouped project gathering under the same program major agricultural areas from five Eastern European countries and aiming at the scientific implementation of modern agricultural practices that helps preserve the Planet's climate, increase the resilience of agriculture and food security to climate change. The project provides a wide range of support for farmers, aiming for a safe transition to regenerative agriculture by implementing effective practices that sequester carbon in the soil, reduce / remove the emissions of CH4, N2O, CO2 that agriculture emits today in significant quantities, and in exchange for the performance monitored by this Project, farmers will receive income from verified carbon credits. The project pursues the implementation of 8 of UN SDG’s seeking certification with VERRA's SD ViSta - Verified Impact Standard. The initial phase of Project considers 1st of December 2019 as the baseline date in which the first agricultural practices implementation started.

name: Improved cookstoves for refugees in Uganda
description: The refugees crisis in South Sudan, led to hundred thousands of households moving from their country to Uganda. In August 2022, the total number of refugees was 1,525,197  persons (382,778 households). This flux increased strongly the deforestation rate in the regions where refugees are installed. A study  conducted in 2029, showed that between 2014 and 2018, there was 34,11é ha of tree cover loss and 29,604 ha of degradation. The sudy also highlighted that in the 14 targeted refugees settlements the demand of cooking fuel was equivalent to 345,000 tons. Which is 4 times the quantity of tree growth within the settlements and the 5 km buffer zone. A joint assessment conducted by FAO and the United Nations High Commissioner for Refugees (UNHCR) in one settlement (Bidibidi) in March 2017  concluded that the aboveground biomass (AGB) stock within the settlement area could meet the needs of the population for only three years, in the absence of any intervention.

name: Zhejiang Jia’ao Biodiesel Production Project
developer: Zhejiang Jia’ao Green New Energy Co., Ltd.
description:
Zhejiang Jia’ao Biodiesel Production Project (hereafter referred to as “the Project”) is located at No.416 Desheng Road, Industry District, Zhouquan Town, Jiaxing City, Zhejiang Province, China. The Project is designed to produce 150,000 tonnes biodiesel BD100 (hereafter referred to as “the biodiesel”) annually made from the feedstock of waste oil/fat. The biodiesel produced will be supplied to consumers to substitute diesel used for car fuel.
The Project produces biodiesel based on waste oil/fat from biogenic origin to substitute petroleum diesel for the use as fuels. Biodiesel is a fuel which produce lower GHG emissions when combusted, hence the GHG emissions will be reduced resulting from such displacement.

name: Hebei Handan Damingchang Biogas Recovery and Utilization Project
project_type: Energy industries (renewable/non-renewable sources); Waste handling and disposal
description:
Hebei Handan Damingchang Biogas Recovery and Utilization Project (hereinafter referred to as the Project) locates in Cao Ren Village, Dangtou Township, Daming County, Handan City, Hebei Province, P.R China. The project is to build a centralized anaerobic animal manure treatment system which collects manure waste from dairy cows from Daming farms in Daming County. The project uses animal manure waste as ferment material to produce biogas in the Completely Stirred Tank Reactor (CSTR) type anaerobic digesters. The recovered biogas will be used for electricity generation at the project site. The electricity generated by the project will be delivered to North China Power Grid (NCPG). The residual waste from the CSTR digesters will be used to produce organic fertilizer at the project site.
The project is expected to avoid GHG emission of methane through recovery and destruction of biogas. In addition, the electricity generated from the biogas will be delivered to NCPG to replace equivalent electricity generated by the fossil fuel fired power plants connected to the grid.

name: Carbon In Flavor and Arome Forests (C-BOSAR)
project_type: Agriculture Forestry and Other Land Use
description:
The Carbon in Flavor and Aroma Forest (C-BOSAR), is a ARR carbon sequestration grouped project proposed by PROJECT SIERRA , designed by ECOTIERRA and
RIOSIERRA with the support of RED ECOLSIERRA . The project is based on improving existent land use models to introduce coffee, cocoa, and honey agroforestry systems. The project aims to develop improved agroforestry systems for the production of shade coffee, cocoa and honey, with organic and fair-trade certification, through tree planting, the restoration of the community-nature relationship, technical training and assistance and contribution to the strengthening of value chains for these products
in the Sierra Nevada de Santa Marta and the Serranía del Perijá.

name: Karaman Landfill Gas to Electricity Project
project_type: Energy industries (renewable/non-renewable sources); Waste handling and disposal
description: The project activity includes capture and utilization of landfill gas (Landfill gas contains approximately 50% methane and is a potent greenhouse gas (GHG)) for power generation, that was vented to the atmosphere in the pre-project scenario. It is estimated that the landfill receives approximately 200 tons of municipal solid waste (MSW) daily since 2012. About 68% of this waste consists of organic materials such as pulp, paper and cardboard, and food waste. The project activity includes landfill gas capture unit and Landfill gas-based Electricity Generating Plant with an installed capacity of 3.720 MWm/3.612 MWe. The electricity generating unit was commissioned on June 10th, 20211, however commercial electricity generation started as on 01/01/20222 and is regarded as the project start date. The electricity generated from the project activity is fed to the National Grid of Turkey.

name: VALLE LAGUNARE - VAL DOGA', CAPOSILE - VENICE CARBON CREDIT ASSESSMENT IN CONTROLLED LAGOON ENVIRONMENT
project_type: Agriculture Forestry and Other Land Use
description:
The project consists of assessing the production/absorption of greenhouse gas CO2 in a eutrophic lagoon environment used for fishing purposes (Fishing Valley). According to the UNFCCC CDM criteria, this project should be considered for the standard VCS, AFOLU and the voluntary assessment of carbon credits based on Annex A of the Kyoto Protocol, which falls into the following category 
- 'Reduction and control of CO2 emissions in agricultural activities'

name: Inner Mongolia Alihe-Jiwen Afforestation Project
developer: INNER MONGOLIA DAXING’ANLING CARBON SINK TECHNOLOGY CO.LTD
project_type: Agriculture Forestry and Other Land Use
description:
The Inner Mongolia Alihe-Jiwen Afforestation Project (hereafter “the project”) is located in northern part of the eastern side of Greater Khingan Mountains, Oroqen Autonomous Banner , Hulun Buir City, Inner Mongolia Autonomous Region, P.R.C. The project is jointly implemented by Alihe Forest Industry Co. LTD and Jiwen Forest Industry Co. LTD, both of which belong to the China Inner Mongolia Forest Industry Group. The project is designed to establish forests on degraded barren lands previously deforested and/or converted croplands.
Most of the lands to be planted were deforested since 193050s. Significant deforested lands were converted to croplands to support livelihood for increased residents. Other land remained as barren lands and have never been reforested since then. Due to human disturbance, desertification and sandification as well as soil erosion, the barren lands are degraded and degrading which would continue under the without project scenario.
1659.73 ha of forest is to be established by direct planting on degraded lands in 13 forestry farm of Alihe Forestry Bureau and 8 forestry farms of Jiwen Forestry Bureau. 61.4% of afforestation activities are carried out in a mixture of different tree (shrub) species for a purpose of enhancing resilience.
Major species and afforestation models include 26.29 ha of Korean pine (Pinus koraiensis Sieb. et Zucc.), 163.90 ha of Mongolian Scotch pine (Pinus sylvestris var. mongolica Litv.), 393.37 ha of spruce (Picea koraiensis Nakai), 57.63 ha of larch (Larix gmelinii (Rupr.) Kuzen), 312.70 ha of mixture of spruce and larch, 202.21 ha of  mixture of spruce and Seabuckthorn (Hippophae sp), 35.03 ha of mixture of Mongolian Scotch pine and Korean pine, 30.37 ha of mixture of Mongolian Scotch pine and Seabuckthorn, 437.83 ha of mixture of Mongolian Scotch pine and spruce. It is expected that the project would produce 532,455 tCO2e of GHG removals in 60 years, with an average annual GHG removals of 8,874 tCO2e

name: SMG - Nepal Cookstove Program in Terai Region of Himalayas
description:
SDGs Covered by the project: SDG 1, SDG 3, SDG 5, SDG 7, SDG 8 SDG 9, SDG 13

The project will replace the traditional, high GHG emitting and low efficient cookstoves like mud and three stone cookstoves with improved cookstoves (ICS). These ICS are more thermally efficient and better for the environment. The project will aim to educate the beneficiaries about healthy cooking habits and practices along with teaching them how to lower their overall household air pollution (HAP) and minimize the health risks in homes.

name: Adjusted Water Management in Rice Cultivation in Zhijiang City
project_type: Agriculture Forestry and Other Land Use
description:
The project changing from continuously flooded to intermittent flooded condition during rice cultivation is conducted in Zhijiang City within Yichang City, Hubei Province of China, with a total acreage of 9,102.53 ha for single-cropping rice. Without the implementation of this project, the continuously flooded method would be continued, so the scenario that rice was cultivated by continuously flooded method is the baseline scenario. Since the organic matter in rice soil under flooded condition can emit a large amount of methane (CH4) because of anaerobic decomposition, the intermittent flooded method is more beneficial to water conservation, production increase and methane emission reduction than the continuously flooded. 
This project solved the problems of excessive water used during rice cultivation which results in not only large amount of methane (CH4) emissions but also low rice productivity by replacing the continuously flooded method with intermittent flooded method, which shortens the period of anaerobic decomposition of soil organic matter. Hence, with the proposed project activity, an estimated amount of GHG emission reduction 4.72 tCO2e/ha for single cropping rice is expected. Annual average estimation of GHG emission reductions from the project activity is 42,981 tCO2e/year, and the total GHG emission reductions are 429,810 tCO2e during the fixed 10 years crediting period. 
This project aims to: 1、Sequester greenhouse gas and mitigate climate changes; - Increase the rice productivity resulting in higher living standard of local farmers; 2、Increase the number of local individuals who have relevant skills due to diversified educational opportunities from trainings; 3、Provide more job opportunities, especially women workers.

name: Jiangsu Qidong Yongyin Recycled PET Project
developer: Jiangsu Yongyin Chemical Fibre Co., Ltd.
description:
Jiangsu Qidong Yongyin Recycled PET Project (hereinafter called 'the Project' aims to produce the PET chips by reprocessing the waste PET products (like consumed package and bottled drink, used cable, etc.) and to replace the same PET product produced from the raw materials. The total production capacity is about 50,000 tons of recycled polyester (PET) chips per year, and the project factory will recycle 62,500 tons waste plastic PET per year. The Project located in No.1099, West Nanyuan Rd, Qidong Economic Development zone, Nantong city, Jiangsu province, China.
Prior to the project implementation, the same amount of PET chips would be produced from raw materials (crude oil and natural gas) which is also the baseline scenario of the project. Therefore, the GHG emission reduction will be generated through the implementation of the project by avoiding the consumption of the equivalent raw materials and reducing related energy consumption as well.

name: Belize Maya Forest REDD+ Project
project_type: Agriculture Forestry and Other Land Use
description: The Belize Maya Forest Carbon Project is partnership between The Nature Conservancy and Belize Maya Forest Trust. The 87,041 hectare Avoided Planned Deforestation project, located in north-west Belize, reduces GHG emissions through the acquisition and protection of forest lands threatened by agricultural conversion.

name: RUQI MOBILITY GUANGZHOU ELECTRIC VEHICLE IN PASSENGER TRANSPORTATION Phase 2 PROJECT
description: Ruqi Mobility Guangzhou Electric Vehicle in Passenger Transportation Phase 2 Project (hereafter “the project”) aims to reduce carbon dioxide and other greenhouse gas emissions by using electric vehicles (hereafter “EV”) to replace fuel vehicles and provide passenger transportation services. The project is carried out by Ruqi Mobility (also known as ONTIME) to provide systematic integration ride hailing services in Guangzhou City, Guangdong Province, China. The project utilizes artificial intelligence service system and electric exchange stations to enable the passengers to switch their transport from fuel vehicles to energy efficient electric vehicles, thus reducing carbon emissions and improving the sustainability of the passenger transportation. The project has included 5,324 electric vehicles manufactured by Guangzhou Automobile Group Co., Ltd, (hereinafter GAC), providing passenger transportation service. Electricity for the electric vehicles is supplied by charging facilities contacted with China Southern Power Grid.

name: SUSTAINABLE CHARCOAL AND IMPROVED COOKSTOVE INITIATIVE USING MICRO-GASIFIER IN INDIA
project_type: Chemical industry; Energy demand; Energy industries (renewable/non-renewable sources)
description:
The proposed project aims at reducing the fuel wood consumption, in traditional cook stoves by disseminating micro-gasifiers stoves and improved cook stoves at subsidized prices.
Moreover, where charcoal generating micro-gasifier stoves are implemented, the consumption of conventional charcoal by traditional charcoal users shall be reduced by providing them charcoal generated in micro wood gasifier stoves.
The project intends to avail the households with clean cooking solutions; thereby, displacing the less efficient traditional cooking stoves i.e. three stone cookstove from the kitchen with micro-gasifier stoves of better efficiency. Replacement of the traditional cooking stoves with these type of stoves will reduce the exposure of the family members, specifically women, to the indoor air pollution and therefore result in saving of health related expenses.
Overall objectives are reduction of greenhouse gases, conservation of forests and woodlands as well as improved health conditions of gasifier users due to improvement in indoor air quality.
The scenario existing prior to the implementation of the project activity instances is the usage of traditional biomass and inefficient cookstoves with poor ventilation, causing excessive indoor air pollution (IAP) and has been a serious health risk for women and children who spend several hours in the kitchen for cooking as well as non-cooking purposes.
The end users of ICS and charcoal will be informed in advance that the use of micro-gasifier will generate carbon credits which in turn is used for subsiding the price of the micro-gasifiers and for recovering the implementation costs.

name: Grouped Project for Philippines Water Purifier Program
developer: Sustainability Investment Promotion and Development Joint Stock Company
description:
The proposed grouped projects aim to solve the problem of providing safe drinking water for residents in Philippines. The project intends to distribution water purifiers that can be supply safe drinking water to households/communities without boiling. Thereby, displacing the firewood which were using by households to boil the water for drinking purpose. For this reason, this proposed project activity will avoid the use of thermal energy and/or low energy and associated emissions. This directly leads to reduced greenhouse gas emissions. Furthermore, it can be helpful to user’s health
The scenario existing prior to the implementation of the project is the actual baseline scenario which is equal to the existing common practice by the households i.e. in absence of the project activity the equivalent amount of thermal energy generated using firewood in three stone open fires to meet the boiling water demand.

name: Grouped Project for Philippines Cookstove Program
developer: Sustainability Investment Promotion and Development Joint Stock Company
description:
The purpose of the grouped project activity is to disseminate energy efficient Improved Cookstove (ICS) to replace existing traditional stove in domestic households/communities (hereafter “users”) in the Philippines. The objective of project activity is to reduce footprint carbon to the atmosphere as well as decrease environment degradation, reduce of drudgery, time, money spent on fuel wood collection and health risk of women and children subjected to indoor air pollution.
The project activity targets households with no previous ICS access. The geographical boundary is in Philippines. ICSs are distributed free of cost to users. Sustainability Investment Promotion and Development Joint Stock Company (SIPCO) financed the implementation of the project in full.

name: Gansu Hui County Muge Swine Farm Manure Management System GHG Mitigation Project
developer: Hui County XINGJIANG Muge Breeding Co., LTD.
project_type: Energy industries (renewable/non-renewable sources); Livestock, enteric fermentation, and manure management; Waste handling and disposal
description:
Gansu Hui County Muge Swine Farm Manure Management System GHG Mitigation Project (hereinafter referred to as the Project) introduces a new Animal Waste Management System (AWMS) to treat manure from this existing pig farm in Hui County, Longnan City, Gansu Province, which belongs to Xingjiang Muge Co.,Ltd. The purpose of the project activity is to treat the manure and wastewater to avoid methane emissions generated in the baseline uncovered anaerobic lagoons. The estimated lifetime of project is 15 years.
First, all manure and wastewater will be collected and then solids and liquids will be separated. The solid manure will be processed in an aerobic composting system and organic fertilizer will be produced, and the fertilizer produced in this process will be distributed to local farmers free of charge. The liquids will be treated by anaerobic digestion and the biogas produced during the treatment process will be captured and sent to a boiler to generate heat, with the excess gas being destroyed through a combustion system (if available). The sludge produced after fermentation is applied as fertilizer to nearby fields, and the wastewater from the anaerobic digester is used for agricultural irrigation.
With the help of the above-mentioned model, a harmless and ecological use of pig manure can be achieved. It is estimated that approximately 900 tons of animal manure will be handled daily by the AWMS. Also, the generated heat through biogas will be only used for daily operation of the AWMSs and the swine farms themselves and will not be provided to other users. For conservativeness, baseline emissions from heat generation are neglected.
The project activity will reduce of GHG in the atmosphere through avoiding methane emissions from anaerobic treatment of swine manure and wastewater. It is estimated that 68,384 tCO2e emission reductions will be generated annually and total emission reductions are 478,688 tCO2e in the crediting period.

name: Hunan Changde Muge Swine Farm Manure Management System GHG Mitigation Project
developer: Changde Dingcheng District Xingjiang Muge Breeding Co., Ltd.
project_type: Livestock, enteric fermentation, and manure management; Waste handling and disposal
description:
Hunan Changde Muge Swine Farm Manure Management System GHG Mitigation Project (hereinafter referred to as the Project) introduce animal waste management system (AWMS) to swine farm in Dingcheng District, Changde City, Hunan Province, China, which are owned by Changde Dingcheng District Xingjiang Muge Breeding Co., Ltd. (here in after ”Xingjiang”). The project activity aims to treat the manure and wastewater from the swine farm to avoid methane emissions generated in the baseline uncovered anaerobic lagoons.
All the manure and wastewater are collected and then be separated first. The solid will be treated in aerobic composting system and the organic fertilizers will be produced, part of the fertilizer produced in this process will be distributed to local farmers for free and the others will be sold in domestic market. The liquid will be treated through anaerobic digestion and the biogas generated during the treatment process will be captured and sent to boilers for heat generation and Surplus biogas will be destroyed through the flaring system (if any). The sludge produced from anaerobic digestion will be treated through aerobic composting together with the solid, the effluent will be supplied to the farmers living around free for agriculture irrigation.The project activity will reduce of GHG in the atmosphere through avoiding methane emissions from anaerobic treatment of swine manure and wastewater. It is estimated that 91,680 tCO2e emission reductions will be generated annually and total emission reductions are 641,760 tCO2e in the crediting period.

name: Adjusted Water Management in Rice Cultivation in Cangxi County in Sichuan Province
developer: Sichuan Cangxi Urban Investment Carbon Sink Technology Co., Ltd.
project_type: Agriculture Forestry and Other Land Use
description:
Adjusted Water Management in Rice Cultivation in Cangxi County in Sichuan province (hereinafter referred to as “the project”) is a project that changes the water regime during the rice cultivation period from continuously flooded to intermittently flooded on rice paddy fields located in Cangxi County in Sichuan province, China. The project involves 24,159 hectares of single cropping rice within the project boundary.
The implementation activities of the project include original ditch repair and rebuild, reservoir repair and rebuild, higher efficient drainage facilities purchase and necessary training for farmers to help them to conduct the intermittent flooded water regime during rice cultivation, which replaces the traditional flooded method. Controllable irrigation and drainage can not only save water resources, but also reduce methane emissions from soil organic matter under anaerobic conditions (flooded state).

name: Danjingshan Adjusted Water Management in Rice Cultivation
developer: Sichuan Huixiang Ecological Agriculture Co., Ltd.
project_type: Agriculture Forestry and Other Land Use

name: Waste Management Project-1 by GLOBAL CARBON SOLUTIONS
description:
The proposed project is a 100 TPD Bio-cng plant located at 534/1 Siruvalayam Road, Mahendra vaadi 
district, Nemili thaluk, Ranipet district,Tamil Nadu, 632502. We manufacture Bio-CNG and bio Manure 
using bio-degradable wastes. The technology used is anaerobic decomposition in a continuous stir tank 
reactor. Anaerobic decomposition is a complex and natural process of degradation of a variety of 
intermediates into Methane, Carbon-dioxide, and other gases.

name: Jinmu AWMS GHG Mitigation Project in Liaoning Province
project_type: Livestock, enteric fermentation, and manure management; Waste handling and disposal
description: The project activity uses dry scraper system to collect the manure automatically and the remaining manure, urine and wastewater are collected and then be separated first. The separated liquid will be treated through anaerobic digestion, The biogas produced during the treatment process will be directly incinerated. The effluent will be used as a liquid organic fertilizer for the irrigation of agriculture.The residual waste from the dry manure storage room will be sent outside of the project site for aerobic composting and then returned to the field as fertilizer.

name: Yangxiang AWMS GHG Mitigation Project In Anhui Province
description: The project activity uses flushing system to collect the manure automatically. All the manureand wastewater are collected and then be separated first. The separated solid will be treatedinaerobic composting system to produce fertilizer. The separated liquid will be treated throughanaerobic digestion, The biogas produced during the treatment process will be collectedandutilized or directly incinerated (Each instance may have some differences). The sludge producedfrom anaerobic digestion will be treated through aerobic composting together with the solidandthe effluent will be used as a liquid organic fertilizer for the irrigation of agriculture

name: Installation of high efficiency cookstoves in Uttar Pradesh and Madhya Pradesh  (India)
description: The purpose of this grouped project “Installation of high efficiency cookstoves in Uttar Pradesh and Madhya Pradesh (India)” is to reduce the rate of deforestation in the remote areas along with reduction of the indoor air pollution. The project will distribute 75,000 ICS (improved cookstoves) to the beneficiaries under first project instance in Uttar Pradesh. The Project Instance (PI 1) in this GP is estimated to offset an annual average of 380,912 tCO2 emission reductions and a total of 2,666,386 tC02 emission reductions over the crediting period of 7 years.

name: Installation of high efficiency wood burning cookstoves in South Africa
developer: C-Quest Capital CR Stoves Pte. Ltd.
description:
The project status is under development. The project involves distribution of fuel-efficient improved cookstoves (ICS) in South Africa. The ICS disseminated through this project will replace the baseline cookstoves. 

Through this project, the distribution and installation of approximately 500,000 ICS will be undertaken for households in South Africa. It is intended that under this project single pot, TLC-CQC Rocket Stove will be distributed. Each household will receive up to 2 ICS per household. The ICS will burn wood more efficiently thereby improving thermal transfer to pots, hence saving fuel. Not only will this halt the rapidly progressing deforestation in South Africa but will also reduce health hazards from indoor smoke pollution and women and children will have to spend less time collecting firewood.

The end user will be informed in advance that the use of ICS generates carbon finance which in turn is used for subsidising the price of ICS and for recovering project implementation costs.

name: Carbono Rural AR NEA
project_type: Agriculture Forestry and Other Land Use
description: The “carbono rural AR NEA” project aims to support sustainable grazing practices in Northeastern Argentina (NEA). The project will target farmers that apply unsustainable grazing practices in NEA grasslands/pasturelands and encourage their transition to better grazing practices. These changes are expected to improve the productivity and sustainability of grazing systems while enhancing soil organic carbon sequestration and reducing GHG emissions.

name: Distribution of LED Lamps for replacing ICLs in India
description: The purpose of this Grouped project “Distribution of LED Lamps for Replacing ICLs in India” is to reduce fossil-fuel based electricity consumption in the rural households of India by introducing more energy efficient LED lamps to replace incandescent lightbulbs (“ICLs”), This would result in reduction in greenhouse gas emissions. The first Project activity in this GP is estimated to generate a total of 537,990 tCO2e and an annual average of 53,799 tCO2e emission reductions over the crediting period of 10 years.

name: Lianzhou Landfill Gas Power Generation Project
developer: Lianzhou Dongkang Renewable Energy Technology Co., Ltd.
project_type: Energy industries (renewable/non-renewable sources); Waste handling and disposal
description: Lianzhou Landfill Gas Power Generation Project (hereafter referred to as the project) is invested and owned by Lianzhou Dongkang Renewable Energy Technology Co., Ltd (hereafter referred to as the project owner). The project captures the landfill gas that would have been released to the atmosphere in the absence of the project and generates electricity with the landfill gas (LFG). The total installed capacity of the project is 3MW. The project consists of 5 sets of 600kW generators which were was operated since 01/06/2021. LFG collected is used for electricity generation with internal combustion generators to generate about 109,379MWh supplying to CSPG during the first 7 years crediting period. The expected average annual emission reductions are 82,464 tCO2e and the total emission reductions are 577,253 tCO2e during the first 7-year crediting period.

name: Tianpeng Adjusted Water Management in Rice Cultivation
developer: Sichuan Huixiang Ecological Agriculture Co., Ltd.
project_type: Agriculture Forestry and Other Land Use
description:
The project changing from continuously flooded to intermittent flooded condition during rice
cultivation is conducted in Southern Pengzhou City within Chengdu City, Sichuan Province
of China, with a total acreage of 12,437 ha for single-cropping rice. Without the
implementation of this project, the continuously flooded method would be continued, so the
scenario that rice was cultivated by continuously flooded method is the baseline scenario.
Since the organic matter in rice soil under flooded condition can emit a large amount of
methane (CH4) because of anaerobic decomposition, the intermittent flooded method is
more beneficial to water conservation, production increase and methane emission reduction
than the continuously flooded.
This project solved the problems of excessive water used during rice cultivation which results
in not only large amount of methane (CH4) emissions but also low rice productivity by
replacing the continuously flooded method with intermittent flooded method, which shortens
the period of anaerobic decomposition of soil organic matter. Hence, with the proposed
project activity, an estimated amount of GHG emission reduction 4.55 tCO2e/ha for singlecropping
rice is expected. Annual average estimation of GHG emission reductions from the
project activity is 56,539 tCO2e/year, and the total GHG emission reductions are 565,390
tCO2e during the fixed 10 years crediting period.
This project aims to:
- Sequester greenhouse gas and mitigate climate changes;
- Increase the rice productivity resulting in higher living standard of local farmers;
- Increase the number of local individuals who have relevant skills due to diversified
educational opportunities from trainings;
- Provide more job opportunities, especially women workers.

name: Angovo Maharitra
description: The project aims to spread improved cookstoves (Angovo Maharitra) to households in 8 rural communities in southern Madagascar, thereby decreasing the consumption of non-renewable wood fuels, slowing local deforestation, reducing the time spent cooking compared to traditional stoves, limiting the exposure to toxic smoke, and improving nutritional status. A total of 15,439 households will benefit from this project, reducing emissions by more than 44,000 tons of CO2 per year.

name: Mila Rano - Safe water access for Madagascar
description:
The purpose of the grouped project activity is to provide safe drinking water to households in southern Madagascar, starting with 5 rural communities initially, but with the aim of involving more in the near future. Through the construction of solar-powered water supply systems, the proposed project activity aims to reduce the need for wood fuel and non-renewable biomass that would had been otherwise used to boil water for water purification. This project is expected to reduce emissions by more than 12,000 tons of CO2 per year.
The geographical boundary is in Madagascar and the target are households in rural communities with no water purifiers; the purified water will be distributed to users free of cost.

name: Improved Cook Stove Project 1, Nkhata Bay District, Malawi - CER Conversion
description:
The project involves dissemination of the Changu Changu Moto high efficiency biomass cook 
stoves to approximately 19,000 households in Nkhata Bay District, Malawi. The project is being 
developed under the small scale CDM methodology AMS- II.G. Energy efficiency measures in 
thermal applications of non-renewable biomass, version 5.
The Changu Changu Moto is a low cost, high efficiency biomass fired cook stove developed 
through extensive trials with the local communities and is specifically designed for local Malawian 
conditions. The stove is constructed from locally available materials and does not require specialist 
construction skills or equipment. The stove design is a brick rocket stove, constructed using 26 
mud bricks and a mud mortar mix. The Chichewan name Changu Changu Moto translates to “Fast 
Fast Fire”, and reflects one of the main benefits of the improved cook stove in reducing cooking 
time and saving wood fuel.
The Changu Changu Moto improved cook stove will replace the low efficiency 3-stone fire stove, 
which is the dominant firewood end-use system for cooking within Malawi. Emission reductions are 
achieved through improving household energy efficiency and thus reducing the consumption of 
non-renewable woody biomass
