name: REGENERATIVE LIVESTOCK CARBON PROJECT WITH A PARTICIPATORY APPROACH IN COLOMBIA
project_type: Agriculture Forestry and Other Land Use
description:
The regenerative livestock farming carbon project in Colombia is developed by the project developer Sosty S.A.S.Sosty supports traditional livestock farmers with degraded and abandoned grasslands to restore the ecosystem services of their lands through the transition and implementation of regenerative livestock grazing activities, which include high density and rotational grazing of cattle and protection of standing forests. These practices will not only contribute to climate change mitigation (additional carbon removed from the atmosphere through the increase of the soil organic carbon) but also to climate change adaptation by increasing the resilience of the ecosystems and the landowners towards the effects of climate change. 

The regenerative activities focus mainly on managed grazing systems which are based on a high-density livestock grazing with high rotation forage cycles (between 60 and 180 days of rest time, depending on the health of forages and level of soil degradation). The grouped project is developed within the Colombian agricultural frontier, which is the delimited area defined by the government, where livestock husbandry and agricultural activities are allowed to be developed.  

The first phase of project implementation includes ten cattle and buffalo livestock farmers, totaling nearly 5,000 ha of pasture area. For the future, it is projected that by 2025 the project will have at least 12,000,000 ha of land with regenerative activities supported by the carbon project throughout Colombia’s agricultural frontier. The project aims to reduce yearly 22,293 t CO2, leading to a total amount of 445,870 tCO2 during the life span of the project (20 years).

name: VICTOR GRAEFF LANDFILL GAS PROJECT
project_type: Energy industries (renewable/non-renewable sources); Waste handling and disposal
description: The proposed VCS project activity titled “Victor Graeff Landfill Gas Project” encompasses the promotion of collection and destruction/utilization of landfill gas (LFG) (rich in methane) through collection LFG and its destruction in high temperature enclosed flare(s) and utilization as gaseous fuel in set of engine-generator sets of an electricity generation infrastructure (with final total combined nameplate installed capacity of 1 MW).

name: Fujian Wuyishan Adjusted Water Management in Rice Cultivation
project_type: Agriculture Forestry and Other Land Use
description: The project to change rice planting from continuous flooding to intermittent flooding was carried out in Wuyishan City, Nanping City, Fujian Province, with a single season rice planting area of 10,492 hectares. Without this project providing ditches to conduct intermittent flooded method, the continuously flooded method would be continued, so the scenario  that  rice  was cultivated by continuously flooded method is the baseline scenario. Since the organic matter in rice soil under flooded condition can emit a large amount of methane (CH4) because of anaerobic decomposition, the intermittent flooded method is more beneficial to water conservation, production increase and methane emission removal than the continuously flooded.

name: PRODUCTION OF CONCRETE WITH CO2 CAPTURE AND CEMENT REDUCTION
description: Carbon Limit is a new company developing a type of concrete that uses substantially less cement than conventional concrete and also contains a mix of materials that absorbs CO2 during the production process and throughout the life of the concrete.  Concrete made with this technology captures CO2 directly from the air and mineralizes it into the concrete.

name: Henan Luoning Afforestation Project
developer: Guizhou Qianhe Carbon Technology Co., Ltd
project_type: Agriculture Forestry and Other Land Use
description: Henan Luoning Afforestation Project (hereafter referred as “the project”) is located in Luoning County, Luoyang City, Henan Province, China. The project is to establish forest on the barren land and wastelands to generate GHG emission reductions and contribute to local sustainable development. Prior to the project implementation, all the project sites are barren land in the hills and wastelands, without its implementation, all the sites will keep the same circumstances with no natural renewal and reforestation. The project start date is 01-04-2020 when the planting started, and the project covers 23,574.53 ha of forest was established by direct planted on barren land in the hills and wastelands in Luoning County, Luoyang City, Henan Province.

name: TOHMA Biomass Power Plant
description:
TOHMA Biomass Power Plant project (hereafter referred to as the project activity) is a biogas to-energy project that generates renewable energy (electricity) by using biogas obtained from anaerobic digestion of animal manure. Animal manure collected from multiple animal farm is treated in anerobic digester and the biogas produced is utilized in cogeneration unit for thermal and electric energy generation. Whereas the generated electricity is fed to the national grid of Turkey, thermal energy is used internally for to meet up the process requirement (warming of the digestor).
The project is being implemented by TOHMA Biyogas Enerji Limited Şirketi, as the Project Owner, in Yeşilyurt/Bindal district, Malatya province, in Turkey.

name: Isorka: Electric Vehicle Charging in Iceland
description:
This project is developed by Ísorka Ltd. and Súrefni kolefnisjöfnun Ltd. under the VCS methodology VM0038, Methodology for Electric Vehicle (EV) Charging Stations v1.0. The methodology outlines the procedure to calculate Greenhouse Gas (GHG) emissions, and issue credits for the development and use of EV charging infrastructure and their EV applicable fleets. 

The project activity includes EV charging stations that are utilised to charge EV applicable electric fleets. The existing scenario is the usage of conventional fossil fuel Light-Duty Vehicles (LDV). Thus, the project activities deliver electricity as an alternative to displace the use of fossil fuels resulting in the abatement of GHG emissions.

The project includes an initial number of EV charging stations that will progressively add additional chargers for registration in accordance to applicability conditions. The project proponent will provide an inventory of all EV charging stations in addition to this document. 

The program is envisaged to reduce on an average around 33215.7 tonnes of CO2e/year and 332157 tonnes of CO2e over 10 years of the crediting period. The Baseline Emissions and estimated GHG reduction are calculated using the total amount of Kwh of electricity sold in Project Year 1 (2021) and Project Year 2 (2022), with further estimations for the following years, 50% increase from Year 3-10, and 35% increase from Year 8-10.

name: Grouped Sustainable Agroforestry Project
project_type: Agriculture Forestry and Other Land Use
description:
ClimeTrek Limited (hereinafter referred as ClimeTrek) and GKF Agroforestry (P) Limited (hereinafter referred as GKF) are proposing a Grouped Agroforestry Afforestation, Reforestation and Revegetation (ARR) project in fallows agricultural, and wastelands owned by individual farmers and communities with low plant cover (hereinafter referred as project activity), located in the geographical boundary of India.
The project activity is a grouped project where various horticultural tree species including fruit bearing tree species, commercial tree species and shrubs will be planted. During the first three years, around 31,984 Ha will be planted in the first project instances covering States of Andhra Pradesh and Telangana; the potential land available within the project region for future project instances reaches whole of India. All project instances within this grouped project activity will consist of Agroforestry projects across India.
Based on ex-ante estimates the project will sequester around 4.02 million tonnes of CO2e over 30-years (tree/ shrub biomass carbon and soil carbon).
The overall objective grouped project activity is to mitigate climate change while contributing to sustainable environmental management, community development and poverty alleviation of farmers in India. The grouped project activity is to utilize the fallows agricultural and wastelands by establishing agroforestry systems consisting of both forest trees and fruit trees.
The additional trees in the landscape will enhance the wildlife habit value and biodiversity. In addition, the soil water storage capacity will increase, and soil erosion will be reduced. Consequently, the climate change resilience of the land use systems, related to droughts, will be increased.
These activities will significantly contribute to livelihood improvement through creation of employment and improved food and nutrition security. The establishment of forest and fruit trees will increase carbon sinks hence more carbon

name: Timor-Leste Improved Cookstoves and Community Development Project
description: The Project involves in the implementation of energy efficient cookstoves or improved cooking stoves (ICS). It intends to reduce harmful emissions, especially indoor air emissions, while also providing the economic, health, local environment and quality of lives of the communities involved.

name: SeaGraze™ Deployment Project - Early Adopters For Radical Methane Reduction
project_type: Livestock, enteric fermentation, and manure management
description: Symbrosia's natural seaweed feed additive, SeaGraze™, reduces enteric methane emissions in ruminants by 80%. SeaGraze™ is made from the red seaweed Asparagopsis taxiformis (A. taxiformis). 9 peer-reviewed studies from institutions including The Commonwealth Scientific and Industrial Research Organisation (CSIRO), UC Davis, and Penn State University have shown that replacing just 0.4% of a cow’s feed with A. taxiformis can reduce the amount of methane the cow produces by up to 98%. During this project, Symbrosia will collaborate with producers, academic researchers, and corporate partners throughout the United States to integrate SeaGraze™ into the diet of beef and dairy cattle and closely monitor the reduction of enteric methane emissions that is created. Initial project instances will be livestock operations located in Hawaii, California, and Oregon. Prior to the implementation of this project, in the baseline scenario, none of these operations supply any methane-reducing feed additive to their livestock. During the seven years of the project’s first crediting period, the project is expected to generate an average of 141,121 tonnes of CO2e reduction per year.

name: NEC AND SAKYU IFM -THE 1ST PILOT FOR FSC FOREST IN JAPAN-
project_type: Agriculture Forestry and Other Land Use
description:
This project is being conducted in Miyagi, Japan by Sakyu Corporation. The geographical coordinates of the project are 38.67769, 141.43124 (Asahidate), 38.67559, 141.40869 (Nashinokiyama), 38.65726, 141.4349 (Uchiyama) with a total area of 14.63 ha, protecting forests in the target area that were previously harvested for commercial timber (The forest management will be improved in the form of protecting the forest in the target area, which was previously harvested for commercial timber (applying methodology VM0010).
Prior to implementation of the project activities, trees in the target area were harvested for commercial timber in accordance with the forest management plan approved by Miyagi Prefecture. With the implementation of the project activities, trees in the target area will be converted into a protected forest to reduce GHG emissions.
Over the 20-year period, GHG emissions are reduced by 4,988 tCO2e, with an average annual emission reduction of 249 tCO2e and a VCU net of buffers of approximately 4,539 tCO2e over 20 years.

name: Guizhou Feitian 21 & Miluo & Mayixi CMM Power Generation Project
description:
Guizhou Feitian 21 & Miluo & Mayixi CMM Power Generation Project (hereinafter referred to as the Project) involves three power plants which utilize low concentration coal mine methane (CMM) for power generation to supply electricity to the coal mines and to China Southern Power Grid (CSPG) if there is any electricity surplus. Feitian 21 power plant is located in Shaopu town, Zhijin County, Bijie City, Guizhou province, while Miluo and Mayixi power plants respectively located in Miluo township, Shuicheng District, Liupanshui City, Guizhou Province and Dashan town, Panzhou City, Liupanshui City, Guizhou Province, China.
The purpose of the Project is to utilize the extracted CMM with low concentration methane concentration to produce electricity. No coal bed methane (CBM) or ventilation air methane (VAM) utilization is involved.
The emissions reduction of the Project comes from two sources: 1) Methane (CH4) emissions as a result of the previously vented gas that will be captured and destroyed in the project scenario; 2) CO2 emissions from the production of the equivalent amount of electricity replaced by the Project that would otherwise have been purchased from the CSPG.

name: Henan Mengjin CMM Power Generation Project
developer: Mengjin Branch of Henan Qingtian New Energy Co., Ltd.
description:

The Project is located in Yuanzhuang Village, Hengshui town, Mengjin County, Luoyang City, Henan Province, China.
The purpose of the Project is to utilize the extracted CMM with low concentration methane concentration to produce electricity. No coal bed methane (CBM) or ventilation air methane (VAM) utilization is involved. The emissions reduction of the Project comes from two sources: 1) Methane (CH4) emissions as a result of the previously vented gas that will be captured and destroyed in the project scenario; 2) CO2 emissions from the production of the equivalent amount of electricity replaced by the Project that would otherwise have been purchased from the CCPG.

name: GIRUÁ LANDFILL GAS PROJECT
project_type: Energy industries (renewable/non-renewable sources); Waste handling and disposal
description: The proposed VCS project activity titled “Giruá Landfill Gas Project” encompasses the promotion of collection and destruction/utilization of landfill gas (LFG) (rich in methane) through collection LFG and its destruction in high temperature enclosed flare(s) and utilization as gaseous fuel in set of engine-generator sets of an electricity generation infrastructure (with final total combined nameplate installed capacity of 1 MW).

name: Sequoia Improved cookstoves grouped project
description:
The grouped project aims to provide individuals with intermediate improved cookstove (ICS). The stoves will be commercialized into several countries in Africa, starting with Togo as a first instance. Stoves will be distributed for free. 
The ICS distributed through this project will encourage households to replace the prevailing inefficient three-stone fireplace or traditional charcoal cookstoves such as charcoal clay cookers and charcoal iron stoves that are predominantly used across the region. The ICS provides for an efficient use of the thermal energy generated though the combustion of biomass while cooking and there is a more efficient transfer of this thermal energy to the cooking pot. There is thus a resultant reduction in both biomass consumption and greenhouse gas emissions.
In addition to the reduction of biomass consumption (and associated reduction in expenses to purchase wood or charcoal – or reduction in time gathering firewood), there will also be an economic benefit in that the ICS will be produced locally in the region and will create jobs which will have a large proportion of female employees.

name: Shine I – Distribution of LED Lightbulbs in South India
developer: C-Quest Capital SG India LED Private Limited
description:
The proposed small-scale grouped project (henceforth referred to as SHINE I – South India) involves distribution of Light Emitting Diodes (LEDs) to rural and peri urban households for domestic lighting in South Indian states of Tamil Nadu and North Telangana.

According to CEA’s (Central Electricity Authority) Load Generation Balance Report 2022-23, actual demand supply gap in the Southern region was -0.4% while the peak deficit was 3.2% during the year 2021-22. Trend shows that there has been a steady increase in peak demand in South while supply has not been able to match up to this demand. This grouped project could have a positive impact on the demand supply gap by introducing energy efficient light bulbs thereby reducing peak hour demand of power in residential areas.

developer: C-Quest Capital SG India LED Private Limited

name: INEGOL INTEGRATED SOLID WASTE STORAGE AND DISPOSAL FACILITY
project_type: Energy industries (renewable/non-renewable sources); Waste handling and disposal
description: The project is located in Bursa Province, İnegöl District, Yeniyörük Mahallesi, Körkuyu. The project İnegöl Integrated Solid Waste Landfill and Disposal Facility (Mechanical Separation Facility, Waste Derived Fuel Preparation Facility and Biomethanization Facility) is operated by Doğu Star Elektrik Üretim A.Ş. The Project Activity includes the Mechanical Separation Facility, the Refused Drive Fuel (RDF) preparation facility, and the Biomethanization Facility, which operates in integration with the existing solid waste landfill facility (SWDS). Within the scope of the project, it is planned to manage the municipal wastes, produce electricity with biogas and produce RDF fuel. The start date of the project activity is considered as 31-December-2020, which is the provisional acceptance date of the first gas engine. Project is estimated to produce 1,616,784 tCO2e net emission reduction over the 7 year crediting period. This project has contributed to the following goals: • Reduction in fossil fuel use (imported or local) by using renewable energy resources. • Displacement of ecologically unsound and climate unfriendly power generation • Extension of nationally sourced power generation. • Improvement of environmental conditions (GHG and odour) and safety in the landfill area • Increase the lifespan of İnegöl SWDS by utilizing biodegradable fraction of MSW more efficiently.

name: Armatec Animal Manure Methane Recovery and Utilization Plant
description:
Armatec Animal Manure Methane Recovery and Utilization Plant (hereafter referred to as the Project) is a biogas-to-energy project that captures biogas from animal manure -via anaerobic digestion- and utilizes it to generate thermal and electric energy through cogeneration units. The animal manure is collected from the neighbouring animal farms with special trucks and transferred to the biogas plant. Continuously stirred tank reactor (CSTR) type anaerobic digesters are used to capture methane-rich biogas. Biogas is then utilized in cogeneration units for heat and electricity generation. The thermal energy is utilized only for heating anaerobic fermenters. The generated electricity is both used for internal electricity requirement and supplied to the national grid. 
The project is being implemented by Armatec Enerji ve İnşaat Limited Şirketi, as the project owner, Çobanlar district, Afyonkarahisar province, in Turkey, whilst the project start date is determined as June 29, 2021.
The project adopts the renewable crediting period of 7 years, twice renewable for a total of 21 years. The estimated average net annual emission reductions are 172,770 tCO2eq/y. Accordingly, the project is expected to generate 1,209,390 tCO2eq/y emissions reduction during the first crediting period.

name: Guizhou Jinsha CMM Power Generation Project
developer: Jinsha Yonder Southwest New Energy Development Co., Ltd.
description: Guizhou Jinsha CMM Power Generation Project (hereinafter referred to as the Project) is located in Taoyuan community, Liutang town, Jinsha County, Bijie City, Guizhou Province, China. The purpose of the Project is to utilize the extracted CMM with low concentration methane concentration to produce electricity. No coal bed methane (CBM) or ventilation air methane (VAM) utilization is involved. Twenty sets of CMM power generators are installed with a total installed capacity of 18MW, destroying 27.2 million m3 of methane annually. After the full operation of the Project, the expected annual exported electricity is 94,656 MWh, which is supplied to the coal mine through the electricity distribution network in Guiyuan coal mine area, and to China Southern Power Grid (CSPG) if there is any electricity surplus, replacing the electricity that would otherwise have been purchased from the CSPG and displace part of the electricity generated by CSPG dominated by fossil fuel-fired power plants. The emissions reduction of the Project comes from two sources: 1) Methane (CH4) emissions as a result of the previously vented gas that will be captured and destroyed in the project scenario; 2) CO2 emissions from the production of the equivalent amount of electricity replaced by the Project that would otherwise have been purchased from the CSPG.

name: Barutçuoğlu Landfill Gas to Electricity Power Plant
developer: Barutçuoğlu İnşaat Sanayi ve Ticaret Limited Şirketi
project_type: Energy industries (renewable/non-renewable sources); Waste handling and disposal
description:
The project activity includes capture and utilization of landfill gas (landfill gas (LFG) contains approximately 50% methane and is a potent greenhouse gas (GHG)) for power generation, that would have been vented to the atmosphere in the pre-project/business as usual scenario. The landfill site is estimated to receive around 126 thousand tons of municipal solid waste (MSW) annually during 2021 followed by annual increment in receipt of waste quantity and is expected to reach around 152 thousand tons by the end of first crediting period (2028). About 59.58% of this waste consists of organic materials such as pulp, paper and cardboard, and food waste.
The technology measures deployed under the project activity includes covering of landfill area, landfill gas capture unit, and gas engine. Gas engine with an installed capacity of 2.906 MWm/2.828 MWe1 utlises collected landfill gas for power generation. Electricity generated is fed to the National Grid of Turkey. The electricity generating unit was commissioned on May 26th, 2021 and is regarded as the project start date2.

name: Anhua LFG Power Generation Project
developer: Anhua Yuanjing Environmental Protection Technology Co. LtD.
project_type: Energy industries (renewable/non-renewable sources); Waste handling and disposal
description:
Anhua LFG Power Generation Project (hereinafter referred to as the project) is located at Anhua MSW Landfill, Yanzhu village, Dongping Town, Anhua County, Yiyang City, Hunan province, P.R China. The purpose of the project is to utilize landfill gas (LFG), which consists mainly of methane, for electricity generation. It includes LFG collection system, LFG pre-treatment system, flaring and electricity generation system. LFG collected will be used for electricity generation with internal combustion generators. The total installed capacity will be 3 MW included four generators with each 0.5 MW and one generator with 1 MW.
In absence of the project, equivalent amount of electricity exported to the grid by the project would have otherwise been supplied by CCPG. Greenhouse gas (GHG) emissions will be reduced by avoiding CO2 emissions from those fossil fuel-based power plants connected to the grid and by avoiding GHG emissions from releasing LFG into atmosphere at the landfill site.

name: LA GIOIA CARBON FARMING IN NORTHERN ITALY
project_type: Agriculture Forestry and Other Land Use
description:
La Gioia farm is located in La Gioia, Alessandria in Northern Italy. The coordinates are attached as a KML file.  Several agricultural practices will be implemented or modified on the land. Taken together, the goal is to reduce the carbon emissions currently emitted by this farm and raise the carbon stored in the soil. In addition, the selected measures will contribute to improving crop yields and soil health. 

To do so, the following methods will be applied on site; Reduction of the inorganic fertilizer application, change of irrigation system, Incorporation of crops residues into the soil, Tillage reduction, Cover crop implementation, Reduction of the fossil fuel use, Switch from crops to woody biomass

The sectoral scope 14 – Agriculture Forestry and Other Land Use (AFOLU) is applicable to the project. Within this sector, this project has been developed under the scope of the methodology for improved agricultural land management (VM0042 VCS methodology).

The project has been found eligible under the scope of the VCS program as it meets all requirements established by the program. 

The crediting period chosen for this project is of 25 years, renewable 4 times. The period lasts from the 01/06/22 to the 1/6/2047. We estimated that 211,7 tCO2/year will be stored in the soil or not emitted.

name: RESTORATION OF HOMESTEAD LAND OF POOR RURAL COMMUNITIES IN ASSAM & MEGHALAYA
project_type: Agriculture Forestry and Other Land Use
description: The proposed Afforestation, Reforestation and Revegetation (ARR) VCS project in the districts  of these two states, aims at bringing sustainable development of the local communities contributing to the whole carbon offset mitigation by restoring 9000 Ha. of farmland. The area will be treated with plantations in Kamrup and Goalpara districts in the state of Assam and Ri Bhoi district in the state of Meghalaya. The project aims to improve its agriculture practices by incorporating crop diversification, inter-cropping, progressive reduction in the use of synthetic chemicals and further replacing it with organic compost like vermiwash, handikhatta, jibaamrit, etc while setting up composting units to promote the recycling of biomass.

name: SANTA MARIA LANDFILL GAS PROJECT

name: ITVR SAO LEOPOLDO LANDFILL GAS PROJECT

As per its project description, combustion of collected LFG occurs in high temperature enclosed flare(s). Power generation from Landfill Gas is predicted to occur in 2023.

name: Elmadag Biogas Power Plant
project_type: Energy industries (renewable/non-renewable sources); Waste handling and disposal
description: Elmadag Biogas Power Plant (hereafter referred to as the Project) is a biogas-to-energy project that involves methane capture through anaerobic digestion and utilization of methane for thermal energy and electricity generation via cogeneration units. The animal manure is collected from the neighbouring animal farms with vacuum trucks and transferred to the biogas plant. Continuously Stirred Tank Reactor (CSTR) type anaerobic digesters are used to capture methane-rich biogas. Biogas is then utilized in cogeneration units for heat and electricity generation. The thermal energy is utilized for heating anaerobic fermenters. The generated electricity is both used for internal electricity requirements and supplied to the national grid.  The project is being implemented by ABRAK ENERJİ ELEKTRİK ÜRETİM ANONİM ŞİRKETİ, the Project Owner, in Elmadağ district, Ankara province, in Turkey. This project adopts the renewable crediting period of 7 years, twice renewable for a total of 21 years. The estimated average net annual emission reductions are 32,858 tCO2eq/y. Accordingly, the project is expected to generate 238,008 tCO2eq/y emissions reduction during the first crediting period.

name: Enteric fermentation emissions' reduction program of Uruguay
project_type: Livestock, enteric fermentation, and manure management
description:
“Enteric fermentation emissions‘ reduction program of Uruguay” is taken place in a country where livestock farming covers a total area of 12,9 million hectares which represents 70% of the total national area (DIEA, 2021). This sector accounts for 57% of national net emissions, of which more than half correspond to methane emissions from enteric fermentation of livestock. This project will comprise approximately 100,000 animals per year, starting with a feedlot of 1,500 animals. In this system animals enter a feedlot with a weight of 415 kg and finish after 110 days with 590 kg. The breeds involved in the feedlot systems are Angus, Hereford and their crossbreeds.
The project will result in a reduction of methane emissions from enteric fermentation in beef cattle and dairy cows by providing a natural additive of composed by essential oils, flavonoids, and tannins: Anavrin. Anavrin® is a product that has been tested in recent years at the universities of Milan, Sassari, Santa Maria in Brazil, and at the Faculty of Veterinary Medicine of UdelaR in Uruguay. In addition, tests have been carried out in other parts of the world, where it was highlighted that the correct use of Anavrin® also improves the animal's daily production, around 70 g, and 1,5 l daily milk gain per capita. This a grouped project that starts with a farm located in the department of “Flores” near its capital city, The project start date is 1st April 2022. New instances (farmers) will be part of the project, benefiting from the use of the product itself but also from the generation of carbon credits, which will be seen as a reduction of the purchase price of the product. In 10 years, the project will be generating 100.000 tCO2, based on the preliminary estimations done by yet to be published papers. The project will monitor the emissions reductions according to VM0041 methodology by direct measurements.

name: Household Biogas Project in Madhya Pradesh & Jharkhand
description: The purpose of the project is to replace the commonly used inefficient wood fired mud stoves technology, with clean, sustainable, and efficient biogas. Each household utilizes cattle dung to feed the digester to produce biogas for cooking purpose. This leads to reduction of greenhouse gas emissions by displacing conventionally used non-renewable biomass with renewable biogas and reduction of greenhouse gas emissions related to animal manure which is left to decay anaerobically. In addition, the hygienic conditions in the rural areas will be improved by an appropriate disposal of waste. Further, residue from the bio digesters can be used as organic fertilizer for land application. Project activity will contribute towards sustainable development by replacing non-renewable source of energy with biogas generated from the biodigesters. The Project is operational in India in the rural areas of Madhya Pradesh and Jharkhand.

name: Installation of high efficiency cookstoves in Sub Saharan Africa by BURN
description:
The purpose of this Grouped project “Installation of high efficiency cookstoves in Sub Saharan Africa by BURN” by BURN Manufacturing Co. is to reduce the rate of deforestation in the remote areas of Sub-Saharan Africa along with indoor air pollution. The project will reduce the time spent by women in collecting fuel wood from large distances. 
Approximately, 3.2 million people die every year prematurely from illness attributable to the household air pollution caused by the inefficient use of fuels for cooking . 
Only 18% of population in Sub Saharan Africa have access to clean cooking fuel technology.  The Improved (ICS) cookstoves has a better combustion process due to which indoor air pollution along with GHG emissions is significantly reduced compared to traditional three stone cooking method. The beneficiaries will be the households in 9 countries of sub-Saharan Africa namely Kenya, Somalia, DRC, Mozambique, Tanzania, Senegal, Ghana, Nigeria, and Ivory Coast. The geographical location of the project is the above mentioned 9 countries.
The baseline scenario is continued use of traditional method of open fire or three stone cookstoves using firewood as fuel in rural areas and charcoal as fuel in urban, semi-urban areas to meet the energy demand for cooking purposes.
This Grouped project deploys highly efficient Improved cook stove (ICS) models, known as ‘Jikokoas’ and ‘Kuniokoas’ reducing charcoal and woody biomass consumption for urban, semi-urban and rural households in the 9 countries mentioned in section 1.12 respectively

name: Community-based Mangrove Restoration Initiative – Lep Lep
project_type: Agriculture Forestry and Other Land Use
description:
The objective of this project is to restore degraded mangrove sites in Kafoutine in Senegal. The project will create a healthy mangrove ecosystem in degraded lands.
The components of the project are reforestation, providing important ecosystem services, climate change mitigation, socio-economic improvements, and active participation of the local community.
Under this grouped project degraded mangroves are restored and enriched. In the first project activity, up to 1.9 million mangroves will be planted in an area of 750 ha, starting in 2023. The species selected for this reforestation project are indigenous and local, namely Rhizophora mangle and Avicennia germinans.
Training and awareness-raising of the local communities are crucial for the success for the project. From the start of the project, stakeholders potentially affected by the project have been involved in the process. This included providing information on all project activities and teaching basics on forest management, monitoring, forest protection activities, climate change, and carbon sequestration. Depending on the given conditions, up to 3,500 seedlings per hectare will planted. The project will sequestrate an estimated 355,000 tCO2 in the 750 ha over a period of 20 years.
The empowerment of the communities is central to the project. The labor requirement for the project will be fulfilled with local employment. Therefore, most of the budget for labor and an additional 50/50 share of carbon credit revenues will remain in the country. The project will promote a working family model where more than 50% of women can actively participate in the project.
Mangrove restoration will further increase fish populations and improve biodiversity. To measure the positive impact on biodiversity, annual biomonitoring will be conducted using eDNA.
Over the 20-year period, the project team will create a healthy mangrove ecosystem, improve the socio-economic status of the community, and foster climate change mitigation.

name: Hubei Badong IFM (conversion of logged to protected forest) Project
project_type: Agriculture Forestry and Other Land Use
description:
The Hubei Badong IFM (conversion of logged to protected  forest) Project (hereafter “the project activity”) is implemented in Badong County, Enshi Tujia and Miao Autonomous Prefecture, Hubei Province of China by Hubei Yangfan Tourism Development Co., Ltd and Guangzhou Guotan Assets Management Co., Ltd, the geo-coordinate of the  project proponent is 110°04'E -110°32'E and 30°28'N - 31°28'N, the total area is 3348.75km2, which includes the Improved Forest Management (IFM) of the forests in the conversion of logged to protected forest.
The area of the project activity is 6584.77 ha, including 875 subcompartments spreading over Chadianzi Town, Dazhiping Town, Dongrangkou Town, Guandukou Town, Lvcongpo Town, Qingtaiping Town, Xinling Town, Shuibuya Town, Yanduhe Town, Yesanguan Town, Jinguoping Township, Xiqiuwan Township, Bashan Forest Farm of Hubei Badong. All these forests are state-owned forests or privately-owned or collective-owned, and have the legal right to forest ownership. The species involved in the project are all native species and the species involved in the project are Chinese Fir, Coniferous Broad Mix and Coniferous Mix.
Before the implementation of the project activity, the trees are logged based on a valid and verifiable government-approved timber management plan for harvesting the project area. The implementation of the project activity converses the trees to protected forest to reduce the GHG emissions for about 706,125 tCO2e in 20 years, the average annual emission reduction is 35,306 tCO2e and Verified Carbon Units with buffer deduction is about 557,829 tCO2e in 20 years, and average annual VCUs with buffer deduction is 27,891 tCO2e.
The project activity will contribute to the environment (biodiversity conservation, rocky desertification prevention and soil erosion control), thus contribute to sustainable development.

name: EMPOWERING COMMUNITIES THROUGH IMPROVED COOKSTOVES
description:
This project aims to reduce carbon emissions and other greenhouse gases by distributing our fuel-efficient, improved wood burning cookstoves (ICS) to rural households in West Africa. These will replace far less fuel-efficient three-stone fires. 

Cookstoves are manufactured in rural Togo, providing infrastructure, economic growth, and employment for the local community.  

The project aims to reduce the time burden of cooking and collecting firewood, which disproportionately falls to women. By reducing the amount of wood required for cooking, women will have more time to spend on educational and income-generating activities.

By providing a family with a fuel efficient cookstove, the indoor air pollution within their home will be reduced, improving health conditions and reducing smoke related illnesses. 

Alongside reducing the amount of GHG in the atmosphere, the reduced need for wood for cooking will help stop rapidly progressing deforestation. 

The project will work towards 8 sustainable development goals creating environmental, health and economic benefits for the end users as well as more employment especially for women.

name: Improved Cookstove Distribution by Climate Detox Private Limited - Phase III
description:
The project's goal is to supply improved cook stove (ICS) in the rural areas of the Indian state of Rajasthan. ICS is an innovative cookstove that uses less fuel. The emissions of greenhouse gases will be decreased if improved cook stoves are used for daily cooking. The initiative will replace the conventional cook stove, which is mostly utilized in rural communities and uses a significant amount of wood to prepare food. The ICS is built with a remarkably high thermal efficiency, which will result in a minimal need for fuel wood use and less greenhouse gas emissions.
The project activity will have a good effect on the rural residents' daily lives and health. It has been demonstrated that ICS produces less smoke, which will lessen the respiratory health problems that result from using a conventional cookstove. On the other hand, ICS recipients will spend less time gathering firewood, and they will use that time to care for their families, children, and other productive tasks. Additionally, because the cookstove is completely enclosed, users and their families will be in a safer environment. The baseline scenario assumes that in the absence of project activities, the target population will continue to use non-renewable wood fuel to satisfy thermal energy needs comparable to those met by project cookstoves.  The project participant intends to distribute 50,000 Improved Cook Stoves in India's rural areas as part of this project activity. The project will remove 368,478 tCO2e of greenhouse gases on average each year. The project participants for this project are Climate Detox Pvt Ltd. And Siddhant Energy Consultants. Under the direction of a prepared team, ICS will be distributed in rural areas.

name: Guangdong Huaiji IFM (conversion  of  logged  to  protected  forest)  Project
developer: Huaiji County Weizhou Construction Investment and Development Group Co., Ltd
project_type: Agriculture Forestry and Other Land Use
description:
The Guangdong Huaiji IFM (conversion of logged to protected forest) Project (hereafter “the project activity”) is implemented in Huaiji County, Guangdong Province of China by Huaiji County Weizhou Construction Investment and Development Group Co., Ltd, the geo-coordinate of the project is 23°28′07″N～24°23′30″N, 110°52′09″E～112°30′49″E, the total area is 355,661.39 ha, which includes the Improved Forest Management (IFM) of the forests in the conversion of logged to protected forest.
The area of the project activity is 14,870.98 ha, including 3,561 subcompartments. All these forests are state-owned forests or privately-owned forests or collective-owned forests, and have the legal right to forest ownership. All the owners authorized the project proponent to access the project to their behalf. The species involved in the project are Pinus massoniana, Chinese Fir and Pinus elliottii. The forest of the project was older plantations under managing. The age of Pinus Massoniana was 20-31, Chinese Fir was 21-39, Pinus Elliottii was 21-38. Before the implantation of the project, the usual type of management was clearcutting.
Before the implementation of the project activity, the trees are logged based on a valid and verifiable government-approved timber management plan for harvesting the project area. The implementation of the project activity converses the trees to protected forest to reduce the GHG emissions for about 2,123,753 tCO2e in 20 years, the average annual emission reduction is 106,187 tCO2e and Verified Carbon Units with buffer deduction is about 1,635,281 tCO2e in 20 years, and average annual VCUs with buffer deduction is 81,764 tCO2e.
The project activity will contribute to the environment (biodiversity conservation, rocky desertification prevention and soil erosion control), thus contribute to sustainable development.

name: Xinfeng AWMS GHG Mitigation Project in Liaoning province
description: The common practice for the swine farm owners to manage the manure is to have uncovered anaerobic lagoons/ponds at their farms in the region. i.e., Prior to the implementation of the project, the animal manure waste was left to decay in uncovered open lagoon and methane is emitted to the atmosphere directly without any methane recovery and destruction facility. In China, the uncovered anaerobic lagoons are a manure treatment method recognized by the state1. In addition, since there is no legal regulation to mandate the farm owners to implement anaerobic digestion, aerobic or other biological treatment techniques and to capture and/or utilize methane generated at these lagoons, therefore the continue of this common practice to treatment the manure i.e., uncovered anaerobic lagoons is the most economic, viable and reasonable for livestock farm owners.

name: Fangchenggang Mangrove afforestation project
developer: Fangchenggang Xinggang Agricultural Development Co., Ltd
project_type: Agriculture Forestry and Other Land Use
description: Fangchenggang Mangrove Afforestation Project is located in Gangkou District and Fangcheng District of Fangchenggang City, Guangxi Zhuang Autonomous Region, China. The purpose of the project is to increase carbon sequestration and contribute to local sustainable development by planting mangroves in degraded mangrove habitats. The project proponent is Fangchenggang Xinggang Agricultural Development Co., Ltd.The purpose of the project is to restore the degraded local mangrove ecosystem and increase forest cover by planting a variety of species of native mangrove, and establish a healthy local ecological and economic system by involving residents in the implementation of the projects directly. Totally 221.9 ha of mangroves have been planted with 5 native mangrove species (such as Avicennia marina, Kandelia candel, Aegiceras corniculatum, Rhizophora stylosa, Bruguiera gymnorrhiza). The implementation of the afforestation project will generate GHG emission removals, improve the local environment, enhance the capabilities of local communities and residents by providing them with relevant technical skills. In addition, the project has restored the degraded mangrove ecosystem and increased forest coverage, provided a suitable habitat for animals, especially for endangered birds which mainly live in mangroves. The project is estimated to generate GHG emission removals of 111,592 tCO2e in 40 years, with an average annual GHG emission removal of 2,789.8tCO2e.

name: Yangxiang AWMS GHG Mitigation Project in Hebei province
description: Yangxiang AWMS GHG Mitigation Project in Hebei province (hereinafter as “the proposed project”) locates in Xingtai City, Xingtai City and Hengshui City, Hebei province, China. name: FUTURE GREEN CARBON PROJECT
project_type: Agriculture Forestry and Other Land Use
description:
Future Green Carbon Project is an AFOLU initiative to be implemented in the Central West
region of Brazil, specifically in the state of Mato Grosso do Sul (MS). It is a voluntary action of
Eldorado Brasil Celulose S/A, aiming at the reforestation of more than
100,000 hectares with new and additional eucalyptus plantations , established exclusively on
non forested and anthropized areas . In addition to the creation of carbon stocks through
reforestation activities for production purposes , the project will also enable the recovery and
conservation of carbon stocks based on native species for conservation purposes. Even tho ugh
the restoration of such areas will be enabled by the project, resulting in direct climate benefits,
VCUs will not be claimed for such activities.

name: Reforestation of land for multiple uses
project_type: Agriculture Forestry and Other Land Use
description:
The grouped project “Reforestation of land for multiple uses” is a voluntary action to promote
sustainable tree planting in the Central-West region of Brazil, specifically in the states of Mato
Grosso (MT), Mato Grosso do Sul (MS) and Goiás (GO), on non-forested lands. Its objective is to
generate net removal of greenhouse gases through converting traditional land use in the region
– e.g. non-forested/agricultural areas – into reforestation actions, based on the engagement of
investors and independent rural producers. Also, the project proposes the restoration of nonforested
lands with the purpose of enhancing carbon stocks of native vegetation, including
protected areas, i.e. Permanent Preservation Areas, Legal Reserves, and other
lands, as applicable to each case.

name: Youyang Water Management with Rice Cultivation
developer: Chongqing Gengfang Agricultural Development Co., Ltd.
project_type: Agriculture Forestry and Other Land Use
description:
The project is to change from continuously flooded regimes to intermittently flooded regimes during rice cultivation in Youyang County, Chongqing City, China, with a total acreage of 16,548 ha of single-cropping rice. A total of 8,533 households (36,351 farmers) were involved in the project. Without the project, local villagers would not have access to intermittently flooded technology and intact facilities to conduct the intermittently flooded method, the traditional continuously flooded method would be continued. The original scenario in which rice was cultivated by the continuously flooded method is the baseline scenario. Due to the anaerobic decomposition of organic matter in the paddy soil under flooded conditions, a large amount of methane can be released, so the intermittently flooded method is more conducive to water efficiency, improving rice yield and reducing methane emissions than the continuously flooded method.
The implementation activities of the project include promoting intermittently flooded technology, technical training for the farmers, facility repair and replacement, etc. According to the needs of rice growth, farmers use pumps and valves to control irrigation and drainage, which not only saves water resources but also reduces methane emissions from soil organic matter under anaerobic conditions. Through the pumps and valves, the necessary water can be supplied to the rice paddies in time in the dry season, and the excess water can be drained from the rice paddies in the rainy season.
The project is expected to reduce the GHG emissions by 365,337 tCO2e in the first seven-year period, with an average annual GHG emission reduction of 52,191 tCO2e. The project aims to reduce GHG and mitigate climate changes, increase rice productivity resulting in higher living standards for local farmers and provide more job opportunities.

name: Heyuan Qizhai Landfill Gas Power Generation Project
developer: Heyuan Zhengbo New Energy Development Co., Ltd.
project_type: Energy industries (renewable/non-renewable sources); Waste handling and disposal
description:
Heyuan Qizhai Landfill Gas Power Generation Project captures the landfill gas that would have been released to the atmosphere in the absence of the project and generates electricity with the landfill gas (LFG). The electricity is supplied to the China Southern Power Grid (CSPG) to replace the electricity generated from coal-fired power plants of CSPG. 
The purpose of the project is to use LFG, which consists mainly of methane, for electricity generation. It includes LFG collection system, LFG pre-treatment system and electricity generation system. The total installed capacity of the project is 3.6MW. The project consists of 3 sets of 1200kW generators which were operated since 16/11/2021. LFG collected is used for electricity generation with internal combustion generators to generate about 176,692MWh supplying to CSPG during the first 7 years crediting period. The expected average annual emission reductions are 133,215 tCO2e and the total emission reductions are 932,508 tCO2e during the first 7-year crediting period.

name: Vega-Hereko Istanbul Waste to Energy Project
project_type: Energy industries (renewable/non-renewable sources); Waste handling and disposal
description:
In order to develop a municipal solid waste management system that will be environmentally friendly and sustainable, Vega-Hereko Istanbul Waste to Energy Project is being implemented by Vega Hereko Enerji Üretim Sanayi ve Ticaret Anonim Şirketi. The project activity is a methane gas power generating plant with a license capacity of 18.012 MWe. 
The project was commissioned with the generation of electricity from April 3rd, 2021, which is regarded as the project start date. The project's lifetime is 16 years, according to the EMRA Generation License. Also, the facility has a mechanical separation plant with 9,000 tons/day capacity. The sorting facility distributes the waste into organics. The separated organic fraction is taken for controlled anaerobic digestion (biological treatment tanks) together with the organic waste received by the facility. The methane recovered from digestion will be combusted through gas engines and the electricity is fed into the grid. Main objective and aim of the project is to take the separated organic fraction to controlled anaerobic digestion process and recover methane from the organic waste. The methane recovered from digestion is combusted through gas engines and the electricity is fed into the grid. The wastewater is re-used in the digesters, then will be sent to ISTAC wastewater treatment plant near the project area. The project is located in In Karakiraz Village, Sile District, in Istanbul /Turkey. This project adopts a crediting period of 7 years. The expected average annual emission reductions are 320,042 tCO2eq/y. Accordingly, the project is expected to generate 2,240,299 tCO2eq emissions reduction throughout its first crediting period.
