name: Climate Action in Myanmar through a community-based Mangrove Restoration
project_type: Agriculture Forestry and Other Land Use
description: The proposed project is located in Bokpyin Township, Kawthong District, Tanintharyi Region, along Myanmar's 2800 km of coastline. Mangroves in the project region have been deteriorated at an alarming rate in recent decades due to overexploitation and other anthropogenic influences. Mangrove degradation has a negative impact on the sustainability of neighboring ecosystems as well as the social well-being of local inhabitants. As a result, Worldview International Foundation (WIF) planned to develop a project to restore degraded mangroves and stimulate socioeconomic development in the Tanintharyi coastal region. Objective of the project is to restore 12,000 ha of degraded mangrove areas in the region. The restoration areas under the project belong to Htaung Ka Met, Noet Ngwar, Han Ka Phyu and Kawt Ba Mar village tracts of Bokpyin Township in Kawthong District.

name: Amazon Guardians REDD+ Project
project_type: Agriculture Forestry and Other Land Use
description:
The growing threats to the forests of the Peruvian Amazon, such as migratory agriculture, land trafficking illegal logging and illegal gold mining, are causing the alarming degradation of forests; the loss and in some cases the disappearance of the most important flora and fauna in the territory; and the general pollution - deterioration of the country’s most valuable ecosystems. Specifically, illegal (gold) mining have caused tragic damage to part of the Peruvian Amazon. Rivers, streams and soils have been contaminated due to this cause to such degree that it will take many years to remediate and recover -to some extent- their initial state. One of the most affected areas in Peru in terms of deforestation, and specifically due to illegal mining, is the buffer zone of the Tambopata National Reserve and the forests located on the right bank (towards Cusco) of the Interoceanic highway in the region of Madre de Dios.

REDD+ Amazon Guardians purpose is to reduce and avoid deforestation within the conservation, reforestation/afforestation, and ecotourism forest concessions located in the buffer zone of the Tambopata National Reserve and adjacent areas which are highly threatened by illegal mining and traffickers who use these areas for illegal crops. REDD+ Amazon Guardians has been designed and developed with the purpose of protecting these valuable forests and their biodiversity, generating environmental services that allow the capture of CO2 and providing opportunities to improve the quality of life for the communities that live and depend on these areas. 

The project is implemented by Bosques Amazonicos SAC (BAM) in partnership with the concessionaire families in the area, grouped in the Federation of Concessionaires of Madre de Dios, FECOMAD.

name: TAIHE COUNTY BIOGAS POWER GENERATION AND ORGANIC FERTILIZER PROJECT
developer: Anhui United Venture Capital Renewable Energy Technology Co.,Ltd.
project_type: Energy industries (renewable/non-renewable sources); Waste handling and disposal
description: Taihe County Biogas Power Generation and Organic Fertilizer Project is located at ShuangXing Village, Shuang fu Town, Taihe County, Fuyang City, Anhui Province, China.This project builds a new livestock and poultry manure management system and collects organic wastes such as manure from many farms to produce biogas power generation and organic fertilizer. Fermentation raw materials are managed by unified collection and transportation. Agricultural waste resources (ie, livestock and poultry wastes in this project) undergo pretreatment and anaerobic fermentation, and the generated biogas is desulfurized and then enters the generator to generate electricity. The waste heat of the generator is used to increase the temperature of the material in the homogenization tank and the fermentation tank. The mud produced by anaerobic fermentation is transported to the nearby farmland through the pipeline network to form an organic ecological cycle industry. The residue is used to produce solid organic fertilizer. The electricity generated is fed into the East China grid, reducing methane and other greenhouse gas emissions. It also avoids the CO2 emissions generated by the power generation process corresponding to the replacement of electricity, thereby achieving greenhouse gas emission reduction.The project activity will reduce GHG in the atmosphere through avoiding methane emissions from anaerobic treatment of manure. The project adopts a 10-year fixed crediting period, It is estimated that 62,834 tCO2e emission reductions will be generated annually and total emission reductions are 628,338 t CO2e in the crediting period.

name: Giciye III Hydropower Project in Rwanda
description:
The project activity involves power generation from a 9.8 MW hydroelectric project on Giciye river located at Musneyi village, Nyagahondo Cell, Rugera Sector, Nyabihu District in Western Provide of Rwanda. The project activity is a run-of-river project being developed by RMT Energy Development Ltd. The project activity comprises 2 Numbers of vertical Pelton Turbines manufactured and supplied by Gugler, Austria each with a generator output capacity of 4,986.9 kW for generation of electricity. The project also comprises 2 sets of synchronous generator having capacity 5600KVA each manufactured and supplied by GAMESA, Spain.   
The project is allotted to the RMT Energy Development Ltd. on basis of design, develop, construct and operate for a period of 25 years. The generated electricity from the project activity will be supplied to grid under a long term (25 years) power purchase agreement signed with The Energy Utility Corporation Limited (EUCL). 
The purpose of the project activity is to produce renewable energy using hydro power and supply the generated electricity to national grid. In the absence of the project activity equivalent amount of electricity would have been generated by the operation of grid mix power plants. The Project activity thus reduces the anthropogenic emissions of greenhouse gases (GHGs) in to the atmosphere associated with the equivalent amount of electricity generation from the fossil fuel based grid connected power plant.

name: Adjusted Water Management in Rice Cultivation in Xionghe Town
developer: Hubei Jiangling County Agricultural Technology Extension Center
project_type: Agriculture Forestry and Other Land Use
description:
Xionghe Town is located in the central and southern part of Hubei Province, located in the hinterland of Jianghan Plain .The project is located in Xionghe Town,Jiangling County, Hubei Province, China, with a total acreage of 10058.55 ha for single-cropping rice. The project activity is designed to construction the cement ditch and reservoir to realize the reducing of methane emissions by conducting intermittently flooded method instead of continuously flooded method during the cropping season in Xionghe Town.
In the baseline scenario, farmers in Xionghe Town use continuously flooded method in rice paddies , which means fields have standing water throughout the rice growing season and only dry out for harvest. However, the organic matter in rice soil under flooded condition can emit a large amount of methane (CH4) because of anaerobic decomposition. In the project scenario, farmers in Xionghe Town changing from continuously flooded to intermittent flooded condition during rice cultivation. By controlled the irrigation and drainage according to the needs of rice growth, can save water resources. On the other hand, multiple aeration during rice cultivation can effectively reduce methane emissions from soil organic matter under anaerobic conditions.
Emission reductions of this project are generated by reducing methane emissions of continuously flooded during rice cultivation in baseline scenario. With the project activity, an estimated amount of GHG emission reduction 4.49 tCO2e/ha for rice is expected. Annual average estimation of GHG emission reductions from the project activity is 45,136 tCO2e/year, the total GHG emission reductions are 315,952 t CO2e in the first 7 years crediting period.

name: DRC REDD+ Carbon Credit Harvesting Project
location: Congo, The Democratic Republic of The
project_type: Agriculture Forestry and Other Land Use
description:
The DRC REDD+ Carbon Credit Harvesting Project, located in central DRC, Africa, is a group project that will protect 13,586,379 hectares of forest from industrial logging, unsustainable fuel wood extraction and slash and burn agriculture. Carbon validation will be undertaken by the Verified Carbon Standard (VCS). The project is developed and managed in a joint venture by forest carbon leaders GEC Communities II, Inc. as General Partner to R.E.D.D. Carbon Credit Harvesting LP (GEC-C) and Global Treaty Corporation (GTC). This project will utilize the methodology, 'Methodology for Avoided Deforestation' approved by the VCS in October, 2012. 

The project will be developed as a REDD+ project with validation planned under the Verified Carbon Standard (VCS). The VCS methodology used for this project will be Wildlife Works’ VM0009 ‘Methodology for Avoided Deforestation’ v2.0, originally validated with VCS in January, 2011 (Version 1.0) with the revised version (version 3.0) receiving validation from VCS in June, 2014.

The DRC REDD+ Harvesting Project falls under VCS sectoral scope 14 - Agriculture, Forestry and Other Land Uses (AFOLU), under project category Reduced Emissions from Deforestation and Degradation (REDD) and most specifically under the activity Avoiding Planned Deforestation (APD). The project falls into this category by the definition provided in the VCS AFOLU Requirements Document Version 3 published 1 February, 2012, by virtue of the fact that it prevents emissions that otherwise would have taken place under a legally commissioned logging concession.

name: Enhancing Rural Livelihoods through Carbon Sequestration by adopting Agro-forestry practices and Natural Climate Solutions
project_type: Agriculture Forestry and Other Land Use
description:
The proposed project activity under VCS will mobilize resource-poor farmers to raise tree plantations on vacant farmlands. It proposes to link resource poor farmers and end users of wood products in order to optimize the land use and to facilitate the co-ordination of wood producers, agronomists, industry, social enterprises and non-governmental organizations to improve the livelihood opportunities of rural households. The project activity is implemented on the degraded farmlands or lands used for rainfed subsistence agriculture. 
Various environment friendly technology-based agroforestry practices and Natural Climate Solutions (NCS) will be adopted to help climate change adaptation and mitigation as part of sustainable land management.

This project will optimise the land use and generate Emission Reductions (ERs). The amount of carbon sequestered through the project activity will be measured, quantified with reference to a baseline to determine the Emission Reductions (ERs) generated. The ERs will be calculated through Above Ground Biomass, Below Ground Biomass and Soil Organic Carbon. In the absence of the project, the lands would have remained degraded and the resource poor farmers would have continued to practice subsistence agriculture. 

The participation of small and marginal farmers as part of the VCS project makes this initiative unique in contributing to their land use choice, improvement of livelihood opportunities and in promoting their capacity to organize and implement climate change mitigation initiatives.

The project implements reforestation on 13,500 ha of degraded private lands in the states of Andhra Pradesh, Telangana and Orissa. The reforestation activities under the project were initiated in 2019. 

The project is estimated to generate 94,200 credits / year on average over a period of 20 years.

name: DelAgua Improved Cookstove Grouped Project
description:
DelAgua Improved Cookstove Grouped Project seeks to replace the inefficient, traditional biomass based cooking technologies with the efficient and improved, clean firewood stoves at household level in Rwanda. The households will receive a clean cookstove of high efficiency to replace the inefficient cooking practices. 
This will include education to the households on project stove usage best practices, and they will experience a reduction in indoor smoke levels to a significant extent. The usage of firewood will be reduced to around 2/3rd of the baseline levels. The project activity will rely solely on Carbon Finance for its operations, and therefore, will provide the project stove units to underprivileged households within the host country for free. The biomass savings will act as the source of Carbon Finance for the project activity. 
The project will lead to additional impacts that will be monitored as the UN SDG indicators, and project will be labeled for SDG impacts under SD VISta.

The purpose of the project is to utilize landfill gas (LFG), which consists mainly of methane, for electricity generation. It includes LFG collection system, LFG pre-treatment system, flaring and electricity generation system. LFG collected is used for electricity generation with internal combustion generators. The total installed capacity is 2.134 MW including 2 generators with 1.067 MW each.

name: Ningxiang Adjusted Water Management in Rice Cultivation
developer: Hangzhou Chunmeng Agricultural Technology Co., Ltd
project_type: Agriculture Forestry and Other Land Use
description:
The project changing from continuously flooded to intermittent flooded condition during rice cultivation are conducted in Ninghai County and Xiangshan County, under the jurisdiction of Ningbo City, Zhejiang Province of China, which have a total acreage of 12,096 ha for single-cropping rice. Without this project providing ditches to conduct intermittent flooded method, the continuously flooded method would be continued, so the scenario that rice was cultivated by continuously flooded method is the baseline scenario. Since the organic matter in rice soil under flooded condition can emit a large amount of methane (CH4) because of anaerobic decomposition, the intermittent flooded method is more beneficial to water conservation, production increase and methane emission removal than the continuously flooded.
With the project implementation, the cement ditches, reservoirs and relevant technical training are provided for these farmers to help them conduct the intermittent flooded water regime during rice cultivation, which replaces the traditional continuously flooded method. During rice cultivation, controllable irrigation and drainage according to rice growth requirements can not only save water resources, but also reduce methane emission from soil organic matter under anaerobic conditions (in the flooded state). In this case, the CH4 emission can be declined by an average of 48%1. Hence, this project activity is estimated to reduce 4.96 tCO2e/ha.
The implementation of the project is expected to reduce the GHG emissions amounting to 419,958 tCO2e in the first seven-year period with an average annual GHG emission reduction of 59,994 tCO2e.

name: Improved Cookstove Distribution by Climate Detox Private Limited- Phase II
description:
The objective of the project is to distribute fuel-efficient cook stoves termed as Improved Cook Stove (ICS) to the rural parts in the state of Gujarat in India. The daily usage of Improved Cook Stove for cooking purposes will reduce the greenhouse gas emissions from burning of fuel wood. The project will replace the traditional cook stove primarily used in the rural households which consumes huge quantity of wood in cooking. The ICS is designed in such a way that it has significantly high thermal efficiency, which will lead to the low fuel wood consumption and thereby reducing the greenhouse gas emission. The project activity will also positively impact the health and daily lifestyle of the rural household. ICS is proven to produce less smoke and thus it will reduce the respiratory health issues which occurs in the traditional cookstove. On the other hand, ICS beneficiaries will have to spend less time to collect the firewood and this saved time they will use in taking care of their family, kids and other productive work. The cookstove is also a safer equipment as it is closed from all sides hence users and their family will be in a safer environment.

The purpose of project activity is to provide a safer and efficient cooking medium to the rural population, which will further result in reduction of greenhouse gas emissions to the atmosphere and conservation of forests.

In the absence of project activities, the baseline scenario is that the target population continues to consume non-renewable wood fuel to meet similar thermal energy needs as provided by project cookstoves.

Under this project activity, project participant has planned to distribute 50,000 Improved Cook Stoves in the rural area of India. The estimated annual average greenhouse gas removal from the project is 368,478 tCO2e.

name: PROJECT MATANI REDD+ DIOS MAYOR DE LOS PUEBLOS CABILLARI
project_type: Agriculture Forestry and Other Land Use
description:
Colombia has approximately 60 million hectares of forest. Of these, 66% is located in the Amazon biome. The Forest and Carbon Monitoring System (SMByC) of the Institute of Hydrology, Meteorology and Environmental Studies (IDEAM), identified that in 2021, 174,103 ha of forest were deforested.
The name given to the Conservation Project is PROJECT MATANI REDD+ DIOS MAYOR DE LOS PUEBLOS CABILLARI, Matani is the Greatest God of the communities that make up the Association of Traditional Indigenous Captains of Vaupés (ACTIVA), made up of the communities of Altamira, Buenos aires, Cachiporro, Mutanacua, Villagladys, Cananari, Morroco, Reforma, Villareal. The Jirijirimo REDD+ Project is located in the Department of Vaupes, corresponding to the Amazon biome of Colombia. Due to its biophysical conditions, this biogeographic zone is strategic for regulating the climate, sustaining biological cycles, conserving soil and water resources, capturing greenhouse gas emissions, and conserving the biological diversity of the region. Amazon region.
Therefore, the indigenous communities linked to the project seek, through their territorial autonomy and their right to free self-determination, to carry out conservation processes framed in sustainability criteria that have to do with the protection of natural forest areas, rescue and protection of their cultural identity and promotion of productive practices that promote the protection of biodiversity and the environmental richness of their territory.
Characteristics that are directly linked to the purpose of REDD+ projects, with the desired sustainable local development, as well as with the purpose of reducing emissions generated due to deforestation and forest degradation. The project MATANI REDD+ DIOS MAYOR DE LOS PUEBLOS CABILLARI  constitutes an area of 814,948 hectares.
The main objective of the project has been is to avoid the unplanned deforestation (AUD) in the Amazon rainforest.

name: Xinjiang Burqin Improved Grassland Management Project Phase II
developer: Burqin Jinhua Urban Construction and Investment Co.Ltd.
project_type: Agriculture Forestry and Other Land Use
description:
Xinjiang Burqin Improved Grassland Management Project Phase II (hereafter as “the project”) is located in Burqin County, Altai City, Xinjiang Uygur Autonomous Region, China. The project is aimed to restore the local degraded grassland ecosystem from adoption of sustainable grassland management practices, such as improving the rotation of grazing animals between summer and winter pastures, limiting the timing and number of grazing animals on degraded pastures, and ensuring appropriate management over the long-term.
The main restoration measure of rest and rotational grazing were implemented in 68,333.33 ha of degraded grassland. For the first five years, grazing was strictly forbidden and then, sustainable grassland management methods will be applied, such as rotational grazing in different pastoral areas, limits the time and number of grazing in the project area to protect the natural grassland resources, curb the deterioration of the ecological environment of the natural grassland. It requires that the grazing time shall be halved by dividing grasslands into seasonal grazing land according to the livestock carrying capacity of the grassland by fence building. Then based on specified grazing order, grazing cycle and zoning grazing time, the grassland is grazed area by area and used in turn. 
Besides these main restoration measures, the project also alleviates soil desertification and restore grassland vegetation to improve soil carbon storage and local biodiversity through grassland management measures, such as daily management measures from other protect projects like rodent and pest control and grassland fire prevention to ensure the long-term sustainable management of the project area.

name: Adjusted Water Management in Rice Cultivation in Xiuzhou District
developer: Hangzhou Chunmeng Agricultural Technology Co., Ltd
project_type: Agriculture Forestry and Other Land Use
description:
The project changing from continuously flooded to intermittent flooded condition during rice cultivation is conducted in Xiuzhou District under the jurisdiction of Jiaxing City, Zhejiang Province of China, which has a total acreage of 12,085 ha for single-cropping rice. Without this project providing ditches to conduct intermittent flooded method, the continuously flooded method would be continued, so the scenario that rice was cultivated by continuously flooded method is the baseline scenario. Since the organic matter in rice soil under flooded condition can emit a large amount of methane (CH4) because of anaerobic decomposition, the intermittent flooded method is more beneficial to water conservation, production increase and methane emission removal than the continuously flooded.
With the project implementation, the cement ditches, reservoirs and relevant technical training are provided for these farmers to help them conduct the intermittent flooded water regime during rice cultivation, which replaces the traditional continuously flooded method. During rice cultivation, controllable irrigation and drainage according to rice growth requirements can not only save water resources, but also reduce methane emission from soil organic matter under anaerobic conditions (in the flooded state). In this case, the CH4 emission can be declined by an average of 48%1. Hence, this project activity is estimated to reduce 4.96 tCO2e/ha.
The implementation of the project is expected to reduce the GHG emissions amounting to 419,531 tCO2e in the first seven-year period with an average annual GHG emission reduction of 59,933 tCO2e.

name: Shandong Xiantan Composting Project
project_type: Livestock, enteric fermentation, and manure management; Waste handling and disposal
description: The project introduced a set of organic fertilizers production lines with an annual output of 40,000 tons to treat the manure from the chicken farms in Yantai City, Shandong Province. The purpose of the project activity is to avoid methane emissions through controlled aerobic treatment by composting of manure. It was designed to treat the chicken manure in Yantai City to produce organic fertilizer. It is estimated that approximately 114,000 tons of manure can be composted aerobically annually for this project.

name: Biodiesel Project by Rajputana Biodiesel Private Limited
description: Biodiesel Project by Rajputana Biodiesel Private Limited (hereafter referred to as “the Project”) is located within the Economic and Technological Development Zone in India . The project is constructed and operated by Rajputana Biodiesel Private Limited and is designated to produce biodiesel with capacity of 25 TPD.

name: Improved Cookstove Distribution by Climate Detox Private Limited- Phase I
description:
The objective of the project is to provide a fuel-efficient cookstove termed as Improved Cook Stove (ICS) to the rural parts in the state of Gujarat in India. The use of Improved Cook Stove for daily cooking activity will reduce the greenhouse gas emissions. The project will replace the traditional cook stove primarily used in the rural households which consumes huge quantity of wood in cooking. The ICS is manufactured in such a way that it has significantly high thermal efficiency which will lead to the low fuel wood consumption and thus less greenhouse gas emissions would occur. 

The project activity will also positively impact the health and daily lifestyle of the rural people. ICS is proven to produce less smoke and thus it will reduce the respiratory heath issues which happens in the traditional cookstove. On the other hand, ICS beneficiaries will have to spend less time to collect the firewood and this saved time they will use in taking care of their family, kids and other productive work. 
The cookstove is also a safer equipment as it is closed from all sides hence users and their family will be in a safer environment. Climate Detox Pvt Ltd and Siddhant Energy Consultants are the project participants for this project. The distribution of ICS will be done in the rural areas under the supervision of an equipped team. All the ICS will be supplied by an experience manufacturer. ICS has been tested in the reputed laboratory for thermal efficiency.

In the absence of project activities, the baseline scenario is that the target population continues to consume non-renewable wood fuel to meet similar thermal energy needs as provided by project cookstoves.

Under this project activity, project participant has planned to distribute 50,000 Improved Cook Stoves in the rural area of India. The estimated annual average greenhouse gas removal from the project is 368,478 tCO2e.

name: Wastes to BioCNG Project by Cities Innovative Biofuels in Patiala, Punjab, India
description: The technology of solid state anaerobic digestion (SSAD) or dry digestion is being introduced in India by Cities Innovative Biofuels Private Limited. Based on this technology, an anaerobic digestion plant using rice straw (and other lignocellulosic biomass), cattle dung and poultry litter as substrates is proposed to be set up near the city of Patiala, Punjab. The plant will have an input capacity of 80 tonnes per day (TPD) of biomass, with minimal need for water and no effluent. BioCNG (3,600 kg/d) and sterile compost (50 TPD) will be the end products and sold locally to dedicated farmer through long term agreement . It will provide a viable solution to the problems of crop residue burning an d disposal of cow dung and poultry litte r in and around urban areas in N orth India. The project is the result of an exclusive collaboration between Cities Innovative Biofuels Private Limited and a Swiss company, Renergon International AG.

name: Chia Tai AWMS GHG Mitigation Project in Guangdong Province
developer: Guangdong Zhanjiang Chia Tai Swine Industry Co., Ltd.
project_type: Energy industries (renewable/non-renewable sources); Livestock, enteric fermentation, and manure management; Waste handling and disposal
description:
Chia Tai AWMS GHG Mitigation Project in Guangdong Province (hereafter referred to as the project) introduces new animal waste management systems (AWMSs) to treat the manure from 15 Existing swine farms in Zhanjiang, Guangdong Province, which are owned by Guangdong Zhanjiang Chia Tai Swine Industry Co., Ltd. The purpose of the project activity is to treat the manure and wastewater to avoid methane emissions generated in the baseline uncovered anaerobic lagoons.
The specific treatment process of this newly constructed project is as follows: All the manure and wastewater are collected and then be separated first. The solid will be treated in aerobic composting system and the organic fertilizers will be produced, which will be distributed to local farmers for free and the surplus will be sold in domestic market. The waste water enters an anaerobic treatment system (enclosed) for reaction and biogas generates. The biogas is captured for electricity generation, with surplus biogas destroyed through the flaring system (if any). The sludge would be produced from anaerobic digestion and the effluent is supplied to the farmers living around free for agriculture irrigation as organic fertilizers together with other fermentation wastes produced in the project. The electricity generated are all used by the AWMSs and the swine farms, and hence the GHG emission reductions generates from the avoidance of methane emissions from the enclosed treatment system and the electricity generation.

name: AVOCADO AGROFORESTRY GROUPED PROJECT IN ISRAEL
project_type: Agriculture Forestry and Other Land Use
description: The main objective of the grouped avocado agroforestry project is to be a regional GHG emissions reduction and removal initiative, pioneer in the concept of combining sustainability activities with agricultural activities for avocado planting. To our knowledge, it is an unique initiative in Israel. All projects are located in Northern Israel. The four projects currently included in the grouped project are located at the following locations; Galed, Ramat Menashe, Ramat Yohanan and Yodfat. Agricultural practices by farmers in Kibbutz in Israel have traditionally involved open field activities such as corn, cotton, and wheat crops mostly with sprinklers (for more details refer to 3.4. Baseline scenario). This situation led the land to being occupied only for a few months each year (seasonal crops) with high levels of soil erosion and energy and water inputs. The proposed grouped project activity involves replacing seasonal crops with permanent avocado plantations, changing the entire ecosystem through the implementation of regenerative agricultural practices and boosting carbon sequestration by avocado tree planting.

name: Ecobase Europe Afforestation Project
project_type: Agriculture Forestry and Other Land Use
description: The Ecobase Europe Afforestation Project (hereafter the “Project”) is an Afforestation, Reforestation, and Revegetation (ARR) project, using the CDM AR-ACM0003 methodology V.2.0. The proposed VCS project activity consists of afforestation of agricultural land/other land, low productive agricultural land, and any other project eligible land across the geographical area of the European Union (all 27 member states), all EFTA member states, the United Kingdom and European EU candidate states (Ukraine, Moldova, Albania, Bosnia & Herzegovina, Montenegro, North Macedonia, and Serbia).

name: GHG EMISSION REDUCTION THROUGH INTERMITTENT FLOODING IN RICE FIELDS
project_type: Agriculture Forestry and Other Land Use
description: The project activity is an 'Alternate wetting and drying (AWD)' activity that is a water saving strategy in irrigated rice production. The main objective of the project is to switch from continuously flooded rice fields to fields that alternately encompass flooded and non-flooded phases which can save significant amount of irrigation water. Thus, the project activity has been designed to change from continuously flooded to intermittent flooded condition during rice cultivation which is conducted in different blocks in the district of Bhopal, Hoshangabad, Raisen and Sehore of the state of Madhya Pradesh, in India. A total of 8,085 hectare for single-cropping rice has been covered under the project activity. During rice cultivation, controllable irrigation and drainage according to rice growth requirements can save water resources, and also at the same time will also reduce methane emission from soil organic matter under anaerobic conditions (in the flooded state). Additionally, in the project activity compost will be used for soil application in the rice fields and thus replace the application of synthetic nitrogen fertilizer. It is estimated that about 58,722 tCO2e emission reductions will be generated annually across the crediting period.

name: Veracruz Mangrove For Life Project
project_type: Agriculture Forestry and Other Land Use
description:
The Veracruz Mangroves for Life Project aims to restore the ecosystems of mangroves and floodplain forests in the Alvarado lacunar system, Veracruz (ALS) contributing to its adaptation to climate change, the conservation of biodiversity and the reduction of GHG emissions. The Alvarado Lagoon System is a 267,000 h ectares wetland complex formed by the estuaries of the Papaloapan, Acula, Blanco and Limón rivers. ALS is home to tremendous biodi versity and provides a bounty of ecosystem services to the c. 130,000 people living in the area. In recognition of its high conservation priority, it is registered as a RAMSAR site and listed as an Important Bird Area.
This ecosystem has faced ALS severe historical degradation, ever since the establishment of Spanish colonizers in the 16th century who first undertook to convert its natural ecosystems into pasture and sugar cane plantations.
The project is a grouped project and will restore 2,101 hectares. This objective will be a chieved thanks to the work of different stakeholders. The project proponent (Livelihoods) will implement the project together with the local communities and the Mexican ONG Pronatura Veracruz (PNV).
The entire project area (2,101 ha) will sequester 50 902 tCO2e per year. Based on this ex ante estimate, the project will sequester 1, 2 7 2, 561 tCO2e over 25 years.

name: MEIOESTE UNICARBO LANDFILL GAS TO ENERGY PROJECT
project_type: Energy industries (renewable/non-renewable sources); Waste handling and disposal
description: The proposed VCS project activity titled “Meioeste UniCarbo landfill gas to energy project” encompasses the promotion at the Meioeste landfill site of destruction and/or utilization and/or supply to consumer(s) of landfill gas (LFG) (rich in methane) through collection LFG and its destruction in high temperature enclosedopen flare(s), utilization as gaseous fuel in set of engine-generator sets of an electricity generation infrastructure (with final total combined nameplate installed capacity of 5 MW) and a predicted supply of upgraded  LFG to consumer(s) with an LFG processing and supply infrastructure of combined installed capacity of 5,000 Nm³/h.

name: Chaco Vivo
project_type: Agriculture Forestry and Other Land Use
description:
Project Chaco Vivo will be developed under the Verified Carbon Standard and Climate, Community & Biodiversity Standards (VCS – CCBS) as an avoided planned deforestation (APD) REDD+ project. Chaco Vivo will help conserve an area of over 1,800 km2, encompassing over 187,000 hectares (464,000 acres) in Paraguay's Gran Chaco ecosystem. Despite the Gran Chaco’s regional and global significance, the region is one of the most deforested on earth, losing over 1,000 hectares (2,471 acres) of tree cover per day. Project Chaco Vivo will mitigate deforestation pressures in the region and protect this important yet critically threatened ecosystem, which provides habitats to more than 3,400 plant species, 500 bird species, 150 mammals, 120 reptiles, and approximately 100 species of amphibians - including numerous endemic and IUCN red list vulnerable, threatened, and endangered species. 

Chaco Vivo is a People Project at heart with numerous communities living within the Project's Area of Influence (AOI), including Indigenous communities of the Maskoi - an ethnolinguistic group of people of Lengua-Maskoi. The Project Area encompassed by Chaco Vivo is a High Conservation Value Area (HCVA) since it consists of natural habitats of outstanding significance and/or of critical importance due to the special biological, ecological, social, and cultural values. 

Key to Chaco Vivo is a robust social program called the L.I.F.E. Program™ (Land-use Initiatives & Forest Enterprises Program). The L.I.F.E. Program™ will provide a tangible system of socio-economic enrichment programs to improve the livelihoods of marginalized populations. The key objectives of the L.I.F.E. Program™ are to directly impact the U.N. SDGs, but also to foster community engagement, project integration, collaboration, and self-sustaining sustainable enterprise creation for generational impact, or G-Impacts™.

name: Western Kenya Soil Carbon Project
project_type: Agriculture Forestry and Other Land Use
description: The Western Kenya Soil Carbon Project promotes the adoption of a range of Sustainable Agricultural Land Management technologies including reduced tillage, mulching, cover crops, green manure, composting, soil & water conservation, integrated pest management, and agroforestry on croplands and surrounding areas for watershed restoration and protection. It is implemented western Kenya in three counties: Bungoma, Kakamega and Siaya. Due to its more favourable agroecology, the region is densely populated, and the lands are extensively cultivated with limited natural vegetation. Farmers practice subsistence agriculture, characterized by low inputs, low yields, and continuous loss of soil fertility. The project is managed by Soil-Carbon Certification Services Ltd (SCCS), a non-for-profit company. SCCS is contracting implementation partner (IPs) to support farmers in their land restoration efforts. The project’s main goals are improved yields, food and incomes for farmers, increased resilience to climate change, and climate change mitigation via increased carbon sequestration in soils and plant biomass. The project activities will generate carbon credits that will be certified under the VCS program and monetized and invested in the project activities to ensure sustainability of the project goals. It is a grouped project covering 32,000 ha, with total VCUs 1.87 million tCO2. Participating smallholders are organized in farmer groups for efficient extension services delivery. The groups sign agreements to be project participants after due process of local stakeholders’ consultations and are then entitled to all extension services and support from the project. The group agreements oblige them to adopt and implement SALM technologies on their lands, support project monitoring, and transfer emission reduction units to the project. The project has a 20-year crediting period and applies the VCS Methodology VM0017 Adoption of Sustainable Agricultural Land Management, Version 1.0.

name: Jintudi Composting Project in Zhucheng City
developer: Zhucheng Jintudi Organic Fertilizer Co., Ltd.
project_type: Livestock, enteric fermentation, and manure management; Waste handling and disposal
description:
The project introduced a set of organic fertilizers production lines with an annual output of 32,500 tons to treat the manure from the chicken farms in Zhucheng City, Shandong Province. The purpose of the project activity is to avoid methane emissions through controlled aerobic treatment by composting of manure.
In absence of the project, all manure waste produced was left to decay in uncovered anaerobic lagoons, which is the most economic, viable and reasonable for livestock farm owners. The proposed project was designed to treat the chicken manure in Zhucheng City to produce organic fertilizer. The proposed project comprises of fermentation system and fertilizer production system, etc. It is estimated that approximately 98,000 tons of manure can be composted aerobically annually for this project.

name: SHANDONG BEICHEN BREEDING SWINE FARM COMPOSTING PROJECT
developer: Lijin Huayu Breeding Swine Co., Ltd.
project_type: Livestock, enteric fermentation, and manure management; Waste handling and disposal
description: This project is to build a composting plant which is designed to treat manure waste from the Beichen Breeding Swine Farm to produce organic fertilizer. The purpose of the project activity is to avoid methane emissions through controlled aerobic treatment by composting manure.

name: Huinan County Afforestation Project
developer: Jinyongli Carbon Oxygen Technology (Jilin) Co., Ltd.
project_type: Agriculture Forestry and Other Land Use
description: Huinan County Afforestation Project is located in Huinan county, Tonghua city, Jilin province of China. The purpose of the project is to increase carbon sequestration and contribute to local sustainable development by planting trees on the barren or degraded lands. Prior to the start of the project, the land in the project area was barren, no forest or wetland except some scattered shrub and grass. Under the project, an area of 13,784ha of barren land in Huinan county was planted with trees of native species, mainly including Korean pine, spruce, larch, Fraxinus mandshurica, Juglans mandshurica, etc. The implementation of the project will generate greenhouse gases (GHG) emission removals and mitigate climate change, improve soil and water conservation and forest cover, enhance local biodiversity by increasing the connectivity of forests, increase competence and capability of local residents by providing them with relevant technical skills and training, and create more permanent job opportunities for local residents especially women and increase income for local communities.  The project is estimated to generate GHG emission removals of 19,001,754 tCO2e in 60 years, with an average annual GHG emission removal of 316,696 tCO2e.

name: Poultry litter to compost using Black Soldier Fly larva in India by Holocene Ecosolutions
description: Holocene Ecosolutions Private Limited (HCE), is in the process of implementing grouped project activities to convert Poultry litter to compost i.e., chicken manure with an annual output of 170 tons per day at different locations across various States & UTs in India. HCE are pioneers in up cycling organic residues from various Agro-processing centers using the Black Soldier Fly (BSF), Hermetia illucens, (Diptera: Stratiomyidae) in India. The primary objective of the project is to effectively demonstrate the use of BSF larva to not only generate feed, but also achieve an environmentally friendly way of managing waste.

name: Xingu-Araguaia Grouped REDD+ Project
project_type: Agriculture Forestry and Other Land Use
description:
The primary objective of the Xingu-Araguaia Grouped REDD+ Project is to avoid the unplanned deforestation (AUD) in a 10,004.42-ha project area, consisting of 100% Amazon rainforest. The project area is in São José do Xingu and São Félix do Araguaia, in the State of Mato Grosso, Southern Amazon.

Beyond the project’s ecological and carbon benefits, a proportion of the carbon credits generated will be dedicated to improving the social and environmental conditions in the project region, specifically contributing to improving deforestation control, and developing environmental education and other social activities. The contribution to sustainability is being monitored through the application of the SOCIALCARBON® Standard.

The present REDD project is expected to avoid a predicted 4,312 ha of deforestation, equating to 1,421,408 tCO2e in emissions reductions over the 30-year project lifetime (15-October-2020 to 14-October-2050), with an annual average of 47,380 tCO2e.

name: Strengthening Rural Livelihood Through Carbon Finance: Agroforestry Practices In Moradabad Forest Circle Of Uttar Pradesh
developer: Department of Environment, Forest and Climate Change, Government of Uttar Pradesh
project_type: Agriculture Forestry and Other Land Use
description: Agroforestry Practices as an alternate to fulfil the rising demand for timber and other non-timber forest produce is promising in long term as it provides both wood and food. Agroforestry can help to conserve and rehabilitate the ecosystem, along with providing better livelihood opportunities to the rural community. The proposed ARR VCS project plans to promote sustainable agroforestry for small-scale farmers to provide them with financial benefits and ensure GHG mitigation in the state of Uttar Pradesh, India.

name: 15 MW Nam Hinboun Downstream Hydropower Project
description: Nam Hinboun Downstream Hydropower Project is developed by Rasita Power Co., Ltd. in Songhong village, Hinboun District, Khammouane province, Lao PDR. The primary purpose of the project is to generate renewable electricity and supply to the Lao Power Grid. Total installed capacity of the project is 15MW, provided by two (2) bulb turbine of 7.5MW each. Project is commissioned on 01/02/2021. The expected annual electricity generated from the project is 79,740 MWh. The electricity generated from the project replaces the grid electricity and thereby avoids associated CO2 emission.

name: Strengthening rural livelihood through carbon finance to agroforestry practices in Saharanpur Forest Circle of Uttar Pradesh
developer: Department of Environment, Forest and Climate Change, Government of Uttar Pradesh
project_type: Agriculture Forestry and Other Land Use
description: Agroforestry Practices as an alternate to fulfil the rising demand for timber and other non-timber forest produce is promising in long term as it provides both wood and food. Agroforestry can help to conserve and rehabilitate the ecosystem along with providing better livelihood opportunities to the rural community. The proposed ARR VCS project plans to promote sustainable agroforestry for small-scale farmers to provide them with financial benefits and ensure GHG mitigation in the state of Uttar Pradesh, India.

name: DISTRIBUTION OF FUEL EFFICIENT IMPROVED COOKSTOVES IN INDIA
description:
The project activity intends to mainstream clean cooking practice through dissemination of fuel efficient improved biomass cookstoves in the rural areas of Maharashtra amongst socially and economically deprived households (households belonging to below poverty line )). The objective of project activity is to reduce anthropogenic emission of greenhouse gases to the atmosphere as well as reduc e environmental degradation and health risk of women and children subjected to indoor air pollution.

Transition to improved cook stoves usage from use of inefficient bi omass fired traditional cook stove is contribut ing towards reduction of greenhouse gas emission by reducing consumption of non renewable biomass in compared to the baseline scenario . Successful operation of the project activity and the health benefits the project has rendered to has also encourage d rural residents to shift from traditional cook stoves usage to improved cook stove usage.

Since the beneficiaries selected under the project activity belongs to socially deprived and economically marginalised ho useholds (households belonging to below poverty line ), therefore investing on improved cookstoves has never been a choice . . Moreover, the beneficiary households have lower level of awareness pertaining to health impact of traditional cookstoves usage.

name: Nesa Solar PV Grouped Project
description: This Nesa Solar PV Grouped Project consists of the commissioning of new, small-scale solar photovoltaic (PV) installations in the Republic of South Africa. The PV installations provide a clean, renewable source of electricity. In addition, the PV facilities increase the security of electricity supplies in South Africa. This is primarily because the national utility, Eskom, is currently unable to provide consistent electricity supplies due to aged and failing infrastructure. The quantity and duration of power cuts in 2022 is expected to be the highest since load shedding was initiated in 2007.

name: Papariko - Restoration of Degraded Mangrove Areas in Kenya
project_type: Agriculture Forestry and Other Land Use
description:
The objective of this project is to reforest degraded mangroves sites in Kwale, Kilifi, and Tana River counties, in Kenya. The project will create a healthy mangrove ecosystem in degraded lands, starting by planting 220 ha in Shirazi, Bodo, Munje, and Funzi Island, in Kwale county.
The main components of the project are to provide a variety of ecosystem services, climate change mitigation, economic considerations, and active participation of the local community. Without the project, carbon stocks in the project area will continue to decline, as the mangrove ecosystems in Kenya suffer a strong degradation process resulting from anthropogenic (e.g., deforestation for wood consumption) and natural causes (e.g., sea tides).
Under this grouped project, degraded mangroves on the Kenyan coast are restored and replanted. In the first project activity up to 196.000 mangroves will be planted. The species selected for this reforestation project are indigenous and local, namely Rhizophora mucronata, Ceriops tagal and Avicennia marina.
The project will monitor soil conditions to measure changes in soil carbon content and maintain soil nutrient levels to improve water quality compared to the baseline scenario. Mangrove restoration will further increase fish populations, improve biodiversity, and provide other important ecosystem services. To measure the positive impact on biodiversity, annual biomonitoring will be conducted using eDNA.
The empowerment of the population is also central to the project. The labour requirement for the project will be fulfilled with local employment. Therefore, most of the budget for labour and an additional 50/50 share of carbon credit revenues will remain in the country. The project will promote a working family model where more than 50% of women can actively participate in the project. People are shown alternative livelihood opportunities that allow them to acquire and grow high-value crops, and invest in beekeeping or ecotourism.

name: Sustainable Paddy Program
project_type: Agriculture Forestry and Other Land Use
description: The project plans to promote improved water management practices in rice cultivation instead of using the traditional practice of continuously flooded irrigation. AWD/DSR are proven methods to reduced methane emission by as much as 48% compared to flooded conditions where large amounts of methane (CH4) gets generated because of anaerobic decomposition. This project is predicted to generate important co-benefits of reducing water usage during rice cultivation, decrease pest and disease attacks, improve soil health etc. Further they're also beneficial for reduced cost of cultivation for small land holders

name: Agoro Carbon USA Pastureland Program
project_type: Agriculture Forestry and Other Land Use
description: Agoro Carbon USA Pastureland Program is a grouped VCS project implemented by Agoro Carbon Alliance. The program will implement a package of regenerative land management activities in pasturelands, these include nutrient management, increasing species diversity, rotational grazing and other regenerative practices. The implementation of these practices will lead to an increase in carbon sequestration rates in the soil, increase in forage quality, overall animal and soil health and improved water management. The main objective of this program is to provide financial, agronomic and educational support to ranchers to implement the aforementioned practices. During the project lifetime, enrolled ranchers will be assisted by the Agoro Carbon agronomic team to implement improved agricultural management practices from their current system standard to a system that capitalizes on sustainable, regenerative production.

name: Grouped Commercial Vehicle EV Project in India
description:
MoEVing Urban Technologies Pvt Ltd. (from here onwards MoEVing) is implementing commercial electric 2 wheeler, 3 wheeler and 4 wheeler instead of fossil fuel powered vehicles. MoEVing provides solutions to top e-commerce, e-grocery, FMCG, logistics and D2C companies to optimize their logistics costs and meet their goals of reducing carbon emissions. At the same time MoEVing works with OEMs, driver cum owners and financial institutions to helps address various constraints that are coming in the way of EV adoption. It was founded in Jan 2021. As of August 2022, the company's fleet of vehicles includes the Ampere, Ather, Hero, Okinawa, Revolt, 2 wheelers and Alti green, ETO, E-Trio, EULER, Omega, Piaggio 3 wheelers. 
Project activity is replacing fossil fuel (Petrol, Diesel and CNG) powered vehicle from baseline. The usage of electricity powered vehicles instead of fossil fuel powered ones leads to lower GHG emissions per distance driven. This is proven in the respective ER calculations. Included Project vehicles are implemented by MoEVing those were owned by MoEVing or operating on lease. Based on lease agreement carbon credit rights are owned by MoEVing, thus avoiding issues of double counting. Only vehicles are counted where such an agreement has been signed.

name: Xinxiang MSW Incineration Project
developer: Xinxiang Capital Environment Energy Co., Ltd.
project_type: Energy industries (renewable/non-renewable sources); Waste handling and disposal
description:
Xinxiang MSW Incineration Project (hereafter referred to as the project) is located in Xinxiang City, Henan Province,  P.R. China. The Project is invested, constructed and operated by Xinxiang Capital Environment Energy Co., Ltd.
With two 750t/d MSW combustion production lines, the project will treat 1,500 tons of MSW per day. The combustion system is composed of two 750t/d mechanical grate incinerators, matched with one set of 35MW steam turbine generator. The project will process 547,500 tons of MSW every year, and consume 284 tons of 0# light diesel as auxiliary fuel. The MSW combustion line will work 8,000 hours every year, generating 218,830 MWh electricity, of which 179,411 MWh will be exported to the Central China Power Grid (CCPG). The implementation of the project will meet the requirement of local MSW harmless treatment, and significantly improve local environment.
By combusting MSW that would otherwise be disposed of at landfill, the project activity avoids the emission of methane that would be generated under landfill condition. In the meanwhile, by utilizing the waste heat from the combustion of MSW, the boilers can produce steam to generate power to replace the electricity that would otherwise be generated by fossil- fuel fired power plants which are connected to the CCPG. Before the implementation of the project, the local MSW was usually disposed of at nearby landfill, where no landfill gas capturing system erected and the landfill gases are released to atmosphere directly. The equivalent power generated by the project was supplied by the the CCPG. The baseline scenario identified is the same as the scenario existing prior to the start of implementation of the project activity.
It is estimated that in the first crediting period of the project (from 19 November 2020 to 18 November 2027), the average annual GHG emission reduction will be 132,263 tCO2e.

name: Fengxi Geothermal Space Heating Project in Xi’an city, Shaanxi Province
developer: Shaanxi Province Xixian new district Fengxi New Town Energy Development Co., Ltd.
description:
Fengxi Geothermal Space Heating Project in Xi’an city, Shaanxi Province (hereafter referred to as “Project”) includes two sub-projects - Non-interference geothermal energy heating project in the middle and deep layers of Fengjingyuan (hereafter referred to as “Project A”) and Fengrun Regional Comprehensive Energy Supply Station (hereafter referred to as “Project B”). 
The project is planned and designed to introduce geothermal energy-based space heating system to realize heat supply to a series new residential and commercial buildings in Xi’an City over winter season, which would have received heat supply from fossil fuel-based heat supply system as a business-as-usual scenario.
Emission reduction credits will be earned using geothermal energy instead of the combustion of fossil fuel for space heating.

name: Tianjin Dahanzhuang LFG Power Generation Project I
project_type: Energy industries (renewable/non-renewable sources); Waste handling and disposal
description:
Tianjin Dahanzhuang LFG Power Generation ProjectⅠ(hereinafter referred to as the Project) is located at the Dahanzhuang landfill site in Balitai town, Jinnan District, Tianjin city, P.R China.The purpose of the project is to capture and utilize landfill gas for power generation. The electricity generated by the project is supplied to North China Power Grid (NCPG). The new gas extraction and utilization systems have been installed by the project. Before the implementation of the project activity, the landfill gas that was captured and utilized by the project was emitted into the atmosphere directly. Equivalent electricity was provided by North China Power Grid (NCPG) which is dominated by coal-fired power stations. This is the scenario that existed prior to the implementation of the project activity and is also the baseline scenario.
In absence of the project, the equivalent amount of electricity exported to the grid by the project would have otherwise been supplied by North China Power Grid (NCPG). Greenhouse gas (GHG) emissions will be reduced by avoiding CO2 emissions from those fossil fuel-based power plants connected to the grid and by avoiding GHG emissions from releasing LFG into the atmosphere from the landfill site.

name: CPA1 - Man and Man Enterprise Improved Cooking Stoves Programme in Ghana (Brong-Ahafo region)
description:
The purpose of the proposed activity “CPA1 - Man and Man Enterprise Improved Cooking Stoves Programme in Ghana (Brong-Ahafo region)”, hereafter referred to as ‘CPA1’, is to combat climate change and contribute to sustainable development of Ghana.
In the baseline scenario, households continue to using non-renewable biomass in traditional cooking stoves. An ICS combusts wood fuel more efficiently, i.e. requires less charcoal than a traditional stove. This reduces CO2 emissions.
CPA1 thus aims to reduce non-renewable wood fuel consumption and greenhouse gas (GHG) emissions of households (hereafter also “end-users”) in the urban and peri-urban Brong-Ahafo region of Ghana by selling about 200,000 affordable Improved Cooking Stoves (ICSs) in replacement of traditional charcoal cooking stoves, so-called coal pots, resulting in 174,201 tCO2 emission reductions per year on average or 1,219,411 tCO2 over the 7-year crediting period.
The CPA implementer is Man and Man Enterprise, a Ghana-based ICS producer and seller. The ICS distributed under CPA1 is the so-called Jiko-type ICS. It is also known as the “Holy cook”, which is the brand name of the Jiko-type ICS produced by Man and Man Enterprise. Compared to coal pots, which have an efficiency of 15%-18%, Holy Cooks have an efficiency of about 30% while providing the same service. This allows better heat retaining, i.e. quicker heating-up and longer cooking times with less wood fuel (and combustion fumes). ICSs work on a simple but mature technology for efficient energy conversion of biomass to heat. As ICS is relatively more expensive than traditional stoves, most households can’t afford to buy ICSs. In order to implement this program, stove subsidy and operational cost support are vital. Ecoeye Co., Ltd., and other Korean Companies have financed all improved cooking stoves distributed to the households until April 2021.

name: Ege Biogas Project
developer: Ege Biyogaz Elektrik Üretim Anonim Şirketi
project_type: Energy industries (renewable/non-renewable sources); Livestock, enteric fermentation, and manure management; Waste handling and disposal
description: Ege Biogas project (hereafter referred to as the project) is a biogas to-energy project that will generate renewable energy by capturing biogas from animal manure -via anaerobic digestion- and utilizing it to produce thermal and electric energy through biogas systems. The project is being implemented by EGE BİYOGAZ ELEKTRİK ÜRETİM ANONİM ŞİRKETİ, as the Project Owner, in Çapaklı quarter, Salihli district, Manisa province, in Turkey. In the project's final environmental impact assessment report, it is estimated that approximately 400 tons of cattle manure and chicken hens generated at animal farms will be collected daily or every two days through special sewage trucks equipped with close-tanks to prevent any odor and/or manure leakages and to be fed into the anaerobic digesters at the proposed biogas power plant. The proposed project activity has two biogas engines installed at the biogas power plant, with 3.120 MWe. The manure produced by 40 neighboring farms is collected and fed into the anaerobic digesters at the project site. The project began to generate electricity on April 23rd, 2021, which is the date of gas engines had implemented. According to Electricity Generation License, the biogas generator system has the maximum operational capacity 3.120 MWe. The project has obtained the approval of Environmental Impact Assessment (EIA) issued by the Ministry of Environment and Urbanization in Turkey on January 9th, 2020, and the Electricity Generation License (EGL) issued by the Energy Market Regulatory Authority (EMRA) in Turkey on December 10th, 2020. This project adopts the renewable crediting period of 7 years, twice renewable for 21 years. The expected average annual emission reductions are 322,680 tCO2eq/y. Accordingly, the project is expected to generate 2,258,762 tCO2eq emissions reduction during the first crediting period and 6,776,286 tCO2eq emissions reduction throughout its three crediting periods for a total of 21 years.

name: Soil+ Project to Incentivize Emissions Reductions and Removals on Agricultural Land in Europe
project_type: Agriculture Forestry and Other Land Use
description:
The aim of the climate protection project is to increase soil organic matter content in arable soils and simultaneously reduce agricultural greenhouse gas (GHG) emissions via a broad scale-up of regenerative agriculture. Therefore the project intends to motivate as many farmers as possible to convert from conventional farming, the most common type in Germany, to regenerative agriculture practices. This is done through financial support and in-depth knowledge transfer using digital platforms (company-owned web application & mobile application). 
Today, conventional agriculture is the predominant agricultural practice in Germany, with dramatic consequences for the overall soil fertility and the soil carbon stocks. Therefore, one focus of the project is to reduce CO2 by increasing the SOC stock. But at the same time the project considers the reduction of CO2, CH4 and N2O emissions from agricultural management activities, such as fossil fuel consumption, fertiliser use or livestock production. This enables a holistic view on the development of GHG-emissions related to regenerative management methods. Other positive side-effects of large scale project application can be taken into account, such as an overall improvement of the soil fertility and health  including i) an increase in water storage capacity, thus providing a higher drought resilience, ii) an increase in anion retention capacity of the soils, thus reducing nitrate leaching rates to aquifers and iii) an improvement of the soil structural stability and infiltration rates, thus minimising the risk of soil erosion events. The project aims to be validated according to the Methodology for Improved Agricultural Land Management (VM0042).

name: Dongfang Municipal Solid Waste Incineration for Power Generation Project
project_type: Energy industries (renewable/non-renewable sources); Waste handling and disposal
description:
Dongfang Municipal Solid Waste Incineration for Power Generation Project (hereinafter referred to as the Project) is located at Dongfang Municipal Landfill Site, Dongfang City, Hainan Province, P.R China. 
The project is established for the purpose of treatment of municipal solid waste (“MSW”) with energy recovery and electricity generation and no heat recovered for thermal generation is involved. The project is designed to dispose of a daily average 800 tons of MSW through two incineration systems, each with the treatment capacity of 400 tons/d of MSW, matched with one set of 18 MW condensing turbine and one set of 20 MW turbo generators. The project will dispose of 292,000 tons of MSW every year, and consume 100 tons of light diesel as auxiliary fuel every year. The expected average electricity generation will be 135,604 MWh per year, of which 116,900 MWh will be delivered to the China Southern Power Grid (CSPG).

name: Shanghe Geothermal Space Heating Project
developer: SINOPEC GREEN ENERGY GEOTHERMAL SHANDONG DEVELOPMENT CO., LTD SHANGHE BRANCH
description:

The Project is planned and designed to introduce the geothermal energy-based space heating system to realize heat supply to a series of new residential and commercial buildings in Shanghe County, Jinan City, Shandong Province over the heating season, which would have received heat supply from fossil fuel-based heat supply systems as a business-as-usual scenario.
Emission reduction credits will be earned using geothermal energy instead of the combustion of fossil fuel for space heating.

name: Eastern Cape Bamboo Forestry Project, South Africa
project_type: Agriculture Forestry and Other Land Use
description: South Africa's Eastern Cape has suffered over a century of land degradation, through a combination of clearance of the original ecosystem for livestock production, over intense grazing, and extended periods of drought. Such land degradation has gone hand in hand with increased levels of unemployment and poverty, with poverty in the province representing the highest in the country. Over the past ten years EcoPlanet has pioneered the use of a naturalized species of sympodial bamboo, Bambusa balcooa, as a tool for restoration of these degraded lands setting the framework for expansion. The proposed project activity uses a landscape approach to afforest extremely degraded farms that can no longer support agricultural activity, in a mosaic fashion. The project provides carbon removal benefits, enhanced ecosystem services, and long term job creation within a sub-municipality that current has >80% unemployment. The project is designed and managed hand in hand with the Eastern Cape Restoration Project, providing a holistic approach to restoration.

name: Agoro Carbon USA Cropland Program
project_type: Agriculture Forestry and Other Land Use
description:
Agoro Carbon USA Cropland Program is a grouped VCS project implemented by Agoro Carbon Alliance. The program will implement a package of regenerative agricultural land management activities such as but not limited to reduced and zero tillage, cover cropping, improved nitrogen management as a means to reduce GHG and decarbonize agriculture. The implementation of these practices will lead to increases in carbon sequestration rates in the soil, reduced soil disturbance and soil erosion, improved crop residue and water management, as well as potentially reducing the total usage of fossil fuels. 
The main objective of the program is to provide the financial, agronomic and educational support needed for growers to adopt new farming practices that not only produce agricultural products in a sustainable and profitable way, but also have a positive impact on climate change.

name: Selva Paranaense Vida Nativa - GS1
project_type: Agriculture Forestry and Other Land Use
description:
Located in the extreme east of the province of Misiones, in San Pedro, the field of native forest where the project is located has 22,878.5 hectares and immersed in the Green Corridor. In this area, controlled logging has been carried out since the 1960s and will decrease as the NIDEPORT project progresses, with harvesting expected to be completed by the end of 2021. The project activity is improved forest management with areas that will be enriched and regenerated by planting more than 250,000 native species individuals annually and others managed to increase forest productivity (bambuacea´s control, and others). 
Although there is not any community, individual or group of people living in the project area, GS1 has been subjected to situations of intrusions and illegal occupations, with burning for planting or deforestation for rudimentary construction, there are numerous cases where the land has been colonized or exploited for agriculture or livestock, where the land is left with high levels of degradation and contamination. 
The project zone, encompassed in an area with population under poverty line, expects to work together with the community identifying risks, HCV areas and needs, in order to implement mitigation actions together. In this line, first meetings with communities have already helped to identify both biodiversity and community´s HCVs, and possible projects regarding housing improvement, health care, among other needs to be identified during the project lifetime.
The climate benefits of the project are defined as the reductions or removals of GHG emissions resulting from forest regeneration, these are expected to reach 3,106,582 tCO2e during the crediting period, averaging 103,553 tCO2e per year.

name: IACO REDD+ Project
project_type: Agriculture Forestry and Other Land Use
description:
Project seeks to address the issue of deforestation in the Amazon biome on a local level at the state of Acre, Brazil . The IACO REDD+ Project is an AFOLU project, and therefore is classified within scope 14. More specifically, the project falls under the Avoided Unplanned Deforestation and Avoided Planned
Deforestation (categories). If this REDD+ project is implemented, 60,805 hectares of Amazon rainforest will be conserved over the first 30 years, avoiding the emission of 26,040,427 tons of CO 2 into the atmosphere. Under the social sphere, the project also brings benefits for the region . The IACO REDD+ project proponents recognize the essential role of the participation of project area residents and neighbors in the success of this project.

name: Eastern Cape Restoration Project, South Africa - Makhanda
project_type: Agriculture Forestry and Other Land Use
description: The Eastern Cape Restoration Project is a revegetation project, aimed at the landscape restoration of the native Albany thicket, within a biodiversity hotspot that has undergone extreme degradation and ecosystem loss. A multi-year drought, combined with a multiple decades of over grazing have led to a scenario whereby vast areas of land can no longer support either economic or ecological functions. The project restores ex-grazing lands with a native species, Portulacaria afra, which shows unique ecological features adapted to the semi-arid project area. Planted at high density and subsequently protected from grazing, the restoration activity facilitates a microclimate and dense canopy cover that subsequently allows for the return of the high floral biodiversity endemic to the project area. The project is a grouped project covering the sub-municipality of Makana and is implemented hand in hand with the Eastern Cape Restoration Project, South Africa - Somerset East, and the Eastern Cape Bamboo Forestry Project, for the creation of a holistic restoration strategy.

name: Methane avoidance in rice cultivation in Hefeng district of Huarong county
developer: Hunan Yueyang Huabanqiao Market Development Co., Ltd.
project_type: Agriculture Forestry and Other Land Use
description:
Huarong country is located in the north of Yueyang City, covers a total area of 1590.95 km2, with jurisdiction over 12 towns, 2 village.  Rice cultivation is an important agricultural operation in Huarong country, not only in terms of food security but also in terms of livelihood and plays a major part in the economy. Huarong country has a population about 713,300, and annual household income of farmers is only CNY 25,941. The project is located in Hefeng district of Huarong country, Yueyang City, Hunan Province, China, with a total acreage of 8,192.02 ha for double-cropping rice. The project activity is designed to construction the cement ditch and reservoir to realize the reducing of methane emissions by conducting intermittently flooded method instead of continuously flooded method during the cropping season in Hefeng district of Huarong country.
In the baseline scenario, farmers in Huarong country use continuously flooded method in rice paddies with the straw on field as the organic amendment inputs, which means fields have standing water throughout the rice growing season and only dry out for harvest. However, the organic matter in rice soil under flooded condition can emit a large amount of methane because of anaerobic decomposition. In the project scenario, farmers in Huarong country changing from continuously flooded to intermittent flooded condition during rice cultivation. By controlled the irrigation and drainage according to the needs of rice growth, can save water resources. On the other hand, multiple aeration during rice cultivation can effectively reduce methane emissions from soil organic matter under anaerobic conditions.

name: MK Group Energy Biogas Plant
description:
MK Group is a Serbian holding company which has four Divisions: 1. Agribusiness (which includes: Farming, Meat, Sugar); 2 Tourism & Real State; 3. Energy; 4. Support. 
MK Group has developed a mitigation project called MKG Energy Biogas Plant. 
This is a biogas-to-energy conversion project that will generate renewable energy by capturing biogas -from organic waste- which will be the fuel to produce thermal and electrical energy through the use of a cogeneration system. The project is developed in Vrbas, Serbia. The proposed project activity has total number of two cogeneration engines installed at the biogas power plant, with the capacity of 1.2 MWe/h each. The annual feed-in electricity is estimated to be 19,920,000 KWh/a; and heat energy recovery equivalent of 19,200 MWh/a. 
The 5% of electricity generated from the project activity would be used for self-consumption. Resulting that 18,924 MWh/a of electricity will be sold up to the Serbian National Grid. With reference to thermal energy, the Biogas plant will self-consume the equivalent of 5,000 MWh/a; whilst 14,200 MWh/a, will be sent to CARNEX (a company that belongs to MK Group). The total emission reduction average for the project activity is per year.

name: Bugnavilla Afforestation Through High-Quality Timber Over Degraded Grasslands
project_type: Agriculture Forestry and Other Land Use
description:
Bugnavilla is a grouped project located in center east region of Uruguay. The project initially comprises a total of 1.984,2 ha of land previously under extensive grazing by beef cattle, on which afforestation for obtaining high value, long lived timber products and for sequestering large amounts of carbon dioxide from the atmosphere will be established. The project ´s first instance will be in “El Tembetarí” property, in the department ( of Treinta y Tres, Uruguay. Forests are based on 25 year rotation Eucalyptus spp. plantations, mostly managed with pruning and three thinning operations, to obtain knot free, high diameter logs suitable for sawing or plywood
production. Plantation will be completed by year 1 of proje ct and forests will be replanted after clear cut harvest. The practices are not certified with the FSC standard. Although they are carried out as if they were, because in the near future it is intended to FSC certified.

name: Balıkesir Animal Manure Methane Recovery and Utilization Plant
description:
Balıkesir Animal Manure Methane Recovery and Utilization Plant (hereafter referred to as the Project) is a biogas-to-energy project that captures biogas from animal manure -via anaerobic digestion- and utilizes it to generate thermal and electric energy through cogeneration units. The animal manure is collected from the neighbouring animal farms with vacuum trucks and transferred to the biogas plant. Continuously Stirred Tank Reactor (CSTR) type anaerobic digesters are used to capture methane-rich biogas. Biogas is then utilized in cogeneration units for heat and electricity generation. The thermal energy is utilized only for heating anaerobic fermenters. The generated electricity is used both for auxiliary consumption at the plant and supplied to the national grid. The project is being implemented by BALIKESİR BİYOGAZ İŞLETMELERİ ANONİM ŞİRKETİ, the Project Owner, in Altıeylül district, Balıkesir province, in Turkey, whilst the project start date is determined as October 17, 2020. 

The project activity avoids methane emission through the above-mentioned capture and utilization processes whose details are provided below in the Project Description document. In addition, the project also reduces CO2 emission from fossil-fuel based electricity generation by supplying biogas-based electricity to the national grid. 

The project adopts the renewable crediting period of 7 years, twice renewable for a total of 21 years. The estimated average net annual emission reductions are 259,361 tCO2eq/yr. Accordingly, the project is expected to generate 1,815,527 tCO2eq/yr emissions reduction during the first crediting period.

name: Recycling Roadways for Carbon Emission Reductions - Midstate Reclamation and Trucking
description:
The Recycling Roadways for Carbon Emission Reductions - Midstate Reclamation and Trucking Project (herein “project”) supports Midstate Reclamation and Trucking in replacing hot mix asphalt (HMA) with foam stabilized base (FSB) and/or emulsion asphalt in pavement projects across the United States. Prior to implementing project methods, pavement contractors often default to using energy-intensive mining, hauling, and high temperature material manufacturing practices associated with HMA. These industry standard activities unnecessarily destroy habitats, release carbon dioxide (CO2), and release volatile organic compounds (VOC).

This project reduces greenhouse gas (GHG) emitting activities throughout the pavement application lifecycle. The project reduces dependence on the mining of virgin aggregate, reduces transportation of raw materials to mix plants, eliminates high-temperature asphalt manufacturing asphalt at high temperatures and, in the case of in-place pavement recycling, eliminates mix-plant to job-site transportation. The project replaces virgin aggregate with reclaimed asphalt pavement.

The project is conducted under VCS methodology VM0039, “Methodology for Use of Foam Stabilized Base and Emulsion Asphalt Mixtures in Pavement Application” and compares carbon emissions between traditional and sustainable designs with similar structural properties. 

Project instances will be added under a single Project Description as allowed by Verra. Other similar Project Descriptions may also be developed with other pavement contractors.
