name: Portland: Regenerative Agriculture & native revegetation on degraded land
project_type: Agriculture Forestry and Other Land Use
description:
The project includes both revegetation techniques in and around agricultural land, on different lands of the Republic of South Africa, providing resilient systems to protect the agricultural land from extreme weather events. The project proposes both the IALM and ARR methodologies together, at different GIS delineated areas on each project instance (land), the agricultural methodology will incorporate regenerative agricultural practices as well as circular use of by-products from the farm, as well as neighbouring farms. 
The ARR compartment of the project will include revegetation of native flora around the farm, facilitating ecological resilience to the project instance and sustaining pollinators throughout the year. This will be scaled to vegetation unit specific revegetation activities and regenerative agricultural practices as applicable per the Improved Agricultural Land Management methodology of the Verified Carbon Standard. This project intends to look at the system instead of looking on how to apply a methodology onto the land, a larger look at biota and their interaction in applied stewardship.
The first project instances occur in the Western Cape province, Southern Cape area of Knysna where a matrix landscape of Fynbos (ever-green shrubland, indicative of Mediterranean climates) and Temperate Forest was found historically.

name: Restoration and Conservation of Dry Afromontane Forest in the Highlands of Eastern Tigray
project_type: Agriculture Forestry and Other Land Use
description:
This project activity targets the restoration and conservation of 30,000 hectares of degraded and deforested lands in the highlands of eastern Tigray. The project area is located inside the Desa’a State Forest which is a dry Afromontane forest and lies between the Tigrinian plateau and the Afar lowlands (elevation between 3100 and 900 m a.s.l.), stretching along the Western edge of the Great Rift Valley escarpment of Ethiopia. The fragmented forest covers about 154,071 ha and is the largest Afromontane remnant forest in Tigray. The restoration project consists of active planting, assisted natural regeneration and conservation activities. In addition to the forest establishment and protection activities, soil and water conservation activities are implemented, including stone check dams, hill side stone terraces, trenches, small ponds and micro basins. 
It is a community-oriented project, which means that a participatory and inclusive approach is taken with the aim to improve the livelihoods of local communities. The degradation of the ecosystem in the project area is the result of unsustainable use and management over a longer period. These practices of overexploitation were mainly driven by grazing, firewood collection and timber extraction in a context of insufficient law enforcement and resource use planning. The drivers of deforestation are being addressed through a combination of providing alternative livelihood opportunities and improving management and law enforcement capacities. The recovery of the forest will restore the carbon stocks in the vegetation and the soil. A vital component of the project is the conservation and enhancement of biological diversity and the promotion of assisted natural regeneration. The project will result into an estimated GHG removal of in total 4.746.785tCO2-e over a period of 50 years.

name: Juruá REDD+ Project
project_type: Agriculture Forestry and Other Land Use
description:
Juruá REDD+ Project is a partnership between Biofílica Ambipar Environment and Amazônia Agroindústria EIRELI, in order to foster forest conservation and the reduction of potential greenhouse gas (GHG) emissions based on a local economic development model that values the “standing” forest through the integration of non-timber forest product management and trading of environmental services.

Juruá REDD+ Project is located at Seringal Valparaíso property, in the Alto Juruá region, between the municipalities of Cruzeiro do Sul and Porto Walter, including an area of 24,076 hectares. Juruá River basin is formed by four micro-basins: the micro-basin of Igarapé do Meio, the micro-basin of Igarapé Primeiro de Março and the Igarapé Grande micro-basin, in addition to the Valparaiso river basin (micro-basin) itself, which is the main drainage network of the rubber plantation region.

The purpose of the project is to reduce GHG emissions from activities regarding to conserve the forest and its natural resources, as well as to maintain carbon stocks, through activities that promote the reduction of deforestation in the region, such as the improvement of patrimonial vigilance, the monitoring of land use change and land cover using satellite images and strengthening the management of non-timber forest products. The performance of activities allied to a good project management, with continuous monitoring and evaluation of activities and results, will allow the Project to reach the expected goals and effects.

Therefore, it is expected that Juruá REDD+ Project prevents, by curbing deforestation, about 3,431,971 tCO2e by reducing GHG emissions throughout 30 years of the project. All the proposed activities to curb deforestation will become economically feasible if the management of non-timber forest products is combined with the trading of carbon credits through REDD+ carbon crediting mechanisms.

name: Heyuan Dengta Landfill Gas Power Generation Project

name: Replacement of ICLs by LED lamps in India – Project 2
description:
The purpose of this Grouped project “Replacement of ICLs with LED lamps in India – Project 2” is to reduce fossil-fuel based electricity consumption in the Rural households of India by introducing more energy efficient LED lamps to replace incandescent lightbulbs (“ICLs”), This would result in reduction in greenhouse gas emissions. 
The Grouped project (GP) will be located within geographical boundary of India. The Project Instance (PI) 1 in this GP is estimated to generate a total of 537,990 tCO2e and an annual average of 53,799 tCO2e emission reductions over the crediting period of 10 years.

name: Installation of high efficiency cookstoves in India by AGS Carbon – Project 2
description:
The purpose of this Grouped project “Installation of high efficiency cookstoves in India by AGS Carbon – Project 2” is to reduce the rate of deforestation in the remote areas along with reduce the indoor air pollution. The project will reduce the need for women to collect firewood for longer time. The project will distribute 75,000 ICS (improved cookstoves) to the beneficiaries under first project instance (PI 1).
The Project Instance (PI) 1 in this GP is estimated to offset an annual average of 348,457 tC02 emission reductions and a total of 2,439,200 tC02 emission reductions over the crediting period of 7 years.

developer: Guangzhou Kaifeng Agricultural Technology Co., Ltd.

name: Reforestation of degraded land in Spain
project_type: Agriculture Forestry and Other Land Use
description:
The proposed ARR-VCS project is a large-scale grouped project centered on the reforestation of degraded lands in Spain. According to the country’s National Action Plan for the UNCCD, approx. 74% of Spain is at risk of desertification and 18% of the land is at high risk of becoming irreversibly desert. This grouped project aims for the long-term restoration of Spain’s forests, achieved through native, mixed-species reforestation that reverses the impact of land degradation, prevents the loss of flora and fauna and improves biodiversity. The planting employs the latest technologies and planting techniques to support the permanent establishment of native forests in predicted bioclimates that may benefit rural communities in time. The long term resilience of forest and vegetation composition will be monitored by an extensive monitoring system to track the effectiveness and resilience of project activities.
The project is managed by Land Life, a tech-driven reforestation company that plants trees at scale to restore degraded ecosystems globally in hubs like Europe, the US and Australia. In Spain, Land Life’s local team based in Burgos ensures the boots-on-the-ground and maintains a close collaboration with local partners and authorities. 
Project activities are implemented and monitored according to approved large scale project methodology AR-ACM0003, with more project instances to be added over the coming years (up to 10,000 ha expected). The first set of project instances covers 167.46 ha of degraded land in Spain, at 4 distinct planting sites: Campos, Pancorbo, Villapadierna and Grisel. To date, a total of 147,369 native trees have been planted in the project areas and these will sequester approximately  49,792 tCO2e over a project crediting period of 60 years. Within this time frame, 40 years are accounted for in each project instance due to land agreement contract terms. The estimated annual average of GHG emission removals is 1,245 tCO2e.

description:
Yueyang County, which is located on the shore of Dongting Lake, is one of the major rice producing districts in China, has a population about 714,615, and annual household income of farmers is only CNY 27,733. The project is located in North of Yueyang County, Yueyang City, Hunan Province, China, with a total acreage of 7,588.94 ha for double-cropping rice. The project activity is designed to construction the cement ditch and reservoir to realize the reducing of methane emissions by conducting intermittently flooded method instead of continuously flooded method during the cropping season in North of Yueyang County.
In the baseline scenario, farmers in Yueyang County use continuously flooded method in rice paddies with the straw on field as the organic amendment inputs, which means fields have standing water throughout the rice growing season and only dry out for harvest. However, the organic matter in rice soil under flooded condition can emit a large amount of methane because of anaerobic decomposition. In the project scenario, farmers in Yueyang County changing from continuously flooded to intermittent flooded condition during rice cultivation. By controlled the irrigation and drainage according to the needs of rice growth, can save water resources. On the other hand, multiple aeration during rice cultivation can effectively reduce methane emissions from soil organic matter under anaerobic conditions.

name: Carbon Sink Afforestation Project in Tongyu County, Jilin Province
project_type: Agriculture Forestry and Other Land Use
description:
Carbon Sink Afforestation Project (hereafter refer to as “the project”) in Tongyu County, Jilin Province is located in Tongyu County, Baicheng City, Jilin Province, and is organized and constructed by the Forestry and Grass Bureau of Tongyu County. Tongyu County is located in the western part of Jilin Province, adjacent to Inner Mongolia to the west and Heilongjiang to the north, and is located in the Songnen Plain in the east of the Greater Khingan Mountains.
The project aims to establish forests on barren land to reduce greenhouse gas emissions and contribute to local sustainable development.A total of 3,266.04 ha (48,990.6 Mu[ A Chinese metric unit of area, 1ha equals to 15 Mu.]) of forests were planted in 27 townships (towns and farms) in Tongyu County.
The project aims to bring into play the benefits of afforestation and sink, and at the same time, bring into play the multiple benefits of forests in terms of protecting biodiversity, improving local living environment and natural landscape, and increasing community income. Based on the crediting period of 20 years, a total of 1,175,818 tCO2e is expected to be generated by 2035, with an average annual emission reduction of 58,791 tCO2e.

name: PlanTogo
project_type: Agriculture Forestry and Other Land Use
description:
The PlanTogo project aims to establish 120.230 hectares of forest plantations in Maritime , Plateaux and Centrale Regions of Togo, over a period of 10 years (2021 2030). The main forest species to be planted are eucalyptus , khaya and gmelina , the project also considers the planting of other species such as bamboo and cashew .
T he purpose of these plantations is to restore degraded lands in the short term and the sustainable production of goods an services in the medium and long term, while contributing to local development and fight against climate change by sequestering CO2.
The project developer is Sequoia Plantations Togo ( who will implement the plantations under two modalities: i) on their own lands and ii) on communal or smallholders lands to who S PT will provide seedlings and technical assistance. Sequoia Plantations Togo is responsible of project monitoring through the entire crediting period.
SPT is a Grouped Project, and project areas are selected considering the land eligibility requirements of the VCS, that is, on lands where there have been no native ecosystems in the last 10 years and without forest at the beginning of the plantation activities. The areas identified for the first instance are constituted by grasslands and shrublands, and current land use is extensive agriculture or cattle grassing. SPT will allow intercropping in the first years of the plantations.
The reforestation activities proposed by Sequoia Plantations Togo will generate a switch in land covert from non-forest to forest and it will lead to the creation of a carbon stock in biomass and in the soil greater than that existing under current conditions. The Net GHG emission removals expected in 20 years is 1 45 690 569 tCO2e (7 284 528 tCO2e/yr)

name: Kruger to Canyons Rangeland Restoration Project
project_type: Agriculture Forestry and Other Land Use
description: The Kruger to Canyons Rangeland Restoration Project is a grouped project located in the globally significant Kruger to Canyons Biosphere Reserve. The area has lost soil carbon due to unrestricted animal movements and high grazing intensities leading to low productivity and bare ground, while this is exacerbated by unfavorable herd structures. Unrestricted grazing is occurring due to a ‘tragedy of the commons’ where communal areas are over-utilized for livestock grazing and knowledge of sustainable grazing practices have lapsed. The project aims to reverse historic rangeland degradation on communal rangelands by introducing rotational grazing through herding and improved animal husbandry, and removing and reducing Greenhouse Gases in the process. Furthermore, project participants will benefit from improved access to livestock markets.

bottles per year will be recycled into 65,000 tons of PET flakes at maximum production capacity. 
Located in Yunmeng County, Xiaogan City, Hubei Province, China, the Project is developed and 
operated by Hubei Jiulong Recycling Technology Co., Ltd. (hereafter referred to as “the project 
proponent”).
Prior to the project implementation, the same amount of PET flakes was produced from raw
materials (crude oil and natural gas); the baseline scenario is the same as the condition prior to 
project initiation. The Project achieves GHG emission reductions by avoiding the consumption of 
the equivalent raw materials and by reducing related energy consumption as well.
It is estimated that the Project will achieve annual GHG emission reductions of 58,067 tCO2e and 
the total emission reductions of 406,469 tCO2e over the first crediting period.

description:
Sichuan Santai Improved Forest Management Project is located in Santai County, Sichuan Province, China. It is implemented by the representative project owner Santai Shengda Development Co. LTD . The project is to protect the forest that will be logged.
Santai County is located in the north-central part of Sichuan Basin,  30 42 34~31 26 35 N,  104 43 04~105 18 13 E.  Santai County covers an area of 2,659 square kilometers. The area of public welfare forest in forestry land is 305,000 mu. The area of commercial forest is 996,300 mu,  among them, there are 946,700 mu of general timber land. The dominant tree species are mainly cypress. 
The project is implemented in the key location commercial forest of Santai County, which distributes in the 33 towns. For the convenient of VCS registration and issuance application, they selected the Santai Shengda Development Co. LTD to represent them as project proponent to implement the GHG related work. 
The project has about 10,972 ha commercial forest, which is nearly mature or mature. Before the implement of the project, the forest in the project area shall be planted according to the design of commercial forest, and logged annually according to the timber logging and managing plan issued by the local forest authority. The main object of the project is to improve the forest coverage rate, protect local ecological environment, reduce carbon emissions and carbon sequestration by enhance the management level and converse logged to protected forest in the project area. The implementation of the project will result in significant carbon sequestration and improve the sustainable development of ecological system. The project is expected to generate 1,479,171.87 tCO2e emission reductions within the crediting of 20 years starting from 01/09/2019 with the average annual emission reductions of 73,958.59 tCO2e; without buffer deduction, the annual and the total emission reductions are 55,468.94 and 1,109,378.9 tCO2e respectively.

name: Animal Manure Management System (AMMS) GHG Mitigation Project In Huoqiu county Anhui province
developer: Huoqiu huizhao Renewable Energy Technology Co., Ltd
project_type: Energy industries (renewable/non-renewable sources); Livestock, enteric fermentation, and manure management; Waste handling and disposal
description:
Animal Manure Management System (AMMS) GHG Mitigation Project In Huoqiu county Anhui province is located at Shidian Town, Huoqiu County, Lu’an City, Anhui Province, P.R.China. The Project is invested, constructed and operated by Huoqiu huizhao Renewable Energy Technology Co., Ltd.. The project will introduce a new waste management system to treat animal manure from 8 livestock farms in Huoqiu County to replace the current open anaerobic lagoons. The treated manure is collected by tank trucks from the livestock farms to the project and the collected material is subsequently treated. 
By treating the manure with closed anaerobic digesters, the project avoids the emission of methane that would be generated from animal manure in current
open anaerobic lagoons. The biogas generated during the treatment process will be partly used for electricity generation and the rest will be supplied to
users nearby for heat generation. The electricity generated will be supplied to East China Power Grid (ECPG) to displace equivalent electricity from ECPG
dominated by fossil fuel-fired plants. The fermented sludge from the closed anaerobic digesters will be treated in aerobic composting system and used as
fertilizer. Wastewater from the treatment system will be used for agriculture irrigation.

name: Tieqilishi Sichuan Liangshan AWMS GHG Mitigation Project
project_type: Energy industries (renewable/non-renewable sources); Livestock, enteric fermentation, and manure management; Waste handling and disposal
description:
The project installs new animal waste management systems (AWMSs) to a group of 4 existing swine farms in Liangshan Yi Autonomous prefecture, Sichuan Province. The purpose of the project is to treat the manure and wastewater to avoid methane emissions generated in the baseline uncovered anaerobic lagoons.
The project replaces the current open anaerobic lagoons with new AWMSs, and each subsidiary swine farm will install one AWMS. All the manure and wastewater are collected and then be separated first. The separated solid are treated in aerobic composting system to produce fertilizer and part of the fertilizer will be distributed to the surrounding farmers free of charge to improve the life condition of farmers and the others will be sold to the market. The separated liquid will be treated through anaerobic digestion and the biogas generated during the treatment process will be captured and sent to the power generation equipment, the power generated are all used by the operation of AWMSs and the swine farms, which was provided by the region power grid. And other surplus biogas is destroyed through the flaring system (if any).
After anaerobic digestion. The sludge produced from anaerobic digestion will be treated through aerobic composting together with the separated solid and the effluent will be used as a liquid organic fertilizer for the irrigation of agriculture.
It is estimated that total 5,063.52*104m3 biogas are expected to be generated annually and each generator is installed in each subsidiary swine farm, total installed capacity of the project is 7.4MW and the annual electricity generation is estimated to be 65,824MWh.

name: Orizon CarbonCrop Rewards Programme
project_type: Agriculture Forestry and Other Land Use
description:
Orizon’s CarbonCrop Programme supports and incentivizes South African farmers/landowners in the transition towards more sustainable agricultural practices by paying out a majority share of the carbon credit revenues resulting from emission reductions and carbon sequestration on our participating project fields. Together with our partners, we support our farmers by providing tailored financial and practical advice, building online tools to assist farmers in their transition, hosting information sessions/webinars and contributing to local research on sustainable agriculture.
The program, with its project boundaries being the geographic boundaries of the Republic of South Africa, will be registered as a grouped project under VM0042 - Methodology for Improved Agricultural Land Management. Each project activity will be carried out and monitored according to this methodology and its supporting methodologies, standards, and tools. Over time this project will include various types of farming practices /land types by adding instances that meet the additionality and applicability conditions as per the methodology.
Our vision is to be a comprehensive partner for our current and future farmers in their regenerative journey, support further research and investment into Regenerative Agriculture (“RA”) and to ultimately help drive a national shift to improve soil health and productivity to secure the long-term future of agriculture in South Africa.

name: Changing Lives via Improved Cooking Initiatives – Philippines
description:
SD Environmental Projects Inc is a social enterprise focused on reducing deforestation in megadiverse hotspots and changing the lives of the most vulnerable communities by improving household economics, health, gender equality and overall quality of life. These vulnerable communities, often residing in areas most exposed to the risks of climate change and deforestation are disproportionately threatened by their impacts.  

The Philippines being severely deforested countries and amongst the most vulnerable countries to climate change is the host country.. The project targets primarily households (with a particular focus on indigenous people) in the Philippines, with no previous ICS access.  The project provides high efficiency biomass cookstoves, replacing existing inefficient open fire cooking methods. By providing the tools and education, project households are able to dramatically reduce their biomass fuel consumption; greatly reduce indoor air pollution including harmful particulate matter, reduce the emission of greenhouse gasses associated with burning biomass fuel; and free-up significant time for more productive uses such as employment or education that would otherwise be spent collecting fuel wood/cooking. 

SD Environmental Projects Inc and Climate Secure India Private Limited will manage the implementation, operation, and ongoing support of the project as the project implementer. 

Thus, the CLiC-Philippines project will bring a positive change to the livelihood of communities vulnerable to climate change by creating sustainable energy access and dependence.

name: Climate Resilient & Community Driven Mangrove Afforestation Programme
project_type: Agriculture Forestry and Other Land Use
description: The project includes restoration of degraded mangrove habitats through the planting of 4,500,000 mangrove seedlings in discrete parcels of land on a total area of 1000 hectares across the island of Sri Lanka. The objective of this project is to initiate a long-term community-based conservation and management programme to increase the extent of tropical mangrove forests and local biodiversity in Sri Lanka.  This project will also provide forest goods and services to the local community members in a sustainable manner.

name: XESET 2 EXTENTION HYDROPOWER PROJECT
description:
The proposed Xeset 2 Extention Hydro Power Project identified and developed by Electricite Duo Laos is located on Xeset river in the vicinity of Ban Baktheung village, Laongam district, Saravane province, Lao PDR. The proposed project activity is a run of river project has created a small reservoir for smooth operation of the project activity.

The nominal installed capacity of the project is 10 MW (the actual installed capacity is 10.454MW comprising 2 turbines with individual installed capacity 5.227MW each), with estimated annual power generation 34.38 GWh. The generated electricity from the project activity will be supplied to the regional grid consisting of Thailand power grid and the Lao power grid.

The purpose of the project activity is to produce renewable energy using hydro power for supplying to grid. In the absence of the project activity equivalent amount of electricity would have been generated by the operation of grid connected fossil fuel based power plants. The Project activity thus reduces the anthropogenic emissions of greenhouse gases (GHGs) in to the atmosphere associated with the equivalent amount of electricity generation from the fossil fuel based grid connected power plant.

The baseline scenario is that the electricity delivered to the grid by the project activity would have otherwise been generated by the operation of grid-connected power plants and by the addition of new generation sources into the grid The estimated annual average and the total CO2e emission reduction by the project activity over the first renewable crediting period of 7 years are expected to be 19,347 tCO2e and 135,429 tCO2e respectively.

name: TERRRA SANTA
project_type: Agriculture Forestry and Other Land Use
description:
The TERRRA Santa project of Improved Agriculture Land Management (IALM), according to the VM0042, will implement sustainable practices in all the project sites in order to reduce and remove GHG, support the local community, increase farmer’s income, and improve biodiversity and natural habitat – important pillars of sustainability.
The existing scenario prior to the implementation of the project was aquaculture with the use of on-land fishponds, producing fish for sale in Israel. This has been a common case in Kibbutzim (collective communities, traditionally based in agriculture) in the last 4-6 decades and currently becoming less profitable due to tax removal and cost increases, therefore some fishponds are not productive and left inactive. In addition, fishpond aquaculture makes use of technologies and practices that have large impacts in terms of, for instance, carbon footprint. 
The project will convert fishponds following rewilding concepts to increase biodiversity and vegetation growth using the earth’s “Muscle Memory”.  The project’s GHG removals will focus mainly on: 
I.	Aboveground biomass that will grow back after each harvesting.
II.	Belowground biomass, which is expected to have a high initial removal rate and small continuous increase.
III.	Soil carbon that accumulates continuously as biomass and sediments are added into the soil. 
Through this project, in collaboration with TERRRA, the Kibbutz farmers will be able to utilize the same fishpond areas to grow vegetation. These will mainly be Common Reed (Phragmites australis), Elephant Grass (Arundo donax), Castor (Ricinus communis), and/or other crops, to be harvested and used as fodder and source for renewable energy.
The IALM project is located in North Israel; it includes a portfolio of assets with a total area of around 500 hectares, which are estimated to reduce and remove 22,704 tons of GHG annually and a total of 454,080 tons over a 20 years period.

name: Methane Avoidance through Biomining of Legacy Waste in India
description: The proposed project activity is a grouped project activity promoted by Himadri Energy International Pvt. Ltd. (hereinafter also called as ”HEIPL”). As number of existing solid waste disposal near metros and urban/semi urban cities in host country, HEIPL envisage to promote legacy waste biomining activity for cleaning old sites and free the land used for such purpose to be used for other developmental work. HEIPL envisage to contribute towards sustainable development and helping to meet the host country targets to increase MSW treatment penetration level. The estimated annual average and the total CO2e emission reduction for the first project instance over the fixed crediting period of 10 years are expected to be 7,569 tCO2e and 75,690 tCO2e respectively.

name: Developing voluntary carbon market project for Periyar Tiger Reserve in India
project_type: Agriculture Forestry and Other Land Use
description: Tiger Reserves are the storehouse of ecosystem services and a majority of rural population depend on forest resources for their day-to-day livelihood. This dependence is in the form of collection of a variety of Non-Timber Forest Produce (NTFP) and collection of firewood and fodder for subsistence and livelihood purposes. Due to this dependence on forest resources and lack of sufficient infrastructure, the local communities venture in the forest areas resulting in degradation of pristine forest and causing human wildlife conflicts. This results in loss of human lives, and wild animals in a retaliatory process. Hence, there is a need to develop a dedicated finance mechanism which shall help in mitigating the conflicts in an efficient way and lead to coexistence and harmony amongst forest fringe communities and wildlife. This project will result in enhancing carbon sequestration by reducing pressures on forests from unsustainable collection of firewood through sustainable firewood management and exploring energy efficient technologies and alternative fuel in and around Periyar Tiger Reserve, Kerala.

name: Huizhou Landfill Gas Power Generation Phase III and IV Project
project_type: Energy industries (renewable/non-renewable sources); Waste handling and disposal
description: Huizhou Landfill Gas Power Generation Phase III and IV Project (hereafter referred to as the project) is invested and owned by Shenzhen PhasCon Technologies Co., Ltd. (hereafter referred to as the project owner). The project captures the landfill gas that would have been released to the atmosphere in the absence of the project and generates electricity with the landfill gas (LFG). The electricity is supplied to the China Southern Power Grid (CSPG) to replace the electricity generated from coal-fired power plants of CSPG.

name: THE ARR HORIZONTE CARBON PROJECT
project_type: Agriculture Forestry and Other Land Use
description: The ARR Horizonte Carbon Project’s purpose is to remove and reduce GHG emissions through an increase in forestry area in the state of Mato Grosso do Sul, at the Cerrado biome, initially near the city of Três Lagoas. The carbon credits are a result of the change of land use in previous pasture areas, through the plantation of Eucalyptus species in an area of 14,427 ha, considered as the first project activity, as well as a result of the recovery of sandy areas, through the plantation of native vegetation most adequate for each case in an area of 999 ha, considered as the second project activity, both classified under the ARR category.

name: CIBO Initiative for Scaling Regenerative Agriculture
project_type: Agriculture Forestry and Other Land Use
description: The CIBO Initiative for Scaling Regenerative Agriculture is a holistic effort to provide financial and technical support to US commodity crop growers that results in their adoption of improved agricultural land management practices and, consequently, greenhouse gas emissions reductions and removals. CIBO’s proprietary remote sensing technologies and process-based crop and soil model (SALUS), combined with technical and financial support from both CIBO and other enterprise partners, provide the incentives, safety net, and guidance that growers across the midwestern Corn Belt region of the United States need in order to overcome the barriers to widespread adoption of improved agricultural land management practices.

name: DEVELOPING CARBON FINANCE PROJECT FOR FARMERS ADOPTING REGENERATIVE AGRICULTURE PRACTICES IN THE INDO-GANGETIC PLAINS
project_type: Agriculture Forestry and Other Land Use
description: The project intends to generate additional income to the small holder farmers of Indo- Gangetic plain region for adopting improved agricultural practices such as zero till farming, cover cropping, crop diversification, farm residue incorporation, optimizing fertilizer application and efficient water management which provide a potential to not just prevent emissions into the atmosphere but also create carbon sinks through sequestration of carbon back into the soil. The project will be a grouped project. Starting with rice-wheat cropping system, the project will be further expanded to maize-wheat, sugarcane, and cotton-wheat/cotton cropping systems. Pulses and Mustard are cover crops widely interspersed in these cropping systems. The project considers 2019 as the baseline year in which the interventions started. Starting with 12 thousand hectares (~28000 Tonnes CO2 Eq. per annum) in 2019, the area will be stabilized at 2 million hectares (~7.0 million Tonnes CO2 Eq. per annum) in 2027 and maintained until 2038.

name: Boomitra Grassland Restoration in East Africa Through Soil Enrichment
project_type: Agriculture Forestry and Other Land Use
description: This project helps pastoralists in deploying practices that contribute to the sustainable development of the Savanna grasslands of East Africa. The pastoralists of this region have largely resorted to implementing traditional grassland management methods on their lands. The grazing of grasslands by both livestock and wildlife is widely prevalent, and degradation of land due to overgrazing is a prominent issue. In this context, the opportunity to introduce improved grassland management practices, including sustainable grazing practices, will significantly help the grasslands of the region and restore carbon to their soil, creating carbon removals while improving overall soil health. In this project, pastoralists will be mobilized to take up a variety of improved grassland management practices. These practices are proven ways to increase soil organic carbon, prevent further degradation of the grasslands, and enable pastoralists to improve their productivity.

name: Samkos REDD+ Project
developer: Royal Government of Cambodia (RGC), Ministry of Environment
project_type: Agriculture Forestry and Other Land Use
description: The Samkos REDD+ Project (SRP) is an initiative designed to promote climate change mitigation and adaptation, maintain biodiversity and create alternative livelihoods under the United Nations scheme of Reducing Emissions from Deforestation and forest Degradation (REDD+). Phnom Samkos Wildlife Sanctuary and Southern Cardamom National Park are significant protected areas in Cambodia because they maintain an intact and sizeable area of primary evergreen forest in the region. Their landscapes are also home to over 59 IUCN Red Listed globally threatened species such as, the Asian elephant, Malayan sun bear, Asiatic black bear, Siamese crocodile, Irrawaddy dolphin, fishing cat, and the pangolin.

name: XiCO2e: Mexican Reforestation Project
project_type: Agriculture Forestry and Other Land Use
description:
The XiCO2e: Mexican Reforestation Project is a grouped project for the afforestation, reforestation and/or revegetation (hereafter referred to as “ARR”) of lands in the states of Tabasco and Tamaulipas in Mexico. The main goals of this grouped project are:
●	To restore degraded areas through the plantation of Gmelina arborea. The project activity will prevent further deterioration of already degraded areas and address soil erosion by providing protection through vegetative cover.
●	To mitigate climate change by removing greenhouse gases (GHG) through biomass growth.
The first project activity instance of the XiCO2e project includes planting 1,014.82 hectares in the state of Tabasco and 204.18 hectares in the state of Tamaulipas, located in southeast and northeast Mexico, respectively. This totals 1,219.01 ha during the monitoring period from 2017 to 2022.
The project will achieve greenhouse gas (GHG) emissions reductions through carbon sequestration by pools via the reforestation with Gmelina arborea. The estimated annual average is 3,726 tCO2e, and the estimated total GHG emissions reduction and removals amount to 111,781  tCO2e. Monitoring activities for the first verification period started on January 11, 2017 and concluded on July 30, 2022.
The scenario before the project's implementation involved degraded lands, with the previous land uses being grassland and agricultural lands, currently abandoned and degraded.”
The project proponents are ALA BOOL ALA BOOL TRUST SA DE CV and FORLIANCE GmbH. The project implementor is PROXYLO S.A.P.I DE C.V.

name: XiCO2e: Mexican Peninsula Forest Project
project_type: Agriculture Forestry and Other Land Use
description:
The XiCO2e: Mexican Peninsula Forest Project aims to increase carbon removal through Improved Forest Management activities in communal-land properties (ejidos) located in the Yucatán Peninsula in the southeastern state of Quintana Roo, Mexico. The project is developed under the Verified Carbon Standard (VCS) methodology VM0003 v1.3 - Methodology for Improved Forest Management Through Extension of Rotation Age (IFM ERA).
The Project Area covers 70,246 hectares and is comprised of semi-evergreen tropical forest with broad species diversity, having as its primary target commercial species such as mahogany (Swietenia macrophylla), Spanish cedar (Cedrela odorata), Sapotilla (Manilkara zapota), Fiddlewood (Vitex gaumeri), Tsalam (Lysiloma bahamensis), Ramon (Brosimum alicastrum), Katalox (Swartzia cubensis), Shaving bush tree (Pseudobombax ellipticum), Copperwood (Bursera simaruba), and Chechen (Metopium brownei), among several other tropical commercial species.
The common practice of harvesting in the ejidos consists of selection cuts of tropical species in management units during the established rotation period. The project will extend the rotation cycle by +5, +4, and +2 years. Additionally, the project aims to implement a monitoring procedure to systematize and centralize information related to forest practices. The project is expected to remove 4,599,024 tonnes of CO2e over 30 years, with an annual average of 170,334 tonnes of CO2e.

name: The Last Habitat REDD+ project
project_type: Agriculture Forestry and Other Land Use
description:
The Last Habitat REDD+ project is located in the Ucayali region, in the central zone of the Peruvian Amazon, one of the regions with the highest rates of deforestation in Peru (31,543.29 ha in 2021). The project area is comprised by two private estates belonging to the project proponent, BAM: the properties of Nuestro Señor Jesucristo with 8,049.87 ha and Selva Maestra with 14,176.13 ha, a total area of 22,226 ha mainly of primary floodable forests.

Located near the city of Pucallpa (Ucayali) and surrounded by deforestation pressures from agriculture, urbanization and others, the project area harbors an extraordinary ecological wealth, being the last habitat or refuge for various species of flora and fauna and a green island of outstanding ecological value. In addition, the are includes several types of valuable forest, among them the aguajales, which are the wetlands with the greatest carbon sequestration capacity in the Amazon, making this an essential ecosystem to conserve.

The Last Habitat REDD+ project is designed under the avoided planned deforestation methodology as this area was originally sold to the project proponent with the authorization to  convert the forested areas in agrarian production lands (camu camu, palm oil, piñon, and cattle ranching). Despite having the legal authorization to carry out traditional productive activities, BAM, with its own resources, has promoted the conservation of these valuable forests and its biodiversity over the years by implementing different strategies and activities such: territorial supervision with technical and legal support, forest surveillance activities, permanent work with communities for improving their capacities in sustainable forestry management, among others. Such conservation efforts will only be feasible and sustainable over time with the support of carbon revenues from the proposed REDD+ project.

name: MARAJÓ REDD+ Project
project_type: Agriculture Forestry and Other Land Use
description: The Marajó REDD+ Project has been designed for the protection of forests and rich biodiversity in the Amazon. It is part of the Agriculture, Forestry and Other Land Use (AFOLU) sector under the Reducing Emissions from Deforestation and Degradation (REDD) project category. Specifically, the project is of the “Avoided Unplanned Deforestation & Degradation” (AUDD) project category.

name: Nehe Adjusted Water Management in Rice Cultivation
developer: Beijing Hongyuan Chuangxin Energy Technology Co., Ltd
project_type: Agriculture Forestry and Other Land Use
description:
The project aims to reduce a large amount of greenhouse gases (GHG) by changing the water regime from continuously flooded to intermittent flooded condition during rice cultivation. The project is conducted in Nehe City, Heilongjiang Province of China, and involves a total acreage of 20,245ha for single-cropping rice. 
Currently, the farmers in the project area are using the continuously flooded method during the rice cultivation. Without the implementation of this project, which provides ditches and technical support to conduct intermittently flooded method, the continuously flooded method would be continued, which is also the baseline scenario. As the organic matter in rice soil under flooded condition can emit a large amount of methane (CH4) because of anaerobic decomposition, after the implementation of the project, the period of flooded condition will be shortened, which will have negative impact on the methane production. In this case, CH4 emission during the cultivation can be declined significantly. Hence, with the proposed project activity, an estimated amount of GHG emission reduction 2.87 tCO2e/ha for single-cropping rice is expected per year during the 10-yr fixed crediting period.
The implementation of the project is expected to reduce the GHG emissions amounting to 580,676 tCO2e in the 10-years crediting period, with an average annual GHG emission removal of 58,067 tCO2e. This project aims to sequester greenhouse gas and mitigate climate changes, save water resources; increase the rice productivity resulting in higher living standard of local farmers and provide more job opportunities, especially women workers.

name: Installation of high efficiency wood burning cookstoves in Indonesia 1
description:
The project involves distribution of fuel-efficient improved cookstoves (ICS) in Indonesia. The ICS disseminated through this project will replace the baseline cookstoves. 
Through this project, the distribution and installation of approximately 500,000 ICS will be undertaken for households in Indonesia. It is intended that under this project two types of single pot portable stove will be distributed, which are SSM S32-X stove and Baldwin stove. Each household will receive up to 2 ICS per household, it could comprise of same or different types of ICS. The ICS will burn wood more efficiently thereby improving thermal transfer to pots, hence saving fuel. Not only will this halt the rapidly progressing deforestation in Indonesia but will also reduce health hazards from indoor smoke pollution and women and children will have to spend less time collecting firewood.

name: Arva Carbon Ready USA
project_type: Agriculture Forestry and Other Land Use
description: U.S. Farmers and Ranchers represent one of the most scalable and cost-effective solutions to draw down greenhouse gas (GHG) emissions and address climate change. Arva Intelligence is a producer-first, B Corporation that uses machine learning (ML) and precision agriculture to optimize sustainable practices and profitability for landowners. Arva was founded on the principle of helping farmers and their suppliers make data-informed agronomic decisions, resulting in improved environmental stewardship for the buyers and an increased efficiency in grower operations. Limited access to data and financial risk concerns have been common barriers to adopting regenerative land management practices in the U.S., and the Arva Carbon Ready USA project will bring tools to farmers and ranchers to help them overcome barriers to adoption. Arva provides solutions through its measurement, monitoring, reporting, and verification platform and will provide its cloud-based, ML-enabled software to collect, integrate, and validate data from the adoption or expansion of on-field regenerative agricultural practices. Access to low-cost, scalable, agricultural carbon offsets is limited by the industry’s disaggregated digital infrastructure. Arva’s established Carbon Ready program allows farmers to upload field boundaries and run scenarios to determine the GHG emission values for practice changes that result in GHG avoidance/reduction and soil organic carbon sequestration. A project goal is to help growers identify the practices and seed best suited for their land and to overcome scalability challenges. To facilitate the collection of soil carbon measurements and verify location, Arva will utilize its newly developed mobile app. The project is designed as a grouped project within the USA. Arva estimates that this project will result in the removal and/or avoidance of 1,000,000 tons CO2e annually by 2023. Total GHG ERRs after the first 20 years of the project are estimated at 17,020,002 tons CO2e.

name: Hongera Reforestation Project (Mt Kenya and Aberdares)
project_type: Agriculture Forestry and Other Land Use
description: The Hongera Reforestation Project (Mt Kenya and Aberdares) is a reforestation and afforestation  initiative designed and funded by Dutch Green Business. The Project aims to increase tree cover in Kenya through two distinct strategies: 1) restoring degraded or deforested areas in Kenya Forest Service lands with native species, and 2) planting agroforestry crop trees on individual farms where smallholders wish to benefit from the income that perennial nuts and fruits can provide. In both cases, site-appropriate tree species will be contributing to regional wildlife habitat or corridors, improving water infiltration, controlling erosion, and sequestering carbon, among other ecosystem services. Prior to project implementation, thousands of hectares of Kenya Forest Service land have been degraded or deforested over time, without the financial resources to restore them. In some cases, reforestation efforts have been attempted, but without the dedication of enough funds to guarantee the survival of these trees when threats like livestock grazing must be constantly warded off through employed patrols. The Project aims to change this dynamic by bringing in external up-front investment made possible through the anticipated sale of Verified Carbon Units generated through project activities. Similar financial barriers are faced by individual farmers, many of whom rely on annual crops like cabbage or potato, and do not have the resources to invest in trees that they are interested in. Their farms are currently lacking in canopy cover, with perhaps a few trees on the property boundaries that are cyclically harvested for fuelwood or timber.

name: BEYAZ PİRAMİT BIOGAS PROJECT
project_type: Energy industries (renewable/non-renewable sources); Livestock, enteric fermentation, and manure management
description: Beyaz Piramit Biogas project is a biogas to-energy project that will generate renewable energy by capturing biogas from animal manure -via anaerobic digestion- and utilizing it to produce thermal and electric energy through biogas systems. The project is being implemented by BEYAZ PİRAMİT TARIM HAYVANCILIK ENERJİ EĞİTİM VE DANIŞMANLIK A.Ş., as the Project Owner, in Çumra district, KONYA province, in Turkey. From a socio-economic perspective, agricultural activities and animal husbandry have historically been primary household income sources for those living in Cumra Region. it is estimated that approximately 550 tons of cattle manure generated at animal farms will be collected daily through special sewage trucks equipped with close-tanks to prevent any odor and/or manure leakages and to be fed into the anaerobic digesters at the proposed biogas power plant The proposed project activity has two biogas engines installed at the biogas power plant, with 3.002 MWe. The manure produced by 12,650 dairy cattle and 2,110,000 hens located on neighboring farms is collected and fed into the anaerobic digesters at the project site.The expected average annual emission reductions are 354,263 tCO2eq/y. Accordingly, the project is expected to generate 2,479,844 tCO2eq emissions reduction during the first crediting period and 7,439,533 tCO2eq emissions reduction throughout its three crediting periods for a total of 21 years.

name: Ipoá REDD+ Project
project_type: Agriculture Forestry and Other Land Use
description: The primary objective of the IPOÁ REDD+ Project is to avoid gross baseline emissions of 2,719,762 tCO2e (averaging 90,659 tCO2e/year), corresponding to 4,200 hectares of avoided deforestation over the 30-year project lifetime (being an average of 140 ha/year). The project operates within private areas totaling 17,386 hectares, 17,329 hectares of which are eligible for REDD+ activities, located in Amazonas State, municipality of Novo Aripuanã. The latter ranks 15th for highest deforestation rates of the municipalities within the Amazon biome according to the Brazilian national deforestation monitoring program (PRODES) as, between 2016 and 2021, it displayed an average deforestation rate of 160km²/year. Long-term, high-impact benefits for communities and biodiversity will be provided by the Ipoá project, which are duly quantified and monitored through the CCB methodological standard. The definition of the actions to be implemented was carried out through a collaborative participatory consultation with community stakeholders. The activities fall into multiple activity scopes including: healthcare, education, occupational health and safety, communication and electrification, employment, and training, within the Community Pillar; fauna and flora research and conservation activities, as well as those addressing high conservation values, in the Biodiversity Pillar; and forest conservation activities articulated under Carbonext’s Forest Integrity Plan in the Climate Pillar. These initiatives will begin as soon as possible to project start in 2022 – 2023, Monitoring Period 1 (“MR1”), and continue along the project lifetime, through MR30 in 2052.

name: Chengmai Water Management with Rice Cultivation
developer: Hainan Sunsea Ecological Agriculture Technology Co., Ltd.
project_type: Agriculture Forestry and Other Land Use
description: The project carried out changes from a continuously flooded regime to an intermittently flooded regime during rice cultivation in Chengmai County, Hainan Province, China, with a total acreage of 12,488 ha of double-cropping rice. Without the project, there would be no ditches, pumps, valves, and reservoirs to conduct the intermittently flooded method, the traditional continuously flooded method would be continued. The original scenario for rice cultivation by the continuously flooded method is the baseline scenario. Since the organic matter in rice soil under flooded conditions can emit a large amount of methane because of anaerobic decomposition, the intermittently flooded method is more conducive to saving water, increasing rice yield, and reducing methane emissions than the continuously flooded method.

name: Dansha Water Management with Rice Cultivation
developer: Hainan Sunsea Ecological Agriculture Technology Co., Ltd.
project_type: Agriculture Forestry and Other Land Use
description: The project carried out changes from a continuously flooded regime to an intermittently flooded regime during rice cultivation in Danzhou City and Baisha Li Autonomous County (hereinafter “Baisha County”), Hainan Province, China, with a total acreage of 12,734 ha of double-cropping rice. Without the project, there would be no ditches, pumps, valves, and reservoirs to conduct the intermittently flooded method, the traditional continuously flooded method would be continued. The original scenario for rice cultivation by the continuously flooded method is the baseline scenario. name: Tibet Ngari Improved Grassland Management Project
developer: National Forestry and Grassland Administration Northwest Investigation and Planning Institute
project_type: Agriculture Forestry and Other Land Use
description:
Tibet Ngari Improved Grassland Management Project (hereafter as 'the project') is located in Ngari Region, Tibet Autonomous Region, China. The objective of the project is to restore the 'black soil beach' and degraded grassland ecosystem through reseeding native grasses and grazing management, such as rest grazing and grazing prohibition, increase carbon sequestration, and promote local development.
Totally, 373,467.02 ha of degraded grassland in Ngari have been managed sustainably including rest grazing and grazing prohibition by fence building and seeding of local high-quality forage.There are three main restoration measures: rest grazing, grazing prohibition and black soil beach restoration. 
In addition to these main restoration measures, the project also alleviates soil desertification and restores grassland vegetation through grassland management measures to improve soil carbon storage and local biodiversity, supplemented by daily management measures of other protection projects, such as grassland fire prevention and rodent control, so as to ensure long-term sustainable management of the project area.
