name: Guoyang MSW Landfill Site LFG Recovery and Comprehensive Utilization Project
project_type: Energy industries (renewable/non-renewable sources); Waste handling and disposal
description:
Guoyang MSW Landfill Site LFG Recovery and Comprehensive Utilization Project (hereafter referred to as the project) is located in Wangqiao Village, Chudian Town, Guoyang County, Bozhou City, Anhui Province, P.R. China. The project is invested, constructed and operated by Guoyang Baichang Renewable Energy Co., Ltd. The objective is to collect the landfill gas (LFG) from Guoyang MSW landfill site (hereafter referred to as Guoyang landfill site) and utilize it to generate electricity.
Guoyang landfill site is located in Wangqiao Village, Chudian Town, Guoyang County, Bozhou City. The project has a total designed capacity 4MW (8*500kW) and combusts the LFG, which contains nearly 50% of methane, to generate electricity and export it to the East China Power Grid (ECPG). The project started construction in December 2019 and started operation on 18/01/2021. 
The project collects and utilizes LFG from Guoyang landfill site for power generation, which would otherwise be released into the atmosphere. Methane in the LFG has been emitted to the atmosphere since the landfill started operation. Therefore the project avoids methane emissions and, at the same time, electricity is generated from a renewable energy source, instead of being provided by the grid. 
The total power generation during the crediting period is estimated to be 127,526 MWh. The estimated annual average emission reduction generated by the project over the crediting period is 62,295 tCO2e per year by avoiding the CH4 emissions from the landfill and the CO2 emissions from the fossil fuel power plants in the ECPG.

name: Jiangsu REO-ECO PET RECYCLING PROJECT
developer: Jiangsu REO-ECO New Material Tech Co., Ltd
description:
Jiangsu REO-ECO PET Recycling Project (hereafter referred to as the Project, or the proposed project) is located in No. 28, Nanhai Road, Hongze Economic Development Zone, Huai'an City, Jiangsu Province, P.R. China. 
The Project is invested, constructed and operated by Jiangsu REO-ECO New Material Tech Co., Ltd (hereafter referred to as the Project proponents). The objective of the Project is to collect the waste plastic and utilize it to product Food-grade Polyethylene Terephthalate (PET).
In the Project, the Polyethylene Terephthalate (PET) residues will be sorted, classified, washed with hot water, dried, compacted, pelletized, and then used as raw materials for production of PET. Prior to the implementation of the Project, the PET residues in municipal solid waste (MSW) were deposited in a disposal site.
The Project recycled PET from (MSW), and then process them into intermediate products, which displacing the production of virgin materials in dedicated facilities, thereby resulting in avoidance of energy use and the related emissions.
The total quantity of PET recycled during the operation period is estimated to be 30,000 tons per year. The estimated annual average emission reduction generated by the Project over the crediting period is 10,247tCO2e per year by avoiding energy consumption.

name: BigCoast Forest Climate Initiative
project_type: Agriculture Forestry and Other Land Use
description: A forest carbon credit project to create greenhouse gas (GHG) emission reductions and removals by converting privately owned operational forest lands to protected forest lands. The project will be implemented following the Verified Carbon Standard (VCS) VM0012 – Improved Forest Management in Temperate and Boreal Forests (LtPF), v1.2 methodology. The project is located in coastal British Columbia, Canada.  This forest carbon project area is non-contiguous, with parcels located throughout Vancouver Island, Cortes Island, and Haida Gwaii.  Old forests, ecologically significant areas, and culturally important areas were targeted for the forest carbon project.

name: REGENERATING DEGRADED LANDS IN FLORIDA THROUGH PONGAMIA
project_type: Agriculture Forestry and Other Land Use
description:
This grouped project aims to reforest and restore degraded agricultural lands by planting Pongamia trees. Reforestation started in 2018, through the planting of 100 to 145 Pongamia  trees per acre (250 to 360 trees per hectare, approximately). The project aims to increase the Pongamia plantation area to 1,000 ha and certify carbon offsets for a period of 20 years following the small-scale afforestation and reforestation methodology (VCS - AR-AMS0007). 
Regenerative agriculture is a system of growing food that reverses climate change by revitalizing natural ecosystems and agricultural lands while improving water quality and soil biodiversity. It improves the health of soils capable of producing high quality, nutrient dense food. Currently, the project areas are in a high state of degradation due to intensive agriculture practices. Although the project represents an intervention on the ground, it favors the increase and recovery of land that enhances the possibility of connecting fragments of forest, reducing fertilization use and providing an additional source of income to the landowners.

name: Mengzi MSW Landfill Site LFG Comprehensive Utilization and Power Generation Project
project_type: Energy industries (renewable/non-renewable sources); Waste handling and disposal
description:
Mengzi MSW Landfill Site LFG Comprehensive Utilization and Power Generation Project (hereafter referred to as the project) is located at Mengzi MSW landfill site (hereafter referred to as Mengzi landfill site), in A De Chong, Chenjia Village, Wencui Street, Mengzi City, Honghe Hani and Yi Autonomous Prefecture, Yunnan Province, P.R. China. The project is constructed and operated by Mengzi BCCY New Energy Co., Ltd.
Mengzi landfill site started collecting and handling waste in 2005.
The project started to construct on 20/06/2021. The project has a total designed capacity 2MW (4*0.5MW) and combusts the LFG, which contains nearly 50% of methane, to generate electricity and export it to the China Southern Power Grid. Total electricity supplied to the grid in the crediting period will be 85,636MWh. VCUs will be claimed from the methane destroyed and the grid electricity displaced. The estimated average GHG emission reductions of the project are 50,235tCO2e and the total GHG emission reductions and removals are 502,349tCO2e during the fixed 10 years crediting period.
Scenario existing prior to the implementation of the project (the same as baseline scenario):
LFG from Mengzi landfill site is emitted to the atmosphere directly.
Equivalent electricity generated by the project is supplied by the China Southern Power Grid, which is dominated by fossil fuel based power plants.

name: Agroforestry and Reforestation for Carbon Sequestration in Indonesia
project_type: Agriculture Forestry and Other Land Use
description:
Agroforestry and Reforestation for Carbon Sequestration in Indonesia is a grouped afforestation and
reforestation project initiated by PUR Projet in 2021. The purpose of the project is to reforest the
degraded land and to promote sustainable agroforestry with local farmers located in the Indonesian
regions of Sumatra Island, Bangka Belitung Islands, Sulawesi Island, and Java Island.

PUR Projet develops agroforestry projects with local institutions (agricultural
cooperatives & rural communities) and local farmers who want to engage into more virtuous
agricultural practices. Providing technical support, training, and free access to seedlings - PUR
Projet will work with participants to plant trees on their land in the interest of protection and
restoration.
The main objectives of the project are as follows:
- Increase climate change resilience of agricultural lands, diversify incomes, and
restore ecosystem services by supporting agroforestry practices.
- Implement full stand rehabilitation and restoration of degraded lands.
- Climate change mitigation through carbon removals generated by tree-planting
activities.
- Raise environmental awareness and knowledge within rural communities and
promote sustainable agriculture practices.

name: Andes Inorganic Carbon Capture on Agricultural Soils
project_type: Agriculture Forestry and Other Land Use
description:
Andes has developed a carbon dioxide (CO2) removal solution based on the action of microorganisms interacting with plant roots, which accelerate the formation of minerals (bio-mineralization) in the soil.
The company is planning to first implement this biotechnology on row crops, including corn, soybean, and wheat, in the United States. In parallel, Andes is also planning to deploy its technology in Canada and South America.
Starting acreage for 2022 will be 25,000 acres with a steep growth during the upcoming years. We are planning to extend the program up to 500,000 acres for the 2023 season. The program will continue growing through the following years, reaching over 65 million acres by 2031.

name: Northern Great Plains Regenerative Grazing Project 2
project_type: Agriculture Forestry and Other Land Use
description:
The Northern Great Plains Regenerative Grazing Project 2 aims to remove greenhouse gasses from the atmosphere by implementing sustainable grazing management on multiple ranches in Montana and parts of Wyoming, Idaho, Washington, North Dakota, and South Dakota. It is a grouped project starting with 10,000 hectares that will generate on average an estimated 17,000 tCO2e of emissions reductions annually, and expected to grow to >1MM acres in the first year. Planned grazing will increase the rest and rotation on pastures above baseline practices and reduce unrestricted grazing by livestock. Pastures will be grazed with higher livestock densities followed by longer periods of rest, increasing both plant productivity and soil carbon inputs relative to baseline conditions. This results in the sequestration of greenhouse gasses from the atmosphere to the soil.
Land operators are provided funding to increase fencing and water infrastructure needed to create more and smaller pastures and to provide the added labor needed to manage more frequent livestock movements. Project participants are required to manage for concentrated animal impact on small pastures with a focus on extended rest periods allowing for regrowth and recovery of leaf tissue, seed establishment, and replenishment of root reserves. In the baseline scenario, the pastures are larger and the livestock movement among pastures is less frequent. This allows grazing animals to select for preferred perennial species, which then become overgrazed and insufficient rest periods favor the encroachment by shrubs, annual grasses, and larger occurrence of bare ground.
The grouped project is on eligible grasslands and parts of Wyoming, Idaho, Washington, North Dakota, and South Dakota. The project area consists of grassland grazed by livestock on participating ranches. Soils throughout the project area are predominantly a mix of sandy and silty clay loams and have been losing carbon for over 100 years due to the continuous, selective grazing under the baseline scenario. Consequently, soils in the project area are modeled to have a high potential to store carbon under intensive, high rotation grazing management.

name: Grouped Captive Solar Power project by Enking International
description: The project involves installation of Solar Photovoltaic (SPV) Panels on rooftops/ground mounted in various states of India. The sole purpose of project activity is to install solar power plant for captive purpose and sur plus generated electricity can be supplied to grid and further equivalent energy will be consumed from grid through net metering arrangement with state electricity board.

name: Macaúbas Landfill Gas Project - CER Conversion
project_type: Energy industries (renewable/non-renewable sources); Waste handling and disposal
description: Macaúbas Landfill Gas Project is a landfill gas collection, use and flare project in Brazil. The project’s core idea is to avoid emissions of methane gas to the atmosphere from the landfill called “Central de Tratamento de Resíduos Macaúbas” (hereinafter referred to as CTR Macaúbas) located in the municipality of Sabará in the state of Minas Gerais, Brazil. The project activity comprises the installation of a new active LFG extraction, flaring and electricity generation systems.
status: Units Transferred from Approved GHG Program

name: Installation of high efficiency cookstoves in India by AGS Carbon
description: The purpose of this Grouped project “Installation of high efficiency cookstoves in India by AGS Carbon” is to reduce the rate of deforestation in the remote areas along with reduce the indoor air pollution. The project will reduce the need for women to collect firewood for longer time. The project will distribute 75,000 ICS (improved cookstoves) to the beneficiaries under first project instance (PI 1). The geographical location of the project is Maharashtra, India.

name: Taiqian County MSW Landfill Site LFG Comprehensive Utilization Project
project_type: Energy industries (renewable/non-renewable sources); Waste handling and disposal
description:
Taiqian County MSW Landfill Site LFG Comprehensive Utilization Project (hereafter referred to as the project) is located at Taiqian County MSW landfill site (hereafter referred to as Taiqian landfill site), in Taiqian County, Puyang City, Henan Province, P.R. China. The project is constructed and operated by Taiqian County BCCY New Energy Co., Ltd.
Taiqian landfill site started collecting and handling waste at the end of 2019.
The project started to construct on 01/05/2021. The project has a total designed capacity 1.5MW (3*0.5MW) and combusts the LFG, which contains nearly 50% of methane, to generate electricity and export it to the Central China Power Grid (CCPG). Total electricity supplied to the grid in the crediting period will be 72,333MWh. VCUs will be claimed from the methane destroyed and the grid electricity displaced. The estimated average GHG emission reductions of the project is 43,296tCO2e and the total GHG emission reductions and removals are 432,960tCO2e during the fixed 10 years crediting period.
Scenario existing prior to the implementation of the project (the same as baseline scenario):
LFG from Taiqian landfill site is emitted to the atmosphere directly.
Equivalent electricity generated by the project is supplied by the CCPG, which is dominated by fossil fuel based power plants.

name: Cleaner cooking access in lower Himalayan region
description: The proposed grouped project activity seeks to reduce greenhouse gases emissions by disseminating fuel- efficient cookstoves in Nepal. The proposed grouped project activity seeks to increase access of households and communities to improved cookstoves by disseminating high thermal efficiency and low greenhouse gas emitting cooking stoves known as Improved Cook Stoves (ICS) to the rural and semi-urban households of Nepal. Their old low efficiency and high greenhouse gas emitting stoves would be replaced. The implementation of the project activity, will result in the reduction of firewood consumption & consequent emissions from combustion leading to climate change mitigation in a sustainable manner. Overall objectives are reduction of greenhouse gases, conservation of forests and woodlands as well as improved health conditions of ICS users due to improved indoor air quality along with drudgery reduction in everyday cooking.

name: Hiwi REDD+ Project
project_type: Agriculture Forestry and Other Land Use
description: The Hiwi REDD+ Project is a 20,505 hectare area of tropical rainforest located close to the municipalities of Bujari, Rio Branco and Porto Acre, in the state of Acre, Northern Brazil. The state of Acre is facing a rise in deforestation due to cattle ranching activities, with an 8.3% increase of cattle heads from 2020 to 2021. The municipality of Rio Branco has the highest cattle herd in the State, with 14% of the total . Bujari also presented an increase of 15.5% from 2018 to 2020 , while Porto Acre the growth was of 23.5% in the same period. Deforestation in the municipalities from 2018 to 2020  had a boost of 198%, 89% and 154%, respectively. The project will promote forest conservation and, consequently, reduce greenhouse gas emission that would occur due to deforestation. A consortium of 4 rural properties comprises the Hiwi REDD+ Project Area.

name: Barry Callebaut feed additive grouped project
project_type: Livestock, enteric fermentation, and manure management
description: The Barry Callebaut feed additive grouped project aims to introduce nature-based feed additives to dairy farms in the United States to reduce greenhouse gas (GHG) emissions from the livestock sector. Methane is a by-product of the enteric fermentation process in cows and is mainly expelled by the animal through belching. The Agolin® Ruminant feed additive used in this project reduces methane (CH4) emissions from enteric fermentation by changing the microbial population in the rumen; it also increases milk production efficiency.

name: Ontario Sustainable Community (OSC)
project_type: Energy demand; Waste handling and disposal
description: This group project is intended to stimulate and reward the Ontarian ICI building owners and operators (Industries, Commerce and Institution) – large or small – for their efforts to reduce GHG emissions, by providing access to the voluntary carbon credit markets and beyond any regulated compliance.  This group project, based under the VM0018 methodology, is designed to be simple, yet rigorous in its application, measurement, and monitoring. Even though the eligible activities vary, energy consumption and waste management, and eventually transportation, are similar across many companies and organizations. The main objectives are as follows: to gradually group inside a Sustainable Community or cluster, up to 50,000 Client Facilities (buildings), located inside the province of Ontario, Canada  that will achieve a potential of 50,278,000 tCO2e of reductions of GHG emissions for the period 2022-2028; to collect ground data in real-time, and consequently, stimulate and enhance Industrial Commercial and Institutional (ICI) buildings to have a better sustainable behaviour. This approach stimulates and rewards all the small actions carried out by each of the ICI sites: diverting industrial and commercial waste from landfills for more efficient waste recovery and increasing energy efficiency in buildings. Transportation efficiency improvements are under development and will be added during the project. This group project will impacts positively on the Sustainable Developments Goals (SDG); 9,10,11,12,13 and 17.  The philosophy of this group project is supported by our endorsement of the Carbon Core concept (CCP) produced in May 2021 by the TSVCM.

name: Tongxu Biogas Recovery and Utilization Project
project_type: Livestock, enteric fermentation, and manure management; Waste handling and disposal
description:
The project is to collect methane from swine manure treatment at Tongxu Lizhai Swine Farm in Tongxu County, Kaifeng City, Henan Province. The project treats the raw manure from 125,650 market swine annually by anaerobic digester, and uses the biogas generated during the treatment process for heat generation. The project owner uses the gravity and scraping system to collect the manure automatically, and all the manure is flushed and pumped to the
anaerobic digester. After anaerobic digestion, the digestate is used for agriculture irrigation aerobically. Therefore, the reduction, resource utilization, harmlessness, and ecological utilization of the manure from the swine farm can be realized.

name: NATURE GENERATOR ONE  Northern Mexico Sustainable Grazing Carbon Capture Project
project_type: Agriculture Forestry and Other Land Use
description: Cultivo’s Nature Generator One as project proponent under VCS VM0026 Methodology for Sustainable Grasslands Management (SGM) will implement a project of sustainable grazing practices on private ranch lands in the geographic area located in the state of Coahuila, Mexico.

name: Blue Ocean Barns - Brominata Enteric Methane Demonstration Project
project_type: Livestock, enteric fermentation, and manure management
description:
The Blue Ocean Barns - Brominata Enteric Methane Demonstration Project (“the Project”) aims to reduce enteric methane emissions from beef and dairy production systems. Asparagopsis taxiformis, a type of seaweed, has been shown to reduce enteric methane production by up to 98% when fed to cattle and, in some instances, improve feed conversion efficiency (Roque 2019, Stefenoni 2020, Kinley 2020, Roque 2021a). Blue Ocean Barns proprietary feed additive, BrominataTM, is an Asparagopsis product that will be fed to cattle as the project activity on different farms throughout the United States.

This is a grouped project that will incorporate approximately three to four project instances (i.e. beef or dairy farms) in three to four states, tentatively including California, Kansas, and Vermont. Prior to implementation of the project, none of the project farms used a feed additive or supplement to reduce enteric methane emissions. Per the methodology and consistent with a conservative approach, this project will only claim tonnes due to the reduction of enteric methane production (not improvements in feed conversion efficiency and related emission reductions), and is anticipated to reduce enteric methane emissions by approximately 835 tonnes (average) annually.

name: Grouped rooftop solar power project by SAEL Limited
description:
The project involves installation of Solar Photovoltaic (SPV) Panels on rooftops of educational institutions in various states of India by SAEL Limited (Previously, Sukhbir Agro Energy Ltd). All the rooftop solar panel units involved in the project are implemented under RESCO model where SAEL acts as a RESCO (Renewable Energy Service Company). Being the RESCO, SAEL has developed, installed, financed, operates and owns the rooftop solar power units and supplies power generated from the project to the consumers on whose premises the rooftop SPV panels are set up. The building owners are the customers of the power generated from the rooftop solar panels who purchase the power from SAEL Limited under long term power purchase agreements signed for 25 years.

The purchased power by the customers is either consumed/utilized by the customers for in the buildings premises or injected to the grid of the Distribution Utility under the mechanism of net metering.

Under the concept of Net Metering, the customers are charged only for the net power that they consume from the electricity service provider that has accumulated over a specific period. In other words, if their renewable energy generating systems make more electricity than consumed, they may be credited or paid for the excess electricity contributed to the grid over the same period. Net metering is also a way to increase the energy in the power grid to keep up with increase in demand during peak power use times, and this is of particular interest to states facing power shortages.

name: HG Afforestation Through High Quality Timber Over Degraded Grasslands
project_type: Agriculture Forestry and Other Land Use
description: The project comprises a total of 790 ha of land previously under extensive grazing by beef cattle, on which a fforestation for obtaining high value, long lived timber products and for sequestering large amounts of carbon dioxide from the atmosphere will be established. Forests are based on 16 year rotation Eucalyptus spp. plantations, mostly managed with pruning and three thinning operations, to obtain knot free, high diameter logs suitable for saw ing or plywood production Plantation will be completed by year 5 of project and forests will be r eplanted after clear cut harvest. The practices are not certified with the FSC standard. Although they are carried out as if they were, because in the near future it is intended to FSC certif ied Planted forests will remove carbon dioxide from the atmosphere and store it in different carbon pools (living above ground and below ground biomass, soil, li tter, non tree vegetation, dead wood and harvested wood products). Monitoring will cover carbon stock changes for living above.

name: Solar Water Pump Project in Kenya
description: The grouped project aims to install state of the art solar irrigation systems in Kenya to mitigate greenhouse gas emissions and assist farmers adapt to these changing climate conditions. With easier access to water for irrigation, the project helps in irrigating the crops even during the dry season (i.e. throughout the year) and planting new crops, thereby increasing the productivity and revenue to the farmers.

name: Poultry Litter to CBG Project by M/s Solika Energy Pvt. Ltd.
description: M/s Solika Energy Private Limited, Hyderabad is setting up a 3.0 TPD compressed biogas (CBG) plant based on poultry litter at Kothaguda village, Kandukur mandal, Rangareddy District in Telangana. The proposed project activity is a step towards supporting the implementation of poultry waste to Bio-CNG production facility in India. The project activity will targets the unexplored potentials of biogas utilization by installing biogas plant with purification system to produce bio-CNG which is equal to CNG in terms of quality and calorific value. The main purpose of the project is to incorporate competent biogas technology and implementation to support in the country by setting up to field scale biogas plant; to be located based on the continuous availability of raw materials. Anaerobic digestion is the prominent technology used for degradation of biodegradable organic waste.

name: TOROS MERAM BIOGAS PLANT
project_type: Energy industries (renewable/non-renewable sources); Livestock, enteric fermentation, and manure management; Waste handling and disposal
description:
Meram Biogas  plant is located in Meram district of Konya, Turkey. Proposed project activity is biogas to energy
project. Within this scope, a biogas and cogeneration facility will be constructed. The digesters and
equipment will be designed to utilize other wastes in the region from agricultural or livestock. Due
to incentives for cattle farms, number of farms and animals will increase in next years and manure
obtained from those farms will create a more significant environmental problem.
Project is designed to collect the manure from those farms and use for biogas and fertilizer
production.  Manure from the digesters will be used as fertilizer.
Installed capacity of project is planned to be 6 MWe (4x1.5MWe). The expected energy generation
is about 42 GWh per year.

name: CO2 INJECTION AND USE OF OTHER MATERIALS TO REDUCE CEMENT CONTENT IN CONCRETE
description:
Ozinga is a leading supplier of ready-mix concrete and other concrete products primarily in the Chicago area.  Ozinga operates 70 ready mix concrete plants across Illinois, Indiana, Wisconsin, Michigan and South Florida.  Under this project activity, Ozinga will use a combination of CO2 injection and alternative materials to develop a concrete mix that has at least a 95% reduction in cement usage, which will result in a net reduction in greenhouse gas (GHG) emissions.  The specific project locations are listed in Appendix I
This project activity will produce ultra-low carbon concrete through the use of high slag replacement hydraulic cement.  As a result of the use of this product, only a fraction of the amount of ordinary Portland Cement is required compared to what is typically found in concrete. Ozinga will be able to produce a concrete that virtually eliminates the use of Portland Cement and can be used under specific applications under ASTM C1157.
Ozinga’s goal is to produce up to 750,000 cubic yards per year from its production facilities in the Midwest.  That would yield an estimated 244,000 tCO2eq reduced per year.  Throughout the crediting period, the average level of emission reductions is estimated to be 128,114 tCO2eq (given the time needed to ramp up).  In the absence of this project activity, Ozinga would use conventional concrete, as it has always done, requiring much larger amounts of cement and thus all of the emissions associated with cement production.

name: Rwandan Improved Cookstove Project
description: This Project involves the distribution of domestic fuel-efficient cook stoves to households within the Republic of Rwanda and will focus on the following districts: Gakenke, Kamonyi, Karongi, Kayonza, Musanze, Ngoma, Nyagatare, and Rwamagana. It is planned to disseminate a total of approximately 500,000 Canarumwe stoves to households, which previously have had no access to improved cookstoves. The improved cook stoves will replace 3-stone fire, which is the predominant stove in the project area. By using the improved cook stoves, fuel consumption will be reduced, thereby reducing the time required for wood collection or reducing costs for firewood for households purchasing wood. The improved efficiency of the stove will also lead to reduced indoor air pollution, thereby improving the health situation especially of women and children.

name: Distribution Of high Efficient Cook Stoves
description: The main purpose of the project is the distribution of fuel-efficient improved cookstoves (ICS) in India. The ICS disseminated through this project will replace the baseline cookstoves. Through this project, the distribution and installation of ICS will be undertaken for households. It is intended that under this project highly efficient cookstoves will be distributed

name: Installation of high efficiency wood burning cookstoves in Angola – Project 2
developer: C-Quest Capital SG Angola Stoves Private Limited
description:
The project involves distribution of fuel-efficient improved cookstoves (ICS) in Angola. The ICS disseminated through this project will replace the baseline cookstoves.  

Through this project, the distribution and installation of approximately 100,000 ICS will be undertaken for households in Angola. It is intended that under this project single pot, TLC-CQC Rocket Stove will be distributed. The ICS will burn wood more efficiently thereby improving thermal transfer to pots, hence saving fuel. Not only will this halt the rapidly progressing deforestation in Angola but will also reduce health hazards from indoor smoke pollution and women and children will have to spend less time collecting firewood. 

The end user will be informed in advance that the use of ICS generates carbon finance which in turn is used for subsidizing the price of ICS and for recovering project implementation costs.

name: BioLite Improved Cook stoves Programme - CER Conversion
description:
The authorized representative of the project, BioLite, is requesting a conversion of 112,613 CERs to VCUs.  More information on the project can be found at CDM PoA Project ID 7997: https://cdm.unfccc.int/ProgrammeOfActivities/poa_db/YNXCPIJ5ZO7DTRGMV0F2AKEU486LQS/view?cp=1. The relevant project documents will be attached soon. The proof of cancellation is attached above.

The CDM Programme of Activities “BioLite Improved Cook stoves Programme” involves the substitution of traditional and inefficient cook stoves with efficient biomass cook stove (wood, charcoal) in rural and/or urban household in India, Kenya and Uganda, in biomass deficient regions. BioLite India Private Limited (BioLite), the coordinating/managing entity (CME) will coordinate the proposed SSC-PoA.
The programme of activity involves replacement of inefficient traditional cook stove with efficient fuel wood cook stoves with single/multiple pans in the rural and/or urban households of biomass deficient areas in India, Kenya and Uganda.
status: Units Transferred from Approved GHG Program

name: Feijó REDD+ Project
project_type: Agriculture Forestry and Other Land Use
description:
The primary objective of the Feijó REDD+ Project is to avoid the unplanned deforestation (AUD) of the 27,248.86 ha project area, and to avoid planned deforestation (APD) of the 5,094.85 ha project area within two private properties in the municipality of Feijó, State of Acre, consisting of 100% Amazon rainforest. 

Beyond the project’s ecological and carbon benefits, a proportion of the carbon credits generated will be dedicated to improving the social and environmental conditions in the project region, specifically contributing to improving deforestation control, and developing environmental education and other social activities. The contribution to sustainability is being monitored through the application of the SOCIALCARBON® Standard. 

The AUD REDD project is expected to avoid a predicted 15,697.94 ha of deforestation, equating to 6,295,553 tCO2e in emissions reductions over the 30-year project lifetime (02-January-2019 to 01-January-2049), with an annual average of 209,852 tCO2e. 
The APD REDD project is expected to avoid a predicted 1,751 ha of deforestation, equating to 7,153,896 tCO2e in emissions reductions over the 30-year project lifetime (02-January-2019 to 01-January-2049), with an annual average of 238,463 tCO2e.

name: Biomass Cogeneration Plant By SCOUL
description: The purpose of the project activity is to utilize available bagasse in SCOUL sugar factory for steam and electricity generation. The project undertaken is a cogeneration plants of capacity 30 MW (with 150 TPH steam generation) located at Lugazi, Uganda. Bagasse based Cogeneration plant will supply steam and electricity to the sugar mill and export the power surplus to the national grid.

name: OKA 2 PROJECT
project_type: Agriculture Forestry and Other Land Use
description:
This savannah Land Afforestation Project on the Batéké Plateau north of Brazzaville aims to develop an alternative and renewable source of charcoal for urban use, based on the establishment of Acacia auriculiformis plantations. Furthermore, Acacia rows will be intercropped with lines of food crops (Cassava in particular), forming agroforestry plantations. 
We also know that another effective tool to combat global warming are 'carbon sink' plantations, i.e. plantations where trees are not harvested, in order to maximize greenhouse gas sequestration in the long term. Half of the project's area will therefore be dedicated to Acacia mangium plantations with the main objective of CO2 sequestration.
These plantations will be set up in anthropogenic savannahs, i.e. land with a biomass stock blocked at a very low stage due to recurrent bushfires. The savannahs are deliberately set to fire at frequent intervals (at least once a year) by villagers to facilitate agricultural, pastoral and cynegetic activities.
As a result, the Project will have several social and environmental benefits such as (1) CO2 sequestration on land that is currently non-forested and unused, (2) Less pressure on the surrounding natural forests, thanks to the production of charcoal from sustainably managed plantations, (3) Job creation in a territory heavily affected by unemployment, increased incomes. As such, the project acts as a driving force of local development and fights against rural exodus or (4) Increased farming production and productivity, contributing to the economic development of local communities.

name: Sustainable Agriculture Land Management Project by Earthallica Naturals
project_type: Agriculture Forestry and Other Land Use
description:
The proposed VCS Agricultural Land Management (ALM) project activity aims at eliminating dependence on chemical fertilizers and pesticides by replacing those with environment friendly organic based soil amendments. The project activity aims at increasing c apacity of soil to sequester carbon and enhance nutrient through mulching, integration of compost and vermicompost manure. The project also holistically aims at achieving sustainable management
practices which not only reduces greenhouse gas (GHG) emission s but also aims at achieving socioeconomic development of the project area.

name: Aztlan Blue Carbon Mangrove CONSERVATION project - Conserving the Marismas NACIONALES of Nayarit
project_type: Agriculture Forestry and Other Land Use
description:
In Mexico, the mangrove areas in Nayarit state are significantly impacted by deforestation. Among the major drivers of the forestation throughout the region, it is possible to identify land use changes altering the hydrology of the region, illegal logging, anthropogenic fires, and shrimp farming, among others.  According to a previous study made for the project proponent, the state of Nayarit had a deforestation rate of 1.03%/year for the period of 2005-2015.

The Project activity is a REDD+ grouped project that aims to address the unplanned deforestation of private and ejidos’ owned wetland areas in the state of Nayarit.  Until this PD version, the grouped project is comprised of 17 project activity instances, being that each one is a wetland area inside an ejido or privately owned land.  In the future, more project activity instances, in state-owned, private or ejidos’ lands, will be added to this grouped project.

Conservation activities include reestablishing canals, maintaining canal structures, soil rehabilitation, deforestation monitoring, cessation of illegal shrimp farming and monitoring of biodiversity.

The project proponent has been engaging with communities in ejidos and private lands since 2016 under a participatory and inclusive approach and will also include more properties as the project is developed.

BlueMX is also conducting strong outreach efforts, conducting capacity building meetings, providing supporting materials in order to empower communities to carry out the conservation activities under a participatory approach integrating cultural, social and gender equity safeguards and in strict respect and transparency to landownership and access to natural resources from the rightful owners of the land.

name: U' Balam'moo A'kalché ó Blue Carbon Mangrove Conservation Project, Conserving Coastal Ecosystems in Campeche to Support Life
project_type: Agriculture Forestry and Other Land Use
description:
In Mexico, the mangrove areas in state of Campeche are significantly impacted by deforestation.  Among the major drivers of the deforestation in the region, it is possible to identify land use changes altering the hydrology of the region, illegal logging, and anthropogenic fires.  According to a study made for the project proponent, the deforestation rate for Laguna de Términos and Petenes is 2.62%/year for the period of 2005-2016.

The Project activity is a REDD+ grouped project that intents to address the unplanned deforestation of wetlands in the state of Campeche. Currently, the grouped project is comprised of 32 project activity instances, 21 in Petenes and 11 in Laguna de Términos.

Until this PD version, the 32 project activity instances are wetland area located inside federally owned, private and ejido lands, across the state of Campeche.  In the future, more project activity instances will be added to this grouped project, being that they will potentially be either in federally/nationally-owned land, private land or in an ejido owned land.

Conservation activities include but are not limited to reestablishing canals, maintaining canal structures, soil rehabilitation, deforestation monitoring, and monitoring of birds and mammals.

The project proponent has been engaging with communities in ejidos and private lands since 2016 under a participatory and inclusive approach and will also include more properties as the project is developed. BlueMX is also conducting capacity building sessions and developing outreach and communication materials to empower communities for jointly conducting the conservation activities.

name: Uh lu'umil Zazil-ha Blue Carbon Mangrove Conservation Project, Conserving Coastal Ecosystems in Quintana Roo to Support Life
project_type: Agriculture Forestry and Other Land Use
description:
In Mexico, the mangrove areas in the state of Quintana Roo are significantly impacted by deforestation. Among the major drivers of the forestation in the region it is possible to identify: storm damage, invasive plants (Casuarina) and real estate development.

According to a previous study made for the project proponent, the deforestation rate in the state of Quintana Roo was 0.25% for the period of 2005-2015. For the Cozumel region specifically, the deforestation rate was 2.74%/year for the same period.

The Project activity is a REDD+ grouped project that intents to address the unplanned deforestation of state-owned, private and ejidos’ mangroves areas in the state of Quintana Roo. Currently, there are 4 project activity instances in this grouped project: 1 in Cozumel and 3 in Othon P. Blanco. In the future, more project activity instances will be added to this grouped project. 

Conservation activities include reestablishing canals, maintaining canal structures, soil rehabilitation, deforestation monitoring, and monitoring of biodiversity.
The project proponent has been engaging with communities in ejidos and private lands since 2016 under a participatory and inclusive approach and will also include more properties as the project is developed. BlueMX will also promote training meetings and materials to empower communities to carry out the conservation activities.

Currently, the grouped project totals 4,860 hectares of wetlands and is estimated to reduce approximately 11,610 t CO2e per year.

name: Reforestation Project in Meghalaya by Shillong Bamboo
project_type: Agriculture Forestry and Other Land Use
description: The proposed project activity is an Afforestation Reforestation and Revegetation (ARR) ARR), through plantation of native bamboo species for the regeneration of degraded lands and livelihood generation in the northeast hilly state of India Meghalaya. Bamboo has the potential to not only address global climate change through its fast sequestration rate of atmospheric carbon, but if combined with value added processing has the potential to address the global trend of deforestation through the provision of a sustainable alternative to traditional timber sources.

name: Changing Lives via Improved Cooking Initiative - India
description: The Grouped project aims to bring a positive change in the livelihoods of project beneficiaries by dissemination of improved cooking devices in India, replacing the use of traditional biomass stoves or lower efficiency biomass stoves (Charcoal/woodfuel) with improved efficiency clean cooking technologies. Climate Secure is the coordinating and managing entity for the Grouped Project, with Earthfit as the co-developer (technology provider and implementation partner). Removall SAS is the founding partner and the key investor in the grouped project. The first project activity under the Grouped project has been initiated in Maharashtra.”

name: Niger Acacia Senegal Plantation Project - CER Conversion
project_type: Agriculture Forestry and Other Land Use
description:
The authorized representative of the project, EcoAct, is requesting a conversion of 44,056 CERs to VCUs.  More information on the project can be found at CDM PoA Project ID 9708: https://cdm.unfccc.int/Projects/DB/ErnstYoung1375258307.15. The relevant project documents and proof of cancellation are attached above. 

This first Nigerien ARR project activity (Niger Acacia Senegal Plantation Project, NASPP hereafter), aims to restore deforested and highly degraded land in the Sudano-Sahelian zone of the Republic of Niger by empowering rural communities to adopt sustainable agro-forestry practices by establishing plantations using native species Acacia senegalensis (Acacia Senegal). This project represents the first effort in Niger to establish Acacia Senegal plantations on a large scale in regions where dry forests are unable to regenerate by natural means. The sale of emission reduction credits from the carbon sequestered in plantations will make the project more viable by providing an additional revenue stream that will supplement income from the sale of gum arabic from the acacia trees.
status: Units Transferred from Approved GHG Program

name: Lanao del Sur Bamboo Reforestation Project
project_type: Agriculture Forestry and Other Land Use
description: The Lanao del Sur Bamboo Reforestation Project is a carbon financed landscape scale restoration project in the province of Lanao del Sur, on the island of Mindanao, Philippines. The project area covers 8,421 hectares of degraded montane landscapes. Project activities target the planting of 2.5 million clumps of native species of sympodial bamboo over a 3-4 year period. Bamboo reforestation activities are combined with the additional planting of 1 million trees of native species on areas not eligible for carbon accreditation, creating a biodiverse and holistic landscape. The project area has been chosen due to its importance as a watershed for neighboring provinces which rely on it for food production, while representing an area that has historically received little development.

name: Wuhan Chenjiachong Landfill Gas Power Generation Project Phase II
developer: Wuhan Jianghuan OneCarbon Energy Development Co., Ltd.
project_type: Energy industries (renewable/non-renewable sources); Waste handling and disposal
description:
Wuhan Chenjiachong Landfill Gas Power Generation Project Phase II (hereafter referred to as “the Project”) is a landfill gas (LFG) recovery and utilization project located at Chenjiachong Landfill Phase II, Chenjiachong Town, Yangluo County, Xinzhou District, Wuhan City, Hubei province, People’s Republic of China. 
The purpose of the Project is to collect LFG from Chenjiachong Landfill Phase II and utilize it for power generation. The Project started construction in December 2019. Four power generators of 1.095 MW each, which add up to 4.38 MW, have been installed, and they were put into operation on 14-July-2020.
The Project achieves emission reductions in two aspects: 1) it avoids methane emissions by capturing and destroying LFG which would have been directly vented into the atmosphere in the baseline scenario; 2) it reduces CO2 emissions by displacing part of the electricity that would otherwise have been supplied by CCPG.

name: Liaoning Xinwang Swine Farm Manure Management System GHG Mitigation Project
developer: Kangping Xinwang agriculture and animal husbandry Co., Ltd.
project_type: Energy industries (renewable/non-renewable sources); Livestock, enteric fermentation, and manure management; Waste handling and disposal
description:
Liaoning Xinwang Swine Farm Animal Manure Management System GHG Mitigation Project (hereinafter referred to as the Project)  introduce animal waste management system (AWMS) to a group of 10 swine farms in Kangping County, Shenyang City, Liaoning Province, China, which are owned by Kangping Xinwang agriculture and animal husbandry Co., Ltd (hereinafter called” Xinwang”). The purpose of the project activity is to treat the manure and wastewater from the 10 swine farms to avoid methane emissions generated in the baseline uncovered anaerobic lagoons.

In this project, AWMS is built to replace the traditional open anaerobic lagoons, and each subsidiary swine farm installed one AWMS. The manure and waster will be collected into the anaerobic digesters and then biogas generated during the anaerobic treatment process will be captured and total 2500*104m3 biogas are expected to be generated annually. Biogas is then sent into biogas boilers for heat production. Every biogas boiler has been installed in each swine farms. All of the heat generated are used by AWMSs and the swine farms, while the rest (if any) will be burned. The sludge produced after fermentation is applied to corn fields as fertilizer, and the wastewater produced by anaerobic biogas digesters is used for agricultural irrigation.
Benefited from the “waste-biogas-fertilizer” pattern, harmlessness and ecological utilization of the swine manure can be realized. All the heat generated by the project will be used by the AWMSs and 10 swine farms. 
The project activity will reduce of GHG in the atmosphere through avoiding methane emissions from anaerobic treatment of swine manure and wastewater. The project is expected to achieve an annual emission reduction of 201,850 tCO2e and a total emission reduction of 1,412,950 tCO2e in the first crediting period.

name: Not Hot Afforestation project
project_type: Agriculture Forestry and Other Land Use
description:
The Not Hot Afforestation project  is designed to afforest non-used agricultural land (meadow)
with birch (Betula pendula) species native to the area. Part of the agricultural lands are not
managed (they do not use food product production). All this time, unmanaged land has brought
virtually no benefit to landowners or to the national economy. There are still about 300 kha of
non-forested agricultural land in Latvia, which meets the criteria of low-valued areas accessible
for afforestation. About 130 thousand ha of agricultural areas have organic soils. The potential for
reducing GHG emissions in such areas are particularly high. 1
This project is a grouped project, located in Latvia.
The Not Hot Afforestation Project will generate GHG removals through sequestration living
biomass and soil organic carbon. These credits are generated using CGM methodology AR-
ACM0003: Afforestation and reforestation of lands except wetlands (version 2).
Implemented activities in the project will remove an amount of 2,203 tons CO₂ in mineral soils
and 55 tons CO₂ in organic soils within 40 years. This means an average of 55 tons CO₂ yr⁻¹ in
mineral soils and 5.87 tons CO₂ yr⁻¹ in organic soils per year. A total area of 5.06 ha activities will
remove 2,438 tCO₂ within 40 years, which means an average of 60.9 tons CO₂ yr⁻¹.
Project will result in a significant contribution to sustainable development of Latvia, mainly
through: i) increased employment and quality of employment; ii) rural development
(decentralization); iii) increased gross value of production; iv) biodiversity preservation and v)
improvement and preservation of soil quality.

name: Malawi Solar Power and Adult Literacy Project
project_type: Energy demand; Energy distribution; Energy industries (renewable/non-renewable sources)
description: SCB Brokers LLC plans to implement a renewable energy project, specifically to provide stable electrical access to underserved peoples while reducing local GHG emissions through the replacement of otherwise carbon-intensive mini-grid captive generation with solar rooftop photovoltaic energy generation.

name: Distribution of ONIL stoves – Project 1
description:
The project involves distribution and installation of ONIL stoves, a type of improved cookstove (ICS). The ONIL stoves disseminated through this project will replace the baseline cookstoves.  

Through this project, the distribution and installation of approximately 35,000 ONIL stoves will be undertaken for households in Guatemala. The ONIL Stove is a fuel-efficient stove that reduces the amount of firewood required by households by up to 58% and results in lower emissions based on its construction. A single ONIL Stove will save 4.501 tons of CO2e per year.   

The ONIL stove will burn wood more efficiently thereby improving thermal transfer to pots, hence saving fuel. Not only will this halt the rapidly progressing deforestation in Guatemala but will also reduce health hazards from indoor smoke pollution and women and children will have to spend less time collecting firewood. 

The end user will be informed in advance that the use of ICS generates carbon finance which in turn is used for subsidising the price of ICS and for recovering project implementation costs.

name: Yunshui Wastewater Treatment Plant Project in Guangdong Province
developer: Yunshui Guangdong Environmental Protection Co., Ltd.
description: The project introduces aerobic wastewater treatment plant to treat wastewater from towns in many regions of Guangdong Province, there are 16 wastewater plants, each using the same treatment process (A2O+MBR). The whole aerobic process includes pre-treatment process, secondary biological treatment process, tertiary deep treatment process and sludge treatment process, with an total maximum design influent flow of 175,150 m3/d and the effluent COD concentration is 40 mg/L. The wastewater is composed of residents' domestic wastewater within the service area. The project can reduce environmental pollution and destroy methane emissions from the open anaerobic lagoons in baseline scenario, the best available low-cost solution for wastewater treatment.

name: Atlantic Forest Biodiversity Conservation Limeira Project REDD
project_type: Agriculture Forestry and Other Land Use
description:
The Limeira Atlantic Forest Biodiversity Conservation Project is located in the state of Paraná, south of Brazil. Its area is located within the Atlantic Forest Biome, home of a great diversity of fauna and flora, including several endemic and endangered species, including the terrestrial tapir (Tapirus terrestrial), the largest terrestrial mammal, described as (endangered, IUNC, 2011) in the Atlantic Forest due to habitat loss ( (Medici et.al., 2011). The preserved forest is an important generator of ecosystems services such as water supply, climate regulation, tourism, energy, unique maintenance , beyond the environment with unique natural beauty. This hot spot on earth suffers a great risk of being converted to non-ecological uses, as 70% of the Brazilian GDP  is concentrated in it, only 12.4% of the original forest is left in Brazil, demonstrating that they cause a huge impact on this forest, which is limited by human development and agricultural.
The project area is the home to more than 50 headwaters, which flow into the São João River, an important water resource in the region. It is part of the only region of the state of Paraná with preserved native vegetation, being an important ecological corridor for the passage of fauna between two large National Parks. Areas such as the project are subject to intense risk every day, mainly due to degradation, which happens little by little, but causes a huge impact on this biome so fragile by human development.
This project extends itself through the territory of the municipalities of Guaratuba and Morretes, inside the rural area where the economy is based on agriculture and extractivism, being bananas and peach palm the main crops. The production and trade of these products is driven by the close Limeira state highways and by the Limeira street which passes through the project’s area from North to South, so it is considered th margins of this road, areas susceptible to deforestation.

name: Boomitra Carbon Farming in the Indo-Gangetic Plains
project_type: Agriculture Forestry and Other Land Use
description:
This project intends to help farmers adopt new improved agriculture practices in the Indo-Gangetic Plains of the Indian subcontinent. Improved agriculture practices include crop residue management, natural farming, crop rotations and more, which enable cropland soils to improve their carbon sequestration capabilities. The region contains large numbers of small and marginal farmers who are highly susceptible to reductions in yields arising from climate change, and there is a strong need for programs and interventions to help them adapt.
In this context, improved agricultural practices provide the opportunity and the power to reverse land degradation and return carbon to the soil, creating carbon removals while improving overall soil health. In this project, farmers adopt a variety of improved agriculture practices. These practices are proven ways to increase soil organic carbon, and enable farmers to improve their productivity: increases in soil organic carbon improve the ability of soils to store moisture and nutrients, and thus also help to increase yields. Boomitra’s research has shown that farmers face various barriers in the adoption of these practices, and this project works towards helping farmers to surmount these barriers, while working with partners to create feasible and sustainable solutions that promote behavioral change at the grassroots level. The financial benefits from carbon credits will provide a direct boost to the livelihoods of these farmers, many of whom are small and marginal farmers.

name: Reducing Gas Leakages within the Titas Gas Distribution Network in Bangladesh
project_type: Fugitive emissions from fuels (solid, oil and gas)
description: The project activity will reduce natural gas leakage in the distribution network of Titas Gas through the implementation of advanced leak detection and repairs (LDAR) procedures. The project activities will include inspection and leak measurements, as well as repair works at components in the natural gas above ground distribution system. using advanced leak detection and measurement technology including HiFlow Samplers. Leak Measurement Devices and Gas Surveyors as well as advanced repair materials. In addition, selected staff of Titas Gas will be trained in advanced leak detection, measurement, and repair techniques.

name: Grassland Restoration and Stewardship in South Africa (GRASS)
project_type: Agriculture Forestry and Other Land Use
description: The Grassland Restoration and Stewardship in South Africa (GRASS) grouped project is designed to unlock, upscale and incentivize the adoption of improved agricultural land management and ecosystem restoration in the grassy biomes of South Africa. The Herding for Health (H4H) model is to be employed under this project. The model includes farmer and herder empowerment through smallholder livestock value chain development to build resilience to climate change. Furthermore, the model supports rangeland restoration and greenhouse gas (GHG) sinks while reducing GHG emissions by sequestering carbon into the soil and reducing methane emissions from livestock enteric fermentation.

name: North Bandai Bamboo Reforestation Project
project_type: Agriculture Forestry and Other Land Use
description:
The North Bandai Bamboo Reforestation Project is a reforestation project that is restoring 2,863 hectares of degraded forest lands within the Ashanti Region of Ghana, West Africa. It is a carbon financed project that integrates the reforestation of 1 million seedlings of sympodial bamboo with remnant standing trees, and areas set aside for biodiversity and conservation. The project area has suffered extreme historical deforestation and represents highly degraded lands that are prone to further loss of remaining tree cover in the absence of the reforestation activity. 

The project is managed alongside the adjacent Bandai Hills Bamboo Reforestation Project to represent a combined 10,681 hectare unique approach to forest landscape restoration.

Their old cookstoves with low efficiency and high greenhouse gas emitting would be replaced with ICS. The implementation of the project activity will result in the reduction of firewood consumption & consequent emissions from combustion sustainable leading to climate change mitigation. Overall objectives of the project activity are to reduce greenhouse gases emissions, conservation of forests and woodlands while improving the health conditions of ICS users due to less emission and improve indoor air quality for everyday cooking.

name: Adjusted Water Management in Rice Cultivation in Jiashan County
developer: Hangzhou Chunmeng Agricultural Technology Co., Ltd
project_type: Agriculture Forestry and Other Land Use
description:
he project changing from continuously flooded to intermittent flooded condition during rice cultivation is conducted in Jiashan County under the jurisdiction of Jiaxing City, Zhejiang Province of China, which have a total acreage of 12,005 ha for single-cropping rice. Without this project providing ditches to conduct intermittent flooded method, the continuously flooded method would be continued, so the scenario that rice was cultivated by continuously flooded method is the baseline scenario. Since the organic matter in rice soil under flooded condition can emit a large amount of methane (CH4) because of anaerobic decomposition, the intermittent flooded method is more beneficial to water conservation, production increase and methane emission removal than the continuously flooded.
The implementation of the project is expected to reduce the GHG emissions amounting to 419,328 tCO2e in the first seven-year period with an average annual GHG emission reduction of 59,904 tCO2e.

Since the organic matter in rice soil under flooded condition can emit a large amount of methane (CH4) because of anaerobic decomposition, the intermittent flooded method is more beneficial to water conservation, production increase and methane emission removal than the continuously flooded.

name: BONOS LAGUNA SÍJIL NOH-HÁ
project_type: Agriculture Forestry and Other Land Use
description:
The Ejido Felipe Carrillo Puerto (from now on “the Ejido”) is in the state of Quintana Roo’s central region, in southwestern Mexico. Declared a Forest Ejido in 1947 (U'yo'olché A.C., 2005). It is currently inhabited by 288 Ejido landowners and their families. The population of the site is mostly comprised of peninsular Mayans. Since its origins, the jungle has been exploited for the extraction of chewing gum found in the chicozapote tree (Manilkara zapota). 

The principal aim of this Project is the removal of greenhouse gas (GHG) emissions through activities that allow the identification, prioritisation, and execution of actions for the adequate management of dry tropical forest, the advancement of sustainable development, the establishment of local governance and the promotion of improved forest management activities.

The Project began in February 2018 and has an expected duration of 30 years; during this period, the removal of 6,459,222 CO2e is expected, this implies an average annual removal of 215,307 tCO2e.
This project will provide community benefits related to the strengthening of local governance and positive externalities to the management of forests. Meanwhile, maintaining sustainable community management practices for tropical forests, with a greater perception of the value of ecosystem services, as well as increasing employment opportunities. 

Finally, is also expected to use the CCB Program in conjunction with VCS to empower local communities and help protect endangered species.

name: Forest Conservation in Boumba-et-Ngoko
project_type: Agriculture Forestry and Other Land Use
description:
The project is located in one of the densest and most important forest areas in Cameroon, in the southern part of the eastern region, near the border with Congo and the Central African Republic. It is a state-owned forest granted in concession for the exploitation of wood resources, and like all neighboring areas, is of great economic interest due to the presence of high-value timber species. Since 2002, this forest unit has been managed by the company La Filière Bois (LFB), which harvests volumes of commercial timber from it, following the terms of the management plan that was drawn up at the start of management.
The VCS Improved Forest Management (IMF) - Logged to Protected Forest (LtPF) project aims to preserve a part of the forest from the exploitation of forest resources, which would anyway be used in the following years as foreseen in the documents approved by the Ministère des Forêts et de la Faune (MINFOF) - Ministry of Forests and Wildlife. The area that will be exempted from the work is approximately 44’413 ha for an estimated volume of 38 m3 /ha of forest not been harvested.
From the implementation of the Project, it is estimated that a net average of 325’885 tonnes of GHG emissions will be avoided from entering the atmosphere annually. Over the entire Project Crediting Period, it is estimated that a net total of 6’517’703 tonnes of GHG emissions will be avoided through the implementation of the Project.

project_type: Agriculture Forestry and Other Land Use
description:
Gansu Zhangye Grouped Afforestation Project (hereafter “the project”) is located in Zhangye City, Gansu Province of China. The project’s aim is to increase carbon sequestration and contribute to local sustainable development by planting trees on the barren lands. The grouped project combines multiple project activity instances into a single, combined project that adds new instances over time. The project proponent sets the geographic boundaries for the grouped project, including where new project activity instances may be added (Section 2.1.7), and establishes criteria for determining the eligibility of future instances (Section 2.1.21).
For the initial project activity instance, 11,011.93 ha of forest is to be planted by direct planting on barren lands in Zhangye City, and the planted trees and shrub are all native species which including Elaeagnus angustifolia (oleaster), Armeniaca sibirica (prumus armeniaca), Populus L. (aspen), Ulmus pumila L. (elm), Picea asperata Mast. (spruce), Pinus sylvestris (mongolian pine), Haloxylon ammodendron (synonym), Caragana korshinskii Kom (caragana microphylla) . It is expected that the scope of the project will increase. For the inclusion of new eligible areas as project instances willing to participate within the grouped project, the new areas shall meet the criteria listing in Section 2.1.21. According to the project design report, 53,000 hectares of new afforestation area is expected to be added from 2021 to 2027. The implementation of the afforestation project will generate GHG emission removals and mitigate climate change; improve soil and water conservation and forest cover; enhance local biodiversity by increasing the connectivity of forests and bring income and job opportunities for local communities and residents.

name: Boomitra Grassland Restoration in Northern Mexico
project_type: Agriculture Forestry and Other Land Use
description: This project works with the ranchers of northern Mexico who raise livestock on individually owned or community-owned grasslands and enables those ranchers to adopt Improved Grassland Management (IGM). Ranchers in this region have traditionally followed practices such as continuous grazing, without any sustainable grazing or water management plans in place. This has resulted in overgrazing, leading to severe soil degradation, loss of vegetative cover and even desertification. When ranchers then become unable to sustain their livelihoods on their degraded ranches, they are sometimes forced to sell their land to farmers who convert the grasslands into croplands, resulting in further CO2 emissions and loss of natural flora and fauna. Through this project, ranchers are adopting new management practices, which include rotational grazing and a variety of water conservation measures. In rotational grazing, livestock are rotated between different sections of a pasture over the course of days, weeks, or months, while other sections of the pasture are allowed to rest. These sections are known as “paddocks”. This practice allows plants to recover and grow in the paddocks that are allowed to rest, and thus allows them to sequester carbon, gradually regenerating the land. In addition, for arid regions like northern Mexico, water conservation measures help increase the availability of water (which would otherwise be lost) for the growth of the biomass, contributing to the regeneration. The livelihoods of the communities utilizing these ranches are improved directly through the carbon credit payments, which provide an additional source of income, and indirectly through the increased productivity of their lands. The regenerated lands also become much less likely to undergo land use change, because the ranchers are better able to sustain their livelihoods. This in turn ensures that crucial habitats for the flora and fauna of the region are protected.

abuse_descr: An inquiry from The Washington Post shows how the pressure to produce carbon credits at a low cost led the company to cut corners in a way that ultimately backfired on the people it was trying to help. Most directly, C-Quest failed to take steps to ensure that its clay and metal cookstoves were being widely used and working properly, critical to ensuring that the project was reducing greenhouse gas emissions and deforestation. name: Boomitra Carbon Farming South of the Vindhyas
project_type: Agriculture Forestry and Other Land Use
description:
This project works with the farmers of southern and central India to help them adopt improved agricultural practices such as residue management and enhanced cropping practices that sequester carbon while increasing productivity. This region is largely composed of small and marginal farmers, with each farming just a few hectares of land. As a result, these farmers are highly susceptible to variabilities arising from markets and weather. 
Over the last century, agriculture in the region has undergone a dramatic shift towards intensification. Since the late 1940s, yields of all staple crops have seen a several-fold increase. This increase was necessary to feed a growing population, but at the same time, it led to an increase of 150kg/ha in the amount of synthetic fertilizer applied to farms, along with similar increases in other crop inputs. An intensive agricultural process focused on maximizing yields every year has led to a gradual degradation of the soils of the region, resulting in CO2 emissions from the lost soil carbon. 
In this context, improved agricultural practices provide the opportunity and the power to reverse this land degradation and return carbon to the soil, creating carbon removals while improving overall soil health. In this project, farmers adopt a variety of improved agriculture practices. These practices are proven ways to increase soil organic carbon, and also enable farmers to improve their productivity: increases in soil organic carbon improve the ability of soils to store moisture and nutrients, and thus also help to increase yields. This project works towards helping farmers to surmount their barriers, while working with partners to create feasible and sustainable solutions that effect grass-roots behavior change. Furthermore, the financial benefits from carbon credits will provide a direct boost to the livelihoods of these farmers, many of whom are small and marginal farmers.

description:
The Guangxi Fangcheng District IFM (conversion of logged to protected forest) Project (hereafter “the project activity”) is implemented in Fangcheng District, Guangxi Zhuang Autonomous Region of China by Fangchenggang Fangcheng District Jinsui Agriculture Investment Co., Ltd, the geo-coordinate of the  project is  107°27'E -108°30'E and 20°30'N - 22°00'N, the total area is 6238 km2, which includes  the  Improved  Forest  Management  (IFM)  of  the forests in the conversion of logged to protected forest.

All these forests are state-owned forests or privately-owned forests or collective-owned forests, and have the legal right to forest ownership. All the owners authorized the project proponent to access the project to their behalf. The species involved in the project are Pinus elliottii and Pinus massoniana. The forest of the project was older plantations under managing. Before the implantation of the project, the usual type of management was clearcutting.
Before the implementation of the project activity, the trees are logged based on a valid and verifiable government-approved timber management plan for harvesting the project area. The implementation of the project activity converses the trees to protected forest to reduce the GHG emissions for about 1,899,564 tCO2e in 20 years, the average annual emission reduction is 94,978 tCO2e and Verified Carbon Units with buffer deduction is about 1,462,648 tCO2e in 20 years, and average annual VCUs with buffer deduction is 73,132 tCO2e.
The project activity will contribute to the environment (biodiversity conservation, rocky desertification prevention and soil erosion control), thus contribute to development.

name: BINZHOU TOPIGS NORSVIN BREEDING SWINE CO., LTD. BINHAI SWINE FARM BIOGAS RECOVERY AND UTILIZATION PROJECT
developer: Binzhou Topigs Norsvin Breeding Swine Co., Ltd. Binhai Branch
project_type: Energy industries (renewable/non-renewable sources); Livestock, enteric fermentation, and manure management; Waste handling and disposal
description:
Binzhou Topigs Norsvin Breeding Swine Co., Ltd. Binhai Swine Farm Biogas Recovery and Utilization Project is located in Zhanhua District, Binzhou City, Shandong Province, P.R China. The project is owned and implemented by Binzhou Topigs Norsvin Breeding Swine Co., Ltd. Binhai Branch.
This project is to build an anaerobic animal manure treatment system to treat manure waste of breeding swine in the Binhai Breeding Swine Farm. The project uses the HDPE membrane enclosed anaerobic digesters to treat animal manure waste, and the biogas produced in this process will be recovered and utilized by the biogas heating system for heat supply during the heating period (October to April next year). During the non-heating period (May to September),the biogas will be burnt through the biogas flare system. The residual waste from the digesters will be handled aerobically to produce organic fertilizer at the project site.
Prior to the implementation of the project, the animal manure waste was left to decay in anaerobic manure management system (uncovered open lagoon) at the Binhai Breeding Swine Farm and methane is emitted to the atmosphere directly without any methane recovery and destruction facility.
The project is expected to avoid GHG emission of methane through recovery and destruction of biogas. For conservativeness, the emission reduction from the biogas heating system is not considered. The project is expected to achieve an annual emission reduction of 11,795 tCO2e and a total emission reduction of 82,563 tCO2e during the first 7-year renewable crediting period.

name: The NFC Uganda Carbon Landscapes Project
developer: New Forests Company Holdings I Limited
project_type: Agriculture Forestry and Other Land Use
description:
The New Forests Company (NFC) was founded in 2004 in Uganda with the vision of creating a sustainable timber resource in East Africa amidst significant deforestation. From the start, the Company adopted a Shared Value approach to doing business that recognizes the need for the three C’s of Conservation, Community and Commerce in order to thrive and be sustainable. Furthermore, NFC has been FSC (Forest Stewardship Council) certified continuously in Uganda since 2009, demonstrating the Company’s commitment to responsible forestry practices that benefit the environment and local communities.
Within 5 years, NFC established three greenfield commercial plantations at Namwasa, Kirinya and Luwunga. Namwasa and Luwunga are government concessions within Central Forest Reserves (CFR) that were proclaimed in the 1930s, but management of the reserves weakened  after independence. The CFRs subsequently suffered from high levels of deforestation and encroachment of subsistence farming and charcoal production. The Kirinya plantation was established on an abandoned sugar cane farm that was established in the 1970s.
abuse_descr: Over 22,000 peasants, some with land titles, were violently evicted from the Mubende and Kiboga districts in Uganda to make way for the UK-based New Forests Company (NFC). Their land claims were being considered by the Ugandan courts when, they allege, the army and police forced them out in several waves of violent evictions which took place up to 2010.

name: Muyuan WJZ AWMS GHG Mitigation Project in Henan Province
project_type: Energy industries (renewable/non-renewable sources); Livestock, enteric fermentation, and manure management; Waste handling and disposal
description:
The project introduces new animal waste management systems to treat the manure from 7 swine farms in Nanyang City and Zhumadian City, Henan Province. Each subsidiary swine farm will install one animal waste management system (AWMS), and the manure is treated on site. The purpose of the project activity is to treat the manure and wastewater to avoid methane emissions generated in the baseline uncovered anaerobic lagoons. 
The project activity uses flushing system to collect the manure automatically. All the manure and wastewater are collected and then be separated first. The solid will be treated in aerobic composting system and the organic fertilizers will be produced, the fertilizer produced in this process will be distributed to local farmers for free and the surplus will be sold in domestic market. The liquid will be treated through anaerobic digestion and the biogas generated during the treatment process will be captured for heat generation. The sludge produced from anaerobic digestion will be treated through aerobic composting together with the solid, the effluent will be supplied to the farmers living around free for agriculture irrigation.
It is estimated that approximately 1,637 tons of animal manure will be handled daily by the AWMS. The biogas released during the anaerobic digestion will be collected and used for heat production. The heat production is estimated to be 657,340GJ. Also, the generated heat will be only used for daily operation of the AWMSs and the 7 swine farms themselves and will not be provided to other users. For conservativeness, baseline emissions from heat generation are neglected.
The project activity will reduce of GHG in the atmosphere through avoiding methane emissions from anaerobic treatment of swine manure and wastewater. It is estimated that 321,663tCO2e emission reductions will be produced annually.
