total area of 1.260.222 ha at the beginning of the monitoring period. The project aims to
contribute to mitigate the effects caused by climate change by reducing 27.686.867 tCO2
emissions derived from deforestation and forest degradation during the 30-year crediting period.
The main activities during the Project lifetime focus in the development of productive activities compatible with
community well-being and nature conservation, providing food security, improving social
investment, strengthening land use planning and self-government structure, monitoring biodiversity and
forest conservation. These activities aim to control and reduce the incidence of deforestation
drivers such as wood extraction, mining and illegal productive activities.
The area is characterized by its high biodiversity along with social unrest and deforestation.
Among the activities carried out by the promoters of deforestation are moving the border of
farming activities (especially subsistence agriculture and livestock), mining, wood harvesting for
commercial and community use, illegal crops and colonization processes. The social problems
are triggered by the absence of the government, lack of sanitation infrastructure, education,
health programs and shortage of technological guidance for sustainable development.
This project focuses on the AFOLU (Agriculture, Forestry and Other Land Uses) sectors. Inside
the category for Reducing emissions from deforestation and forest degradation in developing
countries (REDD+). Its goal is to mitigate the effects caused by climate change through
reduction of CO2 emissions from deforestation and forest degradation, restauration of degraded
forest lands, promotion of the sustainable wood harvesting and carry out development activities
for the community well-being.

name: Henan Shunhe CMM Power Generation Project
developer: Yongcheng Hongqiao Environmental Protection Energy Co. Ltd.
description:
Henan Shunhe CMM Power Generation Project (hereinafter referred to as the Project) is located in Shunhe township, Yongcheng, Shangqiu City, Henan Province, China. The purpose of the Project is to utilize the extracted coal mine methane (CMM) with low concentration methane concentration to produce electricity. No coal bed methane (CBM) or ventilation air methane (VAM) utilization is involved.
Ten sets of CMM power generators will be installed with a total installed capacity of 2.1MW (3*0.7MW), destroying 4.347 million m3 of methane annually. After the full operation of the Project, the expected annual exported electricity will be 11,320 MWh, which will be supplied to the coal mine first through the electricity distribution network in Shunhe coal mine area, replacing the electricity that would otherwise have been purchased from the CCPG and displace part of the electricity generated by CCPG dominated by fossil fuel-fired power plants.
The emissions reduction of the Project comes from two sources: 1) Methane (CH4) emissions as a result of the previously vented gas that will be captured and destroyed in the project scenario; 2) CO2 emissions from the production of the equivalent amount of electricity replaced by the Project that would otherwise have been purchased from the CCPG.

The proposed project comprises of fermentation system and fertilizer production system, etc. It is estimated that approximately 78,000tons of manure and 19,500tons of biomass waste residue can treat annually, therefore total 97,500 tons of waste can be composted aerobically for this project. name: Dak Lak Wastewater Treatment with Biogas System and Methane Recovery
description:
An anaerobic covered lagoon is a simple, effective and reliable technology to capture anaerobic lagoon produced biogas. The material used to cover the anaerobic lagoon is a synthetic high-density polyethylene (HDPE). The necessary materials used must be UV resistant, hydrophobic, tear and puncture resistant, non-toxic to bacteria and has a bulk density near that of water. HDPE is one of the most used geo-membranes used worldwide due to its UV, ozone and chemical resistance. This covering approach in the lagoon prevents methane emissions and reduces odour. This project activity will capture and combust methane gas produced from the anaerobic portion of an existing wastewater treatment system. 
The biogas lagoon is built in the form of an embankment lagoon by earth, the walls and bottom are compacted, lined with 1mm HDPE tarp, and all the surface is covered with 1.5 mm HDPE tarp. The biogas lagoon has a volume of 130,260m3, 151 m long, 136 m wide, 9m deep and is used for the main purpose of decomposing organic compounds in anaerobic conditions. 
To combust the excess biogas, an enclosed type of ground flare with fully automatic operation, including temperature measurement, has been installed. Flaring is fully automatic and continuous: starting when the biogas reaches an established high pressure setting and stopping when biogas pressure drops to an established low pressure setting. An automatic flare ignition system ensures methane is combusted whenever biogas is present at the flare. The flare includes thermocouples to monitor flare exhaust gas temperature, which is measured and recorded.

These forests are also directly critical to the lives and well-being of most of the community residing in this area. The communities around the project area are dependent on arable farming, semi-commercial trading, salaried employees, and charcoal production. The main livelihood of people here is arable farming and charcoal production. The integrated REDD+ Project in Zambia is an Avoided Unplanned Deforestation and Degradation. The project initiative proceeds with promoting mitigation of climate change through conservation and other activities. This REDD+ Project is basically a community based REDD+ project with no evictions and no conflicts involved.

name: Yufeng Adjusted Water Management in Rice Cultivation
developer: Guizhou Xinzhanxin Agricultural Technology Co., Ltd.
project_type: Agriculture Forestry and Other Land Use
description:
The project changing from continuously flooded to intermittent flooded condition during rice cultivation is conducted in Yuqing County and Fenggang County, Guizhou Province, where located in southwestern China with a total acreage of 19,102 ha for single-cropping rice. Without the implementation of this project, which provides ditches to conduct intermittently flooded method, the backward continuously flooded method would be continued, so the scenario that rice was cultivated by continuously flooded method is the baseline scenario. Since the organic matter in rice soil under flooded condition can emit a large amount of methane (CH4) because of anaerobic decomposition, the intermittent flooded method is more beneficial to water conservation, production increase and methane emissions decrease than the continuously flooded.
The implementation activities of the project include cement ditch construction, reservoir construction and necessary training for farmers to help them conduct the intermittent flooded water regime during rice cultivation, which replaces the traditional flooded method. Controllable irrigation and drainage according to the needs of rice growth can not only save water resources, but also reduce methane emissions from soil organic matter under anaerobic conditions (flooded state). In this case, the CH4 emission can be declined by an average of 48% . Hence, with the proposed project activity, an estimated amount of GHG emission reduction 3.13 tCO2e/ha for rice is expected.
The implementation of the project is expected to reduce the GHG emissions amounting to 418,572 tCO2e in the first seven-year period, with an average annual GHG emission removal of 59,796 tCO2e.
This project aims to:
- Sequester greenhouse gas and mitigate climate changes
- Increase the rice productivity resulting in higher living standard of local farmers
- Provide more job opportunities, especially female workers
- Use a proportion of benefits to improve the local children’s education

name: Tanghe AMMS GHG Mitigation Project
project_type: Energy industries (renewable/non-renewable sources); Livestock, enteric fermentation, and manure management; Waste handling and disposal
description:
The project introduces new animal waste management systems (AWMSs) to treat the manure from 11 existing swine farms in Nanyang City, Henan Province. The purpose of the project activity is to treat the manure and wastewater to avoid methane emissions generated in the baseline uncovered anaerobic lagoons. 
All the manure and wastewater are collected and then be separated first. The solid will be treated in aerobic composting system and the organic fertilizers will be produced, part of the fertilizer produced in this process will be distributed to local farmers for free and the others will be sold in domestic market. The liquid will be treated through anaerobic digestion and the biogas generated during the treatment process will be captured and sent to boilers for heat generation and Surplus biogas will be destroyed through the flaring system (if any). The sludge produced from anaerobic digestion will be treated through aerobic composting together with the solid, the effluent will be supplied to the farmers living around free for agriculture irrigation.
It is estimated that approximately 1,759 tons of animal manure will be handled daily by the AWMSs and 3,531.53*104m3 of biogas can be produced annually. Also, the generated heat through biogas will be only used for daily operation of the AWMSs and the 11 swine farms themselves and will not be provided to other users. For conservativeness, baseline emissions from heat generation are neglected.

description:
The project changing from continuously flooded to intermittent flooded condition during rice cultivation is conducted in Xishui County and Renhuai City, Guizhou Province, where located in southwestern China with a total acreage of 18,852 ha for single-cropping rice. Without the implementation of this project, which provides ditches to conduct intermittently flooded method, the backward continuously flooded method would be continued, so the scenario that rice was cultivated by continuously flooded method is the baseline scenario. Since the organic matter in rice soil under flooded condition can emit a large amount of methane (CH4) because of anaerobic decomposition, the intermittent flooded method is more beneficial to water conservation, production increase and methane emissions decrease than the continuously flooded.
The implementation activities of the project include cement ditch construction, reservoir construction and necessary training for farmers to help them conduct the intermittent flooded water regime during rice cultivation, which replaces the traditional flooded method. Controllable irrigation and drainage according to the needs of rice growth can not only save water resources, but also reduce methane emissions from soil organic matter under anaerobic conditions (flooded state) In this case, the CH4 emission can be declined by an average of 48% . Hence, with the proposed project activity, an estimated amount of GHG emission reduction 3.17 tCO2e/ha for rice is expected.
The implementation of the project is expected to reduce the GHG emissions amounting to 417,900 tCO2e in the first seven-year period, with an average annual GHG emission removal of 59,700 tCO2e.
This project aims to:
- Sequester greenhouse gas and mitigate climate changes.
- Increase the rice productivity resulting in higher living standard of local farmers.
- Provide more job opportunities, especially female workers.
- Use a proportion of benefits to improve the local children’s education.

name: Xinjiang Burqin Improved Grassland Management Project
developer: Burqin Jinhua Urban Construction and Investment Co.Ltd.
project_type: Agriculture Forestry and Other Land Use
description:
Xinjiang Burqin Improved Grassland Management Project (hereafter as “the project”) is located in Burqin County, Altai City, Xinjiang Uygur Autonomous Region, China. The project is aimed to restore the local degraded grassland ecosystem from adoption of sustainable grassland management practices, such as improving the rotation of grazing animals between summer and winter pastures, limiting the timing and number of grazing animals on degraded pastures, and restoration of severely degraded land by replanting with perennial grasses and ensuring appropriate management over the long-term.
There are two main restoration measures in the project: 1) Grass seeding was implemented in 5,000 ha of the severely degraded grasslands where grass seeds of local high-quality forage was sowed under the condition of fencing enclosure for 2 years, and then the grassland should be used reasonably and sustainably according to the local approved livestock carrying capacity. 2) Imposing grazing prohibition measures and building fences on 60,000 hectares of degraded grassland in order to strengthen the protection and improvement of the grassland and to prevent excessive cultivation, grazing or human destruction. 
Besides these main restoration measures, the project also alleviates soil desertification and restore grassland vegetation to improve soil carbon storage and local biodiversity through grassland management measures, such as daily management measures from other protect projects like rodent and pest control and grassland fire prevention to ensure the long-term sustainable management of the project area.

name: Nanzhao County MSW Landfill Site LFG Pollution Treatment and Comprehensive Utilization Project
project_type: Energy industries (renewable/non-renewable sources); Waste handling and disposal
description: Nanzhao County MSW Landfill Site LFG Pollution Treatment and Comprehensive Utilization Project (hereafter referred to as the project) is located in Dongzhuang Village, Chengjiao town, Nanzhao County, Nanyang City, Henan Province, P.R. China. The project is invested, constructed and operated by Nanzhao County Baichang New Energy Co., Ltd. The objective is to collect the landfill gas (LFG) from Nanzhao County MSW landfill site (hereafter referred to as Nanzhao landfill site) and utilize it to generate electricity.

name: The Central Europe CowCredit project: A dairy initiative to reduce methane from enteric fermentation in Central Europe
project_type: Livestock, enteric fermentation, and manure management
description:
The Central Europe CowCredit project (multiple instances of Project activity) aims to involve the dairy industry in Central Europe with the purpose to reduce greenhouse gas (GHG) emissions from the livestock sector.  The project activity introduces Mootral® natural feed supplement into dairy cattle diet aiming to reduce methane (CH4) emissions from enteric fermentation by direct inhibition of methanogens in the rumen. 
The project activity includes Germany, Czech Republic, Hungary, Poland, Slovakia and Austria. It aims to add more instances over the 10 years of the first crediting period. The project implementation results in a substantial net reduction of GHG emissions, because of the avoidance of CH4 release into the atmosphere. Methane is a by-product of the enteric fermentation process and is expelled by the animal through belching. Prior to the start of the proposed project activity, there were no similar enteric methane reduction activities, therefore, this leads to CH4 released into the atmosphere (“the business as usual”).  Over the 10 years of the first crediting period, the project will generate an estimated annual average reduction of 600’000 tons of carbon dioxide equivalent (tCO2e) and 6'000'000 tons over the 10 years of the first crediting period (from 01/07/2022 to 30/06/ 2032). The Project is quantified and will be monitored according to VCS methodology “VM0041 Methodology for the Reduction of Enteric Methane Emission from Ruminants through the Use of 100% Natural Feed Supplement” and falls under VCS Sectoral Scope 15, Livestock and manure management.

name: Restoring Mangroves in Mexico's Blue Carbon Ecosystems
project_type: Agriculture Forestry and Other Land Use
description:
Restoring Mangroves in Mexico's Blue Carbon Ecosystems grouped project (’BlueMX Project’), is a mangrove reforestation and restoration project containing many project instances spread across four Mexican states: Campeche, Nayarit, Quintana Roo and Veracruz.  The project is being developed and managed by BlueMX Mangrove A.C. in Mexico (‘BlueMX’) in collaboration with local community landowners called ejidos (including indigenous communities), private landowners, government agencies and other local partners.  

In total, the project activities will restore approximately 35,000 hectares of degraded mangrove areas thereby removing 31,278,014 tons of carbon over 30 years.  It is an Agriculture, Forestry and Other Land Use (AFOLU) project under VCS and the specific project activity referenced in this Project Design Document is Afforestation, Reforestation and Revegetation (ARR).  

The project instances are located in three different ecosystems: 1) the coastal plain of the Gulf of Mexico, 2) the Central Mexico Pacific coast, and 3) the Caribbean coastline on the Yucatan Peninsula.  The marshy and wetland ecosystems constitute one of the most important coastal ecological units in Mesoamerica due to their natural productivity and biodiversity. These regions have experienced significant removal and destruction of mangroves through land conversion to other uses, including industry and agricultural purposes (primarily cattle ranching and now palm oil), Aquaculture (shrimp farming), and local infrastructure development, such as road and bridge construction.

name: SHANDONG LIJIN BREEDING SWINE FARM BIOGAS RECOVERY PROJECT
developer: Lijin Huayu Breeding Swine Co., Ltd.
description:
Shandong Lijin Breeding Swine Farm Biogas RecoveryProject(hereinafter referred to as the Project) locates inLijin Huayu Breeding Swine Farm, Kongjiazao Village, Mingji Township, Lijin County, Dongying City, Shandong Province, P.R China. The project is owned and implementedby LijinHuayuBreeding SwineCo., Ltd.
The project is tointroduces anew anaerobic animal manure management system to treat manure waste (Breeding swine) from Lijin Huayu Breeding Swine Farm. This project uses USR(Up-flow Solid Reactor) to treat animal manure, and collect and destroy the generated biogas to avoid methane emissions.The generatedbiogas will be captured and sent to flaring withinthe project site. The residual waste from the USRdigesters will be sent outside of the project site for aerobic composting and then returned to the field as fertilizer.
Prior to the implementation of the project, the swinemanure waste was left to decay in anaerobic manure management system at the LijinHuayu Breeding Swine Farmand generated methane is emitted to the atmosphere directly without any methane recovery and destruction facility.
The project is expected to avoid GHG emission of methane through recovery and destruction of biogas. The project is expected to achieve an annual emission reduction of 17,727tCO2e and a total emission reduction of 124,089tCO2e during the first 7-year crediting period.

name: Grouped Reforestation Project by Cropzone Agro Forestry Private Limited
project_type: Agriculture Forestry and Other Land Use
description:
Crop Zone Agro Forestry Limited (CZAFL) is proposing a grouped Afforestation, Reforestation and  Revegetation (ARR) in Andhra Pradesh, Telangana, Karnataka and Maharashtra state of India. CZAFL is the Project Proponent (PP) whereas EKI Energy Services Limited (Enking International) is providing 
carbon credit advisory services to the PP. The CZAFL has mobilized the farmers in the selected states of India to plant various tree species on their lands. These tree species range from fruit bearing trees like Indian blackberry, Guava, Mango to commercial species like Teak, Mahogany and Sandal. Simple 
tree cultivation techniques involving planting saplings in the pits with minimum disturbance to the lands have been employed. The lands selected for the project activity is fallow agriculture land. The PP has made contract with the farmers/land owners where they will be given tree saplings and technical support. In return, the PP will reap the benefits through sale of carbon credits. Initially, 501.7 hectares of land has been selected for the first project activity instance. Through carbon sequestration by the planted trees, the project is expected to generate annual average GHG emission reductions of removals of 10,571 tCO2e.

name: Mangrove Restoration Project with Sine Saloum and Casamance communities, Senegal
project_type: Agriculture Forestry and Other Land Use
description:
The proposed mangrove restoration grouped project intends to generate GHG emission removals by restoring the ecosystems through the plantation of up to 16,000 hectares of mangrove. Within the first project instance of this project, the project activities will be carried out over an area of 7,020 hectares, by planting at least 35 million of new mangrove trees. The project area is located in Sine Saloum Delta and Casamance estuary in Senegal, being most of the project area within the boundaries of Protected areas. The plantation will be carried out in places previously selected due to their ecological conditions, together with the local communities, through a design that implies the active participation of communities involved in the project.
The goal of the project is to increase the mangrove area by planting a variety of species of native mangrove, which will increase the positive functions (ecosystem services) that mangroves provide to communities and biodiversity.  The location of the project contributes to the continuity of habitats and ecosystems, since the plantation areas are close to other reforestation project and inside the area of mangrove distribution in Senegal This project is expected to bring positive benefits for different species relevant for the communities as fishes, oysters and mollusks.
WeForest is the Project Proponent and the NGO Oceanium is the Project Implementer of the restoration activities. For the community and biodiversity activities WeForest is in charge and will perform those through other implementing partners and the subsequent agreement with them. WeForest´s fundamental goal is to create social value for rural communities and contribute to their food security through the restoration of their ecosystems. WeForest provides investors access to biodiversity friendly carbon credits that aid the rural communities through large scale and social impact projects.

name: The Dutch CowCredit project: A dutch dairy initiative to reduce methane from enteric fermentation
project_type: Livestock, enteric fermentation, and manure management
description: The Dutch CowCredit project (Multiple Instances of Project Activities)aims to involve the Dutch Dairy industry with the purpose to reduce greenhouse gas (GHG) emissions from the livestock sector. The project activity introduces Mootral® natural feed supplement into beef diet aiming to reduce methane (CH4) emissions from enteric fermentation by direct inhibition of methanogens in the rumen. This process results in a substantial net reduction of GHG emissions, because of the avoidance of CH4 released into the atmosphere, which would occur under normal operating circumstances (“the business as usual”). Over the 10 years of the first crediting period (from 01/07/2022 to 30/06/ 2032), the project will generate an estimated annual average reduction of 190'000 tons of carbon dioxide equivalent (tCO2e).

name: Huineng Low Concentration Coal Mine Methane Utilization Project
developer: Beijing Yonder Environmental Energy Technology Co., Ltd
project_type: Fugitive emissions from fuels (solid, oil and gas); Mining/mineral production
description:
Huineng Low Concentration Coal Mine Methane Utilization Project is located in Huineng coal mine area in Pingding County, Yangquan City, Shanxi Province, People’s Republic of China.Without implementing the project activity, the coal mine methane (CMM) gas extracted due to safety reasons from the Huineng coal mine would be vented into the atmosphere. One of the main components of the CMM gas is methane, a potent greenhouse gas, which would contribute 
to accelerating the climate change if released into the atmosphere. The project activity will capture a large part of the CMM gas and destroy it through utilizing it for electricity production.

name: CONSERVATION OF NATIVE FOREST IN THE BIODIVERSITY HOTSPOT OF PAPUA NEW GUINEA
project_type: Agriculture Forestry and Other Land Use
description:
The project is located on the south-western slope of the Sarawaget Range in Morobe Province. It is comprised of three regions that are based on clan affiliations and is accessible from Lae. It consists of lower montane forest with small areas of lowland tropical rainforest and covers a total area of 226,843 hectares. The project comprises an initial area of approximately 226,843 hectares stretches from Tamigidu on the coast near Lae, all the way to the Morobe/Madang border in the Wantoat/Leron LLG area. It is located on the south-western slopes of the Sarawaget range in Morobe Province, Papua New Guinea and is home to approximately 20,000 people.

Forests in the project area, however, have experienced a continued reduction in biomass due largely to illegal logging and to the establishment of crops, use of firewood, pastures, and settlements. These forests have historically been an important source of income for local families, who periodically harvest timber when the economic needs arise, or to generate income generation sources.

The climate objective of the Project is to avoid and prevent the unplanned deforestation in native forests of PNG, thus avoiding the net emission of 34,026,450 tCO2e through 30 years of Project crediting period.

name: Restoration of Degraded Mangroves and Sustainable Development in Myanmar
project_type: Agriculture Forestry and Other Land Use
description: The objective of this project is to restore 1003 hectares of degraded lands in the Ayeyarwady Division of Myanmar. As per the Verified Carbon Standard (VCS) category, the project falls under the ARR (Afforestation, reforestation and Revegetation) category. The project will create a healthy mangrove ecosystem in degraded lands belonging to Chaung Thar, Kangyi, and Bomie village tracts. Apart from the carbon sequestration, the project will address issues including natural disaster risk reduction, biodiversity improvement and poverty reduction with sustainable livelihoods in the coastal communities.

name: Madagascar Improved Cook Stove Project by KCM-Wood#CPA-W-030
description: The main purpose of this CPA is dissemination of the efficient improved cooking stove woody biomass-based ICS to the rural household of Madagascar. The ICS will burn wood more efficiently thereby improving thermal transfer to pots, which will result in reduced firewood consumption, hence saving fuel. This will not only halt the rapidly progressing deforestation in Madagascar but will also reduce health hazards from indoor smoke pollution and women and children will have to spend less time collecting firewood. Therefore, this will lead to climate change mitigation in a sustainable manner. Overall objectives are reduction of greenhouse gases, conservation of forests and woodlands as well as improved health conditions of ICS users due to improved indoor air quality.

name: The ARR Cerrado Carbon Project
project_type: Agriculture Forestry and Other Land Use
description:
The ARR Cerrado Carbon Project is located at the Cerrado Biome, in the state of Mato Grosso do Sul, Brazil. It is an AFOLU project, and therefore is classified within scope 14. More specifically, the project falls under the ARR category.
The ARR Cerrado Carbon Project’s purpose is to remove and reduce GHG emissions through an increase in forestry area and preservation of native vegetation in the state of Mato Grosso do Sul, at the Cerrado biome, initially near the city of Ribas do Rio Pardo. The project also includes the management and implementation of various social activities at the local communities nearby. The carbon credits are a result of the change of land use in previous pasture areas, through the plantation of Eucalyptus species in an area of 38.708 ha (ARR category).
The plantation activities will be developed in accordance with good forestry practices, and in addition, the project proponents will also seek certification under sustainable programs, such as the FSC, which can confirm the implementation of such practices.

name: Adjusted Water Management in Rice Cultivation in Pinghu City
developer: Hangzhou Chunmeng Agricultural Technology Co., Ltd
project_type: Agriculture Forestry and Other Land Use
description:
The project changing from continuously flooded to intermittent flooded condition during rice cultivation is conducted in Pinghu City under the jurisdiction of Jiaxing City, Zhejiang Province of China, which have a total acreage of 12,545 ha for single-cropping rice. Without this project providing ditches to conduct intermittent flooded method, the continuously flooded method would be continued, so the scenario that rice was cultivated by continuously flooded method is the baseline scenario. Since the organic matter in rice soil under flooded condition can emit a large amount of methane (CH4) because of anaerobic decomposition, the intermittent flooded method is more beneficial to water conservation, production increase and methane emission removal than the continuously flooded. 
With the project implementation, the cement ditches, reservoirs and relevant technical training are provided for these farmers to help them conduct the intermittent flooded water regime during rice cultivation, which replaces the traditional continuously flooded method. During rice cultivation, controllable irrigation and drainage according to rice growth requirements can not only save water resources, but also reduce methane emission from soil organic matter under anaerobic conditions (in the flooded state). In this case, the CH4 emission can be declined by an average of 48% . Hence, this project activity is estimated to reduce 4.78 tCO2e/ha. 
The implementation of the project is expected to reduce the GHG emissions amounting to 419,489 tCO2e in the first seven-year period with an average annual GHG emission reduction of 59,927 tCO2e.

name: IMPROVED FOREST MANAGEMENT THROUGH LOGGED-TO-PROTECTED FORESTS AND REDUCED IMPACT LOGGING IN UFA NGOMBÉ, REPUBLIC OF CONGO
project_type: Agriculture Forestry and Other Land Use
description:
The Project “Improved Forest Management through Logged-to-Protected Forests and Reduced Impact Logging in UFA Ngombé, Republic of Congo (IFM - UFA Ngombé Project)” is designed to improve forest management in 583,326 ha of native Congolese forests legally designated for selective logging. The Project is situated within the UFA Ngombé forest concession which is attributed to and managed by the company Industrie Forestière de Ouesso (IFO), owned by INTERHOLCO AG (IHC). The UFA Ngombé forest concession is divided into four Forest Management Units for 1) the production of timber, 2) community development, and 3) protection and 4) conservation of biodiversity. The Project Area includes areas of High Conservation Value (HCV), including swamps and floodplains in connection with some of the largest peatland complexes in the world, the Cuvette Centrale and the Congo Basin peatland areas. These peatlands are essential for carbon storage, as peatlands store more carbon than any other natural terrestrial system. UFA Ngombé also borders the Ntokou-Pikounda National Park which is home to diverse wildlife, including one of the world’s largest western lowland gorilla populations.
The principle activities of the IFM - UFA Ngombé Project are 1) to implement Reduced Impact Logging (RIL-C) to reduce GHG emissions in one or more source categories (i.e., timber felling, skidding and hauling), and 2) to set-aside areas of Logged-to-Protected Forests (LtPF) to maintain and protect ecosystem services in forest production areas legally designated for selective logging. The Project will apply the VCS VM0035 and VM0010 methodologies to the respective RIL-C and LtPF Project Activities.

name: Waste Energy project in Dadra & Nagar Haveli(D&NH)
project_type: Energy industries (renewable/non-renewable sources); Waste handling and disposal
description:
3R Management (P) Ltd (hereafter referred as “project proponent”) is installing Composting at various locations across India as a grouped project activity. 3R Management (P) Ltd is looking forward to earn carbon credits under VCS mechanism for these composting projects
Composting is a process by which organic wastes are broken down by microorganisms, generally bacteria and fungi, into simpler forms. The microorganisms use the carbon in the waste as an energy source. The degradation of the nitrogen- containing materials results in the breakdown of the original materials into a much more uniform product which can be used as a soil amendment. Heat generated during the process kills many unwanted organisms such as weed seeds and pathogens. Advantages of composting include reduction of waste volume, elimination of heat-killed pests, and the generation of a beneficial and marketable material. Adding compost to soil increases organic matter content.

name: REDD+ Project in Oro Province of Papua New Guinea
project_type: Agriculture Forestry and Other Land Use
description: This REDD+ project is located in the province of Oro in Papua New Guinea. The Oro forests are among the most valuable natural resources. These forests support hundreds of rare and endemic species, making this place a “mega-biodiverse” district. These forests are also directly critical to the lives and well-being of most of our people, including the communities in this province. For decades, these areas are under tremendous stress due to logging, shifting agriculture, and plantations. The demand for unprocessed logs from these areas from the Asian market is the biggest cause of forest loss. However, for the past two decades, forest harvesting has occurred in a destructive and ecologically unsustainable fashion. Secondly, a large portion of the forests is being converted to permanent agriculture and long fallow shifting cultivation. In addition, the human population is been tremendously increased in these areas, and hence the dependence on forest resources increased. Due to the increase in the human population, the poverty among the rural areas is also increased, therefore the subsistence farmers respond to the growing needs of the population by various forms of agricultural intensification. This project is an Avoided Unplanned Deforestation and Degradation (AUD) activity. This initiative proceeds with promoting various activities to mitigate climate change and improving livelihoods.

name: The US Beef CowCredit project: A US Beef initiative to reduce methane from enteric fermentation
project_type: Livestock, enteric fermentation, and manure management
description: TheUS Beef CowCredit project (Multiple Instances of Project Activities and multiple US states) aims to involve the US Beef industry with the purpose to reduce greenhouse gas (GHG) emissions from the livestock sector. The project activity introduces Mootral® natural feed supplement into beef diet aiming to reduce methane (CH4) emissions from enteric fermentation by direct inhibition of methanogens in the rumen. This process results in a substantial net reduction of GHG emissions, because of the avoidance of CH4 released into the atmosphere, which would occur under normal operating circumstances (“the business as usual”). Over the 10 years of the first crediting period, the project will generate an estimated annual average reduction of 300'000 tons of carbon dioxide equivalent (tCO2e).

name: Guizhou Xintian CMM Power Generation Project
developer: Yonggui Energy Development Co., Ltd. Xintian Branch
description:
Guizhou Xintian CMM Power Generation Project (hereafter referred to as “the Project”) refers to a power plant which utilizes low concentration coal mine methane (CMM) for power generation to supply electricity to the Xintian coal mine and to China Southern Power Grid (CSPG). The Project is located in Gantang Town, Qianxi County, Bijie City, Guizhou Province, People’s Republic of China.
The purpose of the Project is to utilize the extracted low concentration CMM to produce electricity. No coal bed methane (CBM)  or ventilation air methane (VAM) utilization is involved. It was planned that CMM power generators with a total capacity of 17.6 MW would be installed for the Project. Based on ex ante estimates, the power plant will destroy a total amount of 35.2 million m3 (under normal conditions ) of methane and export 82,720 MWh of electricity every year, when all power generators are in full operation. The generated electricity is supplied to the Xintian coal mine through the electricity distribution network in the coal mine area; part of the electricity produced by the Project is exported to CSPG after the coal mine demand is fully met.
The Project achieves emission reductions in two aspects: 1) it reduces methane emissions by capturing and destroying methane which would have been directly vented into the air in the baseline scenario; 2) it reduces CO2 emissions by displacing an amount of electricity that would otherwise have been supplied by CSPG.

name: Voluntary Carbon Market Projects for Agroforestry Plantations in Mehsana, Gujarat
project_type: Agriculture Forestry and Other Land Use
description: The demand for timber and other tree-based products is increasing day by day and one feasible alternative to fulfil such a demand would be adopting agroforestry practice as this is one system that can provide both wood and food while at the same time conserve and rehabilitate ecosystem. The proposed ARR VCS project plans to promote sustainable agroforestry for small-scale farmers to provide them with financial benefits and ensure GHG mitigation in the state of Gujarat, India. The project is being conducted in the Mehsana district. The total project area is 2089.95 hectares and the agroforestry plantations done by the farmers from 2018 to 2020 have been considered. name: ZEYN ENERGY BIOGAS PLANT
description:
ZEYN Energy Biogas Plant project is a biogas-to-energy project that generates renewable energy by capturing biogas from animal manure -via anaerobic digestion- and utilizing it to produce thermal and electric energy through biogas systems. The project is being implemented in CERKES district, CANKIRI province, in Turkey. 

The project whose main feedstock is cattle and chicken manure generated at its neighboring farms provides an environmentally friendly solution to manure management problems with which farms are currently facing. The project is supplied manure generated by animals living at neighboring farms daily which are fed into the anaerobic digesters at the project site.

Within the scope of the project, biodegradation of organic wastes coming to the Biogas Plant is taking place in an anaerobic environment. The biogas that is released during the biodegradation of organic wastes is used for electricity and heat production in the biogas unit. 

The proposed project activity currently will have one biogas engine installed at the biogas power plant, with a total capacity of 1,501 KWe/h. Accordingly, the biogas generator system is designed with a total power of 1.501 MWe/h. Whilst heat generated at the plant is used at the facility to warm the digesters, the electricity generated is directly fed to the national grid.

This project adopts the renewable crediting period of 7 years, twice renewable for a total of 21 years. The estimated average net annual emission reductions are 124,121 tCO2eq/y.

consumers/end users (farmers).

name: Saving Colombia's Cloud Forest
project_type: Agriculture Forestry and Other Land Use
description:
The tropical Andes are among the most vulnerable places on earth due to the dual impacts of climate change and human population pressures. With the intense and historic livestock activity in the area, deforestation in the valleys north and south have almost completely isolated the eastern forest. The remaining habitat is an oasis of biodiversity and one of Colombia’s many national treasures. The region also contains two important watersheds: the Río San Juan Antioquia, and Río San Juan Bravo Chocó.  These watersheds provide critical ecosystem services to communities living and working throughout the area and the forests are vital to protection of the headwaters of these important sources of fresh water to the surrounding communities. Without them, landslides, silting, and flooding threaten the health and safety of thousands of residents. 

As our planet’s climate systems continue to be altered, it is highly likely that some or many of the species found in cloud forests will be lost forever. The effects of climate change are already apparent here. As a result, many cloud forest species have started to migrate upslope to maintain a favorable climate. However, their routes are often blocked by a degraded and fragmented landscape caused by agriculture moving up the mountainside and penetrating deeper into the lowlands.   

Our goal is to create a large, protected area for endemic and threatened species to shield them from imminent threats, mitigate climate impacts, and prevent extinctions. Since 2017, we have worked closely with our local partner Fundación Colibri to create a vital connection across a narrow ridgeline. This ecological corridor will safeguard endemic and endangered wildlife and offers important protection for the headwaters of a major river, the primary source of fresh water for communities throughout the region.

name: Zhangye Improved Grassland Management Project
project_type: Agriculture Forestry and Other Land Use
description:
Zhangye Improved Grassland Management Project (hereafter as “the project”) is located in Zhangye City, the northwest of Gansu Province and in the middle of Hexi corridor where the Qinghai Tibet Plateau and Mongolia Plateau meet. The project’s aim is to restore the local degraded grassland ecosystem by seeding grass and building fence on the degraded grassland, increase carbon sequestration and contribute to local development by introducing sustainable grazing and management of grassland. 
The project covers Gaotai County, Shandan County, Mingle County, Sunan County, Ganzhou district and Shandan Racecourse. According to the baseline survey, before the implementation of the project, the grassland in the region has been facing serious degradation and even desertification due to the impact of climate change and human activities. 
Totally, 261,059.80 ha of degraded grassland have been managed scientifically by fence building and reseeding of local high-quality forage. In general, rest grazing and rotational grazing are implemented in slightly degraded areas (the total grass yield decreased by 30%-50% compared with that before degradation), and reseeding is implemented in severely degraded areas. Besides these main restoration measures, the project also alleviate soil desertification and restore grassland vegetation to improve soil carbon storage and local biodiversity through grassland management measures, such as daily management measures from other protect projects like rodent and pest control and grassland fire prevention to ensure the long-term sustainable management of the project area. The project is estimated to generate GHG emission removals of 29,440,243 tCO2e in 40 years, with an average annual GHG emission removal of 736,006 tCO2e.

name: Dekang AWMS GHG Mitigation Project in Sichuan Province
project_type: Energy industries (renewable/non-renewable sources); Livestock, enteric fermentation, and manure management; Waste handling and disposal
description:
Dekang AWMS GHG Mitigation Project in Sichuan Province introduces new animal waste management systems (AWMSs) to treat the manure from 10 existing swine farms in Sichuan Province. Each subsidiary swine farm will install one AWMS. The purpose of the project activity is to treat the manure and wastewater to avoid methane emissions generated in the baseline uncovered anaerobic lagoons. 
The project activity uses flushing system to collect the manure automatically. All the manure and wastewater are collected and then be separated first. The solid will be treated in aerobic composting system and the organic fertilizers will be produced, most of the fertilizer is distributed to local farmers for free and only a small portion will be sold on the domestic market. The liquid will be treated through anaerobic digestion and the biogas generated during the treatment process will be captured for electricity generation. The sludge produced from anaerobic digestion will be treated through aerobic composting together with the solid, the effluent will be supplied to the farmers living around free for agriculture irrigation.
It is estimated that the daily treatment capacity of the AWMS is 2,232 tons of animal manure. The biogas released during the anaerobic digestion will be collected and used for electricity generation and the Residual biogas (if any) will be flared. The total installed capacity of the proposed project is 9.5MW and the annual electricity generation is estimated to be 58,669MWh. Also, the generated electricity will be only used for daily operation of the AWMS and the 10 swine farms themselves and will not be connected to the region power grid or other users. For conservativeness, baseline emissions from power generation are neglected.

name: Xuzhou Yanqun MSW Landfill Site LFG Recovery to Power Project
project_type: Energy industries (renewable/non-renewable sources); Waste handling and disposal
description:
Xuzhou Yanqun MSW Landfill Site LFG Recovery to Power Project (hereafter referred to as the project) is located in Dapeng Town, Tongshan District, Xuzhou City, Jiangsu Province, P.R. China. The project is invested, constructed and operated by Xuzhou Baichang Environmental Energy Co., Ltd. The objective is to collect the landfill gas (LFG) from Xuzhou Yanqun MSW landfill site (hereafter referred to as Yanqun landfill site) and utilize it to generate electricity.
Yanqun landfill site is located in Dapeng Town, Tongshan District, Xuzhou City, and started operation in 2006 with a total design effective capacity of 6,300,000 m3 and a municipal solid waste (MSW) disposal of 1,000 tons/d and an operational lifespan of 19 years. The project has a total designed capacity 3.201MW (3*1,067kW) and combusts the LFG, which contains nearly 50% of methane, to generate electricity and export it to the East China Power Grid (ECPG). The project started construction on 07/12/2019 and started operation on 24/10/2020. The operation period of the project will end on 31/12/2030.
The project collects and utilizes LFG from Yanqun landfill site for power generation, which would otherwise be released into the atmosphere. Methane in the LFG has been emitted to the atmosphere since the landfill started operation. Therefore the project avoids methane emissions and, at the same time, electricity is generated from a renewable energy source, instead of being provided by the grid. 
Scenario existing prior to the start of the implementation of the project activity (the same as baseline scenario) 
•	LFG from Yanqun landfill site is released into the atmosphere.
•	Equivalent electricity generated by the project is supplied by the ECPG, which is dominated by fossil fuel based power plants.   
Project scenario
•	LFG from Yanqun landfill site is partially used for electricity generation. 
•	3×1,067 kW LFG-generator sets  supply electricity to the ECPG.	
The total power generation during the operation period is estimated to be 208,588 MWh. The estimated annual average emission reduction generated by the project over the crediting period is 101,798 tCO2e per year by avoiding the CH4 emissions from the landfill and the CO2 emissions from the fossil fuel power plants in the ECPG.

name: Regenerating Soil Life with waste management
project_type: Agriculture Forestry and Other Land Use; Waste handling and disposal
description:
The project is an innovative integration of industrial composting and increasing carbon stocks in soil. The proposed grouped project was implemented by Ambipar Environmental Solutions within the first instance located in the South of Brazil. The annual average estimation of carbon accrual is 2,337 tCO2e and 38,397 tCO2e of reduction.
Compost application in soil has the potential of contribution to the carbon cycle, where simple nutrients that return to the soil are converted by plants into organic compounds engaging sustainable agricultural land management. 
Soil carbon accrual per unit area is measured in both baseline and project scenarios based on the spatial coordinated sampling gathering data on soil carbon concentration with statistical rigor. The project activities were designed to improve soils, including changes to agricultural practices, compost application and enhance biodiversity in soils. The measurement of the stable SOC concentration was set up to quantify soil dynamics at depth. The soil layers up to 80cm were sampled to estimate changes in carbon stock, excluding the top-soil 20cm.
Prior to the implementation of this project, rural producers do not foresee regenerative agriculture due to the lack of knowledge and technical skills about how to switch to organic input, biological control of plagues and sustainable land management. The previous scenario within the project area outcome low productivity per area, soil degradation and no smart application of the compost provided through the waste management, which implied in deposition applications without potential reuse for climate change mitigation.
Nowadays, this waste gets into the circular economy by its smart reuse and social and environmental positive influence. Ambipar manages great volumes across Brazil for about 50 industrial customers. Built on the raised potential for inclusion of new project activity instances, this grouped project brings up attractive engagement for high carbon landscapes.

project_type: Agriculture Forestry and Other Land Use
description:

The area of the project activity is 7847.48 ha, including 1484 subcompartments spreading over Dahua Town,Duyang Town,Yantan Town,Baima Township,Bansheng Township,Beijing Township,Guwen Township, Gonghe Township,Jiangnan Township,Liuye Township,Qiangxu Township,Yalong Township,Yixu Township,Guhe Township,Qibainong Township,Gongchuan,Duyang  forest farm of Guangxi Dahua. All these forests are state-owned forests or privately-owned or collective-owned, and have the legal right to forest ownership. The species involved in the project are Broadleaf Mix,Pinus massoniana and Chinese Fir.
Before the implementation of the project activity, the trees are logged based on a valid and verifiable government-approved timber management plan for harvesting the project area. The implementation of the project activity converses the trees to protected forest to reduce the GHG emissions for about 1,422,596 tCO2e in 20 years, the average annual emission reduction is 71,130 tCO2e and Verified Carbon Units with buffer deduction is about 1,308,789 tCO2e in 20 years, and average annual VCUs with buffer deduction is 65,439 tCO2e.
The project activity will contribute to the environment (biodiversity conservation, rocky desertification prevention and soil erosion control), thus contribute to sustainable development.

name: CONDOTO REDD+
project_type: Agriculture Forestry and Other Land Use
description:
The CONDOTO REDD+ Project seeks the conservation of forests located in the territories of the afro communities organized as the Major Community Council of Condoto and Iró, located within the municipalities of Condoto and Río Iró, in the department of Chocó. The project zone has a total area of 65.026 ha, out of which 46.191 ha were forest in 2015. The area is characterized for its high biodiversity and rain tropical forests, but also for the presence of deforestation activities and social conflicts. Deforestation drivers include mining activities, subsistence agriculture, and activities of illegal use. Social issues include absence of the state and lack of sanitation, education and health infrastructure and lack of technical guidance regarding sustainable production models.

The project aims to mitigate the effects caused by climate change by reducing CO2 emissions derived from deforestation and forest degradation, restore degraded forest lands, promote sustainable management of forests and develop productive activities to improve community welfare. The project also seeks to protect biodiversity and high conservation values, enhance ecological connectivity and secure natural habitats of vulnerable species (including those within some category of threat and those that represent ecological interest.

name: Soil carbon improvement Project through Grassland Management, in South Africa
project_type: Agriculture Forestry and Other Land Use
description:
The proposed project aims to remove GHG by implementing Sustainable livestock grazing management and controlled fire over multiple grasslands of different provinces in the host country Republic of South Africa. In the baseline scenario, the pastures are larger and the livestock movement less frequent, allowing for unrestricted and selective grazing of perennial grasses. Loss of perennial grasses in grassland ecosystems results in soil loss and erosion, soil carbon loss, reduced water filtration capacity, and reduced productivity of forage.  The Project Activity i.e. 'planned grazing and controlled burning' will increase the rest and rotation on pastures above baseline practices. Smaller pastures implemented by fencing with more rotations allow the recovery of perennial grasses, which foster greater carbon inputs, higher retention of carbon as lignin and cellulose, and greater belowground production. This results in the sequestration of GHGs from the atmosphere into the soil. 

The project has been designated as a ‘Grouped Project’ and plans to increase the number of project instances over a period of time. The first instance includes four land areas Kwazulu Natal
(KZN, 6866.2 ha), Eastern Cape (EC, 71546.64 ha), MPL (3810.4 ha) and “Free State” (11281.9 ha) and this first instance aims to recover around 93,505 ha of land degraded by unrestricted grazing and uncontrolled fire through the implementation of planned rotational grazing and controlled burning.  The overall purpose of this initiative is to develop soil carbon storage through improved grassland management and expected to result in significant removal of CO2 from the atmosphere, as documented using the VCS methodology, “VM0026 – Sustainable Grassland Management”.

name: Shuangbaotai AWMS GHG Mitigation Project in Jiangsu Province
developer: Shuangbaotai Animal Husbandry Group Co., Ltd.
project_type: Energy industries (renewable/non-renewable sources); Livestock, enteric fermentation, and manure management; Waste handling and disposal
description:
The project introduces new animal waste management systems to treat the manure from 4 swine farms in Jiangsu Province. Each subsidiary swine farm will install one animal waste management system, and the manure is treated on site. The purpose of the project activity is to treat the manure and wastewater to avoid methane emissions generated in the baseline uncovered anaerobic lagoons. 
The project activity uses flushing system to collect the manure automatically. All the manure and wastewater are collected and then be separated first. The solid will be treated in aerobic composting system and the organic fertilizers will be produced, most of the fertilizer is distributed to local farmers for free and only a small portion will be sold on the domestic market. The liquid will be treated through anaerobic digestion and the biogas generated during the treatment process will be captured for electricity generation. The sludge produced from anaerobic digestion will be treated through aerobic composting together with the solid, the effluent will be supplied to the farmers living around free for agriculture irrigation.
It is estimated that approximately 676 tons of animal manure will be handled daily by the AWMS. The biogas released during the anaerobic digestion will be collected and used for electricity production. The annual electricity production is estimated to be 19,254MWh. Also, the generated electricity will be only used for daily operation of the AWMS and the 4 swine farms themselves and will not be connected to the region grid net or other users. For conservativeness, baseline emissions from power generation are neglected. The project activity will reduce of GHG in the atmosphere through avoiding methane emissions from anaerobic treatment of swine manure and wastewater.

name: Juruena River REDD+ Project
project_type: Agriculture Forestry and Other Land Use
description:
The primary objective of the Juruena River REDD+ Project is to avoid the unplanned deforestation (AUD) of the 45,675.15 ha project area, consisting of 100% Amazon rainforest. The project area is located within 18 private properties, which are located in the municipality of Cotriguaçu, in the State of Mato Grosso, Southern Amazon. A Sustainable Forest Management Plan is also carried out in some of the properties.

Beyond the project’s ecological and carbon benefits, a proportion of the carbon credits generated will be dedicated to improving the social and environmental conditions in the project region, specifically contributing to improving deforestation control, and developing environmental education and other social activities. The contribution to sustainability is being monitored through the application of the SOCIALCARBON® Standard.

The present REDD project is expected to avoid a predict ed 3,800 ha of deforestation, equating to 1,384,740 tCO2e in emissions reductions over the 30 year project lifetime (12-November-2021 to 11-November-2050).

name: SHINE - Distribution of LED lightbulbs in India-6
description:
The proposed small-scale grouped project activity has already been registered as CPA 10484-P1-0006-CP1 under registered CDM Programme of Activities (PoA) 10484 titled:” SHINE – Distribution of LED Lightbulbs in India” which involves distribution of Light Emitting Diodes (LEDs) for domestic lighting in Uttar Pradesh. 
Uttar Pradesh has one of the lowest demand supply availability amongst the Indian States. The peak demand supply gap in 2016 stood at 12.5%. Post October 2016, the state has endeavored to provide 24 hours power to major towns and cities. However, the rural areas receive anywhere between 16 hours to 18 hours of electricity only. SHINE CPA 6 aims to reduce the peak demand requirement by distributing energy efficient LEDs to rural households.

name: SHINE - Distribution of LED lightbulbs in India-7
description:
The proposed small-scale grouped project activity has already been registered as CPA 10484-P1-007-CP1 under registered CDM Programme of Activities (PoA) 10484 titled:” SHINE – Distribution of LED Lightbulbs in India” which involves distribution of Light Emitting Diodes (LEDs) for domestic lighting in southern state of Andhra Pradesh. 
In Andhra Pradesh, peak electricity demand stood at 13436 MW in the year 2018-19. The government is working towards providing 24x7, reliable 3 phase supply to all domestic, commercial & industrial consumers, however this depends on availability of power. The government plans to achieve this by incremental energy procurement, supplemented by energy conservation efforts. Further, domestic lighting has been identified by AP Government as having second highest saving potential per annum after agriculture. With distribution of energy efficient LEDs, SHINE CPA 7 seeks to achieve this goal of reducing the burden on peak hour consumption.

name: Jiaozuo Zhouliu MSW Landfill site LFG Recovery to Power Project
project_type: Energy industries (renewable/non-renewable sources); Waste handling and disposal
description: Jiaozuo Zhouliu MSW Landfill site LFG Recovery to Power Project (hereafter referred to as the project) is located in the south area of Zhouliu Village, Xiuwu County, Jiaozuo City, Henan Province, P.R. China. The project is invested, constructed and operated by Shanghai BCCY New Power Industry Co., Ltd. The objective is to collect the landfill gas (LFG) from Jiaozuo Zhouliu MSW landfill site (hereafter referred to as Zhouliu landfill site) and utilize it to generate electricity. Zhouliu landfill site started operation in November 2008 with a total design capacity of 2,200,000 m3 and a daily municipal solid waste (MSW) disposal of 550 tons/d. The landfill is envisaged to be filled in by 2018 (closure of the landfill in 2019).  The project has a total designed capacity 2.5MW (5*500kW) and combusts the LFG, which contains nearly 50% of methane, to generate electricity and export it to the Central China Power Grid (CCPG). The project started construction in January 2011 and started operation on 25-03-2011. The project collects and utilizes LFG from Zhouliu landfill site for power generation, which would otherwise be released into the atmosphere. Methane in the LFG has been emitted to the atmosphere since the landfill started operation. Therefore, the project avoids methane emissions and, at the same time, electricity is generated from a renewable energy source, instead of being provided by the grid. Scenario existing prior to the start of the implementation of the project activity (the same as baseline scenario): LFG from Zhouliu landfill site is released into the atmosphere; Equivalent electricity generated by the project is supplied by the CCPG, which is dominated by fossil fuel based power plants. The total power generation from year 2011 to 2021 is estimated to be 45,917 MWh. The estimated annual average emission reduction generated by the project over the crediting period is 31,755 tCO2e per year.

name: Luoyang Landfill Site LFG Recovery to Electricity Project
project_type: Energy industries (renewable/non-renewable sources); Waste handling and disposal
description:
Luoyang Landfill Site LFG Recovery to Electricity Project (hereafter referred to as the project) is located in Chanhe District, Luoyang City, Henan Province, P.R. China. The project is invested, constructed and operated by Shanghai BCCY New Power Industry Co., Ltd. The objective is to collect the landfill gas (LFG) from Luoyang landfill site and utilize it to generate electricity. No flare will be installed in this project activity.
Luoyang landfill site started operation in 2001 with a municipal solid waste (MSW) disposal of 1,300 tons/d and an operational lifespan of 18 years. The project involves the installation of a gas collection system, transmitting system, pre-treatment system and an electricity generation plant. Three sets of gas engines with the total installed capacity of 1.5MW (3*500kW) were installed. The gas engines combust the LFG, which contains nearly 50% of methane, to generate electricity and export it to the Central China Power Grid (CCPG). The project started construction in December 2007 and started operation on 01-03-2009. 
The project collects and utilizes LFG from Luoyang landfill site for power generation, which would otherwise be released into the atmosphere. Methane in the LFG has been emitted to the atmosphere since the landfill started operation. Therefore, the project avoids methane emissions and, at the same time, electricity is generated from a renewable energy source, instead of being provided by the grid.
The total power generation from year 2009 to 2019 is estimated to be 87,750 MWh. The estimated annual average emission reduction generated by the project over the crediting period is 114,743 tCO2e per year by avoiding the CH4 emissions from the landfill and the CO2 emissions from the fossil fuel power plants in the CCPG.

name: Luohe MSW Landfill Site LFG Recovery to Power Project
project_type: Energy industries (renewable/non-renewable sources); Waste handling and disposal
description:
Luohe MSW Landfill Site LFG Recovery to Power Project (hereafter referred to as the project) is located in the northeast area inside of Luohe City MSW landfill site, one kilometre south of Chengang village, Luohe City, Henan Province, P.R. China. The project is invested, constructed and operated by Shanghai BCCY New Power Industry Co., Ltd. Degassing pipelines have been installed on the landfill site only for safety reason, no LFG collection and/or destruction facilities have been installed prior to the project activity. 
The project activity employs a gas collection system, a transmitting system, a pre-treatment system and gas engines with a capacity of 2 MW (4*500kW). The gas engines combust the LFG, which contains nearly 50% of methane, to generate electricity and export it to the Central China Power Grid (CCPG). The project started construction in August 2009 and started operation on 31-05-2010. 
The project collects and utilizes LFG from Luohe landfill site for power generation, which would otherwise be released into the atmosphere. Methane in the LFG has been emitted to the atmosphere since the landfill started operation. Therefore, the project avoids methane emissions and, at the same time, electricity is generated from a renewable energy source, instead of being provided by the grid.
The total power generation from year 2010 to 2020 is estimated to be 113,317 MWh. The estimated annual average emission reduction generated by the project over the crediting period is 44,223 tCO2e per year by avoiding the CH4 emissions from the landfill and the CO2 emissions from the fossil fuel power plants in the CCPG.

name: Suzhou Landfill in Anhui Province Gas Utilization Project
project_type: Energy industries (renewable/non-renewable sources); Waste handling and disposal
description:
Suzhou Landfill in Anhui Province Gas Utilization Project (hereafter referred to as “the project”) is located within Suzhou Landfill at Qianfu Village, Suzhou City, Anhui Province, P. R. China. The project is invested, constructed and operated by Suzhou Smart Energy Environmental Protection Power Co., Ltd.. The objective is to collect the landfill gas (LFG) from Suzhou Landfill and utilize it to generate electricity.
Construction of Suzhou Landfill started in 2005 and was finished in 2007, and the tipping of the waste at the site started in January 2008. The designed capacity of the site is 3.027 million tonnes. The average waste tonnage in 2008 is 405 tonnes/day and it increased by 5% each year, it is expected that the site will be closed for further tipping after reaching the full capacity of the storage 3.027 million tonnes, estimated in year 2022. 
The project involves the installation of a gas collection system and utilization system. The collected gas is utilized in gas engines with capacity of 2.060MW and generates power, and any excess gas is flared initially in an enclosed flare with a capacity of 1000 Nm3/h. 
Landfill gas has been extracted and combusted by flare since 01/01/2010. The construction of the grid connection was completed on 12 October 2012 followed by completion of engine commissioning on 25 December 2012. The project started to export power to the grid on 28 December 2012.
The project collects and utilizes LFG from Suzhou landfill for power generation, which would otherwise be released into the atmosphere. Methane in the LFG has been emitted to the atmosphere since the landfill started operation. Therefore the project avoids methane emissions and, at the same time, electricity is generated from a renewable energy source, instead of being provided by the grid.

name: Shenyang Daxin Landfill Gas to Electricity Project
project_type: Energy industries (renewable/non-renewable sources); Waste handling and disposal
description:
Shenyang Daxin Landfill Gas to Electricity Project (hereafter referred to as “the project”) is located at Northeast direction of Daxin No1 Village, Cailuo Town, Shenbeixinqu District, Shenyang City, Liaoning province, P.R. China. The project is invested, constructed and operated by Shenyang Xinxin Tomorrow Renewable Co., Ltd.. The objective is to collect the landfill gas (LFG) from Shenyang Daxin Landfill and utilize it to generate electricity.
Shenyang Daxin Landfill is one of the two landfills serving Shenyang City. It receives an average of 2,773 tonnes of waste per day and more than 90% of the waste deposited onsite is domestic waste. The designing lifetime of the landfill site is 16 years, and it has received waste since 2003. 
The project consists of LFG collection system, pre-treatment equipments, flaring system, power generation and grid connection system. Five sets of gas engines with the total installed capacity of 5.315MW (1.063MW*5) were installed. Regarding the project activity implementation process, the starting date of project activity is 22/12/2006 as per the signing date of first gas turbine generator purchase agreement and the project was put into operation on 16/09/2009. The second gas turbine generator has been put into commissioning on 28/11/2012. The 3#、4# and 5# gas turbine generators were put into operation on 01/05/2013.
The project collects and utilizes LFG from Shenyang Daxin Landfill for power generation, which would otherwise be released into the atmosphere. Methane in the LFG has been emitted to the atmosphere since the landfill started operation. Therefore the project avoids methane emissions and, at the same time, electricity is generated from a renewable energy source, instead of being provided by the grid.

name: AAC Blocks Project in Siddipet, Telengana by Sree Sai Rama Industries
description: The company Sree Sai Rama Industries are involved in manufacturing of Autoclaved Aerated Concrete (AAC) blocks in Siddipet Dist, Telangana state, India. name: Installation of High Efficient Cook Stoves by EKI Energy Services Limited
description: The main purpose of project is distribution of fuel-efficient improved cook stoves (ICS) in India initially and will expand the same for other Asian and African countries. The ICS disseminated through this project will replace the old low efficient baseline cook stoves. Through this project, the distribution and installation of ICS will be undertaken for households and communities/non-household. It is intended that under this project high thermal efficient cook stoves will be distributed. The ICS will burn wood more efficiently thereby improving thermal transfer to pots, hence saving fuel and greenhouse gases. Not only will this halt the rapidly progressing deforestation but will also reduce health hazards from indoor smoke pollution and women and children will have to spend less time collecting firewood.

name: KONYA ENERGY BIOGAS PLANT
description:
KONYA Energy Biogas Plant is currently one of the largest biogas plants in Turkey with an operational license capacity of 12 MWe/h and became operational April 30th, 2020, with an installed capacity of 6 MWe/h. 

Located in Çumra district, Konya province, it is a biogas-to-energy project generating renewable energy by capturing biogas from animal manure -via anaerobic digestion- and utilizing it to produce thermal and electric energy. 

In its first phase, manure generated by animals at neighboring farms is collected daily through special sewage trucks and fed into the anaerobic digesters. In the baseline scenario, prior to the implementation of the project, manure was left to decay in anaerobic conditions without methane recovery at the farms.

With the project, manure coming to the plant biodegrades in anaerobic conditions. The biogas that is released during the biodegradation of organic wastes is used for electricity and heat production in the biogas unit. 

The proposed project has a total installed capacity of 6,004 KWe/h. The annual feed-in electricity is hence estimated to be 45,015,000 KWh. Whilst heat generated at the plant is used at the facility to warm the digesters, the electricity generated is directly fed to the national grid. 

The project reduces GHG emissions mainly by preventing them, methane in particular, from being emitted directly to the atmosphere from animal manure and replacing the electricity that would have otherwise been generated by the national grid heavily dependent on fossil-fuel-based resources.

This project adopts the renewable crediting period of 7 years, twice renewable for a total of 21 years. It is expected to generate 532,368 tCO2eq/y net emission reductions per annum.

name: HENAN YIYANG AFFORESTATION PROJECT
developer: Guizhou Qianhe Carbon Technology Co., Ltd
project_type: Agriculture Forestry and Other Land Use
description:
Henan Yiyang Afforestation Project (hereafter referred as “the project”) is located in Yiyang
County, Luoyang City, Henan Province, China. The project is to establish forest on the barren
land to generate GHG emission reductions and contribute to local sustainable development. The
project is 13,634.73 ha of forest was established by direct planted on barren lands in Yiyang
County, Luoyang City, Henan Province.
The project activity aims to:
- Sequester carbon dioxide and mitigating climate change;
- Enhance biodiversity conservation by increasing the connectivity of forests;
- Improve the quality and quantity of the vegetation;
- Improve soil and water conservation and contribute to sustainable development.
- Generate income and job opportunities for local communities.
There is no natural renewal and reforestation and all sites were barren hills at least 10 years prior
to the implementation of the project. The main objective specie are Robinia, Platycladus and Oak
Tree which are native species.
With the implementation of the project activity, total GHG emission reductions or removals are
about 16,662,626 tCO2e in 60 years the average annual emission reduction is 277,710 tCO2e
and total GHG emission reductions or removals with buffer deduction is about 14,996,363 tCO2e
in 60 years, the average annual GHG emission reductions or removals with buffer deduction is
249,939 tCO2e.
