name: ecoTrees AG – Paulownia Tree Plantation Management in Romania to Sell Wood Production and the Carbon Offsets
project_type: Agriculture Forestry and Other Land Use
description:
For over five years, ecoTrees AG has been developing and managing Paulownia tree plantations located in Romania. The purpose is two-fold, to create an investment of fast-growing timber trees on previously unused land and reduce global CO2 emissions.

This project will sell wood production and carbon offsets.

Currently, ecoTrees AG manages more than 500 hectares of land in different sites around Romania. We have begun afforestation of 100 hectares with Paulownia trees with ecoTrees AG directly owning more than 60 hectares of Paulownia plantations with the continued expansion every year.

Moreover, we are offering our Swiss customers the chance to participate in our business model. We help them to set up a plantation with a complete management program that includes:
- Finding the land
- Planting the trees
- Managing the trees until harvesting
- Harvesting the trees
- Selling the wood for them

At this moment, we are already managing around 40 hectares for Swiss customers.

ecoTrees chose Romania because they promote afforestation efforts where all plantations use lands degraded and neglected agricultural areas. No new growth forests are touched.

The Paulownia tree is also known as the Kiri, Kaiserbaum, Emperor Tree, and Blue Bell. This wood’s properties have proven to be an excellent choice for noble wooden decks on boats, mouldings, skis, instruments, and furniture production.

The Paulownia tree hybrid we use thrives particularly well in the Central and Eastern European climate. The typical planting density is 700 - 750 trees per hectare. The plantations also help hold the soil and offer work for local inhabitants.

The massive size of the leaves helps trap carbon dioxide more than most tree species. One hectare of Paulownia absorbs about 50 tons of CO2 per year. We estimate that 100 hectares of Paulownia can absorb 5,000 tons of CO2 per year

name: HOUSING DECARBONISATION IN THE UNITED KINGDOM
description:
This project facilitates the decarbonisation of housing stock in the United Kingdom. Emission reductions are generated by reductions in fossil fuel and grid-connected electricity consumption in dwellings that are decarbonised compared to baseline consumption. The aggregated emissions from fossil fuel consumption of dwellings in the United Kingdom make up a significant component of greenhouse gas emissions; they also pose a significant opportunity to reduce real emissions.

This project is defined as a grouped project where the project proponent acts as a central administrator towards the objective of expediting the pace of housing decarbonisation. The project targets a range of individual dwellings all located in the United Kingdom. 

The project proponent collects, monitors, and aggregates data necessary to demonstrate additionality, quantify the resulting emission reductions and to originate voluntary carbon credits in conformance with the VM0008 Methodology.  The project proponent is responsible for overseeing validation and registration of the project with the Verra Registry and managing the verification and sale of the resulting emission reduction credits. 

The main project objectives are:

•	To gradually group together individual dwellings located in the United Kingdom inside a cluster, that will achieve together a significant reduction in real emissions during the project crediting period; 

•	To stimulate and reward dwelling owners for their efforts to reduce greenhouse gas emissions such as insulating, air sealing and improving the central heating system in existing dwellings and facilitating dwelling owners’ access to the internationally recognised voluntary carbon credits market; and

•	To overcome the inherent challenges of aggregating small scale decarbonisation activities, simplify third party auditing and control (monitoring) as well as undertaking centralised data collection activities paramount to the quantification of emission reductions.

name: BALIKESİR LANDFILL GAS (LFG) CAPTURE AND UTILIZATION PROJECT
project_type: Energy industries (renewable/non-renewable sources); Waste handling and disposal
description:
Balıkesir Landfill Gas (LFG) Capture and Utilization Project is being implemented by Landfill Enerji Sanayi ve Ticaret A.Ş. within the boundaries of Balıkesir Solid Waste Disposal Site (SWDS) in Balıkesir province in Turkey.

The proposed project activity has the installed capacity of “14.14 MWe/h”. 

It is planned to rehabilitate the SWDS that receives around 1,200 tons of municipal waste generated at Balıkesir province per day and to generate renewable electric power by capturing and utilizing landfill gas.

Whilst providing sustainable development benefits to the host communities and the host country, the proposed project activity will reduce greenhouse gas (GHG) emissions mainly by 

•	preventing GHG emissions, methane in particular, from being emitted directly to the atmosphere from waste at the Balıkesir SWDS that would be otherwise left to be decomposed;
•	replacing the electricity that would have otherwise been generated by the national grid which is heavily dependent on fossil-fuel-based resources, through generating renewable energy and feeding it to the grid.

The project has begun to generate electricity on October 27th, 2019, which is regarded as the project start date. 

This project adopts a fixed crediting period of 10 years. The expected average annual emission reductions are 185,502 tCO2eq/y. Accordingly, the project is expected to generate 1,855,020 tCO2eq emissions reduction throughout the crediting period.

name: Great British Sustainable Farming Project
project_type: Agriculture Forestry and Other Land Use
description:
The “Great British Sustainable Farming Project” (GBSFP) from One Carbon World (OCW) aims to raise farmers' awareness on the benefits of regenerative agriculture and how changes in agricultural practices can help in climate change mitigation and adaptation. In order to achieve this objective, the project activity consists of several regenerative agricultural land management practices to reduce and remove GHG emissions.

The project is developed as a grouped project within the United Kingdom (UK) boundaries. The project activity intends to add more instances over the upcoming years. The expansion of the project activity will depend on the allowance of the project validation and the project activities instances will have to follow the program eligibility criteria for its inclusion. The project implementation results in an increase of soil organic carbon and a reduction of GHG emissions. 

“Regenerative agriculture” refers to farming and grazing practices that aim to reverse climate change by rebuilding soil organic matter, sequestering carbon, improving degraded soil biodiversity, improving water cycle and restoring soil fertility. Regenerative agriculture does not imply only one practice, it is a combination of techniques. The project activity, based on this type of agriculture, consists of a package of practices that change the pre-existing agricultural management activities that are carried out in the farms, these activities include but are not limited to:
- Reduce fertilizer application
- Improve water management/irrigation
- Reduce tillage/improve residue management
- Improve crop planting and harvesting (e.g. agroforestry)
- Improve grazing practices.

name: Yunnan Jinping IFM (conversion of logged to protected forest) Project
project_type: Agriculture Forestry and Other Land Use
description:
The Yunnan Jinping IFM (conversion of logged to protected forest) Project  (hereafter “the project activity”) is implemented in Jinping Miao, Yao and Dai Autonomous County,Honghe Autonomous Prefecture, Yunnan Province  of China by JinPing County CITY Investment Development  Co., Ltd., the geo-coordinate of the  project  proponent is  102°31'33″E -103°38'44″E and 22°26'40″N - 23°04'32″N,  the total area is 236021.2ha, which includes  the  Improved  Forest  Management  (IFM)  of  the forests in the conversion of logged to protected forest. 
The area of the project activity is 4075.45 ha, including 197 subcompartments spreading over Jinhe Town,Jinshuihe Town, Adebo Township, Dazhai Township, Maandi Township, Mengla Township, Mengqiao Township, Yingpan Township,Laojizhai Township,Tongchang Township,Laomeng Township,Shayipo Township,Zhemi Township of  Jinping Miao, Yao and Dai Autonomous County. All these forests are state-owned forests or privately-owned or collective-owned, and have the legal right to forest ownership. The species involved in the project are Broadleaf Mix and Chinese fir.
Before the implementation of the project activity, the trees are logged based on a valid and verifiable government-approved timber management plan for harvesting the project area. The implementation of the project activity converses the trees to protected forest to reduce the GHG emissions for about 612,993 tCO2e in 20 years, the average annual emission reduction is 30,650 tCO2e and Verified Carbon Units with buffer deduction is about 496,525 tCO2e in 20 years, and average annual VCUs with buffer deduction is 24,826 tCO2e. 
The project activity will contribute to the environment (biodiversity conservation, rocky desertification prevention and soil erosion control), thus contribute to sustainable development.

name: Feitian 11 & Dabatian CMM Power Generation Project
description:
Feitian 11 & Dabatian CMM Power Generation Project (hereafter referred to as “the Project”) is located in Zhijin County and Nayong County of Bijie City, Guizhou Province, People’s Republic of China which involves two power plants which utilize low concentration coal mine methane (CMM) for power generation to supply electricity to the coal mines and to China Southern Power Grid (CSPG) if there is any electricity surplus.

The purpose of the Project is to utilize the extracted CMM with a low concentration of methane to produce electricity. No coal bed methane (CBM)  or ventilation air methane (VAM) utilization is involved. CMM power generators with a total capacity of 6 MW are to be installed for Feitian 11 power plant, and 2 MW for Dabatian power plant, totaling to 8 MW for the Project. It is estimated that the two power plants will destroy a total amount of 17.1 million m3 (under normal conditions ) of methane and export 39,360 MWh of electricity every year, when all power generators are in full operation. The generated electricity is supplied to the coal mines through the electricity distribution network in the coal mine area, replacing the electricity that would otherwise have been purchased from CSPG; part of the electricity produced by the Project may also be exported to CSPG if there is any electricity surplus after the coal mine demand is fully met, thus displacing part of the electricity generated by CSPG dominated by fossil fuel-fired power plants.

The Project achieves emission reductions in two aspects: 1) it reduces methane emissions by capturing and destroying methane which would have been directly vented into the air in the baseline scenario; 2) it reduces CO2 emissions by displacing part of the electricity that would otherwise have been supplied by CSPG.

name: Luohe Geothermal Based Space Heating System
developer: Wanjiang New Energy Group Co., Ltd.
description: The project activity is designed to introduce geothermal energy-based space heating system to realize heat supply to a series of new residential buildings in Luohe city over winter season, which will displace heat supply from isolated coal-fired boilers as a business-as-usual scenario in the project area. It can supply geothermal heat to 8,283 thousand m2 of newly built residential buildings with a total heating load of 414.15 MW. The scenario prior to the implementation of the proposed project activity is that heat supplied to the building areas in winter would be provided by isolated coal-fired boilers. Emission reduction credits will be earned using geothermal energy instead of the combustion of fossil fuel for space heating. The annual average CO2 emission reductions are estimated as 481,744 tCO2e, and total GHG emission reductions for the first crediting period are 2,408,720 tCO2e.

name: Eastern DRC Cookstove Project - South Kivu
location: Congo, The Democratic Republic of The
description: The project aims to provide individuals with intermediate improved cookstove (ICS). The stoves will be commercialized into the community via the local church communities that function in the various locations. The ICS distributed through this project will encourage households to replace the prevailing inefficient three-stone fireplace or traditional cookstoves that are predominantly used across the region. The ICS provides for an efficient use of the thermal energy generated though the combustion of biomass while cooking and there is a more efficient transfer of this thermal energy to the cooking pot. There is thus a resultant reduction in both biomass consumption and greenhouse gas emissions. The biomass traditionally utilized is a mixture of non-renewable biomass from natural woodlands, charcoal produced locally and sold via an informal network of sellers and to a lesser extent some renewable biomass from wood grown for fuel.

name: Adjusted Water Management in Rice Cultivation in South Jiangjin District
developer: Chongqing Gengfang Agricultural Development Co., Ltd.
project_type: Agriculture Forestry and Other Land Use
description:
The project changing from continuously flooded to intermittent flooded condition during rice
cultivation is conducted in Jiangjin, Chongqing City, where located in southwestern China with a
total acreage of 19,193 ha for single-cropping rice. Without the implementation of this project,
which provides ditches to conduct intermittently flooded method, the backward continuously
flooded method would be continued, so the scenario that rice was cultivated by continuously
flooded method is the baseline scenario. Since the organic matter in rice soil under flooded
condition can emit a large amount of methane (CH4) because of anaerobic decomposition, the
intermittent flooded method is more beneficial to water conservation, production increase and
less methane emission reduction than the continuously flooded.
The implementation activities of the project include cement ditch construction, reservoir
construction and necessary training for the farmers to help them conduct the intermittent
flooded water regime during rice cultivation, which replaces the traditional continuously flooded
method. Controllable irrigation and drainage according to the needs of rice growth can not only
save water resources, but also reduce methane emissions from soil organic matter under
anaerobic conditions (flooded state) In this case, the CH4 emission can be declined by an
average of 48%. Hence, with the proposed project activity, an estimated amount of GHG
emission reduction 2.79 tCO2e/ha for rice is expected.
The implementation of the project is expected to reduce the GHG emissions amounting to
374,234 tCO2e in the first seven-year period, with an average annual GHG emission reduction of
53,462 tCO2e.
This project aims to:
- Sequester greenhouse gas and mitigate climate changes.
- Increase the rice productivity resulting in higher living standard of local farmers.
- Provide more job opportunities, especially female workers.
- Use a proportion of benefits to improve the local children’s education.

name: Adjusted Water Management in Rice Cultivation in Yongchuan District
developer: Chongqing Gengfang Agricultural Development Co., Ltd.
project_type: Agriculture Forestry and Other Land Use
description:
The project changing from continuously flooded to intermittent flooded condition during rice
cultivation is conducted in Yongchuan, Chongqing City, where located in southwestern China
with a total acreage of 19,151 ha for single-cropping rice. Without the implementation of this
project, which provides ditches to conduct intermittently flooded method, the backward
continuously flooded method would be continued, so the scenario that rice was cultivated by
continuously flooded method is the baseline scenario. Since the organic matter in rice soil

name: Komaza Smallholder Farmer Forestry Kenya
project_type: Agriculture Forestry and Other Land Use
description: Komaza is a social enterprise founded in 2006 in Coastal Kenya. It was started with the mission of getting subsistence farmers out of poverty by building a profitable forestry business that connects thousands of small-scale tree farmers to high-value wood markets. The afforestation project will include all of Komaza’s planting since 2017 and future planting in Kenya, establishing over 45,000 hectares of micro tree farms with 100,000 smallholder farmers. project_type: Agriculture Forestry and Other Land Use
description:
The Yunnan Dayao IFM (conversion  of  logged  to  protected  forest)  Project  (hereafter “the project activity”) is implemented in Dayao County, Chuxiong Yi Autonomous Prefecture, Yunnan Province  of China by Dayao County New Town Construction Development Investment Co., Ltd., the geo-coordinate of the  project  proponent is  100°53'18″E -101°40'30″E and 25°32'43″N - 26°23'36″N,  the total area is 101,941.5 ha, which includes  the  Improved  Forest  Management  (IFM)  of  the forests in the conversion of logged to protected forest.
The area of the project activity is 6041.6 ha, including 622 subcompartments spreading over Guihua Town, Liuju Town, Longjie Town, Sanchahe Town, Santai Township, Shiyang Town, Tanhua Township, Tiesuo Township, Xinjie Town, Zhaojiadian Town, Jinbi Town, Wanbi Township of Dayao County. All these forests are state-owned forests or privately-owned or collective-owned, and have the legal right to forest ownership. The species involved in the project are Pinus yunnanensis, Alder and Quercus.
Before the implementation of the project activity, the trees are logged based on a valid and verifiable government-approved timber management plan for harvesting the project area. The implementation of the project activity converses the trees to protected forest to reduce the GHG emissions for about 958,007 tCO2e in 20 years, the average annual emission reduction is 47,900 tCO2e and Verified Carbon Units with buffer deduction is about 747,245 tCO2e in 20 years, and average annual VCUs with buffer deduction is 37,362 tCO2e.
The project activity will contribute to the environment (biodiversity conservation, rocky desertification prevention and soil erosion control), thus contribute to sustainable development

name: Tombwe Smallholder Reforestation Project
project_type: Agriculture Forestry and Other Land Use
description: The Tombwe Reforestation Project is a grouped project working across four key regions of Zambia. The reforestation project builds of Tombwe's multi-decade experience building a network of smallholder farmers. The project utilizes degraded lands and thousands of smallholders to plant select species of clumping bamboo. The project has been operational since 2019, and targets the planting of >950,000 seedlings over a ten year period. These plantings will result in significant and quantifiable carbon emissions removals while also providing a sustainable source of biomass for wood fuel and energy use, thereby reducing pressure on remaining trees and woodland areas.

name: Ribeirinho REDD+ Project
project_type: Agriculture Forestry and Other Land Use
description: The project protects over 199,962 ha in Portel, Para, ranked as a region depending on the year, either the 1st or 2nd highest rate of deforestation in the Amazon.  The project goal is to transform Portel, Para one of the poorest, lowest educated regions of Brazil into a stable, developed region that depends on sustainable forest use for its economy.  The project paid for 1252 traditional community families known as ribeirinhos to gain land tenure certificates in order to be able to complete this project.  The project knows that the only way to completely end illegal logging is to have the ribeirinhos stable so they can be the ones that can state “No more”. The project working with neighboring REDD projects plans to build 30 additional high quality schools in the region, that  will be used for children education, adult training, and university laboratories.  These 30 additional high quality schools, health clinics and security offices  are above and beyond the 30 schools, health clinics and security offices.

Serious land conflicts also arise. The proponents of the REDD projects claim to own land that partly belongs to the State of Pará, where the river settlement projects are being implemented.

name: COMACO Landscape Management Project - West
project_type: Agriculture Forestry and Other Land Use
description:
This project description document covers COMACO operations in Muchinga and Central provinces of Zambia. The COMACO Landscape Management Project (CLMP) promotes sustainable agriculture and forest management. The key objectives of the project are to increase smallholder farmer agricultural productivity, provide alternative livelihoods and reduce uncontrolled forest loss and degradation. Hence, the project comprises two components:
1. Sustainable Agricultural Land Management (SALM) component – which aims to promote widespread adoption of agricultural practices including conservation agriculture that increase food production per unit area and farmers’ income. The project promotes the adoption by farmers of legume-based alley cropping, residues management (e.g. mulching; cessation of residue burning), and reduced tillage among other SALM practices.
2. REDD+ (Avoided Unplanned Deforestation) component – which aims to reduce forest loss, and protect and expand areas under natural forest, and conserve biodiversity. This is achieved primarily through land use planning and creation of Community Conservation Areas (CCAs), coupled with sustainable non-extractive forest use, e.g. honey and mushrooms.  
The geographical area of the project stretches across sixteen (16) chiefdoms in nine (9) districts in the Central and Muchinga Province of Zambia, namely: Mulilo, Chikwa, Chifunda, Muyombe, Katyetye, Nkula, Chibale, Kabamba, Chitambo, Mukungule, Chikwanda, Mpumba, Kambombo, Lundu, Tembwe and Mubanga. It is a grouped project as defined in the VCS Standard (version 4.0); this project activity instance comprises 19,059 ha of agricultural land for the SALM component, and 131,491 ha for the REDD+ component. The potential project area for the SALM component is estimated to be about 81,500 ha of agricultural land, and for the REDD+ at 300,000 ha of forest.  
Prior to the project, poor farming practices such as residue burning, shifting cultivation and chitemene agricultural system (the cutting and burning of tree branches) led to rapid soil nutrient depletion and the traditional practices of collecting caterpillars (Lepidoptera), a butterfly/moth larva which is a traditional delicacy to the local people and largely consumed in urban areas of Zambia, involved cutting down trees or their branches leading to forest degradation. Uncontrolled and unregulated charcoal burning and cutting down of trees for wood fuel also contributed to deforestation and forest degradation. There was also a general lack of land use planning and forest management, undertaken in a participatory and coordinated manner – which led to destruction and fragmentation of the natural forests. The COMACO Landscape Management Project uses market incentives to promote adoption of SALM practices for forest and wildlife conservation. It uses land use planning with traditional leaders and communities to identify and zone areas for conservation and forest management known as Community Conservation Areas (CCA). A Community Conservation Plan (CCP) is developed and implemented for specific CCAs – including activities for sustainable forest management. These activities will result in increased and sustainable agricultural production, and forest conservation. Greenhouse gases (GHG) emission reductions will be generated through improved carbon storage on farms, and avoidance of mosaic deforestation from unplanned agricultural land conversion. The project activities will be supported by methodologies approved under a VCS approved GHG program to account for the project’s emissions reductions.
The annual average GHG emission reductions of the project are estimated at 147,925 tCO2-e, and total GHG emission reductions over 20 years are estimated at 2,958,500 tCO2-e. This estimate considers only the first 10 years of GHG emission reductions for the REDD+ component.

name: Lingbi County Wastewater Treatment Plant Project
developer: Lingbi Chenxin Green Industry Development Co., Ltd
description:
Lingbi County wastewater treatment project is located in Suzhou City, Anhui Province, China. The whole aerobic process includes pre-treatment process,secondary biological treatment process, tertiary deep treatment process and sludge treatment process, with a maximum design influent flow of 120,000 m3/d, the influent and effluent COD concentration are 850 mg/L and 50 mg/L separately.
In the baseline scenario, village sewage and some industrial wastewater from the county would have been treated through a series of deep open anaerobic lagoons. The open lagoons are the best available low-cost solution for wastewater treatment, which is also in compliance with the environmental regulations. In the project scenario, the wastewater will be treated through aerobic biological treatment technology, which includes pre-treatment process, secondary biological treatment process, tertiary deep treatment process and sludge treatment process.
Emission reductions are generated by reducing methane emissions of the open anaerobic lagoons in baseline scenario. Annual average estimation of GHG emission reductions from the project activity is 67,302 tCO2e/year,

name: Jinjia Jiayi CMM Power Generation Project
developer: Guizhou Panjiang CBM Development&Utilization Co., Ltd.
description:
Jinjia Jiayi CMM Power Generation Project (hereafter referred to as “the Project”) is located in Xiaochong Village, Pan County, Liupanshui City, Guizhou Province, People’s Republic of China.The purpose of the Project is to utilize the extracted coal mine methane (CMM) with a low concentration of methane to produce electricity. No coal bed methane (CBM) or ventilation air methane (VAM) utilization is involved. 

Six sets of CMM power generators are installed with a total installed capacity of 3.6 MW (6×0.6 MW). When all six power generators are in full operation, the Project is expected to export 17,280 MWh of electricity and destroy 7.2 million m3 (under normal conditions ) of methane every year. The generated electricity is supplied to the coal mines through the electricity distribution network in the Jinjia coal mine area; part of the electricity produced by the Project may also be exported to CSPG if there is any electricity surplus after the coal mine demand is fully met, thus displacing part of the electricity generated by CSPG dominated by fossil fuel-fired power plants.

The Project achieves emission reductions in two aspects: 1) it reduces methane emissions by capturing and destroying methane which would have been directly vented into the air in the baseline scenario; 2) it reduces CO2 emissions by displacing part of the electricity that would otherwise have been supplied by CSPG.

name: Unitán afforestation and reforestation of grazing lands project
project_type: Agriculture Forestry and Other Land Use
description:
The project activity “Unitán Afforestation and reforestation of grazing land project” (hereafter, “Unitán project”) is an afforestation project on extensive cattle grazing pastures area and abandoned agricultural lands using native (Schinopsis balansae) and exotic species (various varieties of Eucalyptus including Eucalyptus gxc) aiming to produce, as a priority product, logs for tannin industry and secondarily, fuelwood. The afforestation with this species will prevent the use of timber from native forests in the future.

Unitán comprises 5 properties located in Chaco and Formosa province, in the NorthEast region of Argentina (the host country), on lightly degraded grassland as a consequence of many decades of extensive cattle grazing and abandoned agriculture land by previous owners. This degradation is expected to continue in the absence of the project. The area of grasslands to be effectively planted and to be included within the Unitán project boundary is then 2,403ha (72.1% of Unitán total area). The unplanted area remaining in part as grassland and native forest remains, become biological corridors used for flora and fauna conservation.

From September 2016 until the time of PDD elaboration, a total area of 939,3 ha of the project was effectively planted. In addition, there is an area of 1,464 ha of planned plantation for the period 2021 to 2025 (mainly in owned and a minor part in leased lands).  In total, the project will have a final scale of about 2,400 ha.

The project utilizes two main species: Schinopsis balansae, a native species, and Eucalyptus (different varieties: mainly gxc and cloeziana), occupying 36%, 64% of the total planted area, and with rotation periods of 40 years, 6 and 20, respectively.
abuse_descr: 'Unitán, is one of the two primary Argentinian tannin manufacturers. It claims that ''although there are confirmed existence of indigenous communities'' in the area ''these communities have no productive or sacred link with the properties that have been included in the project.'' It conducted an online ''stakeholder consultation'' with forty participants. Unitán is accused of contaminating water, mishandling work-related accidents, and overlooking labour rights. Protesting workers, peasant and Indigenous communities have suffered severe police repression. Unitán is also accused of decades of large-scale deforestation and land grabbing to plant tannin-producing quebracho trees in the Chaco and Formosa states. Unitán has recently established a biomass electricity generating plant that will be supplied by its eucalyptus and quebrecho plantations' (grain.org, 2024).

name: KUAMUT RAINFOREST CONSERVATION PROJECT
project_type: Agriculture Forestry and Other Land Use
description:
The Kuamut Rainforest Conservation Project (‘Kuamut Project’) aims to protect and restore 83,381 ha of tropical forest in Sabah, Malaysia. The project is located in the Tongod and Kinabatangan Districts of Sabah, Malaysia. The project area is part of a long-term approximately 1-million-hectare concession granted to Yayasan Sabah on a 99-year lease arrangement with the Sabah Forestry Department (acting on behalf of the State Government of Sabah). Yayasan Sabah is a State-owned para-governmental charitable foundation that was formed in 1966 with the aim of ‘improving the lives of Malaysians living in Sabah’. 
Prior to the start of the project, the project area was designated as production forest (Class II). The area had been repeatedly logged in the past and was designated for further commercial exploitation. Project additionality is explicitly demonstrated by preventing 84,000 hectares of commercial logging over 30 years. Had the project not intervened, the resulting carbon emissions over this period would have contributed 16 million tonnes of carbon dioxide equivalent (tCO2e) into the atmosphere. 
In addition to its contribution to preventing the release of greenhouse gas (GHG) emissions, the project is protecting an important biodiverse habitat, Despite its ex-logged state, the area is known to support very high populations of elephants, banteng and orangutan, and endangered bird species including Helmeted Hornbill, Bornean Peacock Pheasant and Storms Stork.

The grouped project is being implemented by Brightspark Energy Private Limited, an Indian subsidiary of C-Quest Capital LLC.

name: SHINE - Distribution of LED lightbulbs in India-2
description:
The proposed small-scale grouped project activity (henceforth referred to as SHINE CPA 2) has already been registered as CPA 10484-P1-0002-CP1 under registered CDM Programme of Activities (PoA) 10484 titled:” SHINE – Distribution of LED Lightbulbs in India” which involves distribution of Light Emitting Diodes (LEDs) for domestic lighting in North-East Indian states of Tripura, Assam, Meghalaya, Arunachal Pradesh, Mizoram, Manipur and Nagaland.
According to CEA’s (Central Electricity Authority) Load Generation Balance Report 2018-19, actual demand supply gap in the North Eastern region was -2.8% while the peak deficit was 4.1% during the year 2017-18. Trend shows that there has been a steady increase in peak demand in North East while supply has not been able to match up to this demand. This project activity could have a positive impact on the demand supply gap by introducing energy efficient light bulbs thereby reducing peak hour demand of power in residential areas.

developer: Guangxi Liyuanbao Science and Technology Co., Ltd.
description: The proposed project is a newly built composting plant which designed to treat organic wastes to produce organic fertilizer. The proposed project comprises of fermentation system and fertilizer production system, etc.  The instances 1 is site is designed to treat 400,000 tonnes wet organic waste per year and produce 300,000 tonnes fertilizer per year. The instances 2 is designed to treat 150,000 tonnes wet organic waste per year and produce 110,000 tonnes fertilizer per year.

name: Grouped CNG Vehicles Project in India
description:
The major purpose of this grouped project activity is to use CNG Vehicles instead of fossil fuel powered vehicles in India. The usage of CNG powered vehicles instead of fossil fuel powered ones leads to lower GHG emissions per distance driven. Project vehicles included are those sold directly or through authorized dealers. Only vehicles are counted where such an agreement has been signed. This is group project activity where the CNG vehicles can be added via instances throughout the crediting period. There are 30 CNG vehicles involved in the first instance of the project activity. Transport emissions have increased by almost a quarter since 1990 this means the transition to zero emissions will need to be swift and the importance of radical improvement through
fuel switching is growing. In this context there is an ongoing discussion about the role of methane in transport. Some stakeholders - often representing the fossil gas industry - claim the use of methane would contribute to decarbonizing transport in 2016, T&E published a study by Ricardo Energy & Environment that analyzed the role of methane in transport. The study found using fossil gas has no meaningful climate benefits compared to petroleum based fuels, whilst Biomethane cannot be produced in sufficient volumes to make a meaningful contribution.

name: İZMIR LANDFILL GAS (LFG) CAPTURE AND UTILIZATION PROJECT
project_type: Energy industries (renewable/non-renewable sources); Waste handling and disposal
description:
In order to develop a municipal solid waste management system that will be environmentally friendly and sustainable, İzmir Harmandalı Solid Waste Disposal Site (SWDS) Rehabilitation and Landfill Gas (LFG) Capture and Utilization Project is being implemented by İzmir Novtek Enerji Elektrik Üretim A.Ş.    

The proposed project activity is a Methane Gas Power Generating Plant and Mechanical Sorting Facility with the installed capacity of “39.690 MWe”. The project is built within the structure of Harmandalı Solid Waste Landfill Facility in İzmir province, as the third-largest SWDS in Turkey, and will be operated as integrated with the currently installed units. 

It is planned to rehabilitate the İzmir Harmandalı SWDS that receives around 4,500 tons of municipal waste coming from 23 different districts of İzmir province daily and to generate renewable electric power by capturing and utilizing landfill gas.

Whilst providing sustainable development benefits to the host communities and the host country, the proposed project activity will reduce greenhouse gas (GHG) emissions mainly by 

•	preventing GHG emissions, methane in particular, from being emitted directly to the atmosphere from waste at the Harmandalı SWDS that would be otherwise left to be decomposed;
•	replacing the electricity that would have otherwise been generated by the national grid which is heavily dependent on fossil-fuel-based resources, through generating renewable energy and feeding it to the grid.

The project has begun to generate electricity on October 29th, 2019, which is regarded as the project start date. 

This project adopts a fixed crediting period of 10 years. The expected average annual emission reductions are 618,042 tCO2eq/y. Accordingly, the project is expected to generate 6,180,420 tCO2eq emissions reduction throughout its first crediting period. 

For further information on the project, please see the informative video below:
https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=Hl36alapiQg&t=124s

name: Fujian Qingliu IFM (conversion of logged to protected forest) Project
project_type: Agriculture Forestry and Other Land Use
description:
The Fujian Qingliu IFM (conversion of logged to protected forest) Project (hereafter “the project activity”) is implemented in Qingliu County, Sanming City, Fujian Province of China by Fujian Qingliu Forestry Co., Ltd. The geographic coordinate of project is 116°38’ ~117°11’ E and 25°47’ ~26°21’ N, the total area is 180,630 ha, which includes the Improved Forest Management (IMF) of the forests in the conversion of logged to protected forest.
The area of the project activity is 5856 ha, including 698 subcompartments spreading over Dengjia Town, Lijia Town, Litian Town, Lingdi Town, Longjin Town, Linshe Town, Shaqiang Town, Songkou Town, Songxi Town, Tianyuan Town, Wenjiao Town, Yupeng Town, Changxiao Town of Fujian Qingliu Forestry Co., Ltd. All these departments are state-owned forests and have the legal right to forest ownership. The species involved in the project are Chinese Fir, Masson pine and Broad-leaf trees.
Prior to the implementation of the project activity, the trees are logged annually according to a valid and verifiable government-approved timber management plan for harvesting the project area. The implementation of the project activity converses the trees to protected forest to reduce the GHG emissions for about 2,858,234 tCO2e in 30 years, the average annual emission reduction is 95,274 tCO2e and Verified Carbon Units with buffer deduction is about 2,229,423 tCO2e in 30 years, the average annual VCUs with buffer deduction is 74,314 tCO2e.
The project activity will contribute to the environment (biodiversity conservation and soil erosion control), thus contribute to sustainable development.

name: Experimental regeneration of diverse forests on abandoned pastures in Panguana, Peru
project_type: Agriculture Forestry and Other Land Use
description:
Panguana is the oldest biological research station in Peru (founded in 1968) with a focus on studying the immense biodiversity of the Amazon rainforest. The research station is located on the western edge of the Reserva Comunal El Sira (RC El Sira), a national protected area established to protect the pristine montane rainforests of the Cordillera El Sira. The buffer zone of the RCS and its surrounding area is mainly populated by indigenous communities and small-scale farmers. Intensive deforestation in this area in favour of pastures has resulted in fragments of primary rainforests existing primarily as islands between pastures. In this respect, the private nature reserve of Panguana currently forms a peninsula with an intact connection to the untouched rainforests in the heart of the RC El Sira. Restoration of degraded pastureland and rehabilitation of secondary forests adjacent to existing old growth forests at Panguana presents the opportunity to conserve an important biodiversity corridor as well as an effective strategy for rehabilitation of degraded tropical forest across the region.
The project has the following main goals:
    • Restore natural rainforests on pastures within the area of the Panguana foundation (~140 ha)
    • Accelerate forest restoration by testing different approaches and developing best practices for local conditions
    • Introduce sustainable food and tree production systems (permaculture, aquaponics, tree nursery)
    • Only use inexpensive materials and methods, easily available in the region
    • Exchange knowledge and develop a sustainable landscape management together with local stakeholders (indigenous communities, small-scale farmers, local institutions)

It is expected that the project activities will lead to a mean annual removal of ~16 t CO2e per hectare during the first 20 years.

name: Tradewater International Honduras

name: Yongkang huachuan MSW landfill site LFG comprehensive utilization project

description:

name: Viet Nam Improved Cookstove Project by KCM – Improved Cookstove Project in Yen Bai Province – CPA 007
description: The main objective of this CPA is the installation of energy efficient Improved Cooking Stoves (ICS) in the households (HHs) that are using wood as cooking fuel located within the districts of Mu Cang Chai, Luc Yen, Tran Yen and Yen Binh within Yen Bai Province, Viet Nam. A total of 26,000 ICSs are distributed under this CPA. The ICS will result in reduced firewood consumption leading to climate change mitigation in a sustainable manner. Overall objectives are reduction of greenhouse gases, conservation of forests and woodlands as well as improved health conditions of ICS users due to improved indoor air quality.

name: Taiba N’Diaye Wind Power
description:
The project activity involves the installation and operation of a 15 8 .7 MW wind farm in the commune of Taiba N’Diaye , Senegal. Parc Eolien Taiba N’Diaye
(PETN) is Senegal’s first large scale wind energy project and a critical part of the government’s “Plan Senegal Emergent” Emergent”. The project has been built by Lekela and is owned and operated by Parc Eolien Taiba N’Diaye S.A U
PETN is designed to generate electricity for at least 20 years through its 46 Vestas wind turbines. The generated electricity is supplied to SENELEC , the state owned utility, under a long term power purchase agreement (PPA). PETN commissioning since De cember 2019 resulted in a 15% increase in electricity
generation capacity for the country, providing power for over 2 million people.

name: Solid Waste to Bio CNG Production Facility in India
project_type: Energy industries (renewable/non-renewable sources); Waste handling and disposal
description: The proposed grouped project activity is a step towards supporting the implementation and installation of Municipal Solid Waste to Bio CNG production facility in India. The implementation of project activity ensures energy security, diversification of the grid generation mix and sustainable growth of the electricity generation sector in India. The group project activity will targets the unexplored potentials of biogas utilisation by installing biogas plant with purification system to produce bio CNG gas which is equal to CNG gas in terms of quality and calorific value. Biogas technology provides an alternate source of energy in India, and is hailed as an archetypal appropriate technology that meets the basic need for cooking fuel in rural and urban areas. Using local resources, viz. food waste, cattle waste, vegetable and other organic wastes, energy and manure are derived.

name: 413 REDD Project
project_type: Agriculture Forestry and Other Land Use
description: The 413 REDD Project (413 Project) aims to reduce emissions derived deforestation and forest degradation in the Amazonian tropical rain forest. The project proponent is 413 Environmental, LLC, and BMO Radicle Brazil have prepared the PD (Project Design). The project applies the Avoided Planned Deforestation (APD) approach and uses VCS standards and methodologies to a REDD voluntary carbon market. The project's geographical boundary comprises a parcel land named Matá-Matá (500,996 hectares), with 500,996 hectares of primary ancient and undisturbed areas of tropical rainforest. Thus, the project area comprises 476,995 hectares of dense lowland forest, 17,705 hectares of dense alluvial forest and 5,914 hectares of dense sub-montane forest. The parcel land is situated in the municipalities of Manicoré and Novo Aripuanã, southern State of Amazonas, Brazil. The project will generate GHG emission reductions from changes in land use caused by imminent deforestation and forest degradation. The emission of 43,973,073 tons of CO2e will be avoided with the 413 project, considering a lifespan of 30 years, with an annual average of 1,465,769 tons of CO2e calculated for the whole period (2021- 2050) and 34,615,467 for the first 10-year crediting period (2021-2030). The 413 Project seeks to be validated as Golden Level because exceptional climate measures will be undertaken to adapt the population to climate change. The baseline was conceived from the most-likely scenario, which is converting 20% of the forest to pasture for cattle raising. The conversion of forests to alternative land uses of up to 20% of private properties is permitted by the Brazilian Forest Code but the project proponent decided to protect forest and avoid deforestation and forest degradation, reducing CO2 emissions. In the planned deforestation approach, the conversion agent in the baseline is the owner of the area because he has the right to deforest under the current legislation.

name: Zero Carbon Aripuanã River Valley REDD Project 1
project_type: Agriculture Forestry and Other Land Use
description: The Zero Carbon Aripuanã Valley REDD Project 1 (ZCH1 Project) aims to reduce emissions derived deforestation and forest degradation in the Amazonian tropical rain forest. The project proponent is Zero Carbon Holdings, LLC, and BMO Radicle has prepared the PD (Project Design). The project applies the Avoided Planned Deforestation (APD) approach and uses VCS standards and methodologies to a REDD voluntary carbon market. The project's geographical boundary comprises one parcel named Matá-Matá II (153,985 hectares) of primary ancient and undisturbed areas of tropical rainforest. Thus, the project area comprises 153,977 hectares of dense lowland forest of a unique pioneer natural shrubby vegetation. The project will generate GHG emission reductions from changes in land use caused by imminent deforestation and forest degradation. The emission of 13,705,917 tons of CO2e will be avoided with the ZCH1 project, considering a lifespan of 30 years, with an annual average of 456,864 tons of CO2e calculated for the whole period (2021-2050) and 1,301,887 for the first monitoring report, including Jan 1st, 2021 to December 31st 2022.  The ZCH1 Project focuses on activities designated as Avoided Planned Deforestation (APD) and is built on the VCS VM0007 methodology.  The baseline was conceived from the most-likely scenario, which is converting 20% of the forest to pasture for cattle raising. The conversion of forests to alternative land uses of up to 20% of private properties is permitted by the Brazilian Forest Code but the project proponent decided to protect forest and avoid deforestation and forest degradation, reducing CO2 emissions. In the planned deforestation approach, the conversion agent in the baseline is the owner of the area because he has the right to deforest under the current legislation.

The total installed capacity of the project is 1.067MW. The project is expected to supply a total of 81,092 MWh electricity to CCPG during the fixed 10-year crediting period, with the annual average amount of 8,109 MWh.

name: PANAMA FORESTS CONSERVATION PROJECT REDUCTION OF GHG EMISSIONS THROUGH DEFORESTATION AND AVOIDED DEGRADATION.  -Alliance of Indigenous Peoples and Rural Communities of Panama-
developer: APRONAD Asociacion para la Promocion de Nuevas Alternativas de Desarrllo
project_type: Agriculture Forestry and Other Land Use
description:
This is a National Grouped Project that is developed throughout the territory of Panama. It has three objectives: (i) mitigate climate change by reducing GHG emissions from unplanned deforestation that occur due to historical and social factors independent of the project; (ii) contribute to the conservation of biodiversity, including the High Conservation Values related to the Protected Areas determined by the Panamanian State, and (iii) promote the sustainable development of local communities. The following results are expected: (a) the protection of approximately 61,707.41 ha. of primary and secondary forests during the useful life of the project, located in the Protected Areas and their buffer zones. The project would prevent the release to the atmosphere of 11,195,383.00 tCO2e of GHG emissions in 30 years, with an annual average of 198.22 Ton / Co2e per hectare, and (b) forge a strategic alliance between indigenous peoples and settlers and agro-industrial companies, around the conservation of forests, helping to consolidate environmental governance.

The forests of the Project Area are characterized by great biodiversity and are home to the five species with the highest biomass content: Cuipo (Cavanillesia platanifolia), black mangrove (Avicennia bicolor), pine (Pinus caribaea), Espavé (Anacardium excelsum) and rubber (Ficus elastica). Two of the existing species in the Project Area are reported as Critically Endangered (CR): Podocarpus oleifolius and Swietenia macrophylla; eight are endangered (EN) and 52 are vulnerable (VU) according to the IUCN red list and national status.

Livelihood’s activities, including forest maintenance and conservation and community-based rural tourism, will provide communities with opportunities to overcome poverty. throughout the Project. The project will use carbon finance to avoid threats from extensive ranching, agriculture, and selective logging, carrying out different activities to reduce degradation and deforestation.

name: Establishing a Rubber Cultivation Project with Community Engagement in the Eastern & Uva Provinces of Sri Lanka
developer: Rubber Reseach Institute of Sri Lanka

name: Montes del Este afforestation through high quality timber in degraded grasslands
developer: Fideicomiso Financiero Forestal Montes del Este

The project comprises a total of 4.314 ha of land previously under extensive grazing by beef cattle, on which afforestation for obtaining high-value, long-lived timber products and for sequestering large amounts of carbon dioxide from the atmosphere will be established. The project sequesters CO2 through forest plantation in degraded grassland areas, generating net anthropogenic removals by sinks

name: SANTIAGO PONIENTE LANDFILL GAS  PROJECT
project_type: Energy industries (renewable/non-renewable sources); Waste handling and disposal
description:
The proposed project activity has the objective to capture and to flare/use the landfill gas produced in the landfill called - Relleno Sanitario Santiago Poniente, located in the commune of Maipú in Chile.

Prior to the implementation of the project activity the landfill gas partially burned in the Landfill Gas collection and flaring system.

The first phase of the project was the refurbishment to an efficient capture, collection and flaring system to burn CH4 (a greenhouse gas). These actions will reduce odors and adverse environmental impacts.

During the second phase, the project will install generators that will combust the LFG to produce electricity, using part of the electricity for self-consumption at the landfill facilities and the surplus part will be exported to the grid. The flares will be kept in operation due to LFG excess, periods when electricity will not be produced or other operational considerations. The LFG power plant will be expected to install up to 4MW upon project completion. However, the final equipment that will be chosen (as well as the final installed capacity) may vary depending on the availability of the generator equipment in the market at the time of actual implementation of the second phase.

name: Henan Tongbai and Zhenping Afforestation Project
developer: Beijing Qianyuhui Environmental Technology Co., Ltd.
project_type: Agriculture Forestry and Other Land Use
description:
Henan Tongbai and Zhenping Afforestation Project (hereafter referred as “the project”) is located in Tongbai county and Zhenping county, Nanyang City, Henan Province, China. The project is to establish forest on the barren land to generate GHG emission reductions and contribute to local sustainable development. The project is 22,292.4 ha of forest was established by direct planted on barren lands in Tongbai county and Zhenping county, Nanyang City, Henan Province, China. 

The project activity aims to:  Sequester carbon dioxide and mitigating climate change; Enhance biodiversity conservation by increasing the connectivity of forests; - Improve the quality and quantity of the vegetation; Improve soil and water conservation and contribute to sustainable development; Generate income and job opportunities for local communities. 

There is no natural renewal and reforestation and all sites were barren hills at least 10 years prior to the implementation of the project. The main objective specie are Pinus massoniana, Pinus elliottii, Paulownia, Populus, Acer mono Maxim, Broad-leaved tree and Oak which are native species according to the baseline survey. With the implementation of the project activity, total GHG emission reductions or removals are about 22,625,866 tCO2e in 60 years the average annual emission reduction is 377,097 tCO2e and total GHG emission reductions or removals with buffer deduction is about 20,363,279 tCO2e in 60 years, the average annual GHG emission reductions or removals with buffer deduction is 339,387 tCO2e.

name: Renewable Electricity Grouped Project in Africa
description: Renewable Electricity Grouped Project in Africa (hereafter referred to as “grouped project”) is a renewable energy generation grouped project by Luponde Hydro Limited (LHL) (hereinafter referred to as “the project owner” and “project developer”). LHL is fully owned by Rift Valley Energy (RVE), the energy division of Rift Valley Corporation (RVC), which aims to sustainably develop renewable energy resources in East and Southern Africa starting with Tanzania. description:

All these forests are state-owned forests or privately-owned forests or collective-owned forests, and have the legal right to forest ownership. Before the implementation of the project activity, the trees are logged based on a valid and verifiable government-approved timber management plan for harvesting the project area. The implementation of the project activity converses the trees to protected forest to reduce the GHG emissions for about 811,736 tCO2e in 30 years, the average annual emission reduction is 27,057 tCO2e and Verified Carbon Units with buffer deduction is about 633,146  tCO2e in 30 years, and average annual VCUs with buffer deduction is 21,104 tCO2e.
The project activity will contribute to the environment (biodiversity conservation and soil erosion control), thus contribute to sustainable development.

name: The Serra do Amolar REDD+ Project
project_type: Agriculture Forestry and Other Land Use
description:
The Instituto Homem Pantaneiro's (IHP) REDD+ project for the protection of the Amolar Network (in Portuguese Rede de Proteção e Conservação da Serra do Amolar) named REDD+ Serra do Amolar project is part of the Agriculture, Forestry and Other Land Use (AFOLU) sector under the Reducing Emissions from Deforestation and Degradation (REDD) project category. Specifically, the project is part of the Avoided Unplanned Deforestation and Degradation (AUDD) project category.
REDD+ Serra does Amolar project preserves and conserves a representative part of the Pantanal ecosystem, which is about 140,900 ha, and which is located in the strategic region of the Mato Grosso do Sul and Mato Grosso. This region has high levels of deforestation risk caused by land speculation associated with livestock and agriculture. The project has quantifiables climate, community, and biodiversity (CCB) benefits because it provides full-time employment, training, and access for families that live in and around the project area to become self-empowered in a region where there are very few job opportunities. The project also seeks to promote and improve activities seven existing strategic lines, including ecotourism, research, fire prevention and governance/administration, and others.

The Serra do Amolar project meets the criteria of GL3 Gold Level. - Exceptional benefits to Biodiversity, according to the vulnerability criterion described by CCB for presenting critically threatened species (IUCN Red List) as one endangered species – the giant otter (Pteronura brasiliensis) – and five vulnerable species: the lowland tapir (Tapirus terrestris), the white-lipped peccary, (Tayassu pecari), the giant armadillo (Priodontes maximus) and the giant anteater (Myrmecophaga tridactyla) and the bare-faced curassow (Crax fasciolata). The project also has a well-documented population of the near-threatened jaguar (Panthera onca).

name: Soc Son Waste to Power Plant Project
project_type: Energy industries (renewable/non-renewable sources); Waste handling and disposal
description:
The Soc Son waste to power plant project (hereinafter “the project”) includes the construction and operation of a waste treatment plant, which is located at Nam Son waste treatment complex area, Soc Son District, Hanoi. The project is owned by Ha Noi Thien Y Environmental Energy Joint Stock Company, which was established from 3 investors including Soc Son renewable Energy Joint Stock Company, Perfect Wave Holdings Limited Company and Europe Tianying BVBA Company.
The purpose of this project activity is to treat 4,000 ton of municipal solid waste (MSW) per day and generate electricity with the installed capacity of 75 MW. The annual estimated electricity output of 388.05 GWh is supplied to the national grid via the transmission line. The Soc Son waste to power plant will use 5 Waterleau continuous grate-type incinerators for treating MSW and a combination of 5 boilers, 3 steam turbines and 3 generators to recover heat from combustion of MSW for generating electricity.
The project activity help to avoid methane release from SWDS(s) in the absence of the project activity and generate renewable electricity, which displaced part of the electricity otherwise supplied by grid connected fossil fuel fired power plants. Thus, GHG emission reductions can be achieved. The expected CO2 emission reduction from the proposed project is 486,957 tCO2e annually and 3,408,698 tCO2e in total over the first 7 years crediting period.

name: Yunnan Qiubei Afforestation Project
project_type: Agriculture Forestry and Other Land Use
description: Yunnan Qiubei Afforestation Project (hereafter referred as “the project”) is located in Qiubei county, Wenshan Zhuang and Miao Autonomous Prefecture, Yunnan Province, China. The project is to establish forest on the barren land to generate GHG emission reductions and contribute to local sustainable development. The project is 10,033.4 ha of forest was established by direct planted on barren lands in Qiubei county, Wenshan Zhuang and Miao Autonomous Prefecture, Yunnan Province.

name: Distribution of Justa model Chimney Rocket Stoves in Central America
description: In partnership with StoveTeam International (STI) and Trees Water and People (TWP), Justa StoveWorks will disseminate Improved Cookstove (ICS) in Central America that will dramatically increase community access to sustainable energy technology by providing, installing, and maintaining energy efficient and smoke reducing cookstoves at a subsidized rate. The distribution of these stoves directly addresses energy poverty in addition to several other socio-economic challenges facing the communities in Central America. Through the distribution of the Justa chimney rocket stoves, this grouped project reduces demand for wood fuel, slowing local deforestation and empowering rural communities throughout Central America.

name: AMG OHIO COMPLEX GHG EMISSIONS REDUCTION PROJECT
description:
This project quantifies the greenhouse gas (GHG) emission reductions resulting from secondary manufacturing processes which produce metals, metal oxides or alloys from metal bearing waste streams. Secondary metal manufacturing processes are less energy intensive and produce lower amounts of GHG emissions compared to primary metals manufacturing. The emissions reductions result from secondary manufacturing compared to primary metal manufacturing.
The project location spans across the AMG Advanced Metallurgical Group N.V. Ohio Complex with facilities located in Cambridge and Zanesville, Ohio, US.  The principal products from the process at the project location is ferrovanadium, ferronickel, ferromolybdenum and alumina.   The project is estimated to reduce 200,000 metric tons of GHG emissions per year.

Applicable Methodology: Methodology for Reduction in GHG Emissions from Metal Production Using Metal Bearing Waste

name: Southern Paraguay Sustainable Afforestation Project
project_type: Agriculture Forestry and Other Land Use
description:
The project is located in Itaipua and Misiones and is implemented by SilviPar S.A. Silvipar currently has 1,966.67 ha of eucalyptus clones planted and distributed in four properties (Santa Bárbara, Flor Cue, Stella Maris y San Rafael) in the departments of Itapúa and Misiones, to be certified, in accordance with the Verified Carbon Standard (VCS) eligibility criteria for the Agriculture, Forestry, and Other Land Use (AFOLU) projects grouped under the category of afforestation, restoration, and revegetation (ARR).
In July 2022, this project changed its name from Silvipar S.A. forest plantations for the certification of carbon credits to Southern Paraguay Sustainable Afforestation Project and the proponent was changed from Silvipar S.A. to Saiff Hold Co. Ltd.

name: Improving rural livelihood through agroforestry practices in Punjab, India- II
developer: Department of Forests and Wildlife Preservation, Punjab
project_type: Agriculture Forestry and Other Land Use
description: The proposed ARR VCS project plans to promote sustainable agroforestry for small-scale farmers to provide them with financial benefits and ensure GHG mitigation in the state of Punjab, India. The project is being conducted in three divisions of Punjab namely Hoshiarpur, Dasuya and Pathankot. The total project area is 3309.56 ha and the agroforestry plantations done by farmers from 2017 to 2020 are considered. The plantations done by the farmers are in two types (i) the plantations undertaken at personal level and (ii) the plantations undertaken under the Sub-Mission on Agroforestry (SMAF) under NMSA (National Mission on Sustainable Agroforestry) implemented by Punjab Forest Department. The main agroforestry tree species planted in each village for the year 2017, 2018, 2019 and 2020 are clonal Poplar, clonal Eucalyptus, Teak, Shisham, Chandan, Drek. The plantations undertaken by the farmers in their respective farms are block, intercrop or boundary plantations.

name: CNG AgriCarbon Rewards Programme
project_type: Agriculture Forestry and Other Land Use
description: This innovative, and first of its kind programme in South Africa aims to assist farmers to overcome barriers that prevent adoption of improved land management practices by providing technical assistance where needed and channeling rewards for successful climate mitigation and adaptation activities from carbon markets back to the farmers. The programme is designed to expand over time and cover a range of farming activities in South Africa to help drive the change from the current common agricultural practices towards resilient and sustainable agricultural systems.

name: Restoring Degraded Lands for Biodiversity Conservation and Livelihood Development in Brazil
project_type: Agriculture Forestry and Other Land Use
description: The objective of the proposed project in Brazil is to restore degraded lands and improve the connectivity of forest cover to restore genetic diversity and achieve viable wildlife populations of endemic, threatened, and endangered species. The Project focuses on biodiversity conservation and wildlife habitat restoration with the active participation of the local communities.

name: Improving rural livelihood through agroforestry practices in Punjab, India- I
developer: Department of Forests and Wildlife Preservation, Punjab
project_type: Agriculture Forestry and Other Land Use
description:
The proposed ARR VCS project plans to promote sustainable agroforestry for small-scale farmers to
provide them with financial benefits and ensure GHG mitigation in the state of Punjab, India. The
project is being conducted in three divisions of Punjab namely Sahibzada Ajit Singh Nagar, Rupnagar
and Nawanshahr. The total project area is 3,992.71 ha and the agroforestry plantations done by
farmers from 2017 to 2020 are considered. The plantations done by the farmers are in two types
(i) the plantations undertaken at personal level and (ii) the plantations undertaken under the SubMission on Agroforestry (SMAF) under NMSA (National Mission on Sustainable Agroforestry)
implemented by Punjab Forest Department. The main agroforestry tree species planted in each
