name: CIG Pilot Project 1 - Nitrogen Management Credit Program (NMCP) Project
description:
The Project quantifies emission reductions (in the form of nitrous oxide or N2O) arising from a reduction in the rate of fertilizer (synthetic and/or organic) applied to corn crops on farms of the North Central Region (NCR).
The rate reduction arises as a result of the adoption of fertilizer Best Management Practices (BMPs) aimed at application of the right fertilizer type at the right time, using the right placement and at the right rate in order to minimize denitrification, leaching and run-off, and volatilization, and thereby increasing fertilizer efficiency. Moves towards efficient fertilizer use are happening on a global scale, with increased recognition of the dual needs of providing sufficient food for a rapidly increasing population with limited resources, and addressing climate change issues, where fertilizer application is perceived as a significant emission source.
methodology: N2O Emission Reductions through Reduced Use of Fertilizer on Agricultural Crops

name: Edaleen Cow Power, LLC
description: The Edaleen Cow Power, LLC Project is an in-ground plug-flow dairy digester system that was built to capture the biogas from dairy manure, the majority of which would have been stored in an uncovered anaerobic lagoon prior to project implementation. The biogas that is captured from the digester system is used to generate electricity through one generator. Any excess biogas not combusted by the gen-sets is combusted in an open flare. Biogas produced by the digester is monitored continuously using thermal mass flowmeters.
methodology: ARB Compliance Offset Protocol: Capturing and Destroying Methane from Manure Management Systems

name: Elk Creek Coal Mine Methane Destruction & Utilization Project
description: Installation of a facility to collect and utilize CMM from a temporarily idle coal mine. CMM is withdrawn using vacuum pumps from bore holes and then destroyed either via an enclosed flare or three electricity generators. Flow of CMM is measured continuously using flow meters for each destruction device. Methane concentration is measured continuously using gas analyzers. All data is recorded by a data logger.
methodology: ARB Compliance Offset Protocol: Mine Methane Capture Projects

name: Elk Creek Permit Area Abandoned Mine Project
description: Installation of a facility to collect and utilize mine methane from abandoned mines. Mine methane is withdrawn using vacuum pumps from boreholes/wells and then destroyed either via an enclosed flare or three electricity generators. Flow of MM is measured continuously using flow meters for each destruction device. Methane concentration is measured continuously using gas analyzers. All data is recorded by a data logger.
methodology: ARB Compliance Offset Protocol: Mine Methane Capture Projects

name: Emission Reductions in California Rice Management Systems
location: Colusa and Glenn Counties in Californias Sacramento Valley., CALIFORNIA, US
description: The Project aims to support farmers in the changes to rice farming practices that will produce GHG emission reductions and other environmental benefits. This initial group of rice farmers in California is participating in the first validation and verification of the offsets under ACR. The voluntary management practices that will be undertaken by farmers include; early drainage and baling as is relevant and practical for a specific field. Additional management practices may be considered in the future, based on farmer interest and carbon market eligibility. methodology: Emission Reductions in Rice Management Systems

name: Emission Reductions in Midsouth Rice Management Systems
location: Prairie, McGhee, Desha, Mississippi and Craighead Counties in Arkansas, and Coahoma, Bolivar, and Washington Counties in Mississippi, ARKANSAS; MISSISSIPPI, US
description:
The project aims to support farmers in the changes to rice farming practices that will produce GHG emission reductions and other environmental benefits. In addition, the project aims to support the validation and issuance of resulting offsets under ACR.

methodology: Emission Reductions in Rice Management Systems

name: Fielding Environmental HFC Reclamation Offset Project
description: Fielding Environmental (Fielding) is one of only two major refrigerant reclamation and recycling companies in Canada. Refrigerant reclamation and recycling is a core business unit for Fielding and it includes ODS and non-ODS refrigerants that come from various sectors across the country including the automotive sector and the refrigeration and air conditioning sector. Fielding receives refrigerants from authorized wholesalers or directly from contractors and end-users that have collected refrigerant from end-of-life equipment or after equipment retrofits. name: Finite Carbon - Appalachian Carbon Exchange IFM
location: Southern Cumberland Mountains, TENNESSEE; ALABAMA; GEORGIA, US
description:
The Appalachian Carbon Exchange (ACE) project implements the Programmatic Development Approach with multiple landowners to protect ~7,500 acres of mixed hardwood forest in Tennessee, Alabama and Georgia. These carbon-rich forests are located in areas with a high risk of conversion, maintaining and sequestering additional carbon in a highly biodiverse region that provides climate resilient habitat for threatened and endangered species. 
Rooted in bioregionalism, ACE is a non-profit, community first partnership of dedicated landowners and businesses in Appalachia. The land in the ACE IFM project consists of intact mixed hardwood forest that provides habitat connectivity through essential wildlife corridors and climate resilience with its unique topography, both above and belowground. It also helps protect regional water quality and provides access to iconic and beloved outdoor recreation areas. Through its dedicated landowners, the project supports long-term stewardship of these priori
methodology: Improved Forest Management (IFM) on Non-Federal U.S. Forestlands

name: Finite Carbon - Batchawana Bay Forest IFM
description:
Located just outside of Sault Ste. Marie, Ontario, the Finite Carbon - Batchawana Bay IFM project
covers approximately 23,000 hectares of sustainably-managed forestland. The IFM project
incorporates periods of deferred harvesting, timber stand improvement, and retention of snags,
bolstering the health and value of the forest while also increasing carbon stored. Additionally, forest
management activities within the project will meet or exceed Ontario best management practices for
protecting water quality - including increased forest cover in riparian areas and upland forests adjacent
to riparian areas to moderate stream temperatures and mitigate flooding impacts.
methodology: Improved Forest Management (IFM) on Canadian Forestlands

name: Finite Carbon - Bessey Development Company IFM
location: Somerset, Penobscot, Oxford, Waldo, Kennebec, and Lincoln Counties, Maine, MAINE, US
description:
Through this project, Bessey Development is protecting 20,000+ acres of Maine forests under the American Carbon Registrys Improved Forest Management protocol. With lands near Augusta, Maine, the state capital, the project conserves native forest at risk of conversion through 2062, while maintaining and accruing additional sequestered carbon. 

The multi-generational family owner practices sustainable forest management, carbon sequestration and land conservation to benefit rural community economic development, wildlife populations, recreation, air quality and water quality. The mature and diverse forest is American Tree Farm System certified, meeting the highest standards for sustainability, and consists of an even mixture of softwood and hardwood species. Bessey allows unrestricted public access for recreation on their woodlands, as is traditional in New England.
methodology: Improved Forest Management (IFM) on Non-Federal U.S. Forestlands

These two 501(c)(3) non-profit organizations have similar conservation missions, work in the same region of Maine, and are accredited by the Land Trust Accreditation Commission. The project is the first to arise from the Carbon Offset Pilot Program, a partnership between Finite Carbon and Land Trust Alliance. The project area is dominated by a mix of hardwood (maple/beech/birch) and softwood (spruce/pine/fir) forest types typical of Maine forests. description:

location: Aroostook, Penobscot, and Piscataquis Counties, MAINE, US
description: Located in Northern Maine, the Northeast Carry Woodlands IFM project covers approximately 200,000 acres of sustainably-managed forestland. The IFM project supports maintenance of timber harvest levels below annual growth to encourage the health and value of the forest, while increasing carbon stored. Project management activities will serve to protect forest habitat and species found within the project area - including the threatened Canada Lynx. Important habitat components found within the project area include early successional habitat, hard and soft mast, seeps, standing dead trees (snags), coarse woody debris, deer winter areas, and vernal pools. Additionally, forest management activities within the project will meet or exceed the Maine Forest Service Best Management Practices for protecting water quality - including increased forest cover in riparian areas and upland forests adjacent to riparian areas to moderate stream temperatures and mitigate flooding impacts.

Scott Woodlands is SFI-certified and dedicated to leadership and sustainability in all aspects of forestland stewardship and the wood products industry. Its commitment to sustainable forest management, carbon sequestration, and land conservation brings benefits to rural community economic development, wildlife populations, and air and water quality. The Scott forestlands consist of approximately half pine stands and half well-stocked, mixed hardwood stands, adjacent to and near the Savannah River. This intact forest helps protect and maintain the Savannah River, which provides drinking water to 1.4 million people, including two of Georgia's major metro areas, Augusta and Savannah.

location: Mississippi Alluvial Valley, ARKANSAS; ILLINOIS; LOUISIANA; MISSISSIPPI, US
description: The project uses tree planting to establish trees on lands that have been in continuous agricultural use and have not been in a forested state for 10 years. Landowners commit to protecting the trees. Limited harvest is allowed after trees grow to the point where crowding of trees is expected to cause some trees to die, but in no case may harvesting occur if it would result in a basal area of live trees of less than 100 square feet per acre after the harvesting.  Through 2022 the GreenTrees Program has enrolled 136,650 acres.  GreenTrees is a programmatic offset program and continues to enroll new landowners and plant lands to scale GHG removals.
methodology: Afforestation and Reforestation of Degraded Lands

name: Greenwood Dairy Anaerobic Digester
location: Canton, New York, NEW YORK, US
description: The Greenwood Dairy Anaerobic Digester utilizes manure from Greenwood Dairy in Canton, New York. The Project consists of one above-ground, fully mixed anaerobic digester tank designed by RCM International LLC with a soft cover. The circular tank holds a capacity of 180,000 cubic feet. The digester system is operated at mesophilic temperatures and has a 25-day retention time. Biogas from the digester is primarily destroyed in a lean-burn engine-generator set to generate electricity. The Guascor MGG-500 engine can output 484 kW but the Stamford HCM636J generator is limited to 406 kW output. The project also has an enclosed flare to burn excess gas.
methodology: ARB Compliance Offset Protocol: Capturing and Destroying Methane from Manure Management Systems

name: Heartland Methane Abatement and Land Restoration  Packard & Kottke Ranch Project
description: Six orphaned oil and gas wells were plugged in Washington County, Ok. Each of the six wells were officially documented as orphaned wells with the Oklahoma Corporation Commission. The wells had not sold hydrocarbons for many years and were leaking methane to the atmosphere. The wells posed health and well-being risks to the landowners and threatened proximal natural resources. As of May 2023, there were over 17,000 documented orphaned wells in Oklahoma. Over the past decade, the Oklahoma State Funds Plugging Program has plugged an average of ~140 orphaned wells per year. At this rate, even with additional federal funds, state-allocated resources are not available to plug growing inventory in any reasonable timeframe. Rebellion Energy Solutions, the project developer, quantified the leaking methane, took responsibility for the wells for the purpose of proper plugging and remediation, and confirmed total methane abatement post-plugging. The project is mapped to several UN SDGs.
methodology: Plugging Orphan Oil and Gas Wells in the U.S. and Canada

name: Heartland Methane Abatement and Land Restoration Project 2
location: BLAINE, KINGFISHER, NOWATA AND WASHINGTON COUNTIES, OKLAHOMA, US
description: The project activity is the plugging of sixteen orphan wells in Blaine, Canadian, Kingfisher, Nowata, and Washington Counties, OK. Each of the sixteen wells in the project were documented as orphaned wells by the Oklahoma Corporation Commission. The wells were leaking methane to the atmosphere. Additionally, these wells pose health and well-being risks to the landowners and threaten proximal natural resources. Rebellion Energy Solutions, the project developer, has taken responsibility for these wells for the purpose of proper plugging and remediation. Methane leaking from orphan oil and gas wells has been mitigated via the permanent plugging of wellbores. Methane abatement is confirmed post-plugging. Land restoration is voluntarily conducted by the project developer in and around the well sites. The purpose of this project is to offset the fugitive methane emissions that were and would have been generated by the wells in question in the scenario that wells were not plugged.
methodology: Plugging Orphan Oil and Gas Wells in the U.S. and Canada

name: High Island Dairy
description: The High Island Project is a complete mix dairy digester system that was built to capture the biogas from dairy manure, the majority of which would have been stored in an uncovered anaerobic lagoon prior to project implementation. The biogas that is captured from the digester system is used to generate electricity through a set of 5 generators and/or sent to a boiler to provide heat. Any excess biogas not combusted by the gen-set is combusted in an enclosed flare. The effluent pond is also covered, with biogas captured and flared off intermittently. Biogas produced by the digester is monitored continuously using thermal mass flow meters.
methodology: ARB Compliance Offset Protocol: Capturing and Destroying Methane from Manure Management Systems

name: Hodag Forest Project (HFP)
developer: The Conservation Fund, A Non-Profit Corporation
description: The (HFP) is located in Oneida County, Wisconsin. It is a large, contiguous forest situated between the Chequamegon-Nicolet National Forest to the northeast and County Forest lands to the southwest. The property spans the boundary of two major watersheds: Great Lakes and Mississippi River. Forest and forested wetlands dominate the property and are host to iconic species like wolves and bald eagles. Stable but tenuous populations of state-endangered American marten and spruce grouse exist on nearby state and federal land with ranges that are suspected to extend into the HFP.
methodology: Improved Forest Management (IFM) on Non-Federal U.S. Forestlands

name: Homestead Green Energy
description:
Homestead Dairy began in 1979 by Floyd and Dan Houin with 110 cows.  The dairy grew over time and by 2004 the herd was increased to 1,800 milking cows.  As is common practice in the area, manure from the cows were directed to open lagoons where the manure decomposed anaerobically and resulted in large amounts of methane released to the atmosphere.

In August 2013 Homestead Dairy completed the construction of two above-ground, complete-mix anaerobic digesters designed to capture and destroy methane in the newly built Homestead Green Energy facility.  Methane is currently destroyed in two electric-generator sets or in a backup utility flare.
methodology: ARB Compliance Offset Protocol: Capturing and Destroying Methane from Manure Management Systems

name: Hood River County Tree Farm
description: The Hood River County Tree Farm extends from the north slopes of Mt. Hood towards the Columbia River in Oregon. The Tree Farm is managed primarily for the production and sale of forest products. Timber sales are a critical source of revenue for the County; harvests contribute 33 percent of the annual general fund revenue. Recent reductions in other revenue sources, including from the cessation of federal timber harvests and state laws restricting property taxation, combined with increasing costs of providing public services, have put the Tree Farms carbon stocks at risk. Rather than increase per acre harvest rates to generate needed revenue, the County will use carbon revenues to purchase additional timberland to help it meet budget needs. Through this carbon project, Hood River County is locking in a forest management regime that balances carbon sequestration with other management priorities, rather than pursuing a more aggressive harvesting regime and reducing carbon stocks.
methodology: Improved Forest Management (IFM) on Non-Federal U.S. Forestlands

name: Kettle Butte Digester
description: The Kettle Butte Digester utilizes manure from Kettle Butte Dairy near Idaho Falls, Idaho. The Project consists of one above-ground, complete mix anaerobic digester tank designed by Fagen Inc. with a dual-membrane flexible cover supplied by Environmental Fabrics, Inc. The tank is in the shape of a stadium, roughly 220 feet in length and 145 feet wide, holding a capacity of more than a million gallons. The digester system is operated at mesophilic temperatures. location: N5854 Meadowlark Road, Sheboygan Falls, WISCONSIN, US
description:
The Majestic Meadows Facility digester utilizes manure from Majestic Crossing Dairy in Sheboygan Falls, Wisconsin. The Project consists of one rectangular, in-ground digester, designed by Digested Organics LLC. 

This system is Digester Organics first fully Integrated Manure Management System (IMMS) that processes 20,000 gallons of manure per day, effectively harvesting energy through biogas generation, concentrating nutrients for more targeted crop use, and reclaiming clean water for farm use and surface water discharge. The system is a modular, scalable, and tunable high-rate anaerobic digester that converts over 90% of the organic matter into biogas with retention times of only 5 days. The digester system has a 100,000-gallon capacity and is operated at mesophilic temperatures. Biogas from the digester is primarily destroyed in a boiler which produces heat to maintain digester temperatures and a backup flare to burn any excess gas.

name: Replacement of SF6 as a Cover Gas at US Magnesium
location: 60 miles west of Salt Lake City, UT, UTAH, US
description:
SF6 has been widely used in the magnesium industry for more than 30 years.  SF6 is a highly-stable molecule  a major reason why it is such a concern for global warming as it can stay in the atmosphere absorbing solar radiation for 3,200 years.  Because of its stability and non-toxicity, the gas is used by magnesium die casters, producers and recyclers to protect the molten metal from reacting with air.  Without this protection, molten magnesium will oxidize and form magnesium oxide (MgO) deposits that greatly reduce the quality and strength of the final product.  The effective cover gas stabilizes the MgO surface film to form a protective layer that prevents further oxidation.
 For years, the industry has tried to find alternatives to SF6, which generally gets emitted in the process. US Magnesium has undertaken an effort to convert from SF6 to HFC-134a, itself a greenhouse gas but with a much lower global warming potential.
methodology: AM0065: Replacement of SF6 with Alternate Cover Gas in the Magnesium Industry

name: Scott River Shackleford IFM Project
description:
This project is in Northern Californias Mid-Klamath basin comprising 12,364 acres of diverse conifer forest assemblage, with globally significant biodiversity, important headwaters and endangered species, alpine meadows, and wilderness trailheads linking to the Pacific Crest Trail.
The purpose of this IFM project is to increase the forest carbon stocks during the project period by implementing management actions that go above and beyond common practices by creating expanded voluntary buffers, special wildlife areas, reduced intensity silvicultural practices, and increased rotation ages via FSC-certified management practices. The result of these changed management practices will be increased carbon storage on the landscape. Also, this management regime will improve the overall forest health and resiliency of the project area, while creating and maintaining habitat for a range of wildlife species. Carbon revenue will replace some forgone timber revenue over the project period
methodology: Improved Forest Management (IFM) on Non-Federal U.S. Forestlands

name: The Shamrock Ranch Sustainable Forestry Project
description:
The Shamrock Ranch Sustainable Forestry Project encompasses a total area of 17,050 acres (with forest cover of 13,626 acres), with approximately 80% of the land consisting of forested areas. This project is situated in Mendocino County, Northern California. The property predominately includes Madrone, Black Oak and Oregon White Oak with some mix of Douglas fir, Coastal Oak Woodland, Blue Oak Woodland and Montane Chaparral. The Shamrock Ranch is home to a large, trophy caliber population of the rare Tule Elk, as well as abundant trophy class blacktail deer, large flocks of wild turkeys and great numbers of wild Russian boar. 
The mission at the ranch is to find a harmonious balance between conservation efforts and business development by making the cash flow break even.
methodology: Improved Forest Management (IFM) on Non-Federal U.S. Forestlands

name: Thompson Family Forest Restoration Project
location: 15 miles SE of Heppner, Oreogn, OREGON, US
description: The Thompson Family Forest Restoration Project is located in north-central Oregon, approximately 15 miles southeast of Heppner, and includes 9,470 acres. The area primarily consists of pine and fir tree species of younger to medium ages resulting from decades of industrial forest management. The project will achieve GHG removals by enhancing the forest's health and resilience through thinning, harvesting less than annual growth  extending the rotation age, and managing a mix of species that can adapt to climate change. The result of these management actions will increase the forest's capacity to remove and store carbon over time, surpassing common forestry practices, and reduce the risk of stand-replacing wildfires within the project area. The resulting forest will be a mix of larger, older well-spaced healthy and resilient trees that will be adaptable to a changing climate with enhanced habitat for native fish and wildlife species.
methodology: Improved Forest Management (IFM) on Non-Federal U.S. Forestlands

name: TNC-Chestnut Mountain Improved Forest Management Project
description: TNC in Tennessee's newest preserve donated in 2018 by Bridgestone America's Inc. boasts cove and upland hardwood forest and sites undergoing restoration to shortleaf pine forests. The Bridgestone Nature Preserve at Chestnut Mountain forest contains many valuable ecological, educational, open space, cultural, and scenic resource conservation values. Chestnut Mountain also occupies a strategic position in the surrounding forested landscape, and its conservation serves to further consolidate a mosaic of protected areas in the Cumberland Plateau totaling 60,000 acres. TNC envisions Chestnut Mountain as a vital platform to promote forest health and climate-smart certified forestry, and aims to advance three conservation priorities: tackle climate change, protect land and water, and connect people and nature.
methodology: Improved Forest Management (IFM) on Non-Federal U.S. Forestlands

description: The Wabassus DLLT IFM forest project is located in Washington County, Maine. The project is on the Wabassus Tract of the Downeast Lakes Land Trust's Farm Cove Community Forest. name: Willet Dairy
description: The Willet Dairy Project is an in-ground plug-flow dairy digester system that was built to capture the biogas from dairy manure, the majority of which would have been stored in an uncovered anaerobic lagoon prior to project implementation. The biogas that is captured from the digester system is used to generate electricity through one generator or destroyed in a boiler. Any excess biogas not combusted by the gen-sets is combusted in an open flare. Biogas produced by the digester is monitored continuously using thermal mass flowmeters.

description: A-GAS RemTec 2015-2 is the latest project from Reclamation Technologies, Inc. dba A-GAS Americas, Inc.  This project consists of the voluntary destruction of Ozone Depleting Substances from all over the US, including; OH, TX, FL, LA, KS and PA.  The material that was destroyed was destined to be sold in the US refrigerant market where it would be used in equipment that is inefficient and leaky.  This project will result in the avoidance of approximately 134k metric tonnes of CO2 equivalent being emitted into the atmosphere.

description: The Adirondack Farms Livestock Project is a complete mix digester and biogas capture system that was built to capture the biogas from dairy manure, which would have been stored in an uncovered anaerobic lagoon prior to project implementation. The biogas that is captured from the digester system is used to generate electricity through one generator. Any excess biogas not combusted by the gen-set is combusted in an enclosed flare. Biogas produced by the digester is monitored continuously using biogas flowmeters.

description: This AgriCapture Grasslands Project #1 was developed by AgriCapture to conserve rangelands for a minimum of 150 years in Bailey County, Texas. The conservation easement will be held by Texas Agricultural Land Trust.  Further properties may be adjoined over time.

location: AR, MS, LA, MO, ARKANSAS, US
description: AgriCapture Soil Enrichment #1 will be to reduce emissions and enhance soil carbon sequestration on agricultural lands through the adoption of sustainable agricultural land management activities.

name: Albion

name: Alcoa Landfill Gas Destruction Project
description: The Alcoa Landfill Gas Destruction Project is a voluntary landfill gas collection and control system and beneficial use project at the Alcoa/Maryville/Blount County Sanitary Landfill.  The landfill is located in Friendsville, TN, and owned by the City of Alcoa.  The Project Developer is Alcoa Gas Producers, LLC.  At the time of project submittal to the Climate Action Reserve (January 2011), 31 gas wells have been constructed on lined cells, the header system is in place, and the blower flare system is operational (began November 8th, 2010). Future plans for the facility include electricity generation with the local utility (TVA) to purchase the power (up to 999 kW).

name: Alder Stream Preserve
description: The Alder Stream Preserve is an important ecological community in Central Maine. The Northeast Wilderness trust has purchased over 1,600 acres of land in this area and placed it under a permanent conservation easement in order to maintain its forever wild character.

name: Alliance Dairies
location: Gilchrist County; Trenton, FL, FLORIDA, US
description: Alliance Dairies, located in Trenton, FL is replacing the current manure management system (uncovered anaerobic lagoon system with no biogas capture or destruction and long-term solids separation and storage under anaerobic conditions) with a mixed plug flow digester which will capture the biogas produced from the manure.  Biogas will be destroyed in a flare and a gen-set unit that produces renewable electricity.

name: Alliance Dairy
description: The Alliance Dairy Project is a dairy digester system that was built to capture the biogas from dairy manure, the majority of which would have been stored in an uncovered anaerobic lagoon and in long-term solids storage under aerobic conditions prior to project implementation. The biogas that is captured from the digester system is used to generate electricity through one generator. Any excess biogas not combusted by the gen-sets is combusted in an open flare. Biogas produced by the digester is monitored continuously using thermal mass flowmeters.

name: Alligator River Avoided Conversion
description: Avoided conversion of approximately 2,500 acres of forestland in North Carolina to agricultural use.

name: American Environmental Landfill (AEL)
location: Sand Springs (Osage County) near Tulsa, OKLAHOMA, US
description: The American Environmental Landfill (AEL) that is located in Sand Springs, Oklahoma (Osage County) has a permiitted design capacity of 10.1 million tons.  AEL is currently not subject to NSPS requirements based on Tier 2 testing in May 2005.  Montauk projects that the earliest AEL will become subject to NSPS requirements is 12/2012 depending on results of the next Tier 2 test due May 2010.  Montauk's wholley owned subsidiary Tulsa LFG, LLC constructed and operates a landfill gas collection and recovery system at AEL which includes an open flare.  It started operation in February 2009 and the site is currently flaring ~ 650 scfm of 50% CH4 LFG.

name: American Soda LLC Ventilation Air Methane Project
description: The active underground mine ventilation air methane activity will utilize regenerative thermal oxidation units to combust Mine Methane liberated from mining operations that otherwise would have vented into the atmosphere by the mine ventilation system. Ventilation air methane that is liberated from the #4 exhaust ventilation shaft will be captured by the Project and directed in heated ceramic media beds that will oxidize the methane in the ventilation air. The Project will contain instruments to accurately measure and report ventilation air methane concentrations and volumetric flows, exhaust methane concentrations and volumetric flows, monitor destruction device operation, and track energy consumption to operate the Project. All Project equipment and instrumentation will be maintained to the QA/QC requirements of the Compliance Offset Protocol.

name: American Soda LLC Waste Mine Methane Project
description:
The active underground mine methane drainage activity uses post mining gob wells (PGW) systems to capture mine methane (MM) from longwall gob that otherwise
would have vented into the atmosphere. MM captured from PGW systems undergoes gas treatment in preparation for end-use management options. End use management options included in the underground mine methane drainage activity include qualified destruction devices within the refined trona ore process stream as well as incineration. MM monitoring and quantification measures include flow meters
and gas chromatographs to analyze MM.

name: Angelina County Landfill
description: The Angelina County Landfill is an existing permitted Type I Municipal Solid Waste Landfill located 6 miles outside of Lufkin, Texas and is owned by Angelina County. In 2011, a voluntary landfill gas collection and control system will be installed to destroy methane gas emitted by the landfill.

name: Anson County Landfill
description: The Anson County Landfill is located off of Allied Road near Polkton, NC.  The landfill's current contructed footprint is around 40 acres.  The landfill gas collection and control system was voluntarily installed in 2008 and consists of 15 vertical extraction wells connected to a utility flare. The landfill gas is measured for flow, temperature, and methane content.

name: AR-Joy Farm Dairy Digester
description: The project consists of a mixed plug-flow anaerobic digester to process manure from the dairy farm.  The digester generates biogas that is primarily combusted in one electric generator-engine sets.  The gen-set is a lean-burn, spark ignition internal combustion engine with a maximum nameplate rating of 0.335 MW.  An open flare acts as a secondary biogas destruction device when needed and during gen-set maintenance.

name: AR-Joy Farm Dairy Digester

An open flare acts as a secondary biogas destruction device when needed and during gen-set maintenance.

name: Arcata City Forest Barnum Tract
description: This property was formerly owned by a private timber company with a history of intensive harvest management.  The purchase of this ppropertyl by the City of Arcata is a move intended to restore and improve natural resources on these lands and provide habitat connectivity and public access for City owned community forests.  Work has begun to amend this property into the existing City Forest Management Plan and Non-Industrial Timber Management Plan.

name: Arcata Sunnybrae Tract
description: The Sunnybrae and Barnum forest tracts are  dominated by coastal Redwood and Douglas fir.  The City of Arcata purchased these parcels from private landholders in 2006 and 2003, respectively.  Project activity is defined as the purchase of these parcels and the transition away from even aged forest management to conservation based forest management that includes managing for older age classes.  These two tracts will be amended into the City forest management plan and the non-industrial timber harvest permit as part of project activity.

name: Ashford III
description: The Ashford III improved forest management project is located in mixed montane forests of Western Washington Cascades.  The project site is managed for structurally complex older forest to support wildlife that depends on this forest type.  Harvest will be limited, will take significantly less than annual growth and will be done with the goal of ecological restoration.

name: Athens-Clarke County Landfill Project
description:
The landfill consists of two closed unlined areas (EDA-1 and EDA-2), three inactive lined areas (Phase 1, Phase 2, and Phase 3), an active lined area (Phase 5), and with future permitted areas. The landfill gas collection system consists of 11 vertical wells on EDA-1, 10 vertical wells on EDA-2, 14 vertical wells on Phase 1, 14 vertical wells and 2 leachate cleanouts hooked up to gas collection on Phase 2, 6 vertical wells and 4 leachate cleanouts hooked up to gas collection on Phase 3, and a leachate cleanout hooked up to gas collection on Phase 5 for a total of 62 gas collection points.
The collected gas is routed to a Landfill Gas-to-Energy facility which treats the gas via compression, dewatering, and filtering before routing it to a Caterpillar 3520C genset capable of producing up to 1600 kW of electricity that is exported to the local power grid. A candlestick flare is available as a backup control device for the landfill gas.

name: Aurora Ridge
description: An anaerobic digester has been constructed at the farm to capture methane. Previously manure was stored in an uncovered anaerobic lagoon. Now biogas is captured and used to generate electricity. Electricity is sold to a local utility and excess heat is used to heat manure in the digester and a greenhouse.

name: Aurora Ridge Dairy
description: Aurora Ridge Diary installed an anaerobic digester to capture and destory methane. The digester is a modified plug-flow system designed by DVO Inc. Previously manure was primarily stored in an uncovered anaerobic lagoon. Biogas is captured and used to generate electricty in one 740 kW Guascor engine with a back-up flare. Electricity is sold to the local utility and excess heat is used to heat manure in the digester and a greenhouse.

name: Bartow Landfill
location: Bartow County, near Atlanta, Georgia, GEORGIA, US
description: Bartow County SR 249 Emerson MSW Landfill is located approximately 15 miles NW of Atlanta, Georgia.  Bartow County owns and operates the landfill of which Phase I was originally permitted and opened in 1979.  The landfill is currently filling Phase III which has been accepting waste since 2001.  The landfill has a design capacity > 2.5 million cubic meters.  The last Tier 2 testing was completed 5/12/2009.  Based on the results of the 2009 Tier 2 sampling and analysis, the facility is not yet required to design and install an active gas control and collection system.  Montauk Energy Capital designed and installed a voluntary gas collection and control system which includes an open flare in August 2010.  A permit has also been obtained for the construction and operation of a landfill gas fueled internal combustion engine to generate electricity.

name: Berkeley County Landfill Gas Project
description:
The Berkeley County Landfill Gas Project aims to quantity the CRTs associated with the voluntary installation of an active landfill gas collection and destruction system. The Berkeley County Water and Sanitation Solid Waste Management Facility (the Landfill) consists of four different MSW landfills. The Project Activity consists of installing an active landfill gas collection and destruction system in two of these landfills; the old Vertical Landfill and the Subtitle D Landfill. This will involve the installation of 30+ wells
connected with piping in the Subtitle D Landfill and the installation of new wells /
horizontal collectors, piping and the connection of existing passive wells in the Vertical Landfill. Gas from the Subtitle D Landfill will be piped to a candlestick flare, while gas from the Vertical Landfill will be piped separately to a sump, where it will then be directed to the flare.

name: Berkshire Cow Power
description: Pleasant Valley Farms installed an anaerobic digester to capture and destroy methane.  The digester is a modified plug flow system designed by DVO Inc. Biogas is captured and used to generate electricity in two 600 kW Guascor engines with a back-up flare.  Electricity is sold to the local utility.

name: Beulah Municipal Landfill (Dorchester County, MD)
description:
The Beulah Municipal Landfill (sometimes referred to as New Beulah) landfill gas system is a small project located near Hurlock in Dorchester County, Maryland. Project construction is scheduled to begin in the fall of 2008, with operation commencing at year's end. Methane will be collected and then destroyed by combustion in an enclosed flare.

A private company -- Curtis Engine and Equipment -- is financing and developing the project. Because the quantity of landfill gas available is projected to be too small to enable early investment in electricity generators, carbon offset funds would provide the only financial return for Curtis' investment.

name: Bi-County Landfill Gas Destruction Project
description: Bi-County Gas Producers, LLC has constructed a landfill-gas-to-energy facility that currently consists of 57 gas collection points and accompanying gas collection header.  The site operates two stationary reciprocating internal combustion engines that can generate up to 2.95 megawatts at full capacity.   The electricity generated at the site is sold to the Tennessee Valley Authority (TVA).  There is a 1,600 scfm candlestick flare for backup in order to maintain gas collection rates during engine downtime.  The gas collection and control system consists of vertical gas collection wells and liner gas collectors, as well as collection points on the header system to extract gas from the landfill and control fugitive emissions.

The project area is primarily redwood and Douglas-fir trees and has a coastally influenced climate.  The project area is owned and managed by the Conservation Fund.

name: Big Run Landfill Gas Destruction Project
description: The Big Run Landfill is located in Ashland, Kentucky, near the border of Ohio and West Virginia.  The landfill began accepting waste in April of 2004 and is a Subtitle D contained landfill. Construction of the portable blower-flare station by Big Run Power Producers, LLC began in late 2009 and became fully operational on December 23, 2009.  Tier II NMOC emission rates were below the NSPS threshold of 50 Mg/yr at the time of installation, and no other law or regulation required the project. Site specific testing for NMOCs were conducted in May 2010 by Carlson Environmental Consultants, PC. The results were submitted to the State of Kentucky DEP (KDEP) on June 4, 2010 demonstrating a 7.8 Mg/yr NMOC emission rate for 2010 at Big Run Landfill.  The project may, in the future, add a beneficial use component.

name: Big Valley

name: Billings Regional Landfill
description: The Project consists of a comprehensive active landfill gas collection and control system (GCCS) featuring an enclosed flare, utility flare, landfill gas to energy (LFGTE) plant and gas injection into local gas distribution system. The facility is expected to be capable of handling up to 2400 standard cubic feet per minute (scfm) of landfill gas (LFG) at full capacity. Operation at full capacity is expected by 2025. The LFG passes through a purification system, which includes two pressure swing absorption (PSA) beds.  First, carbon dioxide (CO2) is removed and the tail gas from the CO2 PSA bed is routed to the enclosed flare. The purified gas from the CO2 PSA bed is sent to the N2 PSA bed where N2 is removed and the purified gas is then injected into the local gas distribution system. The tail gas from the N2 PSA bed is sent to the LFGTE plant or is sent to the utility flare if the gas is offspec.  The LFGTE Plant currently consists of one internal combustion (IC) engine.

name: Black Warrior Solid Waste Facility
description:
The Black Warrior Solid Waste Facility is a municipal solid waste landfill located in Tucaloosa County, Alabama. The landfill began accepting waste in 1997 and has a design capacity of 8.9 million tons.  The landfill is currently 226 acres.

In early 2009, a GCCS and open flare were voluntarily installed at the landfill to combust landfill gas (LFG).  The GCCS consists multiple veritical wells that feed into the flare skid for LFG destruction.

name: Blue Mountain Biogas
description: The Blue Mountain Biogas project is a small power production facility utilizing methane gas produced from swine manure.  Manure from the swine farms is pumped to centrally located digesters.  The digesters are heated and the manure is mixed to maximize biogas production.  The biogas is then collected, scrubbed and used as fuel for reciprocating engines to produce electricity.  The facility will utilize two Caterpillar 3520 reciprocating engines, each with a nameplate capacity of 1.6 megawatts.  Waste heat from the engines will be captured to heat the digesters to approximately 98 degrees F.  The collected biogas can also be diverted to a flare or used as fuel for a stand-by boiler to produce supplemental process heat.

name: Blue Ridge Landfill

name: Blue Source - Francis Beidler Improved Forest Management Project
location: Berkeley, Dorchester and Orangeburg Counties, SOUTH CAROLINA, US
description:
The Blue Source  Beidler Improved Forest Management Project is located on 5,548 acres of land owned by the National Audubon Society in South Carolina.  The project is dominated by native hardwood species (bald cypress, black gum, red maple, sweet gum, water oak) in uneven aged stands with a smaller component of native softwoods (loblolly, spruce, longleaf pine).
The Project Area includes previously private and commercial forestlands.  The majority of these lands were actively managed for timber production and harvested prior to the acquisition by Audubon.  The region still has active timber operations occurring today, and no regulations or restrictions would have prevented the Owner from continuing timber harvests as of the Start Date.  However, because the Owner conveyed a permanent conservation easement to the Natural Resources Conservation Service, no active management of the Project Area will occur and the property will be permanently conserved as forest.

name: Bluesource - Camelot Landfill
description: The Camelot Landfill Project aims to quantify the CRTs associated with the voluntary installation of a candlestick open flare landfill gas control system.  The system was installed in and has been operational since September 2005.  In 2005, 35-40 wells were installed along the landfill perimeter, along with a candlestick flare and two blowers.  In 2008, the size of the collection system was doubled.  The landfill operator is currently negotiating a contract for the generation of electricity on-site.  It is anticipated that this system will be implemented by the fourth quarter of 2009.  Before the installation of the project collection system in 2005, a separate, pre-project landfill gas control system was installed on a small corner of the landfill on August 29, 2000, and included 7 passive vents.  The reductions in landfill gas emissions from the pre-project existing system will be netted out of project CRT quantification.

name: Bluesource - Carroll Avoided Grassland Conversion Project
description: This 16,000 property in Valley County, Montana will conserve soil carbon through the recordation of a conservation easement prohibiting conversion to agriculture.

name: Bluesource - Indian Creek Landfill Gas Project
description: The Indian Creek Landfill Gas Project (the Project) aims to quantify the CRTs associated with the voluntary installation of an active gas collection system and flare at the Landfill.  The Landfill was opened in 2004 and 10 vertical wells were installed in 2007. The candlestick utility flare was commissioned in November 2008.  It is anticipated that as the landfill expansion progresses, additional extraction wells will be added. The next expansion phase of gas extraction wells is estimated in 2010 or 2011.

name: Bluesource - MP Greenwood Landfill Gas to Energy Project
location: Greenwood County; Greenwood; 1 Mi. N of Greenville, SOUTH CAROLINA, US
description: Methane Power is under contract to develop a landfill gas to energy project at the Greenwood County Sanitary Landfill (GCSL) in Greenwood SC.  Construction of a landfill gas extraction system has been completed along with installation of a flare, a gas treatment and compression system, a five-mile pipeline, and a delivery system located at FujiFILM where the landfill gas is being used as a replacement fuel in boilers.  The project is expected to be fully operational in the fourth quarter, 2009.  The GCSL is operating and permitted for operations for the foreseeable future; it is not under a Title V mandate to destroy NMOCs.  Based on work done by the owner and under current regulations, the Title V action limit should not be reached for at least 6 to 7 years.  No collection system has ever been installed at the site.  Based on methane destruction by the system, in year 1 of operation, the project is expected to produce 79,000 tonnes of carbon offsets; in year 6, 100,000 tonnes.

name: Bluesource - MP Wilson Landfill Gas Project
description: MP Wilson LLC will develop a landfill gas (LFG) project at the Wilson County Sanitary Landfill in Wilson, NC.     The installation of the LFG system will be performed in two or more phases depending on construction costs.  In the first phase of the project, a landfill gas collection system and a 1,000 SCFM blower and open flare system will be installed to collect and destroy LFG.  The project is expected to ultimately produce 114,000 tonnes of carbon offsets per year.  These values are based solely on the destruction of methane by the system.  Over time,  an overall objective of this Project will be to collect the LFG for a beneficial use project, such as to generate heat and/or electricity for the facility or other end-users, while continuing to reduce LFG emissions.   Schedule and timing for installation and operation of gas-to-enery devices has not been decided as yet and will be determined based upon actual gas collection once the LFG system is installed.

name: Bluesource - Sarpy County Landfill Project
description: The Project consists of two phases; Phase one (1) involves the installation of an active landfill gas collection system and flare at the Landfill in December 2010. Phase two (2) of the Project involves an evaluation of the feasibility and the potential implementation of a beneficial use project.

name: Bluesource - Soda Creek Avoided Grassland Conversion Project
description: Bluesource - Soda Creek Avoided Grassland Conversion Project spans over 10,835 acres across McCone County, Montana. Through sustainable management, the project will maintain and sequester carbon throughout the project life.

name: Bluff Road Landfill
description:
The Bluff Road Landfill is owned and operated by the City of Lincoln, NE and is located at 6001 Bluff Road, Lincoln, NE  68517.  The permitted disposal area is approximately 171 acres.  The landfill began accepting waste in October 1988.

The Project includes the initial installation of 54 vertical landfill gas extraction wells, collection system piping, blower/flare station, and valves, pumps, and meters for the purpose of capturing and destroying methane.  Additional landfill gas extraction wells and collection system piping will be installed in phases as the landfill expands vertically and horizontally.

description: The BNW Ranch project area is estimated to be 4098 acres. This property was identified as a priority for conservation because of its habitat value and threat of conversion to crop production. TNC intends to place a no-till conservation easement on the property.

name: Bos Dairy
description: This project encompasses an approximately 4,000 cow dairy operation in Fair Oaks, Indiana that operates a mixed plug-flow anaerobic digester for the digestion of dairy manure.  After spending about 22 days in the digester, the waste is separated for manure solids, and the liquid effluent is stored in a lagoon.  Methane biogas produced by the digester is collected and piped to a series of 3 engine generator sets for combustion.  There is a biogas flare operational at the site to burn any gas not combusted in the generators.

name: Brewer Avoided Grassland Conversion
description: Located in Montana's Northern Great Plains, the Brewer Ranch has voluntarily chosen to permanently protect its soil carbon and forever remain in a grassland state by recording a no-till conservation easement. This conservation easement not only permanently protects soil carbon from release through tilling or other cultivation, but guarantees the ranch will continue to provide critical habitat for grassland species.

name: Bridgewater Dairy, LLC
description: The Bridgewater Dairy LLC Project is an in ground plug-flow dairy digester system that was built to capture the biogas from dairy manure, the majority of which would have been stored in an open lagoon system prior to project implementation. The biogas that is captured from the digester system is used to generate electricity through two generator sets. Any excess biogas not combusted by the gen-sets is combusted in an open flare. Biogas produced by the digester is monitored continuously using thermal mass flowmeters.

name: Brimex Energy and Biogas
description:
The Brimex Energy project consists of the installation of a new biodigester for the management of pig manure to reduce harmful greenhouse gas (GHG) emissions through methane recovery and displacement of carbon intensive grid electricity with renewable biogas energy. The power plant is expected to generate a net amount of 280 kWh of renewable electricity which will be delivered to the national grid.
 
The project activity includes upgraded infrastructure at the farm site including the installation of concrete manure tanks to ensure manure is captured effectively and transport to the biogas power plant site is facilitated and the installation of a solar thermal system, which consists of 40 linear parabolic solar concentrators (Power Trough 110 type) that can provide the biodigester an average temperature of 40 °C through a heat transfer process. In addition, a flare for burning excess biogas and a complementary oxidation lagoon were also installed.

name: Brook View Dairy
description:
Scenic View Dairy II (Freeport) is the third digester project in the state of Michigan and sister project to Scenic View I. The project benefits climate change strategies by reducing the amount of greenhouse gases produced in dairy operations, as well as reducing the greenhouse gases from the public electricity grid, by substituting fossil fuel based power with clean renewable power.

Currently, the manure on this 3,000 cow facility is directed to open lagoons where manure decomposes anaerobically and results in large amounts of methane. Methane is a harmful greenhouse gas. When the project begins operations, manure will be fed into three large tanks where the methane will be captured and used for energy production.

The project is under construction and is expected to begin operations in April 2008.

name: Brook View Dairy Methane Reduction Project
description:
The Brook View Dairy Methane Reduction Project consists of three digester tanks taking manure from approximately 2,500 milking cows and 500 heifers housed in freestall barns. The baseline system at Brook View Dairy consisted of an open, anaerobic lagoon. 

The biogas control and combustion system was installed and first came online in March 2008. The Project consists of three above-ground, complete mix anaerobic digesters. A flushing system automatically delivers manure and milking center wastewater from the main barns to a manure collection pit. The manure pit is constantly agitated and a piston pump delivers the manure to the three digester tanks. The project is generating electricity and has a nameplate capacity of 1.6 megawatts with its two Caterpillar gas turbine engines. The project also has a backup flare.

name: Buncombe County Landfill
description: The Subtitle D Landfill serves  the residents of Buncombe County and has been accepting waste since 1997. Six of the planned ten Subtitle D Landfill cells are constructed and have received waste. Cells 15 were used during the first ten years of operation (1997 to 2007) and are covered with 2 to 3 feet of clayey sand and are vegetated. Cell 6 began accepting waste in 2008 and is the current active cell. This system collects gas from Cells 1-3. The horizontal wells are connected to an open flare system with a maximum capacity of 3,000 scfm. name: Captura de Carbono en San Juan Lachao, Oaxaca
location: San Juan Lachao Pueblo Nuevo, OAXACA, MX
developer: INTEGRADORA DE COMUNIDADES INDIGENAS Y CAMPESINAS DE OAXACA AC
description:
Dentro del área del proyecto se desarrollarán una serie de actividades que se encuentran dentro del Área de Manejo Forestal Sustentable autorizado por la Secretaría de Medio Ambiente y Recursos Naturales (SEMARNAT). El Área de Actividad es definida con una superficie de 2,388 ha. Se espera desarrollar las siguientes actividades que aumenten los acervos de carbono por encima de la línea de base: 

Producción: generación de los volúmenes de aprovechamiento de manera sustentable, manteniendo los bienes y servicios asociados.
Aprovechamiento: extracción de los volúmenes de cosecha, con el mínimo impacto al ecosistema y con alta contribución al desarrollo social y económico.
Conservación: mitigación de los impactos ambientales ocasionados por el aprovechamiento, con el objetivo de  conservar las especies de flora y fauna silvestre, procurando en todo momento mantener la cantidad existente de las mismas.
Restauración: recuperación de áreas que presentan procesos erosivos severos,

description:

name: Captura de Carbono Forestal Ejido Ciénega de la Vaca
description:
El Ciénega de la Vaca vende madera en pie derivado de la aplicación de su programa de manejo forestal, mismo que fue autorizado el 17 de octubre de 2019 bajo el Método Mexicano de Ordenación de Bosques Irregulares (MMOBI).
En cada anualidad ejercida, el ejido aplica técnicas de aprovechamiento sustentable para garantizar la conservación y fomento de los recursos forestales.
Como medidas de conservación, se apega a la ejecución del calendario de actividades tales como apertura y mantenimiento de brechas corta fuego, recorridos de vigilancia, monitoreo de plagas y enfermedades, limpieza de las zonas de corta, acomodo y extracción de material residual, así como obras que sirven para el cuidado de la fauna y flora silvestre.

name: Captura de Carbono Forestal Ejido San Lucas
location: Amanalco de Becerra, STATE OF MÉXICO, MX
description: El Ejido San Lucas obtuvo su primer autorización para realizar aprovechamiento forestal maderable de sus bosques en 1997. A partir de entonces el aprovechamiento forestal se ha convertido en un pilar económico y de organización social del Ejido, generando empleos y ayudando al ejido a desarrollar capacidades de gestión del territorio. Como resultado, el bosque del Ejido ha mantenido la cobertura forestal y con ello los servicios ecosistémicos de los que depende el ejido y que benefician a la población de la cuenca.  La certificación de carbono que se almacene permitirá al ejido desarrollar actividades complementarias al aprovechamiento forestal tales como ecoturismo al mismo tiempo que permitirá un aprovechamiento más enfocado en la conservación de la estructura forestal y de la biodiversidad.

name: Captura de Carbono Forestal en Bosques Urbanos y Periurbanos de la Ciudad de México
location: Ciudad de México, Miguel Hidalgo, DISTRITO FEDERAL, MX
developer: Secretaría del Medio Ambiente / Fondo Ambiental Público del Distrito Federal
description: Es un proyecto agregado integrado por 6 predios: Bosque de la Loma, Bosque de San Juan de Aragón, Bosque de Tlalpan, Centro Educativo Ecoguardas, Parque Ecológico de la Ciudad de México y Bosque de Chapultepec 1ª y 3ª sección.Los bosques donde se ubican estos proyectos son de gran relevancia ecológica para la Ciudad de México, ya que en estos, existe un complejo de barrancas de alto valor ambiental, con ecosistemas naturales representados por bosque de encino y pastizal, que juegan un papel relevante como corredor ecológico natural entre la zona sur y zona poniente de la ciudad. La vegetación es dominada por arbustos de especies secundarias, herbáceas y pastos. La mayor parte de las especies arbustivas no posee espinas, entre las que se encuentran Jarilla (Senecio spp.), Palo dulce (Eysenhardtia polystachya), Mala mujer (Wigandia caracasana), Chapulixtle (Dodonea viscosa), asi como Uña de Gato (Mimosa biuncifera), que es propia de matorral xerófilo característico de la Cuenca de México

location: La Florida, Cardonal, Hidalgo, México, HIDALGO, MX
description:
El proyecto Carbono Otomí La Florida, se localiza en la región Valle del Mezquital del Estado de Hidalgo, en el municipio de Cardonal y en el ejido La Florida. El proyecto se esta desarrollando en un área con una cobertura principalmente de bosque piñonero (Pinus cembroides), y en menor proporción bosque de encino y matorral desértico rosetófilo. 

Los dueños forestales son los habitantes de la comunidad denominada La Florida, ubicada en en Cardonal, Hidalgo, esta comunidad esta integrada por una población indígena y originaria de la región, el grupo al que pertenecen es Otomí también conocido como pueblo Hñähñu, los habitantes de La Florida mantienen en uso su lengua originaria. 

El ejido La Florida realiza un aprovechamiento sustentable de sus recursos forestales, cosecha la semilla del pino piñonero llamada piñón rosa. El proyecto de captura de carbono tiene la directriz de generar beneficios ambientales y económicos que mejoren la calidad de vida de los dueños forestales.

name: Carlos A Madrazo
description: El ejido Carlos A. Madrazo,  se ubica en un corredor biológico que se conoce como Corredor de la Selva Maya (CONANP, 2017), permitiéndole tener conectividad con la Reserva de la Biósfera de Calakmul. Del mismo modo, forma parte de la Región Terrestre Prioritaria denominada Silvituc-Calakmul, de la región Hidrológica Prioritaria denominada Río Hondo y del Área de Importancia para la Conservación de Aves denominada Corredor Calakmul-Sian Ka an (CONABIO, 1998). El 27  de junio de 2021 en Asamblea, Toroto presentó el proyecto de captura de carbono ante el pleno y éste fue aprobado por mayoría. De igual manera nombraron a Toroto como su desarrollador y escogieron también al coordinador del proyecto. El ejido cuenta con 1,628 hectáreas de proyecto y con un total de 688  hectáreas de áreas de actividad.  Se pretende hacer un plan de restauración de la zona para atender la causa raíz de la degradación del ecosistema.

name: CE&S Dairy
description: The project involves the installation of a biogas control system (BCS) that captures and destroys methane gas from an anaerobic covered lagoon digester. The main components of the project are a covered-lagoon anaerobic digester for methane capture, biogas processing equipment, and an internal combustion engine for electricity production. Biogas is piped underground from the digester to the generation facility area, where it is scrubbed, cooled, and fed into the low-NOx engine-generator system

name: Cedar Grove - Maple Valley OWC Composting Project
description: The project consists of the diversion of one or more eligible organic residuals, including residential and commercial food waste, to an aerobic composting facility where the residuals are composted in a system that complies with Best Management Practices that ensure the composting process is operated under optimal conditions.  The project will encompass organic residual handling, pre-processing and aerobic composting at the Everett facility in Everett, WA, operated by Cedar Grove Composting.  The technology employed at this facility is the GORE Cover System and ASP Negative Aeration.

name: Cedar Grove Composting
description: Cedar Grove's Everett Facility employs The GORE Cover System and composts approximately 200,000 tons of organic waste annually.  The waste is a mix of pre and post consumer food waste, and paper, wood, and yard waste from surrounding counties.

name: Cedar Rapids Linn County Solid Waste Agency Landfill Gas Project
developer: Cedar Rapids Linn County Solid Waste Agency
description: The Cedar Rapids Linn County Solid Waste Agency is installing a voluntary landfill gas collection and destruction system. The system consists of vertical and horizontal wells both necessary because of filling sequence to reach final grade and vertical wells are installed. Horizontal collection wells will also be used for leachate recirulation once once final grade is reached. The system includes a blower/flare/controls and a consdensate management system as well as a network of header and lateral piping to convey gas to the flare.  The system is designed to handle approximately 3000 cfm.

name: Central LFG to Energy Project
description: The landfill is a municipal solid waste (MSW) landfill permitted to receive 5,000 tons of waste per day (TPD).    The facility was opened in 1996 and as of 2009 has 1.7 million tons of waste in place.  The exact date of closure is dependent upon the volume of waste deposited at the site. This project (Project) includes the design and construction of a gas collection and control system (GCCS) to produce Voluntary Emission Reductions (VERs) from the capture and destruction of methane gas from the Central Waste Inc. Landfill (CWL) in Alliance, Ohio, owned by Transload America (TLA), a private municipal solid waste disposal company.  The gas may be further used for the on-site generation of electricity to be sold to into the wholesale power markets as renewable energy.

name: Central Sands Dairy LLC
description: biogas from manure is produced in a digester and destroyed in a genset, boiler, and flare

name: Central Sands Dairy, LLC
description: The Central Sands Dairy, LLC Project is an in ground plug-flow dairy digester system that was built to capture the biogas from dairy manure, the majority of which would have been stored in an open lagoon system prior to project implementation. The biogas that is captured from the digester system is used to generate electricity through one generator. Any excess biogas not combusted by the gen-sets is combusted in an open flare. Biogas produced by the digester is monitored continuously using thermal mass flowmeters.

name: Central Sanitary Landfill

The landfill has a gas collection and control system in place over much of the site and gas is currently collected from vertical gas extraction wells. The landfill gas is measured for flow, temperature, and methane content.

name: Charlotte County Zemel Road Landfill Gas Capture Project
description:
Charlotte County is currently
installing an active gas collection system at the Zemel Road landfill. Initially, all gas
will be destroyed by an open flare. However, the County is working on finding a
beneficial use for the gas, most likely through the generation of electricity or the sale
of the landfill gas to a third party. There are no prior destruction devices of any kind
at the site. While the landfill's design capacity is large enough to make it subject to
federal NSPS for MSW landfills, Tier 2 tests show the landfill's NMOC emissions are
well below the threshold of 50 MG/year. Installation of the gas control and collection system is entirely voluntary at this time. The project is expected to go online in April
2010.

developer: Biogas de Juarez S.A. DE C.V.
description:
The Ciudad Juarez landfill started operating in 1994. The landfill has an estimated capacity of 30,000,000 cubic meters and is expected to be closed on 2040. Its footprint is 79 hectares. 

The landfill has three macro cells: A, B and C. Cell A was closed on April 2008 in which a extraction and collection system was installed for landfill gas collection. 

The collected landfill gas is used for electricity generation on-site using a destruction device considered as Rich-burn internal combustion engine as per Mexico Landfill Protocol. 

The electricity generation plant includes a generator-set of 6.4 MW installed capacity (comprised of four generator engines), a 13.8 to 115 kVA transformer during phase I, a transmission line that reach the local electric grid. 

The project has been registered since 30/11/2007  under CDM Standard and is currently being transfered to RESERVE for its second crediting period.

name: CMW Landfill Methane Reduction Project
description: Covanta of SEMASS (Covanta), in conjunction with Carver Marion Wareham Regional Refuse Disposal District (CMW-RRDD), designed, permitted and constructed an active landfill gas (LFG) collection and control system at the CMW landfill located in Carver Massachusetts the purposes of reducing Greenhouse Gas emissions. The LFG collection and control system, installed in 2008, was a voluntary initiative which replaced a pre-existing passive landfill gas vent system, which vented uncombusted LFG directly to the atmosphere.  The active LFG collection and control system was comissioned on January 7, 2009 and consists of an skid mounted utility flare to combust collected LFG connected to system of header piping to convey LFG from the Landfill.  The header piping system is connected to 28 gas collection wells installed in the landfill. The remaining original gas vents have been removed or capped to prevent LFG emissions from the Landfill Surface.  The Landfill is an active disposal facility which recieves a combination of Municipal Solid waste (MSW) and MSW combustion ash.  Portions of the landfill have been closed and capped with a geosynthetic cover.

name: Conhúas
description:
Conhuas es un ejido que se encuentra en el Municipio de Calakmul en el estado de Campeche
en México. Tiene una extensión total de 58,273.47 has y una población aproximada de entre
180 y 200 ejidatarios activos de las etnias maya y chol.
El ejido ha estado buscando certificarse como Área Destinada Voluntariamente a la
Conservación (ADVC), no obstante, la pandemia del COVID 19 hizo que los trámites se frenaran
y apenas están en proceso de solicitud.
Por estar muy cerca a la ANP de Calakmul existen aún importantes vestigios de selva que
constituyen el hábitat de varios animales que están bajo alguna categoría de protección;
podemos mencionar el jaguar, el puma, el ocelote. el tigrillo, el mono aullador, el mono araña, el
hormiguero, el pecarí, venado cola blanca, venado temazate y tapir.
Se propuso llevar a cabo actividades de restauración en un área de actividad de
aproximadamente 47,000 hectáreas de selva baja y selva mediana subperennifolia.

developer: Gallo Cattle Company, a Limited Partnership
description: The Cottonwood Dairy Farm Livestock Gas Capture Project consists of a covered lagoon anaerobic digester located in Atwater, CA.  Anaerobic storage of manure is the baseline waste management practice.  Manure is flushed to the lagoons from the barns using whey from an onsite cheese plant.  Biogas is combusted via 4 engines located on site.  There is an auxiliary flare in the event the engines are not operational.

name: Cottonwood Dairy Livestock Gas Capture Project
description: Manure treated and stored under anaerobic conditions decomposes to produce methane, which, if uncontrolled, is emitted to the atmosphere. This predominantly occurs when livestock operations manage waste with liquid-based systems (e.g., in lagoons, ponds, tanks, or pits). Within the livestock sector, the primary drivers of methane generation include the amount of manure produced and the fraction of volatile solids that decompose anaerobically. Temperature and the retention time of manure during treatment and storage also affect methane production. A biogas control system captures and combusts methane gas created as a result of manure management.

name: Cottonwood Dairy Organic Waste Digestion Project
description: The Gallo Cattle Company Cottonwood Dairy Organic Waste Digestion project reduces GHG emissions through the installation of a biogas control system that captures and combusts methane gas from treatment of manure and cheese waste. The biogas collection and destruction system was installed at the operation in August 2004. The captured biogas is combusted on-site in two engines with a total rated capacity of 700 kW and through a Varec flare.

There is a possibility, under preliminary investigation, that the Project will also send the gas through a pipeline to an off-site facility for thermal destruction in a boiler to provide heat for greenhouses. The Project has not yet started, but is completing the design and permitting process for construction of the collection system and plans to be operational during early 2012.

name: El Chichonal
description:
El Ejido El Chichonal, está ubicado en el municipio de Calakmul, Campeche. Los usos de suelo sobresalientes en el ejido. son el uso agropecuario, de conservación, servicios ambientales y de reconversión productiva. Los tipos de vegetación existentes son selva baja subperennifolia, selva mediana subperennifolia y acahual. El ejido forma parte del Sitio Prioritario para la Conservación de los Primates Mexicanos de nombre Silvituc - Calakmul, así mismo forma parte del Área de Importancia para la Conservación de las Aves (AICA) del mismo nombre. La población total del ejido es de 156 personas de las cuales la mayor parte son hombres, es importante mencionar que el Ejido El Chichonal presenta un alto índice de inmigración pues 94 personas que habitan en la localidad son nacidas en otra entidad (Chiapas).
Dentro de las áreas de actividad se encuentra el tipo de vegetación correspondiente a Selva Mediana Subperennifolia, la cual se caracteriza por ser un ecosistema de alto valor.

name: El Dorado Nitrogen, LP - Nitrous Oxide Abatement Project
location: Chambers County; near Baytown, TEXAS, US
description: The project involves the installation of a catalyst below the oxidation gauzes (a secondary catalyst) whose sole purpose is the decomposition of N2O. The catalyst does not consume electricity, steam, fuels or reducing agents to eliminate N2O emissions, thus, operating costs are relatively low and the overall energy balance of the plant is not affected. Installation is relatively simple and does not require any new process units or redesign of existing ones. The reactor basket support grid and basket will require modifications to accommodate the catalyst. Installation can be done simultaneously with the primary gauze changeover. El Dorado Nitrogen LP has contracted with a secondary catalyst provider to supply and assist with the installation of its catalyst system.

name: Elk Creek Coal Mine Methane Destruction & Utilization Project
description: The project will utilize and destroy post mine drainage CMG from the Elk Creek Portal of the mine. The Elk Creek Portal system is also connected to a set of compressors and a vent to the atmosphere which was used prior to implementation of the project. CMG from Elk Creek is discharged with two blowers into a 20 inch pipeline that carries the gas to the destruction devices. The Elk Creek Portal CMG flow is split between a single Abutec Thermal Oxidizer and 3 engine generators with a combined power generation capacity of 3.15 MW electric. Methane destruction with the first genset online began on 10/31/2013, and the project start date is defined as November 1st 2012.

name: Farm Power Lynden Anaerobic Digester
description:
Farm Power has developed the Farm Power Lynden Project, an anaerobic digester project in Whatcom County, Washington, near the town of Lynden.  Manure from three separate barns is flushed into a central pit, where it is thickened and pumped three-quarters of a mile to a mixed plug flow anaerobic digester designed by GHD Inc. (now doing business as DVO Inc.). 

The biogas generated by the digester is combusted either in an open flare or a high-efficiency Guascor SFGLD560 750kW internal combustion engine to generate heat and power.  After digestion, the effluent from the digester is pumped back to the farm and separated. Some of the separated fiber is processed in a rotating-drum composter. The liquid is stored in lagoons and applied to fields

name: Farm Power Lynden Anaerobic Digester
location: Whatcom County, Near Lyden, WASHINGTON, US
description: Farm Power has developed the Farm Power Lynden Project, an anaerobic digester project in Whatcom County, Washington, near Lynden, which shall generate verified greenhouse gas emission reductions that are in addition to any that would occur in the absence of the project.  The project consists of a mixed plug flow anaerobic digester with a flare and high efficiency reciprocating engine generator set that will destroy the methane captured in the digester generating GHG Credits.

name: Farm Power Misty Meadow Anaerobic Digester
description: Farm Powers Misty Meadow project will install a mixed plug-flow anaerobic digester at the Misty Meadow Dairy to in Tillamook, Oregon to digest the manure of approximately 3,500 animals. The digester will be fueled primarily by manure that is currently managed in an anaerobic lagoon which releases methane to the atmosphere.The project will instead capture this methane inside a mixed-plug flow digester and a covered manure storage tank and combust it in a 750 kW combined heat and power electricity generator. The digester was designed by DVO, Inc, installed by Andgar Corporate, and is owned and operated by Farm Power Misty Meadow LLC.

name: Farm Power Rexville Regional Digester
description: Slightly different at each farm: all manure that was collected in the baseline is sent to the digester, then to screw press separator, then to storage pond. The remaining manure stays on open lots. The farm no longer operates the screw press separator on the farm but instead sends all manure to digester and solids are separated out at digester site. Separated solids are used for bedding.

name: Farm Power Tillamook Regional Digester
description: The Farm Power Tillamook Regional Digester receives manure via pipeline from four neighboring dairy farms with an aggregate total of 2,000 milking cows (Holstein equivalent).  The mixed-plug-flow digester's biogas fuels an onsite combined-heat-and-power genset; it sells electricity to the grid and uses the heat for the facility's thermal load.  The project separates solids from digested effluent and stores the liquid effluent in a covered tank that also captures biogas before pumping the effluent back to the four dairies for land application.

name: Fauth Ranch
description: Located in Montana's Northern Great Plains, the Fauth Ranch has voluntarily chosen to permanently protect its soil carbon and forever remain in a grassland state by recording a no-till conservation easement. This conservation easement not only permanently protects soil carbon from release through tilling or other cultivation, but guarantees the ranch will continue to provide critical habitat for grassland species.

name: Fessenden Dairy
location: Cayuga County; King Ferry, NEW YORK, US
description: A covered lagoon anaerobic treatment system for manure digestion and methane collection and destruction was installed at Fessenden Dairy in July of 2008 to treat manure from their 1500 cow dairy operation in King Ferry, New York.  A USDA Conservation Innovation Grant was used to cost-share the price of the system.  The system is comprised of a 60 mil HDPE floating cover for manure digestion and methane collection, a flow meter for the measurement of biogas, and an enclosed flare for the combustion of biogas captured by the two lagoon covers.  There is a remote monitoring system in place which allows for the continuous measurement and recording of flow, combustion, and operation data.

name: Fiscalini Farms Anaerobic Digester
description:
The Fiscalini Farms Anaerobic Digester is a continuous flow, complete mix mesophilic digester system that handles manure from a dairy herd, whey from an on-site cheese plant, and other imported non-manure substrates. The system consists of two cylindrical digesters with heating pipes integrated into the walls and floor. The exterior of the tank walls are insulated with weatherproof panels. Each digester has a flexible, double membrane roof and is equipped with submerged agitators. Digester effluent is passed through two screw press separators, then to a storage lagoon. 

Biogas at the Fiscalini Farm is destroyed in a Guascor engine generator set and an enclosed flare that is only used when necessary. Biogas flow is monitored on a continuous basis before each combustion device via Endress and Hauser biogas flow meters. The methane concentration of the biogas is also monitored on a continuous basis via an ExTox biogas analyzer.

description: Solvay operates an active trona mine in Southwest Wyoming, 26 miles west of Green River.
