Es un predio de 786.1 hectáreas de superficie que antiguamente se ocupaba para actividades agropecuarias. Hoy en día es un terreno cubierto por diferentes tipos de selvas caducifolias y subcaducifollias en distintos estados sucesionales de crecimiento, lo que nos indica que son selvas en pleno crecimiento con altas posibilidades de almacenar carbono en sus estructuras.
El terreno es relativamente plano con algunas elevaciones no mayores a 100 metros, lo que le confiere al sitio condiciones ecológicas diversas que seguramente propiciarán características favorables para una recuperación sana de la vegetación. Prior to installation of the system, a small candlestick flare was installed as a safety precaution at the leachate lift station to burn passively collected gas from the lift station.

name: Indigo Ag Nitrogen Management
location: AZ, AR, CA, CO, ID, IL, IN, IA, KS, KY, MI, MN, MO, MT, NE, NC, ND, NY, OH, OK, OR, PA, SD, TN, TX, VA, WA, WI, WY, KANSAS, US
description: Indigo Ag is dedicated to our growers and to sustainability. The Indigo Ag Nitrogen Management project allows us to partner with our growers in reducing the amount of Nitrogen applied to their fields.

name: Indigo U.S. Project No.1
location: AL AZ AR CA CO CT DE FL GA ID IL IN IA KS KY LA ME MD MA MI MN MS MO MT NE NV NH NJ NM NY NC ND OH OK OR PA RI SC SD TN TX UT VT VA WA WV WI WY, MASSACHUSETTS, US
description: This is the first carbon project applying the Soil Enrichment Protocol, V1.0. The primary goal of this project is to promote a range of agricultural management practice changes targeted at increasing soil organic carbon (SOC) storage and reducing net emissions of CO2, CH4, and N2O from farms throughout the continental U.S. Indigo Ag helps farmers to implement climate-smart practices through an integrated system of extension and outreach, modeling, agronomy support, and digital data collection tools. Practice changes target fertilizer use, tillage, crop rotations, cover cropping, and livestock management. Beyond climate benefits, the project will increase farm resilience to weather and climate change, promote diversity of the soil microbiome, and increase rural incomes. This is an aggregated project as defined by the SEP. At submittal, the project includes approximately 1,500 growers across approximately 56,000 fields in 21 states. The project design assumes that an increasing number of

name: Ing. Eugenio Echeverria Castellot N° 2
description:
El Ejido Ing. Eugenio Echeverría Castellot No. 2 cuenta con una extensión territorial de 2,564.14 hectáreas, fue fundado hace 30 años cuando llegaron los primeros pobladores, atraídos por la posibilidad de obtener ingresos por la extracción del chicle. Fue renombrado como Ing. Eugenio Echeverría Castellot No. 2, porque durante del período de gobierno de este, se logró la asignación del terreno urbano al ejido.  El ejido está formado por 25 ejidatarios, 30 pobladores (aquellos que no han pedido ser integrados como ejidatarios).
Su extensión territorial está cubierto principalmente con selva mediana Subperennifolia, que es la vegetación dominante de la región, este tipo de vegetación se desarrolla en suelos rocosos, con pendientes y en hondonadas (Flores, 1974), los árboles dominantes no sobrepasan los 25 metros de altura y solo del 25 al 50% de estos pierden las hojas durante la sequía. Destacan como especies dominantes las siguientes: caoba, ramón, Tzalam, chaca rojo, cedro y yaxnik.

name: Intrepid Technology Resources, Inc. Anaerobic Digester at the Westpoint Dairy
description:
The Project, is a treatment facility which applies anaerobic digestion technology
in the disposal/treatment of manure generated by the WestPoint Dairy Farm.
Through the application of anaerobic digestion, methane gas is captured and
purified for use/sale in a natural gas distribution pipeline, and is ultimately
combusted in heating and power applications.

name: Intrepid Technology Resources, Inc. Anaerobic Digester at the Whitesides Dairy Farm
description:
The Project, is a treatment facility which applies anaerobic technology in the
disposal/treatment of manure generated by the Whitesides dairy farm. Through
the application of anaerobic digestion, methane gas is captured and purified for
use/sale in a natural gas distribution pipeline and is ultimately combusted in
heating and power applications.

name: Invista Victoria AAP-VNOX Unit
description: Abatement of N2O in the Victoria, Texas, Adipic Acid off gas stream has been practiced in the VNOX unit since the late 1990's. This project will drive incremental improvement in that abatement efficiency. The project consists of the installation of an alternative abatement catalyst, and a DCS advanced process control application, on the VNOX unit, decomposing the nitrous oxide that would have otherwise been vented to the atmosphere.

name: Invista Victoria NAP-AOP Unit
description: The project consists of the installation of a secondary abatement catalyst on the AOP unit at the Victoria, Texas facility. The technology will deploy the secondary catalyst below the gauze in each of the ammonia oxidation reactors, decomposing the nitrous oxide that would have otherwise been vented to the atmosphere.

name: Irony
project_type: Ozone Depleting Substances - U.S. - ARB Compliance
description:
The Project involves the destruction of eligible ODS contained in 73 30lb sized containers
consisting of approximately 1,910 pounds of 99.52% R-12. The material was sourced in the
United States and aggregated at the point of origin at 13465 Colfax Highway, Grass Valley,
California 95945 (the Facility). The material was then shipped in a single load from the
Facilityto A-Gas America's destruction facility in Bowling Green, OH where it was destroyed in a
Argon Plasma Arc Device achieving a minimum destruction and removal efficiency of 99.99
percent.

name: IX Ranch
location: Blain and Chouteau Counties, MONTANA, US
description: Located in Montana's Northern Great Plains, IX Ranch has voluntarily chosen to permanently protect its soil carbon and forever remain in a grassland state by recording a no-till conservation easement. This conservation easement not only permanently protects soil carbon from release through tilling or other cultivation but guarantees that the ranch will continue to provide critical habitat for grassland species.

location: Huasca de Ocampo; El Zembo, HIDALGO, MX
developer: ASOCIACIÓN DE SILVICULTORES DE LA REGIÓN FORESTAL PACHUCA Y TULANCINGO, A.C.
description: Proyecto Participante AGREGACIÓN 20, HIDALGO

name: Johnston County Landfill Project
location: Johnston County, NC, NORTH CAROLINA, US
description: The project involves the development of a landfill gas collection and control system and future beneficial use project at the Landfill. In particular, vertical extraction wells will be installed in Phases 3, 4, 4a and 5 of the Landfill and an open flare will be installed to destruct the gas. It is anticipated that the wellfield will be expanded and a landfill gas to energy project will be implemented in the future.

name: Katahdin Iron Works Ecological Reserve
location: Piscataquis County, Maine; east of Greenville, MAINE, US
description: The project area is an ecological reserve of approximately 10,000 acres that is part of AMC's larger land ownership of approximately 65,000 acres in central Maine.  The project area was acquired by AMC in 2003.  The reserve is legally designated under a conservation easement held by the Maine Department of Conservation, which was signed in March 2007.  The easement prohibits commercial timber harvesting.  The project area consists of a mix of northern hardwood, spruce-fir, and mixed stands.  Primary species are sugar and red maple, beech, white and yellow birch, red spruce, balsam fir and northern whitecedar.  The project area has a long history of commercial timber harvesting dating back to the 1870s.  As a result, the majority of the project area is in an early- to mid-successional condition with few old stands.

name: Kateri Grassland Project #1
location: Carbon County, MT; Near Roscoe, MONTANA, US
description: This project consists of placing a conservation easement on native grasslands near the Crazee Mountains in Carbon County, Montana. Kateri is working with a private grassland owner to implement the project, while Montana Land Reliance is the easement holder.

name: Kentucky Blue Ridge Landfill
developer: Advanced Disposal Services Blue Ridge Landfill, Inc.
description: The Kentucky Blue Ridge Landfill is located north of Irvine, Kentucky, approximately 30 miles southeast of Lexington. The site consists of approximately 49 acres permitted for landfilling of 149 acres defined in the permit on a 345 acre property. The site consists of the Contained landfill and a separate, closed residential landfill. The total permitted airspace is 8.5 million cubic yards. The landfill voluntarily installed a landfill gas collection and control system in 2005. The system was expanded in 2009. The system includes 14 vertical extraction wells and 2 leachate cleanout wells in the existing waste mass of the Contained landfill. At the flare/blower compound, the landfill gas is measured for temperature, pressure, and methane content prior to destruction in an open flare.

name: Kepel Creek Improvement Forest Management Project
description: The project was acquired by the Yurok Tribe from California Timberlands 2 LLC

name: Kimble Sanitary Landfill Gas Project
description: Project began to collect landfill gas from old closed portion of operation beginning 12/28/2009. Gas is currently collected and destroyed using an open flare system from LFG Specialties.

name: Kings Grove
description: The Kings Grove project is an Improved Forest Management (IFM) Project that is seeking registration under the California Air Resources Board Compliance Offset Protocol  U.S. Forest Projects Adopted: June 25, 2015. The Offset Project Operator is The Kings Grove, Inc. (the TKG). The Project is approximately 1,120 acres in size.

name: Kirkland Natural Pozzolan SCM Project
description: This is an emission reduction project that covers mining, production, storage, transportation and waste handling activities, associated with natural pozzolan (SCM) produced to partially or fully displace portland cement, consumed in cement and concrete industry applications. The Kirkland plant mining and production activities are within the same vicinity. As such, there is no need for long-term storage of raw-materials between mining & production. Additionally, the raw-material transportation from mining to production covers short distances. Processed natural pozzolan undergoes required quality control testing, stored in the plant silos before truck or rail transportation. Final product is sold directly to pre-cast concrete manufacturers and through a blending terminal to the readi-mix concrete end-users.

name: Klamath Forest Carbon Project
location: Siskiyou County, CA and Jackson County, OR, CALIFORNIA, US
description: The Klamath Forest Carbon Project is an improved forest management project on mixed conifer timberland located primarily in Northern California with a small portion in Southern Oregon.

name: L and D Landfill Methane Destruction Project
developer: L and D Landfill, Limited Partnership
description: L and D Landfill is an active 159-acre landfill used for construction and demolition debris disposal.  A carbon system is currently used to control non-methane organic compound (NMOC) emissions from the collected landfill gas (LFG).  Starting in May 2010, a new enclosed LFG flare with an associated blower/flare skid will become operational and the carbon system will go offline.  The flare will be the only LFG destruction device on  site.  Note that the carbon system vented methane emissions into the atmosphere and was not a methane destruction device.

name: La Estancia - ASRTulancingo
developer: ASOCIACIÓN DE SILVICULTORES DE LA REGIÓN FORESTAL PACHUCA Y TULANCINGO, A.C.
description: Proyecto Participante AGREGACIÓN 20 HIDALGO

name: La Gloria de Gante
description:
El proyecto se desarrolla en una finca cafetalera que se ubica en el municipio de Tapachula en el estado de Chiapas, a una altura de entre 1,000 y 1,200 MSNM. La vegetación es de bosque tropical y de pino encino. Hasta ahora hay registro de 200 especies de plantas vasculares distribuidas en 120 géneros y 59 familias botánicas. La riqueza de flora y fauna de la finca es impresionante. El área de actividad de este proyecto se encuentra en los linderos de las propiedad, se conforma básicamente de bosque tropical perennifolio cuya conservación se ve amenazada por la presión de las fincas cafetaleras así como de la expansión de parcelas agrícolas de las comunidades vecinas. También se registra tala clandestina. Para este proyecto estamos considerando 38 has de áreas de actividad de restauración para propiciar el cuidado del ecosistema así como la conservación e incremento de los acervos de carbono.
El área total del proyecto es de 104 has. y formará parte del agregado Finca Guadalupe

name: LA PERSEVERANCIA BIOGAS PLANT
developer: Energía Renovable de Cuautla S.A. de C.V.
description: 1 MW BIOGAS COMBUSTION PLANT, WITH 4 STROKE ENGINE, INSTALLED IN LA PERSEVERANCIA LANDFILL, LOCATED IN CUAUTLA (MORELOS), MEXICO

name: Laguna Om
location: Othón P Blanco, QUINTANA ROO, MX
description: El ejido Laguna Om se ubica en el estado de Quintana Roo, municipio Othón P.Blanco. El ejido tiene muy bien delimitada el área donde se realizan actividades agrícolas y ganaderas, sin embargo tienen miedo de que ante la difícil situación económica prevaleciente la frontera se amplíe y los pobladores quieran tumbar más selva por lo que quieren impulsar programas de ecoturismo, apicultura y restauración de su bosque ya que éste fue fuertemente explotado durante el siglo pasado. El área de actividad a llevar a cabo es de restauración y está contemplada dentro del área destinada voluntariamente a la conservación (ADVC), con un tamaño de 35,042.9 hectáreas de vegetación secundaria arbórea de selva mediana subperennifolia y vegetación secundaria de selva baja espinosa subperennifolia. El ejido se encuentra en la zona de influencia del Tren Maya.

name: Lakeshore Dairy
description: The Lakeshore Dairy Livestock Project is a complete mix digester and biogas capture system that was built to capture the biogas from dairy manure, which would have been stored in an uncovered anaerobic lagoon prior to project implementation. The biogas that is captured from the digester system is used to generate electricity through one generator. Any excess biogas not combusted by the gen-set is combusted in an enclosed flare. Biogas produced by the digester is monitored continuously using biogas flowmeters.

name: Lakeview Farms Dairy
description: The project involves the installation of a biogas control system (BCS) that captures and destroys methane gas from an anaerobic covered lagoon digester. The main components of the project are a covered-lagoon anaerobic digester for methane capture, biogas processing equipment, and an internal combustion engine for electricity production. Biogas is piped underground from the digester to the generation facility area, where it is scrubbed, cooled, and fed into the low-NOx engine-generator system

name: Lambs Dairy Digester
location: Oakfield, New York, NEW YORK, US
description: The Lambs Dairy Digester Project is a plug flow digester and biogas capture system that was built to capture the biogas from dairy manure, which would have been stored in an uncovered anaerobic lagoon prior to project implementation. The biogas that is captured from the digester system is used to generate electricity through one generator. Any excess biogas not combusted by the gen-set is combusted in an open flare. Biogas produced by the digester is monitored continuously using thermal mass flowmeters.

name: Larimer County Landfill Gas Project
description: The Larimer County Landfill Gas-to-Energy Project extracts landfill gas from the Larimer County Landfill in Fort Collins, Colorado.   Produced gas will be used in a 1.6 megawatt electric generator, with power sold to the Poudre Valley Rural Electric Association.

description: Proyecto participante en AGREGACIÓN 20 HIDALGO

name: Lassen
description: ARB compliant IFM project in Shasta County

name: Lawnhurst Farms Methane Reduction Project
description: The above-ground, complete-mix digester at Lawnhurst Farms is owned by Lawnhurst Energy, LLC and became operational in August 2013. The original manure management system relied on an open lagoon, but manure is now managed in an anaerobic digester. The EnviTec Biogas-designed system generates biogas that is destroyed in an engine-generator set and can produce 541 kW of electricity. Any biogas not used in the generator is destroyed in a backup flare.

name: Lawton GCCS
location: City of Lawton, Comanche County, OKLAHOMA, US
description: The project consists of a comprehensive active landfill GCCS including 41 new LFG wells and a candlestick flare.  The system extracts gas from the landfill and sends it to the flare for combustion.  The flare is the only destruction device on site and will only destroy LFG and pilot gas.

name: LCSWMA Landfill Gas-to-Energy Project
developer: Lancaster County Solid Waste Management Authority
description: This project is a joint venture between LCSWMA and PPL Energy Services (PPL), and involves the capture and combustion of methane gas generated at LCSWMA's Creswell (closed) and Frey Farm (active) landfills.  The methane is collected by a network of gas wells at both landfill sites, and conveyed to PPL's 3.2 megawatt gas-to-energy plant located along the Frey Farm Landfill's access road.  The methane is combusted in two 1,600 kilowatt-hour Caterpillar 3520G engine-generator sets.  Operations at the site began in December 2005.  Waste heat generated by the engine-generators is supplied to a nearby dairy operation for use in their ice cream manufacturing process.

name: Lenz Composting
location: 5210 SR 532 Stanwood WA 98292 (Snohomish County), WASHINGTON, US
description: The project consists of the diversion of one or more eligible organic residuals, including residential and commercial food waste, to an aerobic composting facility where the residuals are composted in a system that complies with Best Management Practices that ensure the composting process is operated under optimal conditions. The project will encompass organic residual handling, pre-processing, and aerobic composting at the Lenz Compost Facility in Stanwood, Washington, operated by Lenz Enterprises, Inc. The technologies employed at this facility include high-rate phase, aerated static pile (ASP) composting with controlled forced negative and positive airflow, turned mass-bed (windrow) composting for stabilization, and turned or unturned mass-bed compost curing.

name: Lightning Creek Ranch
developer: Climate Trust Capital Fund I LP
description: The Lightning Creek Ranch project area is estimated to be 4,112 acres. These grassland acres are part of the larger Lightning Creek Ranch, a 12,225 acre working cattle ranch located in eastern Oregon. This property will be protected by a permanent no-till conservation easement. In addition to avoided emissions from conversion to cropland, this project also contributes to larger conservation efforts in the area.

name: Linde
location: White, S. Dakota, SOUTH DAKOTA, US
description: :   A non-mechanical covered in-ground anaerobic digester has been installed to capture and destroy methane emanating from a previously uncovered dairy lagoon.  The lagoon is not required to be covered by any state, national or local regulations.  The bio-gas is destroyed in an enclosed flare.

name: Linde Dairy
location: Brookings County; White, SD, SOUTH DAKOTA, US
description: Linde Dairy, a 1150 cow dairy operation, located in White, SD, partnered with Environmental Credit Corp. to install a flexible cover on one of their open-air storage lagoons.  In October of 2009, Environmental Fabrics installed a 60 mil HDPE floating cover and biogas combustion system to capture and combust biogas that would have otherwise been vented to the atmosphere.

name: Lompico Forest Carbon Project
description: The Lompico Forest Carbon Project is an Improved Forest Management project located on the 425-acre Lompico property in Santa Cruz County, California, and is owned in fee and managed by Sempervirens Fund, a non-profit land trust. Of the 425-acre property, 309 acres are forested with coast redwood forest and associated native hardwoods around 100-years old, with the remaining acreage consisting primarily of coastal scrub and mixed chaparral. The project area is defined as the 285 forested acres that could be legally harvested under current laws and regulations. The project activity precludes all future commercial timber harvests, thereby preventing the CO2 emissions that would have occurred under business as usual (BAU). The long-term sequestration associated with the healthy, growing forest and the permanent prevention of future commercial timber harvest will provide reportable GHG reductions net of the baseline.

location: Santiago Tulantepec; Los Romeros, HIDALGO, MX

name: Lost Coast Forestlands Improved Forest Management Project
location: Humboldt and Mendocino Counties, CALIFORNIA, US
description: This project encompasses around 12,000 acres of privately owned forestland in Southern Humboldt and Northern Mendocino Counties.

name: LP Gill Landfill Gas Recovery Project
description: The L.P. Gill Landfill project is a beneficial use project that captures methane gas from the L.P. Gill Landfill and pipes it to a nearby ethanol plant. The project reduces the amount of methane that would have been released by a rural landfill serving a wide area of northeast Nebraska and neighboring states. The methane is destroyed in a thermal oxidizer in the ethanol plant or in a backup flare at the landfill.

name: Lubrecht Experimental Forest Carbon Project
description: Located to the east of Missoula, Montana, the Lubrecht Experimental Forest Carbon Project is an improved forest management project where the forest is managed to increase carbon stocks relative to baseline by employing uneven-aged management and maintaining higher residual basal area.

name: Lucchesi Tract
description: This parcel was a privately owned tract with a history of intensive  management.  The purchase of this parcel by the City of Arcata is a move intended to restore and improve natural resources on these lands and provide habitat connectivity for City owned community forests.  Work has begun to amend this tract into the existing City Forest Management Plan and Non-Industrial Timber Management Plan and to maintain and improve terrestrial and aquatic habitat conditions within the Jacoby Creek watershed.

name: Lunenburg VA Landfill
description: Lunenburg will collect landfill gas using the newly installed GCCS and destroy the gas in either a flare or a power generation plant.

name: Maas Energy Works Van Warmerdam Dairy Digester
description: The project is a covered lagoon digester installed on an existing dairy farm with a flush manure collection system. The farm milks approximately 1,000 Holstein cows. All manure is directed to the covered lagoon for digestion. The biogas generated under the lagoon cover is used to fuel a 600 kW internal combustion engine and generator. Waste heat from the engine is recirculated into the covered lagoon.

name: Mahoning Landfill
description: Mahoning Landfill is a sanitary landfill that operates an active gas collection and control system that consists of gas collectors and a flare.

name: Mailliard Ranch
developer: Mailliard Ranch, a California Limited Partnership
description: The Mailliard Ranch is an Improved Forest Management Project located in Mendocino County, California.

name: Maloy Landfill
developer: Republic Services Alliance Group II, Inc.
description: The Maloy landfill is an MSW landfill located in Campbell, TX. The voluntary landfill gas collection and control system became active in September, 2022. The system consists of 14 vertical landfill gas extraction wells with associated collection piping and flare skid. The destroyed landfill gas is measured for flow, temperature, and methane content.

name: Manejo Forestal Mejorado La Esperanza
location: Jose Maria Morelos, Quintana Roo, QUINTANA ROO, MX
description: El Ejido La Esperanza se ubica en el municipio de José María Morelos, Quintana Roo en México. Está conformado por 116 ejidatarios. El poblado de La Esperanza tiene 636 habitantes, 320 hombres y 316 mujeres, 89% de las personas hablan alguna lengua indígena. Actualmente el ejido tiene más de 7 mil hectáreas de superficie, de las cuales han destinado 4,155 hectáreas para el desarrollo de un Proyecto de Manejo Forestal Mejorado para proteger, mejorar la calidad de la selva y contribuir a la remoción de emisiones GEI, mediante la captura de carbono. Con este proyecto se desarrollarán actividades orientadas a reducir la deforestación, previendo fuertemente el impacto por incendios forestales, el establecimiento formal y reconocimiento comunitario del área de actividad del proyecto, así como el desarrollo armónico de las actividades propias del ejido.

name: Manglares San Crisanto
description: El Proyecto forma parte de las funciones sustantivas de la Fundación San Crisanto A.C. El presente proyecto no solo significa una esperanza de recursos económicos para seguir con las actividades de conservación del manglar, objetivo fundamental del Ejido San Crisanto, sino que ha fortalecido la participación comunitaria al mismo tiempo que ha fomentado la educación ambiental en la comunidad, comunidades vecinas que nos miran como ejemplo a seguir y en instituciones educativas que colaboran con nosotros mediante la capacitación de estudiantes y formación de capital humano en el área ambiental.

name: Manglares Ursulo Galvan
description: Este es un proyecto que involucra mucho esfuerzo por parte de la comunidad. No solo jovenes sino que igual adultos mayores hicieron su mayor esfuerzo por aprender mas sobre el bosque, cambio climatico y la metodologia que el Protocolo Forestal para Mexico representa. Este proyecto complementa acciones de reforestacion, limpieza fitosanitaria y construccion de canales cortafuego.

name: Maple Hill Landfill
developer: Advanced Disposal Services Maple Hill Landfill, Inc
description:
The Advanced Disposal Services Maple Hill Landfill (ADSMHL) is a municipal sanitary waste landfill located in Macon County on Intrepid Road approximately 5 miles west of the city of Macon, Missouri. The landfill began accepting waste at the site in 1976, which is situated within a property of approximately 430 acres, with 130 acres for waste disposal. The landfill facility is owned by Advanced Disposal Services Maple Hill Landfill, Inc., an indirect wholly owned subsidiary of Waste Management Inc.
The LFG collection and control system was developed within four of the landfill phases and consists of 37 vertical extraction wells and three leachate extraction points. The initial gas system was voluntarily installed and came online in September 2002. The gas from the wellheads is routed via main header line into the flare skid. The landfill gas is pulled by a blower and passes through knockout vessels to remove moisture prior to passing through the flow meter to the candlestick flare.

name: Maple Leaf Dairy East
description:
Maple Leaf Dairy is a family run dairy farm in Wisconsin. Maple Leaf operates an East and West farm adjacent to each other. The East farm is the Home farm that has been in the family for 5 generations.
Maple Leaf has installed an anaerobic digester at each facility to reduce GHG emissions, generate renewable energy, and recycle solids as bedding. The digesters are partially below grade, concrete channel plug-flow type designed by DVO, Inc. The solids are separated and the bedding recycled onsite. Maple Leaf East operates a 650kW Martin Machinery Guascor engine, a boiler and a flare.  Gas flow metering and data collection are performed by a Gen-Tec, LLC Carbon Catcher which utilizes Sage Prime thermal mass-flow meters.  Each combustion device is equipped with a gas flow meter and boiler and flare operations are monitored with thermocouples. The anaerobic digester at each farm is operated as a separate GHG reduction project. The baseline manure management system is an anaerobic lagoon.

name: Maple Leaf Dairy East
description: Maple Leaf Dairy is a family run dairy farm in eastern Wisconsin.  Maple leaf has installed 2 digesters at their facility to reduce GHG emissions, generate local renewable energy and demonstrate to other facilities how to improve their overall environmental footprint.

name: Maple Leaf Dairy West
description: Maple Leaf Dairy is a family run dairy farm in eastern Wisconsin. Maple Leaf operates an East and West farm adjacent to each other.  The West farm was built and became operational in August 2007.  Maple Leaf has installed an anaerobic digester at the West Farm to reduce GHG emissions, generate renewable energy, and recycle solids as bedding. The baseline manure management system was an anaerobic lagoon, and the project combusts biogas in an engine, boiler and flare.

name: Maple Leaf Dairy West
description: Maple Leaf Dairy is a family run dairy farm in Wisconsin. Maple Leaf operates an East and West farm adjacent to each other.  The West farm was built and became operational in 2009. Maple Leaf has installed an anaerobic digester at each facility to reduce GHG emissions, generate renewable energy, and recycle solids as bedding.  The digesters are partially below grade, concrete channel plug-flow type designed by DVO Inc. The solids are separated and the bedding recycled onsite.  Maple Leaf West operates two 650kW Martin Machinery Guascor engines, a boiler and two flares.  Gas flow metering and data collection are performed by a Gen-Tec, LLC Carbon Catcher which utilizes Sage Prime thermal mass-flow meters.  Each combustion device is equipped with a gas flow meter and boiler and flare operations are monitored with thermocouples.  The anaerobic digester at each farm is operated as a separate GHG reduction project.  The baseline manure management system at both farms was an anaerobic lagoon

name: Marble Creek
location: North east of Oroville Lake, CALIFORNIA, US
description: An ARB compliant IFM project in Butte and Plumas County

name: Martell
description: ARB compliant IFM project in Calaveras County

name: Martinsville Methane Collection Project
location: 225 Arden Circle, Martinsville, VA 24112, VIRGINIA, US
description: The City of Martinsville is installing an active landfill gas collection and control system at the closed Martinsville Sanitary Landfill for the purpose of generating carbon credits for voluntarily reducing emissions of methane.  The landfill gas will be controlled by a utility flare and monitored with a continous methane analyzer and a thermal mass flow meter.  In the future, the landfill gas may be used to fuel an electricity generating plant to be located onsite.

name: Matador Ranch and Cattle - Montana
description: Soil enrichment project on 18,623 acres. Action change focused on intensive grazing management, cover crops for livestock, water management

name: May Ranch Avoided Grassland Conversion
location: Prowers County, CO; NE of Lamar, CO, COLORADO, US
description: A high integrity avoided grassland conversion project on ~14,500 acres in Prowers County, Colorado.

name: McCloud River
location: Shasta and Siskiyou Counties, CALIFORNIA, US
description: The McCloud River project will generate emissions reductions through conservation-based management of commercial timberlands about 20 miles southeast of Mount Shasta in northern California. The goal of the project is to generate a reasonable return on investment to the landowners through sound sustainable forest management that increases the total carbon stores and overall timber stocking on the project site over time while achieving a variety of co-benefits, including protecting local water quality, providing habitat for sensitive species, and producing significant volumes of wood that will help to support the local timber economy.

name: McIntyre Ranch
description: McIntyre Ranch is located in the prairie grasslands of Southern Alberta, with over 55,000 acres of contiguous native vegetation and wetlands providing critical habitat for a rich diversity of plant and wildlife species. The ranch has voluntarily chosen to permanently protect soil carbon and forever remain in a grassland state by recording a no-till conservation easement, in collaboration with Nature Conservancy Canada and Ducks Unlimited Canada. The McIntyre Ranch project represents one of the largest conservation initiatives for prairie grasslands in Canadian history.

name: McKinney Landfill

description: The Mississippi River Islands Forest Conservation Project prevents deforestation of 4,070ac of land at high risk of conversion to agricultural use based on appraisals that analyze soil suitability, elevation, water access, economics, and local land use trends.  An estimated 400,000mt CO2e will be preserved in the trees and soil, plus at least 200,000mt removed as the forest grows over time. 515ac of these islands have already been converted to cropland prior to purchase by Trailhead Ventures, LLC, which will be reforested in a separate project. name: N.C.P.E. Benito Juárez
description:
El N.C.P.E. Benito Juárez se encuentra localizado en el municipio de Calakmul, Campeche. Su  tipo de clima  es cálido subhúmedo con temperatura media anual mayor de 22 °C y temperatura del mes más frío mayor de 18 °C y una precipitación que va de los 1,000 a 1,200 mm anuales. 
El tipo de vegetación predominante dentro del ejido es la Selva Mediana Subperennifolia. Este tipo de vegetación predomina en el área destinada a la conservación, ocupando así cerca del 40% de esta superficie. La especie dominante en este tipo de vegetación es el Zapote o chicozapote, que se encuentra asociado a la caoba, el pucté y el ramón.

name: N.C.P.E. Dos Lagunas
description:
El N.C.P.E. Dos Lagunas (Norte) se encuentra a 48 kilómetros al Norte de Xpujil. En 1978 se fundó la comunidad. La principal razón para establecerse en la zona fue la existencia de un cuerpo de agua de donde proveerse. Los fundadores de la comunidad tomaron la decisión de establecer el área urbana junto a la carretera ya que la mayoría de ellos trabajaba en los centros poblacionales aledaños como Hopelchén y en la comunidad de Zoh Laguna y debían desplazarse continuamente para trabajar en la compañía maderera (Caobas Mexicanas) hasta el año de 1989. El primer arribo de pobladores fue en el año de 1975, pero no se estableció como comunidad hasta algunos años después (Maza, 2017).
El núcleo agrario se encuentra localizado en las confluencias de los macizos forestales de la Reserva de la Biósfera de Calakmul, con las colindancias de la región conocida como La Montaña (pero aún dentro del municipio de Calakmul). 
del NCPE está compuesta aproximadamente de un 89% de selvas.

name: N.C.P.E. Valentín Gómez Farías
description:
El ejido Valentín Gómez Farías se caracteriza por ser uno de los ejidos con los suelos más pobres de la región, ya que perdió gran parte de su cobertura forestal a principios de los años 40 ́s, con el programa nacional de desmontes, fue en los años 90 ́s que comenzó a desarrollar programas enfocados a la recuperación de suelos introduciendo cultivos de cobertura como la canavalia y el nescafé, ambas leguminosas con el propósito de fijar nitrógeno al suelo.
Actualmente gran parte de esta cobertura vegetal afectada ya se encuentra recuperada encontrando acahuales de entre 15 y 30 años los cuales han sido objeto de manejo silvícola que permite observar en periodos cortos de tiempo un desarrollo de la vegetación secundaria, una mayor diversidad de especies vegetales y el regreso de la fauna silvestre dentro del paisaje forestal establecido, logrando mantener la cobertura forestal del ejido en un buen estado de conservación y restauración.

name: NCPE Centauro del Norte
description:
Ejido que se localiza en la región de Calakmul en el estado de Campeche. Dentro de las áreas de actividad se encuentra el tipo de vegetación correspondiente a Selva Mediana Subperennifolia, la cual se caracteriza por ser un ecosistema de alto valor y refugio de fauna amenazada como el jaguar (Panthera onca), puma (Puma concolor), hormiguero arborícola (Tamandua mexicana) y una gran diversidad de hílidos y tortugas de agua dulce: Rana brownorum y Rana vaillanti, indicadoras de aguas limpias.
En este sentido, es posible distinguir entre áreas con diferente vocación, destacando el manejo forestal, restauración y rehabilitación. No obstante, todas se encuentran bajo el entendido de preservar la cobertura forestal y la integridad de los ecosistemas.
Para el caso del aprovechamiento Forestal, el ejido designó un Aprovechamiento Forestal Maderable de Nivel Intermedio. El ejido cuenta con un ADVC con 9,722 has

name: New Energy One Livestock Project
location: Outside of Twin Falls, Idaho, IDAHO, US
description: The New Energy One Livestock Project is a centralized digester taking manure from three adjacent dairy farms under common ownership, called Cedar Ridge 1, Cedar Ridge 2, and Cedar Ridge 3 (these dairies, under previous ownership, were known as Rock Creek 1, 2, and 3). The roughly 200-acre set of dairy farms has over 9,000 cows combined, and is located in just outside of Twin Falls, Idaho. The biogas control system was installed and first came online in April 2012 with six above-ground, complete mix, continuous flow digesters. They have a planned hydraulic retention time of 20 days and are operated at mesophilic temperatures. The project is generating electricity and has a nameplate capacity of 3.2 megawatts with its two Caterpillar gas turbine engines. The project also utilizes a boiler and has a backup flare.

name: New River Landfill Gas Methane Destruction Project
description: The New River Resource Authority Regional Solid Waste Management Facility is owned and operated by the New River Resource Authority (NRRA) and is located approximately six miles north of the Town of Dublin. The Facility constructed an active LFG collection and control system in Area A during Fall 2007.  The LFG control system commenced operation on January 14, 2008. The initial phase of the LFG collection system at the Facility was installed during the fall of 2007 in conjunction with the installation of final cap on portions of Area A.  The vertical extraction wells were drilled during August and September 2007 and the LFG collection piping was installed during December 2007. The blower/flare station at the Facility consists of a single Perennial Energy (PEI) 1,250 scfm utility flare, a 1,250 scfm HSI blower.  The flare station was installed in December 2007, and commenced operation on 1/14/08.

name: New River Regional Landfill
description: The New River Regional Landfill (NRRL) is owned and operated by the New River Solid Waste Association (NRSWA).  Waste disposal at the NRRL began in 1992.  Active landfill gas (LFG) collection and flaring from portions of the NRRL was initiated in January 2003, earlier than required by federal and state regulations.  The landfill currently consists of five contiguous lined municipal solid waste landfill cells.  LFG is being collected from an approximate 10-acre area (Cell 1 and part of Cell 2) of the site. The LFG collection system consists of thirty-one 3-ft wide and 3-ft deep horizontal trenches constructed at 120-ft intervals on the landfill surface (including side slopes and one along the toe of the landfill) to capture gas.  This portion of the landfill was covered with a 40-mil very flexible polyethylene exposed geomembrane cap (EGC).

name: Newland Park Landfill
description: Newland Park Landfill (NPL), owned by Wicomico County in Salisbury, Maryland, started as an unlined municipal solid waste (MSW) facility in 1955.  It was brought up to RCRA Subtitle D standards in 1998 with the construction of its first lined facility.  In 2002, NPL began voluntarily operating a landfill gas collection and control system (GCCS) as a preemptive odor control measure.  Following construction of the landfill, gas migration issues have been encountered along the perimeter of the unlined portion of the landfill.  Modifications to the gas migration remediation measures are currently being implemented to resolve this issue.  These measures include: (i) extracting gas from formerly passive ventilation trenches along the perimeter of the disposal area; and (ii) an overall expansion of the active collection within the landfill.  However, during this time, at no point was NPL required to operate a landfill gas destruction device (i.e. flare).

After spending about 25 days in the digester, the waste is separated for manure solids and the liquid effluent is stored in a lagoon.  Methane biogas produced by the digester is collected and piped through a flow meter to an engine generator set for combustion.  There is a biogas flare operational at the site to burn any gas not combusted in the generator.  Flare operation is recorded using a thermocouple; all readings from the thermocouple and flow meters (for the generator line and flare line) are read continuously and the data stored using an electronic data logger system.

name: Oak Grove Harvested Bottom Ash (SCM) Project
description: This is an emission reduction project that covers production, storage, transportation and waste handling activities, associated with the harvested bottom ash (SCM) produced to partially or fully displace portland cement (PC), used in cement and concrete industry applications. The Oak Grove plant is located adjascent to a power plant, where bottom ash (BA) is collected from designated stockpiles and hauled to permitted land-fill for de-watering. Bottom ash is processed by milling and drying to meet the ASTM C618 requirements, and finally blended with fresh fly-ash (FA) at proportions (35%-50% BA), depending on production levels. 100% BA and blended (BA:FA) product are sampled before and after blending for ASTM C618 testing. The finished blended product gets distibuted to the ready-mix and pre-cast plants using heavy-duty trucks. A rail transloading system was installed end of 2023 and started operating Jan 2024.

description: The Yurok Tribe acquired 22,495 acres of former industrial property in the lower Klamath River watershed and within Yurok Ancestral Territory, out of which the Tribe has developed a 21240.5 acre carbon project. name: Phlogiston Phase I
description:
Prior to this project, the exhaust from the adipic acid process was directed to a Selective Catalytic Reduction (SCR) unit or a Thermal Reduction Unit (TRU). The SCR destroys NOX to comply with Clean Air Act Title V permit requirements but is ineffective at abating N2O. The TRU destroys both N2O and NOX but is less effective at NOX reduction. To comply with the Title V permit, the SCR was operated historically for a significant portion of the year. 

Phase I of the project is the installation of an absorption column that will convert NOX to nitric acid via a high-pressure water absorption process. This absorption column will allow the TRU to accept a higher percentage of the flow from the adipic acid plant, resulting in a higher quantity of N2O destroyed. In 2023 Phase II of the project installed a new control device. A second TRU effective at destroying both N2O and NOx was added to provide redundancy and reliability to maintain the highest possible level of N2O destruction.

name: Pixley Biogas, LLC
location: Tulare County, city of Pixley, CALIFORNIA, US
description: The Pixley Biogas digester facility presently operates at two sites that are connected by a pipeline.  Manure is collected at 4J Farms, pumped to the digester located near the Calgren refinery;  digested and the fiber is separated;  then piped back to 4J Farms, where the processed liquid is pumped to the Lined Pond, and later applied to fields as a fertilizer.  The digester type is mesophilic mixed plug flow anaerobic digester, and the method of methane destruction is combustion via duct burner (producing steam for Calgrens energy plant) or flare.

name: Port of Tillamook Bay Regional Anaerobic Digester
description:
Back in 2003 the Port of Tillamook Bay turned the site of the historic blimp hanger that burned down in 1992 into a facility for processing manure from local dairies, establishing the Darlene Hooley Digester. That system was designed to accept manure from 4,000 cows and to generate 400kW of electricity with the resulting biogas.

In June 2013 the Port of Tillamook Bay built a new, much larger digester and decommissioned the old Hooley digester. The new digester was designed to accept manure from 7,000 cows and the new generator has a 1.2MW rating. The new BCS along with the additional dairy farms that had not previously contributed manure to a digester will form the basis for the project boundary of this new project listing.

name: Presque Isle Landfill
location: Northern Maine; Aroostook County; Presque Isle, MAINE, US
description: The Presque Isle Landfill is a municipal landfill serving the greater Presque Isle region.  This secure landfill opened in 1982 and serves a population of 15,000 people.  The landfill is 13 acres in size with waste depths averaging 30-40 feet deep.  The liner system consists of a till liner with a perimeter Leachate Collection System.  Leachate is spray irrigated on-site.  The north and east sideslopes have a final cover system.  The existing landfill is licensed for 1 million cubic yards of space of which 600,000 cubic yards have been filled.  Annual waste intake is 15,000 tons.  There are approximately 420,000 tons of waste in place.  An active Landfill Gas (LFG) system, consisting of 13 vertical extraction wells and a blower/flare, was installed in 2008/2009.  The LFG system was placed in service on October 1, 2009.  A south expansion of the existing landfill is expected to be completed and placed into service in 2010.

location: Estado de México, STATE OF MÉXICO, MX
description:
A raíz de los compromisos internacionales derivados del Acuerdo de Paris, se pretende que las entidades públicas y privadas mexicanas transiten hacia una economía baja en carbono, incrementen su competitividad y enfrenten el cambio climático a través de proyectos acreditados y habilitados para su comercialización en los mercados internacionales., por lo cual un proyecto de captura de carbono contempla un conjunto de actividades planificadas y diseñadas para aumentar las remociones de bióxido de carbono (CO2) de la atmósfera, a través del aumento de los acervos de carbono, ayuda al fortalecimiento de los esfuerzos por enfrentar al cambio climático.
El Ayuntamiento de Toluca, a través de su Programa para el Desarrollo Ambiental Toluca 2030 se trazó como objetivo lograr la disminución de 30% de gases de efecto invernadero al 2030, en base a sus ejes estratégicos 3 y 4 que contemplan la reducir las emisiones contaminantes hacia el entorno natural y la Protección y conservación.

name: Proyecto forestal de carbono del Ejido Lázaro Cárdenas Número 2
description:
El Ejido Lázaro Cárdenas Número 2 se localiza en el municipio de Calakmul, Campeche, México; muy cerca de la frontera con Belice y Guatemala.
La extensión del área de proyecto es de 3740.77 ha, y tiene un área de actividad de Reforestación de 331.13 ha.
Los tipos de vegetación en el área del proyecto son: de selva mediana subperennifolia con formas de vida arbórea, y selva mediana con vegetación arbustiva degradada (acahuales), así como zonas de potreros (principalmente pastizales abandonados).
El ejido cuenta con un ordenamiento territorial comunitario y está en proceso de obtener una autorización para el aprovechamiento de materias primas maderables.
Actividades económicas como la ganadería extensiva generan una fuerte presión sobre los recursos forestales del ejido, los cuáles son abundantes en especies de flora y fauna. Se considera que el proyecto forestal de carbono ayudará a disminuir esas presiones y a generar beneficios sociales, económicos y ambientales en el ejido.

name: Proyecto forestal de carbono del Ejido Pioneros de Río Xhon - Ha
description:

El ejido se ubica en el municipio de Calakmul, Campeche, limitando al sur con Belice y Guatemala.
Los tipos de vegetación presentes en el área del proyecto son selva mediana subperennifolia y selva baja espinosa subperennifolia, así como pastizales cultivados.
El ejido tiene un ordenamiento territorial comunitario, y tomado acuerdos para delimitar áreas forestales permanentes, en las cuáles se desarrolla un estudio para incorporar estas áreas al aprovechamiento de materias primas maderables.
Actividades económicas como la agricultura y la ganadería representan fuertes presiones sobre los recursos forestales del ejido y el proyecto forestal de carbono se ha diseñado como una medida efectiva para disminuir esas presiones.

name: Proyecto forestal de carbono del Ejido San Diego de Tezains, Durango, México
description: El proyecto se desarrollará de acuerdo con el Protocolo Forestal para México (PFP), versión 2.0, de la Reserva de Acción Climática (CAR, Reserva). El área del proyecto considera la superficie forestal fotogramétrica de 61,098.2405 ha, mientras que el área de actividad de Manejo Forestal Mejorado (MFM) considera los 4,626 subrodales con aprovechamiento maderable, los cuales tienen una superficie de 31,321.6260 ha y de las cuales 28,596.952 ha son consideradas como aprovechables, con la reducción de cauces, caminos, líneas eléctricas y claros interiores. El programa de manejo forestal del ejido considera un ciclo de corta de 15 años 20152029, con un volumen aprovechable de 1,249,423.20 m3 total árbol para para los grupos de Pino, Encino, Otras Coníferas, Otras Hojosas, y Pino Muerto. Con la finalidad de llevar a cabo un proyecto forestal de carbono en la actividad de MFM, y con la intención de participar en la remoción de GEIs a través del secuestro de CO2

name: Proyecto forestal de carbono del Ejido Xbonil

El manejo forestal sustentable se combina con otras actividades económicas dentro del ejido, como la ganadería extensiva y la agricultura, se espera que a través del proyecto forestal de carbono se generen incentivos positivos que promuevan la conservación y aprovechamiento sustentable de sus recursos forestales y contribuya a disminuir la presión sobre los recursos forestales del ejido.

name: Reforesting the Land of the Jaguar
description:
Nuestro proyecto consiste en capturar medio millón de toneladas de CO2 en ciclos de 10 años, mediante la reforestación de 2 millones de árboles de palo de tinte (Haematoxylum campechianum) en 1,000 hectáreas de terrenos degradados.
Además de ser nativo de la región, el palo de tinte es una especie de alta densidad y rápido crecimiento, capturando hasta 50 ton CO2 por hectárea por año. El palo de tinte tuvo una importancia mundial en los siglos XVI al XIX, cuando representaba el 40% de la actividad económica de la región.
Estamos ubicados en Palizada, Campeche, al suroeste de la Península de Yucatán, en el área de humedales de la Laguna de Términos, una zona muy rica especialmente en especies de aves.
Nuestro método de reforestación se basa en un enfoque holístico, con principios de permacultura y agroecología, que permiten al mismo tiempo tener alta productividad, gran captura de carbono y enriquecer el ecosistema. El proyecto incluye más de 300 hectáreas dedicadas a la conservación.

name: Reforesting the Land of the Jaguar
description: Our project is restoring 750 hectares of previously degraded forest, which was used for livestock production for more than 50 years. Activities of the project include the reforestation of areas which haven't been converted to forests, the enrichment using native and endemic species, and the conservation and protection of several endangered animals: jaguar, ocelot, howling and spider monkeys, peccaries, jabiru and american storks, among others. In addition to restoring the land, the project aims to be pivotal in the restoration of the surrounding area, which is being impacted by palm oil plantations and deforestation, by providing a natural and regenerative alternative to them.

name: Relleno Sanitario Bordo Poniente IV Etapa
location: Zona Fedreal del Lago de Texcoco, Km. 2.1 2.5 de la autopista México  PeñonTexcoco,  Estado de México., STATE OF MÉXICO, MX
description:
The project comprises extraction, collection and use of landfill gas generated in Phase IV of the Bordo Poniente Landfill, as fuel and electricity generation. The project is part of an integrated landfill closure plan, that included a final cover system, leachate management, landfill gas collection system and a stormwater management system. 

The landfill gas collection sytem includes 490 gas wells, condensate traps, 32 regulation modules and 8 primary pipe collectors, interconected every 61 wells aproximetly. The total HDPE pipe network has a length of 78.6 kilometers. The gas plant has two blowers with a maximun capacity of 3,500 m3/h each and two enclosed flares for high efficoency methane destruction with capacity of 3,500 m3/h each. 

In addition, the project has a 1 MWe Jenbacher genset which generate electricity for self-consumption.

name: Remley Family Farms Anaerobic Digester
description: The Remley Family Farm is a 550-acre farm located in Roaring Branch, PA that raises gilts to maturity. They built the first 4,400-head quad barn in 2007 and have since expanded to include a second such barn and a 9,600-head nursery. A below-ground, complete-mix digester system was installed at the beginning of 2018 with the intent to create additional revenue streams for the farm. The 80' digester processes manure from the 8,800 grower gilts as well as thousands of gallons of local, sugar-based food waste to generate biogas for use in an onsite engine generator set. The generator is capable of producing 225 kW. They can also destroy gas in an on-site enclosed flare. Prior to installation of the digester system, manure was stored in deep storage pits below the barns, causing uncontrolled anaerobic breakdown of the manure.

description: REMC operates a Girdler Nitric Acid Plant (NAP 1) at their East Dubuque, Illinois facility.  NAP 1 was commissioned in 1978.   Plant specifications include a nameplate nitric acid production capacity of 220 short tons per day, a typical gauze campaign length of 120 days, operational 330 days per year, oxidation pressure of 120 psig, and a flue gas temperature of approximately 1000 to 1100 F.  REMC has retained ClimeCo America Corporation to engineer the fit-up of the CRI Catalyst N2O tertiary system and oversee all aspects of the CAR process.  The CRI tertiary catalyst is designed to oxidize 95% or greater of the inlet N2O concentration. The N2O catalyst will be installed downstream of the Ammonia Oxidation Reactor (AOR) and upstream of the tail gas expander.  The start-up of the system is targeted for July 1, 2011.

name: Ridgecrest Dairy
description: A covered lagoon anaerobic treatment system for manure digestion and methane collection and destruction was installed at Ridgecrest Dairy in August of 2008 to treat manure from their ~2000 cow dairy operation in Genoa, New York. The system is comprised of a 60 mil HDPE floating cover for manure digestion and methane collection, a flow meter for the measurement of biogas, and an enclosed flare for the combustion of biogas captured by the lagoon cover. name: Riverview Farm Anaerobic Digester Project
description: Riverview is a carbon offset project generating emission reductions thought the capture and destruction of methane at a dairy farm in Minnesota. In the project scenario, this methane is captured by an anaerobic digester and destroyed on site in the production of electricity.

name: Riverview Farm Anaerobic Digester Project
description: The Riverview Farm Anaerobic Digester Project is an in ground plug-flow dairy digester system that was built to capture the biogas from dairy manure, the majority of which would have been stored in an uncovered anaerobic lagoon prior to project implementation. The biogas that is captured from the digester system is used to generate electricity through three generator sets. Any excess biogas not combusted by the gen-set is combusted in open flares. Biogas produced by the digester is monitored continuously using thermal mass flow meters.

description: The Coastal Headwaters Longleaf Restoration Avoided Conversion Project will initially protect, in conjunction with the associated Improved Forest Management Project, nearly 4,000 acres of forestland from conversion to agriculture and residential development.   Going forward, it commits to restoring the Project Area to native longleaf pine ecosystem and timber cultivation, following decades of plantation loblolly pine production. A perpetual conservation easement, which permanently protects and commits the property to longleaf restoration, was transferred to a public agency in late 2018.  A global timberland investment management organization, a longtime leader in sustainable forest management, developed and manages the project. It was designed with a consortium of conservation partners to not only maintain important working forests and associated rural employment, but also protect, improve and expand critical local water resources and habitat for species including gopher tortoise.

name: Rochelle Municipal Landfill
description:
The project voluntarily captures and destroys methane from the landfill via a system of gas wells, conveyance piping, and condensate removal equipment, and destroys the gas at either an open flare or an energy generation facility. The wellfield consists of an old cell (Unit 1) that is not eligible for carbon credits since it had prior gas destruction, and two newer cells. Unit 2 is closed and contains 32 vertical wells and 8 horizontal collectors. The Horizonal Expansion (containing multiple cells) is the active fill area and contains 12 vertical wells and 10 horizontal collectors with plans for significant expansion. There are a few collectors on the original Unit 1 which are connected to the gas collection system. Any methane collected from this cell is measured and deducted from the credits claimed by this project.
The facility consists of three Caterpillar 3520C Gensets which combust landfill gas to produce up to 4800 kW of electricity that is delivered to the local power grid.

name: Rockingham County NC Landfill Gas Project

Rockingham County received authorization to construct this Project's landfill gas collection and control system from the N.C. Department of Environment and Natural Resources in April 2011, will be submittting an application for a permit to operate this system in December 2011, and will begin operating the collection system once system operation is approved. The Project involves collecting and destroying landfill gas from two sections of a closed unlined sanitary landfill and an open Subtitle D landfill. The Project will have a single flare station located at the Subtitle D landfill.

name: Roeslein Alternative Energy of Missouri, LLC - Ruckman
location: Gentry County, MO, near Albany, MO, MISSOURI, US
developer: Roeslein Alternative Energy of Missouri, LLC
description:
Roeslein Alternative Energy of Missouri (RAEM) is converting 9 hog production manure lagoons into Anaerobic Digestion Systems.  Each lagoon is connected to 8 barns, with each barn holding approximately 1100 finishing hogs.  The project location is in Northwest MO, near Albany, MO.

The conversion process entails first placing an impermeable lagoon cover and gas collection system over each lagoon, of approximately 4 acres in size with 15M gallons of effluent, 6-8% volatile solids + water.  Once the lagoons are covered, in the absence of oxygen, the lagoon will naturally shift to full anaerobic digestion, and produce biogas (65% methane, 34.5% CO2, up to 5000 ppm H2S, and saturated with water at ambient conditions.

The project includes capturing the gas and upgrading the gas to pipeline quality to utilize as fuel, or flaring for up to 100% control.  Scrapers will also be installed in the barn to improve water usage.

name: Rosendale Anaerobic Digester
description:
Offset Project Description: The Rosendale Anaerobic Digester Project is an above ground complete mix digester system with four digestion vessels built to capture biogas produced from dairy manure at the Rosendale Dairy. Prior to construction of the digesters, the manure was stored in an uncovered anaerobic lagoon at the farm.
When originally built the biogas produced by the two original digesters was captured then used to generate electricity through an engine generator set (genset). Excess biogas that the genset did not use was combusted in a flare.
In 2019, two additional digesters were added and the engine was replaced by a biogas clean up and compression system installed to generate renewable natural gas (RNG). A thermal oxidizer (TOX) was installed to combust off-spec gas and a candlestick flare was also installed to combust gas not processed by the RNG system.

name: Scenic View Dairy I
description:
Scenic View Dairy I (Fennville) is the first digester project in the state of Michigan and the first digester project in the US to generate both electricity and pipeline grade natural gas. The project benefits climate change strategies by reducing the amount of greenhouse gases produced in dairy operations, as well as reducing the greenhouse gasses from the public electricity grid, by substituting fossil fuel based power with clean renewable power.

Previously, the manure on this 2,200 cow facility was directed to open lagoons where manure decomposed anaerobically and resulted in large amounts of methane. Methane is a harmful greenhouse gas. Now, manure is fed into three large tanks where the methane is captured and used for energy production.

The projects first came online on in June 2006, and the natural gas injection system came online in summer 2007

name: Scenic View Dairy Methane Reduction Project
description:
The Scenic View Dairy Methane Reduction Project consists of a digester taking manure from the dairy farm and the swinery across the street called Mushroom Farm. The dairy farm is home to 2,200 milking cows and 1,500 heifers. Mushroom Farm is home to 10,000 swine which also contributes manure to the digester.

The biogas control and combustion system was installed and first came online in June 2006. The Project consists of three above-ground, complete mix anaerobic digesters. A flushing system automatically delivers manure and milking center wastewater from the main barns to a manure collection pit. Swine manure from Mushroom Farm began to be delivered to the manure pit in 2008 as well. The manure pit is constantly agitated and a piston pump delivers the manure to the three digester tanks. The project is generating electricity and has a nameplate capacity of 900 kilowatts with its two Caterpillar gas turbine engines. The project also has a dual backup flare.

description: The Cuyamaca Rancho State Park (CRSP) Reforestation Project is a project to create long-term climate benefits and restore a conifer forest which was destroyed by a significant natural disturbance.  CRSP is 40 miles (64 km) east of San Diego within the Peninsular Range of mountains.  The project consists of 2530 acres (1023 ha) in the 24,768 acre (10,023 ha) park, in dispersed patches designed to restore the mixed conifer forests of the park over time.  In October and November of 2003, the Cedar Fire burned over 279,900 acres (113,000 ha) in Southern California including almost the entire CRSP.  Conifer mortality in the park was high (>95%) due to extremely high temperatures which resulted in low seed cone survival.  Post-fire vegetation has been dominated by herbs, shrubs and re-sprouting oak species.  The goals of the project are to restore the biodiversity and ecosystem functioning of the park and protect it from threats of damaging wildfire, disease, and invasive exotics.

name: TMF Biofuels Dairy Digester
description:
I.	The TMF Biofuels Dairy Digester includes anaerobic digesters that receive dairy cow manure and some organic food waste from local food processing facilities.  A total of four digesters comprise the system, two of which are large (18 million gallons total capacity) lined plug flow digesters with geomembrane covers.  A third digester is a one million gallon agitated steel tank digester.  The fourth digester is a one million gallon lined modified plug flow digester with geomembrane cover.  Biogas is collected from each of the digesters via vacuum blower and routed to three Caterpillar G3520C lean-burn engine generators.  Excess gas is routed to open flares.
II.	A.  Monthly average dairy cows contributing to the manure collection system is about 20,000.
B.  The manure collection system is a flush dairy with each barn flushed four times per day.
C.  The baseline manure collection system included solids separation via screens and clarifiers.  Separated solids were placed in windrows and aerobically composted.  Liquid manure was routed through settling cells (8) and stored in Lagoons A, B, and C.  Liquid manure from Lagoon C was pumped onto farm fields in accordance with a land application plan.
D.  Baseline lagoons, settling cells, and pits had no covers.
E.  Approximately 85% of manure from the dairy herd was sent to anaerobic lagoons pre-project.

The farm is connected to the local electric utility's grid and initially, all generation is sold to the utility. name: Windsor-Bloomfield Methane Reduction Project
location: Town of windsor, Connecticut,, CONNECTICUT, US
description: Since 1972, the Town of Windsor has operated a municipal solid waste (MSW) landfill.  The Landfill is an active disposal facility which recieves a combination of Municipal Solid waste (MSW) and Construction & Demolition Bulky Waste. The landfill has not been capped and currently utilizes soil as interim cover material in inactive areas.  In 2003 the Town of Windsor permitted and voluntarily installed the first phase of a temporary landfill gas (LFG) collection and control system at the landfill to control emissions of methane and potential for LFG odors.  The gas collection system, designed for active gas collection and control, was expanded during two more phases between 2004 and 2005.  The LFG control system, an 800 cfm utility flare system manufactured by Perennial Energy, was initially comissioned in December of 2003 after the first phase of collection system installation.  The utility flare system consists of a 6 inch diameter flare stack, an LFG extraction blower, condensate removal, a control system panel and flame confirmation system and monitoring equipment including a flow meter and electronic data recorder.   The collection system is currently comprised of 43 vertical wells and 7 horizontal collectors connected to a header conveyance system comprised of 8-inch and 6-inch buried HDPE pipe.  The Landfill is anticipated to close in the next 2 to 3 years.

name: Yippee Farms
description:
The project consists of a complete mix anaerobic digester to process manure from the dairy farm. The digester generates biogas that is primarily combusted in two electric generator-engine sets. Each gen-set is a lean-burn, spark ignition internal combustion engine with a maximum nameplate rating of

name: Yurok Tribe Sustainable Forest Project
description: In April 2011, Western Rivers Conservancy transferred 22,237 acres of former Green Diamond Resources Company property in the lower Klamath watershed to the Yurok Tribe, out of which the Tribe has developed a 21240.5 acre carbon project.  The Property has cultural importance to the Tribe, as it sits within the Yurok Ancestral Territory. The Tribe will implement a lighter touch harvest strategy that will produce a continual supply of wood through repeated, light entries and the maintenance of a continuous tree canopy. The Tribe will manage the property to preserve and enhance the ecological and cultural value of the property.

name: Yurok Tribe/Forest Carbon Partners CKGG Improved Forest Management Project
description:
The Yurok Tribe CKGG Forest Carbon Project is an Improved Forest Management  project developed under the California Air Resources Board Compliance Offset Protocol  U.S. Forest Projects. The project site is on private land owned in fee by the Yurok Tribe of California in northeast Humboldt County, California.

The project is located on recently acquired land within and adjacent to the nearly 56,000 acre Yurok Reservation. The Yurok Reservation was created by the Hoopa-Yurok  Settlement Act of 1988 and is composed of the former Klamath River Reservation and Hoopa Extension.  The Project Area is located entirely within the Lower Klamath River watershed and Yurok Ancestral Territory.  Very little harvesting has taken place since acquisition.  Management of the property is designed to improve cultural and ecological values while at the same time generating income from carbon offset sales and logging, with the aim of developing higher value and larger trees.

name: Zeolite Used for Cement Replacement
description: Our project is designed to cover scernarios where our zeolite is used as a replacement for ordinary Portland cement (OPC) and/or other cementitious materails with a documented carbon footprint.  These scenarios include ready mix, concrete pavers and other manufactured concrete products today, and likely other concrete applications in the future.  Because there is no heat or significant energy input required during formulation, processing or at the point of application (unlike OPC and many other SCMs), for every ton of OPC that is replaced with zeolite, we prevent approximately one ton of carbon dioxide (CO2) from being created.

name: Araku Valley Livelihood Project
project_type: Agriculture Forestry and Other Land Use
description: Various horticultural tree species and shrubs will be planted on 6,024 ha in this VCS ARR project activity in a 3-year project roll out period. Eight different species groups are distinguished based mainly on similar growth characteristics (similar biomass accumulation rates) and planting densities. All groups will be planted on the 6,024 ha. Coffee will be introduced after 3 years on 3,000 ha. The different species groups of the proposed ARR project activity comprise, among others, Mango, Guava, Custard apple, Orange, Lemon, and other local fruit trees. In addition Teak, Bamboo and various indigenous trees will be introduced. After a tree establishment phase, coffee will be planted under shade. The planting area is located on degraded land with very low plant cover (around 60% of the land is classified as barren land.). The horticultural tree planting will sequester carbon and generate additional income by turning this degraded, low carbon lands into high carbon sites. The overall goal of the project is to improve the livelihood of small and marginalized tribal communities in the Araku Valley of Visakhapatnam district in the state of Andhra Pradesh in India. The project will turn a low carbon landscape into a high carbon multiple use landscape improving food security and generating additional income for the community. The project area will cover 333 villages in 5 different Mandals and as an average approximately 16 planting sites per village. Totally, on 5,442 discrete areas of non-forested land with a geographical identification the horticulture systems will be established. The tribal communities living in the project area are Bhagathas, Valmikies, Kamaras, Porjas and Kondhs. They converse in a dialect of Adivasi Oriya and Kui. The area is very secluded and still many of the villages are inaccessible by vehicles. 90% of the population in the project area is living below the poverty line. The livelihoods of the tribal communities in the region have a distinct set of economic characteristics which differ widely from the lowlands adjoining this area of Visakhapatnam, with respect to climate, soil, rainfall, habitat, flora, and fauna. Subsistence agriculture is the primary livelihood for nearly 99% of the tribes and special characteristics are: • Agriculture through Slash and Burn Technique on hill slopes, known as Podu cultivation; • Gathering of Non Timber Forest Products; • Farming on terraces or in valleys both under irrigated and rain fed condition, and • Cattle and backyards gardens. The current annual average income of households in the region ranges between INR.15, 000 to INR 18, 000 (USD 350-400). Indiscriminate Podu cultivation has resulted in barren lands with increased soil erosion leading to environmental degradation has contributed to poverty and deprivation in the area. Dependence on forest and land has become extremely difficult for the tribal way of live. The rate of growth in population and diminishing forest cover makes them extremely vulnerable. Therefore, an integrated, holistic development approach revolving around building their local resources and skills to improve the agriculture and Non Timber Forest Produce (NTFP) needs to be adopted to address the issue of tribal poverty and build their economies.
abuse_descr: According to the project document, communities have 'agreed' that they will have the right to the fruits and other produce of the horticulture trees, but not to the carbon credits generated by the project. The document says, 'farmers and the communities have agreed that the property rights on the carbon credits generated by this restoration are exclusively allocated to the developer of the Project.' Furthermore, 'under this agreement, the beneficiary community is committed not to assert any property rights over the carbon credits generated and/or to be generated by the Project.' But members of the community claimed that they knew nothing about carbon credits, and that the documents were signed without knowing what was in the document.
